english: Is it better to flood my whole field with stream water or apply water directly to the plant roots?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ nu awo ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli loo okɛ nu awo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Direct root watering uses far less water and keeps weeds from growing everywhere, whereas flooding wastes water through evaporation and run-off.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ekɛ nu fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu afua lɛ baaha nu fɔŋ atsɔ la ni hoɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops wilt quickly even when I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ oya eyɛ mli akɛ mishwieɔ amɛ nu daa leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Watering under high heat causes quick evaporation before roots can drink; watering early in the morning or late evening gives plants time to absorb moisture.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ la ni mli edɔ waa wo mli lɛ, ebaaha etsɔ la oya dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa be ni ekɛnuɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow during a short dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow during dry spells because the roots need water to pull nitrogen from the soil, so water stress creates temporary nutrient deficiency.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu he miihia shishifãi koni amɛjie nitrogen kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, nu he haomɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ be kukuoo mli baa.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry leaves help them in dry weather?
ga: Mulching around Te miŋmɔshi nibii ni baai egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves acts like a blanket that keeps the ground cool and stops moisture from evaporating, helping your crops stay hydrated longer.
ga: Nibii ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ akaho. Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Which crops can I plant if my land gets hot and dry very easily?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa ni edɔ?

english: Drought-hardy crops like cassava, sorghum, millet, or cowpeas thrive better in hot and dry conditions compared to thirsty crops like rice or leafy vegetables.
ga: Nibii ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ akɛto tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai ni baai yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why does the shea tree grow naturally in Northern Ghana, but fails to grow well if I plant it in the forest regions of the South?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shea tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ? Shi enyɛŋ eda jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu yɛ kooi lɛ anaigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Shea trees are adapted to dry climates, long dry seasons, and abundant sunshine found in the northern savanna. In southern forest zones, the high rainfall and heavy shade rot their roots and prevent them from thriving.
ga: Shea tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ amli. hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo ni anaa yɛ kooyigbɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ. yɛ kooi lɛ anaigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa amɛdaraa.

english: Why does oil palm thrive in rainy places like the Western Region, but stays weak if planted in dry savanna areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ tamɔ anaigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ebɛ hewalɛ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ hei ni savannah egbi lɛ.

english: Oil palm trees require heavy, consistent rainfall and warm, humid air year-round to build up water in their trunks and produce heavy fruit bunches. Dry savanna regions simply do not provide enough groundwater for them.
ga: Mu tsei biɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be fɛɛ be, kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛná nu yɛ amɛtsei lɛ amli ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Savannah kpokpaa ni nɔ egbi lɛ haaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do coconut palms grow so well along the sandy coastal beaches of Ghana where other crops dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akokoso tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana ŋshɔnaa hei lɛ? Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi egbi?

english: Coconut palms have highly flexible roots that absorb fresh groundwater beneath sandy soils and can tolerate high levels of salt. Their trunks are also built to bend with strong ocean winds without breaking.
ga: Kokoo tsei yɛ shishifãi ni nyɛɔ amɛhe waa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋã lɛ shishi lɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ ŋmei babaoo gbɛ. Afee amɛtsitsii lɛ koni amɛkoto yɛ ŋshɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ mli ni amɛkuuu.

english: Why do cashew trees drop almost all their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew tsei lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cashew trees shed their leaves to protect themselves from drying out. Leaves lose water quickly in hot, dry air, so dropping them helps the tree preserve moisture inside its trunk until the rains return.
ga: Cashew tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oshi lɛ yɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ eshishifã lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does my mango tree produce hundreds of tiny fruits every year, but then drops most of them before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Yibii ohai abɔ daa afi Shi no sɛɛ lɛ, nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɛɛ baagbee shi dani eda?

english: Trees drop excess young fruits as a survival mechanism when they don't have enough food, water, or energy to support every single fruit to maturity. It protects the main tree from dying of exhaustion.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ aduawai bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ amɛshwieɔ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ amɛbɛ niyenii, nu, loo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai fɛɛ aduawai ahi shi kɛyashi amɛdara. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso titri lɛ he kɛjɛɔ tɔlɛ he.

english: Why do native weeds and wild bushes grow back faster after bush clearing than the crops I carefully plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɛ koo mli tsei bibii lɛ daraa oya beni ajie tsei bibii lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Wild plants have evolved over hundreds of years to survive in local Ghanaian soils. Their seeds can lie sleeping in the dirt for years, ready to jump up instantly to cover bare earth and protect the soil from sun damage.
ga: Koo mli tsei etsake yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ Ghana maŋ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ. Edumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. Efee klalo akɛ ebaatu ehe shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die so quickly if I cut down all the large trees around them on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛji mifo tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni ashi yɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, delicate leaves that get scorched by direct sunlight. Large forest trees act as natural umbrellas, shielding young cocoa from excessive sun and keeping the ground cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ. Koo mli tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni fe nine lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stay short whenever water collects and sits on my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nu faaa yɛ amɛmli be fɛɛ be ni nu baabua amɛhe naa ni eyɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize roots need to breathe air from small pockets in the soil. When water sits on the land without draining, it drowns the roots, preventing them from taking up nutrients and turning the leaves yellow.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛ he bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ nu ta shikpɔŋ ni ejeee kpo lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no haaa amɛná niyenii kpakpai, ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do elderly farmers tell us to clear loose, soft soil into high mounds before planting yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa lɛ kɛɛ wɔ akɛ wɔjie sũ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ dani wɔdu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow straight down into the earth. Building loose, soft soil mounds allows the tuber to expand freely without pushing against hard, packed dirt that would deform or stunt its growth.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afee lɛ haa bulb lɛ mli shwereɔ ni ekɛ ehe wooo shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ ni baanyɛ afite loo eha edalɛ aba lɛ mli.

english: Why do groundnuts grow so well in sandy soil where heavy tubers like yam struggle to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ, he ni ŋmei ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei ni mli tse lɛ shweremɔ wa lɛ?

english: After flowering above ground, groundnut pegs must push themselves back down into the earth to grow nuts. Soft, sandy soil allows these delicate pegs to enter easily, whereas hard clay soil blocks them.
ga: Beni ewo fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ Esa akɛ ŋmei ŋmei lɛ aku esɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɛɛ akɛ amɛaabote mli. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ enaa lɛ.

english: Why are my corn leaves turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen or water. Nitrogen helps the leaves produce food; without enough of it in the soil, the plant pulls nutrients from older bottom leaves to feed new growth, causing the lower leaves to yellow first.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: How do I know the best distance to leave between my maize plants when sowing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni kã ŋmãa tsei ateŋ beni aduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Planting maize too close together forces the crops to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and small cobs. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce full, healthy corn ears.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes my maize stalks to fall over easily during heavy wind and rain?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Maize stalks fall over when root systems are weak, planted too shallowly, or damaged by pests, or when the soil lacks potassium. Strong roots and balanced soil nutrients act as anchors to keep the plant standing.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium Shishifãi ni wa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi.

english: Which local Ghanaian food crops can I harvest quickly if there is a sudden food shortage?
ga: Mɛɛ Ghana maŋ lɛ mli niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ makpa oya kɛji niyenii faaa trukaa?

english: Crops like sweet potatoes, cassava, and early-maturing maize varieties yield food within 3 to 4 months, making them reliable choices for quick harvests during unexpected supply disruptions.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ sweet potatoes, cassava kɛ ŋmãa ni shwereɔ mra lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni no haa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ oya yɛ be mli ni nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ mligbalamɔi ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ baa.

english: What makes cassava a reliable crop for surviving hard economic times compared to grain crops?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa feɔ ŋmãa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛha wala yɛ shika helɛtemɔ mli naagbai amli kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ŋmãa he?

english: Cassava is uniquely tough because its edible roots stay safe underground for many months after maturing. This allows you to leave the crop in the dirt and harvest only what you need as food, acting like a natural storehouse.
ga: Cassava wa titri ejaakɛ shishifãi ni ayeɔ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oshiɔ onibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni okpaa nɔ pɛ ni he hiaa bo akɛ niyenii. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nitoohe.

english: Why do my crops grow well during the rainy season but dry up quickly when the rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ? Shi egbiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛ?

english: Crops with shallow roots only drink water from the top layer of soil. When rains stop, that top layer dries out rapidly; spreading dry plant leaves or grass around the crop base (mulching) helps trap moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ nuɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, ŋwɛi fã lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tso lɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa tso lɛ shishigbɛ (mulch) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I produce a larger harvest of corn on my small piece of land without buying more land?
ga: Mawo ŋmãa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee enɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni mahe shikpɔŋ kroko kɛfata he?

english: You can boost yield on the same land by using certified improved seeds, applying the right fertilizer at the right growth stage, and planting in neat, evenly spaced rows instead of scattering seeds randomly.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odase lɛ ni oookɛtsu nii lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa awo mli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ amli. Ni odu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo, ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, moŋ fe ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã he fɛɛ he.

english: How do I know if my harvested grain is high enough quality to sell for export?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ kɛya maŋsɛɛ?

english: Export buyers look for clean, well-dried grains free of mold, insect damage, or dirt. Properly drying the grain right after harvest to reduce moisture content is essential for meeting export market standards.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii kɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ taoɔ ŋmaa ni he tse, egbi ni muji bɛ mli, koolooi fitemɔ loo muji. Nibii ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aba shi lɛ he miihia koni anyɛ ashɛ jarayeli nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ ahe mlai lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my stored maize spoil or get full of insects so fast after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ fiteɔ loo ŋmeii shwieɔ nɔ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize spoils when stored while still containing moisture, creating ideal conditions for mold and insects. Thoroughly sun-drying grains until hard and storing them in airtight hermetic bags suffocates pests and prevents rot.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto be mli ni edɔ lolo. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii. Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli. Ebaaha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaatsi fitemɔ naa.

english: Why does planting corn on the exact same farm plot every single year reduce my harvest over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ haa miŋmãa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the dirt. Rotating corn with leguminous crops like cowpeas helps replenish soil nitrogen naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa sũ mli nitrogen lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does the price of my harvested corn drop so low during the main harvest season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmaa ŋmãa lɛ jara baa shi nɛkɛ yɛ ŋmãa kpamɔ be titri lɛ mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: During harvest season, almost all farmers harvest and sell their crop at the exact same time. Because the market is flooded with supply, buyers can lower their buying price, whereas during the off-season when corn is scarce, prices rise significantly.
ga: yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli Nɔ ni miihe ashɛ okwaafoi fɛɛ kpaɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ yɛ be kome mli. Ejaakɛ nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ eyi jara lɛ nɔ obɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aba nɔ ni ehé lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa faaa Jara lɛ baafee nɔ ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa.

english: Why do crop buyers offer different prices for my cassava from one week to the next?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ jara srɔtoi haa mi-cassava lɛ daa otsi lɛ?

english: Crop prices fluctuate based on market demand, seasonal availability, transport costs, and how urgently buyers need raw cassava for processing mills or local markets on any given week.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ajara tsakeɔ yɛ bɔ ni jara lɛ taoɔ lɛ naa. Be mli hesaamɔ ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo kɛ oyaiyeli ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ biɔ ŋmei ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛha nitsumɔhei loo maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei daa otsi lɛ.

english: Why do my corn leaves turn yellow before the cob is fully formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ eda kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil or over-watering, which prevents the roots from taking up essential nutrients the plant needs to build green, healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu ewo mli fe nine. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ ana niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛfee baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without producing any fruit during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization. When a flower is not fertilized, the plant sheds it rather than spending energy growing a fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa enyɛŋ ekɛ fɔmɔ awo mli Kɛ́ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi ko fɔ Tsei lɛ fiteɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my bean plants produce plenty of bushy green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔlii babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages plants to focus all their energy on leaf and stem growth instead of reproductive growth like flowering and setting seed pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ama baai kɛ tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, fɔmɔ dalɛ baa, tamɔ fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishijee.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce tiny fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, their roots compete fiercely for soil moisture and nutrients, and their leaves block light from each other, leaving the plant with insufficient energy to grow large fruits.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ waa. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaada ni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground if I delay harvesting them after the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji mikɛ be ni hulutsoo be lɛ eje shishi lɛ sɛɛ fo?

english: As soil bakes and dries out, cassava roots lose water and mature past their peak quality, making them vulnerable to soil fungi and pests that cause rapid root decay.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni egbi lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafite nu ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ fe bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya lɛ yeɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do buyers pay less money for my paddy rice if I leave it on the farm too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ he nyɔmɔ fioo kɛji mishi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mikpa lɛ?

english: Rice left in the field too long gets sun-cracked inside the husk. When it is milled, these cracked grains shatter into small pieces, and buyers pay less for broken rice compared to whole grains.
ga: Omɔ ni ashi yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaná hulu yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ atsɔ mli lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmãa ni egbɛ eshwa nɛɛ fãa bibii bibii. Ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni akumɔ he nyɔmɔ fioo kɛ akɛtoɔ ŋmaa he.

english: Why is it bad to take my corn to the milling center while the grains are still damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baa ŋmãa lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Damp grains clog milling machines, ferment quickly, and create flour that develops mold and turns sour within days, spoiling the final product.
ga: Nibii ni mli efɔ lɛ baatsi tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii lɛ naa. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa oya ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa naagbee nibii ni afee lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do insects attack my stored maize grains even when I keep them inside bags in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛwoɔ kotokui amli yɛ mitsu lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weevil eggs are often laid on the corn while it is still in the field. If the grain is not dried properly or treated before storage, those hidden eggs hatch inside the bags and eat the stored crop from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛwoɔ ŋmãa nɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ agbiko dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo atsuuu he nii dani akɛtoɔ lɛ, Nakai ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: What time in the morning should I start checking my field for daily activity?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mabɔi nibii ni mifeɔ daa gbi lɛ akwɛmɔ leebi?

english: Early morning observation is key; activity typically begins as early as 5:00 AM or is fully underway by 8:00 AM.
ga: Nɔ ni akwɛɔ yɛ leebi lɛ he miihia. Bei pii lɛ, nifeemɔi jeɔ shishi mra leebi ŋmɛji enumɔ loo amɛyaa nɔ amɛtsuɔ nii waa kɛyashiɔ leebi ŋmɛji kpaanyɔ.

english: How early in the morning can I expect activity to start in my field?
ga: Te manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ nitsumɔ baaje shishi mra yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: First signs of activity can appear as early as 5:00 AM in the morning.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nitsumɔ he okadii lɛ baanyɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ 5:00 AM mra.

english: At what time in the morning should water entry ideally begin?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mabɔi nu shwiemɔ leebi?

english: Water entry typically starts from 8:00 AM in the morning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋshɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi leebi ŋmɛji kpaanyɔ.

english: Why is 8 o'clock in the morning such an important time for my field's water cycle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ 8 a.m. ji be ni he hiaa waa kɛha nu ni hoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: 8:00 AM is the benchmark time when water entry begins, making it essential for checking whether normal daily field operations are on schedule.
ga: 8:00 AM ji be ni ato ni nu lɛ jeɔ shishi eboteɔ mli No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni akwɛ kɛji daa gbi ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi ni afeɔ daa lɛ yaa nɔ yɛ be ni ato lɛ naa loo daabi.

english: What is the normal morning routine for water interactions in the field?
ga: Mɛni ji leebi nifeemɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ kɛha nu mli nifeemɔi yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Activity starts early around 5:00 AM to 8:00 AM, and from 8:00 AM onwards, entry into the water takes place.
ga: Nifeemɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi leebi maŋkpa, aaafee 5:00 a.m. - 8:00 a.m. ni kɛjɛ ŋmɛji 8:00 a.m. kɛyaa lɛ, abaawo nu mli.

english: How can I tell if there is a problem with my field based on morning timing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji naagba ko yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ leebi be nɔ?

english: If it reaches 8:00 AM or 9:00 AM and they have not come out of the water as expected, it is a clear sign that there is a problem.
ga: Kɛji akɛ eji 8:00 a.m. loo 9:00 a.m. ni ojeee nu lɛ mli lolo taakɛ okpaa gbɛ lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ naagba ko yɛ.

english: What should I look for by 9 o'clock in the morning to make sure everything is okay?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ matao dani 9 a.m. ashɛ koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: By 8:00 AM or 9:00 AM, normal emergence from the water should have occurred; if nothing has happened by 9:00 AM, your field has an issue.
ga: Beni shɛɔ 8:00 a.m. loo 9:00 a.m. lɛ, esa akɛ aná gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ nu lɛ mli bɔ ni sa. Kɛji nɔ ko bako beni shɛɔ 9:00 AM lɛ, no lɛ naagba ko yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What does it mean if nothing has emerged from the water by 8 o'clock in the morning?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji akɛ nɔ ko ejeee kpo kɛjɛɛɛ nu lɛ mli kɛyashi leebi ŋmɛji kpaanyɔ?

english: Failing to come out of the water by 8:00 AM or 9:00 AM indicates an underlying issue in the field that requires attention.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieee nu lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ leebi ŋmɛji kpaanyɔ loo nɛɛhu lɛ, no tsɔɔ naagba ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehe hiaa ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long can I wait in the morning before concluding there is an issue with my crop water setup?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ mamɛ leebi dani mamu sane naa akɛ naagba ko yɛ nu ni akɛtoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ he?

english: You should observe between 8:00 AM and 9:00 AM; if there is no emergence during this window, you know a problem exists.
ga: Esa akɛ akwɛ enɛ yɛ 8:00 AM kɛ 9:00 AM teŋ kɛji akɛ nɔ ko bako yɛ samflɛ nɛɛ mli. Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ ole akɛ naagba ko yɛ.

english: If I visit my farm at 5 AM and see no movement until 9 AM, should I be concerned?
ga: Kɛ mitee ŋmɔ ko mli leebi ŋmɛji enumɔ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko tsiii ehe kɛyashi leebi ŋmɛji nɛɛhu lɛ, ani esa akɛ mahao?

english: Yes, while activity can start between 5:00 AM and 8:00 AM, if nothing has come out of the water by 8:00 AM or 9:00 AM, it confirms there is a problem.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ nitsumɔ baanyɛ aje shishi yɛ leebi ŋmɛji enumɔ kɛyashi leebi ŋmɛji kpaanyɔ teŋ moŋ, shi kɛji akɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ejeee nu lɛ mli kɛyashi leebi ŋmɛji kpaanyɔ loo leebi ŋmɛji nɛɛhu lɛ, no lɛ naagba ko yɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct hot sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving some shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects them until they are strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ oshi tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ loo odu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually means the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow fast. Applying fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the roots will help the plants recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni biɔ ni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ baawo tso lɛ he Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dried grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Akɛ jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Covering the soil with organic material, called mulching, keeps the ground cool and moist during hot days. It also stops weeds from growing easily and turns into natural plant food as it breaks down.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Ehaa jwɛi hu shwereɔ oya, ni kɛ́ efite lɛ, etsɔɔ tsei adebɔɔ mli niyenii.

english: Planting too close actually reduces your total yield because the crops end up fighting each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow big and produce healthy fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aba shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo ni ewo yibii loo ŋmaa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer right when I plant the seeds or after they sprout?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ oodu dumɔwui loo beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: It is usually best to wait until seeds sprout and develop their first leaves before applying chemical fertilizer. Putting strong fertilizer directly on seeds before they sprout can burn the delicate new roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛjie klɛŋklɛŋ baai lɛ dani okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ wo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Cassava tubers rot when water collects around their roots for too long without proper drainage, especially in heavy clay soils or rainy seasons. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are little caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that attacks the tender growing tips of maize. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf extracts can stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmei ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo neem baa mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato plants often drop flowers when temperatures get too hot or when the soil dries out suddenly. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the plant food and water from the soil long before your main crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the nutrients they need to grow strong and fast.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tsei aniyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baashɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛdara oya.

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the field. Alternating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does wet mud stick to my rice stems when I cut them during harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ muji ni efɔ lɛ kpɛtɛɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe kɛ́ mifo amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When rice grows in flooded or swampy fields, the soil turns into soft mud. As you cut the rice near the ground, the wet clay acts like glue and sticks to the stalks, which later dries into hard dirt lumps.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔji loo ŋmeii ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baatsɔ muji ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Kɛ́ ofolɔ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glu ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ he. ni sɛɛ mli lɛ ebaagbi ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni mli wa

english: How can I harvest my rice without getting soil mixed into the crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa ŋmãa ni sũ eboteee tsei lɛ amli?

english: You can avoid mud by cutting the rice stalks slightly higher above the mud line and placing the harvested stalks directly onto clean tarpaulins or mats instead of laying them on the ground.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa muji kɛtsɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ni ooofo yɛ muji lɛ he lɛ nɔ fioo lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ tsei ni akpa lɛ awo kanvas loo tsɔne ni he tse nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: What is the proper way to thresh my rice so dirt doesn't get into the grain?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ ashwieɔ ŋmãa koni muji akabote ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: Always thresh your harvested rice on a clean wooden frame, a concrete floor, or over a wide tarpaulin so the falling grains never touch loose mud or wet soil.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, shwiemɔ omɔ ni akpa yɛ tso freim ni he tse nɔ, kɔnkrit shikpɔŋ, loo tarp ni mli kwɔ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni ŋmãa ni egbee shi lɛ akashɛ muji ni mli ewo muji loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he.

english: Why does soil cling to crop stems much more during the rainy season than the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater activates the natural clay in soil, making it wet and sticky. During the dry season, the lack of water keeps the soil powdery, so it cannot cling easily to plant stems.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Nu ni bɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ekpɛtɛɛɛ tsei ashishifãi ahe oya.

english: Why does sticky mud from my farm turn as hard as rock after drying in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ ni shwieɔ shi ni jɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ beni ajie lɛ kpo yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Clay soil consists of tiny particles that expand when wet and lock together tightly as they lose water. When the sun dries out the moisture, these particles shrink into solid, stone-like clods.
ga: Sũ lɛ ji nibii bibii bibii. No mli lɛɛɔ kɛji efɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ he kɛji nu elaaje. Kɛ hulu la lɛ gĩ ŋmɔtɔ Nɛkɛ nibii bibii nɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi ni wa ni tamɔ tɛi.

english: Why does rice grow so well in muddy, flooded fields while other crops die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli eyi kɛ muji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi gboiɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special air channels inside their stems and roots that allow them to transport oxygen underwater, whereas most other crops suffocate and rot in mud.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsui krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛyaa nu shishi. yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi Mɛi babaoo baafo ni amɛbaagboi yɛ muji lɛ mli.

english: How can I stop heavy clay soil on my farm from forming hard crusts when it dries?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa kɛ́ egbi?

english: Adding organic materials like well-rotted manure, compost, or rice husks into the ground breaks up heavy clay, helping the soil hold moisture without turning into hard crusts.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaagbala shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa.

english: Why do I find hard dirt stones mixed inside my rice after processing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina tɛi ni wa ni akɛfutu ŋmãa lɛ mli beni atsu he nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When rice is harvested or threshed on bare muddy ground, wet clay sticks to the grains. As the rice dries, these clay pieces harden into small lumps that look and feel like little stones.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ookpa loo ooshwie ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji nɔ Shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ he. Kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ egbi Nɛkɛ shikpɔŋ sũ mli fãi nɛɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi bibii. ni tamɔ tɛ bibioo ko ni enuɔ he

english: Does having mud lumps mixed with my harvested rice affect my price at the market?
ga: Ani muji ni akɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ efutu mli lɛ saa jarayeli jara lɛ he?

english: Yes, market buyers pay less for rice contaminated with dirt clods or stones because it lowers the overall quality and requires extra labor to clean before cooking.
ga: Hɛɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ baawo ŋmãa ni muji loo tɛi bibii ewo mli lɛ he nyɔmɔ fioo. Enɛ baaha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aba shi, ni ebaabi ni atsu nii babaoo koni akɛtsumɔ mli dani ahoo.

english: How can I remove hard mud clods from my harvested rice grains before selling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie muji ni wa kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: You can clean your harvested rice by winnowing it in a strong wind to blow away lighter dirt, or by using wire mesh sieves that allow fine grain to pass through while trapping mud lumps.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsumɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ he kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni okɛbaatswa lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ muji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aya. Aloo okɛ waya ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli ni haa nibii bibii tsɔɔ mli ni emɔɔ sũ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ atsu nii.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. This often happens when the soil is worn out from continuous farming or when heavy rains wash away nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Enɛ fɔɔ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ efite kɛjɛ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Crops compete with each other for sunlight and soil nutrients when spaced too tightly. They stretch upward rapidly to reach light, becoming weak and fragile instead of growing thick stems and healthy leaves.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ kɛji akɛ amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ tsɔ. Amɛgbala amɛhe oya kɛtee ŋwɛi koni amɛyashɛ la lɛ he. egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ Moŋ lɛ, eyɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ baai ni mli wa.

english: Groundnuts belong to a crop family called legumes that naturally trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts fata ŋmãa weku ni ale lɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ he. Ejɛɔ ebɔɔ su mli emɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso ko gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and shrinking into tiny twisted shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibii ni etsake lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that suck sap from under the leaves and spread plant viruses. This weakens the crop and stops it from expanding its leaves properly to catch sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees wither and fall off without producing cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or attacks by small insects like mirids. Without enough shade, moisture, or insect pollination, the flowers cannot mature into pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni sa, ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ, nu ni faaa, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ atatui ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hao amɛ. Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turning black and rotting while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni midu lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium inside the fruit as it grows. It usually happens when watering is irregular—switching back and forth between very dry soil and very wet soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ waa lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the ground if heavy rains fall right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa dani akpa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the field and water sits in the soil for too long, the tubers suffocate and soil fungi rapidly cause them to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ŋmɔji amli nu hoɔ ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Tubers lɛ baafo ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛgboi oya.

english: Why does my yam crop need me to put wooden sticks in the soil for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsei adu sweet potato tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni wain tso lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves off the damp ground toward full sunlight. Staking keeps leaves clean from soil-borne diseases and allows maximum light exposure so the plant can make big tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ ahe tseɔ kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ ahe, ni ehaa la babaoo shɛɔ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ afee bulbs agboi.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: The main plantain tree shares its water and food with every shoot attached to its roots. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong shoots, focusing the plant's energy on producing a larger bunch of fruit.
ga: Plantain titri lɛ jaa nu kɛ niyenii yɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kpɛtɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ateŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ebaaha tso lɛ hewalɛ ahi yibii babaoo ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to sprout if I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often warms up dry soil without soaking it deeply. If a dry spell follows immediately, the germinating seeds dry out and die before their roots can stretch down to moist soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛ nu shwieee nɔ. Kɛji hɔmɔ he okadii ba amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani shishifãi lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over during strong winds before I can harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that stay close to the top of the soil. As the heavy bunch grows at the top, the tree becomes top-heavy, making it easy for winds to push it down unless you prop it with wooden poles or heap extra soil around its base.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji kuu lɛ da yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatswa shi mlɛo Ja okɛ tsei loo muji krokomɛi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni ebɔle shishitoo lɛ he lɛ fi esɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop flowers when the air gets too hot or when there is irregular watering. High temperatures stress the plant and prevent proper pollination, causing the flower to dry up and fall off without making a fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa tsei haoɔ ni etsĩɔ pollination ni sa naa. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or mites, or by viral diseases spread by insects. These pests suck the sap out of young leaves, causing them to twist and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ mli Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛtsiɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why does my maize turn pale yellow and stay short even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lolo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to make green leaves and grow tall. Rain helps the plant drink, but if nitrogen is missing from the soil, the plant cannot feed properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnuɔ nu. Shi kɛji akɛ nitrogen lɛ laaje kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out so fast just a day after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbi kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil exposed to direct sunlight loses water quickly through evaporation. Placing dry grass or leaves around the bases of your crops (mulching) acts like a blanket, keeping the soil cool and holding moisture in the ground longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi wo tso lɛ shishi (mulching) lɛ, ebaatsu nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the earth. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. They need temporary shade crops like plantains planted next to them to block the harsh rays until the cocoa plants grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni mli wa ni shɛɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays soaked with water for too long. Root crops need air in the soil to breathe, and excess standing water suffocates the roots and allows fungal rot to spread.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ koni amɛmu. Ni nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat ragged holes inside the center of my maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni etse yɛ mi-abɛi lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. The mother moth lays eggs in the heart of the maize plant, and when the caterpillars hatch, they hide deep inside the central leaf roll to eat the young leaves safely away from birds.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji fall armyworm tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ. Nyɛ lɛ fɔɔ ewui yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Ebaatee ehe yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni eye baai bibii lɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ okpoi ahe.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb on wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ tso tso nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines produce underground tubers by catching sunlight with their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they get full sunlight and prevents leaf diseases caused by wet soil splashes.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛ amɛbaai lɛ ŋmɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛha hulu la ni fa babaoo ni ekɛtsi baai helai ni shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why do the maize seeds I save from last year's harvest yield much less than the fresh certified seeds I buy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii fioo kwraa fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their strength and uniformity in the next generation, leading to smaller cobs and weaker plants. Buying fresh certified seeds ensures you get high-yielding, vigor-tested plants every season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ haa onine shɛɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo, ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ daa be mli.

english: Why do some new cassava varieties mature in six months while my traditional variety takes over a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei henɔi heei komɛi shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji enumɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi shishijee srɔtoi lɛ he nɔ ni fe afi lɛ?

english: Agricultural researchers in Ghana bred improved cassava varieties specifically for faster growth and disease resistance, allowing tubers to swell quicker without needing as much time in the soil.
ga: Okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ekwɛ ŋmei yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ oya ni ekɛ helai akaye. Enɛ haa bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye be babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my stored bean seeds get full of small holes and white powder after a few months in the storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni powda yɛŋ lɛ beni ehi nitoohe lɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weevil insects lay hidden eggs inside the beans during harvest or storage, which hatch into larvae that eat the inside of the seed. Storing properly dried beans in airtight containers prevents oxygen from letting these pests survive.
ga: Weevil lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni ekɛtee ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ loo nitoo be mli. Enɛ baafɔ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ to tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii nɛɛ hiɔ shi lɛ haaa amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cassava plants dropping off during the dry season in the North?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kooyigbɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural self-defense mechanism against drought. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces water loss through evaporation and stays alive dormant until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ he. Kɛtsɔ baai ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei haa nu ni amɛlaajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ Kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their blossoms without forming fruit when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii beni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries out tomato pollen, making it sticky and unable to fertilize the flower before it drops off. Providing light shade or planting heat-tolerant varieties keeps pollen viable in high temperatures.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha tomato pollen lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa amɛhe wa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔ dani amɛgbee shi. Shading loo dumɔ henɔi ni nyɛɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa pollen lɛ shwereɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli.

english: Why do my yam vines produce larger tubers when I stake them on wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji beni mikɛwoɔ tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high into the sunlight, allowing the plant to produce maximum food through photosynthesis, which gets pumped down into building bigger underground tubers.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Ehaa tsei feɔ niyenii babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. ni akɛpompiɔ shi koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji

english: Why does planting cowpeas alongside my maize make the maize stalks greener and stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ duɔ tsina ŋmãa lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their root nodules. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby nitrogen-hungry crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei ni nitrogen he hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Yellowing starting at the tip and moving down the center of older leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency, showing that the plant lacks the key food it needs to build healthy foliage.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni eyaa shi yɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii ni he hiaa koni ewo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot right on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a water mold fungus that spreads easily in dark, humid conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches lets light and air in to dry out dampness and stop the fungus.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ ahe ni afoɔ babaoo lɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa fɛ̃i lɛ mli egbiɔ ni etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward and stay small and bunched up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by microscopic pests like mites or thrips feeding on leaf sap, or a virus spread by tiny insects. Controlling insect pests early prevents leaf damage and stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Mra Be mli Kooloi ni yeɔ hela lɛ Etsiɔ baai lɛ afitemɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why should I divide my land to grow different crops like corn, rice, and tomatoes instead of planting just one crop everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majara mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ tomato yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii kome yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting different crops in sections protects you from total loss if severe weather or disease hits one specific crop. It also helps keep the soil healthy and provides you with different harvest times and sources of income throughout the year.
ga: Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ hei srɔtoi Ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ kwraa he kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni naa wa loo hela ba nibii pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa kpamɔ bei srɔtoi kɛ shika ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ baa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Is it better for me to clear and plant all my 50 acres of land at once or start with just a small section?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ majie shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre 50 lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo mabɔi kɛ he bibioo ko?

english: It is safer to start with a smaller section, such as 5 or 10 acres, so you can properly manage the labor, costs, and care required. Once you understand how the crops perform on that soil, you can expand gradually to the rest of the land.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooobɔi kɛ he ko bibioo, tamɔ acre 5 loo 10, koni onyɛ otsu nitsumɔ, shika, kɛ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ onu bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ shishi lɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo hei ni eshwɛ lɛ amli fiofio.

english: Why do my corn plants grow tall and thin with small cobs when I plant the seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When corn seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each corn plant enough space lets it get sunlight down to its lower leaves and feed properly to produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ha ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni hulu la ashɛ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he, ni aha lɛ niyenii ni sa koni ekɛ ŋmãa wuji aba.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young corn plants turning yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of corn usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food plant needs to stay green and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa shishi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: What benefit will my soil get if I plant soybeans on land where I previously harvested corn?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔi mishikpɔŋ lɛ baaná kɛji midu soybean yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmãa tsutsu lɛ nɔ?

english: Soybeans belong to the legume family, which means they take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. Planting them after corn naturally restores nutrients to the soil, making it richer for your next crop.
ga: Soybean yɛ ŋmãa weku lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do soybean plants help keep weeds away from my farm once they start growing?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni soybean tsei lɛ aha jwɛi akaje miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji amɛbɔi kwɛ̃mɔ pɛ?

english: As soybean plants mature, their broad leaves spread out to form a thick cover over the ground. This heavy shade blocks sunlight from reaching the dirt, preventing weed seeds from sprouting and growing.
ga: Kɛ́ soybean tsei lɛ dara lɛ Ebaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɛkɛ shade ni mli tse nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ muji lɛ he. Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛdara.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from sudden heat stress or lacks enough water while flowering. Keeping the soil evenly moist during the flowering stage helps the blossoms stay on and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ naa trukaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ehe yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and develop spots during the heavy rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rain and high moisture create ideal conditions for fungal diseases to attack tomato leaves. Planting tomatoes on raised soil beds and leaving enough space between plants allows air to flow and dry out the leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baatutua tomato baai lɛ. Dumɔ tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni oshi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni eha baai lɛ agbi.

english: Why does rice need so much more water on the land compared to crops like corn or soybeans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he hiaa ŋmãa fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo soybeans lɛ?

english: Rice plants are naturally suited for wet soil and heavy water, which helps them absorb nutrients efficiently and prevents weeds from choking the crop. Corn and soybeans have dryland roots that rot if left in standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ ni efɔ, ni tsii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekatsi tsei lɛ anaa Abele kɛ soybeans yɛ shishifãi ni egbi ni fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli.

english: Can I grow rice on high, sloping land, or does it only grow well in flat lowlands?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ loo ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ pɛ nɔ?

english: While there are special upland rice varieties that can grow on higher ground, most traditional rice varieties do best in flat lowlands or valleys where water naturally collects and stays in the soil.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ gɔŋji amli ŋmãa henɔi krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ hei ni kwɔ waa moŋ. Shi aduɔ blema ŋmãa babaoo jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo jɔɔ lɛ amli he ni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ ni eyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong sunlight dries them out quickly. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains around them creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa from scorching heat until their stems grow strong.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hɔɔmɔ ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha amɛgbi oya. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea around the base of the plants helps restore their green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eha edalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: When maize plants are crowded together, their roots fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop thick stalks and large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods to conserve moisture and protect themselves from heat. Once the rains start again, the plant will sprout new leaves and continue growing its tubers under the ground.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baawo baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food for the growing tubers underneath. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground to catch light and prevents fungal diseases caused by wet leaves touching damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛshishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛ la aba amɛnɔ, ni etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baai ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or extreme dry periods. Keeping the soil evenly damp with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto flowers so they can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo bei ni hulu lɛ egbi waa lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsɔɔ tomato.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra shoots growing in the branch joints of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei aniji ahe lɛ

english: Removing these extra shoots, called suckers, prevents the plant from wasting energy on extra leaves. This directs more nutrients into making the remaining tomatoes grow bigger and ripen faster.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine nɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baawo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni eha tomato ni eshwɛ lɛ adara ni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why are the tips of my pepper fruits turning black and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛshwere lɛ?

english: Black, sunken tips on peppers are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium due to uneven watering. Watering your farm on a consistent schedule stops this rot from forming.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pepper diŋ tip lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekafite.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my land improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decompose after harvest, that nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei ashishifãi fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why did the maize seeds I stored in my storeroom fail to sprout after I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ nitoohe lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji adu lɛ?

english: Stored seeds can lose their ability to germinate if they absorb moisture or get damaged by insects and heat. Keeping seeds in tightly sealed, airtight containers in a cool, dry place preserves their ability to grow.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji amɛmu ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloi bibii kɛ dɔlɛ fite amɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ ni akɛtoɔ tsinsii ni atsĩ naa, ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi lɛ baaye abua ni amɛnyɛ amɛdara.

english: Why should I leave the cut bushes and trees on my farmland instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi jwɛi kɛ tsei ni afolɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ?

english: Leaving cut vegetation on the field acts as mulch, which protects the soil from hot sun, retains moisture, and breaks down over time into natural plant food that improves crop yields.
ga: Tsei ni afolɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli, ni yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, amɛgbalaɔ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yaa hiɛ.

english: If my farmland is on a slope, how should I arrange cut tree branches on the ground?
ga: Kɛji akɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ mato tsei niji ni afo lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Laying cut branches horizontally across the slope creates natural barriers that slow down rainwater runoff and stop your fertile topsoil from washing away.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ni akɛtoɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Can using heavy machinery to clear my bush land damage the soil?
ga: Ani nibii ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ mi-hedgerow lɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, heavy machines compress the soil, making it hard for crop roots to penetrate and for water to soak in properly, which can slow down crop growth.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsɔnei ni tsii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaabote mli ni amɛha nu lɛ abote mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: How long does it take for cut branches and foliage laid on the soil to turn into plant food?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ baai ni kã shikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ tsei aniyenii?

english: Leaves and soft weeds decompose within a few weeks during the rainy season, while thick wooden branches can take several months to fully decay and feed the soil.
ga: Baai kɛ jwɛi bibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei niji ni mli tse lɛ baanyɛ ahé nyɔji babaoo dani amɛgboi ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kwraa.

english: What happens to my crops if I don't plant them in precise, straight lines?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji miduuu amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja, ni yɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ nɔ?

english: Irregular planting causes crops to grow too close together in some spots, making them compete for sunlight and nutrients, while making weeding and harvesting much harder for you.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ hei komɛi. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa kɛhaa bo.

english: Why are my young crops turning yellow and weak after I cleared overhead shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe waaa beni mijie tsei ni yɔɔ miyitsei anɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young crops like young cocoa are sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight; without shade trees or nurse plants like plantains to shield them, their leaves burn and growth slows.
ga: Tsei bibii, tamɔ kookoo tsei bibii, nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni baatsu nii akɛ gãimlibii bɛ lɛ, Amɛbaai lɛ baashã ni amɛdalɛ baafee mlɛo.

english: Why do my maize stalks stretch tall and thin instead of growing thick and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Maize stretches upward and becomes weak when planted too close together or under shade, as the plants struggle and reach out to get enough direct sunlight.
ga: Abɛi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛɔ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Is it fine to leave old tree stumps in the ground and plant my cassava around them?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ aaashɛrɛ tsei akutsei momo ashwie? yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛdu ŋmei yɛ he fɛɛ he

english: You can plant around stumps temporarily, but removing them eventually prevents pests, termites, and root rot diseases from spreading to your healthy crop roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu yɛ Temporary tree stump lɛ he Shi kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, yɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai, ŋmeii, kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã otso lɛ shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so fast immediately after I clear a piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ?

english: When you cut down overhead cover, sunlight reaches weed seeds buried in the topsoil, causing them to sprout rapidly before your main crops can get established.
ga: Kɛ́ ofo nɔ ni akɛhaa oyitso lɛ nɔ lɛ Hulu la lɛ shɛɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa shi.

english: When is the best time for me to clear my bush before the main planting season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ majie tsei bibii lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be titri lɛ aba?

english: Clearing toward the end of the dry season allows cut weeds to dry out, making the land ready so you can plant immediately when the first rains fall.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni afo lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi ni afo lɛ agbi. Ha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ afee klalo bɔni afee ni onyɛ odu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and intense heat. Keeping larger shade trees like plantains or timber trees provides cool shelter and retains soil moisture, protecting young cocoa leaves from burning until the trees are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei bibii lɛ akwɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashi tso lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that produce long vines. Supporting the vines with stakes lifts leaves high into the sunlight where they can make energy efficiently, while keeping leaves off the wet ground prevents rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni woɔ wain tsei kakadaji. Wein tso lɛ ni akɛ tsei fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu la lɛ mli. he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, tsi baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ahe koni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the younger top leaves and growing ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa kɛ nɔ ni miiya hiɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay thin and small even though the leaves above ground look bushy and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ amli tsei lolo ni amɛji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is too hard and compacted, cassava plants spend all their energy producing leaves rather than storing food in the roots. Soft, well-drained soil allows roots to swell properly into fat tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, share the same root system and food supply as the main plantain tree. Removing most suckers leaves only the strongest shoot, ensuring all soil nutrients go toward growing a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ jaa shishifã gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ niyenii jɛɛhe kome tamɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ haa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha plantains wuji ni tsii waa lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does my land produce fewer ears of corn when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa toi fioo pɛ beni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop needs from the soil and allows specialized pests and diseases to multiply in the earth. Changing crops each season gives the soil time to rest and rebuild its strength.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai krɛdɛɛi babaoo aya hiɛ yɛ je lɛŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ ehewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How does growing cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the plants decay, they release this natural fertilizer into the ground, enriching it for crops planted next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei fite Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni akɛ sɛɛnamɔ afata tsei ni abaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience stress, such as sudden hot dry spells, irregular watering, or lack of pollination by insects. The plant sacrifices flowers to conserve water and energy until conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ko he, tamɔ trukaa, ni hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ ba. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii kɛ fɔfɔii haaa Tsei kɛ fɔfɔi shaa afɔle koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward and stop growing during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa dalɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up during extreme heat or drought as a self-defense reaction to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing moisture from evaporating too quickly from the leaves.
