ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be mli akɛ hebuu hetoo koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekajɛ baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ.

english: Why do certain cassava varieties grow very well in my district but fail when planted in a different region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei henɔi komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ shi amɛshwereɔ yɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties are naturally adapted to the specific soil types, rainfall levels, and temperature patterns of their native areas. A seed or stem tailored to dry conditions will struggle in regions with heavy clay soil or excessive rain.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ henɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ he pɔtɛɛ ko mli dɔlɛ mli. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli lɛ baaná he sɛɛ yɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji waa loo nugbɔ nɛɔ fe nine lɛ.

english: Why are my maize crops growing thin and weak when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When you plant seeds too close to each other, they fight for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Giving each plant enough space allows the roots to spread and the stalk to grow thick and healthy.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni eshishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: If I want to harvest more crops, should I just clear a bigger plot of land or change how I plant my current plot?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Ani esa akɛ majie shikpɔŋ ni da nɔ loo matsake gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Clearing more land takes extra labor and money, but proper spacing, healthy seeds, and good care on your existing plot can often double your yield without needing extra land.
ga: Shikpɔŋ babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ kɛ shika babaoo. Shi he ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ sa. dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Ni bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ momo lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ shii enyɔ ni shikpɔŋ kroko he ehiaaa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Planting them under fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects them from heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil is too waterlogged. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer restores the plant's green color and energy.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, while legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, restoring soil fertility for future crops.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why do my tomato leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgboi moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and moist throughout the day.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Will cutting off lower branches from my tomato plants help them produce bigger fruits?
ga: Ani mi-tomato tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye abua mi-tomato lɛ ni ewo yibii wuji?

english: Yes, removing lower side stems and leaves helps the plant direct its energy and food toward making bigger, healthier fruits instead of feeding extra leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii lɛ toɔ he gbɛjianɔ. Koni aná aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebote baai krɛdɛɛi amli lɛ

english: How do weeds harm my cassava plants if they are growing on the same soil?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye mi-cassava tsei lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Weeds steal the food, water, and sunlight meant for your cassava roots. Clearing weeds early ensures your cassava roots get full nutrition to grow large and heavy.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ o-cassava shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii ni yeɔ emuu ni amɛdara ni amɛdara.

english: What causes tiny holes in the center of my young corn leaves early in the season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli

english: This is typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding on tender leaves. Inspecting your farm regularly and applying recommended organic or chemical treatments early stops them from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ atsu nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔji akafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do seeds I saved from last year's harvest produce smaller crops than the original store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii bibii fe shishijee dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds lose their high productivity and disease resistance after the first harvest. Buying fresh, certified seeds each season ensures strong growth and high yields.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ amɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ ni amɛyeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa afi lɛ haa amɛdaraa waa ni amɛnáa sɛɛnamɔi babaoo.

english: How can I make my plantain trees produce very big bunches like the large commercial farms do?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi plantains lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ jarayeli ŋmɔji wuji amli lɛ?

english: Plantains need plenty of water, rich organic manure, and regular pruning of extra shoots so the main plant can direct all its nutrients into forming large, heavy bunches.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia plantains. Organic ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he daa bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛfee ŋmɔji wuji ni tsii.

english: What causes the broad leaves of my plantain trees to turn yellow and dry up before the fruit matures?
ga: Mɛni haa midumɔwui lɛ ahe baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ?

english: Early yellowing of leaves usually signals a lack of water during dry periods, insufficient soil nutrients like nitrogen, or leaf diseases like Black Sigatoka.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ mra lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu bɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo tsei ahe helai, tamɔ sigatoka diŋ.

english: Why do my plantain plants grow very slowly even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ lɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Slow growth is often caused by tiny worm-like pests called nematodes damaging the roots underground, which prevents the plant from drinking water and feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ dalɛ ni yaa blɛoo baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi Enɛ haaa tsei anu nu ni amɛye niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant only plantains across my entire farmland without mixing in other crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu plantains pɛ yɛ midumɔ be lɛ fɛɛ mli ni mikɛ tsei krokomɛi efutuuu?

english: Planting only one crop across a large area makes management simpler, but it increases the risk of complete financial loss if a pest or disease outbreaks, and it drains specific soil nutrients quickly.
ga: Tso henɔ kome pɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni da lɛ haa nɔkwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo. Shi ehaa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ shika baafite kwraa lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo hela ko ba. ni ebaafite niyenii mli nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya

english: Why do some farmers plant plantains alongside young cocoa trees on their land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, protecting sensitive young cocoa seedlings from strong sunlight while providing early food and crop income.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ niyenii ni ayeɔ oya kɛ shika ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli baa lɛ haa.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over or snap in the middle when the fruit bunch gets heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi loo efoɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ be mli ni aduawai akui lɛ tsii lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and weak, fleshy stems. When bunches become heavy, strong winds can easily knock them down unless you support the stem with sturdy wooden props.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu bɛ hewalɛ. Kɛji kuu lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha amɛgbee shi oya. Ja okɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do new small plant shoots keep growing out around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain shishitoo titri lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally propagate by sending up baby shoots called 'suckers'. Removing excess suckers keeps them from stealing food and water from the main fruiting tree.
ga: Dumɔwui fɔɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ 'ŋmeii' lɛ ni amɛtsuɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkajuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ mli.

english: Why do some plantain varieties taste sweet and firm when cooked while others turn out soft and watery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain henɔi komɛi ŋɔɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛji ahoo lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu?

english: Different plantain varieties naturally contain different amounts of starch and water, and factors like soil nutrients and harvest timing also change the final texture and taste.
ga: Plantain henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ ŋmei kɛ nu babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni nibii tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ kpamɔ be hu tsakeɔ naagbee ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my plantains before they spoil on the stem?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa plantains lɛ dani amɛgboi yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ?

english: Plantains are ready for harvest when the individual fingers look full and rounded rather than sharp and angled, and the dry flower tips on the ends break off easily.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni inchi fɛɛ inchi tamɔ nɔ ni eyi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni fɔfɔii ni egbi lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ baakumɔ oya.

english: Why do my harvested plantains soften and ripen too quickly before I can carry them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ miifee blɛoo ni amɛmiiya oya tsɔ dani manyɛ mikɛya jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested plantains naturally release ethylene gas which speeds up ripening. Keeping harvested bunches in hot, closed spaces makes them ripen faster, so storing them in cool, shaded, well-ventilated areas keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Plantains ni akpaa lɛ jieɔ ethylene gas, ni no haa amɛshwereɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ to he ko ni mli edɔ ni afo he lɛ, ebaaha amɛshwere oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu boteɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under strong sunlight and dry wind. If they do not have enough shade crops like plantains or shade trees around them, the intense heat dries out the leaves and causes them to turn brown and wither.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Kɛji amɛbɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo, bɔleɔ amɛbaai lɛ ahe lɛ, la ni naa wa lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi ni eha amɛtsɔ asarasu ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: How can I tell if a disease is starting to spread among my cocoa trees before the leaves begin to fall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela lɛ ebɔi mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ dani baai lɛ je shishi amɛgbee shi?

english: Look out for early warning signs on the plant, such as swollen stems, red veins appearing on young leaves, or pods turning black very quickly. Identifying these abnormal plant behaviors early allows you to remove infected branches before the sickness spreads to neighboring trees.
ga: Kwɛmɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii mra yɛ tso lɛ nɔ, tamɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ni efuu kɛ ŋmeii tsuji ni jeɔ kpo yɛ baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Aloo pod lɛ tsɔɔ ediŋŋ oya. Nibii ni ejaaa ni yɔɔ tsei nɛɛ amli lɛ ayɔsemɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ojieɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ dani hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are there small holes all over my crop leaves shortly after the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ.

english: When the rainy season starts, new soft green leaves sprout, which attracts hungry insects and caterpillars. They chew holes through the tender leaves to feed, which can slow down the plant's growth if left unchecked.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ shwereɔ koni amɛgbala kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ. Amɛfoɔ bu yɛ baai bibii amli kɛha niyenii. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as a lack of water, poor soil nutrients, or attacks from tiny insects. If the tree feels it does not have enough energy to feed a growing pod, it sheds the flowers to protect itself.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiihao, tamɔ nu ni bɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii. Aloo kooloi bibii tutuaa lɛ kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ ebɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaahã ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even when the leaves on top look very big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara waa ni amɛhe wa moŋ.

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too tightly, the cassava plant directs all its energy upward into growing tall stems and bushy leaves instead of sending food down to swell the tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ŋmeii tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa eshishifãi ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up into tight tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔji ni mli wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward to protect themselves from losing moisture in extreme heat. It is a natural behavior that helps the plant trap moisture inside until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni ŋmɔtɔ akaje mli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they compete for sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. The plants spend all their strength stretching upward to reach light instead of building strong stems and producing heavy yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛgbalaa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛná la. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tso nɛ mi wa nɛ e woɔ yiblii babauu.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra branches on my cocoa trees when the tree is growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches allows fresh air and sunlight to pass through the middle of the tree. This keeps the tree dry and prevents fungal diseases like black pod from developing, while directing energy into growing larger pods.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la boteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ aya hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akɛ hewalɛ hu yaa pod ko ni da fe no mli.

english: Cocoa pods change color as they ripen. Green pods turn bright yellow, and red pods turn orange-yellow. Waiting until the pods fully change color ensures that the beans inside are mature, sweet, and ready for proper fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii tsuji lɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Mɛɛ kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ amli su lɛ baatsake kwraa koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ egbɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ, ni efee klalo kɛha ŋmeii ni sa.

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, tough root systems designed to survive harsh conditions. Their seeds wake up instantly after rain and absorb nutrients faster than cultivated crop seeds, allowing them to shoot up quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni afee koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Dumɔwui teɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ enɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ. Ehaa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya

english: Why are my crops struggling to grow even when I use water from the nearby river to irrigate them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitao ni amɛkwɛ̃ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ nu nɔ moŋ?

english: Water source pollution, especially from nearby galamsey (illegal mining) operations, carries heavy metals and toxic chemicals that destroy root systems and prevent crops from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: mujiwoo ni jɛɔ nu mli Titri lɛ kɛjɛɔ Operation Galamsey mli. (illegal mining) ni bɛŋkɛ Dade ni tsii kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni haaa tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni sa lɛ yɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil, which happens when crops consume all available nutrients or heavy rains wash them away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei ye niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho amɛ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass and leaves around the base of my crops help them during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai awo he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Mulching acts as a protective blanket over the soil, trapping moisture, reducing soil temperature under intense heat, and preventing weeds from stealing water from your crops.
ga: Mulching tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ baa shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaju nu kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap under the leaves, which can also spread stunt-inducing plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni baanyɛ agbɛ tsei amli helai ni kɛ hela lɛ he okadii baa lɛ ashwã

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in heavy soil that holds too much water, causing oxygen to be cut off from the roots and encouraging fungal diseases.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ kɛha shishifãi lɛ. ni ekanyaa fungal hela

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I cut down all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mifo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat; they require partial shade from larger forest trees or plantain plants to survive their first few years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ koo mli tsei wuji loo dumɔwui amli koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures become too high or when they experience sudden heat and water stress, which prevents proper pollination.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu he haomɔ kpe trukaa. ni tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over right when the fruit bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji aduawai akui lɛ je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and top-heavy fruit, making them easy targets for root-eating pests (nematodes) or strong wind gusts unless supported with wooden poles.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ewoɔ yibii ni tsii. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mɛi ni kooloi ni yeɔ shishifãi lɛ taoɔ amɛ. (nematodes) loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa waa lɛ mlɛo ja akɛ tso ni akɛfiɔ sɛɛ lɛ tsu nii

english: Yam plants are natural climbers; lifting their leaves off the ground increases sunlight exposure for photosynthesis while protecting the leaves from soil-borne fungal rots.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ gɔŋ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa hulu la babaoo baa kɛha fotosintɛsis. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I apply my granular fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ granular fertilizer wooo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains quickly wash top-dressed fertilizer off your field into drains before the crop roots can absorb it, wasting your effort and fertilizer investment.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛjɛɔ oyale mli kɛyaa nubu lɛ mli oya dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ haa mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni afiteɔ kɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and tender roots that dry out easily under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a living canopy that shelters the young cocoa from direct sun and holds moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to grow green leaves. Applying an appropriate nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the crop's growth helps restore leaf color and encourages sturdy stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa he hiaa koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni sa ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ wo mli yɛ tso lɛ shishijee bei amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaa lɛ baa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmeii lɛ ahe awa.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots compete heavily for food and water in the soil while their leaves block sunlight from each other. Spacing crops properly ensures every plant gets enough nutrients and light to produce full, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why should I plant cowpea or groundnuts on my land before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their root nodules, which enriches the soil naturally. When you plant maize on that same soil afterwards, the maize feeds on that leftover nitrogen and grows stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baaye nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ebaada waa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants experience extreme heat stress or erratic watering. Keeping the root zone consistently moist with regular watering and putting mulch around the plants helps cool the soil and protects the flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ ni ejaaa. Kɛ́ ahã shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ahe daa kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do seeds from certified agricultural suppliers yield better than the grains I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ okwaayeli nibii ahe nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically grown and selected for strong vigor, uniform growth, and disease resistance. Seeds saved from past harvests gradually lose these superior genetic traits over generations, leading to smaller harvests and higher vulnerability to diseases.
ga: Adu dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni ahala amɛ yɛ amɛhewalɛ hewɔ. shweremɔ ni tamɔ ekome kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Nɛkɛ sui ni nɔ kwɔlɔ nɛɛ laaje yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ baa shi fioo, ni helai hu baa.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow long bushy leaves but produce small, watery tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi eyɛ bulbs bibii lɛ? He ni nu yɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant directs all its energy into growing lush leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots. Using a balanced fertilizer containing potassium encourages energy to move downward into fat, solid tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ starch baato eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo hewalɛ hewalɛ ni eya shi kɛya bulbs ni mli ewo fɔ ni wa lɛ amli.

english: Why are my maize stalks remaining short and twisted even after I applied fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛ ŋmãa ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Hidden pests like stalk borers or Fall Armyworms eat away at the growing tip inside the stem, preventing the crop from absorbing and using nutrients properly. Fertilizer cannot fix structural damage caused by active pest infestations, so controlling the pests early is necessary.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ stem borers loo cutworms yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ asaa nibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ efite lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ye tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ mra. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to capture maximum sunlight for photosynthesis, which creates the sugars needed to swell the tuber underground. Staking also keeps leaves off wet soil, preventing fungal diseases and leaf rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛha fotosintɛsis. Enɛ haa sugar ni he hiaa koni akɛwo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ baa. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why does my pepper crop keep growing taller with lots of green leaves but no flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yaa nɔ ekwɛɔ lɛ? Kɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi fɔfɔi bɛ mli?

english: High levels of nitrogen stimulate continuous leaf and stem growth while delaying flowering. To trigger pepper plants to stop growing leaves and start setting flowers, the plant needs balanced nutrition that includes higher phosphorus and potassium levels.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo haa baa kɛ tso lɛ dalɛ yaa nɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Niyenii ni ja, ni phosphorus kɛ potassium ni fa babaoo fata he lɛ he miihia tsei, koni ewo chili tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkpa baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni amɛbɔi fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei lɛ shã ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Leaving large shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains nearby creates a protective canopy that cools the soil and shields the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know which direction to push my cassava stem cuttings into the ground when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni esa akɛ matsi ŋmei nine lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the tiny raised buds along the cassava stem. These buds should point upwards toward the sky so the leaves can sprout directly out and up into the light; planting them upside down forces the plant to waste energy trying to correct its growth.
ga: Kwɛmɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni teɔ shi yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ he lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni baai lɛ anyɛ ada tɛ̃ɛ kɛya la lɛ mli. Tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ejaje bɔ ni edaa lɛ.

english: What happens if I plant too many maize seeds together in the exact same hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo fee ekome yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are crowded into one spot, the growing stalks fight each other for soil food, water, and sunlight. This competition leaves you with thin, weak plants that produce very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bua amɛhe naa yɛ he kome lɛ, tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nu lɛ mli, kɛ hulu la lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko nɔ ko.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow and drooping after water sits on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni nu ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air in the soil to breathe just like humans need air. When standing water covers the farm, it suffocates the roots, preventing them from taking up nutrients and causing the leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Taakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa adesai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Beni nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ ha ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Ehaaa amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Is it safe to put fresh animal waste directly on my vegetable garden, or will it harm the crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mashɛrɛ kooloi ahe jwɛi heei ashwie mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo ebaaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Fresh manure is full of strong gases and heat that can burn delicate plant roots. If you pile it up and let it decompose and cool down for a few weeks first, it transforms into gentle, rich food for your crops.
ga: Nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ eyi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ. Kɛji okɛto ni oha egbo ni edɔ otsii fioo komɛi dani Ebatsɔ niyenii ni mli jɔ ni yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: The main plantain tree has a limited amount of food to give. If too many young shoots grow around it, they steal food from the mother plant, resulting in tiny bunches; keeping only one or two suckers ensures full, heavy bunches.
ga: Niyenii fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ plantain titri lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ, ebaaju niyenii kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ dɛŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Suckers 1 loo 2 pɛ ni ooohiɛ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why do my yam tubers stay very small even when the leaves on top look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: If weeds are allowed to grow thick around the yam mound, their roots steal the underground space and fertilizer meant for the yam, stopping the tuber from expanding deep and wide.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ jwɛi lɛ gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ babaoo yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe lɛ ahe lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ baaju shikpɔŋ shishi he kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ ji koni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛkagbɛ ashwã.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a water-loving fungus that spreads in damp, high-humidity air. Rain splashing off the soil transfers the fungal spores onto low-hanging pods, causing them to turn black and decay.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ fungal spores lɛ yaa pods ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly drop all their flowers without growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ ni eduuu pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience severe heat or water stress. The plant senses that it does not have enough water to support fruits, so it drops the flowers to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu mli haomɔ mli. Tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, eshiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and collapse during the daytime even when the ground is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This daytime wilting is usually caused by tiny germs in the soil that enter the roots and clog the tubes carrying water up the stem. Even if the soil is wet, the water cannot reach the top of the plant, causing it to droop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ hulutsoo be nɛɛ baa. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni etsiɔ paipii ni kɛ nu yaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ naa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ sũ lɛ mli efɔ po lɛ, nu lɛ nyɛɛɛ ayashɛ tsei lɛ ayiteŋ, ni no haa sũ lɛ mli tseɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough to grow big cassava roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmei wuji?

english: Good cassava soil is soft, loose, and drains water well. Hard, clay soil prevents cassava tubers from swelling beneath the ground, while loose soil lets the roots expand easily.
ga: Cassava shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ji shikpɔŋ sũ lɛ tsiɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: What causes my tomato fruits to turn black and rot at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ shishigbɛ dani ekwɛ̃?

english: This is caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant lacks calcium or gets irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant take up minerals properly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji blossom end rot, ni baa kɛji calcium bɛ tso lɛ mli loo akɛ nu haa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa minerals lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing all over my cabbage leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ kaabe baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Insects like caterpillars love to eat soft green leaves when wet weather arrives. Inspecting the leaves early and spraying natural neem leaf extracts can stop caterpillars from destroying the crop.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛye baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ. Baai lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni adebɔɔ mli neem baa lɛ mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my yam plants need long wood stakes to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make energy for growing heavy tubers underground. Climbing up stakes spreads the leaves toward the sun, resulting in bigger yields.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulbs ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Tso lɛ nɔ kwɔɔ baaha baai lɛ akwɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii babaoo ni afeɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by extreme afternoon heat or dry soil. Giving them steady moisture during hot weeks helps the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How can I tell the exact time my groundnuts are ready to harvest from under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the leaves turn yellowish and drop. Pulling up one test plant should show dark brown or black markings on the inside of the pods.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Esa akɛ kaa tso kome ni ajieɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ aná okadii ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ yɛ pod lɛ mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize start rotting or getting insects quickly inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ loo kooloi bibii miibote ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya nɛkɛ?

english: Maize rots in storage if grains still hold wetness inside. Sun-drying the maize until the grains are very hard before storing prevents mold and insect damage.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ tee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa waa dani akɛto lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa kɛ kooloi fiteɔ nii.

english: Why is it bad for my garden crops if I water them in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛmli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering under strong afternoon sun causes water to evaporate before roots drink it, and hot water droplets on leaves can stress the plant. Watering early in the morning is best.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ lɛ ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aná haomɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth, or that the ground is waterlogged. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or improving drainage helps the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tso lɛ dalɛ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he loo nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛná amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting groundnuts before planting maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei dani adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally captures nitrogen from the air and fixes it into the soil. When you plant maize in that same field the following season, the maize feeds on the natural nitrogen left behind, resulting in higher yields.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ odu ŋmãa yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa yeɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves during the dry season, and does it mean they are dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ eegbo?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a natural survival mechanism to save water. The plant is not dead; it goes dormant and safely stores energy in its underground roots until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ebaawɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli shweshweeshwe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollinators. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and ensuring proper shade during peak sun can help hold the flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ faaa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni akwɛ koni hulutsoo be lɛ mli aná hulutsoo be ni sa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi amɛhe.

english: Tomato leaf curling is frequently caused by leaf-curl viruses spread by tiny insects like whiteflies, or by extreme heat and drought. Managing whiteflies with neem oil spray and keeping the soil moist helps prevent severe damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni haa tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ tsu ŋmeii yɛji ahe nii, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite waa.

english: Why should I plant plantains next to my young cocoa seedlings in a fresh farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Plantains grow quickly with wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa trees need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tso lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I tie my yam vines onto wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akpɛtɛ tso he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves toward sunlight so they can make more food for the plant, while keeping leaves away from wet soil prevents fungal rot, leading to larger and healthier tubers.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato lɛ baai lɛ akwɛ hulu la lɛ hiɛ bɔni afee ni efee niyenii babaoo aha tso lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akafite. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut away extra small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for food, water, and sunlight. Pruning them away leaves only one or two strong suckers, ensuring the main plant produces a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ kɛ plantain wulu lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ofolɔ amɛ lɛ, tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baashi. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Covering soil with dry organic material, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from evaporating under the hot sun, prevents weed growth, and eventually breaks down into natural compost.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni yɛ naagbee lɛ efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or get eaten by insects in storage even when the cobs felt dry when I picked them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ efite loo kooloi ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ yeɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei lɛ nu he akɛ egbi beni miwo lɛ moŋ.

english: Maize grains often hold hidden internal moisture even when the outside feels dry to the touch. If maize is not thoroughly dried on tarps in the sun until hard before storage, remaining moisture attracts mold and insect pests like weevils.
ga: Abele ŋmeii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi kɛji akɛ ota he moŋ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa yɛ tarpaulin nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa dani akɛto. Fɛ̃i fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ baagbala ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: In intense afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. They temporarily drop their leaves to save moisture and usually recover when the sun cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he, ni bei pii lɛ, amɛhe feɔ shoo kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly. Heat stress forces the plant to drop flowers to protect itself.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake trukaa Dɔlɛ haomɔ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie fɔfɔi amɛshwie shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide the shade and moist climate young cocoa needs until it gets older.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni kookoo bibii taoɔ lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow tall, thin, and yield very small harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, amɛhe kwɔ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why aren't my maize seeds sprouting out of the ground after planting them last week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ otsi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to sprout if they were buried too deep in the soil, if the soil lacks moisture, or if underground insects ate the seeds before they could push through.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ mli.

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, but cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally enriching the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi cowpea lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds on my farm grow much faster than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive hard weather, so their roots steal water and nutrients from the soil much faster than domesticated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya kwraa fe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni akɛkwɛɔ shia lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing water during dry heat, or because tiny insects like whiteflies are sucking juices from the underside of the leaves.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji miinu nu kɛmiijɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ hewɔ.

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves mean hungry caterpillars or beetles are eating the plant tissue. Applying natural neem oil sprays can help keep these insects off your farm.
ga: Buu bibii ni yɔɔ kaaba baa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ miiye tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akabote oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I buy new hybrid maize seeds instead of saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Seeds saved from past harvests slowly lose their strength and yield less over time. New improved varieties are specifically bred to grow stronger stalks, resist common local pests, and produce larger cobs even during unpredictable weather.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nikpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Hewalɛ baa shi ni ebɛ nitsumɔ babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli. Afɔ tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛha tsei ni wa fe tsutsu lɛ aba. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni bɛ shiŋŋ po mli.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer says a crop variety is 'early maturing'?
ga: Kɛji akɛ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ ‘miida mra’ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ?

english: An early maturing variety grows, flowers, and produces food in a shorter amount of time—often 2 to 3 months instead of 4 or 5. This allows you to harvest before a short rainy season ends.
ga: Henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ baakwɛ̃, amɛbaawo fɔfɔi ni amɛbaawo niyenii yɛ be kukuoo mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ nyɔji 4 loo 5 najiaŋ, ni no haa okpaa nii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ baa naagbee.

english: Why do some new crop varieties stay green during dry spells while my local crops wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei komɛi hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni mimaŋ tsei lɛ gboɔ lɛ?

english: Drought-tolerant varieties are developed with deeper root systems that pull water from deep in the soil and leaf surfaces that conserve moisture, helping the plant survive when rains stop early.
ga: Afee tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow during the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is stressed. It can happen if the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, if pests are attacking the roots, or if the plant is dropping leaves to survive hot and dry weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao. Ebaanyɛ eba kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua shishifãi lɛ. Aloo kɛji tso lɛ miiho ebaa lɛ koni ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow tall and strong, so planting them together naturally feeds the maize without extra cost.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ awa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmãa aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni shika kroko fataaa he.

english: Why do my crops need fertilizer if my field has produced food for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔji lɛ ahe hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ miŋmɔji lɛ ewo niyenii afii babaoo nɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they take nutrients out of the soil. Over time, the soil becomes tired and empty; adding fertilizer restores those missing nutrients so future plants can grow properly.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni be shwieɔ mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni wɔsɛɛ tsei lɛ anyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if I am planting my maize seeds too close to each other?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui miidu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: If maize is planted too close, the stalks grow thin, weak, and tall because they are fighting for sunlight. The cobs will also stay small because the roots are competing for water and food in the soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baafee bibioo, egbɔjɔ, ni ekɛlɛ ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Kooloi lɛ baakã he afee bibii ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my young crops more than my mature crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ awui fe miŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and tiny leaves, so weeds easily block their sunlight and steal water. Older crops have larger roots and tall leaves that shade out weeds on their own.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai bibii. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi tsiɔ hulu la naa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu. Tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji kɛ baai ni kɛlɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhaa jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if caterpillars are attacking my crops before the whole field is damaged?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii miitutua miŋmɔshi nibii dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ efite?

english: Look closely at the young middle leaves for tiny chewed holes, ragged leaf edges, or small dark waste pellets. Catching these signs early lets you treat the crop before the pest spreads.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ona buji bibii ni atsɔ mli, ŋmeii bibii ni etse, loo ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli. Okadii nɛɛ ni ooomɔ mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni ohere oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala dani tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color completely—turning from deep green to bright yellow, or from dark red to orange. Harvesting them at this stage ensures the beans inside have reached full size and sugar content.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa. Etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. aloo kɛjɛ tsuru ni mli edɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ayiɔ obɔ kɛ dalɛ ni sugar yɔɔ mli.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up so they can catch direct sunlight to make food for growing big underground tubers. It also keeps the leaves off wet soil, which prevents rot and leaf diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛha niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei ahe helai anaa.

english: How do my groundnut plants produce nuts underground after flowering above the soil?
ga: Te mi-peanut tsei lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii beni amɛwo fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After the yellow groundnut flowers bloom above ground, the plant grows small stems called 'pegs' that bend down and push themselves into the soil. The groundnut pods then grow and mature underground at the ends of these pegs.
ga: Beni ŋmei fɔfɔi ni ji yellow lɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ Tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Peanut ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ anaagbee.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites that feed on leaf juices, or by a virus spread by these insects. Spraying neem oil or appropriate pest control measures stops the pests so healthy leaves can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Neem fɔ loo gbɛi krokomɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: What is eating holes in the central leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the center growing point of the plant. Applying recommended sprays or neem extracts directly into the leaf center controls these caterpillars.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni edaa yɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaakudɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long or drains poorly after heavy rains. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo nu shwieee shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my watermelons split open on the farm before they are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Watermelons crack open when they absorb a sudden heavy amount of water after a dry period, causing the fruit inside to swell faster than the skin can stretch. Keeping the soil moisture consistent prevents this cracking.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛji trukaa lɛ, eŋɔ nu babaoo yɛ be ko sɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fũuɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow roots that lose water quickly in direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa protects them from harsh heat until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni kɛ́ hulu la kpɛ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, kɛ cocoa tsei bibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he, ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the suckers grow around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ yɛ mi-plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around one stem creates competition for nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in small plantain bunches. Pruning extra suckers leaves more energy for the main stem to yield a large bunch.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Tso kome he lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii feɔ plantains. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfee ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate that the maize plant is low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs for green leaf growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or decomposed manure will help restore healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔlii lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛdara ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from heat stress, inconsistent watering, or lack of soil nutrients. Regular watering and keeping the root area cool with mulch helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni ashwieɔ shi daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni ashwieɔ daa kɛ shishifãi lɛ ni akɛ muji woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my crops stop growing well if I plant maize on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and attracts pests that prefer that crop. Rotating with legumes like beans or letting the land rest restores the soil's strength naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni egbalaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ nakai tso lɛ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii atsake loo oha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa trees turning brown and curling up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves curl and burn when exposed to direct sunlight without shade. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa shields them from severe heat and retains soil moisture.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ baabɔle amɛhe ni amɛbaashã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Is it better to burn dried weeds on my farm or leave them on the soil surface?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni egbi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ loo mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving dried weeds on the ground as mulch keeps the soil cool, traps moisture, and breaks down into natural fertilizer, whereas burning destroys topsoil nutrients and dries out the land.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ be mli ni shãa lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli gbiɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but yield very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔji ni eyɛ baai shi eyɛ bulbs bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen-heavy fertilizer causes the cassava plant to spend all its energy growing foliage above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ ebaa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my corn, or will they steal food from each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa? Aloo amɛbaaju niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: Cowpeas and corn benefit each other when planted together. Cowpeas absorb nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the corn grow strong without competing.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ekomekomei. Cowpeas shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: How deep should I bury my maize seeds when planting so they sprout healthy?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Maize seeds should be planted about two to three centimeters deep. Burying them too deep deprives them of air, while planting too shallow leaves them vulnerable to birds and heat.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimitai enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ. Kɛ́ afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee shoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa okpoi kɛ latsaa yeɔ amɛ awui.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow from the tip down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tips and moves along the central vein indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which the plant needs to build green leaves and grow.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naagbee ni etsɔɔ tsitsi lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɔ tso tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha efo kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves toward sunlight so they can make more food to build bigger underground tubers, while keeping the foliage off hot soil prevents disease.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ baaha baai lɛ akwɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii babaoo ni amɛkɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ koni helai akamɔ bo.

english: What causes armyworm caterpillars to suddenly appear and eat my crop leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii jeɔ kpo nyɔɔŋ kome mli ni amɛyeɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ?

english: Moths lay clusters of tiny eggs on the undersides of leaves, which hatch simultaneously into hungry caterpillars; checking under leaves early allows you to catch and manage them before they multiply.
ga: Kplukai lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui bibii yɛ baai lɛ ashishi. ni fɔɔ amɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ yɛ be kome too mli, ni amɛkwɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ omɔɔ amɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii dani amɛfɔɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop in the hot afternoon sun even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Pepper plants temporarily curl or droop their leaves during peak afternoon heat to slow down water loss through evaporation, and they naturally stand back up once the temperature cools down in the evening.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baakumɔ loo amɛbaagbee shi be kukuoo ko yɛ shwane mli dɔlɛ be mli. Koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. ni ebaate shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under the harsh sun. Plantains grow fast and produce large leaves that provide living shade, keeping the soil moist and protecting the young cocoa trees until they are strong enough to withstand direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why does my plantain shoot out so many small shoots around the main stem, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miikwɛ̃ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni bɔleɔ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, ni ani esa akɛ majie amɛ?

english: Plantain plants produce baby shoots called suckers to reproduce. If you leave all of them growing together, they will steal water and nutrients from the main tree, causing small plantain bunches. You should cut away most suckers, leaving only one or two strong ones for the next harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii koni amɛkɛfɔ bii. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ fɛɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, amɛbaaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli, ni no baaha plantains lɛ afee jwɛi bibii. Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo. Ekome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ kɛha nikpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruit bunch becomes big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have soft stems and shallow roots that cannot support heavy weight, especially during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a bamboo pole or strong wooden Y-stick helps hold up the heavy bunch until it is ready for harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akwɛ nibii ni tsii nɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso loo tso ni wa ni tamɔ Y fiɔ tso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehiɛ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ amli kɛyashi amɛbaafee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa.

english: How can I tell when my plantain bunch is mature enough to be cut down?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi plantains kuu lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ afo?

english: A plantain bunch is ready for harvest when the individual fruits lose their sharp corner edges and become plump and rounded. Additionally, the small dried flower tips at the end of each plantain will break off easily when touched.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko sɛɛ efo ni ebatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Kɛfata he lɛ, fɔfɔi bibii ni egbi lɛ ashishifãi Plantain fɛɛ plantain ashishifãi lɛ fãa oya kɛji akɛ ata he.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient plants need to make leaves green and healthy. Applying animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their green color and help them form big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔji ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔji wuji.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow very slow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Even with heavy rain, weeds swallow up the nutrients before your crop's roots can reach them, so clearing weeds early allows your crops to get all the nourishment.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa moŋ, shi jwɛi hu yeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Curled leaves with yellowish patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting improved, disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural officers prevents this sickness from destroying your farm.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ. Kɛ́ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ duɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ he ni yɔɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When maize plants are packed too closely, their leaves block sunlight from each other, and their roots fight over the same small portion of nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and light to produce strong stalks and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la ni jɛɔ amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii bibii. nakai nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand easily underground. If the soil is hard and packed down, the growing tuber struggles to penetrate the ground, forcing it to bend, twist, or stop growing big.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Bulbs ni miida lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni nyɛɔ enɔ koni ebɔle, etsɔ, loo ekpa dalɛ

english: Extremely high temperatures can destroy the delicate pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from developing into fruits. When pollen fails, the flower simply drops off the plant. Providing light shade or planting in cooler seasons prevents flower drop.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa baanyɛ afite ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. ni etsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatsɔ yibii. Kɛji pollen lɛ faaa lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛjɛ tsei lɛ anɔ. Shade loo dumɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: This yellowing and curling is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. The disease prevents the leaves from making food properly, which results in very small cassava tubers under the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ shihilɛ nɛɛ jɛɔ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ mli. ni ji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ ni hiɛɔ Hela nɛɛ haaa baai lɛ ahoo jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ faaa kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, cold, and dark environments. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and air into your farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni ooofee koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I trim off the extra leaves at the bottom of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo baai ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mitato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Trimming the lower leaves stops soil-borne sicknesses from splashing onto the plant during rain. It also helps the plant direct its strength into growing larger tomatoes instead of unnecessary leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afo baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ akashwie tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ hu ni ekwɛɔ ehewalɛ nɔ koni ekɛkwɛ tomatoi wuji moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai ni he ehiaaa baatsu nii.

english: Young cocoa trees are fragile like human babies and burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly with broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas to protect the young cocoa during its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa tamɔ adesai abifabii, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or beans on the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas grab good air nutrients and put them back into the dirt, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds the maize, while the maize stalk gives the beans support to climb.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ekwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker if I plant maize on the exact same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize sucks the same specific food out of the soil every season. Planting it continuously drains the soil completely, so switching crops or planting beans helps the soil rest and rebuild its strength.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ mli kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni ehaa ehewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers when the dry Harmattan season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?
