english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers to protect themselves and save water when the soil dries up and the air becomes hot and dusty.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛbu nu he kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni sũ hu ebɔle he.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Instead of growing fat cobs, they spend all their energy stretching upwards to reach the light.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ Moŋ lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsu nii ni amɛkɛgbala amɛhe kɛtee ŋwɛi koni amɛyashɛ la lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops suffer even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ awui yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive eaters that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight faster than your crops can get to them, leaving your crops hungry and weak.
ga: Jwɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ basabasa. Enɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aná. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii ni ogbɔjɔ.

english: How do I know that my yams are fully mature and ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When the green leaves and vines above the ground naturally turn yellow and dry up, it means the plant has finished sending food down to mature the yam tuber underground.
ga: Beni baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ egbe niyenii ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa shi lɛ naa koni amɛha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate roots that easily burn and dry out under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or bananas alongside your young cocoa provides them with a natural umbrella, keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo banana yɛ cocoa tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo adebɔɔ mli tsei aba. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the crop is lacking an essential plant food called nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer around the base of the plant helps restore its healthy green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ tso niyenii ko ni he hiaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛbaabɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaye abua ni eha tso lɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ ni eha edalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even when I clear it well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the exact same piece of land year after year drains the soil of its natural nutrients. Rotating your crops—such as planting cowpeas, peanuts, or beans after maize—puts nitrogen back into the soil and helps restore its fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii. Onibii ni okɛbaatsake, tamɔ tsina ŋmei, ŋmei, loo ŋmei ni ooodu yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ, ni eye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a tiny water mold that spreads quickly when the air is damp and water droplets splash from infected pods. Clearing thick weeds around your trees to let in sunlight and fresh air, along with removing any black pods right away, helps keep the remaining crop healthy.
ga: Nu mli ŋmeii bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. No gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Ajieɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ koni aná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ajie ŋmeii diji lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes in the fresh middle leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai heei lɛ anɔ?

english: These holes are usually caused by tiny caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm that hide inside the growing center of the plant. Checking your farm early in the morning and applying recommended natural sprays like neem leaf extract or proper treatments can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni sa atsu nii. Abaanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava cuttings so I get big tubers?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu amɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni anyɛ ana bulbs wuji?

english: Cassava roots need enough open space underground to expand and draw nutrients from the soil. Spacing your cassava cuttings about one meter apart ensures the plants do not fight with each other for water and sunlight, resulting in bigger and heavier roots.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kasava niji lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji aaafee mita kome koni tsei lɛ akashi akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ hulu la he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraa ni amɛtsii hu.

english: Yam plants are natural vines that produce leaves to catch sunlight and send energy down to build tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where they could rot, helping the vine catch maximum sunlight and grow larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli wain tsei ni woɔ baai ni amɛkɛmɔɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baa shi koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa wain tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Too many young shoots growing around one plantain stem steal food and water from the main tree, leading to small, light fruit bunches. Leaving only one main tree and one strong sucker ensures all the soil's strength goes into producing a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei bibii babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Leads to small, lightweight fruits. Kɛ́ ashi tso titri kome pɛ kɛ tso bibioo kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwo plantains babaoo.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants dropping off without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni mifeee pepper ko lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells, or a sudden lack of moisture in the soil. Giving your plants consistent watering and placing light mulch around the base keeps the root zone cool so the flowers can turn into peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa miigba tso lɛ naa. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ mli trukaa Ha tsei lɛ nu daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli fioo. Ebɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he koni shishifã lɛ he afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough water for me to start sowing my seeds safely?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ shweshweeshwe?

english: You can check by picking up a handful of topsoil and squeezing it tightly into a ball. If it holds together without dripping wet water or crumbling into dry dust, the soil has just the right amount of moisture for your seeds to sprout safely.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni oooŋɔ ni okɛmiimɔ mli ni okɛfee bɔɔlu ni mli wa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ ni mli efɔ loo egbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ sũ ni egbi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ ni sa pɛpɛɛpɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing young cocoa trees with the shade and soil moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet weather when excess tree branches trap moisture. Pruning your shade trees and clearing weeds allows sunlight and air to dry the pods and prevent the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Beni tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ afolɔ ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa helai baaa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves look like they have holes and small sawdust-like dirt inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ bu kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the fall armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the plant leaves to feed. Checking your field early and applying recommended neem extracts or insecticides can protect your crop before severe damage occurs.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ahe baai amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao niyenii. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ abu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ aba.

english: Why does a purple-flowered weed make my maize plants look dry and stunted even when there is rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni fɔ̃ɔ purple lɛ haa mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbi ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: That weed is Striga, also known as witchweed. Its roots attach directly to your maize roots underground to steal water and food, so uprooting it before it produces seeds and rotating your crops helps clear your field.
ga: Nakai jwɛi lɛ ji striga. Ale lɛ hu akɛ Witchweed. Eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ o-corn shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ojie shishifãi lɛ dani amɛwo dumɔwui, ni okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli atse.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Once cassava reaches full maturity, it stops storing food and begins absorbing excess water from heavy rains, making the roots watery and vulnerable to soil rot. Harvesting tubers when they are mature prevents this loss.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Ekpaa niyenii ni ekɛtoɔ lɛ ni ebɔi nu ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɔmɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli nu yɔɔ mli, ni eyɛ oshara akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛdara kwraa lɛ, no tsiɔ nɛkɛ laajemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why should I rub wood ash on my cut seed yams before placing them in the mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso sũ awo ŋmeii ni afo lɛ anɔ dani mikɛwo gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Wood ash dries out the fresh cuts on the seed yam and creates a barrier that protects it from fungal rot and soil insects while it is underground before sprouting.
ga: Tso lɛ mli sũ lɛ baaha fãi heei ni yɔɔ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ agbi. ni ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ sũ mli kooloi ahe be mli ni eyɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato plants often shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the base of the plant helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛkɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ be fɛɛ be kpe. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing tall and weak with very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miida ni egbɔjɔ ni pepper fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are planted too close together, they compete for light and nutrients, causing them to stretch upward instead of branching out to bear fruit. Giving each plant proper spacing allows them to grow wide and yield heavily.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee niji ni amɛwo yibii. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara babaoo ni amɛwo ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my field before planting my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani madu ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting them first naturally enriches your soil, providing free food for your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ odu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni okɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko aha kɛha o-corn feed ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops seem to need more water as they grow older even if the rain was enough when I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii beni amɛdaraa lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa beni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: As crops grow bigger and start producing grains or fruits, their root systems and plant bodies require much more water to build the final harvest than when they were small seedlings.
ga: Beni tso lɛ daa ni ebɔi dumɔwui loo yibiiwoo lɛ Tso lɛ shishifã kɛ egbɔmɔtso lɛ hu biɔ nu babaoo koni ekɛ naagbee nɔ lɛ aba fe beni eji dumɔwu bibioo lɛ.

english: What should I do to protect my crops if the rain suddenly stops after I have already planted?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mabu miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around your plants with dry grass or leaves (mulching) to trap soil moisture, clear away weeds so they do not steal water, and hand-water if a water source is nearby.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai (mulch) awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ koni ekɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ koni amɛkaju nu. Ni nu kɛtsɔ nine nɔ kɛji nu jɛɛhe ko yɛ ni bɛŋkɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from a lack of water during the growing season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu ni faaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Watch for leaves that roll up or wilt during the heat of the day, lower leaves turning yellow early, or slowed growth. If plants look dull and wilted early in the morning, they are severely stressed for water.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi loo egboɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya. loo edalɛ blɛoo Kɛji tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ leebi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ yɛ nu ni tsii waa shishi.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell. If regular rains do not continue, your newly germinated seeds will dry up and die because their roots are still very shallow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ daa Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lolo.

english: Is there a specific time during crop growth when a lack of rain damages the final harvest the most?
ga: Ani be ko yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ yeɔ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ awui fe fɛɛ?

english: Yes, critical mid-growth stages (such as 30 to 40 days after planting) when plants begin flowering and forming seeds or fruits are very sensitive. A water shortage at this exact stage drastically cuts your final harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, be ni tso lɛ daa lɛ teŋgbɛ (ni ji gbii 30 kɛyashi 40 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ) beni tso lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni ewoɔ dumɔwui loo aduawai lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ waa. Nu ni faaa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaha onaagbee kpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi waa.

english: Why do extension officers emphasize paying extra attention to crops around 40 days after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ esa akɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii aaafee gbii 40 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: Around 40 days, many staple crops transition from growing stems and leaves to developing flowers, cob heads, or seed pods. Any stress from drought or nutrient deficiency at this mid-stage directly reduces how much crop you harvest.
ga: Yɛ aaafee gbii 40 mli lɛ, tsei babaoo ni hereɔ gbɔi lɛ baajɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ amli kɛya fɔfɔi, cob bulbs, loo dumɔwui amli. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ hɔmɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni okpaa lɛ aba shi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are my crops growing plenty of healthy green leaves but giving me a poor yield at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo shi yibiiwoo faaa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Healthy leaves only show strong early growth. High yields require continuous care, sufficient water, and balanced nutrients later in the season when the plant shifts its energy from making leaves to building fruits or grains.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baatsɔɔ dalɛ oya pɛ. Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be, nu ni fa bɔ ni sa, kɛ niyenii ni sa yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ beni tsei tsakeɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai amli lɛ koni amɛwo aduawai loo ŋmaa lɛ.

english: How often should I inspect my field to make sure my crops are progressing well towards a good yield?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ kɛmiiya yibii kpakpai ahe?

english: You should check your field two to three times a week so you can spot early signs of dry soil, pest attacks, or nutrient deficiencies before they permanently damage your crop yield.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ otsi mli. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ ona shikpɔŋ ni egbi, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ he okadii mra. Dani amɛbaafite onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ daa

english: When is the best time for me to apply supplements or fertilizers to my growing crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mitsei ni miida lɛ amli?

english: Supplements should be applied when the soil is moist and plants are actively growing—usually once shortly after the seeds sprout and again during major growth stages before flowering.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei miida waa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ dalɛ be titri lɛ mli dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Can applying fertilizer or organic supplements help my crops survive a dry spell?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, healthy crops with strong root systems built from proper soil nutrients can tolerate dry periods much better than weak plants growing in nutrient-poor soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛshishifãi ni wa ni ama shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋmɛ be ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii bɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I put three or four maize seeds in the same hole when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ woɔ bu kome mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Giving each seed its own space allows the roots to spread out and grow into strong plants with full ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛhe. Ni aaaha dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tso ni wa ni ŋmãa toi eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out so quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Soil dries out when direct sunlight and wind strip away its moisture. Covering the ground around your plants with dried leaves or grass—known as mulching—keeps the ground cool and traps moisture in the dirt.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Ale shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni okɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi baaha lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ muji lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Applying fertilizer like urea early in the plant's life helps restore the bright green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he yɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli tse lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ shi amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ tomatoi lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from high heat or inconsistent watering. Watering your plants regularly at the base early in the morning helps the flowers stay attached and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ eshishigbɛ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the center of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on maize leaves. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended pesticides directly into the plant funnel will stop them from destroying your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔji lɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck sap from the leaves and transmit plant diseases. Spraying your pepper plants with neem oil or appropriate insect treatments helps keep leaves healthy and flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni egbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ shwie pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Alternating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and naturally breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Why is it important to weed my farm when my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo?

english: Young crops are weak and easily overwhelmed by fast-growing weeds that steal their food and water. Weeding early ensures your crops get all the sunlight and soil nutrients they need to build a strong stem.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ niyenii kɛ nu lɛ yeɔ amɛnɔ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa.

english: Most cassava varieties are ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can test a plant by carefully digging around the base; if the roots are thick and firm, the entire crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ oka tso lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ ni oootsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli tse ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow and droop when heavy rain floods my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha miŋmɔji lɛ amli nu lɛ?

english: When excess rainwater sits on your field for too long, it drowns the crop roots by cutting off air. Without air, the roots cannot take up food, which turns the leaves yellow and makes the plant look weak.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi oŋmɔji amli be kakadaŋŋ Ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aye niyenii. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni eha tso lɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ.

english: What simple step can I take to protect my crops if water keeps collecting in the low areas of my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii bibii komɛi ni manyɛ mafee koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe? Kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: You can dig shallow drainage channels along the natural slope of your land so that standing water moves away from crop roots and drains out of the farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko. Nyiɛmɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋshɔkei ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe ni ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it good to apply fertilizer on my farm right after a heavy rainstorm has flooded the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ?

english: No, you should wait until the water settles and soil is only moist. Applying fertilizer to flooded soil causes the nutrients to wash away before your crops can absorb them.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ omɛ pɛ kɛyashi nu lɛ baaho ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hoɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why have my plants stopped growing taller even though I planted them several weeks ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ ekpa shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ midu lɛ otsii komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Crops usually get stuck or stunted because the soil lacks plant food, the soil is packed too hard for roots to expand, or tiny pests are attacking the roots underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe niyenii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui Etutuaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a crop that stopped growing is dead or if it can still recover?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekpa kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ egbo loo ebaanyɛ ekwɛ̃ lolo?

english: Look at the center growth point and stem of the plant. If the inside remains soft and green rather than brown and dry, the plant is still alive and can bounce back with proper fertilizer and care.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ dalɛ he kɛ eshishifã lɛ. Kɛji emli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔŋ ni egbi lɛ Tso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa nɔ.

english: How long should I keep young seedlings in the nursery bags before moving them to the main field?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makɛ midumɔwui lɛ awo ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui lɛ amli dani mikɛ amɛ awo saatso wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: Most crop seedlings need about two to four weeks in the nursery until they are strong enough, usually when they have grown 4 to 6 true leaves and developed firm roots.
ga: Tsei amli dumɔwui babaoo he miihia aaafee otsii enyɔ kɛyashi ejwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli beni dumɔwu lɛ yɛ baai diɛŋtsɛ 4 kɛyashi 6 kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my new seedlings look weak and wilted for a few days right after I plant them in the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui heei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings go through 'transplant shock' because their young roots were disturbed during moving. Giving them temporary shade and watering them in the early morning or evening helps them adjust quickly.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ atsɔ Amɛyeɔ ‘transplant shock’ he amanehulu ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ haoɔ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ aha amɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni aha amɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe oya.

english: Does walking through my farm along the same crop rows every day hurt the crops?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mitsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli daa gbi lɛ, ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, walking repeatedly over the same ground packs the dirt hard like concrete. Hard soil makes it difficult for crop roots to breathe and spread out to find water.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ onyiɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ lɛ, ebaaha muji lɛ mli awa tamɔ kɔnkrit. Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛna nu.

english: Why is it important to leave enough space between my crop plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato he ko bɔ ni sa, moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing prevents plants from fighting each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which results in bigger fruits and healthier harvests.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la he akaŋ. nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, ni no haa aduawai ni daraa kɛ ŋmaa ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa.

english: Why do my crops dry out faster when I water them in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering during peak heat causes most of the water to turn into steam and evaporate into the air before reaching the roots. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the afternoon.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko tsɔɔ lasu ni efoɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo shwane.

english: What is the best time of the year for me to plant new cashew seedlings on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu cashew dumɔwui heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant cashew seedlings is at the beginning of the major rainy season. Planting early in the rains gives the young seedlings enough time to grow strong roots before the harsh dry season starts.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu cashew dumɔwui ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why do I need to leave so much space between my young mango trees when planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ babaoo yɛ mango tsei ateŋ kɛ́ midu nii lɛ?

english: Mango trees grow into very large trees over time. Leaving wide spacing ensures that each tree gets enough sunlight, water, and nutrients without competing with neighboring trees, which leads to bigger fruits and healthier trees.
ga: Mango tsei daa ni amɛfeɔ tsei wuji yɛ be ni sa mli. Gbalamɔ amɛ gbɛ babaoo koni tso fɛɛ tso aná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔ akaŋ Enɛ haa aduawai wuji kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I grow crops like maize or cassava between my young cashew trees while they are small?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ mi-cashew tsei lɛ ateŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping short-term crops like maize or cassava between young tree crops is very useful. It gives you food and income while the cashew trees grow, and weeding your food crops also keeps the field clean for the young trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Tsei bibii ateŋ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Ehaa bo niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni cashew tso lɛ daa lɛ. Ni oniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tseɔ kɛha tsei bibii.

english: Why are my young cashew trees dropping their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cashew trees naturally drop some of their leaves during hot, dry periods to prevent water loss and save energy. As long as the branches remain green and flexible, the tree is just surviving the heat and will grow fresh leaves when the rains return.
ga: Cashew tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Koni nu akafite ni akɛ hewalɛ akafite. Shii abɔ ni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ baahi shi akɛ eŋɔli ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ latsaa be lɛ mli kɛkɛ ni amɛbaaná baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: How do cashew trees manage to stay green and survive in dry areas where other crops burn up?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni cashew tsei hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hei ni nu bɛ ni tsei krokomɛi shãa lɛ?

english: Cashew trees have long, deep taproots that reach deep into the underground soil where moisture is stored. This allows them to draw water even when the topsoil is completely dry.
ga: Cashew tsei yɛ shishifãi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni mli kwɔ ni yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛtoɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ajieɔ nu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli egbi kwraa po.

english: Why do extension officers recommend pruning the lower branches of my young mango trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afolɔ mi mango tso bibioo lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting off lower branches helps the tree develop a strong central stem and a clear trunk. It also improves air flow under the tree, reduces pests and diseases, and makes it easier for you to weed around the base.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ shishigbɛ tso ni mli wa, ni atsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ hu yaa hiɛ. Haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baa shi ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni ojieɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. shishitoo lɛ mlɛo

english: Why does a mango tree planted from a seed take much longer to produce fruit than a grafted seedling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii fe dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ?

english: A tree grown directly from a seed must go through a long juvenile phase of building strong stems and roots before it can make fruit, taking up to 5 to 7 years. A grafted seedling comes from a branch of an already mature fruit-bearing tree, so it can produce fruit in just 2 to 3 years.
ga: Esa akɛ tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsɔ gbɛ ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ amaa shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa yɛ amɛblahiiaŋ kɛ oblayeiaŋ dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Eheɔ aaafee afii 5 kɛyashi 7. Akɛ dumɔwui fɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni ewo yibii momo lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ewo yibii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli.

english: My mango tree produces a lot of flowers, but most of them fall off without turning into fruit. Why is this happening?
ga: Mi mango tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi amɛteŋ babaoo baagbee shi ni amɛbatsɔmɔɔ yibii. Mɛni he je nɛ e baa jã a?

english: Flower drop can be caused by dry winds, insect pests attack, or a lack of water when the tree is flowering. Protecting trees from pests during flowering and ensuring good soil care helps more flowers turn into healthy fruits.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi afite. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa loo nu ni bɛ beni tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Kɛ́ abu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔii babaoo babaoo atsɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do some cashew trees on my farm produce many nuts while trees right next to them produce very little?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew tso ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be mli ni tso ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ? Yibiiwoo fioo ko pɛ

english: Trees grown from mixed seeds often have different genetics, meaning some naturally yield more than others. Differences in soil depth or pest attacks on individual trees also affect how many nuts each tree can produce.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui ni efutu mli lɛ yɛ fɔmɔ nii sɔrɔtoi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei komɛi woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa fe ekrokomɛi. Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tsei aŋkroaŋkroi anɔ lɛ hu saa ŋmeii ayibɔ ni tso fɛɛ tso baanyɛ ajie lɛ he.

english: Why do my fruit trees yield heavily one year and then produce very little fruit the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo afi kome, ni afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: This pattern is called alternate bearing. Producing a huge harvest exhausts the tree's stored nutrients, so it spends the following year recovering and growing new leaves instead of producing a large crop.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ style nɛɛ akɛ bearing ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ. Nikpamɔ babaoo fiteɔ niyenii ni tso lɛ eto lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ kɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛsaa ehe ni ehaa baai heei kwɛ̃ɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants turn yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential food for growth, or that waterlogged soil is preventing the roots from taking up nutrients from the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Aloo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with many green leaves but produces very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Baai eŋɔlii babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or fertile soil without enough potassium, it spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aha ŋmei nitrogen ŋmei babaoo loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmei ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves start curling up and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is caused by tiny pests like thrips or mites sucking the sap from under the leaves, or by a viral disease carried by those insects that distorts normal plant growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nakai kooloi bibii lɛ kɛbaa ni fiteɔ tsei adalɛ ni sa lɛ mli.

english: Why do improved seed varieties yield more food than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are bred specifically to resist common local diseases, withstand drought, and turn soil nutrients into grain much more efficiently than traditional seeds that lose their vigor over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ ni etsakeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ dumɔwui amli jogbaŋŋ fe blema dumɔwui ni hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops manage to stay green and produce pods even when rain does not fall for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛko otsii babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants have long taproots that dig deep to reach hidden moisture, and their leaves can close slightly during the hottest part of the day to stop water from escaping.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ shishifãi kakadaji ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛyashɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ he. Ni ebaai lɛ ŋmɛɔ fioo yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu akaje mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into tomatoes during very hot sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures kill the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing them from forming fruit, so the plant drops the unpollinated flowers to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ gbeɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. rendering them unproductive No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why does my yam crop need wooden stakes to climb on to produce larger tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Staking spreads the yam leaves out high above the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to manufacture food and store it in the underground tuber.
ga: Staking gbɛɔ sweet potato tsei lɛ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ená hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli lɛ

english: Why do I need to plant plantain or banana trees near my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu banana dumɔwui loo tsei yɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sun; plantains grow fast and provide broad leaf shade and moisture to protect young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya ni ehaa baai ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ etsu hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he nii.

english: Why do fall armyworms eat my maize leaves mostly during the early morning and late evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms yeɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo leebi maŋkpa kɛ gbɛkɛ maŋkpa lɛ?

english: Armyworms dislike intense midday sun and heat, so they hide inside the central funnel of the maize leaves during the day and come out to feed when the weather cools down.
ga: Armyworms sumɔɔɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ yɛ gbi mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni amɛje kpo koni amɛyatao niyenii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during heavy rainstorms even when the wind is not strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ waaa moŋ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots; when heavy rains soak the ground, the soft, muddy soil can no longer hold the roots, causing the top-heavy plant to collapse under its own weight.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ ha sũ lɛ mli fũu lɛ, sũ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni sũ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shishifãi lɛ dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii fe fɛɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsiimɔ shishi.

english: Why should I leave shade trees on my farm instead of clearing all of them to make room for cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaajie tsei muu fɛɛ koni aha gbɛ aha kookoo lɛ,.

english: Shade trees protect young cocoa from direct sunlight, cool down the farm temperature, and drop leaves that decompose into natural manure to feed your cocoa trees and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ha hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi ni oha baai ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaha kookoo tsei lɛ niyenii ni amɛha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: How does planting tall trees around my farm boundaries protect my crops during the dry season?
ga: Tsei kakadaji ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te ŋmɔ husui buɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Boundary trees act as windbreaks that slow down dry Harmattan winds, reducing the speed at which water evaporates from your soil and preventing strong winds from blowing down tall crops like maize and plantain.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ husu lɛ naa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔnei ni haa Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. ni etsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekatswa tsei kakadaji tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is short on nitrogen, an important plant food. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the newer top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ anɔ hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism plants use to preserve water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to intense sunlight to keep from losing moisture too quickly.
ga: Baai lɛ akumɔ ji hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ akafite lɛ oya.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpea or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When those roots break down, they release natural fertilizer into the soil that helps the maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ nakai shishifãi lɛ fã lɛ, amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava suckers very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots fight underground for water and nutrients while their leaves fight above ground for sunlight, resulting in thin plants with small tubers.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ bulb bibii baa.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why does my yam crop grow plenty of green vines and leaves but produce small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ wain tsei kɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen manure early on, the yam plant spends all its energy producing leaves above ground instead of sending sugars down to build big underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mra mli lɛ Sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaatsu sugar kɛba shi koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is rich and healthy without taking it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ hewalɛ ni mikɛyaaa laboratori?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, smells fresh like earth, crumbles easily in your hand without forming hard blocks, and contains earthworms and decaying leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ hee. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa baaa. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni egboi hu yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my crop roots burn or die when I put chemical fertilizer right against the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shãa loo amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ wo he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is made of salts that draw water out of plant roots if placed too close, causing the root tissues to dry out and burn instead of absorbing nutrients.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei ni baajie nu kɛjɛ tsei shishifãi amli kɛji akɛ akɛwo amɛhe tsɔ lɛ feɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifã lɛ mli fãji lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to tie long sticks to my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ akpɛtɛ sweet potato wain tso ko he beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce energy. Lifting the leaves off the ground allows the plant to catch full sun, which feeds the underground tuber to grow big.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa hulu la lɛ fɛɛ. ni woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii anɔ koni amɛdara

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main stem. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree gets enough food to produce heavy, high-quality bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tsei niji ni tsii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off without forming small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by too much heat or drought, or when tiny insects called midges cannot pollinate them. Maintaining shade trees keeps the field moist so midges can work.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ ni fa babaoo hao amɛ. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii Anyɛɛɛ afee nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ pollination. Tsei lɛ ni oooha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shia lɛ mli feɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni ŋshɔŋloo lɛ anyɛ atsu enitsumɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants full of ragged holes with tiny caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm pests that feed on young leaves inside the center whorl. Applying recommended treatments or clean ash/sand into the whorl early helps destroy them before they ruin the farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ. Ni akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii loo sũ/ŋã ni he tse awo ring lɛ mli mra. Ye obua ni akpata amɛhiɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves twisting up and turning yellow with green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. Using disease-resistant cassava stem varieties stops the virus from affecting your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ji nɔ ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ Kɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ haaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa okpamɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: This is usually bacterial wilt, a disease living in the soil that enters roots and blocks water from reaching the top of the plant. Rotating tomatoes with crops like maize helps clear the disease from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji hela ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni eboteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi amli ni ehaa nu shɛɛɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ helai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the swollen branches on my cocoa trees turning red and losing leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei niji ni efuu ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ ni amɛbaa lɛ miiho lɛ?

english: This is Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. Because there is no chemical cure for the virus, infected trees must be cut down to save the healthy trees surrounding them.
ga: Enɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ ji akɛ tsofa ko bɛ ni baanyɛ atsa hela lɛ. Esa akɛ afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ koni akɛhere tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants turn light yellow after heavy rain falls continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes away essential plant food like nitrogen deep into the soil beyond the roots' reach, while waterlogged soil prevents roots from breathing properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe shishifãi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does keeping standing water in my rice field help the crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni mikɛtoɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Flooding suffocates and kills land weeds that compete with rice for space and nutrients, while swamp rice plants are naturally built to grow happily in submerged water.
ga: Nu afua lɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ jwɛi ni kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná he ko kɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ agbɔjɔ ni egbeɔ amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, abɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛ miishɛɛ yɛ nu ni boteɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: How do I know that my plantain bunch is fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantain tso lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Plantains are mature when the sharp edges or ridges on individual fingers become rounder and smoother, the dry flower tips break off easily, and the upper leaves of the plant start turning yellow.
ga: Plantains lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he kɛ́ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nineshi nii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nɔ lɛ bafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Fɔfɔi ashishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛkuɔ oya. Ni tso lɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow before the fruit bunch is fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani aduawai akui lɛ dara kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves before fruit maturity usually mean the plantain lacks nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, or it is experiencing water stress from dry spells or poor soil drainage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium bɛ plantain lɛ mli. aloo ni enaa nu he haomɔ yɛ hulutsoo be loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves fall off during the dry season, and does it mean the crop is dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigboi?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry periods to save water and keep the root tubers alive underground. Once the rains return, fresh leaves will sprout again without damaging your yield.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha shishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Baai heei baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni efiteee onibii.

english: Staking gets yam leaves up into direct sunlight where they can make more food for the plant. Elevating the leaves helps produce bigger tubers and keeps the plant safe from rot on wet ground.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha niyenii babaoo aha tso lɛ. Baai lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa bulbs wuji feɔ, ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe koni ekafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ.

english: Why is my maize producing tassels and flowering early when the plants are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi oya nɛkɛ? Tso lɛ yɛ kuku waa lolo?

english: Maize flowers early when it faces severe stress early in life, such as prolonged drought or poor soil fertility. The plant rushes to produce seeds to survive before it reaches full height.
ga: Abɛi woɔ fɔfɔi mra kɛji akɛ ekɛ haomɔ ni naa wa kpe yɛ eshihilɛ mli mra, tamɔ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ. Tsei kɛ oyaiyeli woɔ dumɔwui koni amɛhi shi dani amɛshɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing short and yellow in some parts of my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ miikwɛ̃ kuku ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi lɛ?

english: Stunted and yellow cowpeas often point to low soil fertility, poor root development caused by parasitic weeds like Striga, or root-knot nematodes attacking the root system.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsina ŋmeii ni ji dwarf kɛ yellow cowpeas lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa shi. Shishifãi ni ehiii ni jwɛi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ tamɔ Striga loo root-knot nematodes ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ kɛbaa.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black while hanging on the trees?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ beni mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and overly shaded conditions. Pruning shade trees and clearing weeds helps sunlight dry out the pods and prevent infection.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni afoɔ ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ haa hulu la lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaaa helai aba.

english: Why do my sweet orange trees drop a lot of small fruits right after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ woɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo yɛ fɔfɔii asɛɛ?

english: Orange trees naturally shed tiny fruits they cannot support if they lack enough water or nutrients. Heavy fruit drop usually signals that the tree needs consistent watering or better fertilizer.
ga: Orange tsei baawo yibii bibii. Taakɛ eji lɛ, anyɛɛɛ atsɔse amɛ kɛji nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, yibii ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni awo tso lɛ nu babaoo daa loo awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when weather conditions get too hot, when soil moisture changes suddenly between too wet and too dry, or when the plant lacks nutrients like phosphorus and calcium.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ trukaa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ teŋ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ kalsium

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the hot afternoon even when the soil is still damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: Tomatoes lose water through their leaves faster than roots can absorb it in intense afternoon heat. If soil fungi or nematodes have damaged the roots, the plant wilts temporarily until cooler hours.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo nematodes fite shishifãi lɛ Tso lɛ baagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashi ebaajɔ.

english: Why do all my plantain crops produce fruit at the exact same time instead of spreading out over the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ fɛɛ woɔ yibii yɛ be kome mli moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When plantain suckers are planted at the same time in similar soil and rain conditions, they mature at almost the exact same speed. To avoid having all your harvest arrive at once, you need to stagger your planting dates throughout the season.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ shihilɛi ni tamɔ amɛhe nɔ Dumɔwui lɛ daraa yɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ oyaiyeli ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ mli. Enɛ ji koni nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ akashɛ shikome. Esa akɛ otsake gbii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do some of my plantain crops stay firm longer after harvesting while others turn soft very quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi hiɔ shi shiŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi feɔ blɛoo oya waa lɛ?

english: Different varieties of plantains have different skin thicknesses and starch levels. Plantains with thicker skins hold their moisture better and stay firm longer, which makes them better for long journeys to the market.
ga: Plantain henɔi srɔtoi lɛ yɛ hewolo nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ srɔtoi. Plantains ni hewolo lɛ mli wa lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ehi jogbaŋŋ po kɛha gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ kɛmiiya jara nɔ.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller with every new shoot that grows from the same stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii be fɛɛ be ni tso lɛ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ mli tso hee ko baakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: When too many young shoots grow around one main plant, they all fight for the same soil food and water. Cutting away extra shoots leaves only the strongest ones, ensuring the plant has enough energy to make large bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛshiɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee kui wuji.

english: Why does my plantain crop take so long to produce its first bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantains require large amounts of water and nutrients like nitrogen and potassium to start flowering. If the soil lacks food or experiences dry weather early on, the plant delays flowering until conditions improve.
ga: Nu babaoo kɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium he miihia plantains koni ebɔi fɔfɔi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ mli loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi yɛ shishijee mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ asɛɛ kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know which small plantain shoots to keep and which ones to cut off from the main plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male plantain tsei ni esa akɛ makwɛ? Ni mɛɛ ŋmeii esa akɛ afo kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ he?

english: Shoots with thin, spear-like leaves have strong underground connections and will grow into healthy, heavy-fruiting trees. Shoots with wide, broad leaves early on have weak roots and will produce small, poor-quality fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi. Eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsakpaa ko ni mli wa. ni ebaada ni etsɔ tso ni wa ni ewo yibii ni tsii. Tsei bibii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛmli lɛ baaná shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛbaawo yibii bibii ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young plantain crops turning yellow and drooping during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves droop and turn yellow to protect themselves and conserve water when the air is hot and the ground is dry. Covering the ground around the base with dry grass helps hold moisture in the soil.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛbu nu he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Can I plant plantains on the same piece of land with my cassava without the crops fighting each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmei ni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewuuuu?

english: Yes, you can grow them together if you space them properly. Cassava draws nutrients near the soil surface while plantain roots go slightly deeper, so proper spacing prevents them from choking each other.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome kɛji ojara he lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Cassava gbalaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Yɛ be mli ni plantain shishifãi lɛ yaa mli fioo lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe kɛjɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my harvested plantains ripen and spoil so fast before I can take them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ ni egboɔ oya dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, plantains naturally produce a gas that speeds up their own ripening. Keeping the harvested bunches under direct sunlight or in hot rooms makes this gas work faster, causing the fruit to spoil quickly.
ga: Kɛji akpa Plantains lɛ, ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ni haa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshwereɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ to hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ loo yɛ tsu ko ni mli edɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔi lɛ atsu nii oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibii lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my plantains develop soft black spots when I load them onto trucks for long distance travel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ nɔ tsɔi diji ni yɔɔ blɛoo beni mikɛwoɔ lɔle mli kɛyaa gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Black spots are bruises caused by pressure and rough movement when plantain bunches rub against each other during transport. Cushioning the bunches with plantain leaves in the truck reduces this damage.
ga: He ni ediŋŋ ji fãji ni nɔnyɛɛ kɛ nyiɛmɔ ni mli wa kɛbaa beni plantain ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ gbɛfaa mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ plantain baai wo lɔle lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ nɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my healthy-looking plantain trees suddenly fall over even when there is only a light wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ miigbee shi trukaa lɛ? He ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa blɛoo lɛ?

english: Tiny insects or worms underground often eat away the roots of the plantain, destroying its anchor in the soil. Even though the top of the tree looks green, it can no longer hold its own weight.
ga: ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii Bei pii lɛ Shikpɔŋ shishi yeɔ plantains shishifãi. ni efiteɔ eŋmei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ ayitsei lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli moŋ Shi enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɔjɔmɔ lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do some cocoa trees on my farm give bigger pods than the older trees planted long ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji fe cacao tsei ni adu be saŋŋ ni eho lɛ?

english: Different cocoa trees come from different plant families or seeds. Older varieties like traditional Amelonado produce smaller pods, while newer hybrid varieties released by research centers grow faster and produce larger pods with more beans.
ga: Cacao tsei srɔtoi jɛɔ tsei awekui loo dumɔwui srɔtoi amli. Henɔi ni etsɛ, tamɔ blema amelonado lɛ, woɔ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii heei ni niiamlitaomɔ he lɛ jie lɛ kpo lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I cut down all the large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle direct sunlight all day. Shade trees shield young plants from scorching heat, cool down the leaves, and help the soil hold water so the seedling can grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ehaa baai lɛ mli jɔɔ Ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli koni dumɔwui lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why does cocoa grow very well in wet forest areas like the Eastern Region but struggles in drier places?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni kooi ni mli edɔ yɔɔ tamɔ bokagbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi esa akɛ okɛ ohe awo mli yɛ hei ni egbi lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees need regular rainfall, rich soil full of organic food, and high humidity to thrive. Drier areas lack enough underground moisture, causing the leaves to dry up and drop off before pods can mature.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ hia nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi kɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ hulutsoo babaoo kɛha dalɛ Hei ni egbi lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ shishi hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: If I cut off excess shoots and branches from my cocoa tree, won't that reduce my crop harvest?
ga: Kɛ mifolɔ ŋmeii kɛ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, Ani no haŋ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Removing dead or overgrown branches actually helps the tree. It allows sunlight and air to reach all parts of the plant, prevents diseases from hiding, and directs the tree's energy into making flowers and pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni egboi loo ni eda fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Tsi helai anaa koni amɛkatee amɛhe Ni okɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ afee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ.

english: My cocoa tree produces many small flowers, but why do most of them fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny beneficial insects called midges to carry pollen from flower to flower. If the weather is too hot, dry, or if there are no wet leaf layers on the soil for midges to live in, flowers drop off unpollinated.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni ekɛ pollen woɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, edɔ, loo kɛji akɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ eko bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni dwarf lɛ baanyɛ ahi mli lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni pollination bɛ mli.

english: Can I plant cassava close to my young cocoa trees to harvest extra food?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava yɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni makpa niyenii krokomɛi?

english: Cassava roots stretch far and greedily drink water and food from the topsoil, which steals nourishment from young cocoa plants. Planting plantains or cocoyams is better because they protect cocoa without aggressively competing for soil food.
ga: Cassava shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ hiɛjoomɔ, ni amɛnuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei bibii amli lɛ Dumɔwui loo kookoo ni aduɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he ni ekɛ hiɛdɔɔ etswaaa niyenii he akaŋshii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot whenever the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Continuous rain creates cold, damp air that allows a fungal disease called Black Pod to spread. Raindrops splash the fungus from pod to pod, so keeping weeds low and pruning branches lets air in to keep pods dry.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ kɛ hulutsoo baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ shwie ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ pod kome mli kɛtee pod kome mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi lɛ ba shi ni ofolɔ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli ni eha jwɛi lɛ agbi.

english: My cocoa trees are very old and producing fewer pods every year—is there a way to make them bear plenty fruit again?
ga: Mi-cocoa tso lɛ egbɔ waa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ daa afi. Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ aha amɛwo yibii babaoo ekoŋŋ?

english: Old trees lose the power to carry water and nutrients efficiently to the top. You can cut back old main branches to encourage fresh, young shoots to sprout from the trunk, or gradually replant the farm with improved young seedlings.
ga: Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii jogbaŋŋ kɛya ŋwɛi. Obaanyɛ ofolɔ tsei niji wuji momo lɛ koni ŋmeii bibii heei akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi, loo fiofio lɛ okɛ dumɔwui bibii ni asaa amɛhe lɛ adu amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cocoa trees very close to each other so I can fit more trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni manyɛ madu tsei babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When trees are squeezed too close together, their roots fight over soil food and their branches entangle, blocking sunlight. This dark, overcrowded space creates a wet home where pests and pod rots easily destroy your whole crop.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atswa tsei ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni eniji lɛ baabɔle amɛhe ni amɛtsi hulu la lɛ naa. Nɛkɛ he ni yɔɔ duŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi babaoo nɛɛ haa shia lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ pod rot baanyɛ afite onibii fɛɛ yɛ mlɛo.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa leaves are yellowing from lack of water or because the soil needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo lɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔŋ?

english: When plants lack water, leaves curl up, wilt, and feel crispy during hot afternoons. When plants lack soil nutrients, leaves stay soft but lose their rich green color, turning pale yellow even when the soil has moisture.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe ejɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ baakã he ahi shi blɛoo shi amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa lɛ baaje mli. ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall but producing very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Maize plants often put all their energy into growing tall stalks instead of cobs when they get too much nitrogen fertilizer or when they are planted too close together, leaving little energy for the grains to swell.
ga: Abɛi tsei sumɔɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni amɛwoɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛji akɛ onine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni amɛkɛbaafu.

english: How can I make my cassava tubers grow bigger and heavier before harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛtsii dani akpa?

english: Cassava roots need loose, well-drained soil and adequate potassium to swell. If the soil is too hard or compacted, the roots cannot expand and will stay small and thin.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli tse. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni eyɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafu Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛbaakã he amɛfee bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ.

english: Why are my sweet potatoes splitting open underground before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes crack open when heavy rain comes suddenly after a long dry spell. The sudden intake of water causes the inside of the tuber to expand faster than its skin can grow.
ga: Sweet potatoes shwieɔ shi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Nu ni anuɔ trukaa lɛ haa yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ada.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my tomato plants turn yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen nutrient or is being overwatered. The plant moves whatever food it has left to the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen niyenii loo eená nu babaoo. Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it normal for my pepper plants to drop their flowers before setting fruits?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients as a defense mechanism to preserve energy during stressful weather.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa he, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai. akɛ gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni akɛbu hewalɛ he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni haa mɔ haoɔ lɛ amli

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my yams so they don't spoil easily in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii? Bɔni afee ni ekafite oya yɛ nitoohe.

english: Yams are fully mature when the leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up naturally. Harvesting at this point ensures the tubers have accumulated maximum starch and will last long in storage.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ebua ŋmeii babaoo naa ni amɛbaahi shi be babaoo yɛ nitoohe lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea pods look healthy on the outside but have tiny holes and damaged seeds inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔji lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ kponɔgbɛ shi amɛyɛ bu bibii kɛ dumɔwui ni efite yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pod-boring insects lay eggs inside the cowpea flowers, and the hatching caterpillars feed on the seeds inside the pod before you harvest them.
ga: Kplukai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ tsina fɔfɔi amli. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ dani amɛkpaa.

english: Can I use seeds saved from tomatoes I bought at the market to plant my next farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛ tomato ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Seeds from market tomatoes are often hybrid varieties. When you plant them, the next crop may produce weak plants or fruits that are completely different from the parent tomato.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato dumɔwui ni jɛɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome. Beni oduɔ lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ajie tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo aduawai ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa yɛ fɔlɔ tomato lɛ he.
