english: Excess suckers compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the mother plant to produce a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ ŋmei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ awo ŋmei wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under hot direct sun. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that shade young cocoa trees and keep the soil moist during their first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, stops water from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to apply fertilizer to my crop field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Fertilizer is best applied early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the soil is moist and the weather is cool, as high mid-day heat can burn the plant roots when mixed with fertilizer.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food that helps crops grow big and stay dark green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Eji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa ni amɛnáa su ni tsuɔ waa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small flowers without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Drop ni etsɔko pod?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by dry weather, lack nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny midges in the air to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo tsei bibii bɛ. Nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ni baaha fɔfɔii lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my tomato fruits turning black and sunken on the bottom end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiibote shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes are caused by a condition called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often due to uneven watering.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing green sprouts even when kept in a cool barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃mɔ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛto ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally wake up from their rest period after a few months to try and grow into new plants, especially when humidity in the air changes.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ koni amɛka amɛkwɛ ni amɛtsɔ tsei heei. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsake.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and getting smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or a virus spread by these insects as they feed on the sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛyeɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ

english: Cassava roots rot in the ground when the soil stays waterlogged for too long after heavy rains, allowing fungal diseases in the wet dirt to attack the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atutua shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants snap or fall over easily even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po lɛ?

english: Plantain plants fall over when tiny pests like nematodes or banana stem weevils weaken the underground roots and corm, destroying the plant's support system.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii lɛ ha shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔ. ni fiteɔ tso lɛ yelikɛbuamɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ

english: Why am I finding holes and dirt that looks like sawdust inside the funnel of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the young maize leaves, eats the plant stem, and leaves behind its waste.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli, ni eyeɔ tsei ahe ŋmeii ni eshiɔ jwɛi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist so young cocoa can survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow before the crop even matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach, or the soil may simply need compost or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Aloo ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen awo mli.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough to plant cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmei?

english: Good cassava soil should be loose, sandy-loam soil that drains water easily. If your soil heavy clay that holds water and creates puddles, the cassava tubers will rot underground instead of expanding.
ga: Esa akɛ cassava shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ŋã yɔɔ mli. Nu ni hoɔ oya Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni hiɛɔ nu ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi. Cassava shishifãi lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over whenever strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that stay near the surface. If planted in loose soil without mound support, or if nematodes damage their roots, the heavy plant cannot support itself against strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni gɔji bɛ nɔ loo kɛji akɛ nematodes fite shishifãi lɛ Tsei ni tsii lɛ nyɛŋ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too high or when soil moisture fluctuates drastically from very dry to very wet. This stress prevents pollination, causing the plant to drop its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why does my cowpea crop produce so many leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cowpea plants to focus all their energy on growing leafy vines rather than flowers and pods. Avoiding high-nitrogen fertilizers allows the plant to flower and fruit properly.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ he nii moŋ fe fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or viruses spread by whiteflies. Removing affected leaves early and using organic neem oil spray helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni ŋmeii egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Ajieɔ baai ni ena hela lɛ mra Ni akɛ organic neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii koni eye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my cabbage leaves and how do I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are caused by caterpillars, particularly the diamondback moth caterpillar. Inspecting leaves regularly and applying natural sprays made from neem seeds can keep caterpillars away.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii amli. Titri lɛ, ŋmei ni yɔɔ ojarawatɛ sɛɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ amli daa ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛ neem dumɔwui fee lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii lɛ akabote mli.

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines turn yellow and naturally dry up at the end of the rainy season, showing that energy has finished transferring into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hewalɛ lɛ egbe shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli shwiemɔ naa.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get damaged by tiny insects inside the storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii fiteɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ? Yɛ shĩa lɛ mli?

english: Grain damage in storage is caused by maize weevils, which lay eggs inside grains when harvest isn't dried fully. Drying maize until it is hard and storing it in airtight bags or clean, dry stores stops weevils from multiplying.
ga: Dumɔwui ni fiteɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ ji ŋmãa ŋmeii, ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛji amɛgbiko kwraa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ewa ni akɛto vacuum kotokui amli loo shwapo ko ni mli tse ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akafa babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct heat from the sun. Planting shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa creates living umbrellas that shade the delicate seedlings and keep the soil moist while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui, yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ wala mli ni haa hulutsoo baa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil runs out of nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their green color and help them grow big ears.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ efo, ni no ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa abɛi koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha toi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua toi lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from sudden dry spells, high heat, or poor soil nutrients. Watering regularly at the roots and adding organic matter keeps the plant stable so the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haaa mɔ he waa lɛ ye tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu daa ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Fɔfɔi lɛ batsɔ aduawai lɛ.

english: What is eating the inner leaves of my young maize crop and leaving small holes behind?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ mli baai lɛ ni eshiɔ bu bibii yɛ esɛɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the funnel of the young maize plant. Applying neem leaf extract or approved pest control solutions directly into the plant's central leaves stops them before they destroy the stalk.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly wet conditions. Pruning extra tree branches allows sunlight and breeze to dry the pods, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni edɔ fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ. Koni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã

english: Why do my cassava tubers become smaller every year when I plant on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava removes a lot of food from the ground during growth. If you plant it repeatedly on the same land without resting the field or adding manure, the soil becomes exhausted, leading to smaller tubers.
ga: Cassava gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ. Kɛji odu shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ ohe ejɔɔɔ ohe loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafo, ni no baaha ŋmeii bibii aba.

english: Why do groundnuts or beans make the soil better for maize when planted nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls natural food called nitrogen out of the air and puts it into the soil. This works like free natural fertilizer that helps neighboring maize plants grow better.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high off the ground to catch direct sunlight to make plant food. Staking keeps the leaves away from hot soil and direct pests, allowing the plant to build bigger tubers below ground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha tsei ahe tsei lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why should I spread dry grass and leaves around the bottom of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai abɔle mi-pepper tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the earth quickly, lowers soil temperature, and blocks weeds from growing around your crop roots.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ aba shi ni otsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ naa.

english: How do I know if the ground is wet enough to plant my corn after the first rain of the year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should check if the rain has soaked into the soil deep enough to cover the length of your hand. Planting after only a light rain can cause seeds to sprout and quickly dry up if hot days follow before the next rain.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛha onine lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi oya kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ba.

english: Why do strong winds during the rainy season easily knock down my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni tswaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: When heavy rain drenches the field, the soil gets soft and muddy, making it hard for roots to hold on. Strong winds then push against tall, leafy plants and easily tip them over or break their stems.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɔ̃ɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baatsɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ muji. Ehaa ewaa ahaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaakpɛtɛ he Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa tsei ni yɔɔ baai kakadaji lɛ anɔ. ni egbeeɔ shi loo efoɔ tsɔne lɛ mli oya

english: What can I plant around the edges of my farm to stop heavy winds from blowing down my maize?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ madu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa koni kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa ŋmãa lɛ shi?

english: Planting a border of tall, deep-rooted trees or fast-growing grass like vetiver acts as a windbreak, slowing down strong storm gusts before they reach your delicate crops.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ loo jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ vetiver jwɛi lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ baa shi dani eshɛɔ onibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe.

english: Why do some of my crops need wooden stakes tied to them before the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi akpɛtɛ tsei ahe dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Staking gives tall or heavy-fruiting plants extra physical support so that strong storm winds and heavy rain don't snap their stems or push them down into the mud.
ga: Staking haa tsei ni kɛlɛ loo ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ náa gbɔmɔtsoŋ yelikɛbuamɔ kroko. Enɛ ji koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akakumɔ tso lɛ mli loo akatsi lɛ awo muji lɛ mli.

english: If a rainstorm bends my young crops to the ground, can they stand back up on their own?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ ha miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ Ani amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ shi?

english: Young plants with flexible stems will often naturally bend back up toward the sunlight after a few days, as long as their main stem isn't snapped and the roots weren't torn out of the wet ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni nyɛɔ efoɔ lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba hulu la mli yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ, kɛji akɛ shishifã titri lɛ ekuuu ni shishifãi lɛ ejeee he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: How do I choose crops that will finish growing if the rainy season only lasts three months?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ohala tsei ni obaadu be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eshwɛ nyɔji 3 pɛ?

english: You should look for short-duration or early-maturing crop varieties that take 60 to 90 days to harvest, ensuring they fully mature before the dry weather returns.
ga: Esa akɛ otao ŋmeii srɔtoi ni shwereɔ kuku loo ni shwereɔ mra ni heɔ gbii 60 kɛyashi 90 dani akpaa koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ amɛshɛ shweremɔ he dani shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ aba.

english: Which types of crops naturally stand up better to heavy wind and rain?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ji nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ amɛhe waa yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Crops that grow low to the ground, root crops like sweet potatoes and cassava, or plants with deep taproots and flexible stems handle stormy weather much better than tall, top-heavy grains.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ. Tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi, tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei. loo tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni nyɛɔ etsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu ahum he nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni kɛlɛ ni tsii.

english: What will happen to my crops if the three-month rain stops earlier than expected?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nyɔji etɛ mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: If the rain cuts off early while crops are still flowering or forming fruit, the plants will stress and dry out, leading to smaller harvests or crop failure due to lack of water.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi loo amɛmiiwo yibii lolo lɛ. Tso lɛ baaná haomɔ ni ebaagbi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ baa shi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow so much faster as soon as the heavy rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya waa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: Rainwater dissolves stored nutrients in the soil so the roots can absorb them quickly, triggering a sudden burst of stem and leaf growth.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ oya. Ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ daa trukaa.

english: Does planting my seeds deeper in the soil stop my plants from falling over during stormy weather?
ga: Ani midumɔwui lɛ ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi yɛ ahum be mli?

english: Planting at the correct depth helps roots establish deeper and anchor firmly into the earth, giving the plant a stronger foundation against heavy winds.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ he ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ mli wa waa kɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa.

english: Why does soil turn into mud and lose its grip on plant roots after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ muji ni enyɛŋ emɔ tsei ashishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water fills all the tiny air spaces in the soil, causing dirt particles to slide past each other easily and loosening the ground's firm grip around plant roots.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ muji bibii lɛ baatsɔ amɛhe. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tsei shishifãi ahe lɛ mli tseɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and drying up during the hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight and high heat. They need temporary shade trees like plantain or cassava to block the sun and keep the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca. Enɛ ji koni akɛtsi hulu lɛ naa ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots growing around the main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajieɔ dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: If too many shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they all fight for food, light, and water. Keeping only one or two strong shoots ensures the main plant gets enough strength to produce large bunches.
ga: Kɛji plantain tsei lɛ dara kɛbɔle Tso titri kome he lɛ fa tsɔ. Tsoi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, kane, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee panicle agbo.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning yellow starting from the tips down to the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which helps it stay green and grow. Adding NPK fertilizer or well-decayed manure gives the plant the food it needs to recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi eŋɔli ni edaa. Kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young maize crop and leaving green dust inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ sũ eŋɔli yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center of the maize plant to eat soft leaves. Spraying with recommended organic mixtures like neem extract or approved pesticides early in the morning kills them off.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akɛfutuɔ nibii ni ajieɔ yi akɛ afee tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie amɛnɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe amɛ.

english: Why is it risky to plant my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: The first rain often cools the air, but the soil underneath remains warm and dry spells usually follow. Waiting for two or three steady rains ensures enough water stays deep in the ground for young seeds to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔɔ, ni bei pii lɛ, egbiɔ yɛ enɛ hewɔ lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni dumɔwui bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water collects around them for too long during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni aduɔ ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: What happens to my yam plants if I do not train the vines to climb on wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mitsɔseee wein tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɔ tsei ni akɛfee tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Yam leaves need to climb high to capture maximum sunlight to create food for the tubers underground. Without wooden stakes, the leaves lie on the hot ground, catch diseases easily, and produce smaller yams.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji tso ko bɛ lɛ Akɛ baai lɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. helai baanyɛ amɔ amɛ oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii

english: Why do my groundnut flowers bend down and push themselves into the soil after opening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛgbele sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts produce their flowers above ground, but once pollinated, the plant naturally grows a long peg that burrows into the soil to grow the groundnut pod underground. Soft soil makes it easier for these pegs to dig in.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ pollinated Tsei lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmeii kakadaji yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛfoɔ koni amɛkɛdu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa peg lɛ akɛ ebaafo.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into small cups and refusing to grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛkpoo akɛ amɛaafee wuji lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids that suck the sap out of soft leaves and pass viruses to the plant. Using neem oil spray or keeping weeds out of the farm keeps these insects away.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ni ekɛ hela lɛ yaa tso lɛ nɔ Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akabote tso lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime heat gets too extreme or when the plant experiences water stress. Supplying enough water around the root zone and mulching the soil helps the plant keep its flowers to form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli tamɔ tomato.

english: Can I use tap water from a pipe to water my crops, or does it have to be rainwater?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ hose mli lɛ aha mi tsei lɛ nu? Aloo esa akɛ efee nugbɔ nu?

english: You can use clean pipe water for your crops, but rainwater is often better because it contains natural dissolved nitrogen and lacks chlorine or chemicals that can accumulate in the soil over time.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nu ni mli tse ni jɛɔ hose lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛha onibii. Shi bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ nu hi fe no ejaakɛ nitrogen ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ mli. Ni chlorine loo tsofai ni baanyɛ abua shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning or in the middle of the day?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the plant roots to absorb moisture before the sun heats up, which prevents the water from evaporating too quickly and protects leaves from heat stress.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ dɔɔ amɛ. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya tsɔ. ni ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: How do I know if my maize crop is getting too much or too little water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele lɛ miihe nu babaoo loo miiye fioo tsɔ?

english: If maize leaves roll up tight during the day, the plant is thirsty; if the leaves turn pale yellow and the ground stays muddy, the roots are drowning from too much water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kumai baaye tso lɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tee nɔ efee muji lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ ebote nu mli tsɔ.

english: How do my crops take in food from fertilizer to grow big?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Plants take up fertilizer nutrients that dissolve in soil water through their roots, using that liquid food to build strong stems, green leaves, and heavy ears or tubers.
ga: Tsei kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ nu mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Ekɛ nu ko tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ tsei ni wa, baai eŋɔli, kɛ toi loo yitsei ni tsii.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my corn plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant is starving for nitrogen, a key food element it needs from fertile soil or manure to make healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Is it true that tomatoes and peppers are close relatives, and why does that matter for my field?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ji wekumɛi ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes and peppers belong to the same crop family, meaning they eat the same soil nutrients and suffer from the same pests, so you should not plant them in the same spot year after year.
ga: Tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso weku kome mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ, ni amɛyɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ esaaa akɛ oduɔ amɛ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi.

english: If a disease hits one cassava plant in my farm, will it spread quickly to the rest?
ga: Kɛji hela ko ba ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ ekome nɔ Ani ebaagbɛ eshwa tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ amli oya?

english: Yes, because cassava plants in the same farm are close relatives with the same weaknesses, insects like whiteflies can easily carry diseases from one sick plant to surrounding healthy ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, akɛni ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ ji wekumɛi ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa ni yɔɔ oshara kome hewɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ nɔ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ.

english: Why do some farmers plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly underneath; planting them together gives you two harvests from one plot and keeps weeds from taking over the bare soil.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa mra. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa fiofio yɛ shishi lɛ. Nibii ni ooodu yɛ he kome lɛ baaha oná yibii enyɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekaye shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Do my young cocoa seedlings need shade trees, or should I clear all big trees away?
ga: Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he miihia tso ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Aloo esa akɛ majie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade trees because their delicate leaves burn easily in full sun, and shade helps keep the soil cool and moist while the plants establish deep roots.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui bibii lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Ni hulutsoo be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ maa shi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbours that drink the soil water and eat the fertilizer meant for your crop, starving your crop of sunlight and space to expand.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii hiɛjoolɔi ni nuɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ he ko ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ egbɛ eshwã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaaa.

english: Why should I measure and line up my farm neat and straight instead of just planting seeds anywhere there is open dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu miŋmɔ lɛ he ni mafee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ anɔkwale? Moŋ lɛ, dumɔ wui yɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tse.

english: Planting in clear, organized rows gives every crop its own space, air, and sunlight to grow strong. It also makes it much easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest without stepping on young plants.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni mli tse ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ hulu la koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Agbɛnɛ hu, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa nibii ni okɛ onaji shwieee tsei bibii anɔ.

english: What will happen if I plant my crops too close to each other in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ he kome?

english: When crops are crowded together, they fight like hungry children over the limited food, water, and sunlight in that spot. This makes all of them grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in a very poor harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii miibua amɛhe naa lɛ Amɛwuu tamɔ gbekɛbii. hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ koni amɛkɛ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la fioo ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛ fɛɛ amɛdaraa, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do I need to dig and loosen the hard soil with my hoe before pushing seeds into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ shɔvel atsa shikpɔŋ ni wa dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Loosening hard dirt softens the earth so tender young roots can easily push down deep to search for water and food. Hard soil acts like a wall that traps and starves young plant roots.
ga: Muji ni wa lɛ ni ooogbala mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ shi kɛya shɔŋŋ oya koni amɛyatao nu kɛ niyenii. Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo ni mɔ̃ɔ tsei bibii ashishifãi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: After clearing my land with a cutlass, is it better to burn the cleared grass or leave it on the dirt?
ga: Okɛ tsɔne atsu nii ni okɛjie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ani ehi akɛ aaashã jwɛi ni ajie lɛ loo ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaving cleared grass to rot naturally forms a blanket over the dirt that keeps the soil cool and moist during hot days. As it rots, it also turns into rich, free natural food for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni he tse ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni efiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ feɔ blanket yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ egbo lɛ, ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii babaoo ni aheee nɔ ko haa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: If I bring stranger farmers onto my land under a sharecropping arrangement, what crops are best for them to plant first?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ okwaafonyo ko ni mileee lɛ ba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ sharecropping kpaŋmɔ shishi Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ amɛbaadu klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Fast-growing food crops like maize, cassava, or vegetables are best for new farm arrangements because they give quick food and income in the first year while the soil is being opened up.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo aduawai ji nɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔ hee he saamɔ. Ejaakɛ ehaa niyenii kɛ shika baa oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbeleɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to clearly agree on which crops can be planted when sharing farm land with caretaker workers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akpɛlɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni abaanyɛ adu lɛ anɔ yɛ faŋŋ mli kɛ́ akɛ mɔ ko ni kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ miija ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Short-term crops like maize are harvested and finished quickly, but long-term tree crops like cocoa or oil palm stay on the land for decades. Defining the crops prevents disputes over who owns the land in the future.
ga: Akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni agbeɔ naa oya. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo loo ŋmei fɔ Ebaahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ béi ni kɔɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he wɔsɛɛ lɛ naa.

english: Can I plant cassava or plantain in the same field with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava loo plantain yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, young cocoa seedlings burn easily in bright sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantain or cassava act as living umbrellas that protect young cocoa from direct sun while providing you food while you wait for cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava tsuɔ nii akɛ shade ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ehaa bo niyenii be mli ni omɛɛɔ kookoo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn yellow and stop growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiikpa shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are like aggressive visitors that steal food, fertilizer, and water directly from the roots of your crops, leaving your main crops starving and malnourished.
ga: Jwɛi tamɔ gbɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa.

english: Why should I wait for steady rain before putting my seeds into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Seeds need a constant supply of moisture to wake up and sprout. If you plant in dry soil after just one light rain, the hot ground will bake and destroy the seed before it can grow roots.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji odu shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ, shikome pɛ Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baashã ni egbe dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ shishifãi.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller every season if I plant the exact same crop on the same plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi kɛji akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: The same type of plant drinks the exact same nutrients from the dirt every season. Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil dry of that specific plant food, leaving the soil exhausted.
ga: Tsei nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ daa be mli. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi be fɛɛ be kɛjɛ nakai tso niyenii lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops look wilted in the afternoon heat even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: On hot afternoon days, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to conserve water and usually recovers by nightfall.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Dumɔwui fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu nu he, ni bei pii lɛ, amɛhe baajɔ amɛ beni gbɛkɛ shɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to place chemical fertilizer right touching the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain concentrated salts that pull moisture out of plant tissues. Touching the stem directly burns the plant's skin and feeding roots, which can stunt or kill the crop.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ hewolo ni eha shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo egbo.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means your soil is short on nitrogen. The maize plant automatically pulls nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas can capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally feeding your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛku sɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow lots of green leaves but fail to produce peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewooo pepper lɛ?

english: Giving pepper plants too much nitrogen fertilizer encourages them to build stems and leaves instead of flowers. Without flowers, the plant cannot set fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha pepper tsei lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii kɛ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Kɛji fɔfɔi bɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: When temperatures get too hot or rains are too heavy, tomato pollen becomes sticky or dry and fails to pollinate the blossom. Unpollinated flowers naturally drop off the plant.
ga: Be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ waa tsɔ. Tomato pollen lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ebaagbi ni enyɛŋ ekɛ pollen awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do tiny holes and chewed edges appear inside the fresh leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli lɛ je kpo yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai heei lɛ amli.

english: This damage is typically caused by armyworm caterpillars feeding on tender leaves inside the central growing point of the plant, where they hide from daylight heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ dalɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. he ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ he lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot in the ground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the soil for days, the roots drown from a lack of air, allowing rot organisms to invade.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, bɔɔ nii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ atutua.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get full of small holes and brown powder after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni akɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Insects called grain weevils lay invisible eggs in the corn kernels around harvest time. In storage, these eggs hatch into tiny grubs that eat the insides of the grain, leaving behind holes and dusty flour.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed weevils lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa yɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Kɛ́ akɛtoɔ lɛ, nɛkɛ wuji nɛɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. ni yeɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ Ashi bu kɛ ŋmãa ni sũ eyi mli obɔ lɛ yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellowing and curling cassava leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading the Cassava Mosaic Virus. Removing and burning infected plants early prevents the sickness from spreading across your entire farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ cassava mosaic hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra kɛ shãa Enɛ baatsi hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my pepper fruits turning black and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ ashishigbɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black rot on pepper fruits, known as blossom-end rot, happens when the crop does not get enough calcium. Irregular watering causes this because plant roots need steady soil moisture to draw calcium from the ground into the fruit.
ga: Ale ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ aduawai anɔ lɛ hu akɛ blossom end ŋmɔtɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ kɛ enɛ baa ejaakɛ tso shishifãi lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ koni ekɛgbala calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize stalks fall over so easily whenever a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over, or lodge, when they are planted too close together or planted too shallowly in the soil. Giving your maize proper spacing and mounding soil around the base strengthens the roots so they can withstand strong wind.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ nɔ. Abɛi kɛ sũ ni abua naa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa. Shishitoo ko baawo shishifãi lɛ ahe hewalɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures become too hot or when they do not get water consistently. High heat stresses the plant, causing it to abort flowers to conserve energy for survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ amɛ nu daa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ fɔfɔii akpa nitsumɔ koni amɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Leaving larger canopy trees or planting plantains provides shade and retains moisture, protecting young cocoa from getting scorched and dying.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ ni oooshi loo tsei bibii ni ooodu lɛ baaha hulutsoo be aba ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa kɛ gbele he.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil lacks nutrients before I plant my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ dani madu tsei?

english: If previous crops grew slowly, had pale or yellowing leaves, or yielded small fruits, your soil is likely low in nutrients. Looking at natural weed growth can also give clues, but applying organic manure generally rebuilds soil strength.
ga: Kɛji tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ da fiofio Eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ loo ewoɔ aduawai bibii Ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ bɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daraa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ole nɔ ko. Shi yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cowpea and maize together in the same field, and will it help my crops grow better?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ? Ni ani ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, intercropping cowpea with maize is beneficial. Cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that nourishes the nitrogen-hungry maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ he. Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa ni nitrogen yeɔ amɛ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to local conditions and possess strong root systems. They absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than young crops, which is why clearing weeds early gives your crops a fair chance to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into powder and get full of small holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ powder ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani ebaayi obɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: Stored maize turns to powder because small insects called grain weevils eat through the seeds. Drying your grain thoroughly before storage and using airtight containers or approved storage powders prevents insect damage.
ga: Abele ni ato lɛ tsɔɔ powda ejaakɛ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmaa ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni agbiɔ dani akɛtoɔ Ni akɛ tsɛnsi ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛtoɔ he lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni kooloi akafite nii.

english: Why do some of my planted yam setts rot in the ground instead of sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ ekomɛi miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam setts rot in the ground when the soil is overly wet and waterlogged, or if the setts had pre-existing rot or pest damage before planting. Planting healthy setts in well-drained mounds prevents water from collecting and rotting the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ jwɛi lɛ miifite loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite dani adu. Kɛ́ adu hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ gɔji ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi nu naa koni ekabua bulb lɛ naa ni efiteɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Leaving or planting shade trees acts like a natural umbrella, keeping the soil moist and protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle sunlight.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ ni ashiɔ loo aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy for growing big tubers beneath the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the wet soil, preventing leafy fungal diseases and letting the leaves catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa baai lɛ anɔ lɛ naa ni oha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni abaanyɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food responsible for green growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help restore the leaves to a healthy green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni jɛɔ tsei amli ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii daa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help my farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown near maize, they release this nutrient into the dirt, naturally feeding the maize plants without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa Amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé ŋmãa kroko kɛfata he.

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass (mulching) blocks the harsh sunlight from evaporating soil moisture quickly. It keeps the soil cool and soft while preventing weed seeds from getting enough light to sprout.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya oya. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni efeɔ bɔdɔɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ hu aná la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why should I plant cassava stem cuttings at an angle instead of pushing them straight down or laying them flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi yucca tsei lɛ aniji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni matsi amɛ kɛya shi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ? Aloo okɛma shi shiŋŋ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slanted angle encourages roots to spread deep into the soil for stability and moisture, making it easier to harvest tubers later compared to laying them flat.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli fe bɔ ni akɛ amɛ fɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell. Seeds planted too early will sprout but may wither and die in dry dirt before the main rainy season reliably begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when extreme daytime heat stresses the plant or when water levels fluctuate too sharply between dry and wet spells, preventing proper pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. aloo be mli ni nu lɛ mli shwereɔ oya yɛ be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi kɛ be ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ teŋ. Enɛ haa anyɛɛɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes the green leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly into tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni haa baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni efeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids hiding underneath leaves to drink plant sap, or by viruses carried into the plant by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛyaa tsei amli lɛ nɔ

english: Why do I need to cut away the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant nutrients away from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree grows large, healthy bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ yibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ baaná dumɔwui wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide large leaves that shade the young cocoa plants, protecting them and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa is strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni oha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants turn yellow starting from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil or the roots are soaked in too much water, preventing the plant from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ ebote nu mli tsɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: Why does my land give me smaller crop yields every year even though I clear and weed it regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mifoɔ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi daa moŋ.

english: Crops remove nutrients from the soil every season. If you do not add manure, fertilizer, or rotate crops, the soil becomes exhausted, leading to smaller yields regardless of how clean the farm is.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeee lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite, ni no baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse ha.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are planted too close together, cassava puts all its energy into growing stem and leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures become too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when insects fail to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl upward and stop growing proper fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miihoso ni ekpa aduawai ni sa lɛ adalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do cabbage plants sometimes fail to form tight, hard heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, kaabɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ afee yitsei ni mli wa ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages need cool weather, plenty of water, and steady nutrients to form tight heads. High heat or irregular watering causes them to produce loose leaves instead of a solid head.
ga: Kaabaji he miihia kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ, nu babaoo, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa koni eyitsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni bulb lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam rot in the soil is caused by poor soil drainage that keeps water standing around the roots, allowing fungal diseases and tiny worms called nematodes to attack the tubers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa ji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni haa nu hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than my crops after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, native plants naturally adapted to the local climate and soil, allowing them to steal rainwater and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know the best time to sow my seeds once the early rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady and moisten the soil deeply over several days, so seeds do not sprout and then dry up if the rains pause for a long period.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ daa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i gbii babaoo. Enɛ baatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do grasscutters keep coming onto my field to destroy my cassava and sugarcane?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ mi-cassava kɛ mi-sugarcane ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grasscutters are attracted to sweet, starchy crops like cassava tubers and sugarcane stalks because they provide quick energy and water. Planting tall border crops or erecting mesh fencing can deter them from entering your main farm plot.
ga: Mɛi ni shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ sumɔɔ tsei ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ starch tamɔ ŋmei shishifãi kɛ ŋmei tsei. Ejaakɛ ehaa hewalɛ kɛ nu oya. Gɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ooodu loo trellis ni oootswa lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛkabote oŋmɔ titri lɛ mli.

english: Why does wild grass grow back so much faster than my crops after I weed my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Wild grasses have deep root systems and seeds that can sleep in the soil for years waiting for rain. They are naturally tougher than cultivated crops and quickly steal nutrients if not removed early.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo, ni amɛmiimɛ nugbɔ. Amɛhe wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe tsei ni ama shi lɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: Why do I have to travel to clear new land far away from the village just to get a good maize yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ofã gbɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ hee ni kɛ akrowa lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ nɔ koni onine ashɛ ŋmãa kpakpa nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the earth every season. When land is farmed repeatedly without rest or fertilizing, the soil gets exhausted, forcing farmers to look for fertile bushland further away.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛ́ atsu shikpɔŋ nɔ nii shii abɔ ni hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ni no haa okwaafoi lɛ taoɔ koo mli shikpɔŋ ni baa nii babaoo yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dried leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, acts like a shade blanket. It keeps the ground cool, preserves moisture during hot days, and prevents weed seeds from getting sunlight to grow.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛtsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli ni ehaaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akashɛ hulu la he koni amɛdara

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is too wet and the roots cannot breathe, or that heavy rain has washed essential nitrogen out of the soil away from the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ nitrogen ni he hiaa waa lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehe ejɛ tsei shishifãi ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before setting fruit when the heat gets strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ yibii beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: Hot temperatures and dry winds put stress on pepper plants. To protect themselves from drying out, they drop their flowers to save water until cooler weather returns.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he No hewɔ lɛ amɛjieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my plantain suckers too close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When planted too close, plantains fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin stems, produce small bunches, and fall over easily in windstorms.
ga: Kɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ Amɛfeɔ ekãa ni amɛkɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii bibii ni egbeeɔ shi oya kɛji ahum tswa lɛ

english: Why do seeds I saved from last year's harvest produce smaller crops than new seeds bought from the agricultural store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii bibii fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli shwapoi amli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specifically bred for high performance in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special traits, resulting in weaker growth and smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ baa shi ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: Can I grow cassava and maize together on the same piece of land without harming my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mifiteee miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, cassava and maize work well together. Maize grows fast and is harvested early, while cassava grows slower and takes over the extra space after the maize is harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he kroko yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What crops can I grow on my farm to easily feed farm animals like grasscutters and rabbits?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni manyɛ mahã ŋmɔ mli kooloi tamɔ jwɛi ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmeii niyenii yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ?

english: Elephant grass, sugarcane, maize stalks, and sweet potato vines are easy to grow and provide rich forage that grasscutters and rabbits love to eat.
ga: Shɔji jwɛi, ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmãa tsei kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ waaa ni amɛhaa niyenii babaoo ni jwɛi ŋmɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛye.

english: Why should I put my harvested produce on a rack after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi aduawai kɛ aduawai ni mikpa lɛ awo shĩa lɛ nɔ beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Placing your harvested produce on a rack allows it to sit elevated so that over a month or two, it dries completely and safely before you put it in bags or take it to sell.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ okpamɔ lɛ wo adeka lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa anyɛɔ awoɔ nɔ koni egbi ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe nyɔŋ kome loo enyɔ dani okɛwo baagi mli loo ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: How long do I need to leave my harvested crops on the drying rack?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi mikpamɔ lɛ yɛ tsɔne ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ nɔ?

english: You should leave your produce on the drying rack for about one to two months until you see that it is perfectly dry.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi o-fruits kɛ vegetables lɛ yɛ gril lɛ nɔ nyɔji kome kɛyashi enyɔ kɛyashi obaana akɛ amɛgbi kwraa.

english: How do I know when my crops on the drying rack are ready to be taken down?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ grid lɛ nɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie?

english: After waiting for one or two months, you will visually observe that the produce has become perfectly dry, indicating it is time to take it down.
ga: Beni omɛ aaafee nyɔji kome loo enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ Obaana kɛ ohiɛ akɛ aduawai kɛ aduawai lɛ egbi kwraa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛya.

english: What should I do with my crops once they are fully dried on the rack?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji amɛgbi yɛ adeka lɛ nɔ?

english: Once your produce is perfectly dry, you can take it down from the rack and either put it into bags for storage or take it somewhere to sell.
ga: Beni onibii lɛ egbi kwraa. Obaanyɛ ojie kɛjɛ adeka lɛ nɔ ni okɛwo kotoku mli ni okɛto loo ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he.

english: Can I bag my harvested produce immediately after taking it from the field?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo minibii ni mikpa lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, you should first place your produce on a rack for one to two months so it can dry perfectly before you put it into a bag.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ oshi onibii lɛ yɛ shĩa lɛ nɔ nyɔji kome kɛyashi enyɔ koni egbi kwraa dani okɛwo kotoku lɛ mli.

english: Is it safe to take my produce straight to the market right after picking it?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ minibii lɛ baaya jara nɔ tɛ̃ɛ beni mikpa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is better to place your produce on a rack first and wait one or two months until it is perfectly dry before taking it somewhere to sell.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ o-fruits kɛ vegetables lɛ awo shĩa lɛ nɔ ni omɛ nyɔŋ kome loo enyɔ kɛyashi amɛbaagbi kwraa dani okɛ amɛ ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ he ko.

english: What is the proper procedure for drying my crops during this harvest season?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbiɔ miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kpamɔɔ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Place the produce you harvest on a drying rack, wait one to two months for it to become perfectly dry, and then take it down to bag or sell.
ga: Okɛ okpamɔ lɛ awo tsɔne lɛ nɔ. Mɛɛ nyɔji kome kɛyashi enyɔ ni egbi kwraa. Kɛkɛ lɛ, akɛwoɔ kotoku mli loo ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: What happens if I leave my crops on the rack for a month or two?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ shĩa lɛ mli nyɔŋ kome loo enyɔ?

english: Leaving your crops on the rack for one or two months allows them time to dry completely so they are ready for market or bagging.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ adeka lɛ nɔ nyɔŋ kome loo enyɔ lɛ, ehaa enáa be ni egbiɔ kwraa, ni efee klalo akɛ abaawo jarayeli loo awo kotoku mli.

english: Where is the best place to keep my harvested produce so it doesn't spoil before sale?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mikɛ minibii lɛ ato koni ekafite dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: You can place your harvested produce on a drying rack where it can sit safely for a month or two until it dries completely.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ okpamɔ lɛ awo tsɔne ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ nɔ, he ni ebaanyɛ eta shi shweshweeshwe nyɔŋ kome loo enyɔ kɛyashi ebaagbi kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I sell my produce in the first month right after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihɔ̃ɔ minibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Waiting one to two months while your produce rests on a drying rack ensures it becomes perfectly dry, which prepares it properly for bagging and selling.
ga: Mɛɛ nyɔji kome kɛyashi enyɔ be mli ni onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ ta tsɔne lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni okwɛ koni egbi kwraa. Enɛ saa amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛha baagi mliwoo kɛ jarayeli.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow first, the plant is lacking nitrogen, which is its main growing food. The maize plant moves the nitrogen it has left from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the new leaves at the top.
ga: Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very leafy and tall but produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai kakadaji ni kɛlɛ shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen from chemical fertilizers or rich animal dung without enough potassium, the plant spends all its energy building stems and green leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots below.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ no lɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛdu tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ toɔ sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why am I seeing small ragged holes and dark dirt inside the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides deep inside the heart of the maize shoot during the daytime, chewing on the young folded leaves before they unfurl.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ baai bibii ni afolɔ mli lɛ ni oooye dani ojie amɛ kpo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and dry up during the hot afternoon even when the ground is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: This is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a sickness in the soil that clogs the tiny water pipes inside the tomato stem, preventing water from traveling up to the leaves no matter how wet the soil is.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ nu paipii bibii anaa Tomato tso lɛ mli Enɛ haaa nu aya ŋwɛi kɛya baai lɛ anɔ, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni sũ lɛ mli edɔ ha.

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden stakes to climb on to give me big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ? Kwɔ ni okɛ yitso agbo aha mi?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to manufacture food. Staking lifts the vine high so the leaves can catch maximum sunlight, producing more energy to feed and swell the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Staking baaha wain tso lɛ aya hiɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛduɔ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts together with my maize make the maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ duɔ ŋmãa lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ mli waa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has small nodes on their roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural food in the soil that nearby maize plants can feed on.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni eyɛ nodes bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ sũ mli ni ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from stress like severe heat, lack of water, or soil that is too dry, choosing to save their energy to stay alive rather than produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ. Amɛhalaa akɛ amɛbaato hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce fruit when I do not clear the old stems away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani midumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ? Akɛni minyɛɛɛ majie tso momo lɛ kɛjɛ mihe hewɔ lɛ?

english: Old plantain stems and extra suckers continuously suck away water and food from the mother plant. Removing extra suckers leaves all the soil nourishment for one main plant to flower and produce heavy bunches quickly.
ga: Plantain tso lɛ shishifãi momo kɛ eshishifãi krokomɛi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri kome lɛ aná niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ, ni ebaafɔ̃ yɛ kui amli oya.

english: Why do my crops often die if I plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, midumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain only wet the surface soil, and a hot dry spell usually follows. Young seeds germinate from the initial wetness but their tender roots dry out and die before the real continuous rainy season begins.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ pɛ. ni bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni mli edɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui bibii kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shishijee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. Shi shishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani anɔkwa nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yaa nɔ lɛ baaje shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big shade trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and hot wind. Leaving bigger trees creates a cool environment and keeps moisture in the soil, giving young cocoa the shelter it needs to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni eda lɛ agbele mli lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa he ko ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi.

english: When crops do not get enough water, their leaves start to curl, turn yellow, or look droopy during the hottest part of the day. If you push your finger two inches into the soil and it feels completely dry, your crops need watering immediately.
