ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. tsɔ ŋmɔŋ Loo efee tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ onine tsi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli inchii enyɔ ni enu he akɛ egbi kwraa. Ehe miihia ni okɛ nu awo onibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves often happen when crops get too much water, which drowns the roots and prevents them from breathing. It can also mean the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen. Letting the soil dry slightly between waterings helps solve this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ ná nu babaoo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛmu. Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ ni egbi fioo yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsuɔ ​​naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: What happens to my crops when water sits on the farm field for too long after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Standing water blocks air from reaching the crop roots underground. Without oxygen, the roots begin to rot, which stops the crop from absorbing food and can eventually kill the plant.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aŋɔ niyenii, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbe tso lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to local soils, so they quickly grab water and nutrients faster than farmed crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing food and sunlight from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛhi kɛha he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ni oootsi ohe mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Does leaving thick bush and weeds around my plot really affect my final harvest?
ga: ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ Ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ saa mi naagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, thick weeds compete directly with your crops for light, water, and soil nutrients. They also hide farm pests and diseases that can spread to your crops and lower your overall yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Amɛkɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã onibii amli lɛ hu teeɔ. ni okɛ nitsumɔ fɛɛ ni otsuɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: What is the best way to prepare overgrown land before I put my seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa he ko ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine dani aduɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Clear the bush completely, remove large roots, and turn the soil over. This clears away competition from wild plants, loosens the dirt for young roots to grow, and allows sunlight to reach the new seedlings.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ. Gbalamɔ shishifãi wuji lɛ ni otsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie akaŋshii kɛjɛ koo mli tsei amli. Gbalamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ koni shishifãi bibii lɛ akwɛ̃. ni oha hulu la lɛ ashɛ dumɔwui heei lɛ ahe

english: How do I choose the right spot on my farmland for crops that need constant moisture?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala he ni sa kɛha he ni aduɔ tsei ni he hiaa ni nu yɔɔ mli daa lɛ?

english: Look for low-lying areas or places near natural water streams where water drains slowly. Dark soil that feels slightly sticky when wet usually holds moisture much longer than light, sandy soil.
ga: Taomɔ he ko ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo he ko ni bɛŋkɛ adebɔɔ mli faa ko ni hoɔ blɛoo lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni su diŋɔ ni nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ fioo kɛji efɔ. Amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ fe shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni su yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my crops are fully mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Most crops show clear signals like leaves changing color from bright green to brown or yellow, stalks drying out, or fruits reaching full size. Harvesting at full maturity ensures good crop quality and longer shelf life.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo jieɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo, tamɔ baai ni tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse kɛyaa asarasu loo ŋmɔŋ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni gbɛ́ɔ, loo aduawai ni daraa kɛyashɛɔ amɛdalɛ he. Nikpamɔ yɛ be mli ni eda lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops produce flowers but fail to bring out any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers can drop off without making fruit if the crop experiences extreme heat, water stress, or lack of pollination from bees. Keeping the soil moist and avoiding strong chemicals during flowering helps fruits form.
ga: Fɔfɔi baanyɛ agbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. nu mli haomɔ loo pollination ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni mli wa he yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops right at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Planting early allows seeds to use early rains to build strong, deep roots. This strong root system helps the crop grow fast and survive better if dry spells occur later in the season.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ nugbɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni mli kwɔ. Nɛkɛ shishifãi ni mli wa nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛji hɔmɔ ba yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ.

english: How do I know if I am putting too much fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo miiwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Excess fertilizer can burn crop roots and cause the tips and edges of leaves to turn brown or yellow. Using more than the recommended amount damages the plants and wastes money without improving yield.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha baai lɛ ashishigbɛ kɛ amɛhe lɛ atsɔ asarasu loo ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ni fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaafite tso lɛ ni ebaafite shika ni okɛ yibiiwoo lɛ eyaaa hiɛ.

english: Why do different crops need different types of fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi ahe hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Different plants require different nutrients to produce well; for example, leafy crops need more nitrogen to grow leaves, while flowering and fruiting crops need phosphorus and potassium to produce strong fruit and grains.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi biɔ niyenii srɔtoi koni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ he miihia amɛ nitrogen babaoo koni amɛbaai lɛ akwɛ̃. Beni tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná phosphorus kɛ potassium koni amɛwo yibii kɛ ŋmaa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can applying too much chemical fertilizer spoil my soil for future seasons?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ afite mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, heavy over-use of chemical fertilizers can make the soil overly acidic and harm beneficial living organisms in the earth, which reduces soil fertility over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee acid tsɔ ni eye wala ni yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ je lɛŋ lɛ awui. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain plants or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from harsh heat and keeping the soil moist until the trees grow stronger.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui loo shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli shade. Buu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi tsei lɛ baawa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, a key food plant leaves need to stay green and make energy. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen away, so adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the maize regain its deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni niyenii titri tsei lɛ baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛha hewalɛ aba. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Fertilizers must dissolve in moisture before plant roots can absorb them. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil leaves concentrated salts directly against roots, which can burn the roots and dry out the crop.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli dani tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ aya shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii agbi.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when there is too much rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain leaves water sitting in the field, it drowns the roots and creates the right environment for water rot fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo lɛ, nu shwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nu lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite amɛ.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that produce leaves along the stem. Raising the vines on stakes lifts leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to build big tubers, while preventing soil-borne diseases from touching the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni woɔ baai yɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Wein tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ baawó tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni enyɛ ená hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ baashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them leaves only the strongest shoot, ensuring the mother plant produces a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ, juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ ajieɔ babaoo lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ woɔ dumɔwui wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot or when water supply changes suddenly. Heat stress causes pollen to dry up, preventing the flower from forming fruit, so the plant drops the flower to save energy.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsake trukaa. Dɔlɛ haa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Ehaa fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ awo yibii No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do groundnut flower stems bend down and push themselves into the ground after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants flower above ground, but the actual nuts grow underground. After pollination, the flower stem grows into a long peg that pushes down into the soil so the seed pods can develop safely hidden from light and heat.
ga: Peanut tsei fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ, shi ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. after pollination Fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifã lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ ŋtayaa kakadaŋŋ ni tsiɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa shweshweeshwe, ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ la kɛ dɔlɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out plant juices, which damages leaf tissue and twists normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ mites loo thrips, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni efiteɔ amɛdalɛ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize leaves have ragged holes and small dark dirt inside the center funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli buji ni etse kɛ muji bibii ni tsuɔ waa lɛ? Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Ragged holes and dark droppings inside the central funnel are classic signs of Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the growing heart of the maize plant during the hot part of the day and eat young leaves.
ga: Buu ni etse kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ diŋ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadii. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii.

english: Why do seeds brought from cold foreign countries struggle to produce good yield when I plant them on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ maji ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops originally from cold or temperate regions are naturally built for low temperatures. When brought to Ghana's tropical climate, the intense heat stresses the plants, causing them to grow poorly, yield less, or wither.
ga: Abɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ hei ni mli ejɔ loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛha hulutsoo be ni baa shi. Kɛ akɛba Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei lɛ adalɛ ni ehiii. Ehaa yibii fioo loo egboɔ

english: Why do local crops like cassava grow so easily here, but crops like apples fail to grow on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni maŋ tsei tamɔ ŋmei lɛ akwɛmɔ waaa yɛ biɛ lɛ? Shi tsei tamɔ apolo nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cassava is naturally adapted to warm, tropical environments like Ghana, so it copes easily with the sun. Apple trees originate from cool climates and need prolonged cold periods to trigger fruit growth, which our local weather cannot provide.
ga: Cassava nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ Ghana, no hewɔ lɛ eŋmɛɔ hulu la gbɛ oya. Apple tsei jɛɔ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ, ni amɛbiɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli ejɔ be kakadaŋŋ koni amɛha amɛyibii lɛ ada. ni wɔ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi nyɛŋ aha.

english: How can I know if a new seed variety will survive the heat on my farm before I buy it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui heei baahi shi yɛ latsaa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli dani mahe amɛ?

english: Look for seeds labeled as 'heat-tolerant' or 'tropicalized,' or ask for local varieties developed specifically for West Africa. These varieties are bred to withstand high temperatures without losing their yield.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui ni aŋmala nɔ akɛ ‘heɔ dɔlɛ’ loo ‘tropical’ loo bi ni aha bo dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee aha Afrika Anaigbɛ pɔtɛɛ. Afɔ nɛkɛ tsei srɔtoi nɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli ni amɛkafite yibiiwoo.

english: Under intense afternoon heat, plants lose water faster through their leaves than their roots can drink from the soil. Leaf curling is the plant's natural shield to reduce its surface area and prevent excessive water loss.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ shishi lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni hoɔ fe nine lɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers during the sunniest months instead of forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yaa nɔ efɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔi ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ

english: When temperatures get too high, crops experience heat stress, which prevents proper pollination. The plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself from dying in the hot weather.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hulutsoo be mli haomɔ. ni tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my sweet pepper fruits developing pale, dry patches on the side facing the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell peppers lɛ mli tse ni egbi yɛ hei srɔtoi yɛ afã ni kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ lɛ?

english: This is crop sunburn, which happens when intense direct sunlight cooks the skin of the fruit. Leaving enough leafy foliage on the plant helps shade the developing fruits from extreme heat.
ga: Enɛ ji hulutsoo ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he okadi. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ha aduawai lɛ ahewolo lɛ shwere. Kɛ́ ashi baai ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow and pale during a long period of bright sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme sunlight and heat can overload the leaves and slow down their ability to process nutrients and make food, causing them to show signs of stress like pale or yellowish leaves.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine kɛ dɔlɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ atsu nii fe nine. ni ehaa nyɛmɔ ni oyɔɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni okɛhooɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ jieɔ haomɔ he okadii, tamɔ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds take so long to germinate or die in the ground when I plant them during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ loo amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High soil temperatures can bake the soil and shock sensitive seeds, preventing them from sprouting or killing the delicate young roots as soon as they try to emerge.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni nuɔ shoofeemɔ he lɛ. Etsiɔ shishifãi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ loo efiteɔ shishifãi bibii kɛji amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ.

english: Why do my carrots stay very small and thin compared to the large carrots sold in big markets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi karɔt lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ mlɛo waa kɛ akɛto karɔt wuji ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jarayeli hei wuji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Carrots naturally prefer cool soils to swell up and store food. In tropical heat, the plant spends most of its energy trying to stay cool rather than developing a thick, sweet root.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, Karɔt sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ. koni ekɛfutu ni ekɛ niyenii ato hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo shishifãi ni mli edɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ amli.

english: Does warm, sticky weather during the night affect how my crops grow?
ga: Ani gbɛkɛ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ he?

english: Yes, plants need cool nights to rest and store the energy they made during the day. When nights stay very warm, crops continue to burn up energy just trying to breathe and cool down, which reduces their overall yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei he miihia gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ koni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ato. Nyɛsɛɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaya nɔ ashã hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ kɛkɛ ni amɛmu ni amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ. Enɛ baaha nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and fall off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees lose moisture rapidly during the dry Harmattan winds. Without shade trees like plantains or leguminous forest trees to break the wind and block harsh sunlight, heat stress forces the cocoa plant to drop its leaves to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo ŋmeii kooi bɛ, ni baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa ni amɛtsi hulu ni naa wa lɛ naa. Dɔlɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a sharp V-shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ mli kɛjɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves in a V-shape indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives plants their green color and fuels growth, so adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer can correct this shortage.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ V lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa amɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloi amli ŋmeii ni egbo loo ŋmeii ni akɛ nitrogen fee lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu nɛkɛ shweremɔ nɛɛ he nii.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the crop harvest is finished and root residues decay, that stored nitrogen enriches the soil naturally for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni shishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ fite. Nitrogen ni ato lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial to spread dry grass and crop leaves around the roots of my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ oookɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai ashwie mi-aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering soil with organic material (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool under hot sunlight, traps ground moisture so plants stay hydrated longer, stops weed growth, and turns into natural manure as it rots.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ekpaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni egboɔ lɛ

english: What is eating ragged holes into the leaves right in the center funnel of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni elaaje yɛ baa ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli?

english: This pattern of damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central growing point (the whorl) to feed on young leaves, and early treatment with recommended sprays or botanical treatments like neem extractions helps suppress them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe yɛ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ (ring) koni amɛye baai bibii. kɛ mra be mli tsamɔ Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli tamɔ neem mli nu lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ atsĩ amɛnaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards, shrinking, and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe, amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites feeding on the sap, or by viruses spread by whiteflies. Applying insecticidal soap or neem oil spray early helps stop these pests from weakening the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ latex lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akagbɔjɔ tso lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in heavy soil for too long, it pushes air out and drowns root tissues, creating ideal conditions for fungal diseases to invade and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Nu lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baatutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with strong wooden Y-shaped props or bamboo stakes helps carry the bunch weight until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ Y loo ŋmei tso ni akɛfee tso lɛ fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ mli tsiimɔ lɛ kɛyashi ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Extreme daytime temperatures and low soil moisture cause flower blossom drop because heat stresses the plant, stopping pollination. Regular watering during flower formation and maintaining light shade helps protect blossoms.
ga: Gbi mli latsaa ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fioo lɛ haa fɔfɔii fɔɔ ejaakɛ latsaa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. ni akpa pollination Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ feɔ lɛ, kɛ hulutsoo ni mli tse ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs daylight to make food. Staking lifts leaves high into the sunlight and off the humid ground, boosting photosynthesis so energy flows down to make larger underground tubers while preventing ground-level leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛhoo. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi yɛ hulu la mli kɛ kpo nɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Ehaa fotosintɛsis yaa hiɛ bɔni afee ni hewalɛ aya shi ni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ baa helai anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Lower cassava leaves naturally turn yellow and drop as the plant gets older so it can focus its energy on growing tubers underground. However, if it happens to very young plants, it usually means the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen or the soil is too dry.
ga: Cassava baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ jwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii lɛ adumɔ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shi, kɛji akɛ enɛ ba tsei bibii waa anɔ lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ egbi tsɔ.

english: Why does my cassava yield very small tubers even though the leaves grow very tall and leafy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe wa waa lɛ?

english: When cassava plants produce lots of leaves but small roots, it usually means the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium. The plant uses all its energy to build green foliage instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni ŋmei tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi shishifãi bibii lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo yɛ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ baai eŋɔli moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots spoil and turn brown just two days after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ miifite ni efee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ ni mikɛfo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava is harvested, the roots react with oxygen in the air and lose their natural defense system, causing rapid spoilage. This is why fresh cassava must be processed quickly into gari or flour to preserve it.
ga: Kɛji akpa ŋmei lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ baafee ekome. kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ ni laajeɔ Ekɛ fitemɔ baa oya Enɛ hewɔ ni esa akɛ afee ŋmei hee oya ni afee lɛ gari loo ashikiŋsha bɔni afee ni ehi shi lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to give good tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni akwɔɔ koni ená ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to manufacture food for the growing underground tuber. Climbing up stakes keeps the leaves spread out toward the light and off the wet ground where they could rot or catch diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Tso lɛ nɔ kwɔɔ haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa la lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi loo hela aba amɛmli lɛ.

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing too much water during high heat. Shrinking their exposed surface area helps the plant hold onto moisture until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite fe nine yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ mli ni hulutsoo baa.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their blossoms before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛyibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when daytime heat becomes too intense or when rainfall is uneven. Heat stress stops the flower from pollinating properly, so the plant sheds the flower instead of producing fruit.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be. Heat haomɔ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and die even when there is plenty of water in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by root rot or fungal wilt. Excess water blocks oxygen from reaching the roots, allowing soil fungi to destroy the root system so it can no longer send water up to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni egbo loo ŋmeii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ trukaa. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, atsuuu nu kɛyaaa baai lɛ ahe dɔŋŋ.

english: Why does planting beans in the same farm with my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and legumes have special roots that grab nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer in the soil. This extra fertilizer nourishes neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees act like infants and burn under harsh, direct sunlight. They need partial shade from larger trees like plantains or timber to keep them cool and hold moisture in the soil during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ abifabii ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo tsei ahe. Enɛ ji koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even if there seems to be plenty of land for all of them to grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ babaoo yɛ ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ moŋ.

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal essential water, light, and nutrients right out of the soil around your crops. This starves your planted crops and leaves them weak, stunted, and vulnerable to pests.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ni ebaaha amɛgbɔjɔ, amɛhe afee shoo, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aye amɛ.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and soft during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in high humidity and damp shade. Clearing weeds, pruning excess shade branches, and frequently harvesting mature pods allows air to circulate and reduces the moisture the fungus needs to spread.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli. weeding Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo tsɔ ni amɛbuaa ŋmeii ni eda kwraa lɛ anaa shii abɔ Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ aba shi.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from heat stress, lack of water, or lack of pollination by tiny insects called midges. Keeping partial shade trees on your farm maintains cool temperatures and moisture, helping midges survive and pollinate your trees.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo ŋmeii bibii ni haaa amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hewɔ. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo fã ko yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be ahi shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa dwarf lɛ ni ehiɔ shi ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing in a V-shape starting from the tip of lower leaves means your maize lacks nitrogen fertilizer. Maize needs nitrogen to grow green and healthy, so applying NPK or urea fertilizer early in the growth stage will fix this.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ V ni jɛɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ o-ŋmã lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo urea atsu nii mra. Yɛ dalɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, abaatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize look chewed up with small powdery holes inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ashɛre ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Powda lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing whorl of the plant. Applying recommended insecticides or neem extract directly into the central funnel early in the morning kills the pest before it destroys the plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei ni miida lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ wo ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛkpãtã tso lɛ hiɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in waterlogged soil where water sits for too long. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why do my plantain trees snap and fall over when the fruit bunch gets big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and fibrous stems that cannot easily support heavy fruit bunches during strong winds. Propping up the stem with a strong bamboo or wooden fork right under the fruit cluster prevents the tree from falling.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ mlɛo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tso ni wa loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei tsu nii ni akɛfi tso lɛ shishi yɛ aduawai akui lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: How can I stop my harvested seed yams from sprouting too early in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa sweet potato dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃ oya tsɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Seed yams sprout early when kept in warm, dark, and damp conditions. Storing them on wooden racks in a cool, well-ventilated traditional yam barn keeps them dry and delays sprouting until planting time.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ amɛ ato tsei ahe yɛ blema sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha amɛgbi ni ebaaha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ asɛɛ afo kɛyashi be ni abaadu lɛ baashɛ.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually a viral disease transmitted by tiny whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies with insecticidal soap or neem oil and removing infected plants prevents the virus from spreading to healthy tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni shwieɔ tomato mli lɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ akudɔ ŋmeii yɛji. Ni tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tomatoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers during very hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed flowers under extreme heat and drought to conserve water and protect themselves. Mulching around the base of the plant with dry grass helps hold soil moisture and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ shishi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my farm help the maize I plant in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ŋmãa ni midu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the cowpea plant dies and decays in the soil, it releases natural nitrogen fertilizer that nourishes the next crop planted on that land.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji cowpea tsei gboi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaajie nitrogen ŋmɔshi nii kɛjɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops lack nitrogen—which acts like food for plants—or that heavy rains have logged the soil with too much water. Applying a balanced fertilizer or improving field drainage helps the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli, ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ tso niyenii. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why aren't my maize seeds coming up after I buried them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too deeply, they run out of stored energy before their young shoots can break through the surface to reach sunlight, causing them to die beneath the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ tsɔ Hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baa shi dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the field, resulting in poorer yields over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily scorch under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide wide leaves that shade and protect the young cocoa while preserving moisture in the soil.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ haa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ ehe, yɛ be mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up toward the sunshine so they can gather energy for larger underground tubers, while also keeping the leaves off wet soil where fungal diseases easily spread.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli koni ebua hewalɛ naa kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ he.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there seems to be plenty of space on the farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji etamɔ nɔ ni he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with crops by stealing water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Even if space looks adequate, weeds starve nearby plants of the vital resources needed for healthy growth.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ akaŋ waa kɛtsɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la, eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni jɛmɛ fa bɔ ni sa moŋ Shi jwɛi hu haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ náa nibii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains cause standing water around the roots, the soil becomes waterlogged, choking the roots and causing them to decay underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing tall and thin without bringing out many flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ mlɛo shi ewooo fɔfɔi babaoo lɛ?

english: Tomato plants stretch upward and become tall and spindly when they do not receive enough direct sunlight. They use all their energy reaching for light instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛdara ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtaoɔ la moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai.

english: Why are all the flowers falling off my pepper plants before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, dry conditions, or poor soil nutrients. Shedding flowers is the plant's natural way of saving energy to survive stress.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shihilɛi ni mli egbi, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ he. Fɔfɔi ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ haomɔ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my bean plants droop in the afternoon heat even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can absorb it from the soil. The leaves temporarily droop to conserve moisture until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi gbɛkɛ mli hulutsoo baa.

english: Why does the soil on my farm keep getting hard and difficult to dig after a few farming seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli wa ni ewa akɛ aaafo mli yɛ okwaayeli bei fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil becomes hard when organic matter is depleted and the ground is overworked or left bare under the heavy sun. Using practices like mulching, adding manure, and leaving crop residues on the field keeps the soil soft, moist, and healthy over the years.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waɔ kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli efo. ni atsuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii fe nine loo ashiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Nifeemɔi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli.

english: How do my daily farming choices affect the long-term quality of my farmland?
ga: Te okwaayeli ni mihalaa daa gbi lɛ saa miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Good soil practices act like an investment in your land. When you protect your soil from over-tilling and erosion, it retains its richness and stays loose, ensuring your farm remains productive for years without deteriorating.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nifeemɔi kpakpai tamɔ shika ni okɛwoɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji obu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaya nɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaafee nɔ ni shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa oŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii afii babaoo ni efiteee.

english: What common farming practices should I avoid if I want my soil to stay fertile?
ga: Mɛɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni afɔɔ feemɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ he kɛji miisumɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: You should avoid burning leftover stalks and leaves after harvest, constantly plowing too deep, and leaving soil exposed to heavy rains and intense heat. These habits wash away nutrients and turn soft topsoil into hard dirt.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa ŋmeii kɛ baai ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ ashãa. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ tsɔ ni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Sui nɛɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ feɔ sũ ni wa.

english: What basic steps should I follow to consistently get a good harvest from my corn?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titri esa akɛ mafee koni maná yibii kpakpai kɛjɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli be fɛɛ be?

english: To get high corn yields consistently, plant certified seeds at the start of the rains, keep proper spacing between plants, weed early before weeds steal nutrients, and apply fertilizer at the right stages of growth.
ga: Bɔni afee ni oná ŋmãa ni fa babaoo be fɛɛ be lɛ, Dumɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Ha tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa ahi shi. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Dani jwɛi lɛ baaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii yɛ be ni sa ni sa mli

english: Why do some farmers get high corn yields every season while my harvest changes so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi naa ŋmãa babaoo daa afi yɛ be mli ni mikpamɔi lɛ srɔtoi babaoo lɛ?

english: Farmers with stable, high yields usually follow consistent land preparation, pest management, and soil fertility practices every year rather than changing methods frequently or delaying farm tasks.
ga: Okwaafoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛnyiɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ nifeemɔi asɛɛ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔmɔ nii daa afi Yɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsakeɔ shii abɔ loo ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ ni akɛbaagbe naa lɛ najiaŋ

english: How does early weeding affect how well my corn grows?
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Te enaa ŋmãa dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeding early gives young corn plants full access to soil nutrients, water, and sunlight without competing against aggressive weeds, allowing the corn to grow thick stalks and large, healthy cobs.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ naa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ fɛɛ. ni ekɛ jwɛi ni baa shi lɛ yeee akaŋ Ehaa ŋmãa lɛ naa ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Is it possible for me to plant and harvest groundnuts twice in a single year in Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ni makpa ŋmei shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Yes, because groundnuts mature quickly in about three to four months, farmers in regions with two rainy seasons can plant a first crop during the main rains and a second crop during the minor rains.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmeii daa oya yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ loo ejwɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ kpokpai ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ bei enyɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ adu klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli, ni amɛdu nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be fioo lɛ mli.

english: Why are groundnuts considered good for the soil when planted before other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ ŋmei akɛ ehi kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ́ adu dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means they capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the land, leaving fertilizing nutrients behind for crops like corn planted next.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛshiɔ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What special field care do groundnuts need when they start flowering?
ga: Ani ŋmeii biɔ ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko kɛji amɛbɔi fɔfɔi?

english: When groundnuts flower, the stems bend down and push pegs into the soil to form nuts underground. Keeping the soil loose and weed-free around the base of the plant helps these pegs enter the ground easily.
ga: Beni ŋmeii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ lɛ Akɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni akɛ ŋmeii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jwɛi bɛ nɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo.

english: How do I know if my land is ready and healthy enough before I increase my farm size?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo ni eyɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa dani mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli babaoo?

english: Your land is ready for scaling up if your current soil stays loose, retains moisture, and consistently supports strong crop growth without requiring double the effort just to keep plants alive.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha shweremɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ nɔ amrɔ nɛɛ mli etse lolo. Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni oye obua tsei lɛ adalɛ koni amɛhe awa ni amɛya nɔ daa Ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni ji shii enyɔ awo mli koni tso lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why is cocoa grown mostly in the Western and Ashanti regions instead of the drier Northern parts of Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ kookoo yɛ Anaigbɛ kɛ Ashanti kpokpai lɛ anɔ titri lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e ji kpokpa nɛ hɛ mi ngɛ Ghana yiti je.

english: Cocoa trees need heavy rain, rich forest soils, and high humidity to produce pods, which are naturally found in southern regions like Western and Ashanti. The Northern region is drier with longer dry seasons, making it better suited for grains and legumes rather than cocoa.
ga: Nugbɔ ni naa wa he miihia koko tsei. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ baa nii. kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo koni ekɛfee pods Anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ anaigbɛ hei tamɔ Anaigbɛ kɛ Ashanti. Kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ egbiɔ ni eyɛ hulutsoo be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Enɛ haa ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmaa kɛ ŋmeii fe kookoo.

english: Why are grains like millet and sorghum grown more in Northern Ghana than crops like cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ ŋmaa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa babaoo yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo lɛ?

english: Millet and sorghum have deep root systems and low water requirements, allowing them to survive in drier weather and sandy soils typical of Northern Ghana, where cocoa would dry up and die.
ga: Sorghum kɛ sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni nu ni he hiaa lɛ faaa. Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni ji Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ nɔ. Kookoo lɛ baagbi ni ebaagbo.

english: Why do cocoa trees drop their flowers without producing pods when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni bɛ ŋmeii kɛji hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees experience extreme sun and heat stress, they shed their flowers to save water and energy so the tree itself can survive the dry period.
ga: Kɛ́ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ hao kookoo tsei lɛ, Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide essential shade and shade moisture, protecting young cocoa during its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli

english: Why should I trim off extra branches and side shoots from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ niji kɛ esɛɛ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Trimming opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and airflow can reach the inner branches. This prevents fungal diseases like black pod and helps the tree send its energy into growing big pods.
ga: Edging gbeleɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ ashɛ tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Koni akɛtsi fungal helai tamɔ black pods naa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ amaje koni ekɛfee pods wuji.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stop growing during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Maize needs water to pull nitrogen and other nutrients out of the soil. When dry spells occur, the leaves turn yellow because the plant cannot absorb the food it needs to stay green.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛgbala nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be ko ba. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why does cassava survive hot and dry weather better than my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ jogbaŋŋ fe mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its top leaves during dry periods to stop losing water, relying on its deep root system and stored energy in underground tubers until rains return.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei shwieɔ eŋwɛi baai lɛ anɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni shwieɔ lɛ akpa. Ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ nɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yams need soft, loose soil to expand their tubers downward. Mounds give roots room to grow large while allowing extra rainwater to drain away so the tubers do not rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato koni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ gɔji haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛ koni amɛdara. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha nugbɔ nu lɛ atsɔ mli koni bulb lɛ akafite.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull natural nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa.

english: Why does adding animal manure to my farm help my crops during dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔ mli kooloi ashishifãi ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts like a sponge in the soil, holding onto moisture longer so plant roots can still drink water during dry spells while slowly releasing plant nutrients.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiɛɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu nu lolo yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ, ejieɔ tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green. Heavy rains can also wash this food deep into the ground where small roots cannot reach it yet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ aho niyenii nɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ shishifãi bibii amli. Lolo lɛ enyɛɛɛ eshɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin even when the stems and leaves grow tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants get too much rich food or manure in the soil, they spend all their energy growing top foliage instead of sending energy down to expand the underground tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ niyenii loo ŋmei babaoo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami kɛ yaa si konɛ e ha nɛ tsɔwi ɔmɛ nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ nɛ bli.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves get scorched and turn brown during the bright dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves lose water quickly under full sunlight. Without shade trees like plantains or forest trees to block the direct sun, the heat dries out the leaves faster than the roots can draw water from the soil.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Kɛji tsei komɛi bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo aba, tamɔ tsei bibii loo koo mli tsei ni baatsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa lɛ, Dɔlɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ gĩɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my pepper plants are drooping because of afternoon sun or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu lɛ hewɔ loo hela hewɔ?

english: If a crop is drooping simply from hot sun, its leaves will recover and stand up straight in the cool evening. If the leaves stay limp overnight, a soil disease or root pest is blocking water flow inside the plant.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ hewɔ lɛ Ebaai lɛ he baa shi ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsi nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why should I cut Elephant grass to feed my livestock while it is short instead of waiting for it to grow very tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afo shwuɔ jwɛi koni akɛha kooloi niyenii yɛ be mli ni jwɛi lɛ yɛ kuku moŋ fe ni ooomɛ ni etsɔ shɔŋŋ babaoo?

english: Young grass is soft, easy to digest, and rich in nutrients that help animals grow or give milk. Once it grows very tall, the stems turn hard and woody, losing most of their food value and making it tough for animals to eat.
ga: Jwɛi bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, ehiɛɔ mli oya, ni eyɛ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni amɛdaraa loo amɛhaa nu. Kɛ eda waa lɛ Tso lɛ wa ni eyɛ tso. Ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ laajeɔ ni ehaa ewaa ahaa kooloi akɛ amɛaaye nii

english: Why do caterpillars hide deep inside the leaves of my young maize plants during the daytime?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm crawl into the tight leaf funnel to hide from hot sun, heavy rain, and birds, while safely feeding on the softest growing parts of the crop.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ baai ni mli wa lɛ amli koni amɛyatee amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ okpoi ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards like cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites sucking plant juices, or by a virus transmitted by those insects that disrupts how the leaves expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni tsiɔ baai lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ naa lɛ nɔ

english: Why do planting cowpeas on my plot make the soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the plant dies, that stored food remains in the earth to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruits during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat makes the pollen inside tomato blossoms dry up, so the flowers cannot set seeds. When pollination fails, the plant sheds the useless flowers to save its strength.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui. Kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tso lɛ baashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa lɛ ashwie koni ekɛbu ehewalɛ he.

english: Why do yam tubers rot underground when water sits on my field after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need air in the soil to stay alive and healthy. When flooded water blocks oxygen from entering the soil, the tubers suffocate, allowing rot fungi to enter and destroy them.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ nu lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ, atsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ naa koni ekabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Miyitso nyɛɛɛ amu. Aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ akpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize often mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients too deep for the roots to reach. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer or compost helps the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe kɛtee shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the sap, or by a virus carried by those insects. Using neem oil spray or safe insecticides early on helps protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Neem mu ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: What causes the flowers on my tomato plants to drop off before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni miiha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when water is irregular, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Giving plants consistent water and shade during peak heat helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa tsei yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during harmattan as a defense mechanism to save water. The dry winds pull moisture from the leaves rapidly, so shedding them prevents the main stem and roots from drying out completely.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ harmatta beaŋ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ atswa amɛ kɛtee lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ shishifãi titri lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water suffocates the roots by blocking oxygen in the soil. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield when I plant on the same piece of land year after year without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Continuous planting drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving nature time to replenish them. Leaving the land to rest or rotating with crops like beans restores natural soil fertility.
ga: Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa adebɔɔ be ni ekɛ nakai niyenii lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ koni ekɛjɔɔ ehe loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I build back the fertility of my land after taking it back from someone who farmed it heavily?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ beni miŋɔ kɛjɛ mɔ ko ni tsu okwaayeli waa yɛ nɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can restore exhausted soil by planting leguminous cover crops like cowpeas or mucuna, which fix nitrogen into the soil, and by adding decomposed animal manure before planting main crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmeii loo mucilagina ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ saa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ kooloi aŋmei ni egbo ni akɛwoɔ mli dani aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does burning bush before planting seem to help crops at first, but harm the soil later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei bibii ni ashãa dani aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Shi ani oooye shikpɔŋ lɛ awui yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Burning creates ash that releases quick nutrients for the first crop, but the intense heat destroys organic matter and beneficial soil organisms, leading to poor soil structure and erosion over time.
ga: Shãa haa ashwishwɛ ni jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa oya. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ kpataa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehiii ni shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant plantains next to my newly planted cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛɔ akɛ adu plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sun. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as temporary shade umbrellas, protecting young cocoa plants until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli shade. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall and thin with very small ears when I sow seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni toi lɛ hu ji bibii beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil food. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to form thick stalks and large ears.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli tse kɛ toi wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close to each other so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ mikɛ babaoo awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. This competition makes all the plants grow weak and thin, resulting in much smaller yields than if they had enough space.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baafee bibioo fe kɛji akɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is hungry and lacks an important plant food called nitrogen, or the soil has too much water around the roots. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ebɛ tso niyenii ko ni he hiaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni efeɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat, too little water, or irregular rainfall. When the plant feels stressed, it sheds its flowers to save energy just to stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. nu fioo tsɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee Kɛ́ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ he koni ehi wala mli kɛkɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crop beds with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle midumɔ nii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under the hot sun and stops water from drying out quickly. It also prevents weeds from growing easily and decays into rich plant food over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya Etsiɔ jwɛi hu naa koni ekakwɛ̃ oya ni efite ni etsɔ tsei niyenii ni jara wa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot every season drains all the specific nutrients that crop loves from the soil and allows pests that attack that crop to multiply in the dirt. Planting different crops each season keeps the soil rich and healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ, ebaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I find small holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the tops of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ayitsei amli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The worm hides inside the tight leaves at the center of the stem to eat the tender growing leaf tissues while hiding away from the hot sun and predators.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni eye tso lɛ baa lɛ mli fãji ni miida blɛoo lɛ. be mli ni ekɛ ehe teeɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomatoes turn black and rot before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by irregular watering, which stops the plant from absorbing calcium from the soil while the fruit is forming. Keeping the soil consistently moist throughout the dry days prevents this bottom rot.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ lɛ daa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aŋɔ calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ shishigbɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why should I trim off some of the side branches on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ?

english: If a tomato plant grows too many branches, it wastes its energy making leaves instead of fruit. Removing extra side shoots forces the plant to send its nutrients directly into producing bigger and healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji o-tomato tso lɛ yɛ niji babaoo Ebaafite hewalɛ ni ekɛbaafee baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni etsɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ gbɛ koni ewo tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and yield very little food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee bibioo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and act like food thieves in your farm. They steal the fertilizer, soil water, and sunlight that your main crops need to grow big, leaving your crops weak and hungry.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, shikpɔŋ nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa onibii titrii lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ hu baaye bo.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow instead of staying deep green as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow maize leaves usually mean the crops are hungry for nitrogen or are trapped in waterlogged soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted manure gives the plants the food they need to turn dark green and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo ehiɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I plant three or four maize seeds in one single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds grow in one hole, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This makes them grow thin, weak, and produce tiny cobs. Planting one or two seeds per hole gives each plant enough room to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii. Dumɔwu kome loo enyɔ ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hewalɛ baawo yibii kpakpai.

english: What is eating small ragged holes into the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ he?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide in the growing center of the plant. Spraying approved insecticides early in the morning or late evening when the caterpillars are active stops them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tsei lɛ adalɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi lɛ miitsu nii. Ebaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafite onibii lɛ.

english: How can I store my harvested maize so that weevils do not destroy it before I can sell it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato koni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ akabote mli dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Weevils attack maize that still has moisture. You should dry your maize under the sun until the grains are very hard, then store them in sealed airtight bags (like PICs bags) or treat them with recommended grain storage powder.
ga: Weevils tutuaa ŋmãa ni mli edɔ lolo lɛ. Esa akɛ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli (tamɔ PIC kotoku) mli loo okɛ dumɔwui atomɔ powda ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtoɔ he lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why does rice grow better in flooded or swampy land while my maize rots in water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ ewo muji lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa fiteɔ yɛ nu mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally have hollow stems that carry air down to their roots even when standing in water, which helps them suppress weeds and feed well. Maize roots cannot breathe under water and will drown and rot if flooded.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli ewo muji ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ baa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli kɛ́ amɛdamɔ nu mli po. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni enaa niyenii. Abɛi shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ nu shishi. ni ebaagbee nu mli ni ebaagbo kɛji nu afua lɛ ba.

english: Why do I need to clear and level my swamp field smoothly before planting rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔjie ŋmei hei ni wɔfee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani wɔdu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Leveling your field ensures that water spreads evenly across the entire farm. If the field is uneven, deep water will drown rice plants in low spots while plants on high ground will suffer from dry soil and weed growth.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ ni ooofee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ haa nu lɛ mlijaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛji he lɛ bɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ atsɔ shishi yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my rice to get maximum yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa koni maná yibii babaoo?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains on the plant turn from green to a golden-yellow color. Waiting too long makes the dry grains break easily or drop to the ground, leading to heavy losses.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji omɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ mlijaa oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli. Kɛ́ mɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi, amɛgbala oya loo amɛgbee shikpɔŋ. ni kɛ fitemɔi ni tsii baa

english: Why does my soil produce lower yields now compared to when I cleared the land years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto be mli ni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Every crop you harvest takes nutrients out of the land. Over time, the soil becomes empty and exhausted. You can restore your soil's energy by adding animal manure, compost, or fertilizers, and by rotating crops.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni okpaa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni be shwieɔ mli lɛ, sũ lɛ feɔ efolo ni etɔɔ. Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly and look stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing thieves that steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your main crop. Clearing weeds early in the crop's life keeps all the soil food available for your crop to grow big fast.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni daa oya, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii titrii lɛ. Tsei ni ajieɔ yɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara oya.

english: Will planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize help my farm?
ga: Ani tsina loo ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?
