english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing it. This helps your maize grow better while giving you an extra harvest to sell for money.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ baaye abua ni o-abele lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ebaaha oná yibii krokomɛi ni okɛbaahɔɔ kɛha shika.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to stop burning my bush before planting even though it clears the land faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ kooi anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mɛi akɛ amɛkpa kooi ashãa dani amɛdu, eyɛ mli akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie amɛ oya moŋ?

english: Burning clears the land fast, but the intense heat kills beneficial soil insects and burns away natural organic nutrients. Over time, burning leaves your soil dry and weak, which leads to poorer harvests.
ga: Shãa baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbeɔ sũ mli kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni eshãa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Shãa baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni ehiii kwraa

english: What happens to my soil if I leave cut weeds on the farm to rot instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi jwɛi ni afolɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛgbo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mashã amɛ?

english: Leaving cut weeds on the ground creates a natural blanket called mulch. It keeps the soil cool under hot weather, retains rainwater in the ground, and feeds the soil with rich nutrients as it rots.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Too nugbɔ nu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni okɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo aha shikpɔŋ lɛ be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting rubber trees before I can start harvesting latex to get money?
ga: Kɛ́ wɔdu rɔbɔt tsei wɔgbe naa lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ wɔmɛ dani wɔje latex ni wɔbua naa lɛ shishi koni wɔnine ashɛ shika nɔ?

english: Rubber trees usually require about six to seven years of growth before their trunks become thick enough for tapping. They are a long-term investment that requires patience before bringing in income.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei biɔ ni amɛdara afii enumɔ kɛyashi kpawo dani amɛshishifã lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atswa. Eji shika ni akɛwoɔ nitsumɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni biɔ tsuishitoo dani aná shika.

english: How does planting trees on my farm help protect my land during heavy rainstorms?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Tree roots act like strong nets underground that hold the soil together so heavy rains do not wash away the fertile topsoil. The leaf canopy also reduces the force of rain falling directly on the soil.
ga: Tso shishifãi tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋshɔŋloo ni mli wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieee sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ hu haa hewalɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young tree seedlings wither so quickly during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ oya yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Young tree seedlings have shallow roots that cannot reach deep underground water yet. Without shade or mulching to cover the soil, the intense sun evaporates the surface moisture and causes the seedlings to dry up.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he lolo. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ko bɛ Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or vegetables on the same field where I just planted young rubber trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo aduawai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu rɔbɔt tso nɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, while tree seedlings are small and do not shade the ground, you can grow food crops between the rows for the first two to three years. This gives you food and income while waiting for the trees to grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ tsei bibii lɛ faaa ni amɛhaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po. Shi obaanyɛ odu niyenii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ loo etɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha oná niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni omɛɛɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why does my maize produce very small ears when I plant it underneath big grown trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ toi bibii waa kɛ́ mikɛdu tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Maize needs full sunshine to grow strong and make heavy grain. Large trees block sunlight with their canopy and their roots steal most of the water and nutrients from the soil.
ga: Abɛi he miihia hulu ni fa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa kɛ dumɔwui ni tsii. Tsei wuji kɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Ni tsei ashishifãi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo.

english: Why do some trees drop all their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ahe baa fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a tree's natural defense against heat. Leaves release water into the air, so by dropping them, the tree saves its internal water to survive through dry spells until rains return.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ hebuu. Baai lɛ jieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ashi tsei lɛ ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if my soil is tired and needs a break or a change of crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni majɔɔ mihe loo atsake ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Tired soil turns pale or hard, holds very little water, and causes crops to look weak and yellowish even when rain falls normally. If your harvest drops year after year on the same spot, the soil needs rest or nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ewaa. Ehiɛɔ nu fioo ko pɛ Ni ehaa tsei feɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po. Kɛji okpamɔ lɛ ba shi afi fɛɛ afi yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu he miihia hejɔɔmɔ loo niyenii kpakpai.

english: Is it better for me to plant only one crop on my whole farm or mix different crops together?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome yɛ miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni akɛfutu mli?

english: Mixing crops helps protect you from total failure if pests or bad weather hit one crop type. Combining crops with different root depths and sunlight needs also uses the soil's resources more efficiently.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni okɛfutuɔ nii lɛ baabu ohe kɛjɛ sɛɛkuu kwraa he. Kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi gbohii ná tso pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ hewalɛ Nibii ni aduɔ ni shishifãi srɔtoi kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa lɛ feɔ ekome lɛ hu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. When the soil runs low on nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has from its older lower leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: How does planting cowpeas in my field help make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with natural soil bacteria to take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and its leaves decay, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmei tso ko ni jɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ejie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto eshishifãi amli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni ebaa lɛ egbo. Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is the center leaf of my maize plant turning brown and dying while the outer leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli lɛ?

english: This symptom is called 'deadheart' and is usually caused by stem borer caterpillars that hatch and chew their way inside the stem. By feeding inside, they cut off water and nutrients to the newest leaf growing at the center.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ ‘tsui gbele’ ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni boteɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ he ni amɛfɔ yɛ lɛ ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛtsɔ emli ni amɛboteɔ mli lɛ nɔ Amɛfoɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛyaa baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from underneath the leaf. Their feeding damages the leaf tissue and can pass on plant viruses that stunt leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. Amɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ tso mli helai ni tsiɔ baa lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers during the dry season without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high during the dry season, the heat damages the flower pollen, preventing proper pollination. Because the flower cannot form a seed, the plant sheds the flower to save its remaining water and energy.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Dɔlɛ fiteɔ pollen. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my rice plants produce empty husks with no grains inside if the water dries up while they are flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔtɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ? ni dumɔwui bɛ mli Kɛji nu lɛ gĩ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Rice plants need steady water during flowering to transport nutrients into the developing seeds. Drought during this critical period prevents the plant from filling the husks, leaving empty, lightweight chaff at harvest.
ga: Nu he hiaa omɔ tsei daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya dumɔwui ni miida lɛ aŋɔɔ. Hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ nɛkɛ be ni he hiaa waa nɛɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkawo amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ. Shĩ ŋmãa ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ oshwie. Etsiimɔ waaa kɛji akpa

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their tiny early flowers when the rains are delayed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shiɔ fɔfɔi bibii kɛji nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers as a natural defense mechanism against drought. Without enough water in the soil, the tree cannot support flower development and drops them to conserve moisture for stem and leaf survival.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ he. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye abua fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ ni egbee shi koni ekɛto ŋmɔtɔ he koni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛ baai lɛ ahi shi.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature and ready for harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efolɔɔɔ mli?

english: Cassava typically matures between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to swell and crack from expanding roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa kɛjɛ shishifãi ni mli lɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and stake my yam vines high off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni madu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to manufacture food, which then flows down to build large underground tubers. Staking keeps leaves high in the sun and off damp ground where fungal rot and leaf spot diseases thrive.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, efoɔ kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ hulu lɛ nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni fungus rot kɛ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die if I plant them in an open field without any plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily scorch and lose moisture under full sun. Planting fast-growing plantain trees beside them provides vital shade and humid air until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to endure direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ Tso lɛ masɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ aba kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ.

english: Can I use crushed eggshells from my kitchen to help my crops grow better?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni atswa kɛjɛ shĩa lɛ atsu nii koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, crushed eggshells contain calcium, which strengthens crop roots and stems while preventing problems like fruit blossom end rot in crops like tomatoes and peppers.
ga: Hɛɛ, calcium yɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni atswa lɛ amli. ni haa tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahewalɛ yaa hiɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ naagbai tamɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ anaa.

english: How do I know if my crop soil needs calcium, and how can eggshells help?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-potting sũ lɛ he miihia calcium? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ aye abua?

english: If your crop fruits rot at the bottom or young leaves look twisted, your soil may lack calcium. Adding crushed eggshells provides a steady supply of calcium to rebuild soil strength.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ yibii lɛ miifite yɛ shishi loo baai bibii lɛ miifee tamɔ nɔ ni efite Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ calcium bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni atswa lɛ fata he lɛ, ehaa calcium ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is a compound fertilizer and how does it help my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii? ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: A compound fertilizer is a mixture that combines multiple key plant nutrients—like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium—into single granules to feed your crops a balanced diet.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nibii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium. Ha lɛ akɛ pellet kome koni ekɛ niyenii ni sa aha otsei lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to mix natural materials with store-bought chemical fertilizers?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii baafutu tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Yes, combining natural materials like eggshells with compound fertilizers gives your crops both quick nutrient boosts and long-lasting soil improvement when prepared correctly.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛfutu mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ be kakadaŋŋ kɛji akɛ asaa he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I mix different fertilizer materials together in water before applying them to my land?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi afutu nu mli dani mikɛwo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, blending fertilizers together in water creates a uniform liquid mixture, ensuring every plant gets an equal share of nutrients when you water them.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu mli yɛ nu mli lɛ, ehaa efeɔ nu ni akɛfutuɔ nii. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛji okɛ nu wo amɛmli.

english: Why do some farmers soak their fertilizer in water for a few days before putting it on their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ nu mli gbii fioo komɛi dani amɛkɛwoɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Soaking fertilizer in water breaks down hard particles, dissolving the nutrients into the liquid so the plant roots can drink them up easily without waiting for rain.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo nu mli lɛ, efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa lɛ. shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ nɔ ewoɔ nu mli Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu nu mlɛo ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛmɛ nugbɔ lɛ.

english: How long should I let a homemade liquid fertilizer mixture sit before applying it to my crop field?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mahã mi-shĩa nu ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ ahi shi dani mikɛwo midumɔi lɛ amli?

english: Letting the fertilizer soak in water for about four days gives enough time for the solid particles to fully break down and release their nutrients into the liquid.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwie nu mli aaafee gbii ejwɛ lɛ, ehaa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa lɛ fiteɔ kwraa ni amɛjieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa nu lɛ mli.

english: What actually happens inside a bucket when I leave fertilizer soaked in water for several days?
ga: Mɛni baaba yɛ tanki lɛ mli? Beni ashiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ nu mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Inside the bucket, water breaks open the chemical bonds of the solid particles, turning concentrated minerals into an easily digestible liquid tea for your crop roots.
ga: Yɛ tanki lɛ mli lɛ, nu lɛ gbálaa tsofai ni yɔɔ nibii ni mli wa lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli. Tsɔɔmɔ minerals ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu tii ni anyɛɔ ashɛɔ oya kɛha otso lɛ shishifãi.

english: Why must I make sure fertilizer particles are fully dissolved in water before watering my crops with it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ etsɔ nu lɛ mli kwraa dani mikɛ nu awo mitsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Undissolved fertilizer lumps can sink into the soil and burn tender roots with concentrated chemicals. Fully dissolving the particles ensures safe, even feeding.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli lɛ amli fãi baanyɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ tsofai ni mli wa ashã shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Nibii bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kwraa lɛ haa shweshweeshwe shihilɛ baa. Niyenii po

english: Why do crops absorb food faster when I give them liquid fertilizer instead of dry fertilizer granules?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya kɛ́ mikɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ha amɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni ji ŋmeii lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Plant roots can only drink nutrients that are dissolved in liquid. Liquid fertilizers skip the step of needing rain to break down dry granules, feeding the crop immediately.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu niyenii ni mli ewo nu mli pɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ gbɛ ni biɔ nugbɔ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛgbala ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ amli ni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during long dry spells to conserve water and survive drought. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning purple along the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ purple kɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the soil lacks enough phosphorus, an essential nutrient that helps plants build strong roots and grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hia ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Extreme heat damages tomato pollen, preventing flowers from fertilizing properly. When temperatures get too high, the plant drops unpollinated flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ tomato mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ aná fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee nɔ lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many tiny flowers, but only a few turn into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ fioo ko pɛ tsɔɔ cocoa ŋmeii ni yeɔ emuu lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support. The tree selectively drops surplus flowers and tiny pods through a process called cherelle wilt to ensure it has enough energy to ripen the remaining pods.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ halaa fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Etsɔɔ gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherelle wilt lɛ mli koni ena nɔmimaa akɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ ashwere.

english: What is making small ragged holes in my maize leaves and leaving tiny caterpillars inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni baa lɛ. Yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young leaf funnels and stems. Detecting them early helps you treat the crop before severe damage occurs.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ baai bibii kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ. mra mli nibii ni ana Ebaaye ebua bo ni ohere oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala dani nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ aba.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster after rain than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants with aggressive root systems that allow them to absorb water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops, giving them a natural head start after rain.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Ha amɛje shishi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do other farmers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps neighboring maize plants grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the ground and spreads them out toward sunlight, allowing the plant to produce more food and grow larger underground tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Removing extra shoots, called suckers, stops them from stealing water and nutrients from the main plant, ensuring the parent tree grows a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkajuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ adara ni etsɔ plantains ŋmɔ agbo ni tsii.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one generation of high yield. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special traits, resulting in weak plants and much lower yields in the second season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛ yibiiwoo babaoo aba yinɔ kome. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my crops not producing big yields even though my farm land has dark and rich soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni baa nii moŋ?

english: Rich dark soil holds organic matter, but crops still need specific balanced nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. If one key nutrient is missing or if the soil is too acidic, the crops cannot absorb the food they need to produce high yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii, ni tsuɔ waa lɛ hiɛɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii biɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko ni sa lolo, tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri kome bɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ kɛkɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce smaller tubers every time I replant it on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii be fɛɛ be ni mikɛbaadu ekoŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava draws specific nutrients heavily from the ground. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts those nutrients and allows soil-borne pests to build up, so rotating crops or resting the land is necessary to keep yields high.
ga: Cassava gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo. Kɛ́ adu shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, no haa nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa sũ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ he miihia koni aná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up tightly during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize rolls its leaves as a natural defense mechanism to reduce leaf surface area exposed to the sun, which slows down water loss. It is a signal that the plant is thirsty and conserving moisture until cooler temperatures return.
ga: Abɛi baa ni atsiɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbaa baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaha nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye tso lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off the plant without forming any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme midday heat, prolonged dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping soil moisture steady and balanced helps the plant hold its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo nitrogen fertilizer babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: At what stage in its growth does my maize crop need water the most?
ga: Mɛɛ be mli mi ŋmãa lɛ dalɛ he hiaa nu fe fɛɛ?

english: Maize needs water most during the flowering and tasseling stage when the cobs are forming. Lack of water at this critical time prevents the cobs from filling out with grains, leading to empty or incomplete cobs.
ga: Nu he hiaa abele fe fɛɛ yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ toi be mli beni ŋmeii lɛ miifee lɛ. Nu ni bɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be ni he hiaa waa nɛɛ mli lɛ baatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekawo ŋmaa lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ yaka loo amɛyeee emuu.

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow tall and thin with small stems when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain needs direct sunlight to build strong, thick trunks and heavy fruit bunches. When shaded, the plant wastes its energy stretching upwards towards the sun instead of expanding its stem and roots.
ga: Plantains he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee tsei ni wa, ni mli tse kɛ aduawai tsei ni tsii. Kɛji akɛ eyɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa hulu lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ ashwã

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and turn pale even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa fiofio ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that aggressively steal nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your crops. Even with enough water, your crops go hungry because the weeds eat first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji nu fa bɔ ni sa po Oŋmɔshi nibii po hɔmɔ miiye amɛ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards and getting thick and rubbery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiifee tamɔ rɔba lɛ?

english: Upward leaf curling in tomatoes is often a sign of a plant virus transmitted by tiny insects like whiteflies, or a reaction to intense heat. Protecting young plants from insects early stops the leaves from failing and failing to nourish the fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ he okadi loo nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa kɛji edɔ waa. Tsei bibii ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa ni amɛkagbee shi ni anyɛɛɛ aha aduawai lɛ niyenii.

english: How does adding animal manure to my farm help my crops grow better than without it?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds beneficial soil organisms that break down organic material into nutrients plants can easily consume. It also acts like a sponge, helping your soil hold onto moisture during dry periods.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni gbálaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli kɛfeɔ niyenii ni tsei baanyɛ aye mlɛo lɛ niyenii. Etsuɔ nii hu tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Can I save seeds from the high-yielding hybrid maize I harvested to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for a one-time high yield in the first generation. If you plant the saved seeds from that harvest, the resulting plants will lose their vigor, grow unevenly, and produce much smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo shikome pɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Tso ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli. shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee ni yibiiwoo lɛ faaa kwraa

english: Why do my crops look fine in the morning but droop and look sick when the afternoon sun comes out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo waa leebi shi amɛgboɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛ́ shwane hulu lɛ je kpo lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon, intense heat causes plants to lose water faster than their roots can suck it up. This heat stress weakens the plant and makes hidden diseases or wilting symptoms suddenly show up.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. ni ehaa helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ he okadii baa trukaa.

english: Can crop sickness really travel through the air to infect my farm?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyashɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, many crop diseases are caused by tiny fungal spores or bacteria that float in the air. Strong winds and warm afternoon air currents can carry these germs from a neighboring farm straight to your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai babaoo jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii loo bacteria mli. floating in the air Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ni hoɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ ajie helai nɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛya onibii amli.

english: Why do I notice fewer crop diseases during the continuous rains than during hot sunny days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyɔseɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai fioo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei ni yaa nɔ lɛ amli fe gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain continuously washes spores off leaves and keeps temperatures cooler. However, when the rain stops and strong sunshine warms up the wet crops, it creates the ideal humid environment for diseases to rapidly appear.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ yaa nɔ etsuɔ ​​tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nii kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ. Shi, kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni efɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, Ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mli edɔ baa koni helai akabote mli. jieɔ amɛhe kpo oya

english: How does sudden hot weather right after a rainstorm affect my plants?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ saa mitsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Rain provides the moisture that disease germs need to wake up, and the immediate hot sunshine creates a warm, steamy environment that helps the germs grow fast while stressing your plants.
ga: Nugbɔ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ koni amɛte shi. Ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ehaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ daa oya yɛ be mli ni otsei lɛ miihao lɛ baa.

english: Does direct afternoon sunlight kill crop diseases or make them worse?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ agbe helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo eha amɛhe afee shoo fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: While strong sunlight can dry out some surface moisture, intense afternoon sun usually stresses your plants, making them weaker and more vulnerable to diseases that thrive in warm conditions.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ekomɛi gĩɔ moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni helai ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops get brown spots after the morning dew dries off in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni leebi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Morning dew leaves droplets on the leaves, and when the hot afternoon sun heats those droplets up, airborne fungal spores use that warm water to sprout and bite into the leaf, creating brown spots.
ga: Leebi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shĩɔ nu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ni kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ ha nakai ŋmeii lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Airborne fungal spores lɛ kɛ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkpãtã baai lɛ amli. ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa

english: Will planting shade trees on my farm help stop my crops from getting sick in the heat?
ga: Ani tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akaye hela kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Yes, shade trees protect crops from the harsh afternoon sun, keeping the soil cool and reducing heat stress so your plants stay strong enough to fight off airborne sicknesses.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shwane hulu ni naa wa lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi. Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwu amɛshi helai ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli baa lɛ.

english: Is it good to spray chemical medicine on my sick crops during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makɛ tsofai afɔ mi tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: No, you should avoid spraying in the hot afternoon because the strong sun makes the chemical evaporate too quickly before working, and it can also burn the hot leaves of your crops.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okpa tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baaha tsofai lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ dani atsu nii. Ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baai hu ashã.

english: How can I tell if a plant sickness came from the air or from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso hela ko jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo shikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: Airborne sicknesses usually start as spots or blights on the upper leaves and branches that face the wind, while soil sicknesses typically start around the roots or the bottom leaves near the dirt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli baa lɛ jeɔ shishi akɛ ŋmeii loo shãa yɛ baai kɛ tsei niji ni kwɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ helai jeɔ shishi yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli loo yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to inspect my farm for airborne diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji helai ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli baa lɛ yɛ mli?

english: It is best to inspect your farm in the late afternoon because that is when symptoms like wilting, leaf spotting, and heat stress caused by airborne germs are most visible on the plants.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, okadii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, baai ni shwieɔ shi, kɛ dɔlɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni anaa yɛ tsei anɔ fe fɛɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they compete for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Giving each plant enough space allows it to grow strong stems and produce larger maize cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than the crops I carefully plant on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ duɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tough and strong. They are used to surviving in poor soil and harsh conditions, so they quickly steal water and food away from farm crops that need more care.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛhe wa ni amɛhe wa. Etsɔ amɛhe akɛ amɛaahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni ehe hiaa ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize plants turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food plant needs to stay green and grow. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the crop regain its rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Amɛji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour fertilizer right against the stem of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is very strong and acts like salt on tender plant skin. Placing it right against the stem can burn the plant and kill it; placing it a short distance away allows the roots to safely drink up the food.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli wa waa ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ ŋoo yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛma tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ ashã ni egbo. Kɛ́ okɛto he ko ni kɛ shishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnu niyenii shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with lots of leaves, but only producing tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii. Shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ

english: When the soil has too much water or nitrogen food, the plant puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending food down to build big cassava tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu loo nitrogen nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛfee ŋmei shishifãi wuji

english: Plantain leaves curl and hang low to protect themselves from intense heat. It is the plant's natural way of reducing water loss through its leaves so it can stay hydrated until the cool evening.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbaa nu ni amɛlaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my tomato plants without making any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather is too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water. When under stress, the plant drops its flowers to conserve energy just to stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. be mli ni amɛyɔɔ haomɔ shishi lɛ Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli kɛkɛ.

english: Why does my cassava taste bitter when I harvest it during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ ŋɔɔ waa kɛ́ akpa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava goes through severe heat and dry weather, it produces natural defense chemicals inside its roots to protect itself from water loss. These chemicals create a bitter taste until regular rains return.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsɔ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli lɛ, Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli koni nu akafite. Tsofai nɛɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ baa kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open sunlit field without shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu la kpɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni tsei bɛ shade mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, sensitive leaves that easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Plantain trees or shade trees act like large umbrellas that protect the young cocoa plants until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Roots need air in the soil to breathe just like people do. When heavy rain stays on the farm for too long without draining, it drowns the roots and creates the wet conditions that cause tubers to rot.
ga: Taakɛ gbɔmɛi ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha shihilɛ ko ni mli ewo fɔ ni baanyɛ aha bulb lɛ agbo aba.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. They require shade trees or plantain plants around them to act as natural canopy protection, preserving soil moisture and sheltering their tender leaves while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei loo plantains ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he miihia amɛ. Bɔni afee ni abu adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ he Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛbaabii bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do tiny pods on my cocoa tree dry up and turn black before they grow into big pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: This is often caused by a natural self-thinning process called cherelle wilt, where the tree sheds extra pods it cannot support. However, it can also be triggered by severe lack of water, poor soil nutrition, or pest attack early in the pod's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry wilt. Biɛ ji he ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, ebaanyɛ eba kɛjɛ nu ni faaa waa yɛ mɔ mli lɛ hu mli. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa yɛ pod lɛ dalɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires high amounts of nitrogen to stay green and grow strong, so when the soil lacks it, the plant moves available nitrogen to newer top leaves, causing older bottom leaves to yellow.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa lɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize crop curl up tightly like tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural protective response to severe heat and drought. Curling reduces the leaf surface exposed to the sun and wind, which helps the plant conserve water until temperatures cool down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hetoo kɛha dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ. Curling haa baa lɛ nɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when heavy rains continue for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the field for extended periods without proper drainage, it drowns the roots, causing fungal rot and decay underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ ŋmɔ ko mli be kakadaŋŋ ni nu lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines on wooden sticks instead of letting them spread across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tso yɛ tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows leaves to catch maximum sunlight needed to produce energy for heavy tubers. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and leaf rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la babaoo, ni he hiaa koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulb ni tsii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants fall off without forming any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Flower drop occurs when plants experience temperature extremes, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant drops blossoms to save energy for basic survival rather than fruit production.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes split and crack open while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miigba ni egbɛ eshwa be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Fruit cracking happens when plants absorb a sudden rush of water after a dry spell. The inside of the tomato grows rapidly with water faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst.
ga: Yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ ŋɔ nu ni baa trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ daa oya kɛ nu oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall down so easily when the fruit bunch begins to swell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow, fibrous roots and a soft pseudostem. As the fruit heavy bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy, requiring bamboo props or stakes to keep it upright against strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni yɔɔ fiber kɛ pseudostems ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ da Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Esa akɛ amɛkɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli loo ŋmei tsei atsu nii koni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why does my land yield much smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting the same crop on the same plot drains specific nutrients faster than the soil can replenish them. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi baajɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo nakai niyenii lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly when the afternoon sun becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot afternoons as a self-defense mechanism to save water. By rolling up, less surface area of the leaf is exposed to the hot sun and dry air, which prevents the plant from losing too much moisture.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ amɛhe koni akɛbu nu he. kɛji akɛ abɔle ehe lɛ, hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shɛɛɛ baa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akafite ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cassava plants turning yellow and crisp during this hot dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɛkɛ hulutsoo be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and intense sunlight scorch tender leaves when soil moisture is low. Without enough water in the soil, the plant cannot cool itself down, leading to leaf burn and yellowing.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la haa baai lɛ feɔ blɛoo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee amɛhe fɛ̃i. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Is it better for my vegetables if I water them early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mi-aduawai lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛmli leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning. Watering during the hot afternoon causes much of the water to evaporate into the air before the plant's roots can drink it up, wasting water and leaving the crop thirsty.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu. Enɛ fiteɔ nu ni ehaa kumai yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell if my crops are thirsty before they start dying in the heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kumai miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani amɛje shishi amɛgboi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Thirsty crops will show soft, wilting leaves during the warm parts of the day, a loss of shiny green color, or slow growth. You can also dig 2 to 3 inches into the soil; if it feels dry and crumbly, the crop needs water.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ baajie baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni egboi yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Su eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ lɛ laaje. loo shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo Obaanyɛ otsa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ inchi 2 kɛyashi 3 kɛji onu he akɛ egbi ni egbɔjɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia tsei.

english: Can giving my crops too much water during a very hot week actually hurt them?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli fe nine yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛ awui?

english: Yes, overwatering during hot weather can drown the plant roots by cutting off air in the soil. Hot, waterlogged soil causes roots to rot, making the plant unable to take up nutrients and causing leaves to turn yellow.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nine yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ. ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I keep water in my soil so my crops do not dry out quickly when the rain stops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛ?

english: You can cover the bare soil around your crops with dry grass, straw, or leaves, which is called mulching. This layer acts like an umbrella that traps moisture in the ground and shields the soil from direct heat.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ sũ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko awo ehe. Akɛ jwɛi, jwɛi loo baai duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela, emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does water just run off the surface of my farm soil instead of sinking in when the ground is very dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebote mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa lɛ?

english: Very dry, sun-baked soil creates a hard crust that repels water initially. Loosening the topsoil lightly with a hoe allows rainwater or irrigation water to sink deep down into the root zone instead of washing away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa ni hulu lɛ shãa lɛ feɔ ŋshɔŋloo ko ni wa ni shwieɔ nu yɛ shishijee mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ blɛoo lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔshiimɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ abote shishifã lɛ mli shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni nu lɛ baaho.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather suddenly changes from hot sun to heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ trukaa lɛ? Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛtee nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa?

english: Sudden weather changes create shock for the pepper plant. The sudden shift in temperature and water availability forces the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy for its stem and roots until conditions stabilize.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ba trukaa lɛ ha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ naa kpɛ amɛhe waa. Tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa yɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he amɛha amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings look weak and flat on the ground right after I move them into the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ tee hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings damages small roots responsible for drinking water. Under hot sun, the seedling loses water faster than its damaged roots can draw it up, causing temporary wilting until the plant settles into its new environment.
ga: Dumɔwui ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi bibii. no ji nɔ ni kɛ nu ni anuɔ baa Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Dumɔwui laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi ni efite lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gboɔ be kukuoo ko kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ baanyɛ atsake ehe ewo shihilɛ hee lɛ mli.

english: Will planting taller trees near my small vegetable farm help protect my plants from extreme heat?
ga: tsei kakadaji ni aduɔ He ko ni bɛŋkɛ aduawai ŋmɔ bibioo ko Ani minɔ lɛ baabu mitsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he?

english: Yes, shade trees or tall companion plants break strong hot winds and lower the ground temperature. This creates a cooler surrounding environment, slowing down water loss from both the soil and your vegetable leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei kakadaji ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ ni baa shi lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni ebɔle he lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ o-vegetable baa lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do some crop varieties mature faster than others even when planted on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi shwereɔ oya fe ekrokomɛi kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli po lɛ?

english: Different varieties are bred with specific genetic traits. Some improved varieties are developed to mature in just three months, while older or traditional varieties might take four months or longer under the same growing conditions.
ga: Akwɛɔ kooloi srɔtoi ni yɔɔ fɔmɔ nii pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Afee ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni kusum mli ŋmeii srɔtoi ni etsɛ loo nɔ ni fe nakai lɛ baanyɛ ahé nyɔji ejwɛ loo nɔ ni fe nakai yɛ shihilɛi ni amɛdaraa yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ shishi.

english: How does choosing a early-maturing variety help me if the rains stop early?
ga: Te ŋmeii srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ ni mihalaa lɛ baaye abua mi tɛŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra?

english: A variety that matures in three months allows you to harvest before the soil loses moisture, protecting your yield from drought compared to a variety that needs four months in the ground.
ga: Srɔtoi lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli, ni no haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii dani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Buu onibii ahe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Akɛ enɛ toɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni biɔ nyɔji ejwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Does a crop that matures in three months produce less harvest than one that takes four months?
ga: Ani tso ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli lɛ baawo yibii fioo fe tso ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji ejwɛ mli lɛ?

english: Not necessarily. Modern fast-maturing varieties are specifically bred to yield high amounts of grain in a shorter time, giving you a full harvest while saving you a month of field care.
ga: Dabi, atsɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei srɔtoi ni daa oya lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo babaoo yɛ be kukuoo mli. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, ni ehaa okɛ nyɔŋ kome kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do farmers in my community prefer some seed varieties over others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ sumɔɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi komɛi fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Farmers usually prefer varieties that reduce farm labor and time in the field, such as seeds that yield quickly in three months rather than four, allowing for faster returns on investment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi sumɔɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni haa ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ kɛ be ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baa shi, tamɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli moŋ fe nyɔji ejwɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni anáa shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo oya.

english: What is a foundation seed, and why is it recommended for my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji dumɔwu shishitoo? Ni mɛni hewɔ ajieɔ lɛ yi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Foundation seed is pure seed grown under strict quality control to maintain strong genetic traits. Using it ensures your crop grows uniformly and delivers expected benefits like early harvesting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni he tse ji dumɔwui ni he tse ni adu yɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa shishi koni akɛhiɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sui ni mli wa lɛ amli. Gbɛ nɛɛ ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehaa sɛɛnamɔi ni okpaa gbɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmaakpamɔ mra.

english: Is there extra work involved when using foundation seed for my crops?
ga: Ani nitsumɔ kroko fata he kɛji akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ashishitoo miitsu nii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Foundation seeds require proper initial handling and correct planting steps, but once planted, the ongoing management is standard and yields uniform crop growth.
ga: Dumɔwui shishijee biɔ shishijee nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa kɛ dumɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni ja. Shi kɛ́ adu lɛ, abaakwɛ nɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Can I just save seed from my fast-maturing harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni shwereɔ mra lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Saving seed directly from your harvest can cause the crop to lose its special traits, like early maturity and high yield. Returning to certified or foundation seed ensures reliable performance.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni okpa lɛ to tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite sui krɛdɛɛi ni eyɔɔ, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ mra kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo. Kuu sɛɛ kɛya dumɔwui loo shishitoo ni awo he odase lɛ nɔ lɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nitsumɔ nɔ.

english: How does planting a 3-month crop variety affect my farm labor compared to a 4-month crop?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ nyɔji 3 lɛ saa miŋmɔ lɛ mli nitsumɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto nyɔji 4 ni aduɔ lɛ he?

english: A 3-month crop reduces the total days you spend weeding, watering, and protecting your field by a full month, saving you labor costs and effort.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii nyɔji 3 lɛ, gbii fɛɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ jwɛi, okɛwoɔ nu, ni okɛbuɔ oŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi kɛyashɛɔ nyɔŋ muu fɛɛ. ni haa nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ baa shi.

english: Can planting a shorter-duration crop allow me to farm twice in one rainy season?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ baaha anyɛ atsu okwaayeli shii enyɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome mli?

english: Yes, using a variety that matures in three months gives you enough time to harvest early and potentially plant a second short-season crop before the rainy season fully ends.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ okɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha oná kpamɔ be mra, ni ekolɛ obaaná kpamɔ kuku ni ji enyɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba naagbee kwraa.

english: How do I decide when to harvest an early-maturing crop variety?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ be ni esa akɛ akpa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ ahe?

english: Early-maturing varieties follow a shorter internal clock; you should track the calendar months from planting—such as three months instead of four—and watch for natural signs like drying leaves and hardened grains.
ga: Henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ yɛ mligbɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa kuku. Esa akɛ okwɛ kalanda nɔ nyɔji kɛjɛ dumɔ mli, tamɔ nyɔji etɛ yɛ ejwɛ najiaŋ. Ni otao adebɔɔ mli okadii, tamɔ baai ni egbi kɛ dumɔwui ni wa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the underground tubers. Lifting the vines on stakes also keeps the leaves off the damp ground so they do not rot or get diseased.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Koni akafite loo hela

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crop roots with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or mulch acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground, stops weeds from taking over, and keeps the soil cool during very hot days.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi loo mulch tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket, ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli

english: Why are the leaves of my growing maize plants turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil that plants need to stay green and build strong stalks and leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná tsei kɛ baai ni wa.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts on my farmland after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the earth, but groundnuts and beans actually take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally restoring your land for the next season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shi yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ogbɛhe lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why must I wait for the main rainy season before planting my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ dani odu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Seeds need a steady supply of moisture to sprout and build strong roots. Planting early during dry spells causes the seeds to dry up and die in the hot soil.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ adu mra yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops. When weeds are left in the farm, your main crops become starved and cannot grow full fruits or grains.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Beni ashi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdu aduawai loo ŋmaa ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are small holes appearing on the leaves of my young maize plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eje kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ kome?

english: Caterpillars like the fall armyworm hide deep inside the plant during the hot day and come out at night when it is cooler to feed on the soft leaves.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ koni amɛbaye baai bibii.

english: When the weather gets extremely hot or the soil gets too dry, tomato plants become stressed and drop their flowers to conserve energy and survive.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: My cassava plants have started producing flowers; does this mean the underground roots are ready to harvest?
ga: Mi-cassava tsei lɛ miibɔi fɔfɔi. Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Flowering is just part of the cassava plant's natural life above ground and does not mean the tubers are mature. The roots usually need more time underground to swell and fill with starch.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwereɔ lɛ ji yucca adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fã kome pɛ. Ni etsɔɔɔ akɛ yitso lɛ baada kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi lɛ he hiaa be babaoo koni amɛfu ni amɛwo amɛmli ŋmei lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my crops still manage to survive even when the leaves look weak during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi hiɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants store energy in their roots and stems during good weather. Even when drought or pests damage the outer leaves, the crop uses these internal energy reserves to stay alive and recover once rain returns.
ga: Tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa be mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ hɔmɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui baanyɛ afite baai ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ moŋ, shi no sɛɛ lɛ, Crops kɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli nɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ehi wala mli ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: How can I tell if a new crop variety is high quality while it is still growing in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tso henɔ hee ko hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lolo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can assess quality early by checking for strong stem growth, deep green leaves, quick recovery after rain, and a natural ability to resist common local insects without heavy spraying.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ mli mra. Kɛtsɔ tsei ni he wa lɛ adalɛ ni akwɛɔ lɛ nɔ. dark green leaves He ni amɛhe baa oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ kɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ maŋbii amli kooloi ni akɛ tsofa ni tsii shwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ.

english: Can crops that I grow for food also be used to treat common illnesses in my household?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ tsei ni miduɔ kɛha niyenii lɛ atsa helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ mishia lɛ?

english: Yes, many traditional food crops in Ghana, such as moringa, ginger, and cassava leaves, contain natural nutrients and medicinal compounds that offer health benefits alongside nutritional value.
ga: Hɛɛ, kusum niyenii babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ekomɛi ji moringa, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei baai. Adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ tsofai ni haa mɔ náa hewalɛnamɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ yɛ mli.

english: How long should I test a new seed variety on my farm before planting it across my entire land?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ maka dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ dani madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: It is best to test a new seed variety on a small plot for one full year or growing season. This allows you to observe how it handles both the rainy season and dry spells before making a big investment.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooka dumɔwui srɔtoi heei lɛ okwɛ yɛ he bibioo ko afi muu fɛɛ loo amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be. Enɛ haa okwɛɔ bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be fɛɛ he nii eha dani okɛ shika babaoo woɔ mli.

english: Why do government-supplied seeds often produce a bigger harvest than seeds I save from my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ dumɔwui ni nɔyeli lɛ kɛhaa lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Government-supplied improved seeds are specially bred by plant scientists to fight off local diseases, grow uniformly, and yield more fruit compared to traditional seeds that weaken over multiple generations.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsake ni nɔyeli lɛ kɛhaa lɛ ji nɔ ni tsei ahe nilelɔi ekwɛ nɔ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛkɛwu amɛshi helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. kwɛ̃ɔ daa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ni egbɔjɔ yɛ yinɔi babaoo ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when heavy rain leaves standing water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water fills the tiny air pockets in the soil, preventing root respiration. Without oxygen, the roots cannot absorb key nutrients like nitrogen, causing the leaves to turn yellow from nutrient starvation.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni no haaa shishifãi lɛ amu. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my soil better for the crop I plant next?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into rich plant food in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii ni jara wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot if I leave them in the ground too long after they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava reaches full maturity, soil moisture and naturally occurring soil bacteria begin to break down the starch in the tubers, causing decay if they are not harvested on time.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ mli helai ni baa trukaa lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbalaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ. Ekɛ fitemɔ baa kɛji akpaaa yɛ be naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms during very hot sunny days without producing any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli ni pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes heat stress in pepper plants, forcing them to drop flowers to conserve moisture and energy rather than attempting to support fruit development.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa pepper tsei amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ajie fɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ akafite. Mohu ɔ, mo bɔ mɔde nɛ o ha nɛ yiblii nɛ wa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce far fewer pods now than they did when they were younger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo fioo fe beni eyɔɔ gbekɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their internal transport system and root efficiency decline, leading to reduced flower formation and lower pod production.
ga: Beni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa kɛhoɔ afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, gbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ amɛmli kɛ bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi, ni pod ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do agricultural officers ask us to uproot cocoa trees that still have green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi biɔ ni ajie kookoo tsei ni baai eŋɔli lolo lɛ?

english: Some serious diseases, like the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, spread secretly inside the tree long before the leaves dry up completely. Uprooting infected trees immediately stops the sickness from traveling through the roots and insects to infect healthy trees nearby.
ga: Helai komɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ teemɔŋ. yɛ tso lɛ mli dani baai lɛ agbi kwraa Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haaa hela lɛ aya shishifãi kɛ kooloi amli oya koni egbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: If my neighbor's cocoa farm has a crop sickness, can it spread to my farm even if I keep my own boundaries clean?
ga: Kɛji okutsoŋnyo lɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ tso hela Ani ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa mihusui lɛ ahe tseɔ moŋ

english: Yes, crop diseases and tiny pests like mealybugs or fungal spores can easily travel across farm boundaries through wind, rain spray, insects, birds, or shared tools.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ mealybugs loo fungal spores baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kooloi bibii, okpoi loo nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛjaraa lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ mli husui lɛ amli mlɛo.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot whenever heavy rain falls for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates wet, damp conditions that help the Black Pod fungus grow quickly. Pruning thick branches lets sunlight and air into the farm to dry out the leaves and stop the rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni haa blackpod fungus lɛ daa oya. niji ni mli tse ni afoɔ Ha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha baai lɛ agbi ni ekpa amɛ ni amɛkafite.

english: Why do the old cocoa trees my grandfather planted produce fewer pods than before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tso momo ni mitsɛkwɛ̃ du lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older than 25 to 30 years, their roots become less efficient at pulling food from the ground, causing the tree to lose energy and produce smaller harvests.
ga: Beni cacao tsei lɛ daraa fe afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ he waaa ni ewoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their tiny flowers without them turning into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Nɔ ni fa ni etsɔko pod ni eyi obɔ?

english: Cocoa trees shed extra flowers if there are not enough tiny insects (midges) to pollinate them, or if the tree is stressed by hot sun, dry soil, and a lack of soil food.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baakwɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ. Aloo kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi, ni niyenii faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the new hybrid cocoa seeds give pods faster than the traditional seeds we used years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii heei ni akɛ tsofai ewo mli lɛ feɔ ŋmeii oya fe blema ŋmeii ni wɔkɛtsu nii afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties are specially bred by scientists to grow faster, tolerate local conditions better, and start bearing fruit in 2 to 3 years compared to older varieties that take up to 5 years.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi ekwɛ kookoo ni akɛfee tsofai krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara oya. ehiɛɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ ni ebɔi yibiiwoo yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, kɛ akɛto kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni heɔ afii enumɔ lɛ ahe.

english: If COCOBOD helps me cut down my diseased trees, how long will I have to wait to harvest from new trees?
ga: Kɛji COCOBOD ye ebua mi ni mifo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpa tso hee?

english: If you plant the new hybrid seedlings provided during farm rehabilitation, you can expect the new trees to start bearing their first cocoa pods within 2 to 3 years.
ga: Kɛji odu hybrid dumɔwui heei ni asaa he yɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ be mli lɛ Obaanyɛ okpa gbɛ akɛ tsei heei baaje amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli.

english: Will new cocoa seedlings grow well if I plant them directly in the same spot where old trees were uprooted?
ga: Ani kookoo tso hee baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ni atse momo lɛ yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The soil where old trees lived for decades is usually tired. Adding manure or compost and planting temporary shade crops like plantains first helps feed and refresh the ground for new seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni tsei momo ehi nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ lɛ fiteɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baafata he ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eha ehe ajɔ kɛha dumɔwui heei.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and burn during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains nearby to act as umbrellas and trap moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Is it safe to plant heavy root crops like cassava right next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli tse, tamɔ ŋmei, yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe?

english: Cassava roots grow very big and aggressively steal food and water from the soil. Plantains are better companion crops because they give shade without choking the young cocoa roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa waa ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Plantains ji tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he ejaakɛ ehaa hulutsoo ni ehaaa kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why should I leave wide space between my maize plants instead of planting seeds closely together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi he ko ni da yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows its roots and leaves to grow strong, resulting in bigger ears of corn.
