ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for leaf growth. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and keeps the plant strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tightly during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl to protect themselves from extreme heat and water loss, or because tiny insects like mites are feeding on the underside. Watering early in the morning and inspecting for pests helps resolve this.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Aloo ejaakɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yeɔ nii yɛ eshishi. Nu ni akɛhaa leebi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ saa naagba nɛɛ he.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot, when the soil gets too dry, or if insects are not moving pollen around. Regular watering and keeping the soil moist helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛji kooloi bibii tsiii pollen lɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũuɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and thin even though the vines and leaves look very big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ wain tso lɛ kɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the plant puts all its energy into growing green leaves above ground rather than expanding tubers below. Balanced soil nutrients help the roots swell large.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ e-bulbs lɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa waa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava crop is fully mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-cassava tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tuber lɛ mli fũuɔ lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to harvest all my crops at once or leave some in the soil until I need them?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo mashi eko yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛyashi be mli ni ehe baahia mi?

english: Root crops like cassava can safely remain in the ground for a while, but grain crops like maize must be harvested once mature to prevent rain, mold, birds, and insects from destroying your yield.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe be ko. Shi esa akɛ akpa ŋmaa nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa, beni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ koni nugbɔ, ŋmeii, okpoi, kɛ kooloi akafite onibii lɛ.

english: Why do tiny insects appear inside my maize bags after a few months of storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-ŋma kotokui lɛ amli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Insects like weevils come from microscopic eggs laid on the grain before harvest. Thoroughly drying your corn in the sun until it is hard, and using sealed, airtight bags prevents pests from multiplying.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii anɔ dani akpaa lɛ amli. Okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa. Ni kɛ akɛ kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafɔ.

english: Why do my harvested sweet potatoes start rotting quickly after I place them in my store room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya beni mikɛwo nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes rot quickly if they are bruised during harvest or kept in a warm, unventilated room. Curing them in a dry, shaded area for a few days after harvest toughens their skin and prevents rotting.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ mli. Kɛ́ atsa yɛ he ko ni egbi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha hewolo lɛ mli awa ni ebaatsi fitemɔ naa.

english: What kind of pests are usually responsible for completely cutting off the leaves on my crops overnight?
ga: Mɛɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ji nɔ ni ekolɛ ekɛ baa fɛɛ ni mifoɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ba nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: Pests such as grasscutters and soldier ants are well known for attacking farm crops by chewing and completely severing leaves and young stems.
ga: Ale tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ jwɛi ŋmɔji kɛ asraafoi ŋmɔji jogbaŋŋ akɛ amɛtutuaa okwaayeli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ baai muu fɛɛ kɛ tsei bibii ni amɛfoɔ ni amɛfoɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do grasscutters cause damage to crops on a farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔnei ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii?

english: Grasscutters act as destructive pests that feed on crops by cutting down plant stems and stripping the leaves off completely, which stunts plant growth.
ga: Mɛi ni shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ tsei ashishifãi ni amɛfoɔ ni amɛjieɔ baai lɛ fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tsei nyɛŋ akwɛ̃.

english: Can soldier ants actually harm my crops, and what does their damage look like?
ga: Ani asraafoi ŋmeii baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ? Ni mɛni ji amɛfitemɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, soldier ants can act as severe farm pests that swarm plants and cut off leaves completely, leaving your crops stripped bare.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, asraafoi ŋmeii baanyɛ atsu nii akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii ni hiɛdɔɔ yɔɔ mli ni shwieɔ tsei anɔ ni amɛfoɔ baai lɛ fɛɛ. Shi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efolo.

english: How can I tell if leaf-cutting pests are actively attacking my farm field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ baai lɛ miitutua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: When you arrive at your farm and see severed leaves on the ground or plants with their leaves cut completely off, leaf-cutting pests like soldier ants or grasscutters are present.
ga: Kɛ oshɛ ŋmɔ ko mli ni ona baai ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ loo tsei ni afo amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ Ayɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ baai, tamɔ asraafoi ŋmeii loo jwɛi ŋmeii.

english: Why is it bad for my plants if pests cut off all their leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mitso lɛ kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwie baai lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plants rely on their leaves to make food from sunlight; when pests completely cut off the leaves, the crop cannot grow, produce yield, or survive.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛjɛ hulu la mli. Beni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ fɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃, amɛwo yibii loo amɛhi shi.

english: What usually happens when pests start cutting leaves off crops in my area?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ bɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ ahe tsei?

english: Left unchecked, leaf-cutting pests will continue to slice off leaves and stems until whole sections of your farm are entirely stripped and destroyed.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwieɔ baai lɛ baaya nɔ afolɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishi kɛyashi be mli ni oŋmɔ lɛ mli he fɛɛ he lɛ baafite kwraa ni efite.

english: Is there a specific chemical product I can use to stop pests from cutting leaves off my crops?
ga: Ani tsofai komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ mikɛtsu nii koni mikɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkafo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai?

english: Using a protective chemical treatment like Blue Kama can effectively control leaf-cutting pests and prevent them from destroying crop leaves.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa tamɔ bluekama ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwieɔ baai lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tsei ahe baai.

english: What is the recommended treatment when I notice soldier ants cutting down my farm crops?
ga: Be ko lɛ, mina asraafoi akutsei ni miifolɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Te esa akɛ maná tsamɔ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Applying a suitable pest control chemical like Blue Kama helps eradicate soldier ants and protects your crop leaves from being stripped.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii, tamɔ Blue Kama tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie asraafoi ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ ohe, ni ebaabu otso lɛ baai lɛ ahe koni akajie amɛ.

english: What action should I take immediately if I visit my farm and see pests actively cutting crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mitee ŋmɔ ko mli ni mina kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ miifolɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai?

english: You should apply a recommended pest defense solution like Blue Kama immediately to stop the pests from destroying the remaining foliage.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛgbeɔ ŋmeii, tamɔ Blue Kama lɛ awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ŋmeii akafite tsei ahe tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Can chemical sprays help protect my crops against large pests like grasscutters and soldier ants?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji tamɔ jwɛifolɔi kɛ asraafoi aŋmeii ahe?

english: Yes, targeted chemical products like Blue Kama can act as an effective defense to discourage and control pests like grasscutters and soldier ants on your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ tamɔ Blue Kama lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii akɛ gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa koni akɛnijiaŋ aje wui ni akudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ jwɛifolɔi kɛ asraafoi aŋmeii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How does using a motorized water pump help my crops grow better than just relying on the rain?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu pɔmp ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: A water pump gives you control over when and how much water your plants get. This prevents water stress during dry spells, allows you to farm year-round, and leads to healthier crops and higher harvests.
ga: Nu pɔmp haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ be kɛ bɔ ni nu ni otsei lɛ baaná lɛ fa ha. Enɛ baaye abua ni akafee nu he haomɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Ehaa otsuɔ okwaayeli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa babaoo baa.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop is not getting enough water during a dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: When maize lacks water, its leaves will roll up tightly like straws during the hottest part of the day to save moisture. If the shortage continues, the lower leaves will turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Kɛ́ nu bɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ, abɔleɔ ebaai lɛ ahe waa tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli koni ŋmãa akafee nɔ ko. Kɛji akɛ shweremɔ lɛ tee nɔ lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbi.

english: Why is it better for my vegetables if I water them early in the morning rather than in the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛmli leebi moŋ fe shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning lets the roots absorb moisture before the sun gets too hot. In the afternoon heat, much of the water evaporates before reaching the roots, and hot water droplets on leaves can scorch them.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ. Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ Nu lɛ mli babaoo shwieɔ shi dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛshã.

english: What happens to my crops if I put chemical fertilizer on the soil when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. If applied to dry soil, the concentrated fertilizer sits directly against the roots and can burn or kill the plant.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsu nii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ ni ebaanyɛ eshã loo egbe tso lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants turn yellow when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills all the empty spaces in the soil with water, pushing out the air. Without air, the roots cannot breathe or take up plant food, which causes the leaves to yellow and drop.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa he fɛɛ he ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yiɔ kɛ nu. ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛye tso lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing fruit when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high or water is low, tomato plants drop their blossoms as a defense mechanism to save energy rather than trying to support fruit they cannot feed.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ faaa Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye lɛ,.

english: Why do my cocoa pods dry up and turn black on the trees before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ediŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and heavily shaded farms. Pruning branches to let in sunlight and air helps prevent it.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu he.

english: How do I know if my plantain leaves are drooping because of lack of water or a disease?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ nu ni bɛ loo hela hewɔ ni plantain baai lɛ miigbee shi lɛ?

english: If it is a lack of water, all the leaves will wilt slightly during the dry heat and recover when watered. If it is a disease like wilt, lower leaves will turn yellow and collapse permanently at the leaf base even when water is available.
ga: Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ fɛɛ baagboi fioo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. ni ebaatsa kɛji akɛ awo lɛ nu Kɛji hela ko tamɔ wilt ji lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebaagbee shi daa yɛ shishigbɛ kɛji nu yɛ po.

english: Why do my garden crops grow better when I cover the soil around them with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ sũ wo amɛhe lɛ? Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, traps soil moisture, keeps the roots cool, prevents heavy rain from washing away soil, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why do my yam tubers need large soil mounds to grow well instead of planting them directly in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ he hiaa shikpɔŋ agbo ko koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaadu amɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow large underground and need soft, loose, well-aerated soil to expand easily. Mounds also prevent waterlogging around the tuber, which can cause rotting.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛbiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo. Gɔŋ lɛ hu tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle yitso lɛ he. Enɛ baanyɛ aha egbo.

english: Why are wild bush animals suddenly coming onto my farm to eat my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ lɛ miiba miŋmɔ lɛ mli trukaa koni amɛbaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: When you clear land near a forest, you remove the natural homes and wild food sources of forest animals. Because your farm sits right at the edge of their habitat, crops like cassava, maize, and cocoa become an easy substitute food source for them.
ga: Kɛji ojie shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ koo ko lɛ Obaajie adebɔɔ mli shia kɛ koo mli niyenii jɛɛhe ni koo mli kooloi yɔɔ lɛ kɛya. Akɛni oŋmɔ lɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛhe lɛ naa hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ kookoo bafeɔ niyenii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye.

english: What can I plant along the borders of my farm to discourage animals from entering?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ naa koni kooloi anijiaŋ aje wui koni amɛkabote mli?

english: Planting continuous rows of spiky or bitter crops like pineapples, chili peppers, or dense prickly hedges around your border creates a physical and sensory wall that deters animals from crossing into your field.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii loo ni mli edɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni nyiɛɔ amɛsɛɛ ni ooodu yɛ ohusu lɛ he lɛ haa gbɔmɔtsoŋ kɛ henumɔŋ gbɛtsii nii ko baa ni tsiɔ kooloi anaa koni amɛkafo kɛbote oŋmɔji lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young crops scorch and dry up after I clear all the large trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Large forest trees act like giant umbrellas that block harsh sunlight and keep the soil cool and moist. Removing all trees exposes the bare soil to direct sun heat, which quickly bakes the roots of young crops.
ga: Koo mli tsei wuji lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi wuji ni tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ. Tsei fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli baa. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ashã oya.

english: Why are strong storm winds knocking down my maize more easily now?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miiha mi-abele lɛ miigbee shi mlɛo bianɛ lɛ?

english: Forest trees serve as natural windbreaks that slow down heavy gusts. Without a barrier of tall trees around your land, strong winds hit your crops directly with full force, bending or snapping their stems.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ baa shi. Kɛji tsei kakadaji komɛi bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ. ha tso lɛ shishi loo efo

english: Why are aggressive new types of weeds taking over my farm after land clearing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi hee ko ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa baye miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ?

english: Forest tree canopy keeps the ground in shade, keeping weed seeds asleep. Once you clear the trees and open up the sky, direct sunlight and rain trigger those dormant weed seeds in the soil to germinate rapidly.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ hɔnɔ. ni ekɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ Kɛ́ ojie tsei lɛ ni ogbele ŋwɛi Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nugbɔ baagbe jwɛi dumɔwui ni ewɔ lɛ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: How do I know if my soil is getting tired and needs me to fix it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni asaa?

english: Tired soil gives clear signals: leaves turn pale yellow instead of dark green, crops stay stunted, rain water runs off instead of sinking in, and the ground feels hard like concrete when dry.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ haa okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ shihilɛ ni mli wa mli. Nugbɔ nu hoɔ kɛyaa shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo. Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee shiŋŋ tamɔ kɔnkrit kɛji egbi.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the dark topsoil on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Bare, cleared land has no leaf cover to break the fall of raindrops or plant roots to bind the earth together. Heavy rain hits bare dirt directly and washes away the fertile top layer where plant food lives.
ga: He lɛ mli tse ni agbele naa, ni baai bɛ ni baaha nugbɔshiimɔi ni miigbee shi lɛ afee duŋ loo tsei shishifãi ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ekome. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni efoɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni baa nii ni haa tsei niyenii lɛ.

english: Why do old farmers say I should leave part of my land unplanted to rest for a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa lɛ kɛɛ akɛ esa akɛ mashi shikpɔŋ ko ni aduko nɔ koni mikɛhe ajɔɔ mihe afii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Leaving land to rest allows wild plants to grow, drop leaves, and rot naturally. This process recharges the ground with organic nutrients and restores soil structure without costly chemicals.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe lɛ haa koo mli tsei kwɛ̃ɔ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ mli ekoŋŋ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa tsuuu nii.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow during dry spells even when planted in rich soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Plants cannot eat dry nutrients directly from dirt; they need water to dissolve plant food so roots can drink it in. Without water, crops starve even in rich soil.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ aye niyenii ni egbi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Nu he miihia amɛ koni amɛkɛjie tsei aniyenii koni amɛha shishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni anuɔ. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii po nɔ.

english: Why do my plants grow very tall leaves but fail to produce fruit under heavy shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ waa shi enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ?

english: Plants rely on direct sunlight to make energy for flowering and fruiting. In deep shade, a plant stretches all its energy upward just to search for light, leaving no food power left to make fruits.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyatao la. Niyenii hewalɛ ko bɛ ni eshwɛ ni baaha nɔ ko aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow before the plants are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tsei lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on growing maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer can help restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the ground, leaving the soil tired. Cowpeas and other beans take nitrogen from the air and trap it back into the soil, naturally restoring fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi kɛ nitrogen babaoo ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ he ajɔ Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aku sɛɛ aha onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines grow plenty of big leaves but produce very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi amɛshishifãi lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or manure, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of roots below. Sweet potatoes need soil rich in potassium and phosphorus to form big tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmeii babaoo Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baatsu nii. Shikpɔŋ ni potassium kɛ phosphorus eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmeii koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rain causes water to sit on the farm without draining, the roots drown and rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hooo. Shishifãi lɛ gbee shi ni amɛgboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and break during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ egbi ni egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ harmatta be ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The hot, dry harmattan winds suck moisture out of large leaves faster than the roots can drink from dry soil. Covering the ground around the plant base with dry leaves or straw (mulching) holds water in the soil longer.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai agboi amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli. Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle otsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers crack and split open in the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miigba ni amɛmiigba yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Yams split when rain falls suddenly after a long dry period. The sudden surge of water makes the inside of the tuber grow faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to crack.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fãa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ sɛɛ. Nu ni hoɔ oya trukaa lɛ haa yitso lɛ mligbɛ fã lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ akpã mli. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread plant viruses. Spraying the crop with soapy water or neem leaf extract can help control these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo neem baa mli nu shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they lack water, when insects like mirids damage the stems, or when the farm gets too much direct sunlight. Retaining some shade trees and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ nu faaa. Beni kooloi bibii tamɔ atatui ba ni amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ loo be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ naa hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ Tso lɛ ni oooha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: When is the best time of day for me to spray chemical treatments on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: The best time to spray is early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the weather is cool. Spraying in the hot midday sun causes the chemical to evaporate quickly and can burn the crop leaves.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai lɛ shwie hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ atsɔ oya ni eha tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashã.

english: How can I tell if my land is good enough to support a vegetable farm like tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ aduawai tamɔ tomato nɔ?

english: Good land for vegetables has dark, crumbly soil that drains water easily after rain without leaving standing pools. If wild green leafy weeds are growing densely on the plot, it usually means the soil has good natural nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ aduawai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nu hoɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ ni eshiii nubui. Kɛji koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ kwɛ̃ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and woody instead of big and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei yɛ agboi ni yɔɔ blɛoo najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become woody when left in the ground too long past maturity or when the plant suffers severe water stress early on. Harvesting between 9 and 12 months depending on the variety yields soft, high-quality roots.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ bafeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni amɛdara tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ naa nu he haomɔ ni naa wa mra. Nikpamɔ lɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa.

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant stem varieties is the best way to keep your cassava leaves healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi, ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ ŋmeii ahe baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ ni aduɔ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ ŋmeii anɔ.

english: Does the part of the cassava stem I plant make a difference to my harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni miduɔ lɛ haa srɔtofeemɔ baa mikpamɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting cuttings taken from the middle of a healthy stem works best. Top green parts dry out too quickly in the heat, while bottom woody parts sprout slower and unevenly.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ yɛ latsaa mli. yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ daa blɛoo ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Besides checking the age of the crop (usually 8 to 12 months), you can look for the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, or carefully dig up just one root to test the size.
ga: Kɛfata afii ni tso lɛ eye lɛ kwɛmɔ he (bei pii lɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12) lɛ, obaanyɛ otao baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni miigbee shi lɛ hu, loo okɛ shishifã kome atsu nii blɛoo koni oka bɔ ni edara ha lɛ okwɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit bunch starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and weak stems that struggle to hold heavy fruit against strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a bamboo fork or wooden pole prevents the tree from bending or snapping.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛmɔ aduawai ni tsii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni akɛfee tso lɛ fi tso lɛ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo ekakumɔ.

english: When too many suckers grow around one mother plant, they compete for water and nutrients. Keeping only two or three strong suckers gives the main plant enough food to grow large, healthy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ fɔlɔ kome he lɛ, Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and turn brown during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ mli egbi ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that lose water very fast under hot sun. Mulching the base of the plant with dry leaves or crop waste keeps the soil cool and retains water for the roots.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya waa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain bunches ripen on the tree before they even grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwereɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Premature ripening occurs when the plant is stressed by severe drought, heat, or root damage from soil pests. Protecting the root area with mulch and shade reduces stress so fruit can mature fully.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwereɔ oya baa kɛji hɔmɔ ni naa wa, dɔlɛ, loo shishifãi ni jɛɔ sũ mli nibii ni fiteɔ nii amli lɛ haoɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulutsoo buɔ shishifã lɛ he lɛ, ehaa haomɔ baa shi bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ anyɛ ada kɛyashɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava and plantain together on the same land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei kɛ plantain yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, you can intercrop them safely as long as you give them enough space. Planting plantains further apart ensures light still reaches the cassava plants underneath so both produce good yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu tsei yɛ amɛteŋ shweshweeshwe, kɛji akɛ oha amɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dumɔ plantains lɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ koni la ayashɛ ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ lolo. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛ fɛɛ amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why does my soil give me smaller crops every time I plant cassava in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmei yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Cassava takes a large amount of nutrients out of the soil every season. Planting in the exact same spot continuously exhausts the soil, so rotating crops or leaving the land to rest restores fertility.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afite be fɛɛ be. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ loo hei ni atsakeɔ koni akɛjɔɔ he lɛ baaye abua ni fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I delay planting past the start of the main rainy season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ fo fe nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee?

english: Delayed planting often leads to significantly lower yields because crops miss the peak soil moisture, struggle through shorter growing periods, and face higher heat and pest pressure late in the season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa fe fɛɛ. Ni oootsɔ dalɛ be kukuoo mli ni okɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kpeɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ.

english: Can I still get a good tomato harvest if I plant late into the dry season using manual watering?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná tomato kpakpa lolo kɛji mikɛ nu ni mikɛwoɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mihe lɛ tsu nii kɛdu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naagbee gbɛ?

english: Yes, but dry season tomato farming requires heavy, regular irrigation and mulch to keep the soil cool, as severe heat stress can cause flowers to drop before setting fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi tomato ni aduɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ biɔ nu ni mli wa, ni afɔɔ nɔ daa, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo dani aduawai lɛ aba.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, severe dry spells, or lack of nutrients. The plant drops flowers to save its own energy when conditions are unfavorable for bearing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni naa wa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he yɛ shihilɛi ni esaaa kɛha yibiiwoo mli.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and leafy but fail to produce big fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai shi ewooo yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes plants to focus all their energy on leaf and stem growth. To produce big fruits, the plant needs balanced nutrients, especially phosphorus and potassium.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ adalɛ he nii. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. Titri lɛ, fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium kɛha yibii wuji.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism plants use to reduce leaf surface area and prevent water loss under intense sunlight and high temperatures.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba baa lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsi nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi lɛ naa.

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular, preventing the roots from taking up calcium steadily.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do tomato plants in my field suddenly wilt and die off one by one from the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miigboi ni amɛmiigboi komekomei lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by soil-borne fungal or bacterial diseases that block the plant's water pipes, preventing water from moving from the roots to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ tso lɛ nu paipii lɛ anaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya baai lɛ amli.

english: If I plant my tomatoes closer together, will I get a bigger total harvest from my land?
ga: Kɛji midu tomatoi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ Ani maná yibiiwoo fɛɛ babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too closely creates fierce competition for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also reduces airflow, which spreads diseases and typically leads to smaller fruits and lower overall yield.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ hu baa shi. ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa ni bei pii lɛ, ehaa aduawai bibii kɛ yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous good tomato harvest produce weaker plants and smaller yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mitsutsu tomato ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Many commercial seeds are hybrid varieties bred for specific traits. Saved seeds from hybrids lose these special characteristics in the next generation, resulting in mixed growth and lower yields.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfutuɔ nii kɛhaa sui pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ sui nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni futuɔ kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: How does applying animal manure to my farm help my crops survive dry spells better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ?

english: Organic manure acts like a sponge in the soil, improving its ability to hold onto moisture so crop roots can access water longer during dry periods.
ga: Organic fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ náa nu be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomatoes turn soft and spoil quickly before reaching buyers in big cities like Accra?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya dani eshɛɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ maŋtiase wulu ko tamɔ Accra lɛ aŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes spoil fast during long transport if they are picked when already fully ripe or if the soil lacks calcium during growth. Picking them at the 'breaker stage'—when they just start turning pink—keeps them firm enough to survive long journeys to distant markets.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa loo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ Amɛhalamɔ yɛ Amɛ ‘gbɛ ni amɛfoɔ’—be mli ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ pinki kɛkɛ lɛ—haa amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ kɛmiiya jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ amli.

english: What makes market traders from the city prefer one farmer's tomatoes over another?
ga: Mɛni haa maŋ lɛ jarayelihe jarayelɔi lɛ sumɔɔ okwaafonyo kome tomato fe mɔ kroko?

english: Traders look for firm, bright tomatoes that are uniform in size and free of insect marks or rot. Consistent watering, proper pest management, and picking the fruits before they get too soft will give you the quality buyers pay higher prices for.
ga: Jarayelɔi taoɔ tomato ni kpɛɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni dalɛ po yɔɔ mli ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa daa Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ ni sa Ni aduawai ni oookpa dani efee blɛoo tsɔ lɛ haa onáa nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ woɔ jara babaoo.

english: How long does a mango tree take to start bearing fruit compared to quick crops like tomatoes?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mango tso ko jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi? Kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa oya tamɔ tomato he?

english: While tomatoes give you a harvest within 3 to 4 months, grafted mango trees usually take 3 to 4 years to start bearing fruit. However, once a mango tree starts producing, it can continue yielding fruit every year for over 30 years without replanting.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni tomato woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, mango tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi kɛ́ mango tso ko bɔi yibiiwoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eya nɔ ewo yibii daa afi nɔ ni fe afii 30 ni ehe ehiaaa ni adu lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Mango trees grow large branches and thick leaves over time. Giving them plenty of space—about 10 meters apart—ensures each tree gets enough sunlight and fresh air, which prevents fungal diseases and encourages more fruit growth.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ woɔ niji wuji kɛ baai ni mli tse yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ babaoo, ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 10 lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa aduawai daa babaoo.

english: Can I plant short-term crops like tomatoes or maize between my young mango trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo tamɔ tomato loo ŋmãa yɛ mi mango tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, you can grow vegetables or food crops between young mango trees for the first 2 to 3 years. This allows you to earn income and feed your family while the mango trees are still small and haven't cast broad shade over the farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu aduawai loo niyenii nibii yɛ mango tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli, ni no baaha oná shika ni okwɛ oweku lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mango tsei lɛ darako lolo ni amɛbɛ hulutsoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Do weeds stop growing under mango trees once the trees grow big and thick?
ga: Ani jwɛi baakpa kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ mango tso shishi kɛ́ eda ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: As mango trees mature, their heavy leaf canopy blocks sunlight from reaching the ground. This natural shade prevents most weeds from growing underneath, which saves you labor and weeding costs compared to open crop fields.
ga: Kɛ́ mango tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, ŋwɛitsu lɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ tsiɔ jwɛi babaoo naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ shishi. Enɛ haa nitsumɔ kɛ jwɛi shwiemɔ he nyɔmɔwoo baa shi kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji ni agbele naa lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I keep planting tomatoes on the same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu tomato yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes repeatedly on the same plot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows tomato pests and soil-borne diseases to build up. Rotating tomatoes with crops like cassava or beans keeps the soil healthy and stops diseases from spreading.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, abaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tomato mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ aba. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei atsake tomato. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open while they are still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when their water supply is uneven, such as a sudden heavy rainfall after a long dry spell. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the outer skin, causing it to burst. Keeping soil moisture steady helps prevent cracking.
ga: Tomatoi fiteɔ kɛji nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ. Yibii lɛ amli fã lɛ daa oya fe kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ, ni no haa egbɛɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa etse.

english: Why do the flowers on my mango trees fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mango tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Mango flowers drop off mostly due to pest attacks, fungal diseases during rainy periods, or severe dry weather when the flower buds form. Protecting the trees with proper pruning and safe spray treatments before flowering saves the blossoms.
ga: Mango fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli. Fungal helai yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa beni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ abu tsei ahe kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe nɔ dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and turn yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread leaf curl virus during warm weather. Protecting young plants with nets or controlling whiteflies early keeps the plants green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ leaf curl hela lɛ amɛshwãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli. Tsei bibii ahebuu kɛtsɔ ŋshɔŋ loo mra be mli whitefly hebuu nɔ Ebaaha tsei lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow while the rest of the plant is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure early in the season keeps leaves green and improves your grain yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know if the caterpillars on my farm are fall armyworms, and why do they destroy my maize so quickly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni afolɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ amɛmiifite mi-abele lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Fall armyworms have a clear upside-down 'Y' shape on their heads and four dark spots on their tail end. They cause rapid damage because they hide inside the tender growing center of the plant, eating the leaves before they fully open.
ga: Autumn shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ‘Y’ ni tsɔɔ amɛhe ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ amɛyitsei anɔ kɛ ŋmeii ejwɛ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ amɛtsitsii lɛ anaa. Amɛfiteɔ nii oya ejaakɛ amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ dalɛ he lɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe kwraa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small even when the leaves on top grow huge and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ dara ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together or given too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant spends all its energy growing branches and leaves above ground instead of expanding its underground roots into thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei niji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli etsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fruit from forming. When temperatures stay too high, the plant drops its unfertilized flowers to conserve energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ efeee Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa trees to turn black and rot before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Pruning heavy branches and clearing weeds lets sunlight into the farm, drying out excess moisture and preventing the rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. niji ni tsii ni afoɔ ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ koni hulu la abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli Gbimɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ. ni atsĩ fitemɔ naa

english: Why is it risky to plant a lot of pepper just because my neighbor got high prices for pepper last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ ji oshara yɛ akɛni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ná ŋmeii jara ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ?

english: Crop prices change constantly; if every farmer plants pepper at the same time, the market becomes flooded at harvest time, causing prices to crash. It is safer to confirm buyer demand or plant different crops to protect your income.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ajara tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji okwaafoi fɛɛ du ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ Nu eyi jara lɛ nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji jara ni baa shi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oooma nɔ ni hɔlɔ lɛ biɔ lɛ nɔ mi loo ooodu nibii srɔtoi ni okɛbu oshika he.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give high yields for only one generation. Replanting seeds saved from a hybrid harvest produces weaker plants, uneven cobs, and a much lower total yield.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ kome pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ hybrid ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ. Cob lɛ ejaaa. ni nɔ ni afee lɛ fɛɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do weeds hurt my young crops more during the first month than when the crops are older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli fe be mli ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have small root systems and need maximum sunlight, water, and fertilizer to get established. Weeds steal these vital resources during the critical early stages, permanently stunting the crop's growth.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛbiɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo dani amɛdara. Jwɛi juɔ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ yɛ shishijee be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ dalɛ afee mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why should I pinch off the low side-branches of my pepper plants when they are young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli beni eji gbekɛ lɛ?

english: Removing early lower shoots encourages the plant to build a strong main stem and deeper roots first. This creates a sturdier structure capable of carrying heavier fruit without breaking later in the season.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ mra lɛ, ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni efee shishifã titri ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa tsɔne lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni baanyɛ awo aduawai ni tsii ni ekuuu yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot so quickly in storage after I dig them up from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams easily rot when bruised or cut during harvesting because bacteria enter through the open wounds. Curing harvested yams in a shaded, well-ventilated spot allows cuts to heal and the skin to thicken before storage.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ loo afo amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli ejaakɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ boteɔ pilamɔ ni agbele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ atsa sweet potatoes ni akpa yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni pilamɔi lɛ atsa ni hewolo lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani akɛto.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni haa baa lɛ daa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it bad if I put too much fertilizer on my crops at once?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe shikome?

english: Yes, applying too much fertilizer can burn the roots and leaves, damaging or killing the crop. Excessive fertilizer can also be washed away by heavy rain before the plant can use it, wasting your money.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi kɛ baai ashã. Ebaanyɛ efite loo efite ŋmɔshi nibii. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ dani tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii. Enɛ baaha ofite oshika.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small flowers without producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Agbee shi ni afeee pod?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree experiences stress from extreme sun heat, lack of soil moisture, or insect attacks. Planting shade trees and mulching around the roots helps retain water and protect flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa ni aduɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot inside the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water in the soil cuts off oxygen to the cassava roots, causing root rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ni no haa amɛgboiɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting even though the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt or root rot fungi in wet soil. The disease blocks the water-carrying tubes inside the plant, causing it to wilt even when plenty of water is in the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo ŋmeii shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ nu ni akɛyaa tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Enɛ haa egbiɔ kɛ́ nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli po.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips. Spraying recommended insecticides or neem oil solutions helps control these insects and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebu baai heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea crop right when the flowers appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ je kpo pɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers and soft young pods are sweet and tender, which naturally attracts pests like pod borers. Timely spraying with protective pest control measures during flowering keeps pods safe.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ŋɔɔ ni amɛhe jɔ. Amɛgbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pod borers. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ahiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Yes, beans and maize grow very well together. Beans take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which naturally nourishes the maize plants and improves overall yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli. Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tso lɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa yibiiwoo fɛɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants take so long to yield when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting plantains too close creates overcrowding, forcing them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving them proper spacing allows each plant to fruit faster and produce bigger bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha gbɔmɛi ayi obɔ fe nine. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. He ni sa ni ato lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ewoɔ yibii oya ni ewoɔ kui wuji.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops while they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil food from young crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the nutrients and light it needs to grow quickly without competition.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ la fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to plant plantains on the same land when setting up a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ beni atoɔ kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil cool until the cocoa trees are old enough to handle direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni hulu la baanyɛ ashɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch direct sunlight easily. Getting maximum sunlight allows the plant to produce more energy and grow much larger tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ashɛ amɛbaai lɛ ahe oya. Hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ haa tsei feɔ hewalɛ babaoo. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-decayed manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant roots decay after harvest, that nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli kɛ́ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my cassava crop lose all its leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava sheds its leaves during dry periods to conserve water and prevent itself from drying out. The plant is not dead; once the rains return, it will quickly sprout fresh green leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛhiɛ nu mli ni ekɛtsi enaa koni ekagbi. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Baai eŋɔli heei baakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Yɛ mi kookoo tso lɛ nɔ koni egbee shi ni etsɔko kookoo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by heat, dry soil, or a lack of pollinating insects like midges. Keeping shade trees on the farm and maintaining soil moisture helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nibii ni haa fɔfɔii tamɔ midge lɛ bɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my crop roots turn black and rot when water stays pooled on my farm for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water covers the ground for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing them to drown, stop taking up food, and rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa amɛshwieɔ nu mli, amɛkpaa niyenii yeli, ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from under the leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects. Controlling the insects prevents further leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kooloi ahe nitsumɔ baaye abua ni akafite baa lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: This condition, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium, usually because the soil moisture is uneven. Keeping the soil consistently damp helps the plant uptake calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa lɛ hewɔ ni enɛ baa lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce smaller yields even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa midumɔ nii lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for fertilizers and sunlight in the soil. When weeds are left in the farm, they steal the nutrients that your crops need to form large fruits, tubers, or grains.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji ashi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Ejuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛfee aduawai wuji, ŋmeii, loo dumɔwui.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has to the top leaves to keep growing, so applying nitrogen fertilizer at the right stage will help turn all leaves green and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ fɛɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Pepper flowers often fall off when the air gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Providing consistent watering and light shade during extremely hot days helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruits form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ shigbeemɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: How do I know which side of a cassava stem cutting should face up when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male fã ni esa akɛ madu mi-cassava niji lɛ yɛ nɔ?

english: Look closely at the small buds or 'eyes' where leaves used to grow on the stem. Make sure these buds are pointing upward toward the sky before sticking the bottom end into the ground so the new shoots grow up correctly.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni be ko ni eho lɛ baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ miitsɔɔ ŋwɛi dani okɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam leaves need to capture as much sunlight as possible to make food. When you stake the vines upright, the leaves spread out into the sunlight instead of bunching on the ground, allowing the plant to send more food down into growing big tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai he miihia hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ wain tso lɛ ma shi shiŋŋ lɛ Baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii babaoo majeɔ bulb ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling tightly and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking sap from the young shoots and spreading viruses. Controlling these pests early with neem oil spray keeps the leaves healthy and flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ nɛɛ nɔyeli mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water, food, and sunlight away from the main mother plant. Leaving only one strong sucker ensures the mother plant has enough strength to grow a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi sucker ni mli wa kome pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso nyɛ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdumɔwui wuji ni tsii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my farm help improve the land for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha he ni miyɔɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the earth, feeding whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does rice need so much standing water in the field compared to crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants can grow easily in flooded soil, but most weeds cannot survive under water. Keeping shallow standing water in the paddy stops weeds from growing without harming the rice roots.
ga: Omɔ tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Shi jwɛi babaoo nyɛɛɛ ahi shi yɛ nu shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa ni efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the dry earth around my cabbage roots with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle kaabe shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass acts like a protective blanket that keeps the hot sun from drying out the moisture in the ground. This keeps the plant roots cool and moist, reducing how often you need to water.
ga: Mulch ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ bɔ ni okɛ nu shwieɔ shi shii abɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my young orange tree dropping its small green fruits before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso bibioo lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Dani ebaada agbo?

english: Young citrus trees drop extra fruits if they do not have enough water or nutrients to support them all, or if pests damage the stems. Regular watering during dry weeks and applying balanced fertilizer helps the tree hold onto its fruit.
ga: Citrus tsei bibii lɛ baawo aduawai krokomɛi kɛji amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ fɛɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kpata tso lɛ shishi lɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baaye abua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aduawai amli.

english: If I plant rubber trees on my land, how many years will I have to wait before I can start collecting latex from them?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu rɔbɔt tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ mɔ ko amɛ dani anyɛ akpa latɛs lɛ?

english: Rubber trees usually take about 6 to 7 years to reach maturity. They are ready for tapping once the trunk reaches a circumference of about 50 centimeters at chest height.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛdaraa. Efee klalo akɛ ebaatswa kɛji akɛ tsɔne lɛ he lɛ ebɔle ehe aaafee sɛntimitai 50 kɛjɛ etsitsi lɛ he.

english: Why do rubber farmers tap their trees very early in the morning instead of later in the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ rɔbɔt okwaafoi tswaa tsei leebi moŋ fe gbi lɛ?

english: Latex flows much better when temperatures are cool and humidity is high. During the hot afternoon, the tree loses moisture, causing the latex to dry quickly and stop dripping.
ga: Latex lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kwraa kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo. Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ mli ejɔ. Ehaa latex lɛ gĩɔ oya ni ekpaa shwiemɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Large trees provide essential shade and retain soil moisture, protecting fragile cocoa seedlings from scorching heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni eda lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Buu kookoo dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava farm curling up and developing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by small insects called whiteflies. It reduces the plant's ability to make food, resulting in smaller tubers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji Cassava Mosaic Virus, ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ amɛshwãa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Ehaa tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo.

english: What causes my yam tubers to turn soft and rot inside the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Yam rot underground is usually caused by waterlogged soil that lacks good drainage, or by fungal infections entering the tuber through cuts made during planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato fitemɔ baa. aloo kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni boteɔ tuber lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ mli yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow and staying small even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ bibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow maize leaves often indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Heavy rain can wash nutrients away beyond the reach of the plant's roots, requiring additional manure or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fe tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with weak stems that fall over easily in the wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete for sunlight and grow overly tall and weak trying to reach the light.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni ebaada tsɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eshɛ la lɛ he.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of essential nutrients like phosphorus needed for fruit development.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni he hiaa koni aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why do my newly transplanted plantain suckers dry up within a few weeks of planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei ni midu ehee lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli kɛjɛ be mli ni midu lɛ?

english: Suckers often die if their roots were damaged during removal, if they were planted during a dry spell without enough moisture, or if plantain stem borers attacked the bulb.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii gboiɔ kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ amɛ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli Aloo kɛji akɛ plantain stem borers lɛ tutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are my oil palm trees producing flowers but failing to form solid fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi ewooo aduawai akui ni wa lɛ?

english: Oil palms require specific tiny insects (weevils) for pollination. If pollination does not happen, or if the tree lacks nutrients like potassium, the flowers drop without forming oil-bearing fruits.
ga: Mu tso lɛ biɔ kooloi bibii (moths) kɛha pollination. Aloo, kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii ni woɔ fɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants burning when there is direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that dry out easily under full sun. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts as a living shield, keeping the plants cool and moist until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ tsɔne ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tight during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from water loss. It is a natural response that reduces the surface area exposed to the heat, helping the plant save moisture during dry spells.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu akafite. Eji adebɔɔ mli hetoo ni haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hulutsoo baa lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do insects destroy my vegetable crops more during the dry season than during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-vegetables lɛ babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dry conditions make plants weak and thirsty, making it harder for them to fight off pests. Warm temperatures also speed up insect breeding, leading to larger pest populations during dry periods.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni kumai yeɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa waa akɛ aaawu ashi tsɛŋemɔ helai. He ni mli edɔ lɛ hu haa kooloi kɛ amɛhe feɔ yakayaka nii oya. Enɛ haa ŋmeii babaoo baa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on the same farm with my maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and puts it into the soil. This naturally enriches the soil, giving neighboring crops the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to recover. It also creates a safe home for soil diseases and pests that specifically target that crop.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Ehaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ feɔ shia ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe hu.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow plenty of leafy stems but very few fruits when I use too much chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo tsu nii lɛ?

english: Fertilizers high in nitrogen encourage quick leaf and stem growth. When plants get too much nitrogen early on, they use all their energy on leaves instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai kɛ tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya. Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo mra Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Crowding plants causes them to fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stems and very small crop yields compared to properly spaced plants.
