ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa, ni ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ baa kɛ akɛto tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: How do weeds growing around my yam plants cause the tubers to stay so small?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te fee tɛŋŋ ni mi sweet potato tso lɛ ná eshishifãi bibii nɛkɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your yam plants need. Without enough food and light, the yam plant cannot feed its underground tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa o-sweet potato tsei lɛ. Kɛji niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ mlɛo bɛ lɛ, Sweet potato tsei lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why do I need to cut away some of the extra shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, drink water and food from the mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main plantain tree has enough energy to grow a heavy bunch.
ga: Tsoi krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots Nuu nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to plow and loosen the soil deep down before planting root crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni mafo mli dani madu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Loosening the soil makes it easy for roots and tubers to expand deep into the ground. It also helps rainwater soak deep into the earth where plant roots can find it during dry days.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Eha nugbɔ nu hu boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ ana lɛ yɛ gbii ni nugbɔ enyɔ shi lɛ amli.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a natural survival behavior to save water and protect their underground tubers. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo su ko ni akɛbuɔ nu he ni abuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ahe. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know which direction to plant a cassava stem cutting in the soil so it grows properly?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ odu o-cassava tso lɛ yɛ bɔni afee ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Look closely at the small buds along the stem where leaves used to grow. Those small buds must point upwards toward the sky so the roots grow down into the soil and the shoots grow straight up.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Esa akɛ nakai fɔfɔi bibii lɛ anyiɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ be ko ni eho lɛ asɛɛ jogbaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ adara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ŋmeii lɛ hu adara kɛya ŋwɛi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do I need to heap soil high into mounds before planting my yam seed pieces?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabua sũ ŋmɔtɔ naa dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand into large tubers. Mounding the soil creates a deep, well-aerated bed that allows the tubers to grow big easily and protects them from sitting in water during heavy rains.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ bulbs agboi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ haa he ko ni mli kwɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa yitso lɛ ni edaa mlɛo. ni etsĩ enaa koni ekatara nu mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over on its own right when the fruits start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ aduawai lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that struggle to hold up heavy fruit bunches. Supporting the main stem with a strong, forked wooden pole helps bear the heavy weight until the plantains are ready for harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛmɔ aduawai akui ni tsii amli. Tso titri lɛ ni akɛ tsei ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ muji lɛ sɛɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do the small cocoa pods on my tree turn black and dry up before they fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Ani mitsei lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani amɛshɛɔ shweremɔ he?

english: This behavior is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads in humid, shaded conditions. Pruning extra shade branches and clearing weeds allows sunlight and air to dry out the pods and keep them healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ni ji black pod lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ subaŋ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo ni afolɔ mli kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing tall and skinny without producing large cobs of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo abele ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. Spacing them out properly gives each plant enough energy to form big, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmãa toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce a lot of green leaves but very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔlii babaoo shi fɔfɔi fioo pɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages bean plants to spend energy producing leaves instead of flowers. Balanced nutrients and avoiding excess chemical fertilizer encourage the crop to bloom and set pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛfee baai moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Niyenii ni ja kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turn black and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni midu lɛ shishi lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This behavior, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture steady helps the tomato fruit grow without dark rotted spots.
ga: Atsɛɔ subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato aduawai lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni ŋmɔtɔ diŋ bɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling is a defense response when tiny pests like aphids or thrips suck the sap from young leaves. Inspecting the undersides of the leaves and using neem oil or insecticidal soap stops the damage.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ko ni akɛbuɔ he kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips miinu nu ni jɛɔ baabii bibii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha nɔ ni efite lɛ akpa.

english: Why does my farmland stay wet and swampy long after rain, making my crop leaves turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Poor drainage traps water around root zones, choking roots of air and making leaves turn yellow from root distress. Building raised ridges or shallow drainage channels allows excess rain water to flow away safely.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ. ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ahe haomɔ mli. Nugbɔshiimɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct heat from the sun. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that create shade, keeping the young cocoa plants cool and moist during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo. Ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and grow very weak when I put too many seeds into one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ waa kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds grow in the same spot, their roots fight each other for food and water in the soil, and their leaves block light from one another, leaving them all starved.
ga: Beni dumɔwui babaoo tsɔ ni miida yɛ he kome lɛ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ ye amɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn brown and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry weather to stop water from escaping through the leaves. This helps the plant protect its underground tubers and stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛbuɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the dry Harmattan wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ tswa lɛ?

english: The hot, dry Harmattan wind causes trees to lose water quickly, so the cocoa tree drops flowers and small pods to conserve water and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ haa tsei amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. No sɛɛ lɛ, cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Koni okɛ nu ato he ni obu ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites sucking juices from under the leaves, which spreads plant viruses and stops normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli ni ekpaa dalɛ ni sa.

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water sits in the soil for too long without good drainage, creating conditions where fungal germs can attack and breakdown the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu kpakpa hoɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛgbala mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my maize crops produce smaller harvests when I plant them on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil repeatedly without giving the ground time or different plants to restore its richness.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ. ni ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ loo tsei krokomɛi be koni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛwo amɛfɔmɔ nii lɛ ekoŋŋ

english: Why do the lower leaves of my plantain trees turn bright yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, so it moves available food from its older leaves up to nourish the new, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when daytime temperatures get too high or when they experience sudden water stress, as the plant cannot support fruit development under stress.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ amɛna nu he haomɔ trukaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nyɛɛɛ aye abua aduawai ni yaa hiɛ yɛ nɔnyɛɛ shishi.

english: Weeds are wild, naturally tough plants that are better adapted to local soil conditions, allowing them to absorb nutrients and water much faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni wa kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli. ni baanyɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii kɛ nu oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Can I just take the corn I bought at the market and plant it on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa ni ahe yɛ jara nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Corn bought at the market is usually meant for food, not planting. Using certified seeds from a reliable supplier gives you crops that resist local diseases and yield much bigger cobs than regular market grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ ŋmãa ni aheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa niyenii, shi jeee ŋmãa ni aduɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni jɛ mɔ ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ enɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha oná tsei ni nyɛɔ helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe jarayeli ŋmaa.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for soil food, water, and sunlight. Giving each plant enough space ensures it gets all the sunlight and nutrients it needs to produce big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ená hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo tso agbo ni mli wa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Applying the right fertilizer early gives the crop the nourishment it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsuɔ nii mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara waa.

english: How do I know the right time to put fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Crops need fertilizer when they are growing fast, usually a few weeks after sprouting and again just before flowering. Applying it at the wrong time wastes money because the plant cannot absorb it properly.
ga: Tsei he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ́ amɛmiida oya. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ, kɛ ekroko hu dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ akɛwo mli yɛ be ni esaaa mli lɛ, ebaafee shikafitemɔ ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is all fertilizer the same, or does my corn crop need a specific type?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ji ekome? Aloo ani mi-abɛi tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko?

english: Different crops need different types of plant food. Corn needs balanced fertilizers like NPK early on for root and leaf growth, followed by nitrogen-rich types like Urea to build heavy grain cobs.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi biɔ tsei niyenii srɔtoi. Abɛi he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ NPK mra. kɛha shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ Nyiɛmɔ sɛɛ kɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ urea koni ekɛfee dumɔwui ni tsii.

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's natural way of protecting itself from losing too much water in the heat. It is a signal that your crop is stressed and urgently needs rainfall or watering.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekafite nu babaoo yɛ latsaa be mli. Eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihao ni nugbɔ loo nu he miihia amɛ oya.

english: Why do my crops grow very well on one side of my land but stay small on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã kome shi amɛhe ehiaaa yɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Soil quality is not always the same across a whole field. One area might have richer soil or hold water better, while the poor area may need extra manure or fertilizer to catch up.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su lɛ ji ekome yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Ekolɛ he ko baanyɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni baa nii babaoo loo nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni hei ni ohiafoi yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ abi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he kɛha nibii ni akɛtoɔ.

english: Why are there small caterpillars chewing holes in my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. They hide inside the central leaves of the plant and chew through them, which can stunt the corn's growth if not treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ ŋmãa dalɛ naa kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why do weeds cause my crop plants to grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm; they quickly drink up the water and fertilizer meant for your crop. Clearing weeds early leaves all the nutrients in the soil for your plants.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛnuɔ nu oya ni amɛwoɔ onibii amli ŋmɔshi nibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baajie niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛha otsei lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my corn is fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Corn is ready when the green husk leaves around the cob turn dry and brown, and the grains feel hard when you press them firm with your fingernail.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo beni ŋmeii eŋɔli lɛ jeɔ kpo ebɔleɔ he lɛ. Cob lɛ egbi ni eyɛ asarasu. Ni dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛ́ okɛ onineshi tsɔne lɛ miimɔ amɛnɔ waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings burning and drying up in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitso ni amɛmiigbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, full sunlight. They need shade trees or plantain plants above them to block the hot sun and keep the soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei loo tsei ni haa amɛnáa ŋmɔlɔ koni amɛná ŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantain alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ mimasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ?

english: Plantain grows fast and has big leaves that act as a shelter for cocoa seedlings, protecting them from harsh sunlight while giving you crops to sell or eat while waiting for the cocoa to produce.
ga: Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shĩa kɛha kookoo dumɔwui. Buu dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. kɛfata ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa koni ahɔ̃ɔ loo aye be mli ni amɛmɛɔ ni afee kookoo lɛ he

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to build strong green leaves and grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I apply my fertilizer after it rains instead of when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the crop roots can drink it in. Placing fertilizer on dry soil can burn the plant roots and waste the fertilizer.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Why will planting my crops very close together give me a smaller harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mitsei lɛ ni miduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ woɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and small fruits.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaawuu koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fioo. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ aduawai bibii baa.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight that your crops need to stay healthy and produce a good yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with wooden sticks instead of leaving them on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei adu sweet potato wain tsei lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up into the sunlight so the plant can make more food to grow big tubers, while keeping leaves off the damp ground prevents rotting.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni amɛkafite.

english: What is causing small holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ

english: These holes are usually made by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides in the leaves of young corn plants and eats them before the plant matures.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli ni amɛyeɔ nii dani tsei lɛ daraa lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ nɛkɛ buji nɛɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and testing one plant shows tubers that feel firm and filled with starch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni kaai ni afee yɛ tso kome nɔ lɛ jie bulbs ni nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyi kɛ starch lɛ kpo.

english: Why do hybrid seeds I buy produce better crops than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni miheɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially combined in a laboratory to give high yields and fight off diseases, but saved seeds lose those special qualities in the next generation.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ feɔ ekome yɛ laboratori ko mli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ewo yibii babaoo ni ekɛ helai awuu. Shi dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Can my young maize plants recover and grow back if cattle eat the top leaves?
ga: Ani mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛdara ekoŋŋ kɛji tsinai ye baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yes, if young maize plants are grazed before their growing point rises above ground level (usually before the 4 to 5 leaf stage), the plant can regrow new leaves from the base, though harvest may be delayed.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ aye ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ dani he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ etee ŋwɛi fe shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. (bei pii lɛ dani baa 4 kɛyashi 5 lɛ baashɛ) tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ baai heei kɛjɛ shishigbɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nikpamɔ lɛ baanyɛ asɛɛ afo moŋ.

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow in parts of the field where heavy farm animals walked frequently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi babaoo ni ŋmɔ mli kooloi babaoo fɔɔ jɛmɛ yaa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy animal hooves press soil particles tightly together, creating compacted soil that squeezes out air and makes it difficult for crop roots to spread, breathe, and soak up water.
ga: Hooi ni tsii lɛ nyɛɔ sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ anɔ waa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. ni ehaa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã, amɛmu, ni amɛŋɔ nu

english: What fast-growing plants can I grow around my farm boundary to keep stray livestock out of my field?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ makwɛ yɛ mihe? miŋmɔ lɛ naa koni kooloi ni elaaje lɛ akashɛ miŋmɔji lɛ ahe

english: Planting dense living hedges like vetiver grass, Jatropha, or thorny shrubs around your field creates a natural physical barrier that deters wandering animals while helping to prevent soil erosion.
ga: Tsoi bibii ni yɔɔ wala mli tamɔ vetiver, jatropha loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ ni ooodu lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli, adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ kooloi ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ anaa yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ naa.

english: Are there specific crops I can plant on my farm borders that grazing animals naturally refuse to eat?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ madu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ naa ni kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ kpooɔ ni amɛyeɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Crops like hot chili peppers, ginger, and sesame contain natural chemicals, strong smells, or bitter tastes that livestock dislike, making them effective defensive border crops.
ga: Tsofai ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli, ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa, loo ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa ni kooloi sumɔɔɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ chili peppers, ginger, kɛ sesame mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ tso ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni buɔ mɔ he.

english: Why do my maize crops grow taller and greener when I plant beans or cowpeas between the rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen gas from the air and release it into the soil, providing free, natural plant food that helps nearby crops like maize grow faster and stay healthy.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very thin stalks and small cobs when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ ŋmeii bibii beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, leading to weak growth and smaller yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai wuɔ amɛhe koni amɛná nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni faaa Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo fioo baa.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough moisture for my seeds to germinate safely after the first rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha midumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil into a ball; if it holds its shape without dripping water and crumbles easily when gently pressed, the moisture level is ideal for seed planting.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ fioo ko ni okɛfee bɔɔlu. Kɛji akɛ ehiɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli ni nu shwieee shi ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ anyɛ nɔ fioo lɛ, no lɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sa kɛha dumɔwui adumɔ.

english: Dropping leaves during hot dry weather is cassava's natural defense mechanism to stop water from evaporating through its leaves, allowing the stem and roots to stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni ashiɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni buɔ ŋmei he koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli kɛho. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Leaf curling on hot days is a plant's temporary defense to shade itself and reduce moisture loss; as long as the plant uncurls in the cooler evening, it is simply protecting itself from heat.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ buɔ ehe yɛ be kukuoo mli koni eha ená hulutsoo ni ekɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Eji koni obu ohe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the ground when water sits on the field after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need oxygen from the soil to stay healthy; standing water drowns the root system and creates ideal conditions for soil fungi to invade and decay the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni sũ mli ŋmeii lɛ abatutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many tiny flowers, but only a few of them actually turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi amɛteŋ fioo pɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but they rely on tiny insects called midges to move pollen from one flower to another. If there are not enough midges or good moisture in the farm, most flowers drop off without forming pods.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi amɛyeɔ kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii koni amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko mli. Kɛji ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: What is pollination, and why do insects need to visit my crop flowers?
ga: Mɛni ji pollination? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni kooloi bibii ayasara fɔfɔi ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Pollination happens when insects like bees or tiny midges carry pollen from one flower to another. This act fertilizes the flower so it can stop dropping and start growing into a fruit or pod.
ga: Pollination baa kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii kɛ pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛtee ekroko mli. Nifeemɔ nɛɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ fɔmɔ nii koni amɛkpa shigbeemɔ ni amɛje shishi amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning up in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. When they lack shade from bigger plants like plantains, the sun burns their leaves and starves them of water, making them turn yellow.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ amɛnáaa hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ lɛ, hulu lɛ shãa amɛbaai lɛ ni ehaa nu sɛɛ foɔ amɛmli. ni haa efeɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot while they are still hanging on the tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: This is black pod rot, which is caused by a fungus that spreads in wet, dark conditions. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and wind pass through the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod rot, ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ kɛbaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do cocoa pods grow directly on the main tree trunk instead of on the thin outer branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe niji bibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally flower and fruit on the thick trunk and main branches because cocoa pods grow heavy, and the strong trunk supports their weight until they mature.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ amɛniji wuji anɔ. Ejaakɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ shwiili. Ni tso ni he wa lɛ baafi muji lɛ sɛɛ kɛyashi ebaada.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods to fill my baskets with good seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ koni mikɛ dumɔwui kpakpai awo mli? Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli?

english: Pods are ready to harvest when their skin changes completely from green or deep red to a bright yellow or orange color. Harvesting too early means weak seeds, and harvesting too late causes seeds to sprout inside.
ga: Efee klalo akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baakpa kɛji amɛhewolo lɛ tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli kwɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ kwraa. Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ tsɔɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ. Ni nikpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mli.

english: Why am I harvesting fewer baskets of crops this season even though I planted the same acreage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsii amli lɛ fioo yɛ be nɛɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ he kome moŋ?

english: Soil loses its nutrients after supporting crops for many seasons. Without returning nutrients through manure or compost, the soil gets tired and produces smaller harvests over time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ beni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ bei babaoo mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ akuuu sɛɛ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baaa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui ni ewooo yibii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my farm crops look wilted during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu po?

english: On hot afternoons, leaf pores open and plants lose water to the air faster than roots can draw it from the soil. The plant droops briefly to conserve moisture and usually recovers when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ baagbele. Ni tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baashwie baai yɛ be kukuoo mli. koni ekɛha hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni bei pii lɛ, ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Should I clear all the big shade trees off my land before planting my main crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu tso titri lɛ?

english: No, keeping some large trees provides cool shade and protection from strong winds for crops like cocoa. The fallen leaves from shade trees also decompose into rich, natural soil fertilizer.
ga: Dabi, tsei wuji komɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo. Baai ni egbee shi kɛjɛɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ hu fiteɔ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why does my crop plant grow very tall with many green leaves, but fails to bear any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Plants grow excessive leaves instead of fruit when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough phosphorus or potassium. Balancing the nutrients encourages the plant to stop growing leaves and start fruiting.
ga: Tsei woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli ni phosphorus loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ja lɛ baawo tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkpa baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni amɛbɔi yibiiwoo.

english: Why do I need to leave a specific wide gap like 60 centimeters between my maize plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ abɔ he aaafee 60 cm moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow strong stalk support and produce large, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii baa.

english: Why is it safer for me to test a new seed variety on a small patch of land before planting my entire farm with it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maka dumɔwui heei makwɛ yɛ he bibioo ko lɛ? dani adu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hu

english: Crops react differently to local soils and weather. Testing on a small plot lets you see how the plant behaves in your specific farm conditions without risking your main food supply or whole investment.
ga: Tsei feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe. Kaa ni ooofee yɛ shikpɔji bibii anɔ lɛ haa onaa bɔ ni tsei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ oŋmɔ mli shihilɛ pɔtɛɛ mli. Ni okɛ niyenii titri ni onáa loo shika fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ wooo oshara mli.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my harvest to plant next season like my forefathers always did?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni mikpaa lɛ toɔ ni mikɛduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli, taakɛ miblematsɛmɛi lɛ fee be ko ni eho lɛ?

english: Many modern high-yielding seeds are bred to give maximum harvest only in their first planting. If you save and replant those seeds, the new plants lose their strong traits, growing unevenly and yielding much less crop.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui babaoo ni woɔ yibii babaoo koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ to ni odu lɛ Tsei heei lɛ baafite amɛhefɛo ni wa. Edaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Why does a crop variety that yields very well on a farm in another region fail to grow on my own land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni anyɛɛɛ adu tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii waa yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops are sensitive to local conditions like soil type, rainfall pattern, and temperature. A crop bred for wet, rich soil will struggle or fail if planted in dry or sandy soil, even if it is a high-quality seed.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nuɔ shihilɛi tamɔ shikpɔŋ henɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ dɔlɛ he. Tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, ni woɔ yibii lɛ baaná amanehulu loo amɛbaafee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo ŋã nɔ. Kɛji akɛ eji dumɔwu ni hi jogbaŋŋ po.

english: What happens to my cassava crops if I put too much chemical fertilizer in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Excess chemical fertilizer burns crop roots and forces the plant to grow thick green leaves while failing to develop large root tubers underground. It can also pollute and sour your farm's soil over time.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni fa fe nine lɛ shãa tsei ashishifãi ni enyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ be mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee shishifãi wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ebaanyɛ efite shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hu ni eha efee acid yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why does covering the ground with dry grass around my young vegetable plants keep them green during dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi dumɔwui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass acts like a protective shade that prevents the hot sun from evaporating ground moisture, keeping the crop roots cool and hydrated longer.
ga: Nibii ni akɛbaa loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekajie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the exact same bed of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, weakening future harvests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my young maize plants turn yellow and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal food, water, and light away from crop roots. Without enough sunlight and soil nutrients, maize leaves cannot produce the energy needed to stay green and grow.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli. Kɛji hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Abɛi baai nyɛŋ ajie hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and lose leaves when I cut down all the bigger trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ beni mifoɔ cacao tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally require shade to protect their soft leaves from harsh direct sunlight. Without tall trees to block the heat, the young crop dries out and becomes severely stressed.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Kɛji tsei kakadaŋŋ abɛ ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ naa lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛhaoɔ waa.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up and turn yellow during heavy rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and humidity encourage fungal diseases and insect pests like whiteflies to spread quickly across crop leaves, damaging their ability to carry water and food throughout the plant.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ waa lɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ whiteflies lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya yɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli fɛɛ. Efiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii baatsɔ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and dry under the bright sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to act as living umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist until they grow older.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Yellowing starting at the bottom leaves of maize usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the fresh new leaves at the top, leaving the old bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ ni oooha amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cassava plant have huge leafy stems above ground but small, thin tubers underground when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or excessive water early on, it puts all its energy into making leaves and stems instead of storing energy underground in the tubers.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ yɛ shishijee mli Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee baai kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ oyitsoŋ lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants drop and wilt when heavy rain floods my field for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Roots need air from the soil to breathe just like humans do. When water sits on the farm without draining, it drowns the roots, causing them to rot and stop sending water up to the leaves.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ejeee kpo Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Ehaa fitemɔ baa ni ekpaa nu ni ekɛyaa baai lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce smaller fruits when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, their leaves fight each other for sunlight and their roots fight for the same water and nutrients in the soil, so no single plant gets enough food to thrive.
ga: Kɛji abua tsei anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso ko bɛ ni nine shɛɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni eda.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they get stressed by extreme afternoon heat, poor watering, or when beneficial insects like bees are not around to visit and pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa ha amɛ hao yɛ shwane mli. nu ni ehiii Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ jɛmɛ koni amɛbasara ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl and droop in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In the hot sun, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can pull water from the soil. Curling and drooping is the plant's natural way of shrinking its leaf surface to save moisture until the afternoon cools down.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Curling kɛ drooping ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi shwane mli hulu lɛ baashɛ shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale and grow much slower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops. They act like unwanted guests eating the crop's food before the crop gets a chance to drink or feed.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbɔi ni ataooo amɛ, ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ nii loo amɛyeɔ nii.

english: Yam leaves produce food for the tuber using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward the sun and keeps them dry, preventing leaf diseases and giving the vine maximum energy to build big tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tuber lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ. Etsiɔ foliar helai anaa ni ehaa wain tso lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ bulbs agboi.

english: Why is my plantain tree producing small bunches even though it grew many sucker shoots around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ daa kɛfeɔ kui bibii eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ?

english: The small sucker shoots growing around the main plantain trunk share the same root system and steal nutrients away from the main mother plant. Removing extra suckers allows all the plant's energy to go directly into making a bigger fruit bunch.
ga: Tso bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ. Plantain tso titri lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii ni ejuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ aduawai akui wuji.

english: Why do these new, modern maize seeds yield so much more than the seeds I save from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa dumɔwui nɛɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specifically bred in laboratories to withstand local diseases, handle heat better, and produce larger cobs. Seeds saved from previous harvests lose these strong traits over time, leading to smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli yɛ laboratori ko mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛye helai ni baa jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Dɔlɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baa Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ baafite sui nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow even after I apply modern fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Crops turn yellow if the soil is too dry for the plant to absorb the fertilizer, if too much chemical burns the roots, or if heavy rain washes the nutrients away before the crop can take them in.
ga: Tsei lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Tsofa babaoo haa shishifãi lɛ shãa. Aloo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why does animal manure take longer to make my crops grow compared to chemical fertilizer in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ashishifãi heɔ be babaoo dani ekɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ kɛ akɛto tsofai ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers release nutrients instantly to the roots, giving a fast reaction. Animal manure must first be broken down by tiny organisms in the soil before the plant can feed on it, which takes more time but improves the soil for longer.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. cause a quick reaction Esa akɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ akumɔ kooloi ashishifãi lɛ amli. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tsei baanyɛ aye. Enɛ heɔ be babaoo shi ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ be babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. They need shade trees to act as natural sunshades that keep the leaves cool and retain moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants falling off during the dry season, and is the crop dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigboi?

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally when water is scarce to save moisture in its roots. The plant is not dying; it is protecting itself until the rains return to grow new leaves.
ga: Cassava baajɛ ebaa lɛ ashwie shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi lɛ bɛ. Tso lɛ gbooo, ebuɔ ehe he kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ eba ni baai heei baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do pests keep destroying my crops even after I spray them with modern insecticides?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie nɔ po lɛ?

english: Bugs can survive if the chemical is sprayed at the wrong time of day, if heat evaporates the medicine too fast, or if the same chemical is used repeatedly, allowing the insects to become immune to it.
ga: Kplukai baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji akɛ afɔse tsofai yɛ be ni esaaa mli. Dɔlɛ lɛ haa tsofa lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ Ebaaha kooloi lɛ anyɛ atsu tsofa lɛ he nii.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I harvest more crops from my small plot of land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani jeee mi nɔ ni?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with tall, weak plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa bibioo.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year if I plant maize on the exact same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year without giving the earth time to rest or replenish itself, while attracting more crop-specific pests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaaaa je lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe loo ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, egbalaa tsei pɔtɛɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo.

english: Why is it better to spray weed chemicals on my farm early in the morning rather than at afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ leebi fe shwane lɛ?

english: Early morning spraying allows the plants to absorb the liquid while the leaves are cool. In the hot afternoon sun, the heat evaporates the chemical before it works and can scorch the plant leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ mli ejɔ lolo lɛ. Yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Dɔlɛ lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛjeɔ shishi. ni ebaanyɛ eha tso baai lɛ ashã

english: Yam tubers grow underground and need soft, loose mounds to expand easily. If the soil is hard, rocky, or unplowed, the roots struggle to push through, resulting in small and deformed yams.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe miihia ni amɛná shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ babaoo koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo atsuuu he nii lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni efite.

english: When is the best time of day for me to spray chemical treatments on my crop fields?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: The best time to spray is early in the morning or late in the afternoon when temperatures are cool and winds are calm. During hot midday hours, heat causes the chemical liquid to evaporate into the air before killing pests, and wind can blow the spray away from your leaves.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu efee kpoo. Yɛ shwane mli gbi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Dɔlɛ lɛ haa tsofa mli nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani egbeɔ kooloi lɛ. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ kɛjɛ obaai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I see small holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the top leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Ni muji tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ aŋwɛi baai lɛ amli.

english: This is a sign of caterpillar feeding, such as the Fall Armyworm, which burrows deep into the growing point of the stalk during the night. The sawdust-like dirt is actually the waste the pest leaves behind as it feeds on the soft inner leaves.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii kɛyaa he ni tso lɛ tso lɛ daa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ gbɛkɛ lɛ miiye niyenii. Muji ni tamɔ ŋmei lɛ ji muji ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shiɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ beni amɛyeɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees burn and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate roots and thin leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Without temporary shade plants like plantains planted overhead to block the intense heat, the seedlings lose water faster than their roots can pull from dry soil, causing the leaves to dry up and drop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo. ni nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni mli wa tɛ̃ɛ Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko bɛ, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ yiteŋ koni ebu he kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience severe heat stress, severe drought, or too much water logged at the roots. When the plant feels under threat, it drops its blossoms to conserve energy for basic survival instead of producing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo ni naa wa he haomɔ he. hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli Beni tsei lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe miiwo gbeyei Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha shishijee wala yɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ.

english: This yellowing indicates a nitrogen deficiency in your soil. Nitrogen is the main food crops need to grow green and tall; when it is missing, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ ebɛ lɛ, tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my main crops right after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitso titri lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive, fast-growing root systems that steal water and nutrients much faster than young crops. If you do not weed your farm clean before applying fertilizer, the weeds will eat the plant food first and overcrowd your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa. Enɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya kwraa fe tsei bibii. Kɛji okɛ jwɛi shwieee oŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baaye tsei lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ni ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayi obɔ.

english: Why do I get thinner stalks and smaller yields when I plant my corn seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmeii ni mli tseee nɔ ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete against each other for limited sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients. Because no single plant gets enough food, all of them remain weak and produce tiny ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la ni faaa, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ tsei fɛɛ yaa nɔ egbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa bibii.

english: How do I know if the ground has enough moisture after the first rains for me to start planting maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ?

english: Dig about hand-deep into the topsoil, grab a handful of dirt, and squeeze it tightly in your palm. If the soil forms a firm wet ball without crumbling away immediately, the ground has absorbed enough rainwater to support seed germination.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aaafee nine kome mli. Okɛ sũ ni okɛwo onine mli lɛ atsu nii ni okɛmimɔ onine mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni efooo amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbalaa nugbɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes in the same soil year after year allows tomato-specific pests and soil diseases, like bacterial wilt and root nematodes, to build up in high numbers. Switching to crops like maize or cassava starves those pests and allows the soil to recover.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tomato nɔ pɔtɛɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai, tamɔ bacteria wilt kɛ root nematodes. accumulate a lot Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nakai kooloi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra bottom branches and shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kɛ suckers ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing lower branches forces the plant to send all its water and energy toward making larger fruits rather than extra leaves. It also keeps leaves off the wet ground and improves air circulation, preventing fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Kɛtsɔ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ atsu enu kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ he nii koni ekɛwo yibii agbo yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa baai lɛ ehiɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ anɔ, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ oya. Tsi fungal helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ naa.

english: What is this green plant growing directly on my cocoa tree branches, and why is it bad for my crop?
ga: Mɛni ji tso eŋɔli nɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kokoo nine lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: That plant growing on your branches is a parasite known locally as adedeɛ (mistletoe). It attaches directly to the wood of your cocoa tree to steal water and nutrients, which weakens the tree, causes branches to dry up, and significantly reduces your yield.
ga: Tso ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ otso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni ale lɛ akɛ adenium (mistletoe). Ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ kookoo tso he tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. egbiɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ni ehaa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa

english: How do parasitic plants like adedeɛ manage to start growing high up on my tree branches without soil?
ga: Parasitic tsei tamɔ Adedaeɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aje shishi akwɛ̃ yɛ tso nine ni sũ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Birds eat the sticky berries of the adedeɛ plant on other trees and drop the seeds onto your cocoa branches. The sticky seed glues itself to the bark, germinates, and sends root-like structures directly into your tree's stem to feed.
ga: Loofɔji yeɔ adedeɛ tso lɛ yibii ni kpɛɔ yɛ tsei krokomɛi anɔ lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, shwiemɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ okkoo nine lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni wa lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ, ni amɛtsuɔ nibii ni tamɔ shishifãi kɛyaa tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛyaye niyenii.

english: What is the best way for me to remove adedeɛ from my trees so that it does not grow back?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ majie ededeɛ lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ?

english: You should cut off the affected branch a few inches below where the adedeɛ is attached using a sharp pruning hook or saw. Simply pulling off the leaves leaves the parasite's root embedded inside the branch, causing it to regrow quickly.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei ni mli wa loo ŋmei ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ afo tsei niji ni ena hela lɛ he lɛ he ni kɛ he ni ededeɛ lɛ ekpɛtɛ he lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi 2-3. Gbalamɔ baai lɛ kɛkɛ. Parasite lɛ shishifãi lɛ hu bafeɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ mli. Ehaa ehe feɔ ehee oya

english: Will cutting off branches infected with adedeɛ hurt my cocoa tree's overall growth?
ga: Niji ni adidaeɛ hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ afolɔ Ani ebaana hewalɛ gbonyo yɛ kookoo tso lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ nɔ?

english: Removing an infected branch actually saves the whole tree. While you lose a small branch today, leaving adedeɛ on the tree will eventually destroy the entire branch and slowly kill the tree, costing you far more pods in the long run.
ga: Niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ hereɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ yiwala diɛŋtsɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɛnɛ obaafite tso nine bibioo ko moŋ, shi kɛ́ oshi adedeɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, yɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaafite tso lɛ nine muu lɛ fɛɛ ni ebaafite nakai tso lɛ fiofio Enɛ baaha ofite pods babaoo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Can I spray chemical weedkillers to destroy adedeɛ growing on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ afɔse koni mikɛfite adidae lɛ. Nɛgbɛ nakai nɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ?

english: No, you should never spray weedkillers on adedeɛ because the parasite is embedded directly into your cocoa tree's living skin. Any chemical strong enough to kill the parasite will also damage or kill your cocoa tree.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ Adedeɛ nɔ. Akɛni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ boteɔ cacao tso lɛ hewolo ni hiɛ ka lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsofa fɛɛ tsofa ni he wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ agbe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ hu baafite loo ebaafite o-cacao tso lɛ.

english: Why are my trees producing small cocoa pods and fewer flowers even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ woɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni fɔfɔii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: If your trees have adedeɛ growing on them, the parasite steals the fertilizer nutrients before they can reach the cocoa flowers and pods. You must remove the parasite first so your trees can use the fertilizer to grow heavy pods.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ miida yɛ tso nɔ lɛ Parasite lɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani eshɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔji lɛ ahe. Esa akɛ ojie tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo etsitsii ni tsii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I see more adedeɛ growing on cocoa trees that are directly exposed to hot sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa cacao tsei babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ cacao tsei ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Adedeɛ thrives in strong daylight. Cocoa trees that lack adequate shade trees around them get extra sunlight, which helps the parasite grow faster and spread more aggressively across your farm.
ga: Adedeɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Cocoa tsei ni bɛ hulutsoo tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Tso lɛ baaná hulu la kroko. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ daa oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check for and remove adedeɛ?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ ni majie adadeɛ?

english: You should inspect your farm every three to four months. Removing adedeɛ while it is still small prevents it from flowering, producing berries, and spreading seeds to other healthy trees on your farm.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ Kɛ́ ajie adenium lɛ be mli ni eyɔɔ bibioo lolo lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekawo fɔfɔi. feemɔ tsei ayibii ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ

english: What should I do with the adedeɛ branches after I cut them off my trees?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee Adede nitsumɔhe nine lɛ? Beni afo lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ sɛɛ?

english: Once adedeɛ is completely cut off from the host tree branch, it dies and cannot grow back from the soil. However, if it has berries, gather the cut branches and clear them away so birds cannot eat the berries and drop seeds on other trees.
ga: Kɛ́ afo adedeɛ ko kwraa kɛjɛ tso ni hiɛ kã nine mli lɛ. Ebaagbo ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi, kɛji akɛ tsei ayibii yɛ lɛ Bua tsei niji ni afo lɛ anaa ni oshɛrɛ amɛ ashwie. Enɛ ji koni okpoi akaye tsei ayibii lɛ ni amɛkashwie dumɔwui amɛshwie tsei krokomɛi anɔ.

english: Can adedeɛ spread onto my cocoa farm if my neighbor does not clean his trees?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji mikutsoŋnyo lɛ etsuuu etsei lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, birds freely fly between nearby farms and will carry adedeɛ seeds from your neighbor's infected trees to yours. It is best to encourage your neighboring farmers to clear their trees as well to keep the whole area safe.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, okpoi foɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ateŋ yɛ heyeli mli. ni ekɛ adedeɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ okutsoŋnyo tso ni hela emɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha bo. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooowo okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛjie tsei ni amɛkwɛ jɛmɛ fɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that dry out very quickly under direct heat. They need shade crops like plantains or bananas nearby to shield them from strong sun and keep the moisture in the soil while they establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya waa yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiisumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo banana ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni amɛtoɔ amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to stay green and grow tall. When nitrogen runs out in the soil, the plant pulls it from older bottom leaves to feed new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii tso titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ ba shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ jieɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When water sits in the ground for too long without draining, the roots drown from a lack of oxygen, allowing fungi in the soil to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagboi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atutua ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air so their leaves can catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the leaves produce energy, which travels down to feed the tuber underground and make it grow large and thick.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛjieɔ hewalɛ ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences sudden stress, such as severe heat, dry spells, or a lack of key soil nutrients like calcium. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔi trukaa, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, be ni nu hɔmɔ baa, loo niyenii ni he hiaa waa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why should I cut away extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: The small shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for water, sunlight, and food from the soil. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to concentrate its energy on growing a large bunch of fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ suckers. Amɛkɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso lɛ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad to spray insect chemical on my cowpea farm when the flowers are open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi yɛ mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Friendly insects like bees visit open flowers to feed and help pollinate them so healthy cowpea pods can form. Spraying harsh chemicals during bloom kills these helpful insects, resulting in fewer pods on your harvest.
ga: Kplukai ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo, tamɔ ŋmeii, yaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛha amɛ niyenii ni amɛye amɛbua kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ koni tsina ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ baagbe nɛkɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ. Enɛ haa pods fioo pɛ baa okpamɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing huge leaves without forming a hard head in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai wuji ni efeee yitso ni wa yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head when given too much nitrogen fertilizer or when temperatures get too high. Excessive nitrogen forces the plant to keep growing outer leaves instead of wrapping tightly into a firm center bulb.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ ajie yitso kɛji akɛ akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nitrogen babaoo nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ehiɛɔ esɛɛ baai lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a fĩɔ lɛ saminya kɛ peeɔ bulb ko ngɛ e kpɛti.

english: Why does planting groundnuts alongside my maize make the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ du ŋmei lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When the groundnut roots decay, they leave this free, natural plant food behind for crops like maize to feed on.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛsaa sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ sɛɛ koni amɛkɛye tsei tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Why should I cover my planted ginger beds with dry grass or palm leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai aha mi-ginger saatso ni midu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dried leaves, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool and damp, which ginger loves. It also blocks sunlight from reaching weed seeds, stopping them from growing and taking nutrients away from your ginger roots.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. ni ji nɔ ni ginger sumɔɔ Etsiɔ hulu la hu naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Enɛ haaa amɛdara, ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off the extra suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: If too many suckers grow at once, they steal food and water from the main tree, causing small fruit bunches. Leaving only the main tree and one strong sucker ensures you get big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ shikome Ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Ewoɔ aduawai akui bibii. Tso titri lɛ kɛ tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni eshwɛ koni ona plantain jwɛi agbo ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where they might rot and helps them catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaya hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi, ni ebaaha amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an important food for growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the plant will bring back its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛfataa Tsei ahe lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot continuously drains all the nutrients out of the soil and attracts persistent pests. Swapping maize with beans or cowpeas returns nutrients naturally back into the soil.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be, ni egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I wait until after it rains before putting fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Applying chemical fertilizer to dry ground can burn plant roots and waste the fertilizer. Moist soil helps the fertilizer dissolve safely so the roots can drink up the nutrients.
ga: Tsofa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni eha tsofa lɛ afite. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi shweshweeshwe bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily and protects the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ oya ni ebuɔ ŋmei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young maize stalks have holes chewed through the leaves from the inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ bu ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛmli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding inside the central shoot of the plant. Checking your crops early and applying neem seed extract or recommended treatments directly into the central funnel stops them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni oookwɛ onibii amli mra Ni okɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ awo gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha nakai tsei lɛ akpa.

english: Curling leaves are caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from underneath the leaves. Spraying the leaves with light soapy water or natural botanical sprays helps control these pests.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ Loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot or when the plants do not get consistent water. Watering your crops regularly at the base helps keep the plants stable so fruits can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Kɛ́ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ eshishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni ewo yibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the corn is fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani abele lɛ shwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient maize needs to grow strong and green. When nitrogen is low, the plant pulls nutrients from its older, lower leaves to feed the upper growing leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee eŋɔli.
