Kɛ nitrogen lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: The young shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plant for nutrients, water, and sunlight in the soil. Cutting away most suckers and leaving only one or two healthy ones directs energy back into the main stem to grow a larger bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Yam plants make food in their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground into maximum sunlight and airflow, which prevents fungal rot on the leaves and helps the plant store more energy down into growing a bigger underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akafite yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtoɔ hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs wuji.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field alongside my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally enriches the soil, providing free nutrients for the maize crop growing beside or after them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii kpakpai ni aheee nɔ ko. loo no sɛɛ

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings wilting and dying when planted in an open field without tall crops around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and cannot survive direct, intense sunlight. They need temporary shade from fast-growing crops like plantains or cassava to protect them from heat damage and keep soil moisture high while their roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo yucca lɛ adɛŋ. Koni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ lɛ he, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ahi shi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetable crops with dry grass help them survive during hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, shields the soil from the direct heat of the sun. This stops soil moisture from evaporating quickly, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ baatsi shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why shouldn't I grow pepper or garden eggs on the exact same piece of land where I harvested tomatoes last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-pepper eggs loo abɔɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mifo mi-tomato lɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Tomatoes, peppers, and garden eggs belong to the same crop family and share the same pests and soil diseases. Planting them continuously in the same spot allows disease organisms to build up in the soil, leading to sick crops in the next season.
ga: Tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔi yɛ tsei akuu kome mli, ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kome. Tsei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baaná hela yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes through the central leaves of my young corn plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ye bu ko kɛtsɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, pests that hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the hot daytime and come out at night to feed on tender leaves. Spotting them early allows you to apply recommended treatments directly into the plant funnel to stop them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni oje kpo gbɛkɛ koni oye baai bibii Oyoo amɛ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekpa amɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, rotten spots at the bottom even when the plant stems look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ eyɛ mli akɛ shishifãi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the developing fruit, usually triggered by inconsistent watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the roots continuously absorb calcium and prevents the fruit bottoms from spoiling.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛjieɔ calcium, ni ehaaa aduawai lɛ ahiɛ akafite.

english: How can I tell when cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efoŋ?

english: Cassava plants show signs of maturity when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the ground around the base of the plant starts to crack as the underground tubers swell up.
ga: Cassava tsei jieɔ dalɛ he okadii kpo kɛ́ amɛshishi baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Bare stems left Ni he ni tso lɛ shishi yɔɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow when water sits on my farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When water covers your field for long periods, it pushes out the air that roots need to breathe. Without air, the roots cannot absorb nitrogen from the soil, which makes the leaves lose their green color and turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ nu ha oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa ni shishifãi lɛ amu lɛ kɛyaa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ahe su eŋɔli lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells to save water. Losing leaves reduces the amount of moisture the plant releases into the hot air, allowing it to survive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Baai ni laajeɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni tso lɛ jieɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Ha ehi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow crooked and small instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, light soil to expand smoothly underground. If the soil is hard, packed down, or full of rocks, the growing tuber struggles to push through and ends up short, thin, or twisted.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ, Growing bulbs lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔ kuku, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do birds attack my rice crop mostly when the heads are soft and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ babaoo be mli ni amɛyitsei lɛ ji bibii lolo ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Birds prefer rice during the 'milky stage' because the developing seeds are soft, sweet, and easy to crush. Once the grains dry out and harden, birds find them much harder to feed on.
ga: Okpoi sumɔɔ ŋmãa yɛ ‘milk stage’ beaŋ ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe ŋɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Beni ŋmãa lɛ gĩɔ ni ewaa lɛ, ebaawa waa kɛha okpoi akɛ amɛaaye.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up like tiny bowls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ tsɛnsii bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of young leaves. This uneven damage forces the leaves to curl upward as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ fitemɔ ni ejaaa nɛɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and pale even when I use good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kpakpai tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your crops. When weeds surround your crops, the crops starve and stretch tall and thin trying to find sunlight.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ mli. Beni jwɛi ebɔle oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛbaakpã mli kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbɔɔ koni amɛna hulu la lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees take much longer to produce fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ́ midu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: Planting plantains too close causes their large leaves to shade one another and their roots to fight for the same soil food. Without enough sunlight and space, the trees grow much slower.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛbaai wuji lɛ atsĩ amɛnaa. Ni tso shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii he akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛji hulu la kɛ he ko bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo kwraa.

english: Why do tiny young pods on my cocoa trees turn black and shrivel up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji No hewɔ lɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi dani amɛdara.

english: This is often 'cherelle wilt,' which happens when the cocoa tree realizes it does not have enough water or nutrients to feed all its pods, causing it to naturally drop excess fruit to protect itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ ‘cherelle wilt’, ni baa beni cacao tso lɛ yɔseɔ akɛ cacao tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha pod muu lɛ fɛɛ aye abua lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, cacao tso lɛ jieɔ yibii ni fa fe nine yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛbu ehe he.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into tomatoes during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: High heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers so they cannot be fertilized. When a flower is not pollinated, the plant drops it because it cannot form a fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baafite pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔmɔ nyɛŋ aba mli. Beni fɔfɔii lɛ bɛ pollination lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbee shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller harvests every year even when I plant at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi lɛ? Kɛji midu yɛ be ni sa mli po.

english: Every time you harvest crops, they take nutrients out of the ground. If you do not return strength to the soil using compost, manure, or fertilizer, the soil gets exhausted and cannot feed future crops well.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii lɛ, ebaafite ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my full-grown cocoa trees suddenly drying up and dying in one part of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei ni eda lɛ miigbi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Sudden drying of cocoa trees is often caused by diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus or root rot fungi, which destroy the tree's internal tubes, stopping water and nutrients from reaching the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ kookoo tsei lɛ agbiɔ trukaa. ni fiteɔ tso lɛ mli paipii lɛ Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ shɛɛɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: What should I do immediately if I see one dead cocoa tree on my farm to protect the rest?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina cacao tso kome ni egbo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛbu cacao tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe?

english: You should isolate and cut down the infected tree along with surrounding contact trees, as roots underground touch each other and spread viral diseases quickly across the entire farm.
ga: Esa akɛ otsi tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ kɛ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe ni ofolɔ amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ taa amɛhe ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Why does my farmland seem much hotter and drier than it used to be years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni egbi fe bɔ ni eji yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing shade trees and broader climate shifts have exposed farm soils directly to intense sunlight, which dries out topsoil moisture quickly and leaves crops stressed.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baaha ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya, ni ekɛ haomɔ baa tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are dying from a lack of rainfall or from a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ miigboi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ loo hela hewɔ?

english: Drought causes trees across the entire farm to wilt uniformly, whereas diseases usually cause localized damage, such as swelling on stems, black spots on pods, or single patches of dying trees.
ga: Hɔmɔ lɛ eha tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ egbi pɛpɛɛpɛ. Yɛ be mli ni helai srɔtoi Bei pii lɛ, amɛfiteɔ he ko, tamɔ tso lɛ shishi fũuɔ, ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi, loo tsei ni miigboi lɛ ahe ŋmeii.

english: Can my free-roaming chickens spread diseases or cause harm to my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani mi-kooloi ni mikɛ amɛ yeɔ amɛhe lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã loo aye mi-cacao tsei lɛ awui?

english: Chickens do not spread cocoa viral diseases, but excessive scratching around young seedlings can expose shallow roots, damage delicate stems, and dry out the soil surrounding the base.
ga: Kooloi gbɛɛɛ kookoo hela lɛ eshwaaa. Shi kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwie shi tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ afee mlɛo. efiteɔ tsei ni waaa lɛ ni ehaa sũ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ egbiɔ

english: Why are insect pests damaging my cocoa pods more during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi babaoo fiteɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Insects like mirids (akate) multiply faster in warm temperatures and tend to feed heavily on young pods and shoots when trees are already weak from heat stress.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ mirids (akate) fɔɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ni amɛfɔɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yeli kɛ́ hulutsoo haomɔ ha tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and overly shaded conditions, spreading easily when rain droplets bounce from infected soil onto low pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔi shwie shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛtee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What causes my cocoa flowers to drop off the tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cacao fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Flowers fall off when the tree lacks key nutrients like potassium, suffers from insect attacks, or faces extreme stress from sudden dry spells right after flowering.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni kooloi bibii tutuaa lɛ. aloo ekɛ haomɔ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa lɛ mli kɛbaa beni fɔfɔi lɛ ewo sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ kpeɔ.

english: Why does my farm soil seem to lose its power to grow healthy cocoa after many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛduɔ kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ afii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous harvesting takes away essential minerals from the soil, and without replacing them using organic manure or fertilizers, the land becomes depleted and unproductive.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ nibii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tsuuu nii lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaawo yibii.

english: Why are shade trees necessary for protecting my soil and young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ he hiaa koni akɛbu mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Shade trees act as shield umbrellas that reduce direct sun heat, drop leaves that decompose into rich organic manure, and help hold moisture deep in the ground for cocoa roots.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ko ni haa dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. Baai ni egbee shi, ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛha kookoo shishifãi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient, or the soil has too much water. Applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer like urea or adding compost helps restore the green color and crop health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ lɛ mli nu babaoo yɔɔ mli Nitrogen ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from water stress during dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or insect attacks from pests like capsids. Ensuring proper shade cover and managing insect pests help the flowers mature into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ nu he haomɔ kpe amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli. Niyenii ni ehiii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids lɛ adɛŋ. Shade ni sa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my maize farm so it does not go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni akafite?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil while the crop is actively growing. A first application is recommended about two weeks after planting, followed by a second application four to six weeks after planting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ tsofa lɛ woɔ ŋaa aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Nyiɛmɔ sɛɛ kɛ shi ni ji enyɔ yɛ otsii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ.

english: Why do my rice plants grow many leaves and stems but very few grain heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer early in the season causes rice plants to focus on leaf growth rather than grain production. Balancing nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium encourages strong grain development.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ yeɔ hiɛ fe dumɔwui afeemɔ. Nitrogen kɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa ŋmaa ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot in the soil before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Cassava tubers rot when water collects around their roots during heavy rains, creating conditions for fungal diseases. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. kɛ fungal disease Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb lɛ mli.

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by bacterial wilt, a disease living in the soil that blocks water from moving up the plant stem. Rotating crops with maize or cassava and planting disease-resistant seed varieties helps prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni haaa nu aya tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ ni aduɔ dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: What is making the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and transmit viruses. Spraying the crop with neem oil extract or recommended insecticides can keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies kɛ chili baa baa. ni shwieɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni ekɛ hela lɛ baa Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha kooloi nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during light rains or wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees tumble when pests like root nematodes or stem borers destroy their root system underground. Mounding fresh soil around the base and planting clean, healthy suckers builds strong roots that anchor the tree.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi tamɔ root nematodes loo stem borers lɛ fite amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ hee ni abɔleɔ he Shishitoo ni he tse, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii feɔ shishifãi ni wa ni haa tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi.

english: Why are my harvested yams getting smaller every season even though I use the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi lɛ? Ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii?

english: Planting yam continuously on the same plot drains essential nutrients from the soil over time. Rotating yam with leguminous crops like cowpea or groundnut puts natural nitrogen back into the land to rebuild soil strength.
ga: Kɛ́ adu sweet potato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ. Enɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛtswa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Weeds are naturally hardy wild plants that absorb water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early in the crop's lifecycle prevents them from choking your main plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛheɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite otsei titrii lɛ.

english: Why does the market price of my plantains drop so low during certain months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ jara baa shi yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Plantains tend to mature at the same time across many farms during the peak harvest season. When the market is flooded with abundant supply, buyers have many choices and prices naturally drop because sellers are competing to clear their stock before it spoils.
ga: Plantains lɛ fɔɔ shweremɔ yɛ he kome. yɛ ŋmɔji babaoo amli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ jara lɛ yɛ nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baaná nibii babaoo ni amɛbaahala ni jara lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ nii lɛ miitswa akaŋ koni amɛjie nibii ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ dani amɛfite.

english: Why are plantains so expensive and hard to find in the market during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains jara wa waa ni ewa akɛ aaana yɛ jara nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees need a lot of water to produce bunches. During the dry season, fewer trees produce fruit, leading to a shortage in the market. When supply is low but people still want to buy plantains, prices go up significantly.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia plantains koni ekɛfee panicles. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tso lɛ baawo yibii fioo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji jarayeli mli nibii ni faaa Beni nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ faaa shi gbɔmɛi miisumɔ ni amɛhe plantains lolo No hewɔ lɛ jara lɛ etee ŋwɛi waa.

english: How can I plant my plantain suckers so that I don't harvest everything at the exact same time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu dumɔwui koni mikakpa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: You can practice staggered planting by planting small batches of suckers every few weeks or months instead of planting your whole field in one day. This spreads out your harvest over the year so you always have plantains to sell when prices are higher.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ staggered dumɔ nii akase kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Daa otsii loo nyɔji fioo komɛi Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome mli Enɛ baaha okpamɔ lɛ agbɛ ashwã afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, oyɛ ekãa be fɛɛ be ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ kɛ́ jara lɛ tee hiɛ.

english: Why do some of my plantain trees produce much smaller bunches after a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi shwereɔ bibii kwraa yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees feed heavily on soil nutrients with every crop they yield. If you do not add manure, compost, or fertilizer, and if you leave too many suckers growing around one mother plant, the soil gets exhausted and the bunches become smaller.
ga: Dumɔwui yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ tso fɛɛ tso ni woɔ yibii mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he, ni oshi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, single mother tree Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaho ni ŋmeii lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Why do my plantains turn yellow and soft so quickly after I cut them down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya beni mifo amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, plantains release a natural gas called ethylene that causes them to ripen rapidly. High temperatures, direct sunlight, and rough handling or bruising trigger the plantain to release more of this gas, speeding up the ripening process.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa Braves lɛ, ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene, ni no haa ehoɔ oya. Nibii ni mli edɔ waa, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nitsumɔ ni mli wa Loo ŋmɔlɔ baaha plantain lɛ ajie gas nɛɛ babaoo kpo. ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya oya.

english: What simple things can I do to keep my harvested plantains fresh while waiting for buyers?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo Abaanyɛ akɛ ekomɛi atsu nii koni akɛha dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ahi shi ehee be mli ni amɛmɛɔ mɛi ni baahe lɛ.

english: Keep your harvested bunches intact on the stalk and store them in a cool, well-ventilated, shaded area away from direct sunlight. Avoid stacking heavy bunches on top of each other to prevent bruising, which accelerates decay.
ga: Ha ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ahi tso lɛ shishi ni okɛto he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ. Eyɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni eyɛ hulutsoo, ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɛɛ jɛmɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni tsii ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe lɛ ahe koni akafite, ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ aya oya.

english: How do I know the best time to harvest my plantains so they stay good for transport to market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa mi-plantains lɛ? bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekɛya jara nɔ

english: Harvest plantain bunches when the individual fingers are full and rounded but still deep green. If you wait until a few fruits start turning yellow on the plant, the whole bunch will ripen too quickly during transit and spoil before reaching buyers.
ga: Kpaa plantains beni inchi fɛɛ inchi eyi ni ebɔle shi eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ. Kɛji omɛ aahu kɛyashi aduawai fioo komɛi je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, Aduawai lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshɛɔ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: How does heat during transportation affect the quality of my plantains?
ga: Te dɔlɛ ni baa yɛ gbɛfaa mli lɛ saa dumɔwui lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive heat in closed trucks or under hot sun makes plantains breathe faster and sweat, causing them to soften and develop black spots rapidly. Covering them with fresh palm fronds or keeping air flowing helps keep them cool and firm during travel.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine yɛ lɔle ni aŋã mli loo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa omuɔ oya ni okɛ latsaa shwieɔ shi. Ehaa hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ahe tsei heei ha amɛhe loo oha kɔɔyɔɔ je kpo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛhe jɔɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbɛfaa mli.

english: What can I do with my surplus green plantains so I don't lose money when no one is buying them fresh?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee kɛ plantains eŋɔli ni fa fe nine koni mikafite shika be mli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko heee amɛ ehee lɛ?

english: You can process unsold green plantains into plantain flour by slicing, sun-drying, and milling them. Plantain flour can be packaged and stored for many months without spoiling, allowing you to sell it later at a stable price.
ga: Abaanyɛ afee plantain ni ahɔ̃ɔɔ lɛ plantain ashikiŋsha kɛtsɔ amɛfolɔ, ni amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli, kɛ amɛshwiemɔ nɔ. Abaanyɛ akɛ plantain ashikishaŋ awo kotoku mli ni akɛto nyɔji babaoo ni efiteee. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ jara ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and the fruits fail to fill out during long periods without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ egbi ni aduawai lɛ eyimɔ obɔbɔ kɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants are made mostly of water and require constant moisture to carry nutrients from the soil up into the stem and fruits. Without adequate water, the plant cuts off supply to the fruit to survive, resulting in skinny or stunted plantains.
ga: Nu ji nɔ ni akɛfeɔ plantains babaoo ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli be fɛɛ be koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi kɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ baafo aduawai ni amɛnáa lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa plantains lɛ feɔ mlɛo loo egbɔjɔ.

english: How can a plant disease enter my farm if none of my crops were sick before?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai abote miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Ni kɛji akɛ hela emɔko miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dã hu?

english: Diseases can travel silently into healthy farms through infected planting materials, farm tools carrying contaminated soil, floodwater, wind, or even visitors walking in from infected fields.
ga: Helai baanyɛ afã gbɛ dioo. kɛya ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli kɛtsɔ dumɔ nibii ni hela emɔ mli lɛ nɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he nibii ni sũ ni mli ewo muji, nu afua, kɔɔyɔɔ, loo saralɔi po ni nyiɛɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛbaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Can farm tools like cutlasses and hoes pass sickness from one crop to another?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli nibii tamɔ dadei kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ agbɛ helai ashwã kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli kɛya ekroko mli?

english: Yes, cutting an infected plant leaves disease germs or sap on the tool blade, which gets pushed directly into healthy plants when you prune or weed next.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa helai loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ shwieɔ shi. Abaatsi enɛ awo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ be kroko ni obaakpa loo obaajie jwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods catch diseases even when there are no sick trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli hela emɔ eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Fungal spores that cause diseases like black pod are microscopic and can easily be carried across long distances by wind, heavy rain splash, or flying insects from neighboring farms.
ga: Fungal spores ni kɛ hela baa, tamɔ black pods lɛ, daraaa kwraa ni kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kooloi bibii ni foɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ kɛya he ko shɔŋŋ oya.

english: Is it safe for me to bring cassava stem cuttings from another region to plant on my farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ ŋmei ni afolɔ kɛjɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ aba koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It can be risky because stem cuttings from other regions might look healthy on the outside while carrying hidden viruses or pests that will infect your entire soil and local crops.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ afee oshara ejaakɛ tsei ni afolɔ kɛjɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ baanyɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ baaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if new crop seeds or suckers brought to our community are safe to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui loo ŋmeii heei ni akɛba wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni abaanyɛ adu?

english: Safe planting materials usually come certified by agricultural extension officers or recognized nurseries where crops are inspected and treated to ensure they are free of diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaayeli he nitsulɔi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ ji mɛi ni haa dumɔ nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ he odaseyeli. Akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ni atsaa amɛ koni ana akɛ hela ko bɛ mli.

english: Why should I avoid buying plantain suckers from traders along the roadside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ plantain tsei ahemɔ he kɛjɛ gbɛjegbɛ nɔ jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ?

english: Roadside suckers often come from unknown sources and can carry destructive soil pests like nematodes or diseases like banana bunchy top that destroy your field long-term.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ gbɛjegbɛ nɔ lɛ jɛɔ hei ni aleee ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ nematodes loo helai tamɔ banana ŋmeii ni baanyɛ akpata oŋmɔji lɛ ahiɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ aba.

english: What should I do with crops that show strange yellow spots so they do not ruin the rest of my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ? Bɔni afee ni mikafite miŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: You should uproot the infected plants completely, carry them away from the field in a bag, and burn or bury them deeply so insects or wind cannot spread the sickness to healthy plants.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie tsei fɛɛ ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ. Jiemɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛwo kotoku mli ni oshã loo ofu lɛ shɔŋŋ. Enɛ baatsi kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni amɛkagbɛ helai amɛshwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How can I protect my healthy farm when neighboring fields around me are infected with disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ be mli ni akutso ni ebɔle mi lɛ mli bii lɛ emɔ hela lɛ?

english: Create a clean border space around your farm, wash your tools with soap or fire-sanitize them before work, and avoid letting people walk directly from infected fields into yours.
ga: Feemɔ husu he ko ni he tse yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he. Kɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ helai ahe nibii ahe dani otsu nii. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ gbɔmɛi ni oooha amɛnyiɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni hela lɛ emɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛbote he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why does a crop disease disappear during the dry season and then return when the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai laajeɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa lɛ?

english: Many disease germs go dormant in dry soil or fallen leaves during dry spells and wake up to attack fresh plant shoots as soon as rain brings moisture.
ga: Helai babaoo yaa shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni eteɔ shi koni etutua tsei ahe ŋmeii heei kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ, ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do some crop varieties survive a disease while other crops on the same field die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yeɔ wala yɛ helai amli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ gboiɔ lɛ?

english: Different plant varieties have naturally stronger immune systems, allowing resistant types to fight off disease germs while weaker traditional varieties fall sick.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nii ni gbeɔ helai ni he wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛhe waaa lɛ, shishijee henɔi lɛ baaná hela.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees burning and turning yellow during the intense dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive, thin leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees like plantains or shade-providing forest trees to block the harsh sun and keep moisture in the ground, the young leaves dry up, burn, and fall off.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ŋmɛɛɛ amɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo koo mli tsei bɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli lɛ, baai bibii lɛ baagbi, amɛbaashã, ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn completely black and rot when the weather becomes very wet and rainy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and damp conditions. Heavy rain allows the fungus to spread quickly from pod to pod, especially if the farm canopy is too thick and prevents sunlight and fresh air from drying the farm.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli. Titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli tse tsɔ. ni etsĩ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa koni ekaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the leaves and center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that lays eggs on green maize leaves. The hatched caterpillars crawl into the central leaves (the whorl) to feed on the tender young growth, which can destroy the plant's ability to produce corn ears if not treated quickly.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii baai eŋɔli anɔ lɛ. Kplukai ni efɔ lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli (whorls) koni amɛye tsei bibii ni daraa lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi lɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ oya.

english: Why does my land yield less maize every year even though I clear and plant at the same time each season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ be kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Crops like maize continuously pull vital nutrients out of the ground. When you plant the exact same crop on the same field every season without adding compost, manure, or rotating with leguminous crops like cowpeas, the soil becomes exhausted and depleted.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ odu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeee lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become soft, watery, and rot in the soil if I leave them in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, nu yɔɔ mli ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil to remain healthy. When heavy rains cause waterlogging around the roots, air cannot reach them, which causes harmful soil fungi and bacteria to multiply and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ehaa nu feɔ ekome kɛbɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why do my yam vines grow poorly and produce smaller tubers if I let them creep on the bare ground instead of staking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji miha amɛkpã shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo shishifãi lɛ?

english: Yam vines need tall wooden stakes so their leaves can spread out high off the ground to capture maximum sunlight for plant food. When vines trail on hot or damp soil, their leaves get shaded, overheated, and easily infected by soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛha amɛ tsei niyenii. Kɛ́ wain tso lɛ nyiɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛdɔɔ fe nine, ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ yeɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do the plantain suckers I dig up from old farms produce smaller bunches than clean plantlets from nurseries?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei ni mifo kɛjɛ ŋmɔ momo ko mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii fe plantain ni he tse ni jɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Old plantain suckers often carry hidden pests like banana root weevils or tiny worms (nematodes) inside their stem bases. Clean nursery plantlets start free from pests and diseases, allowing them to grow stronger roots and bear larger, healthier bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, tamɔ banana shishifãi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii. (Nematodes) lɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Ajeɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ tsei akwɛmɔhe ni he tse lɛ shishi kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai srɔtoi amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛwoɔ bii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without growing into any fruits when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing successful pollination. When temperatures are too high, the plant becomes stressed and drops its unpollinated flowers to conserve energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. ehaa pollination yeee omanye Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi ni pollination bɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards, shrinking, and turning light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe, amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like whiteflies, thrips, or aphids. These insects suck sap from the leaves and often transmit leaf-curl viruses that stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ whiteflies, thrips, loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni bei pii lɛ amɛhaa muawai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no haaa tso lɛ ada.

english: Why do experienced farmers say that planting cowpeas or beans improves the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have beneficial bacteria living on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When the legume crop finishes, this natural nitrogen stays behind to fertilize the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa lɛ agbe naa Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ sɛɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli ŋmãa.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop leaves during severe dry spells to reduce water loss, but providing shade trees keeps the soil moist and reduces leaf loss.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Shi hulutsoo ni oooha lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when there is continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ ni naa wa miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: When excess rain waterlogs the soil for too long, it cuts off air to the cassava roots, creating a wet environment that causes underground fungi to rot the tubers.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaafo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛya ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni feɔ shihilɛ ni mli ewo nu Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii fiteɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with small cobs when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, each plant fights for sunlight and soil nutrients, causing them to grow tall and weak instead of forming full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso fɛɛ tso kɛ ehe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops if I plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop relies on and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it good for my crops if I plant groundnuts on the field before planting corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani midu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil with natural fertilizer for the corn that comes next.
ga: Akpɔlɔi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba lɛ.

english: Why are earthworms a good sign in my farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ji okadi kpakpa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Earthworms dig tunnels that allow plant roots to breathe and absorb rainwater easily, and their waste acts as natural manure for crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii tswaa ŋmeii ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmuɔ mlɛo ni amɛmuɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ. Ni jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before setting fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or lack of water causes stress to pepper plants, making them drop their flowers to conserve energy and survive.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa chili tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ajie amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why should I pinch off the extra side branches growing on my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Side branches waste food and water that the main stem needs, so removing them helps the plant direct energy into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ afã lɛ fiteɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa tso titri lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, niji ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛwoɔ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do worms hide inside the leaf funnels of my young maize plants during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworm hide deep in the central leaves to protect themselves from the hot sun and birds while eating the soft, growing parts of the plant.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ okpoi ahe. beni eyeɔ tsei lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ

english: Why do weeds grow faster and ruin my crops even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have stronger roots and grow faster than most crops, allowing them to steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your crops can use them.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei babaoo. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted alongside them to protect their sensitive leaves while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni abu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose most of their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fite yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry spells to save water and keep the underground tubers alive. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves without damaging your harvest.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni amɛfiteee onibii lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. When leaves get full sun, they produce more energy to swell the tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa lɛ Ebaaha hewalɛ babaoo aba ni ekɛgbala tuber ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why are there small caterpillars eating the leaves inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the fresh leaves at the center of maize plants. Identifying them early allows you to apply recommended control methods before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ. Amɛyɔsemɔ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔ amɛ lɛ atsu nii dani ofite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning down to one or two strong shoots ensures the main plant produces a heavy, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ofo tso niji kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo plantains tsei ni tsii ni mli wa.

english: Why does my farmland yield much less maize when I plant it on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ baa shi kwraa beni miduɔ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your maize with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas helps restore vital nutrients back into the land.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii atsake o-corn lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do crops like groundnuts and cowpeas make my soil richer for future crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Legumes have helpful bacteria on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil plant food. When the roots decay, they leave natural fertilizer behind.
ga: Legumes yɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni ehaa efeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not during heavy downpours. Applying right before heavy rain will wash the nutrients away into streams before roots can absorb them.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛwo mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa faa lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Flower drop usually happens when plants face extreme heat, poor watering habits, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni laajeɔ lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ shɛ la ni naa wa waa he. nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni ehiii loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my tomato plants develop dark spots and turn brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is often a fungal disease caused by rain splashing soil containing fungal spores onto the lower leaves. Pruning low leaves and covering the soil around the plant stem with dry grass helps prevent infection.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afo baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akabote tso lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can capture maximum sunlight to grow big tubers. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ koni ekahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields if I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants compete with each other for water, sunlight, and plant food in the soil, causing them to stay small and produce poor harvests.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni jɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do older farmers cover the soil around their young crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation during hot days, and stops weeds from sprouting easily.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to stay green and grow heavy ears, so adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tso lɛ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni eha toi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsii lɛ ahi shi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the ground when heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when water sits around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot, during sudden dry spells, or if the plant does not get steady water and proper nutrients while flowering.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa trukaa loo kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni sa nɔ daa be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same spot on my land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot wears out specific soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the soil year after year.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant juices, or by a plant virus carried by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo tsei amli helai ni ji mɛi ni kɛ nakai kooloi lɛ baa lɛ kɛbaa

english: Why should I clear weeds from my farm when my crop seedlings are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni midumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are weak and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for fertilizer, sunlight, and water. Weeding early gives your crops the space and food they need to start strong.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii, hulu la kɛ nu. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their tender leaves lose water too quickly and get scorched. Planting them under fast-growing shade crops like plantain or shade trees protects them until their roots grow deep enough to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, cacao tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ ni amɛshãa. Kɛ́ adu tsei nɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantain loo shia tsei ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baashɛ amɛhe bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, wet, and humid conditions. Pruning excess branches and clearing weeds helps air flow through the farm to dry out the pods and reduce fungal growth.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni eha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aba shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a common sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to build strong leaves and green color. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps fix this.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji tso ni niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ mli koni efee baai ni wa, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Yam leaves need to capture as much sunlight as possible to produce the energy required to grow big underground tubers. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground, catching more light while preventing leaf diseases caused by damp soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ aba. Staking baajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. ni enine ashɛ la babaoo nɔ Agbɛnɛ hu ni atsĩ foliar helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when water stays on my field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen from the soil to stay alive. When water covers the field without draining, it starves the roots of air, causing fungal rot that destroys the tubers before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nu ha ŋmɔ ko nɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei ni fiteɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani akpaa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and soft before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato aduawai shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant steadily absorb calcium from the ground.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on leaf sap, or viruses spread by these insects. Spraying early with neem extract or recommended insecticides stops the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Akɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. lɛ baakpa nɔ ni efite lɛ

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans make my soil better for corn next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have friendly soil bacteria on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the cowpea plant leaves decay, that natural nitrogen becomes free plant food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ su yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni tsina tsei lɛ miifite Nakai adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ bafeɔ tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize shoots with brownish powder left behind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn yitsei lɛ anɔ buji ni etse kɛ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ?

english: This is signature damage caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central whorl of young maize. Checking your farm weekly and applying neem leaf extract or targeted insecticides into the shoot controls the pest.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ko ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa otsi ni okɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ awo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ koni akɛkudɔ kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ.

english: Why should I add animal manure or compost to my farm soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Compost acts like a sponge and nutrient bank in the soil. It improves the soil's ability to hold water during dry spells while slowly releasing plant food to your crops over time.
ga: Kɔmpost tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ, Jiemɔ tsei aniyenii kɛya onibii amli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and small roots. Full sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the topsoil before their roots can drink enough water, which is why they need shade trees or plantains nearby to protect them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii. Hulu lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni egbiɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni haa ehe hiaa ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni amɛbu amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why must I plant my maize seeds at specific distances instead of throwing them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni mashɛrɛ amɛ ashwie shi kɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. Proper spacing gives each plant enough food and light to grow big ears of maize.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni baai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why should I plant my crops across a hill slope instead of up and down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔji anɔ moŋ fe ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Planting across a slope creates small barriers that trap rain water and prevent heavy downpours from washing away your fertile topsoil and crop food.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛ gbɛtsii nii bibii baa. No baaha nugbɔ nu lɛ ahi shi ni ebaatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii ni fa babaoo lɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential soil nutrient that gives leaves their deep green color and helps the plant grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Eji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or when insects fail to pollinate the blossoms. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, called blossom-end rot, happen when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, which is often caused by irregular watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry spell of hot weather. If seeds sprout during this dry period, the young seedlings will wither and die before the main rains arrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ lɛ anɛ.

english: Why do weeds lower my crop harvest even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and act like thieves in your farm, stealing water, fertilizer, and sunlight directly away from your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up toward the sun to catch light and make food. The more sunlight the leaves get, the larger the tuber growing under the ground will be.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛná la ni amɛhoo nii. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, Babaoo ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ baafee agbo.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if I leave them in the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Once cassava reaches full maturity, heavy rains and waterlogged soil can stop the roots from breathing, causing soil fungi to attack and rot the tubers before you can dig them up.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ dani obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ atsu nii.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects young cocoa from harsh sun while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi tsei ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why must I place tall wooden sticks in the ground for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei lɛ awo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ nɛkɛ? kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni mi sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves high up into the sunlight to make food. Staking keeps the foliage off the damp ground, which prevents leaf rot and allows the underground tubers to grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli koni efee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni ekafite, ni ebaaye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdara babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do some farmers cover the dry dirt around their crop stems with dry bush grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle tsei ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool under the hot sun and stops water from evaporating, helping crops survive dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩɔ nu naa koni ekaho Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: Will planting my maize seeds very close together give me a bigger yield from my small farm?
ga: Kɛ́ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli. mi nɔ loo daabi

english: No, planting maize seeds too close together forces the plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space ensures thick stalks and full, heavy ears of corn.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ená ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmãa toi ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests that target that crop to build up in the field. Rotating with crops like beans restores soil fertility and starves pests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ be fɛɛ be ni Seasons lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ, tamɔ ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ, ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ.

english: How do common weeds harm my cassava crops if they are just growing next to them?
ga: Te jwɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ baaye mi-cassava tsei lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛmasɛi?

english: Weeds steal vital water, sunlight, and plant food directly from the soil that your cassava needs. Clearing weeds early gives your crop full access to nutrients so it can form large roots.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa waa, hulu la kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni o-cassava he hiaa lɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efee shishifãi wuji.

english: Why does my cassava plant have plenty of big green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, the cassava plant puts all its energy into leaf growth rather than root expansion. Loosening the soil helps the plant store food in thick tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ mli alɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii toɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers usually fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Providing steady moisture at the roots during hot weather helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ ahã shishifãi lɛ mli fũu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and wilt during the afternoon even when the weather is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During the hottest hours of the day, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can suck water from the ground. Wilting is the plant's natural way of reducing water loss, and leaves usually recover by evening.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Wilting ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa nu ni efiteɔ lɛ baa shi. Ni bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ he baajɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: If I pour a large amount of chemical fertilizer on my crop all at once, will it grow twice as fast?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai babaoo fata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ be kome mli. Ani ebaada oya fe nakai shii enyɔ?

english: Applying too much fertilizer at once can burn the crop's roots and destroy the plant. Giving small, measured applications at specific growth stages feeds the crop safely without damaging it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni egbe tso lɛ. Nibii bibii ni asusuɔ he yɛ dalɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii shweshweeshwe ni efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. Applying well-decomposed manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or Urea gives the plants the strength to turn green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings rot in the ground when I plant them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings need damp soil to sprout, but if the ground becomes waterlogged, the stem cannot breathe and soil fungi will attack it. Planting on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to flow away while keeping the root area damp enough for growth.
ga: Cassava ni afo lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ koni ekwɛ̃. Shi kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutuaa lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers until they develop into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ehiii. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni etsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that dry out and burn quickly in direct sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains nearby protects the cocoa from harsh sunshine and holds moisture in the air.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei bibii ni shwereɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu kookoo he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: If I plant my corn seeds very close together, will I harvest more corn from my field?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the crops compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, weak stalks that yield tiny or empty corn cobs. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to form large ears.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ toi wuji.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up into tight tubes during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants roll their leaves up during the hottest part of the day to protect themselves from losing too much water. It is a natural defense signal showing that the plant is stressed by heat and needs good soil moisture to stay healthy.
