ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Eji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni buɔ mɔ he akɛ tsei lɛ miihe dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni amɛmiitao shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep soil to push downward as they expand. If the soil is hard, stony, or compacted, the tuber cannot grow straight down and becomes twisted or stunted as it pushes against the hard ground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya mli beni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ shi tɛ̃ɛ. ni etsɔɔ sɛɛ loo egbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ kɛtee nibii ni wa nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and split during the dry harmattan wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛjaraa yɛ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry harmattan air sucks moisture out of broad plantain leaves faster than the roots can drink from the soil. Covering the soil around the base of the plantain with dry grass or cocoa husks keeps the root zone cool and hydrated.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi ni ji harmattan lɛ shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ plantain tso lɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmeii shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle plantains lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahe feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are fully ripe and ready to pull out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts show maturity when the leaves begin to turn yellow and dry up. You can test a few plants by pulling them up; if the inside of the seed pods has dark brown markings instead of remaining white, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Peanuts lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ oka tsei komɛi okwɛ kɛtsɔ amɛ ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli lɛ yɛ okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eshɛ nikpamɔ.

english: Why do small insects destroy my stored maize even after I have dried it in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ beni migbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli po lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils often lay invisible eggs on the grain while it is still in the field or drying on the ground. Storing the dried corn in airtight storage bags deprives the pests of oxygen and prevents them from multiplying and damaging the grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ dumɔwui ni anaaa amɛ lɛ awoɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo loo amɛmiigbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi wo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ ana kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ni etsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafee babaoo ni amɛkafite dumɔwui.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant plantains together with young cocoa seedlings on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ kookoo tsei bibii feɔ ekome kɛduɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and can easily burn or dry out under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the vital shade and moisture cocoa needs during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã loo amɛgbi oya. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo lɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for green leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or waterlogs the roots, preventing them from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni haa baai eŋɔli lɛ daa lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii loo nu ni hoɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nii.

english: Can cassava still produce good tubers if I plant it in poor or exhausted soil?
ga: Ani ŋmei baanyɛ awo ŋmeii kpakpai lolo kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ?

english: Cassava is a naturally tough crop that tolerates poor soils and dry weather better than most crops. However, while it will survive and yield in poor soil, adding organic manure will greatly increase the size and number of the tubers.
ga: Cassava ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ naa fe tsei babaoo. Shi, eyɛ mli akɛ ebaanyɛ ehi shi ni ewo yibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ moŋ, Shi kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛyibɔ ​​aya hiɛ waa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. High heat and lack of water cause stress, making the plant discard flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛji akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa. Ha tsei ashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are there small holes and dark dirt inside the center leaves of my growing maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni muji ni tsuɔ waa yɛ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides in the inner center (whorl) of the maize plant to eat the fresh leaves. Treating the plants early with neem oil or recommended insecticides targets the caterpillar before it destroys the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli teŋgbɛ (rings) koni amɛye baai heei. Tsei ahe nitsumɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear the bush and put tall sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ amli ni mikɛ tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ ama shi koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves high up into the sunlight to make food for building tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the wet soil, preventing fungal diseases from rotting the plant.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewó ebaa lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni akɛtsi tsei anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Planting too close actually reduces your harvest because the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow strong stalks and big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aba shi ejaakɛ tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable garden in the afternoon heat or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu shwane loo leebi?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil can absorb moisture before the sun gets too hot. Watering in the hot afternoon heat wastes water through quick evaporation and can heat up the soil around the roots, causing stress.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite nu yɛ la ni hoɔ oya lɛ hewɔ. ni ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli adɔ ni ekɛ haomɔ aba

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves, or transmitting a virus. Spraying insecticidal soap or neem spray controls these pests so new leaves can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem spray shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni baai heei anyɛ akwɛ̃ bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my maize so it doesn't rot or mold in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Bɔni afee ni ekafite loo ekafee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Maize is fully ready for harvest when the outer husks turn brown and dry, and the grains become hard and glassy. Harvesting while grains are still soft and wet attracts mold and dangerous fungi during storage.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kwraa kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa ni ebaafee glase. Kɛ́ akpa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ be mli ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ lolo ni edɔ lɛ, ebaagbala ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛba be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn or carry away all the weeds after clearing my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa loo mikɛ jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ yaa he kroko beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving cleared weeds on the farm allows them to decay into natural mulch. This protects the soil from direct heat, helps it retain moisture, and restores strength and nutrients back to the ground for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛgboi ni amɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ baabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛhaa onibii.

english: How does leaving dead weeds on my land help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egboi ni mishiɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: As dead weeds decompose, they break down into rich organic matter that feeds the soil organisms and releases essential food that your growing crops need to stay healthy.
ga: Beni jwɛi ni egboi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ Amɛgbalaa amɛhe amɛwoɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ wala yeɔ hewalɛ ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa otsei ni miida lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kpo.

english: How can I tell if my farm land has lost its strength and needs help?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso lɛ hewalɛ miiho ni ehe miihia yelikɛbuamɔ?

english: Signs of weak soil include crops with pale or yellowing leaves, slow crop growth, poor yields during harvest, and soil that hardens quickly after rain.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lɛ he ji tsei ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔŋ. tsei lɛ adaa blɛoo Yibiiwoo ni ehiii yɛ kpamɔ be mli kɛ shikpɔŋ ni waɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ

english: Why is it important to check the wind direction before I spray my crops with chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa dani akɛ tsofai afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Spraying in the direction of the wind ensures the chemical blows away from you onto the plants, protecting your face and body from inhaling dangerous chemical mist.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai lɛ shwie he ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ ajɛ ohe kɛya tsei lɛ anɔ. Buu ohiɛ kɛ ogbɔmɔtso he kɛjɛ tsofa ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni okɛmuɔ lɛ he.

english: What is the right direction to walk when spraying liquid chemical on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ni ja ni esa akɛ akɛshwie tsofai ni ji nu nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: You should always walk so the wind is blowing away from your back or side, moving downwind so you do not walk directly into the wet chemical mist you just sprayed.
ga: Esa akɛ onyiɛ be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ miitswa kɛmiijɛ osɛɛ loo osɛɛ. Ni okɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya koni okanyiɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛbote tsofa ni mli ewo fɔ ni okɛshwie nɔ kɛkɛ nɛɛ mli.

english: What happens if I spray my farm chemicals randomly without following a clear direction?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ tsofai shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ trukaa ni mikɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ tsuuu nii?

english: Random spraying leads to uneven coverage where some crops receive too much chemical and get burned, while other crops are missed entirely and remain vulnerable to pests.
ga: Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haaa nɔ ko nɔ ko nɔ ko nɔ. Tsei komɛi náa tsofa babaoo ni amɛshãa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi Efoɔ mli kwraa ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aye amɛnɔ.

english: What basic things do my young crops need to grow strong and healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee nibii he hiaa mi tsei bibii lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ?

english: Young crops need sunlight, adequate water, good soil nutrients, and sufficient space between plants so their roots and leaves can feed without competing with neighboring crops.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ hia hulu la. Nu ni fa Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei ateŋ ni baaha amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ aye niyenii ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow slower during the dry period of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ afi lɛ mli nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants rely on water to transport food from the soil to their leaves. When water is scarce, crops conserve energy by slowing down their growth until moisture returns.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu nɔ koni amɛkɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Beni nu faaa lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ amɛdalɛ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the farming methods my parents used not always work as well today?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli gbɛi ni mifɔlɔi kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuuu nii be fɛɛ be yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weather patterns, rainfall timing, and soil condition change continuously over time, meaning modern farmers need updated techniques like soil conservation and continuous learning to stay successful.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, nugbɔshiimɔ bei, kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ yaa nɔ etsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaafoi lɛ miitao ŋaai ni hi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ. kɛ nikasemɔ ni yaa nɔ koni eye omanye

english: Why should I keep learning new farming techniques instead of sticking to what I already know?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makase okwaayeli he ŋaai heei lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makɛ mihe akpɛtɛ nɔ ni mile momo lɛ he

english: Farming conditions shift as new pests appear and weather patterns change, so learning updated methods helps you protect your crop yield and prevent losses every season.
ga: Okwaayeli shihilɛi tsakeɔ be mli ni kooloi heei baa ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi hu tsakeɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, gbɛi heei ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ akasemɔ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe, ni ebaatsi nibii ni laajeɔ lɛ anaa daa be mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when water collects and sits on the farm for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa ni ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess water sits on top of the ground, it blocks oxygen from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate and decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni efiteɔ.

english: How does heavy rain affect the fertilizer I put around my young maize crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rains can wash water-soluble fertilizer deep into the soil below the reach of young roots, or wash it away across the surface, leaving the maize without essential nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nu mli shwieɔ shi lɛ awo sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ ashishi. loo ahoɔ ashwieɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ Enɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ ŋmãa mli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually a response to heat stress, uneven watering, or tiny sap-sucking insects damaging the underside of young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ ji hetoo kɛha dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi daa loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni fiteɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes rapidly from dry to wet, causing stress that stops fruit formation.
ga: Tomato baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Enɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni haa aduawai baa lɛ baa.

english: Why do plantain trees fall over so easily after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay near the surface. When heavy rains soften the surrounding soil, the heavy stem easily loses its support against strong winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa waa lɛ, tsɔne ni tsii baanyɛ afite sɛɛfimɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do young cocoa leaves dry out and burn when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without protective shade crops, sun exposure dries out the leaves faster than roots can draw water.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ Hulu la lɛ haa baai lɛ gĩɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu.

english: How can I tell if small insects floating or walking on standing water in my field are bad for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii ni hoɔ loo nyiɛɔ nu ni damɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miigba miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ?

english: Most water insects like water striders eat other small bugs and are harmless to plants, while crop pests spend their time directly eating leaves, stems, or roots.
ga: Nu mli kooloi babaoo, tamɔ water striders lɛ yeɔ kooloi bibii krokomɛi ni amɛyeee tsei awui. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ yeɔ amɛbe amɛyeɔ baai, amɛshishifãi, loo amɛshishifãi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do insect pests multiply so quickly on my vegetable field during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ oya yɛ mi aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Warm and humid weather shortens the lifecycle of insects, allowing eggs to hatch faster while providing plenty of soft, fresh plant growth for them to feed on.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ lɛ haa kooloi ashihilɛ be lɛ feɔ kuku. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni wɔji lɛ fɔɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛduɔ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ.

english: Weed seeds are hardy native plants adapted to the local soil, allowing them to absorb moisture and surface nutrients much faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ji maŋ tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from around the base of my yam mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds around yam mounds steal water and nutrients meant for the tuber, while creating dark, moist hiding spots for pests like beetles that attack subterranean roots.
ga: Jwɛi ni bɔle sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ladybugs ni tutuaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ feɔ he ko ni mli edɔ ni edɔɔ.

english: Why do my maize and plantain plants fall over whenever a strong wind blows across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa kɛ mi-plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops fall over, or 'lodge,' when their root systems are weak or the soil around the stem is loose. Piling soil tightly around the base of the stem (earthing up) and planting at correct depths helps anchor the roots firmly against strong winds.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi loo ‘efɔ̃ɔ’ kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli etse. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ ha tso lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ (bonding) ni odu yɛ he ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔmɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: My plantain tree is bending under the weight of its fruits. What can I do to keep it from snapping before harvest?
ga: Midumɔwui lɛ miiho yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi. Mɛni mafee koni amɛkakumɔ dani kpamɔ?

english: Heavy fruit bunches create top-heavy weight that makes plants easy targets for wind. You can support the main stem by propping it up with a sturdy bamboo pole or a branched wooden stick placed firmly underneath the heavy bunch.
ga: Yibii akui ni tsii lɛ feɔ tsɔne ni tsii ni haa tso lɛ feɔ nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atswa lɛ oya. Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei tso ni wa loo tso nine ni wa ni akɛ niji ewo shishi lɛ afi tso titri lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are some of my rice seeds sprouting quickly while others rot in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya shi ekrokomɛi hu fiteɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seed quality and moisture levels determine how seeds sprout. High-quality, well-stored seeds germinate evenly within a few days when soil is moist, whereas damaged or poorly stored seeds absorb water without growing and quickly decay.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ahe fɛo kɛ bɔ ni amɛmli nu lɛ fa ha lɛ baatsɔɔ bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃. Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ato jogbaŋŋ lɛ baakwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni efite loo ni akɛtoko he jogbaŋŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my young maize plants turn yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves is a sign that the maize plant lacks nitrogen. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the plant steals this vital nutrient from its older bottom leaves to feed new top growth.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ Tsei juɔ nɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them very close together to try to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ koni mibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni maná yibii babaoo?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall, weak, and thin, resulting in smaller fruits or grains and a lower total yield.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii mli nibii ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ daa, egbɔjɔɔ, ni egbɔjɔɔ, ni no haa aduawai loo dumɔwui bibii baa, ni yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow well in muddy water, but my cassava roots rot when water collects on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa folo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni mli ewo muji mli lɛ? Shi ani ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air passages that allow their roots to breathe in flooded soil. Cassava roots need dry, well-drained soil to access air and will suffocate and rot if submerged in standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi ni haa amɛshishifãi lɛ muɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ. ni ebaagbɔjɔ ni ebaagbo kɛji akɛ awo lɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli.

english: Extreme heat, dry air, or water stress causes tomato plants to drop their blossoms. The plant discards its flowers to preserve energy and survive when growing conditions become too difficult.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu he haomɔ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ mli wa tsɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield every year when I plant maize on the same plot of land continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Maize consumes large amounts of specific nutrients from the soil every season. Planting it repeatedly on the same plot drains those nutrients, causing the soil to become tired and reducing future plant growth.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu nii shii abɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, no haa nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tsei ni baa lɛ baa shi wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and bigger than my planted crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally adapted to survive harsh local conditions and absorb water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crop gets the food and light it needs to grow.
ga: Kooloi amli jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ mra Enɛ baaha tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ aná niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why did my crop leaves turn brown and look scorched after I applied fertilizer during a dry week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ otsi ni nu bɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers are strong salts that need water to dissolve into plant food. Applied to dry soil, fertilizer draws moisture out of the plant's roots, burning the leaves and harming the crop.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni shwieɔ shi koni akɛha tsei niyenii. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, Fertilizer lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa baai lɛ shãa ni eyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awui.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when there are no bigger plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei wuji bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense, direct sunlight. Planting taller crops like plantains nearby provides protective shade and holds soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are small insects eating holes in my harvested maize while it is stored in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli be mli ni eyɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects like grain weevils lay eggs inside seeds when crops are harvesting or drying. If grains are bagged while still slightly damp, the eggs hatch quickly and the insects multiply inside the warm environment.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui amli kɛji akpa amɛ loo amɛgbi. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmaa lɛ wo kotoku mli be mli ni edɔ fioo lolo lɛ, Ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ oya ni kooloi bibii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need for healthy green growth. Adding manure or NPK fertilizer gives the crop the energy it needs to produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Legumes like cowpeas feed the soil by taking nitrogen from the air and storing it in their roots. This naturally enriches your land, helping neighboring crops grow better without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niiatsɛmɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai ni jara wa waa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases to build up in the dirt. Rotating your crops gives the soil time to recover and stops pests from taking over.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I cut down all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need partial shade to shield them from burning under the hot sun and drying out. Keeping a few shade trees or planting plantains alongside them keeps the soil moist and protects the young plants.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛkashã ni amɛkagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetables with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetables lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool under direct sunlight. It traps water in the ground so you do not have to water as often and stops weeds from competing with your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Etoɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu awo mli shii abɔ ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye akaŋ kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: If seeds are buried too deep, they waste all their stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil before reaching sunlight. Planting seeds about a finger's depth gives them the best chance to sprout quickly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ ni ekɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ dani eshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni mli kwɔ aaafee inchi kome lɛ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha shweremɔ oya.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long without draining away. Planting your cassava on top of raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to run off, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. Be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ atsɔ mli. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso he hiaa mi koni makwɔ ŋmei tso lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight for leaf growth and tuber formation. Staking gets the leaves off the wet ground, which prevents diseases and helps the plant produce larger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la babaoo kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ kɛ tuber feemɔ. Staking baajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa mɔ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat or irregular watering. Providing steady watering at the roots and planting during suitable seasons keeps the flowers healthy so they turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni amɛhaaa amɛ daa. Kɛ́ afɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu daa ni adu yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni no hewɔ lɛ amɛwo yibii.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites attacking the young leaves. Spraying with neem water or proper pest treatments stops the insects so fresh leaves can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni ŋmɔɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Neem nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛbaagbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Etsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni baai heei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young plantain leaves dry up and turn brown during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ahe baai lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plantain leaves burn easily when exposed to intense heat and strong direct sunlight without enough water in the soil, which causes the edges of the leaves to dry out and die.
ga: Plantain tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn under full heat from the sun; they need shade trees or plantain plants to protect them and keep the surrounding soil moist while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei loo plantains ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he miihia amɛ koni ebu amɛhe ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why are white, dry patches appearing on my tomatoes while they are still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni egbi yɛ mi-tomato lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is sunscald, which happens when direct, harsh sunlight bakes tomatoes that are not shielded by leaves, effectively burning the skin of the fruit.
ga: Enɛ ji nu ni mli edɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shã tomato ni baai lɛ ebuuu he. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ ahewolo lɛ shãa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid spraying pesticides on my crops during the bright afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Spraying during peak afternoon heat causes the chemical liquid to concentrate and evaporate too fast, which can burn the crop leaves and reduce the medicine's effectiveness.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tsofai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofai ni ji nu lɛ afee ekome ni etsɔ la oya tsɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ahe baai ashã ni eha tsofa lɛ hewalɛ aba shi.

english: Is it good to burn my farm land before I plant my new maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ashã ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ dani adu ŋmãa hee?

english: While burning clears weeds quickly, the fire burns away vital organic matter and good nutrients in the soil, leaving your land weaker and less productive over time.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ shãa yeɔ ebuaa ni egbeɔ jwɛi oya moŋ, shi la hu baashã nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why is my land producing smaller yields every year even though I plant the same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously wears out the soil by taking away the exact same nutrients every season without giving the ground time or different plants to recover.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ niyenii mli nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli daa be mli ni ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ loo tsei krokomɛi be ni amɛkɛbaatsa amɛhe lɛ nɔ.

english: How does covering my soil with dry grass or leaves help my crops during the dry season?
ga: Te jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Mulching acts like a blanket that shields the ground from the burning sun, keeping soil moisture locked in and preventing the topsoil from wearing away.
ga: Mulching tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on land where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize wears out nitrogen from the soil, but leguminous crops like beans naturally put nitrogen back into the ground, restoring your soil's energy.
ga: Abɛi haa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Shi ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmeii, kɛ nitrogen kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ

english: Why are the edges of my maize leaves turning brown shortly after I put chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ewo ŋmãa baa lɛ naa lɛ, etsɛɛɛ ni etsɔɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ?

english: Applying too much fertilizer or placing it directly against the stems burns the plant roots and leaves by pulling water out of the plant tissue.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ shishi loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why did my cassava leaves curl up and burn after I sprayed weedkiller nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weedkillers can float in the wind or seep through the ground, causing chemical burns on surrounding crop leaves even if you did not spray them directly.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nɔ loo amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tsofa shãa tso baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ spray ko tsuuu nii tɛ̃ɛ po.

english: Why would I need a greenhouse to grow vegetables in Ghana when our weather is already warm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maná ŋmɔ ko ni akɛduɔ aduawai yɛ Ghana lɛ? Beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ wɔmaŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ momo lɛ?

english: Greenhouses are not just for keeping plants warm in cold countries. In Ghana, a greenhouse protects your crops from heavy rain, harsh direct sunlight, and destructive pests, allowing you to grow healthy vegetables all year round.
ga: Jeee tsei ni yɔɔ maji ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ mli dɔɔ. Yɛ Ghana lɛ, greenhouses yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii Eyeɔ ebua bo ni oduɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: I only have a small piece of land; can using a greenhouse help me harvest more crops?
ga: Shikpɔŋ fioo ko pɛ miyɔɔ. Ani greenhouse ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua mi ni makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Yes, greenhouses allow you to maximize small land space because you can grow high-yielding crops close together in a controlled environment without losing plants to bad weather or pests.
ga: Hɛɛ, greenhouses lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ he bibioo ko tsuɔ nii babaoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, obaanyɛ odu tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo. amɛfee ekome yɛ he ko ni akudɔɔ ni tsei lɛ fiteee yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ fɔŋ loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Won't my crops burn inside a greenhouse because the weather in Ghana is already hot?
ga: Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãŋ yɛ greenhouse lɛ mli ejaakɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ momo, aloo jeee nakai?

english: Greenhouses designed for warm regions like Ghana use proper ventilation, insect nets, and special shade covers that lower the inside temperature and allow air to circulate so plants do not overheat.
ga: Greenhouses ni afee aha hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ tamɔ Ghana lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa, kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmɔlɔi krɛdɛɛi ni haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni tsei lɛ akadɔ fe nine lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Can a local welder build a usable greenhouse frame for me, or do I have to import an expensive one?
ga: Ani maŋ lɛ mli welder ko baanyɛ ama greenhouse ni tsuɔ nii aha mi? Aloo esa akɛ mikɛ frem ni jara wa aba maŋsɛɛ?

english: A local welder can fabricate a strong greenhouse frame using affordable local metal or pipes, as long as it is covered with the correct agricultural net and plastic sheets meant for crop protection.
ga: Mɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ maŋ lɛ mli dade loo paipi ni jara waaa ama greenhouse ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Shii abɔ ni akɛ okwaayeli ŋshɔŋlooi ni ja kɛ plastic ŋshɔŋlooi ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baaha nɔ.

english: Why do some farming practices imported from countries like Israel or Australia fail when we try them on our farms in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli nifeemɔi komɛi ni akɛbaajɛ maji tamɔ Israel loo Australia lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ wɔka amɛ wɔkwɛ yɛ wɔ diɛŋtsɛ wɔŋmɔji amli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Farming practices from other countries are tailored to their specific soil type, humidity, and rainfall. If you do not adapt those methods to match Ghana's local soil and climate conditions, the crops will not grow properly.
ga: Okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni jɛ maji krokomɛi anɔ Afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ henɔi pɔtɛɛ, hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ. Kɛji akɛ otsakeee nakai gbɛi lɛ kɛyaaa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ anɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwereŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: I hear dry countries like Israel produce high crop yields; can their watering methods work on my farm?
ga: Minu akɛ maji ni mli egbi tamɔ Israel woɔ yibii babaoo. Ani gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ nu woɔ mli nɛɛ kɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, practices like drip irrigation developed in dry countries work very well in Ghana because they deliver water directly to the plant roots, saving water and reducing weeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, nifeemɔi tamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni afee yɛ maji ni nu bɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ etsu nii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ Ghana. Ejaakɛ amɛkɛ nu yaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nu baa shi ni ehaa jwɛi baa shi.

english: How do I know if a new crop variety or farming technique brought from outside Ghana will work on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso henɔ loo okwaayeli gbɛ hee ko ni akɛba kɛjɛ Ghana kponɔgbɛ lɛ baatsu nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Before trying a new foreign method on your whole farm, test it on a small trial plot or consult your local extension officer to see if it has been tested and adapted for Ghanaian soils.
ga: Dani obaaka maŋsɛɛ gbɛ hee ko okwɛ yɛ oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ Ka yɛ kaa shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Aloo bi mɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni ona kɛji aka lɛ akwɛ ni ekɛ ehe ewo Ghana shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does heavy rainfall during the wet season harm my crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Too much rain washes away essential plant nutrients from the soil, damages fragile leaves and flowers, and creates high dampness that causes fungal diseases and root rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hoɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Efiteɔ baai kɛ fɔfɔi ni waaa lɛ. ni ekɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ baa lɛ baa.

english: Is land size or weather control more important when deciding to grow high-value vegetables?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo he hiaa fe fɛɛ yɛ yiŋkpɛɛ ni akpɛɔ akɛ abaadu aduawai ni jara wa waa lɛ mli?

english: Both matter, but protecting your crops from harsh weather and pests often allows you to produce higher yields on a small piece of land than traditional farming on a large plot.
ga: Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ he miihia. Shi bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni oná yibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo nɔ fe bɔ ni afeɔ kusum nifeemɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu nɔ lɛ.

english: What kind of crops give the best returns if my farm land is very small?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei haa sɛɛnamɔi ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛji akɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ faaa kwraa?

english: High-value vegetables like tomatoes, sweet peppers, and cucumbers are best for small land areas because they produce heavy yields per square meter and sell for good prices in local markets.
ga: Aduawai ni jara wa waa tamɔ tomato, bell pepper, kɛ kukumba ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha hei bibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ewoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ sqɛɛ mita kome mli, ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ yɛ jara kpakpa nɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin without big cobs when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii wuji bɛ mli beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The maize plants stretch tall to reach the sun instead of using energy to grow strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmãa tsei kɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ, ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are often a sign that tiny sucking insects, like whiteflies, are feeding on your plants or spreading a plant disease. It can also happen when the plant is stressed by hot weather or a lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ, miiye tso lɛ loo amɛmiigbɛ tso hela amɛmiishwã. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba tsei anaa.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help my crops survive dry periods?
ga: Mulching around Te jwɛi ni mikɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a shield against the hot sun. It keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from growing and stealing water from your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ gãimlibii ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju nu kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, too little water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Ensuring regular watering during hot spells helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. nu fioo tsɔ loo nitrogen fertilizer babaoo yɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni enyɛ ewo yibii.

english: Fertilizer works best when applied in two stages: first, about two weeks after planting when seedlings have leaves to process nutrients, and second, when the plant is knee-high. Always apply fertilizer when the soil is moist so the roots can drink it in.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli yɛ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni adu nii lɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ náa baai ni amɛkɛbaatsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nii ahe nii. Ni nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ Kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ etsitsi nɔ lɛ Ha ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be fɛɛ be kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting cassava together with maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly over many months. Planting them together gives you two different harvests from the same land and ensures the soil stays covered, which protects it from heavy rain.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa fiofio yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ lɛ fee ekome lɛ, ebaaha oná yibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛ he kome. ni eyeɔ ebuaa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he

english: What causes cocoa pods to turn black and rot directly on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cool, damp conditions. Trimming excess branches to let sunlight into the farm and removing infected pods quickly helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest produce smaller crops than the original seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii bibii fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Many modern seeds are bred specifically to give a high yield for only one season. The seeds harvested from those plants lose their special strength in the second generation, so buying fresh certified seeds gives you much better harvests.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui babaoo pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ be kome pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ nakai tsei lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ni ooohe lɛ baaha oná kpamɔ kpakpa kwraa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cassava roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the bottom leaves dry out and fall off, usually 9 to 12 months after planting. Harvesting too early leaves you with small, watery roots, while waiting too long makes the roots tough and woody.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ ahi ohe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ ni amɛfee tamɔ tso.

english: Why does my soil dry out so quickly even a few days after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi po sɛɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Soil with low organic matter or high sand content cannot hold onto water for long. Adding compost, animal manure, or decomposed plant material improves the soil structure so it holds water like a sponge for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔji ni nɔ ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa loo ŋã babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ahi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsei ni egboi fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehiɛɔ nu mli tamɔ sponji kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Large trees provide essential shade and retain soil moisture, protecting fragile young cocoa leaves from burning until the crop matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni eda lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Buu kookoo baai bibii ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he kɛyashi tso lɛ baa eda kwraa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce food for the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet soil, increasing sunlight exposure and preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for leaf growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore green growth and increases corn yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ akwɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my corn help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni ŋmãa yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil, feeding nearby corn plants and improving ground health for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Covering soil with dried organic material, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground during hot days, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your field.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ.

english: When cassava plants are overcrowded, they compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This results in thin plants with very small roots instead of large, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei komɛi yɛ shishifãi bibii kwraa yɛ bulb agbo ni mli wa najiaŋ.

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that quickly steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight intended for your crops. Removing weeds early leaves more resources for your crops to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oná nibii babaoo ni okɛbaahã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off instead of forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of specific nutrients. Keeping the moisture level steady helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ ni bɛ Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ hi shi daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes inside the funnel leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai ni tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the soft inner leaves of growing maize. Spotting them early allows you to use targeted sprays or organic deterrents before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Amɛ ni ooona mra Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni tsiɔ nii anaa lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by several hot, dry weeks. Waiting for the rainy season to fully establish ensures seeds have continuous moisture to germinate and survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ otsii babaoo ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ni abaamɛ koni eba shi kwraa lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Can I really use my leftover empty cocoa husks as fertilizer for my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni eshwɛ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ atsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha mi kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, empty cocoa husks are rich in essential plant food like potassium and organic matter. When left to break down near the base of your trees, they turn into natural fertilizer that enriches the soil and helps your trees yield more pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko mli lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ tsei niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Kɛji ashi amɛ koni amɛkumɔ yɛ tso ko shishi lɛ Amɛbafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: How far away from the tree trunk should I pile the empty cocoa husks on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mato kookoo ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: You should place the husks in a ring a few feet away from the main trunk around the shade line of the tree. Keeping them away from direct contact with the trunk prevents trapped moisture from rotting the bark or spreading fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ awo ŋmeii lɛ amli aaafee ninetalɔi 2-3 kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifã wulu lɛ he ni bɔle tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ naa koni ekafite tso lɛ yibii lɛ loo ekagbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ eshwa.

english: How long does it take for heaped cocoa husks to turn into food for my cocoa roots?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo ŋmeii ni ato naa lɛ bafeɔ niyenii kɛhaa mi kookoo shishifãi lɛ?

english: Cocoa husks usually take a few months to fully rot and break down into rich black soil matter, depending on moisture and heat. As rain washes through the rotting husks, nutrients soak down into the soil for the roots to feed on.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii lɛ heɔ nyɔji fioo dani amɛfiteɔ kwraa ni amɛkuɔ amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ diŋ ni jara wa. Edamɔ hulutsoo kɛ dɔlɛ nɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ tswa yɛ ŋshɔŋloo ni miifite lɛ nɔ lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ aye.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm soil is tired and needs extra food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ etɔ ni ehe miihia ni aha lɛ niyenii kroko?

english: Tired soil often causes tree leaves to turn pale green or yellow instead of deep green. You may also notice that your trees produce smaller pods or shed their flowers before fruits can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ haa tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Ekolɛ obaana akɛ otso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ yibii.

english: Can I use cocoa husk fertilizer on my food crops like plantains and vegetables too?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ cocoa husk ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii yɛ mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains kɛ aduawai anɔ?

english: Yes, decomposed cocoa husks work very well for plantains, maize, and garden vegetables. The natural nutrients inside the husks help improve root strength and fruit growth for almost any farm crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ plantains, ŋmãa kɛ abɔɔ mli aduawai anɔ. Adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ aduawai daalɛ yaa hiɛ kɛha nɔ ni miihe ashɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Will piling fresh cocoa husks on my land spread black pod disease to my healthy trees?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmeii heei ni mikɛtoɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baagbɛ black pod hela ashwã mitsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: If the harvested pods were sick with black pod, putting them fresh near healthy trees can spread the fungus. It is best to let diseased husks dry out fully or decompose in a pile far away before spreading them as manure.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ hela mɔ amɛ kɛ ŋmeii diji Sũ ni akɛaawo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashwã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmãa ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ agbi kwraa loo efite ni etsɔ ŋmeii dani okɛshwie nɔ akɛ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but only a few turn into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi tsei fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ?

english: A cocoa tree drops extra flowers when it does not have enough water, sunlight balance, or soil nutrients to feed every pod. Giving the trees natural fertilizer and proper shade helps more flowers stay attached and grow into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi krokomɛi kɛji nu, hulu la, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulutsoo ni sa ha tso lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: What causes the leaves on my cocoa trees to turn yellow and fall off during the year?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ afi lɛ mli?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the tree is missing key soil nutrients like nitrogen, is receiving too much direct hot sun, or is suffering from dry roots during dry spells.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni ekɛ ehe ewo hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli tsɔ. aloo naagbai ni kɔɔ shishifãi ni egbi he lɛ kpeɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: How does covering the soil with crop husks help my cocoa trees during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Bɔ ni tsei ni akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Piling crop husks around the root zone acts like a blanket over the dirt. It shields the ground from hot sun, slows down water evaporation, and keeps the soil cool and moist for much longer without rain.
ga: Tso mli ŋmeii ni atoɔ he kɛbɔleɔ Shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and tender roots that cannot handle intense, direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa from harsh sun heat until their leaves grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Be kukuoo mli tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni baai lɛ mli waa.

english: How do I know if there are too many big trees on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsei wuji babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If your farm feels too dark, your crops look weak, or you find it difficult to walk around and work, you likely have too many trees blocking light and space.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ tsɔ Oŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ. Aloo ewaa kɛha bo akɛ oootsi ohe kɛya he fɛɛ he ni otsu nii, oyɛ tsei babaoo ni tsiɔ la kɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ naa.

english: Should I remove all the trees on my land before planting my crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: No, you do not need to cut down every tree. You should only remove some of the excess trees so you have enough light and space to work while leaving a few to protect the soil.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa ni ofo tso fɛɛ tso. Esa akɛ ojie tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ekomɛi pɛ. Bɔni afee ni oná la kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛtsu nii. Kɛtsɔ fãi komɛi ni ashiɔ koni akɛbu sũ lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it so difficult for me to clear and work on my land when there are many trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa kɛhaa mi akɛ matse mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni matsu he nii lɛ? Be mli ni tsei babaoo ebɔle he lɛ?

english: Having too many trees creates heavy shade, thick branches, and tangled underground roots that physically block your tools and make farm maintenance very tiring.
ga: Tsei babaoo tsɔ feɔ hulutsoo, tsei niji ni mli tse, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni ebɔle amɛhe ni tsiɔ odɛŋdadei lɛ anaa. Ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ feɔ nɔ ni tɔ̃ɔ mɔ waa.

english: How does cutting down a few selected trees help my remaining crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei fioo komɛi ni ahala lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Removing extra trees opens up the sky to let in direct sunlight and reduces competition underground, giving your crops the energy they need to grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaagbele ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa koni hulu la lɛ aba mli tɛ̃ɛ. ni eha shikpɔŋ shishi akaŋshii aba shi Ehaa onibii lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are my crops growing thin and tall instead of becoming thick and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miikwɛ̃ ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together or shaded by bigger plants, they stretch upward to search for sunlight, which makes their stems weak.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo tsei wuji tsi amɛnaa lɛ Tso lɛ baagbala ehe kɛya ŋwɛi koni eyatao hulu la. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Can having too much shade from large plants reduce the yield of my crops?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ahe hulutsoo babaoo baanyɛ aha mi yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, crops need sunlight to produce their own food. If large plants block the sun, your crops will not have enough energy to produce big fruits or healthy harvests.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia hulu la koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛná niyenii. Kɛji tsei wuji tsi hulu la lɛ naa Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwo yibii wuji loo yibiiwoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant too many crops in one small area?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ he bibioo kome?

english: Overcrowding causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in stunted growth for almost all the plants in that spot.
ga: Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ nakai kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ edaŋ kɛyashɛɛɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ.

english: Will large tree roots underground take food away from my crop roots?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baajie niyenii kɛjɛ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli?

english: Yes, tree roots spread wide and deep to drink water and take nutrients from the soil, which can starve nearby crops if the trees are too close.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛnu nu ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha hɔmɔ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ kɛji tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ.

english: Why do crops planted directly next to wild, bothersome plants look unhealthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ koo mli tsei ni haoɔ mɔ lɛ ahe lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ehiii kwraa lɛ?

english: Bothersome wild plants grow fast and aggressively steal water and nutrients from the soil right out from under your crops' roots.
ga: Koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ashishi.

english: How can I prevent unwanted wild plants from bothering my main crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi koo mli tsei ni ataooo lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ?

english: You need to clear bothersome plants early and remove their roots from the soil so they cannot compete with your main crops for nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ kɛjɛ ohe mra. ni ejie shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ ji koni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with lots of leaves, but the roots inside the ground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo?

english: When crops get too much shade or too much nitrogen fertilizer, they put all their energy into growing leaves and tall stems above ground instead of sending energy down to build big tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, a haa he wami kɛ baa si konɛ e kɛ pee yi wulu ko.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen food from the soil, or the soil is too full of standing water, which prevents the roots from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni ekã shi babaoo Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Pepper leaves curl when tiny insects like aphids or thrips suck the sap from under the leaf, or when the plant catches a plant virus spread by whiteflies. The curling is the plant's reaction to damage.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ŋmɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ. aloo kɛ́ tso ko he hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ emɔ tso ko. Curling ji bɔ ni tso ko feɔ enii ehaa kɛji efite.

english: Why do my okra plants stop producing new pods after I leave a few big ones to dry on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ kpa ŋmeii heei feemɔ beni mishi ŋmeii wuji fioo komɛi yɛ tso lɛ shishi koni amɛgbi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When an okra pod grows big and forms hard seeds, the plant thinks its job of reproducing is finished, so it stops making new flowers. Harvesting young pods regularly forces the plant to keep making new ones.
ga: Kɛ okra ŋmeii lɛ dara ni amɛná dumɔwui ni wa Tso lɛ susuɔ akɛ egbɛfaŋnɔ lɛ egbe naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ekpaa fɔfɔi heei afeemɔ. Kɛ́ akpa tso lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni eya nɔ ewo ŋmeii heei.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when water is irregular, or when there is too much fertilizer. High heat destroys the pollen inside the flower, so the plant drops the useless blossom.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ nu lɛ ejaaa loo kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa lɛ.

english: Why does my groundnut plant flower above ground, but the groundnuts grow under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ miikwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: After a groundnut flower is fertilized, it grows a long stem called a 'peg' that bends down and pushes itself into the soil. The actual groundnut pod can only develop once that peg is safely buried under soft earth.
ga: Beni atswa ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ ŋmɔshi nii sɛɛ lɛ Eyɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘peg’ ni shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Anɔkwa ŋmeii baanyɛ aba pɛ kɛji akɛ afu ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ shishi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my sweet pepper fruits developing black, rotten spots on the bottom while still on the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi bell pepper aduawai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni fiteɔ yɛ amɛshishi be mli ni amɛyɔɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium to the growing fruit, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil dries out completely and then gets flooded.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha yibii ni miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi kwraa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ nu afua.

english: Why do I see white powdery dust covering the leaves of my garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa sũ yɛŋ ni ehà eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: That white powder is a fungal disease called powdery mildew. It spreads when plants are crowded too closely together and humid air gets trapped between the leaves.
ga: Pauda yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ emɔ baai lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines suddenly start turning brown and dying early before the rainy season ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines usually means pests like yam beetles are eating the tuber underground, or fungi in the soil are rotting the main root system so water cannot reach the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei ni agbiɔ oya tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ sweet potato ŋmeii miiye ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Aloo ŋmei ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miiha shishifã titri lɛ miifite. No hewɔ lɛ nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize farm turning yellow before the corn is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and healthy. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer early in the season fixes this issue.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks fall over easily whenever a small storm hits my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shi mlɛo be fɛɛ be ni ahum bibioo ko baatswa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over when seeds are planted too close together, forcing stems to grow thin and weak, or when roots are too shallow. Planting with proper spacing and mounding soil around the base gives the roots stronger support.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ yitso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ loo be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ Dumɔ ni akɛ he ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni abua naa ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni ewaje shishifãi lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava shows it is ready when the bottom leaves naturally dry up and drop off, and the soil directly around the base of the stem begins to crack as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Akɛɛ Yucca efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tuber lɛ mli fũuɔ lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with thick green leaves, but the tubers under the ground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa tsɔ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves on top instead of tubers underneath. Using balanced soil nutrients and rotating crops helps the plant grow larger tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo Yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmei tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni adu yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why are the small young cocoa pods on my trees turning black and drying up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mitsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp, and overly shaded conditions. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and air flow through the farm to stop the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni helai akpa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into actual fruits during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ anɔkwa aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from forming fruit. Providing light shade or watering early in the morning helps keep the plants cool enough to set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. ni ehaa etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ Shading loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Pepper leaves curl when tiny insects like aphids or mites suck the sap from under the leaves, or when the plant is trying to protect itself from extreme heat and dry soil.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites lɛ nu nu ni yɔɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ. Aloo kɛ́ tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he.

english: Why do some of my bean seeds rot in the soil instead of sprouting after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaakwɛ̃ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bean seeds rot if they are planted too deep where oxygen cannot reach them, or if the soil stays overly wet and soggy right after planting.
ga: Beans lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ fe nine beni adu lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ

english: Why is planting my crops in neat straight rows better than scattering the seeds randomly on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo ni ja lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni mikɛduɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows makes sure every plant gets its fair share of sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without crowding, while also making weeding and harvesting much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛtsiii amɛhe gbɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why is it important to put wooden sticks next to my yam plants for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tso ko ma sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi koni amɛkwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to feed the plant. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also prevents leaves from rotting and helps the tubers underground grow much larger.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛfi tso lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkafiteɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetables with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Aduawai ni jwɛi loo baai yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly in the heat, and stops weeds from sprouting.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji edɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃
