english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient in the soil, or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients too deep for the roots to reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛtee shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which results in thin, weak plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How does mixing dried poultry manure into my soil help my crops?
ga: Te kooloi ashishifãi ni egbi ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Poultry manure acts as a rich natural food for your crops, releasing nutrients slowly into the soil while helping the ground hold on to water better during dry weeks.
ga: Kooloi ashishifã tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jara wa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛtsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fiofio lɛ nɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when the weather gets extremely hot, when the plants do not get consistent water, or when there are not enough insects around to pollinate the blooms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ

english: What causes ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the fall armyworm, a pest that feeds on the growing center of maize plants. Spraying early with recommended botanical or chemical treatments helps protect your crop.
ga: Fall armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ shwie nɔ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so poorly even when it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops, and they can also act as breeding grounds for harmful insects and plant diseases.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ebaanyɛ etsu nii hu akɛ he ni kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahelai fɔɔ yɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava plants are ready to be dug up for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ koni akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the main stem starts to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa

english: Why should I plant my crops in straight lines instead of scattering the seeds across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ mashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines makes it easy to walk through your farm, remove weeds, apply fertilizer evenly, and ensure every plant gets equal access to sunlight and soil nutrients.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa oŋmɔ lɛ mli nyiɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo. Kwɛmɔ jwɛi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli daa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei fɛɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: What does it mean when you tell me to use specific planting distances like 20 by 20 on my land?
ga: Kɛ okɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui akuu pɔtɛɛ ko tamɔ 20 x 20 atsu nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: Specific planting distances mean measuring a set amount of space between each plant and row so that crops have enough room to spread their leaves and roots without choking each other.
ga: He pɔtɛɛ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ asusu gbɛ ni kã tso fɛɛ tso kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋ lɛ he koni eha tsei lɛ aná gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtsiii amɛhe gbɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete for water, sunlight, and food from the soil, which causes them to grow thin, weak, and produce very small harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do plants grow healthier when I leave enough space between them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mishi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: Proper spacing gives the plant's roots room to gather food from the ground while letting fresh air and sunlight reach every part of the plant, keeping diseases away.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ buaa niyenii naa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ. Koni akɛtsi hela naa

english: Why does a farm inspector care about how neatly my plants are arranged on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ susuɔ bɔ ni ato mitsei lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Inspectors check farm arrangement to ensure you are following proper farming practices, which guarantees that your field will yield a good harvest and qualify for support or certification.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kwɛɔ bɔ ni akwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ahaa lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ akɛ oonyiɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni sa asɛɛ. Enɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná yibii kpakpai ni esa akɛ aná yelikɛbuamɔ loo odaseyeli.

english: Can I be disqualified from a farming project if I do not follow the recommended planting spacing?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ajie mi kɛjɛ okwaayeli gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli kɛji mikɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ aduɔ nii lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, standard projects require farmers to follow specific spacing so that inputs like seeds and fertilizers are not wasted on overcrowded farms that will produce low yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛjianɔtoo ni ato lɛ biɔ ni okwaafoi lɛ akwɛ gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ. Enɛ ji koni nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tamɔ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akafite yɛ ŋmɔji ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ faaa.

english: What is the difference between traditional random planting and direct distance planting?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ kusum naa dumɔwui ni aduɔ trukaa kɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ teŋ?

english: Traditional random planting places seeds wherever there is open space, while direct distance planting uses exact measurements between plants to maximize your farm's total yield.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi ni akɛduɔ nii trukaa lɛ kɛ dumɔwui woɔ he fɛɛ he ni gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɔɔ. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔ tɛ̃ɛ heɔ susumɔi pɔtɛɛ yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ. Koni oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does planting in neat rows make weeding easier for me?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ haa jwɛi lɛ anɔyeli feɔ mlɛo?

english: Row planting creates clear pathways between your crops, allowing you to move freely with a hoe or cutlass to clear weeds without accidentally damaging your main crops.
ga: Row planting haa gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ baa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ. Ehaa okɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei fãa gbɛ oya koni ojie jwɛi ni okpaaa onibii titrii lɛ ahiɛ yɛ oshara mli.

english: Why do crops planted in straight rows suffer less from disease than crowded crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ helai nyɛɛɛ aba amɛnɔ tamɔ tsei ni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Straight rows allow wind to blow through the farm easily, keeping leaves dry and preventing moisture-loving diseases and pests from spreading rapidly across your field.
ga: Nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni ja lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli mlɛo. hã baai lɛ agbi Ni otsi helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli oya.

english: How do I know if the pathways between my crops are wide enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa?

english: Pathways are wide enough if an officer or farmer can comfortably walk through the field to inspect plants and carry tools without stepping on stems or brushing against leaves.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi lɛ baafee shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa kɛji mɛi ni tsuɔ he nii loo okwaafoi lɛ baanyɛ anyiɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ hejɔlɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ tsei lɛ ni amɛwo nitsumɔ dadei ni amɛnyiɛɛɛ tsei lɛ anɔ loo amɛshwieee baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees dry up and turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains grown nearby to shield them from excessive heat and retain moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo plantains ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main plant. Leaving only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main plantain tree gets enough food to produce large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwu titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii ni tsii ni dara.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin without producing big corn cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii wuji bɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly allows every plant to get enough food and light to form full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot exhausts specific nutrients from the soil and allows corn pests and diseases to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. ni ehaa ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs to lift its leaves toward sunlight to catch light and produce food, which is then stored underground to grow big tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni shwereɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛná la ni amɛwo niyenii. ni abaato shikpɔŋ shishi koni akɛdu bulb tsei wuji

english: Which part of the cassava stem is best for me to cut and plant in my farm?
ga: Kasava tso lɛ fã ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafolɔ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The hard, mature middle part of the stem grows best. Very soft tops rot easily, while the very bottom part can be too woody to sprout healthy leaves quickly.
ga: Tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni wa ni eda lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ. Tso lɛ mli tsei lɛ darako kwraa ni amɛgboiɔ oya. yɛ be mli ni shishigbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ afee tsei tsɔ ni ebaaha baai ni mli wa lɛ akwɛ̃ oya.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or irregular watering, as the plant tries to conserve water rather than feed growing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he moŋ fe ni amɛaaye aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense behavior where pepper plants roll up their leaves to reduce water loss through evaporation during intense afternoon heat.
ga: Leaf curling ji adebɔɔ mli su ko ni buɔ mɔ he. he ni pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why did applying too much fertilizer cause my crop leaves to burn and dry out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mitso lɛ mli fe nine lɛ haa mitso lɛ baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts. Using too much draws water away from the plant's roots into the soil, causing the leaves to dry up as if exposed to heat.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ yɛ ŋoo babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛtsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ tamɔ nɔ ni akɛ amɛ ewo la mli.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my young cassava plants even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa mi yucca bibioo lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than cassava plants and actively steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the soil, preventing the cassava roots from developing.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmei tsei ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ cassava shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes near my yam plants for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ he koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb off the ground so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy the plant needs to grow large, healthy tubers under the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛ bulbs agboi ni mli wa akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep dropping their flowers instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Excessive heat, sudden dry spells, or a lack of moisture cause severe stress to tomato plants, making them drop their flowers to save energy rather than producing fruit.
ga: la ni mli edɔ fe nine kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi trukaa loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Groundnuts mature underground, so once the yellow flower is pollinated above ground, the stalk naturally grows downward into the soil where the nut can safely form.
ga: Peanuts kwɛ̃ɔ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ŋmeii lɛ baafee shweshweeshwe yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves look limp and droopy in the hot afternoon sun but wake up by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli shi kɛ́ mite shi leebi maŋkpa lɛ?

english: In strong afternoon heat, leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink it up. The plant wilts on purpose to slow down water loss, then recovers at night when temperatures cool.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tsei gboiɔ kɛ yiŋtoo akɛ amɛbaaha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. No sɛɛ lɛ, ehiɛɔ shi gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions, especially during the rainy season when sunlight cannot reach inside dense tree branches to dry off moisture.
ga: Fuŋ ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli beni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe koni ekɛha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi lɛ.

english: What makes the leaves on my hot pepper plants twist and curl tightly together?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ekome?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on leaf sap and spreading viruses that distort new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu kɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ni fiteɔ baa heei adalɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when heavy rains stay too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills all air spaces in the soil with water, root crops cannot breathe, allowing harmful fungi and bacteria in wet soil to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves means the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil, so the plant steals nutrients from its oldest leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tso hee ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during rainstorms when carrying fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay near the soil surface, making the heavy fruit bunch top-heavy so strong winds can easily pull the entire root system out of wet ground.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ha aduawai akuu lɛ afee nɔ ni tsii-kɛ-tsii. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall, thin, and weak with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa, egbɔjɔɔ, ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crowded plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving none of them with enough strength to produce big cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni buaa amɛhe naa lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct sunlight and high heat. They require shade crops like plantains or shade trees to cover them and keep the soil moist during their first few years of growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni ekɛbaa lɛ mli.

english: Why does it take several years before my cocoa trees start producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani mi-cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need time to build a strong stem structure and deep root system to support the weight of heavy pods. While traditional varieties take 4 to 5 years to bear fruit, modern hybrid varieties can start producing pods in about 2 to 3 years.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia be koni amɛma amɛshishifãi ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baaye abua amɛshishifãi ni tsii lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni blema tsei srɔtoi lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my crop plants curl up and droop in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves during the heat of the day as a protective response to reduce water loss through evaporation. If the leaves bounce back in the evening when temperatures drop, the plant is simply conserving moisture.
ga: Tsei baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli koni nu akafite kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ Tsei lɛ miikwɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ kɛkɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa tree falling off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Trees naturally drop extra flowers they cannot support, but heavy flower loss is often caused by a lack of rainfall, poor soil nutrients, or damage from insects like mirids that feed on delicate flower stems.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ nɔ lɛ kpo. Shi bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ ji nɔ ni haa fɔfɔi babaoo laajeɔ lɛ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo nɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees giving me fewer pods than they produced years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo fe nɔ ni ewo nakai afii fɛɛ ni eho lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 15 to 20 years, their natural productivity declines and they become more vulnerable to soil nutrient depletion and diseases. Old trees need heavy pruning, fertilizer, or replacement with new seedlings to restore farm yields.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tso ko ye afii 15 kɛyashi 20 lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baa shi. ni amɛyɔɔ oshara babaoo akɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baafite kɛ helai srɔtoi. Ehe miihia ni afo tsei momoi lɛ, awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo akɛ dumɔwui heei awo amɛ najiaŋ koni ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do I need to cut off branches from my cocoa tree if I want more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso niji kɛji miitao aduawai babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak, dead, or overgrown branches that steal food and water from the main tree. Cutting them back lets sunlight reach the main trunk where cocoa pods grow and allows the tree to focus its energy on producing fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni egbɔjɔ, ni egboi, loo ni eda fe nine ni juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ niji lɛ. Kɛ́ afo mli lɛ, hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tso titri lɛ he ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa yibiiwoo nɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and shady conditions. Pruning heavy tree branches and clearing weeds helps air and sunshine dry out the farm, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi waa kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ mli egbiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ

english: Why do pests attack my crops more heavily when the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: The start of the rainy season causes plants to flush with soft, new leaves and shoots, which attract insects looking for fresh food and moisture to reproduce quickly.
ga: Nugbɔ be lɛ shishijee kɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii baa tso lɛ nɔ. Egbalaa kooloi bibii ni miitao niyenii hee kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛfɔ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow instead of rich green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is starving for essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that too much standing water around the roots is preventing the plant from breathing and absorbing food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miiye tso lɛ. Aloo nu ni yɔɔ dioo ni ebɔle lɛ Shishifãi babaoo tsɔ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekamu ni ekɛ niyenii akamɔ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant food crops like cassava or plantain together with my tree crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ mi tsei lɛ baadu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ?

english: Intercropping food crops with tree crops helps protect young tree seedlings, keeps weeds down, and provides your family with food and extra income while you wait for your slow-growing tree crops to mature.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ tsei baadu lɛ baaye abua ni ebu dumɔwui bibii ahe, ebaaha jwɛi akabote mli, ni eha oweku lɛ aná niyenii kɛ shika kroko yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ tsei ni daraa blɛoo lɛ ni amɛdara lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow much faster when natural rainwater falls compared to when I use stagnant water from a nearby pond?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa oya waa kɛ́ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ nɛ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto be mli ni mikɛ nu ni yɔɔ kpoo ni jɛ nubu ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ he.

english: Rainwater picks up nitrogen directly from the atmosphere as it falls, giving crops an instant nutrient boost. Stagnant water from ponds often lacks oxygen and can carry soil-borne pathogens that slow down plant growth.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ beni egbeeɔ shi lɛ. Ehaa tsei naa niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ Bei pii lɛ Nu ni damɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔi amli lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni haa tsei lɛ daraa oya lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off when floodwater stays on my farm for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need oxygen from the soil to breathe. When water sits on the land without draining, it suffocates the roots, causing them to rot and stopping the plant from taking up food, which makes the leaves turn yellow and fall.
ga: Tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaaa tso lɛ aye nii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants lean and stretch towards the side where the sun rises?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miitsi ehe ni ekɛ ehe miibɔ hulushitee he lɛ?

english: Plants produce special natural growth chemicals that make their stems stretch toward sunlight. They do this automatically so their leaves can capture maximum light to produce food for growth.
ga: Tsei feɔ tsofai krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ mli ni haa amɛshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Amɛfeɔ enɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha dalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up in the hot afternoon sun but stand straight again in the cool morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shwane hulu lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ni ooodamɔ tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ nɔ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon heat is a defense behavior. The plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, preventing water from escaping through tiny leaf pores.
ga: Baai ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji subaŋ ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ aba shi. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my groundnut seeds after the first rains start in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the rain settles the soil deep enough—usually after two or three good rains—so the ground stays consistently moist. Planting in dry soil after just one light shower causes seeds to dry up and die.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa—bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ—koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, why do the stalks grow tall and thin without giving me big ears of corn?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ ŋmãa lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni efeee ŋmãa toi wuji lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. The plants stretch thin trying to reach light instead of using their energy to develop thick stems and large corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ, amɛgbala amɛhe bibii koni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ la he.

english: Why do some of my bean seeds rot under the dirt while others sprout quickly out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ ekomɛi gboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi jeɔ kpo oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds buried too deeply or placed in overly wet, heavy soil cannot get the oxygen and warmth they need to wake up. They suffocate and rot before the shoot can break through the ground surface.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ loo ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ tsɔ ni etsii lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ dɔlɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛte shi lɛ. Amɛmuɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop many of their small green pods before they grow into full cocoa fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ dani eda ni etsɔ kookoo aduawai ni eyi obɔ?

english: This behavior is called pod wilt. The tree naturally drops excess young pods when it senses it does not have enough water, sunlight, or soil nutrients to nourish all of them to maturity.
ga: Atsɛɔ subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ pod wilting. Tsei shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛsu naa kɛ́ amɛnu he akɛ nu, hulu la, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni baaye abua amɛdalɛ ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster on my farm than my yam crops even though they both get the same rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ amɛnáa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ kome moŋ.

english: Weeds are wild local plants with deep, aggressive root systems naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions, allowing them to grab soil nutrients and rainwater much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nugbɔ nu mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why does cutting off the top tip of my leafy garden vegetables cause them to branch out with more leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi abɔɔ mli aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishifãi ni afoɔ lɛ haa amɛwoɔ niji kɛ baai babaoo lɛ?

english: The main growing tip sends a chemical signal that stops side branches from growing. When you cut that tip off, the plant releases its side buds, causing it to grow bushier with more harvestable leaves.
ga: Nɔ titri ni yaa hiɛ lɛ tsuɔ tsofa okadii koni ekɛtsi niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara. Kɛ́ ofo nakai naagbee lɛ Tso lɛ baagbala sɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa jwɛi babaoo kɛ baai babaoo ni abaanyɛ akpa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and dying off before the corn is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This usually happens because the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs to stay green, or because the plant isn't getting enough water. The maize plant pulls remaining nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele yɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli. aloo akɛni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa hewɔ lɛ Abɛi tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, severe dry soil, or a lack of pollination. When temperatures are too high or water is scarce, the plant drops its flowers to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa. loo pollination ni bɛ Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu bɛ Tso lɛ baashi efɔfɔi lɛ yɛ nɔ koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits on the field without draining, it starves the roots of oxygen and creates conditions for soil fungus to cause root rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbee ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo lɛ aba.

english: How do I know if the small worms eating my maize leaves are Fall Armyworms?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ ji Fall Armyworms?

english: Fall Armyworms hide inside the center top (whorl) of the maize plant, eating ragged holes in the leaves and leaving behind powdery, sawdust-like waste inside the leaf folds.
ga: Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ aŋwɛi teŋgbɛ (ring) lɛ mli. Eyeɔ bu ni ekumɔ yɛ baai amli ni eshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I do not plant plantains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji miduuu amɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees have broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hɔɔŋ. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo koni ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants yield smaller fruit when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When tomatoes are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same soil nutrients and water, while their leaves shade each other from sunlight. This competition leaves the plant with less energy to grow large fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tomatoi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tomato lɛ baai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haaa tso lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaawo yibii wuji.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the vines off the damp ground on stakes also protects the leaves from soil diseases and leaf rot.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ hu buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How do weeds growing near my crop reduce my final harvest yield?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aha minaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your crop needs to grow. They can also act as hiding spots for insects and diseases that jump onto your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ etsu nii hu akɛ he ni koolooi kɛ helai teeɔ amɛhe yɛ. ni shwieɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ

english: Why does the maize I harvest look small and uneven if I plant seeds saved from last year's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ bibioo ni eshɛɛɛ he kɛji midu dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi ni midu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many modern seeds are hybrids bred for a high yield in their first planting. Saving and replanting seeds from that harvest causes the crop to lose its strong growth traits, leading to lower yields and irregular plant sizes.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui babaoo ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui amli. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ amɛdalɛ su ni mli wa lɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ adalɛ hu kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: Why is it harmful to apply chemical fertilizer when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baawo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it safely. When applied to dry soil, the concentrated fertilizer chemicals can burn and kill the plant roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei shishifãi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen nutrient in the soil, or the roots are sitting in too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Aloo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and look dead under the hot afternoon sun but wake up again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ? Shi te shi ekoŋŋ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink from the ground. They droop to protect themselves and conserve water, then bounce back overnight as temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛbu nu he. Kɛkɛ lɛ, efoɔ ehe ekoŋŋ nyɔɔŋ kome be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants before any fruits grow out of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the plant lacks nutrients. Keeping the soil damp with mulch and watering regularly during dry weather helps the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũu ni akɛ nu shwie nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: My cassava plants have grown very tall with huge leaves, so why are the tubers under the soil so small?
ga: Mi-cassava tso lɛ daa waa ni eyɛ baai wuji. Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, cassava puts all its energy into growing big leaves and stems instead of roots. The plant needs potassium nutrient in the soil to direct its energy into expanding the tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi kɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Tsei he miihia potassium yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛgbala amɛ bulbs lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa tree turn black and spoil during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is a fungal sickness that spreads quickly when the farm is too damp and shaded. Pruning extra tree branches lets sunlight and wind flow through the farm to dry out the cocoa pods.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ ŋmɔji amli hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɛ. Afoɔ tsei niji krokomɛi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small shoot suckers to keep growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow creates heavy competition, as they steal food and water from the main mother plant. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring your main plant produces a large bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ekɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa otso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that builds big tubers underground. Lifting the vines on sticks keeps the leaves exposed to the sun and prevents them from rotting on wet soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni feɔ bulbs wuji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ, hulu la shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ, ni ehaaa amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal water, fertilizer, and light before your crops can take them. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the nourishment they need to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my seeds very deep inside the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ midumɔwui lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, they run out of stored energy trying to push up through the heavy soil before reaching light. Planting seeds at shallow depth helps them sprout quickly and strongly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋwɛi dani ashɛ la lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and builds up crop-specific pests. Rotating with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts returns good nitrogen nutrients back to the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kpakpa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong heat. Planting shade crops like plantains next to them creates living umbrellas that shelter the cocoa from direct sun and keep the soil moist while the young trees establish their roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make food. It can also happen if heavy rains flood the field, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkɛfee niyenii Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔ ko mli nu, ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant suffers from lack of water during flowering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulching around the roots helps the plant retain its flowers so they turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli, ni no haa ebafeɔ tomato.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest beneath the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava plants show they are ready when their lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping naturally, the stem becomes woody, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack open from the swelling tubers.
ga: Yucca tso tsɔɔ akɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Tso lɛ tsɔɔ tso. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important for me to gather and dispose of diseased leaves and rotten pods away from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mabua baai ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ anaa ni majie kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving diseased plant materials or fallen fruit in your farm leaves behind pests and fungal spores. Clearing away rotten leftovers starves pests and stops infections from spreading to your healthy crops.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi tsei ahe nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo aduawai ni egbee shi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaashi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai. Niyenii ni efite ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ooojie lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, ni ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant seeds too close to each other in the same row?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients. This competition makes the plants tall, thin, and weak, which leads to lower yields during harvest.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛɔ amɛhe mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why did my crop leaves dry up and look burned after I poured fertilizer right next to the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbi ni amɛshã beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is rich in salts that can pull water out of plant roots and stems if placed in direct contact. Applying fertilizer a short distance away from the stem and watering it into the soil prevents root burn and lets the plant feed safely.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli kɛji akɛ amɛkpe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo tso lɛ shishi fioo ni okɛ nu wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ akashã, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ena niyenii shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and stake my yam vines so they can climb high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo mli koni amɛkwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce the food required to grow big tubers underground. Staking the vines elevates the leaves into the sun and prevents shade from weeds, allowing the plant to build thick, healthy roots.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ adu wain tsei lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akashɛ hulu lɛ nɔ, ni ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and look weak during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling during intense afternoon heat is a natural reaction crops use to protect themselves from losing water. If the soil has enough moisture, the leaves will relax and open up again by evening.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeleɔ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my vegetable seedlings in the nursery growing very long, thin stems that easily fall over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ daraa kakadaŋŋ nɛkɛ lɛ? Ani tso lɛ mli etse ni egbeeɔ shi oya?

english: Seedlings stretch and grow thin when they do not receive enough daylight inside the nursery shade. They are reaching out for sunlight, and without enough light, their stems remain too soft and weak to support the plant.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala ni amɛbaafee bibioo kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Amɛkpã amɛniji amli koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. ni la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Etso lɛ mli lɛ, no mli lɛ eyɛ blɛoo lolo ni ebɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tso lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that create natural shade and retain soil moisture, protecting tender cocoa trees during their early growth stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: How do I know the best time to start planting my maize in the major rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: You should wait until the rains become steady for about two consecutive weeks so the ground holds enough moisture. Planting after the very first isolated rainfall can cause seeds to dry out if a unexpected dry spell follows.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be aaafee otsii enyɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji hɔmɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ ba.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and healthy, so applying compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will restore leaf color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are there small ragged holes appearing on the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in leaves are commonly caused by pests like the fall armyworm feeding on the plant. Inspecting your farm early allows you to treat affected plants with approved remedies before the pests destroy the central growing shoot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni amɛye tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni fãa yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Haa okɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsaa tsei ni ena hela lɛ. dani kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baafite ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ;

english: Is it better to plant seeds saved from my previous harvest or buy certified seeds?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli loo aaahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli?

english: Certified seeds are specially developed to resist local pests and diseases while yielding more crops. Seeds saved from past harvests tend to lose vigor and yield less over repeated seasons.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ bei ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays around them for too long due to poor drainage. Planting on raised soil ridges or mounds helps water drain away easily, keeping roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ Dumɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ oya. Ha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why should I prune extra shoots and dead branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni egboi kɛ tsei niji kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to sunlight and airflow, which reduces high humidity that causes black pod disease. It also directs the tree's energy into producing pods rather than excess foliage.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaagbele ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni fa ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi. Etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ hu gbɛ koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why does clearing weeds early make my crops grow much bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ni miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ babaoo?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing vital resources, allowing your main crop to grow freely.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nibii ni he hiaa. Ye obua onibii titrii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ heyeli mli.

english: How can I stop heavy rains from washing away the good soil on my hillside farm?
ga: Matsi nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekaju shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ kɛya. Ni ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ hu?

english: Making soil ridges or planting barriers across the slope stops fast-moving rainwater. This slows the run-off, letting water soak into the ground instead of washing topsoil away.
ga: Kɛ́ afee ŋshɔkpɔ loo gbɛtsii nii ni adu yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaakpa nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ ajɛ mli blɛoo. Kɛtsɔ nu lɛ ni oooha ebote sũ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant groundnuts before planting maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baadu ŋmei dani edu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, it uses this natural nitrogen boost to grow stronger without needing as much added fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli nɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ŋmãa babaoo he ehiaaa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and cool moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are usually a sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and pulling out sick plants early stops the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Aduɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing tall and pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miidara ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen from healthy soil or fertilizer to build strong green leaves and form large, heavy cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa ni efee ŋmãa wuji ni tsii.

english: What is eating holes in the center leaves of my young corn plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeli nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is caused by the fall armyworm caterpillar. These pests hide deep inside the funnel of the young corn plant during the day to stay cool and come out at night to chew on the tender new leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi mli koni amɛha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i, ni amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ koni amɛbaye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry soil. During hot spells, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy so that it can survive the heat.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves droop during the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgboi moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, tomato leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can drink it up. As long as the leaves bounce back and stand tall again by evening, this afternoon wilting is just the plant's natural defense against heat.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Shii abɔ ni baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ shwane nɛɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he kɛkɛ.

english: Yes, cowpeas and maize grow very well together. Cowpeas naturally gather nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil, which fertilizes the maize, while the maize stalks give cowpea vines support to climb.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei feɔ ekome kɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Cowpeas buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei yeɔ ebuaa cowpea wain tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: How do I know under the ground when my yams are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams tell you they are ready under the ground when their green leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up completely. This signals that the vine has stopped growing and has pushed all its energy into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato kɛɛ bo akɛ efee klalo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni ebaai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ wain tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ewo eyitso mli.

english: Wild weeds have tough, deep root systems that wake up instantly when rain falls. Crop seeds take longer to germinate and root, so clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing light, water, and food from young crops.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni mli kwɔ. ni baate shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ Dumɔwui heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la, nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei bibii amli.

english: Seeds carry limited food stored inside them to sprout. If buried too deep, the shoot exhausts all its energy trying to push through the heavy soil and dies before reaching the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ niyenii fioo ko ni akɛtoɔ amɛmli koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli ni amɛgboi dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without any trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ mli kwraa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their delicate leaves from strong sunlight and to keep the surrounding soil moist. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or leaving some tall trees helps protect them until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni ooodu loo tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni oooshi amɛdamɔ shi lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, a key nutrient maize needs to grow green leaves and healthy cobs. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer can solve this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ, aná baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater stays trapped around the roots for too long, it cuts off oxygen and creates room for rot-causing fungi to destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa gbɛ kɛhaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ koni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting bamboo sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite be ni mikɛ ŋmeii ama shi koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking gets yam leaves up off the ground into direct sunlight, allowing the plant to make enough food energy to build large, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, restoring nutrients that maize used up during its growth.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Koni ekɛ niyenii ni ŋmãa yeɔ yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, prolonged dry spells, or irregular watering, which stresses the plant and prevents fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa ewo yibii.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in the leaves inside the funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ he?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the leaf tube. Spotting them early allows you to control them with targeted treatments before they destroy the whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai amli ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛ ni oooyɔse mra Ehaa okɛ tsofai ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ kudɔɔ amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking leaf sap and spreading viruses, which prevents leaves from expanding normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã bɔ ni sa.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the shoots coming up around my plantain stem keep growing together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mihe lɛ? Mi plantain tsei lɛ feɔ ekome kɛkwɛɔ.

english: Allowing too many shoots (suckers) to grow from one plantain root forces them to steal food and water from each other, resulting in smaller bunches. Pruning down to 2 or 3 stems per mat yields much bigger fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ suckers (tso) babaoo gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛjɛ plantain kome shishifãi amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ amɛnɔ ni amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ bibioo Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii 2 loo 3 yɛ mat kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha yibii ni da kwraa aba.

english: Why is it critical to clear weeds from my crop field within the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ he ni miduɔ yɛ lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are weak and easily choked out by fast-growing weeds competing for water, sunlight, and fertilizer. Clearing weeds early ensures young crops get maximum resources to establish strong root systems.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ gbeɔ amɛ oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ aná nibii babaoo ni amɛkɛma shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight. Shade trees or plantain plants protect delicate cocoa seedlings from excessive heat and water loss until their leaves are strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei loo plantains ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine kɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Kɛyashi baai lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient plants need to grow healthy green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have small ragged holes and look chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii ni etamɔ nɔ ni ashɛre lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the center of young plants and feed on tender leaves. Spotting them early helps you treat the farm before the pests destroy your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe woɔ tsei bibii ateŋ ni eyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛtaomɔ mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni ohere oŋmɔ lɛ yiwala dani kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afite onibii.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow strong and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni etsɔ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my pepper plants with dry leaves during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool and stops water from evaporating quickly. This helps your crops stay hydrated during dry periods.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil if I do not harvest them on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akpaaa amɛ yɛ be naa lɛ?

english: Once cassava roots reach maturity, leaving them in wet soil causes them to absorb excess water, leading to rot or making the tubers woody and hard to eat.
ga: Beni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Kɛ́ ashi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ekɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ loo ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ tso ni ewaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam plants need wooden stakes to climb on instead of just trailing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooonyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food for developing large tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni biɔ hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ akwɛmɔ. Staking hu buɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing lots of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off due to extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping soil moisture consistent and ensuring proper plant spacing helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ tsei lɛ abɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Why shouldn't I spread chemical fertilizer on my field right before a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes fertilizer away into gutters or deep into the soil before plant roots have time to drink it up. It is best to apply fertilizer when soil is moist but heavy rain is not expected.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa nubui amli loo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi akpaaa nugbɔ ni naa wa gbɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to start planting cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmei dumɔ?

english: Healthy soil feels dark, loose, and crumbly in your hands, allowing roots to breathe and spread easily. If soil is too hard or lacks organic matter, cassava roots cannot expand fully, resulting in poor yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ duŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nine mli, ni no haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã kwraa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni ehiii

english: Why does my land yield fewer crops after planting the same crop in the same field for several years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating crops, such as planting beans after maize, restores nutrients naturally and breaks insect pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. Rain can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach it, requiring compost or fertilizer to restore it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Nugbɔ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed their flowers before growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or insect damage. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil encourages plants to focus all their energy on leaf and stem growth instead of root development. Balanced soil nutrients ensure energy goes into building large tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ama baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ adalɛ nɔ. yɛ shishifãi ni baa lɛ najiaŋ Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ haa hewalɛ yaa bulb agboi afeemɔ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my vegetable crops curling up and turning dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies hidden under the leaves, or by viral diseases they carry. Inspecting under the leaves early helps catch pests before they damage the whole crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli ni amɛhiɛɔ lɛ Baai lɛ ashishi kwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni amɔmɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, overly wet conditions. Trimming extra branch leaves lets sunlight and air into the farm to dry off moisture and stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ baai krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ejie ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: What is the benefit of buying certified seeds instead of using saved seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ he yɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Certified seeds are bred to resist local pests, tolerate drought better, and produce uniform, high-yielding crops, whereas saved seeds can lose their vigor and carry diseases over from the previous season.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Hɔmɔ he tsuishitoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ daa ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ helai ni jɛ nyɛsɛɛ be lɛ mli lɛ aba.

english: How does spacing my crops properly during planting help them grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ to he ni sa yɛ be mli ni miduɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Proper spacing ensures that plants do not compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. When planted too close together, crops remain thin and weak.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe wooo hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli kɛji adu ni ebɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso lɛ baakã he ahi shi mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize for long-term storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa koni akɛto be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Maize is ready for storage harvest when the husks turn completely brown and dry, and the grains become hard enough that your fingernail cannot easily dent them.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni amɛgbi lɛ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaŋ otsitsii lɛ atsɔ mlɛo.

english: How far apart should I plant my palm trees on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmei tsei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Oil palm trees need about 9 meters of space between each tree in a triangular pattern. This gives their large leaves room to catch sunlight without shading neighboring trees and stops roots from fighting over soil nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ mu tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee aaafee mitai 9 yɛ tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ koŋ etɛ mli lɛ teŋ. Enɛ haa baai wuji lɛ náa he ko ni amɛnáa hulu la ni amɛtsiii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anaa. ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ awuu yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my land is suitable for growing palm trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmei tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: Palm trees thrive in deep, flat or gently sloping soil that drains water easily without swampy waterlogging. The land also needs consistent rainfall and plenty of direct sunlight throughout the year.
