ga: Palm tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ni shwieɔ shi blɛoo lɛ nɔ. ni haa nu hoɔ mlɛo ni nu ŋmeii bɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu he miihia nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Can I grow cassava or maize between my palm trees while they are still young?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei ateŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, during the first two to three years when the palm trees are small, you can grow short-term food crops like maize or legumes between the rows to earn income while waiting for the palms to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ ji bibioo. Obaanyɛ odu niyenii ni heɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Yɛ linei lɛ ateŋ koni ana shika be mli ni mɛɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ

english: How long will it take for my newly planted palm tree to start bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-palm tso ni midu ehee lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Improved oil palm varieties typically start producing their first fruit bunches 3 to 4 years after field planting, and they can continue bearing fruit for 25 to 30 years with proper care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ aduawai akui lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii afii 25 kɛyashi 30 krokomɛi kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my palm trees turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-palm tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen or magnesium, or that water is settling around the roots. Applying the right balanced fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen loo magnesium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo nu ko yɛ ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my young palm fruit bunches drying up and falling off before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm yibii bibii lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Premature fruit drop occurs mainly due to severe dry spells, nutrient deficiency in the soil, or poor pollination. Regular watering during droughts and proper fertilizer application help fruits stay on the tree.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ aduawai ni shwieɔ shi oya baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbiɔ waa. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds around the base of my palm trees slow down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ tɛŋ tsei ashishi lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds act as competitors that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your palm roots. Keeping a weed-free circle around the base of each palm ensures the tree gets all available food to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akaŋshilɔi ni juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ afee kooloo ko ni jwɛi bɛ mli ni bɔle tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Is it good to cut off the lower leaves from my palm trees?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ?

english: Pruning off dead or dry lower leaves is beneficial because it opens up space to harvest mature fruit bunches cleanly and prevents pests from nesting in dead plant material.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egboi loo egbi lɛ ni aaafo lɛ he ejaakɛ egbeleɔ gbɛ kɛha aduawai akui ni edara ni he tse ni akpaa. ni etsĩɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee amɛ ŋmeii yɛ tsei ni egboi amli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my palm fruit bunch?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei yibii lɛ?

english: A palm fruit bunch is ready to harvest when 5 to 10 loose orange fruits naturally break off and fall to the ground. This signals that the oil content inside the fruit cluster has reached its maximum level.
ga: Palm aduawai akui efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni aduawai 5 kɛyashi 10 ni ji orange lɛ mli gbala yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mu ni yɔɔ aduawai akuu lɛ mli lɛ eshɛ he ni eshɛɔ fe fɛɛ.

english: How many farm workers do I need to manage one acre of palm trees?
ga: Okwaafoi anitsulɔi enyiɛ he miihia mi koni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmei tsei acre kome nɔ?

english: For an established one-acre oil palm farm, one to two general farm workers are typically sufficient to handle routine tasks like weed control, leaf pruning, and harvesting fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛha mu ŋmɔ ni ato ama shi ni dalɛ ji acre 1 lɛ Nitsulɔ kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ fa kɛha nitsumɔi ni afeɔ daa tamɔ jwɛi akwɛmɔ. baai ni afoɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni akpaa

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and rolling up tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Leaf yellowing and rolling in young maize often signals nitrogen deficiency or drought stress. It can also happen when pests like Fall Armyworms attack the central growing point of the plant, cutting off vital nutrient flow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworms tutua tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni edaa lɛ. ni efoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ mli

english: What causes small green caterpillars to chew big holes in the leaves of my crops overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ŋmɔ buji wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the leaves or soil during the heat of the day and emerge at night or early morning to feed aggressively on young crop leaves.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai loo shikpɔŋ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli. ni ejeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa koni ekɛ ekãa aye baai bibii lɛ.

english: Cassava is typically ready 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees off my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need partial shade to shield their tender leaves from harsh tropical sunlight. Clearing all large trees leaves them exposed, causing severe heat stress and dehydration.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui taoɔ hulutsoo fioo ko koni ebu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Tsei wuji fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa baa mɔ mli.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black rotten spots on the bottom while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular or during sudden dry spells while the fruit is developing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ nu lɛ be fɛɛ be loo yɛ be mli ni hɔmɔ baa trukaa be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers instead of forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when temperatures get excessively high, during dry spells, or if too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to grow leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Aloo kɛji akɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ ha tso lɛ kwɛ̃ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant beans or groundnuts on the same land where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for heavy-feeding crops like maize in the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo aha niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crop plants right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions; their seeds lie dormant in the soil and absorb water and nutrients much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Edumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete fiercely with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak stalks and poor yield.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I wait for the rainy season to settle properly before sowing my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Sowing after just one early rain can cause seeds to sprout, but if a dry spell follows immediately, the tender young shoots will dry out and die in the hot ground.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi kɛji hɔmɔ ba ni nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, Young tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How long does a newly planted cocoa tree take before it starts producing pods for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties can take 4 to 5 years. Proper weeding, shade management, and soil fertility help trees reach maturity faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni kusum kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahe afii 4 kɛyashi 5. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ Shade nɔkwɛmɔ Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a small fraction get pollinated by tiny insects called midges. Dry spells, poor soil nutrients, and lack of natural pollinators cause unpollinated flowers to drop off naturally.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kplukai bibii pɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ lɛ pollin. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge, hulutsoo be, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii. kɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔfɔi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell when a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready to be picked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color distinctly depending on their variety—green pods turn bright yellow, while red or purple pods change to an orange-yellow color. Tapping a ripe pod also produces a hollow sound as the seeds loosen inside.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔtɔi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baatsake amɛhe su waa yɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ naa. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. yɛ be mli ni pods tsuji loo purple lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ otswa pod ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hu, ehaa gbɛɛmɔ ko ni mli ewo muji baa be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ mli lɛ.

english: How often am I supposed to harvest ripe pods from my cocoa trees during the main season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa cacao tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ be titri lɛ mli?

english: You should harvest ripe pods every 3 to 4 weeks during the peak season. Leaving ripe pods on the tree for too long causes seeds to germinate inside and invites diseases and pests to attack the pod.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ daa otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ fa babaoo lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli ni ebaafɔ̃ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nine koni amɛbatutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why is it important to ferment cocoa beans under banana leaves right after breaking the pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afee kookoo ŋmeii yɛ banana baai ashishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni atswa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Fermentation for 5 to 7 days removes the sticky white pulp, kills the seed germ, and develops the rich chocolate flavor and brown color inside the beans. Unfermented beans remain purple, taste bitter, and sell for a lower price.
ga: Kɛ́ afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ gbii 5 kɛyashi 7 lɛ, ebaajie ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni wa lɛ. Gbemɔ helai ni yɔɔ dumɔwui amli lɛ ni eha tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ kɛ su ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ aba. Beans ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ewo mli lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ purple, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ, ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛ jara ni baa shi.

english: Why are some of my cocoa pods turning dark brown or black and rotting on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, shaded conditions during heavy rains. Clearing weeds, pruning branches for better airflow, and removing affected pods early helps prevent it from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. weeding Tsei ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ gbɛfaŋnɔ naa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees dry out and burn during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot tolerate intense direct sunlight. Planting shade plants like plantains or shade trees alongside young cocoa protects them from heat stress and sun damage while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to cut off young shoots and extra branches growing out from the trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mikoo tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These extra shoots, called chupons, suck nutrients and water away from the main tree without producing many pods. Removing them allows the tree to focus its energy on flowering and swelling ripe cocoa pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ, shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ he ni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo baaa. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ agbala ejwɛŋmɔ kɛya fɔfɔi ni baa kɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ amli fũu lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my mature cocoa farm to stop producing as many pods as it used to in past years?
ga: Mɛni miitsi mi-kokoo ŋmɔ ni eda lɛ naa koni ekawo ŋmeii babaoo tamɔ bɔ ni efee yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Declining yields happen due to aging trees, nutrient depletion in the soil, heavy shade blocking sunlight, or hidden infections like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus. Pruning shade trees, applying fertilizer, and managing pests can restore pod yields.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa beni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shade ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa loo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, shade tsei ni afolɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ baanyɛ aha pod lɛ afee ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees need fertilizer to grow bigger and produce more pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi cacao tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ agbo ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: If your trees show pale yellow leaves, slow stem growth, small pods, or low yields, the soil is likely low in nutrients. Applying cocoa-recommended fertilizer at the start of the rains helps feed the roots and boost pod growth.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmeii ni daa blɛoo, ŋmeii bibii, loo yibiiwoo ni baa shi Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni Cocoa woɔ he ŋaa lɛ fata he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: If my cocoa pods show signs of disease, should I still harvest them or just leave them on the tree?
ga: Kɛji mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ jie hela he okadi kpo Ani esa akɛ maya nɔ makpa loo mashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: You should harvest diseased pods as soon as you spot them and remove them from the farm. Leaving sick pods on the tree allows fungal spores to spread through rain and wind to healthy pods and neighboring trees.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ pɛ kɛji ona amɛ ni ojie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛtsɔ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ kɛya ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Can I leave diseased cocoa pods on the ground after I harvest them?
ga: Yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ Ani manyɛ mashi kookoo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: No, leaving infected pods on the farm floor allows disease spores to survive in the soil. Rain splashing on the ground can carry those spores back up onto your healthy trees, so it is best to bury or safely destroy them away from your farm.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa helai ahe ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ aku sɛɛ kɛba otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofu amɛ loo okpãtã amɛhiɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ he ko ni kɛ oŋmɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: How does disease move so quickly from one crop to another in my field?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crop diseases usually spread through wind, rain splashes, insects moving between plants, or infected harvesting tools. Clearing infected plant parts early helps break this chain of transmission.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ koolooi ni nyiɛɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ nɔ. loo ŋmaakpamɔ nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ Tse lɛ fãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe ni aaafɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akumɔ nɛkɛ hela ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ nɛɛ mli.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce fruits twice in a single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ yibii shii enyɔ yɛ afi kome mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally follow weather patterns in Ghana, creating two harvest seasons: a major crop season brought on by the main rainy season, and a smaller mid-crop season following the minor rains.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ sɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa kpamɔ bei enyɔ baa: dumɔ be titri ni baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli. kɛ dumɔ be bibioo ni yɔɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ.

english: Why is it important to pile up cocoa pods after harvesting them before opening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ato kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni akpaa lɛ sɛɛ dani agbele lɛ?

english: Gathering pods into piles for a few days before breaking them allows the beans inside to ripen uniformly, which makes fermentation smoother and improves the quality and flavor of the cocoa.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni abua naa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii Gbii fioo komɛi dani akumɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aho jogbaŋŋ. ni haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ehaa kookoo lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ

english: Why do some flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without ever turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: It is normal for cocoa trees to shed flowers they cannot support. However, excessive flower drop can happen if the tree is stressed by dry weather, lacks soil nutrients, or is under attack by pests like capsids.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua. Shi kɛlɛ, fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ fe nine baanyɛ aba kɛji akɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids tutuaa lɛ

english: Is it safe to harvest my cocoa crops without applying any chemicals during the season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaakpa kookoo tsei ni akɛ tsofa ko tsuuu nii? Yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: You can harvest without chemicals, but unmanaged pests and diseases may greatly reduce how much you harvest. If you prefer not to use synthetic chemicals, good farm hygiene and proper pruning can help control losses.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa lɛ ni okɛ tsofai tsuuu nii. Shi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ aba shi waa. Kɛji akɛ osumɔɔɔ ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi tsuɔ nii. Okwaafoi amli hetsemɔ kpakpa kɛ tsei ni afoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ nibii ni laajeɔ lɛ.

english: My family has farmed this cocoa land the same way for forty years; why are my crop yields lower now?
ga: Miweku lɛ hu etsu kookoo he nii yɛ nakai gbɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ afii nyɔŋmai ejwɛ sɔŋŋ nɛ. Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni mitsuɔ lɛ miiba shi bianɛ lɛ?

english: Over decades, soil nutrients naturally wear out, and older cocoa trees lose their youthful strength. Updating your methods with soil fertilizers, modern pruning, and replacing very old trees can bring your yields back up.
ga: Afii nyɔŋmai abɔ nɛ ni shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ efite yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ laajeɔ amɛblahiiaŋ kɛ oblayeiaŋ. Ogbɛi ni Otsɔɔ nɔ Otsuɔ Nii Kɛtsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ Nɔ Nibii ni Okɛwoɔ Mli lɛ Nɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi Kɛ tsei ni egbɔ ni oootsake lɛ baanyɛ aha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What happens if I let my cocoa tree grow very tall without trimming the top branches?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji miha kookoo tso lɛ da waa ni mifolɔko ŋwɛi niji lɛ?

english: When a cocoa tree grows too tall, it spends most of its energy feeding leaves and wood instead of making pods. Tall trees are also harder to harvest and spray, making disease control difficult.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ da tsɔ lɛ, Cocoa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo yeɔ baai kɛ tsei moŋ fe ni amɛaama ŋmɔji. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ hu wa akɛ abaakpãtã ni akɛ tsofa afɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa helai anɔyeli feɔ nɔ ni wa.

english: How do I know the right time to spray my farm to protect my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ koni mikɛbu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Chemical spraying should match the life cycle of pests like capsids and the arrival of the rainy season when fungal diseases thrive. Following a seasonal calendar recommended by an extension officer ensures you spray at the most effective time.
ga: Esa akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ wala shihilɛ, tamɔ capsid kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa beni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ akpã gbee. Kɛji onyiɛ be mli kalanda ni o-extension staff lɛ wo he ŋaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔse yɛ be ni hi fe fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods keep over-ripening on the tree if I leave them for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ shwereɔ fe nine yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods continue to mature rapidly once ripe. If you do not visit your farm regularly to pay attention to them, the pods will quickly become over-ripe, which can damage the beans inside.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛdaraa oya kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ. Kɛji oyaaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa koni okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama nɔ. Pods lɛ shwereɔ oya fe nine. Enɛ baanyɛ afite kɔfe yibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What happens if I delay harvesting my ripe cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Delaying your harvest leads to over-ripened pods. When left unattended on the tree, the beans inside will not remain in good condition and can easily spoil.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ ashwere fe nine. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ shihilɛ kpakpa mli ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm needs more of my attention during the harvest season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ehe miihia ni akwɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: When you walk through your farm and see over-ripened cocoa pods or find beans that are not well-formed inside, it is a clear sign your trees need closer care and timely harvesting.
ga: Kɛ́ otsɔ ŋmɔ ko he ni ona kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine loo dumɔwui ni ehiii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. No ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni akwɛ otsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akpa amɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What causes the beans inside my cocoa pods to be poorly formed?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee nɔ ni ehiii lɛ?

english: If cocoa trees do not receive regular attention and proper care, the crop exerts its strength unevenly, leading to pods with beans inside that fail to form fully or correctly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɛɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Crops bɛ hewalɛ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni dumɔwui yɔɔ mli lɛ efeee kwraa loo efeee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are some of the cocoa beans inside my ripe pods small or flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ amli lɛ ekomɛi ji bibii loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Beans fail to develop properly when the tree is neglected during pod growth. Proper farm attention ensures the tree has what it needs to form full, healthy beans.
ga: Peas nyɛŋ adara jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ aku hiɛ ashwie tso lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni pod lɛ miida lɛ. Okwaafoi akwɛmɔ ni sa haa tsei lɛ naa nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does spending time caring for my farm improve my cocoa beans?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ be ni mikɛbaakwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mikookoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Regular care keeps the trees healthy so that when pods ripen, the beans inside develop into well-formed seeds instead of spoiling or forming poorly.
ga: Tso lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ daa yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. koni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ shwere lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ atsɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefite loo ehiɛ bɛ shihilɛ kpakpa mli lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees need to draw water from the soil when the pods are already ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ buaa nu naa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees pull moisture up from the ground into the ripe pods to keep the inside of the fruit healthy and protect the beans from drying out or spoiling.
ga: Cacao tso lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli koni eha aduawai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebu kɔfe ŋmɔtɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi loo amɛkafite.

english: How can I keep the inside of my ripe cocoa pods from spoiling before I pick them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha kookoo ŋmeii ni egbɔ lɛ amli akafite dani mikɛto?

english: The cocoa tree prevents pod spoilage by drawing water up from the soil into the ripe fruit, which preserves the moisture and quality of the beans inside.
ga: Cacao tsei tsiɔ pod lɛ fitemɔ naa kɛtsɔ nu ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does soil water matter for cocoa pods that are already fully ripe?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ nɔ nu he hiaa koni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ adara kwraa?

english: Yes, even when cocoa is ripe, the tree relies on soil moisture to supply water to the pods, ensuring the internal beans stay protected until harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ kookoo lɛ egbɔ momo moŋ. Tsei lɛ hu damɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛ nu aha amɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ haa abuɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be mli.

english: What does it mean when someone says an unattended cocoa tree exerts its strength?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni mɔ ko kɛɛ akɛ cacao tso lɛ tsuɔ nii waa ni mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ he lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: When a cocoa tree does not get regular care, it grows without proper direction, using up its energy in ways that lead to over-ripened pods and improperly formed beans.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ kookoo tsei anɔ daa lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni gbɛtsɔɔmɔ kpakpa bɛ he. Akɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ fe nine ni amɛnáa dumɔwui lɛ ahe mfoniri ni esaaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I remove all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need protection from strong sunlight because direct heat burns their leaves and dries out soil moisture. Keeping larger shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantains creates a cool shelter that helps young cocoa survive until it matures.
ga: Esa akɛ abu kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ haa jɛmɛ feɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb on tall wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha ekpã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need sunlight on every leaf to manufacture food for growing tubers underground. Staking lifts leaves off damp soil, reducing disease risk and allowing maximum sunlight exposure so tubers grow bigger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la kɛjɛɔ baa fɛɛ baa mli koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ helai ni baanyɛ aba lɛ shi ni oha hulu la babaoo bɔ ni ooonyɛ koni bulbs wuji lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I place seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting maize with proper spacing ensures every stem receives enough food and air to produce big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dense plants lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha toi lɛ adara.

english: Why are the leaves of my green maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso ni ji eŋɔli lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant nutrient needed for green growth. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea helps leaves turn green again and boosts yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize crops heavy-feed on soil nutrients, leaving the earth weak. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my corn leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ yɛ bu ko ni akɛtee ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: These holes are caused by pests such as the fall armyworm, which attack the growing tips of young maize. Applying recommended control measures early directly into the funnel destroys the caterpillars before they ruin the whole yield.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. ni tutuaa ŋmãa bibii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ he nii mra lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Kɛboteɔ tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baafite ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that transmit leaf-curl viruses while feeding. Spraying neem oil solution controls these insects and helps young leaves open up normally.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites lɛ kɛ chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni kɛ leaf curl virus lɛ baa beni eyeɔ niyenii lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni eye ebua baa bibii lɛ ni amɛgbele amɛhe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do small black insects make powder out of my harvested maize after a few months in the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ tsɔ powda kɛjɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi shwapo lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: These insects are grain weevils that lay eggs inside dried maize kernels to feed on them during storage. Drying maize thoroughly and storing grain in airtight hermetic bags suffocates the insects naturally without chemicals.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji dumɔwui amli kooloi ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ni egbi mli koni amɛye be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmãa lɛ to kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because roots need oxygen to breathe, and excess stagnant water attracts harmful rot bacteria. Planting cassava on raised earth ridges or mounds helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛmu. Ni nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ gbalaa helai ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do the bright yellow flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee tomatoi lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes rapidly between wet and dry. Mulching the soil keeps ground moisture stable and cool, helping flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ. Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ehaa edɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What is the difference between cereal crops like maize and legume crops like beans?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa teŋ?

english: Cereals like maize are grass-type plants that produce starchy seeds and consume lots of soil nutrients, while legumes like beans produce seeds in pods and actually fix nitrogen back into the soil to feed themselves and other plants.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli tamɔ ŋmãa ji jwɛi ni woɔ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ ni eyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii woɔ dumɔwui yɛ ŋmeii amli ni amɛsaa nitrogen lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni amɛkɛkwɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛ tsei krokomɛi anɔ.

english: People keep using the words 'grains' and 'cereals' when talking about maize—are these two different things?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mɛi kɛ wiemɔi ni ji ‘ŋmãa’ kɛ ‘ŋmãa’ tsuɔ nii kɛ́ amɛmiiwie ŋmãa he. Ani esoro nibii enyɔ nɛɛ?

english: They refer to the same crop in everyday farming: 'cereal' describes the grass plant itself, while 'grain' refers to the hard, dry seed that you harvest from the plant for food.
ga: Amɛtsɔɔ tsei ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ daa gbi okwaayeli mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. ‘Cereal’ tsɔɔ jwɛi tsei, yɛ be mli ni ‘ŋmãa’ tsɔɔ dumɔwui ni wa ni egbi ni okpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei amli kɛyeɔ niyenii.

english: Why do my maize crops leave the soil feeling tired after harvest, but groundnuts do not?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ etɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ? Shi Peanut nuuu he akɛ etɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes up heavy amounts of nitrogen and food from the soil to grow its tall stalks and cobs, whereas groundnuts are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, leaving the soil richer.
ga: Abɛi kɛ nitrogen kɛ niyenii babaoo ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Shi ŋmei lɛ, ŋmei ji ŋmei ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo

english: Why do agricultural officers always tell me to plant beans or groundnuts in the same field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Alternating maize with legumes cleans and restores the soil because legumes return the vital nitrogen nutrients that the heavy-feeding maize crop pulled out during the previous season.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha ehe awa ekoŋŋ. Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ kuɔ nitrogen niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa ŋmãa ni ajie yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How does growing legumes alongside my main grain crops help my farmland over time?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli?

english: Legumes act as living natural fertilizer makers by adding nitrogen to the soil, while their leaves fall off and turn into organic matter that holds moisture in the ground for future grain crops.
ga: Legumes tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɛ ka kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Beni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell if my maize crops are starving for food in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi-ŋma lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When maize lacks proper nutrition like nitrogen, the lower leaves start turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips backward, and the whole stalk remains thin and weak instead of growing dark green and sturdy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni sa, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa sɛɛ. Ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kã he efee mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ e hɛ mi nyami nɛ e he wa.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs with missing kernels when there is a dry spell during flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ dumɔwui ni elaaje yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Flowering is the most sensitive stage for maize; dry weather dries out the sticky silk threads on the cob, preventing pollen from fertilizing the kernels and leaving empty spaces on the cob.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔmɔ ji be ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmãa. Shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa siliki ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ mli gbiɔ, ni no haaa pollen lɛ akawo ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli ni ehaa he ko bɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it so important to clear weeds from my young maize field early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa waa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-baby corn ŋmɔji lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ?

english: Young maize grows slowly in its first few weeks, so weeds will quickly steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for the young plants, causing permanent stunting if not removed early.
ga: Abɛi bibii lɛ daa blɛoo. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛhaa tsei bibii. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela baa shi daa kɛji ajieee lɛ mra.

english: Why do pests and diseases attack my field more heavily when I plant only maize on the same land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa he ni miyɔɔ lɛ beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop year after year builds up a permanent home and continuous food supply for specific pests and diseases in your soil, allowing their numbers to multiply rapidly.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ooodu afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa shia ni hiɔ shi daa kɛ niyenii ni yaa nɔ ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai komɛi ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. ni no haa amɛyibɔ ​​yaa hiɛ oyayaayai

english: How do I know the exact right time that my maize grains are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer husks dry up and turn paper-brown, the stalks lose their green color, and a small black spot forms at the base of the kernel where it attaches to the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ egbi ni etsɔ wolo ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. Tso lɛ yitso lɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ dumɔwu ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ shishi.

english: Cassava cuttings should ideally be planted about one meter apart from each other. If you plant them too close, their leaves will shade each other and their roots will fight for nutrients, leading to smaller roots at harvest time.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afo lɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ odu amɛ kɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Amɛbaai lɛ baaha amɛhe. ni eshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ baafee bibii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Which part of the cassava stem is best for me to cut and plant?
ga: Kasava tso lɛ fã ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafolɔ ni madu?

english: The strong, mature middle section of a healthy stem is best for planting. The top stem is too soft and dries out quickly, while the lower stem near the ground is often too woody and sprouts slowly.
ga: Tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha dumɔ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ tsɔ ni egbiɔ oya. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ shishigbɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ tsei tsɔ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo.

english: How do I know that my cassava is ready to be uprooted?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvesting when the leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off, leaving only a few leaves at the top of the stem, or when the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Baai fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Aloo beni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting in the ground before I uproot them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mijie amɛ lɛ?

english: Tuber rot is usually caused by excess water sitting in the soil, which prevents the roots from breathing and encourages fungal growth. Planting on ridges or mounds helps drain away heavy rainwater.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine ni buaa ehe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tuber rot baa. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo gɔji anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ.

english: Is it okay for me to cut off the cassava leaves weeks before uprooting the roots?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ afolɔ ŋmei baai otsii babaoo dani atswa amɛshishifãi?

english: Cutting off the leaves early stops the plant from making food, which can cause the tubers underground to lose quality or start rotting. It is best to keep the leaves intact until you are ready to harvest.
ga: Baai ni afoɔ mra Ebaaha tsei lɛ akafee niyenii. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii loo amɛje shishi amɛgboi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohiɛ baai lɛ amli kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaakpa amɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops curl up during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon is a crop's natural defense against heat. The plant rolls its leaves to reduce leaf surface area and prevent water loss through evaporation.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ hebuu kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha baa lɛ nɔ he lɛ aba shi ni amɛtsi nu ni shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young crops turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil or poor root growth due to overly wet ground. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer can help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when there are lots of weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo be mli ni jwɛi babaoo ebɔle he lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively steal nutrients, sunlight, and soil moisture. Clearing weeds early gives your crops the space and food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant legumes like groundnuts together with my cassava on the same plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava with legumes like groundnuts benefits the soil because groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground, naturally feeding your cassava.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha o-cassava lɛ

english: What causes tiny holes in the leaves of my crops, and how does it hurt the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi tso lɛ baai anɔ Ni te eyeɔ tsei awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Holes in leaves are caused by chewing insects like beetles or caterpillars. When leaves are damaged, the plant cannot produce enough food to grow strong stems and large tubers or grains.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ koolooi ni yeɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Kɛji baai lɛ fite lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii ni he wa lɛ adalɛ. kɛ bulb loo dumɔwui wuji

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key soil nutrient. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away nutrients or when excess water stays trapped around the root system for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛtee loo kɛ́ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do some of my yam tubers grow long and thin while others grow big and fat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ekomɛi kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu dara ni amɛhe ejɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose soil mounds to expand easily. If the soil underneath is hard or packed with stones, the roots struggle to swell sideways, resulting in thin, misshapen yams instead of thick, heavy ones.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia gɔŋ ko ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni shwieɔ shi koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli wa loo eyɛ tɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfu kɛya afã. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa ni tsii najiaŋ

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my cassava cuttings after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei be mli ŋmei?

english: You should plant your cassava stem cuttings right after the first two or three heavy rains have thoroughly soaked the soil. This ensures the soil holds enough moisture long enough for the stems to sprout fresh roots without drying out in a sudden hot spell.
ga: Esa akɛ odu o-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ fioo ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi heei akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ yɛ latsaa be mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my vegetable crops curl up tightly during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense trick plants use to save water. By rolling up their leaves, the plant exposes less surface area to the hot sun, preventing water from evaporating out of them too quickly.
ga: Baai akumɔ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu ŋaa ni tsei kɛbuɔ nu he. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɛɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree before I can pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ mafolɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads fast in cool, damp, shaded conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning extra cocoa branches lets air and sunlight flow through, which keeps the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kookoo tsei lɛ ahe jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: What makes armyworms show up on my farm so fast and eat up all the young maize shoots?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii baa miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Armyworm moths fly in and lay hundreds of eggs on young leaves overnight, especially when a dry period is followed by light rain. When all the eggs hatch at once, thousands of caterpillars emerge together to feed on tender green shoots.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fãa kɛboteɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ baai bibii anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ fioo. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be. Kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ shwie amɛhe lɛ, ŋmeii akpei abɔ buaa amɛhe naa koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes rapidly from dry to wet. Excessive heat damages the flower pollen, so the plant drops the blossoms to conserve its strength.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya kɛjɛ he ni egbi kɛtee he ni edɔ. Dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ fiteɔ pollen lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why does my pepper plant keep growing lots of leaves but refuses to give me pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi ehaaa mi pepper yibii lɛ?

english: Giving pepper plants too much leaf-growing fertilizer (like high nitrogen) causes them to spend all their energy making tall, bushy stems instead of flowers. Balanced fertilizer encourages the plant to shift from leaf growth to fruiting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ wo baai lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii fe nine (tamɔ nitrogen ni fa babaoo) lɛ, ebaaha pepper tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ fɔfɔii najiaŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ adalɛ mli kɛyaa yibiiwoo mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my plantain suckers close together to get more bunches from my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ plantain tsei lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná ŋmeii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting plantains too close forces them to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and plant food. Spacing them properly ensures each stem receives enough sunlight and nutrients to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei niyenii ahe yɛ amɛteŋ. Kɛ́ akɛto tso lɛ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Can I save seeds from the maize I harvest this season to plant again next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni mikpaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: If you planted commercial hybrid maize, saving those seeds will lead to weaker plants and much lower yields next season. Buying fresh certified seed each season ensures every plant grows uniform, strong, and productive.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmãa ni akɛfee jarayeli ŋmãa lɛ Nakai dumɔwui lɛ ni oookɛto lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa aba yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa pɛpɛɛpɛ, hewalɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually show that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which feeds green leafy growth. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient deep into the soil where roots cannot reach it, or waterlogged soil can stop roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ, ni no haa niyenii kɛhaa baa eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Aloo sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu.

english: How do I know when my cassava stems under the ground are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava plants show signs above ground when tubers are mature, such as the bottom leaves turning yellow and dropping off. You can also gently dig away soil around the base of the plant to check if the root tubers have grown thick enough.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ baajie okadii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akpo beni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ, tamɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ hu atsu nii blɛoo koni ona kɛji shishifãi lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch as much sunlight as possible, which the plant uses to make food and grow big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Akɛ tsei lɛ hoɔ nii ni amɛduɔ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of beneficial insects to pollinate the blossoms. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps plants hold onto their flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔii lɛ amli kɛyashi yibii lɛ baawo.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and wrinkling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves. Spraying plants with a mild neem oil mixture or soapy water can control these insects and stop the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni mli ejɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye kooloi nɛɛ anɔ ni ekpa ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp but not flooded, ideally right after a light rain or when mild showers are expected. Avoid putting down fertilizer right before a heavy downpour, which can sweep nutrients off the topsoil.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛ fioo loo be mli ni akpaa nugbɔ fioo ko gbɛ lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he dani nugbɔ anɛ waa. Enɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Planting seeds too close together makes crops fight with each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Giving each plant proper space ensures every stalk gets enough food to build strong stems and full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ fɛɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha efee tso lɛ shishifã ni wa kɛ ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense to protect itself from losing water in intense heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the leaf surface area exposed to direct sun and retains moisture until the air cools down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni elaajeɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa tso lɛ baa shi yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: Weeds grow fast and steal soil nutrients, water, and space away from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the season makes sure all the fertilizer and rainwater go straight into feeding your main plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nu kɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ fɛɛ yaa onibii titrii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and burning during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct sunlight because their foliage is soft and sensitive. They need shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to shield their leaves from intense heat while their root systems develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small shoots to grow around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii shwereɔ yɛ midumɔwui titrii lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around a plantain tree, they compete with the mother plant for nutrients and water in the soil. Pruning extra suckers and keeping only one or two strong ones ensures larger and healthier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu ko he lɛ, amɛkɛ tso nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei krokomɛi ahe ni okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaha plantains lɛ afee wuji ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom of a maize stalk usually indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil, which is the main nutrient maize plants need to build strong leaves and stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa tsei koni amɛma baai kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves with little worms hiding inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Ani okɛ ohe ewo baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that feeds on young maize leaves and burrows into the center funnel of the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni efoɔ bu kɛyaa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why does swamp rice survive standing in flooded water while my maize crops die if flooded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔŋ ŋmãa hiɔ shi yɛ nu ni eyi obɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ kɛji nu afua ba enɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special air channels inside their stems and roots that carry oxygen down from above the water level, allowing their roots to breathe underwater while drowning out competing weeds.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsui krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shi kɛjɛɔ nu lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ yɛ nu shishi yɛ be mli ni amɛmiimɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when heavy rains fall for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil. When water settles around the roots for extended periods, air cannot reach them, creating conditions that cause fungal and bacterial rots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu ŋmɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni baanyɛ aha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ aba.

english: Why do I need to set up long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kakadaji ahe hiaa mi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines are naturally climbing plants. Supporting them with stakes lifts their leaves into direct sunlight, which gives the plant the energy it needs to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni shwereɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋtayaai fi amɛsɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start turning dark and spoiling just two or three days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ bɔi duŋ ni amɛgboi beni atsa amɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, cassava roots quickly react with oxygen and undergo natural decay because their skin is damaged during harvesting. This is why cassava must be consumed or processed into products like gari shortly after harvest.
ga: Kɛji akpa Cassava shishifãi lɛ kɛ oxygen tsuɔ nii oya ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe akɛni hewolo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni esa akɛ aye ŋmei loo afee lɛ nibii tamɔ gari beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses that distort normal plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni shwieɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when temperatures become too high or when soil moisture is inconsistent. Extreme heat stresses the plant and prevents flowers from successfully pollinating to produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee nɔ ni yeɔ omanye koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my rice plants turn yellow when water stays on the field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When standing water is too deep or stagnant, the roots cannot breathe and struggle to take up essential nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ nu lɛ mli kwɔ tsɔ loo ekã shi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do seeds I buy from the official Agric office produce better yields than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa tsutsu lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds from the Agric office are specially bred and processed for high purity, strong germination, disease resistance, and high yield potential, whereas saved seed quality degrades over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni Agric Agency ewo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsuɔ he nii koni ehe tse waa. Ekwɛ̃mɔ ni mli wa, helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahe hilɛ baa shi yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants roll up tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot afternoons as a self-defense mechanism to reduce surface area, preventing excessive water loss through evaporation until temperatures cool down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ shi. Tsi nu ni fiteɔ fe nine kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do Armyworms destroy my maize crop so much faster than other caterpillars?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Armyworms miifite mi ŋmãa oya fe ŋmeii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Fall Armyworms feed aggressively inside the growing funnel of the plant, eating the tender new leaves before they can open and multiplying rapidly in hot weather.
ga: Fall Armyworms yeɔ nii waa yɛ tsei ni daraa lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ dani amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwereɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil or planting stem cuttings incorrectly makes the cassava plant spend all its energy growing leafy branches above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ji niji ni daa lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmei baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high or when soil moisture fluctuates sharply, preventing successful pollination and fruit formation.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya. Etsiɔ pollination kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ naa.

english: Why is it important for me to plant plantains on the same field with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu banana yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight; plantains grow fast and provide large leaves that shade the young cocoa plants and keep the soil moist during dry periods.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my field of rice is completely ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa?

english: Rice is ready for harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the seed heads turn a golden-yellow color and the grains are firm and hard when bitten.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 batsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ akɔmɔ amɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants dry up and burn after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Applying too much chemical fertilizer at once creates excess salt around the roots, which pulls moisture out of the plant instead of feeding it, causing the leaves to scorch.
ga: Tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ haa ŋmei babaoo baa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ he moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops grow thin and weak during the first month after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: In the early weeks, crop roots are small, and fast-growing weeds steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your crop needs to build a thick stem.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ Tso shishifãi lɛ daraaa. Ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves and weak root systems that cannot withstand harsh sun. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside them creates a canopy that protects the cocoa from sunburn and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ emasɛi. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must be planted with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the plant wastes energy trying to redirect its growth, leading to weak stems and poor root yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛyitso lɛ Tsei lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsake gbɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni shishifãi lɛ hu efeee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it necessary to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves toward the sunlight so the plant can make more food to grow large tubers underground. It also keeps leaves off the hot, wet soil, which prevents rot and fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii babaoo ni ekɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ebuɔ baai lɛ hu ahe kɛjɛɔ sũ ni mli edɔ ni efɔ lɛ he. Nɔ ni tsiɔ baa ni fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape along the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips in a V-shape indicate that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. Applying compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant regain its green color and form larger corn ears.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ V lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-ŋmãa lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji ŋmɔji lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni da.

english: How does growing groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my main crops improve the soil?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in tiny nodules on their roots. When these roots decompose, they release natural fertilizer into the soil, feeding nearby crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes into the young leaves inside my maize funnels?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-corn cones lɛ amli lɛ amli?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by moths inside the plant's leaves. Controlling them early with appropriate biopesticides or recommended treatments prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the maize.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ tsei ahe baai lɛ amli lɛ amli. Amɛ nɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo tsofafeemɔi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmãa ni miida lɛ yitsei lɛ.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the developing fruit. It usually happens when watering is uneven; maintaining consistent moisture in the soil helps the plant absorb calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering soil with dry organic matter is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that traps moisture in the dirt, suppresses weed growth, and keeps plant roots cool during dry, hot weather.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ latsaa be mli lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without turning into pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by intense heat, drought, or soil that is too dry. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the plant hold onto its blossoms so they turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ, loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do weeds sprout and spread so much faster than my planted food crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly absorb rainwater and plant food from the soil before cultivated crops can. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get the light, water, and nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nugbɔ nu oya ni amɛdu niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nakai. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa tsei lɛ náa la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is like food for leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the root area.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni tamɔ niyenii kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing very bushy leaves but taking so long to produce flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi ekɛ be babaoo fɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen, the cowpea plant spends all its energy producing green leaves instead of triggering flower and pod production.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ Cowpea tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekanya fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground when the rainy season is too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when soil stays waterlogged for too long because roots need air to stay healthy. Excess water suffocates the roots and allows fungal diseases to attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii helai tutuaa amɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting shoots even while stored in a dry barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ akɛto ŋmɔ ko ni egbi mli po lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break their rest period after a few months as part of their growth cycle, using the food stored inside the tuber to sprout new shoots for the next season.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafo amɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ akɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ fã. Akɛ niyenii ni ato yɛ bulb lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii heei kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many small flowers without them turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? yɛ babaoo mli ni etsɔko kookoo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands more flowers than they can support. Dropping excess flowers helps the tree save water and nutrients to grow healthy pods from the flowers that stay.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ fe bɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baajɛ fɔfɔi ni eshwɛ lɛ amli lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and turn brown from the bottom leaves upwards before fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: This pattern often indicates a leaf fungal disease or root damage, which restricts the plant's ability to pull up water and nutrients from the soil to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ tsɔɔ baa lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ hela loo shishifãi ni efite. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ anyɛ agbala nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛya baai lɛ amli.

english: Why are my tomato plants flowering well, but the flowers keep falling off without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato?

english: Extreme daytime heat or warm nights can damage tomato pollen, causing the flowers to drop off instead of setting fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi mli loo gbɛkɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe tomato mli ŋmeii. Ehaa fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi yɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ najiaŋ

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids hiding under the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies.
