ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my okra pods become tough and hard to chew so quickly after forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ mli wa ni ewa akɛ oooye beni afee lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Okra pods grow very rapidly. If they are not harvested within 3 to 5 days after flowering, the plant builds hard fiber inside the pod to protect the developing seeds.
ga: Okra ŋmeii lɛ daa oya waa. Kɛji akɛ akpaaa yɛ gbii 3 kɛyashi 5 mli yɛ fɔfɔii ni ewo lɛ sɛɛ. Tso lɛ feɔ tsɔji ni wa yɛ tso lɛ mli koni ebu dumɔwui ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why do some of my harvested groundnut pods turn out completely empty inside with no nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi efee efolo ni ŋmeii ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts need calcium in the topsoil while the underground pods expand. Without enough calcium, the outer shell forms but the seeds inside fail to grow.
ga: Calcium he miihia ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ. Kɛji calcium faaa lɛ, kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ko baafee. Shi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How do I extract the active strength out of plant leaves to make a natural crop spray?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie hewalɛ ni tsuɔ nii lɛ kɛjɛ tsei ahe baai amli koni mafee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: You extract the useful essence by finely crushing or chopping fresh leaves, soaking them in water for 12 to 24 hours, and then straining out the plant pieces so only the liquid extract remains.
ga: Ojieɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ baai heei lɛ ni oootsi loo ooofo mli bibii lɛ nɔ. Okɛwo nu mli ŋmɛlɛtswai 12 kɛyashi 24, no sɛɛ lɛ, shwiemɔ tso lɛ mli fãi lɛ koni nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ pɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does my homemade leaf spray seem weaker at fighting pests than store-bought chemical sprays?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ tsei ahe ni mifeɔ yɛ shia lɛ bɛ hewalɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tawuu mli fe tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Fresh plant leaves naturally have a lower concentration of active ingredients than factory chemical sprays. Because this leaf potency is mild, you need to use a larger quantity of leaves per liter of water to make an effective spray.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsei ahe baai heei lɛ amli nibii ni tsuɔ nii lɛ faaa fe tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ kɛjɛɔ nitsumɔhei lɛ. Akɛni baai lɛ ahe nitsumɔ waaa hewɔ lɛ No hewɔ lɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ baai babaoo atsu nii yɛ nu lita kome mli kɛha tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the correct amount of natural liquid extract to mix per liter of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male adebɔɔ mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ falɛ ni sa ni esa akɛ afutu nu lita kome mli?

english: Measuring the right amount per liter ensures the spray is strong enough to work without harming the crop. Extension officers recommend specific leaf-to-water ratios so you achieve the correct strength every time you mix.
ga: Lita kome susumɔ ni sa lɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ nitsumɔ ni eyeee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui. Mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ esa akɛ okɛ baai lɛ awo nu mli bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni oná nɔ ni sa be fɛɛ be ni okɛbaafutu mli.

english: Should I spray my crops with liquid plant extracts every single day?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tso mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ daa gbi?

english: No, crops should not be sprayed daily. Over-spraying can stress the plant, clog leaf pores, or cause chemical burns; most crops only need liquid sprays applied once every week or two.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ ashwieɔ tsei anɔ tsofa daa gbi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai fɔ̃ nɔ fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ aná haomɔ, ebaatsi baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ anaa, loo ekɛ tsofai ashã. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tsei babaoo anɔ lɛ he miihia shikome loo daa otsii enyɔ pɛ.

english: How many times can I reapply natural crop treatments during a single growing season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ mikɛ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be kome mli?

english: You can reapply treatments every 7 to 14 days throughout the season as needed. Regular reapplication protects new leaves that have grown since your last spray and replaces spray washed off by rain.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ daa gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ bɔ ni he hiaa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ wo mli ekoŋŋ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai heei ni eba kɛjɛ be mli ni akɛ naagbee tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ ahe. ni ekɛ spray ni nugbɔ shwieɔ lɛ yeɔ najiaŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn brown or scorch after I spray them with liquid mixtures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo shãa beni mikɛ nu ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ eshwie nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf scorch usually happens when the mixture is too strong or when you spray during the hot midday sun. Diluting the spray with more water per liter and applying it early in the morning or late evening prevents leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashãa baa kɛji akɛ nɔ ni akɛfutu lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ okɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shwie nɔ. Okɛ nu babaoo awo spray lɛ mli yɛ lita kome mli. Ni okɛwo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ koni ekafite baai lɛ.

english: Does rain wash away the liquid pest treatments I apply to my crop leaves?
ga: Ani nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, heavy rain easily washes natural leaf sprays off the crop surface. If it rains shortly after you spray, you will need to reapply the solution once the plant leaves are dry again.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baanyɛ afɔ adebɔɔ mli baai ni shwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ oya. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ tsofa ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ Ehe baahia ni okɛ tsofa lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ beni tso lɛ baai lɛ egbi ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: Can I store leftover leaf extract spray to use next week, or will it spoil?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tso ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli ni eshwɛ lɛ ato koni mikɛtsu nii otsi ni baa lɛ? Aloo ebaakumɔ?

english: Natural leaf extracts lose their potency quickly after being mixed with water because the organic ingredients break down. It is best to prepare fresh extracts and use them within 24 to 48 hours.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi oya kɛji akɛ akɛ nu efutu mli beni nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofee tsofa hee ni okɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli.

english: How do crop leaves absorb nutrients and medicine when I spray them directly?
ga: Te tso lɛ baai lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ tsofa kɛji mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Plant leaves have tiny microscopic pores called stomata that open during cool hours. When you spray liquid on the leaves, the crop absorbs the nutrients directly into its system much faster than through the roots.
ga: Tso baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni atsɛɔ lɛ stomata ni baagbele yɛ gbɛkɛ mli Kɛ́ okɛ nu lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya kwraa kɛyaa gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ fe bɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray liquid extracts on my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ afɔ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ?

english: The best times are early morning or late afternoon when temperatures are cooler. This prevents the spray from evaporating too quickly and stops the sun from burning the damp leaves.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ. Enɛ baatsi tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ, ni ebaaha hulu la akashã baai ni efɔ lɛ.

english: How can I know if the plantains from my farm are good enough to be exported to other countries?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ plantains ni jɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akɛya maji krokomɛi anɔ?

english: Foreign buyers look for clean, undamaged, fully green plantains of uniform size without spots, pest damage, or disease marks. Proper harvesting techniques and gentle handling prevent bruising, ensuring your crop meets international export standards.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ plantains eŋɔli ni he tse, ni efiteee, ni amɛdalɛ tamɔ nɔ kome ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he, nɔ ko bɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai efite, loo nɔ ko bɛ he. Gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpaa nibii kɛ bɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii blɛoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ majimaji ateŋ nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it better to harvest my plantains while they are still green or wait until they turn yellow if I want to sell to distant markets?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaakpa plantains be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ? Aloo mɛ kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji miisumɔ ni mahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: You should harvest plantains while they are mature but still completely green. Green plantains last much longer during long-distance transportation without spoiling, giving buyers time to ship and sell them fresh.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa plantains be mli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ shi amɛ fɛɛ amɛji ŋmɔji lolo lɛ. Plantains eŋɔlii lɛ hiɔ shi be babaoo yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he ko shɔŋŋ ni efiteee. Enɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛbaahã ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: What causes my harvested plantains to rot quickly, and how can I make them last longer?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Plantains spoil quickly when exposed to direct heat, rough handling, or bruising during harvest. Storing harvested bunches in cool, shaded, well-ventilated areas and avoiding stacking them too deep prevents heat buildup and rotting.
ga: Plantains baafite oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli. nitsumɔ ni mli wa loo fãji komɛi ba yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ amɛhe ni oooto he tsɔ lɛ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo kɛ fitemɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do buyers offer me very low prices for my plantains during certain months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ mi plantains lɛ haa yɛ jara ni baa shi nɛkɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Prices drop when many farmers in your region harvest at the exact same time, creating a surplus in the market. When supply is higher than what buyers need, prices go down according to market demand.
ga: Jara lɛ baa shi kɛ́ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ kpa nii yɛ be kome mli. ni kɛ nibii ni fa fe nine baa jara nɔ Beni nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ fa fe nɔ ni hɔlɔ lɛ taoɔ lɛ. Jara lɛ baa shi yɛ bɔ ni jara lɛ taoɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do plantain prices keep changing in the market instead of staying at one stable price?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains jara ni akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeehi jara kome ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain prices fluctuate based on supply and demand, transportation costs, and seasonal availability. When demand from major cities or exporters is high but supply is low, buyers pay higher prices to secure the crop.
ga: Plantain jara tsakeɔ yɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa kɛ nɔ ni ataoɔ, shika ni akɛmajeɔ, kɛ be mli ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Beni nibii ni ataoɔ kɛjɛɔ maji wuji loo mɛi ni kɛ nibii majeɔ maŋsɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ fa shi nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ faaa. Esa akɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ awo nyɔmɔ babaoo koni amɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: How can I adjust my planting schedule so I harvest my plantains when market prices are high?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsake be ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ koni manyɛ makpa plantains be mli ni jara wa waa lɛ?

english: By staggering your planting times rather than planting everything at once, you can harvest during the off-season or dry periods when fewer plantains are available in the market, allowing you to demand better prices.
ga: Kɛtsɔ be ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ mlijaa nɔ moŋ fe ni ooodu nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okpa amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ loo be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ. Na bo jara ni hi fe no

english: How can I make my plantain trees produce larger bunches so I can earn more profit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi plantain ŋmɔji lɛ adara bɔni afee ni maná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo?

english: To grow larger bunches, clear weeds regularly, apply rich organic manure or fertilizer, and prune away excess shoots so that the main plant gets all the water and soil nutrients it needs.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni okwɛ jwɛi babaoo lɛ Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ daa. Kɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa atsu nii. Ni ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ana nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ mli.

english: How long does a plantain tree take from the day I plant it until the bunch is ready to harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani plantain lɛ daa kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshɛɔ be mli ni eshɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ he?

english: A plantain tree usually takes between 11 to 15 months to produce a harvestable bunch, depending on the soil fertility, rainfall, and plant variety you choose.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ heɔ nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 15 dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni abaanyɛ akpa. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ tso henɔi ni ohalaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain tree turning yellow and dry before the fruit is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛyibii lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can be caused by a lack of nutrients like nitrogen, prolonged dry weather, or plant diseases like Panama disease. Applying compost and keeping the soil moist helps maintain healthy green leaves.
ga: Niyenii tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ, loo tsei ahe helai tamɔ Panama hela lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How many suckers should I leave around my main plantain tree for the best yield?
ga: Esa akɛ mashi tsei bibii enyiɛ mabɔle dumɔwu titri lɛ he koni ewo yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: You should prune excess shoots and leave only 2 to 3 strong suckers of different ages around the parent tree. Leaving too many suckers causes competition for nutrients, resulting in small, lightweight bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi tsei ni hiɛ hewalɛ 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ ni eye afii srɔtoi yɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ekɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni tsiimɔ waaa lɛ baa.

english: Why should I leave big trees on my farmland instead of cutting them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Trees protect your crops from harsh heat, hold water in the ground during dry periods, and their fallen leaves rot to create natural manure that feeds your crops.
ga: Tsei buɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Ekɛ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Ni tsei lɛ ahe baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ koni ekɛfee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa onibii lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my food crops dry up so fast during the hot season when there are no trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli be mli ni tsei bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Trees block strong wind and harsh sunlight while holding water deep in the ground. Without them, the hot sun evaporates moisture from the soil very quickly, leaving your crops thirsty.
ga: Tsei tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa, yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ amɛbɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya. Ha kumai aye onibii lɛ

english: Why does my soil become hard and weak after I cut down all the bushes and trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbɔjɔ nɛkɛ beni mifo mi tsei bibii kɛ tsei lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tree roots hold the soil together. When trees are removed, heavy rains easily wash away the rich topsoil that contains all the food your crops need to grow.
ga: Tso shishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome. Beni afoɔ tsei Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Why do my young seedlings burn so easily when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants are like babies—their leaves are very soft and cannot handle direct hot sun all day. They need shade from surrounding trees or crops until they grow strong enough.
ga: Tso bibioo ko tamɔ abifao. Ebaai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ adɛŋ. kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow after I spray weed-killing chemicals on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ eshwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: If chemicals are mixed too strong or sprayed directly on your crops instead of just the weeds, the medicine acts like a poison and burns the plant's leaves and roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsofai lɛ efutu waa tsɔ loo akɛshwie onibii anɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe jwɛi lɛ pɛ. Tsofa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ poison ni ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ baai kɛ shishifãi.

english: Can spraying strong chemicals on my farm make the harvest unsafe for my family to eat?
ga: Ani tsofai ni mli wa ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmaa lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha miweku lɛ ni amɛye?

english: Yes, if you use unsafe chemicals or harvest your crops too soon after spraying, the chemical residue stays inside the crop and can cause sickness when eaten.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai ni bɛ shweshweeshwe tsu nii loo okpa onibii oya tsɔ beni okɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ, ni kɛ́ aye lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aba.

english: How do I know if the chemical spray I am using is destroying the natural strength of my soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miifite shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: If earthworms disappear, the soil gets very hard like stone, and your crops refuse to grow unless you add more and more artificial fertilizer every year, the chemicals have damaged your soil.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ laaje lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa waa tamɔ tɛ. Ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereŋ ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he daa afi. Tsofai lɛ miifite oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do crop diseases seem to get worse even though I keep spraying chemicals every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ahe helai ehiii kwraa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ nɔ daa afi moŋ?

english: Overusing chemicals can kill the friendly insects and good soil organisms that naturally protect your farm, allowing bad pests and sickness to spread faster.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii kpakpai ni buɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai gbohii gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: How does bad water or chemicals in the ground make my crops get sick?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni nu fɔŋ loo tsofai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hela?

english: Crops drink water from the soil through their roots to feed themselves. If the soil water is contaminated with harsh chemicals, the plant drinks the poison and becomes weak or dies.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛye amɛhe. Kɛji tsofai ni mli wa ewo nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baanu tsofa fɔŋ lɛ ni egbɔjɔ loo ebaagbo.

english: If nearby land is dug up and trees are cleared, how does that affect my farm's crop yield?
ga: Kɛji atsa shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni ajie tsei lɛ Te ebaana ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Digging up surrounding land disturbs the natural flow of clean water, washes poor subsoil onto your land, and exposes your crops to hotter weather, causing low harvest yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ ni atsaa lɛ gbalaa nu ni mli tse ni hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ mli. Tsumɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sũ ni ehiii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees take so many years before they start producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need time to build strong root systems and sturdy branches capable of carrying heavy pods. While traditional cocoa trees take 4 to 5 years to bear fruit, modern hybrid varieties developed for Ghanaian soils can start producing in just 2 to 3 years.
ga: Cacao tsei he miihia be koni amɛma shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ niji ni mli wa ni baanyɛ atere ŋmeii ni tsii. Yɛ be mli ni blema cacao tsei lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei srɔtoi ni akɛfee Ghana shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli.

english: Why do cocoa pods grow directly out of the main tree trunk instead of at the end of thin branches like mangos do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ, shi jeee yɛ tsei niji bibii lɛ anaagbee lɛ? Tamɔ mango?

english: This natural trait is called cauliflory. Cocoa pods are heavy and full of wet seeds, so the tree grows them directly on its thick trunk and main branches where there is enough structural strength to hold their weight without breaking.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli su nɛɛ akɛ kɔlifloa. Cocoa tsei lɛ amli tsii ni dumɔwui ni efɔ eyi mli obɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ daa yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni mli wa lɛ kɛ eniji wuji lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ, ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua muji ni amɛkuuu.

english: How long can a well-maintained cocoa tree continue to yield fruit for my family?
ga: Be enyiɛ cacao tso ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii aha miweku lɛ?

english: With good farm management such as regular pruning, weed control, and soil fertilization, a healthy cocoa tree can remain productive and yield good harvests for 30 to 40 years or more.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ kpakpa nɔ tamɔ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai afii 30 kɛyashi 40 loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and broad leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. They need shade from temporary nurse crops like plantains to shelter them from direct heat and keep moisture in the soil while their roots grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni eshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land has the right kind of soil for starting a cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa ni manyɛ maje kookoo ŋmɔ shishi?

english: Cocoa thrives in deep, dark, soft topsoil that drains water easily without creating standing pools. Soils that are very rocky, heavily clay-based, or flood frequently during heavy rain are not good for cocoa roots.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli edɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu hoɔ oya ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi daa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ tɛi waa. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Aloo nu afua ni baa shii abɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ehiii kɛha kookoo shishifãi.

english: Can I plant cassava in the same field as my newly planted cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni adu ŋmei tso hee lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: It is best to avoid cassava near young cocoa because cassava roots spread aggressively and suck up a huge amount of nutrients and water from the soil, competing heavily with young cocoa seedlings and slowing their growth.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ tapioca ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo ni mli jɔ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛmuɔ niyenii kɛ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa ni ehaa amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why do many of the tiny flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ fã ni fa lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage get pollinated by tiny beneficial insects called midges. Stress from drought, lack of soil nutrients, or severe weather also causes the tree to shed excess flowers it cannot support.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛmli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. hɔmɔ haomɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii lɛ haa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi aahu akɛ anyɛɛɛ akwɛ amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves get brown burned patches on them that look like they were scorched by fire?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ yɛ shãa he okadii ni tamɔ nɔ ni ashã amɛ lɛ?

english: This burn pattern is caused by sap-sucking pests like mirids (capsids). They pierce young stems and leaves to feed, injecting toxic saliva that kills the leaf tissue and leaves a dry, burnt appearance.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ shãa nɛɛ baa ji kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids (capsids). Amɛfoɔ tsei bibii kɛ baai amli koni amɛye nii. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi, ni eshã.

english: Why do green cocoa pods turn black and rot right while hanging on the tree during rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ trukaa ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ amɛkpɛtɛ tsei ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp, and cold conditions. Keeping weeds down and pruning branches allows sunlight and air flow into the farm to help dry out the trees and prevent the fungus.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Eji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ, ni jɛmɛ ejɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni tsei lɛ agbi ni etsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Why is it necessary to cut off excess branches from my growing cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead, diseased, or unnecessary branches so the tree does not waste energy on useless leaves. It directs nutrients into pod production while opening up the canopy to let sunlight through, which prevents disease.
ga: Niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ jieɔ tsei lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baa pod feemɔ mli kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ ni egbeleɔ koni hulu la atsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akamɔ mɔ.

english: How do I know when my crops are hungry for soil nutrients or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiye hɔmɔ kɛha shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Crops show hunger through their leaf color and growth rate; pale or yellowing leaves, stunted height, and thin stems are clear signals that your plants lack essential food in the soil.
ga: Tsei jieɔ amɛ hɔmɔ kpo kɛtsɔ baa su kɛ amɛdalɛ oyaiyeli nɔ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔŋ, ni egbɔjɔ, kɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ otso lɛ mli.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and wilting during a long dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants yellow and droop because a lack of water stops them from pulling nutrients out of the soil, causing the plant to starve and dry out.
ga: Abɛi tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbeeɔ shi ejaakɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ haaa enyɛ ejie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: How does adding compost or manure to my soil help my crops survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: Organic manure acts like a sponge underground, holding moisture in the soil longer and slowly feeding nutrients to plant roots during dry spells.
ga: Organic ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ, ni fiofio lɛ, ekɛ niyenii haa shishifãi ni duɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Will using a machine to plow my land help my crops grow better than clearing by hand?
ga: Ani tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni mikɛ niji baatsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii?

english: Mechanized plowing breaks hard soil deeper and more evenly, which allows crop roots to spread easily, breathe, and pull water from deeper underground.
ga: Tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ gbáa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa efeɔ ekome. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, amɛmuɔ, ni amɛgbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce larger roots when I plant them on raised soil mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ shishifãi wuji yɔɔ mli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounding loosens the soil, giving cassava roots room to expand easily without heavy resistance while preventing water from gathering around the roots and causing rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oootswa lɛ baaha egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii enaa. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu, nu ni akabua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi ahe ni ekafite lɛ naa

english: Cowpea plants fold or curl their leaves in extreme sun to reduce their exposure to heat, which conserves water inside the plant so it does not dry out.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ loo amɛfoɔ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ tso lɛ mli koni baai lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming fruit when water is scarce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni nu faaa lɛ?

english: When water is extremely limited, tomato plants shed their blossoms to save energy and stay alive rather than spending scarce resources on growing fruit.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa kwraa lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi wala mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii ni anaaa lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce smaller yields if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa midumɔ nii lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds act like aggressive neighbors that steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops, leaving your plants hungry and weak.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Shi otsei lɛ ni hɔmɔ aye amɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Certified seeds are specially selected to resist local diseases and handle harsh weather, resulting in higher crop yields that give you a better return on your money.
ga: Ahala dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai ni amɛkpee kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baa ni no hu haa onáa sɛɛnamɔi kpakpai.

english: Why does trimming excess branches from my cocoa trees help them produce more cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi cacao tso lɛ niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ cacao ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning lets sunlight and air reach all parts of the tree to prevent disease, while redirecting the tree's energy into growing pods instead of unnecessary leaves.
ga: Kpojiemɔ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ he fɛɛ he koni helai akamɔ tso lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, atsakeɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ lɛ afeeɔ ŋmeii ni miida yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Do my mango trees really need chemical medicines to yield well, or can they just grow naturally on their own?
ga: Tsofai he miihia mango tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo obaanyɛ okwɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: While wild trees survive on their own, commercial mango farming requires proper soil nutrients, weed management, and pest protection. Without careful management, wild-growing trees produce fewer, smaller, and diseased fruits that are hard to sell.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ koo mli tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe moŋ, Shi mango ni aduɔ yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa. jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe Kɛji akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ woɔ aduawai fioo, bibii ni helai yɔɔ mli ni ewa akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do farmers around here use the word 'medicine' when talking about crop inputs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ biɛ lɛ kɛ wiemɔ ‘tsofa’ tsuɔ nii kɛ́ amɛmiiwie nibii ni haa anáa nii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Farmers call fertilizers, insecticides, and fungicides 'medicines' because they serve a similar purpose to human medicine: fertilizers nourish a weak plant, insecticides kill harmful pests, and fungicides cure fungal infections to keep the crop healthy.
ga: Okwaafoi tsɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ kooloi bibii akɛ ‘tsofai’ ejaakɛ amɛyiŋtoo tamɔ adesa tsofafeemɔ nɔ, ni ji ni amɛha tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ niyenii. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsaa ŋmeii ahe helai koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I use one single chemical medicine to solve every crop problem on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa kome atsu ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe nii?

english: No, different plant problems require specific treatments. Spraying an insect killer will not cure a fungal disease or feed poor soil, so you must identify the exact issue before choosing a crop medicine.
ga: Dabi, tso naagba fɛɛ naagba biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai loo ehaaa shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ oyɔse naagba lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani ohala tso tsofa.

english: Is it safe to harvest and sell my fruits immediately after spraying them with crop medicine?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makpa mi aduawai lɛ ni mahɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tso tsofa efɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: No, every crop medicine has a required waiting period after spraying. You must wait a specific number of days so the chemicals break down safely, ensuring the fruit is non-toxic for buyers.
ga: Dabi, tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma fee lɛ biɔ ni amɛmɛ be ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ omɛ gbii babaoo dani tsofai lɛ afite shweshweeshwe. Na nɔmimaa akɛ aduawai lɛ efeŋ nɔ ni gbeɔ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ.

english: Can I use chemical sprays to force my mango trees to flower and produce fruit out of season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mi-mango tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii koni ekɛnyɛ mi-mango tso lɛ nɔ ni ewo yibii yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Yes, flower-inducing chemicals can trigger off-season fruiting, but doing so regularly disrupts the tree's natural resting cycle and requires extra water and fertilizer to keep the tree alive.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni haa fɔfɔii baa lɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo ni bɛ be ni sa mli lɛ aya hiɛ. Shi enɛ ni afeɔ daa lɛ gbalaa tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe shihilɛ lɛ mli. Ni ehe miihia ni akɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he koni tsei lɛ ahi shi.

english: What will happen to my crops if I keep using medicines to force them to produce higher yields?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai fɔji tsu nii koni mikɛnyɛ amɛnɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Overusing chemical forcing agents stresses the plant, drains the soil of natural nutrients, and can lead to branch dieback, poor fruit quality, and lower total yields in future seasons.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná haomɔ. Ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ niji lɛ agboi aba. aduawai ni ehiii kɛ yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ ba shi yɛ bei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: If I force my fruit trees to yield constantly without a rest period, will it shorten their lifespan?
ga: Kɛ minyɛ tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ nɔ koni ewo yibii be fɛɛ be ni ekpaaa lɛ, Ani wala be lɛ baafee kuku?

english: Yes, forcing a tree to bear fruit continuously without adequate recovery time exhausts its root energy, making it prone to diseases and significantly shortening its productive lifetime.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso ni anyɛɔ nɔ koni ewo yibii be fɛɛ be ni be ni sa bɛ mli ni ekɛbaatsa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi. ekɛ helai baa oya ni ehaa nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ wala be feɔ kuku waa.

english: Why do my mango trees produce so many blossoms, but very few of them turn into big fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei woɔ yibii babaoo shi tsei fioo pɛ woɔ yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Mango flowers drop easily due to pest attacks like thrips, fungal diseases like anthracnose, or severe dry weather. Protecting early flowers with proper care helps them stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Mango fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ thrips, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose, loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe yɛ shishijee mli kɛtsɔ hiɛdɔɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are turning yellow because of disease or because the plant is hungry?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hela hewɔ loo hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ?

english: Nutrient deficiency usually causes uniform yellowing across older or newer leaves without spots, while fungal or bacterial diseases create irregular black or brown spots, yellow halos, or rotting patches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ haa baai momo loo ehee lɛ feɔ nɔ ni he tseee, ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ amɛhe. yɛ be mli ni fungal loo bacteria helai kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa baa. halo ŋmɔŋ loo fitemɔ he okadii

english: Why does my mango orchard give me a massive harvest this year, but almost nothing the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso yibii lɛ wo yibii babaoo nɛkɛ afi nɛɛ? Shi afi ni baa lɛ, eshwɛ fioo ni afeee nɔ ko kwraa?

english: This behavior is called alternate bearing. After producing a heavy crop, the tree exhausts its stored energy and needs a year to build back strength unless supported with post-harvest pruning, water, and fertilizer.
ga: Atsɛɔ subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ sɛɛkuu-kɛsaramɔ. Beni tso lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii sɛɛ lɛ Hewalɛ ni ekɛto lɛ laajeɔ ni ekɛ afi tsuɔ nii ni ekɛtswaa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ. Ja ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nikpamɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do the new improved cocoa seedlings produce so much more harvest than my old cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo dumɔwui heei ni mifee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe mi-kookoo tsei momo lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties, often called hybrids, are specially bred to mature faster, withstand local diseases better, and direct more energy into producing pods rather than just growing tall branches.
ga: Atsɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ hybrids lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛshwere oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ Ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ pods fe niji ni kɛlɛ kɛkɛ ni edaa.

english: If I plant more trees closer together on my farm, will I get a bigger total harvest?
ga: Kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani maná yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni da fe no?

english: Overcrowding trees causes them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This stress makes trees weak and lowers your yield. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough air and light to produce maximum fruit.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa onibii ni owoɔ lɛ baa shi. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I cut down all the big shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct heat. Shade trees act as a protective barrier against harsh sunlight and help keep moisture in the soil until the young cocoa is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I cut off some of the healthy-looking branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches that waste the tree's energy. It opens up the tree canopy to let sunlight and air pass through, which prevents fungal diseases and encourages the tree to grow bigger pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa ni haa tso lɛ hewalɛ hoɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ ni agbeleɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji.

english: Can I put fertilizer on my farm during the dry season so the soil is ready before the rains?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli koni mikɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ anɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so that plant roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer in dry soil is wasteful because the wind can blow it away, and the concentrated chemical can burn plant roots.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ ji fitemɔ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ ajie kɛya. Ni tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi ashã.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep dropping off the stem without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by lack of water, attacked by insects, or when there are not enough tiny insects (midges) around to pollinate the flowers properly.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa, ni kooloi bibii tutuaa lɛ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods start turning black and rotting during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ diŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, cool weather. Raindrops splash spores from the soil onto low pods, and excess humidity lets the fungus grow quickly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, ni mli ejɔ mli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ kɛyaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo baaha ŋmɔtɔ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the soil lacks nitrogen. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves the small amount it has from the older lower leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ baajie fioo kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: How do weeds in my field reduce the weight of the crops I harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mikpamɔ lɛ mli tsiimɔ baa shi?

english: Weeds grow very fast and steal nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your crops. When your crops don't get enough food, they produce smaller fruits and grains.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaawo aduawai bibii kɛ ŋmaa.

english: Why does my land yield less harvest now than it did five years ago when I first started farming it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe bɔ ni eji afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ beni mibɔi okwaayeli klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Crops pull food out of the ground every season. If you continuously farm the same land without adding manure or fertilizer, or letting the soil rest, the nutrients get completely used up.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji oya nɔ otsu okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he. loo ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baafite.

english: When bottom leaves turn yellow, your maize is usually hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green and grow fast. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant recover.
ga: Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ Bei pii lɛ, nitrogen hɔmɔ yeɔ O-ŋmã. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn completely black and dry up on the branches?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly in very damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess branches to let air and sunlight into the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Fungi hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ enɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays soaked with water for too long during heavy rains. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps extra water drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Kasava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers before any pods actually form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miigbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by hot, dry weather or when small insects attack them. Giving the farm proper shade and managing pests helps the tree hold onto its flowers so they can turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni nu egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tutuaa ŋmɔ lɛ ni akɛ hulutsoo ni sa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, rotten spots at the bottom while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, often because water supply is irregular. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding compost helps the fruits grow smooth and healthy.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni bɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food to grow tall and produce large, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my crop seeds during the major rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: You should wait until the rains become steady for about two weeks so the soil stays deep wet. Planting after just one early rain can cause seeds to sprout and then dry up if rain stops for several days.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be aaafee otsii enyɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ kpa gbii babaoo.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with seeds that can stay dormant in the soil for years. Clearing the land gives those hidden seeds full sunshine and rain, letting them sprout faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa. Dumɔwui komɛi yɛ ni baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛhiɛ aka shi. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ aná hulu la kɛ nugbɔ kwraa. Ehaa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not grip deep into the ground, and heavy bunches make them top-heavy. Staking the plants with strong wooden poles gives them extra support against storm winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni ŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ni jwɛi ni tsii baaha amɛgbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni wa fĩ otso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha enyɛ eshi ahum ni tswaa lɛ babaoo.

english: Why do I need to plow my land properly before planting maize instead of just clearing the surface weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsu shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu ŋmãa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Plowing loosens hard, compacted soil so that young maize roots can easily grow deep to search for water and nutrients, while also burying weed seeds so they do not compete with your crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ ni ewa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ ji koni ŋmãa shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛtao nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fuu jwɛi dumɔwui koni amɛkɛ onibii akaye akaŋ.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks with tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii baa. loo dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava sheds its leaves during dry periods as a self-defense mechanism to reduce water loss and conserve energy in its underground roots until rain returns.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants yield more fruit when I grow groundnuts on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural food supply that feeds neighboring crops like peppers.
ga: Peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ chili peppers niyenii.

english: Why does my crop burn and dry up if I put fertilizer directly against the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is concentrated salt; putting it directly against the stem draws moisture out of the plant tissue, burning the roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ fãji lɛ amli. ni eshãa shishifãi lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: The first rain is often a false start followed by hot, dry days; sowing immediately can cause your seeds to sprout and then dry up and die before regular rains settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji amale shishijee. Gbii ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni ooodu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha odumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ aba.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my last hybrid harvest produce smaller crops than the original store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii bibii fe shishijee dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one generation; the seeds harvested from them lose those high-performing traits, leading to uneven growth and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛhaa yinɔ kome. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ nitsumɔ su ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why do weeds kill my young crop seedlings so much faster than older crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi gbeɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ oya fe tsei ni edara lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have small roots and few leaves, so tall, aggressive weeds easily steal all their light, water, and nutrients before the crop can establish itself.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai fioo. Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ juɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ dani tso lɛ baanyɛ ama shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the large forest trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie koo mli tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn under direct sunlight; they need shade from larger trees to keep the soil moist and the air cool until their root systems fully mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ baashã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji adɛŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baadara.

english: What makes the leaves of my tomato plants curl up and stop producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo?

english: Leaf curl is a viral infection usually spread by tiny whiteflies; once infected, the plant concentrates its energy on surviving rather than producing healthy tomatoes.
ga: Leaf curl ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni bei pii lɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛji akɛ hela lɛ emɔ Tsei lɛ, amɛbaakwɛ wala nɔ fe tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbaafee.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil has too much water drowning the roots. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer helps the leaves turn green so the plant can make big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, loo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ miiho. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop and wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In extreme heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it up from the soil. The plant droops to protect itself from losing more moisture, and it will usually stand tall again when the evening cool arrives.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baajie amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ ba.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up with yellow patches and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies or spread through infected stems. The leaves become damaged and cannot produce food, which prevents the roots underneath from growing large.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ loo egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Baai lɛ efite ni niyenii nyɛɛɛ afee. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ daraaa.

english: No, planting too close forces the maize plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They will grow tall and thin, producing small or empty cobs, whereas proper spacing gives each plant enough food to bear large cobs.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii agbo ko.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow short, twisted, and small instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kukuji, amɛtsiɔ amɛhe, ni amɛfeɔ bibii moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers expand downward into the earth, so if the ground is hard and compacted, the tuber cannot push through easily. Making soft, raised mounds or ridges gives the roots loose soil so they can expand long and smooth.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Yitso lɛ boteŋ mli mlɛo. Gɔji loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ ni ooofee lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ abaanyɛ afee lɛ kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees burn and wither when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under full, direct sunlight. They need partial shade from plantain plants or bigger trees to keep them cool and moist until their stems become tough and mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo tsei wuji amli koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi be mli ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baawa ni amɛdara.

english: My pepper plants produce many flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without forming peppers. Why is this happening?
ga: Mi pepper tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ. Mɛni he je nɛ e baa jã a?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of food in the soil. Keeping the soil evenly damp and adding compost helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: This black rot is caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering. When watering is uneven, the plant cannot move calcium from the soil into the fruit, causing the tissue at the bottom to collapse.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black rot hela nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai lɛ amli. ni haa fãji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ fiteɔ

english: Why does leaving weeds around my young cassava slow down its growth so much?
ga: Mɛni Hewɔ ni Jwɛi ni Ashiɔ yɛ Mibi lɛ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ miiha edalɛ miiba shi babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the sunlight, water, and food from the soil before your cassava roots can reach them. Clearing weeds early ensures your cassava gets all the soil nutrients it needs to build big tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are tiny ragged holes appearing in my young corn leaves, with dirt that looks like sawdust inside the leaf stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm that hide inside the central roll of the corn leaf. They chew the tender leaf tissue before it opens, leaving behind small holes and waste that looks like sawdust.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe fãji dani amɛgbeleɔ. kɛtsɔ bu bibioo ko kɛ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei ni ashiɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen or the soil is too waterlogged. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost early helps the plants regain their green color and produce large, full ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛaawo mli mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ aná amɛ su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmãa toi ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plants experience heat stress, lack of water, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from extreme heat helps the flowers set into healthy fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my cassava cuttings when the rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Plant cassava stems right after the early rains have made the soil moist but not soggy. This gives the cuttings enough water to sprout strong roots quickly before any dry spell sets in.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ shi ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ aba. Enɛ haa tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi ni wa akwɛ oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Why do my plantain shoots take so long to fruit after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains grow slowly if they have to compete with too many sucker shoots or lack water and organic matter. Removing extra suckers so only two or three grow with the main plant lets it focus its energy on producing fruit faster.
ga: Plantains baakwɛ̃ fiofio kɛji akɛ amɛyɛ akaŋshii babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmeii amli loo kɛji amɛbɛ nu kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni tsei titrii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi shi yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama yibiiwoo ni ebaawo oya lɛ nɔ.

english: What is causing my pepper leaves to curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking the juices from the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves open and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ baa mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ mli tseɔ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my bean pods get full of tiny holes right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean pods lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Dani abaakpa nii?

english: Insects like pod borers lay eggs on the flowers and young pods, and the hatching worms eat into the beans. Inspecting crops regularly and using approved pest control before pods mature protects your yield.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ pod borers lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ pod bibii anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni baa lɛ baaye ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli daa ni okɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛgbeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsu nii dani pods lɛ adara lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and crooked instead of big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams grow small and bent when the soil is too hard, stony, or poorly prepared. Making deep, soft soil mounds or ridges allows the tubers to expand freely underground and absorb plenty of nutrients.
ga: Sweet potatoes bafeɔ bibii ni ekotoɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo asaaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Gɔji loo ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afeɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi amɛhaa amɛhe ni amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds away from my young crops early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ midumɔwui lɛ amli mra lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow strong and resist diseases.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛte shi amɛwo helai.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their small young pods before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? Babaoo dani eshɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop small pods, known as cherelle wilt, when the tree doesn't have enough water, light, or food to support all of them. Proper pruning and feeding reduce this loss so more pods survive to maturity.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ Cherelle Wilt lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu, kane, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ aye abua. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ nɔ ni elaaje nɛɛ aba shi. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does changing the crop I plant on my land each season help my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mitsakeɔ daa be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi yɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly attracts specific pests and drains the same nutrients from the soil. Rotating different crops, like switching between maize and cowpeas, starves pests and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaagbala kooloi komɛi ni yeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa teŋ tsakemɔ. Ebaaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I cut down all the large shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ hulutsoo tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct sunlight. Sunlight destroys the leaf pigments and overheats the plant, so shade trees are essential to shield them and trap moisture around their leaves until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Hulu la fiteɔ su ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ mli dɔɔ fe nine. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ he miihia koni abu he ni ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ ahi shi. baai lɛ kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking exposes the leaves to maximum sunlight and prevents them from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo, ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Yellowing along the center of older maize leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is necessary for healthy leaf growth, and when it is low, the plant moves what little it has to newer leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai ni egbɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni kɛ́ fioo ko yɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baajie nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ fioo kɛya baa hee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise planting cowpea or groundnuts on the farm before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔji amli dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the roots decay, they leave natural plant food in the soil for future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, amɛshiɔ tsei niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ abele.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit. It often happens when soil water levels fluctuate sharply, preventing the plant from pulling calcium up through its roots.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsake oya. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala calcium kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural way of saving water during dry weather. With fewer leaves, less water evaporates into the dry air, allowing the roots to stay alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni ŋmei tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ he yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ lɛ. Beni baai lɛ faaa lɛ Nu fioo baaho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into little cups and stop growing leaves properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? ni ekpaa baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking juices from under the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by these insects that distorts normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. ni fiteɔ dalɛ ni sa lɛ

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to shoot out of the ground when I plant them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni mikɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds contain only a limited amount of stored energy. If planted too deep, the seed runs out of food energy trying to reach the surface and dies underground before it can touch the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato. Kɛji adu mli tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ niyenii hewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani hulu la lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce very small fruits when I plant them close together to fit more on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ miŋmɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting too close together causes plants to compete intensely with one another for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. This leaves each individual plant too weak to develop large fruits.
ga: Amɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and thin even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital soil nutrients and root space away from your crops. Rain helps both plants, but the weeds aggressively absorb the nutrients your crops need to build strong stems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe. Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei srɔtoi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Shi jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods as they grow older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo beni edaa lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 25 to 30 years, their roots and branches become less efficient at transporting nutrients and water to produce flowers. Over time, old trees also accumulate diseases, leading to lower yields unless they are pruned or replaced.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tsei ye afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛniji lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛkɛ niyenii kɛ nu aya koni amɛwo fɔfɔi. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ buaa helai anaa. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ja afo loo atsake.

english: How do I know when my old farm has reached the end of its life and needs to be replanted?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni miŋmɔ momo lɛ eshɛ esɛɛnamɔ shihilɛ naagbee ni ehe miihia ni adu ekoŋŋ?

english: When your crops consistently produce very low yields despite getting fertilizer, good rainfall, and pest control, or when most trees become diseased and weak, it shows the farm has reached its age limit and needs fresh planting.
ga: Beni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii ni baa shi waa be fɛɛ be yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛhaa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni helai babaoo emɔ tso lɛ ni ebɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ eshɛ afii ni esa akɛ eye lɛ he, ni ehe miihia ni aná ŋmɔshi nibii heei.

english: Why does my soil yield much less food today compared to when I started farming it ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli lɛ? Kɛ akɛto be ni mibɔi okwaayeli afii 10 ni eho nɛ lɛ he.

english: Every time you harvest crops, they carry away nutrients from the soil. If you plant continuously for years without adding manure, compost, or fertilizer to restore those nutrients, the soil becomes tired and produces smaller harvests.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu nii be fɛɛ be afii babaoo ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he koni ekɛ nakai niyenii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmaa lɛ baa shi.

english: What happens if I keep planting maize on the exact same land every season?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly consumes the same nutrients over and over while giving soil-borne pests and diseases a permanent home, causing your plants to become weaker and yields to drop over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Esa akɛ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii shii abɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ feɔ shia ni hiɔ shi daa. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin but fail to bring good fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo shi etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Instead of using energy to grow heavy fruits or tubers, they waste energy stretching upward to reach light.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛdu aduawai loo bulbs ni tsii lɛ, Amɛfiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛná la.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long due to poor drainage. Waterlogged soil suffocates the roots and creates the right environment for fungi to cause root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top, causing the lower leaves to pale.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from very high heat, dry conditions, too much nitrogen fertilizer, or lack of insects and wind to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa, shihilɛi ni mli egbi, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. aloo kooloi bibii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni baaha fɔfɔii lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ

english: Why do some young crops need shade trees around them while other crops die if they don't get full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo ebɔle ŋmɔshi nibii bibii komɛi ahe lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi gboiɔ kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Young crops like cocoa naturally grow under larger trees in forests, so shade protects them from hot sun while they are delicate. In contrast, sun-loving crops like maize need direct sunlight to produce energy for growth.
ga: Nibii bibii tamɔ kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ tsei wuji ashishi yɛ koo lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, shade lɛ buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he be mli ni tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo lɛ. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ enɛ lɛ, tsei ni sumɔɔ Hulu, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha dalɛ.

english: How do plantain trees help my young tree crops survive during their early years?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui yeɔ ebuaa mi dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli?

english: Plantains grow quickly and have wide leaves that act like natural sun umbrellas. They shade delicate young tree seedlings, cool the ground temperature, and help keep moisture in the soil until the seedlings grow strong.
ga: Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli parasols. Amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ni amɛhaa tsei bibii amli dumɔwui bibii lɛ feɔ hulutsoo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe waa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning light green and yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to grow healthy green leaves. Applying compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer when the soil is moist helps the crop recover.
