ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni wa lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ shi.

english: Why do my crops yield less harvest when I plant maize on the exact same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpea or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko woɔ nɔ lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi kɛ baai gboi yɔɔ mli lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha mi.

english: Covering soil with plant materials, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the earth, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from sprouting and stealing nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ tsei ahe nibii haa lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu la lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are there small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dark droppings in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ buji bibii ni egbɛ eshwã kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ? Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding on the tender inner leaves. Early inspection and spraying with targeted organic or approved pest controls will prevent them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kwɛmɔ mra kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akwɛɔ nɔ loo akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Ensuring consistent soil moisture and partial shade during extreme heat helps flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ fioo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during windstorms when the fruit bunch starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ mli beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that can easily be weakened by soil pests like root nematodes. Supporting the main stem with a strong bamboo or wooden prop prevents heavy bunches from pulling the tree down.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ŋmeii wuji akagbala tso lɛ shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small and thin even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than most cultivated crops and aggressively capture sunlight, soil moisture, and fertilizer meant for your crops, effectively starving them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ. ni emɔɔ hulu la shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ Ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha onibii. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni mɔɔ shi nɔ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my crops so it doesn't harm them?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛkaye tsei lɛ awui?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist after rain, but not during heavy downpours that wash it away. Keep the fertilizer a few inches away from the plant stem so it does not burn the roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi koni shishifãi lɛ akashã.

english: Why do the leaves on my newly transplanted cocoa saplings turn brown and dry out during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso ni midu ehee lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow roots that burn under full, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantain nearby creates a living umbrella that protects the young cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if a cassava stem cutting is strong enough to give me a high yield?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Healthy cassava cuttings should come from the middle section of a mature plant that is 8 to 12 months old. Look for firm stems that are about thumb-thick with visible, undamaged buds along the length.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei kpakpa ni afo lɛ ajɛ ŋmei tso ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli. Taomɔ tso ni ma shi shiŋŋ ni tamɔ tsitsi bibioo. Eyɛ ŋmeii ni anaa jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee yɛ elɛɛmɔ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my young seedlings seem to need different care than mature crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe hiaa ni akwɛ amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young plants are tender like infants and need protection from harsh weather, high shade, and specific nutrients to build strong roots, whereas mature crops focus energy on building flowers and fruits and require different nutrients.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo tamɔ abifabii ni amɛbiɔ ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, hulutsoo babaoo, kɛ niyenii krɛdɛɛi ahe koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Be ni tso lɛ daa lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai feemɔ he nii. ni amɛbiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛi srɔtoi

english: Do I need to change the type of fertilizer I apply as my crops grow older?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni matsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ be mli ni mitsei lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Yes, crops need nitrogen early on to grow healthy stems and leaves, but as they shift to the flowering and fruiting stage, they need phosphorus and potassium to produce healthy seeds and fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, nitrogen he miihia tsei mra. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ afee shiŋŋ Shi kɛ́ tso lɛ tsake kɛtee fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo be mli lɛ Amɛhe miihia amɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium koni amɛwo dumɔwui kɛ yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow as the plants get bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often show that the crop's nutrient demands have changed as it matures, or that it is lacking specific nutrients like nitrogen in the soil during a fast growth phase.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ etsake beni edaa lɛ. aloo niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ

english: How do I know when my crop has changed from the growth stage to the fruiting stage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ etsake kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ lɛ amli kɛtee yibiiwoo be lɛ mli?

english: Crops show physical signs like the appearance of flower buds, stem hardening, and a slowdown in leafy growth, signaling that their daily nutrient and water needs have changed.
ga: Tsei jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii tamɔ fɔfɔii akpojiemɔ, tsei ashishifãi ni wa, kɛ baai adalɛ blɛoo. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ daa gbi niyenii kɛ nu he hiamɔ nii etsake.

english: Why should I treat pest problems differently when my crops start flowering compared to when they were seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsu tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai ahe nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi lɛ fe be mli ni amɛji dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Seedlings attract leaf-chewing insects, while flowering plants attract pest species that target blooms and young fruit, so treatments must be adjusted to protect flowers without harming beneficial pollinators.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ baai lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kwɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi kɛ amɛyibii bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ afee tsofai ni akɛbuɔ fɔfɔi ahe ni eyeee ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ awui.

english: Why do my young crops die shortly after I transplant them into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Transplant shock occurs when root systems are damaged or exposed to sudden intense sunlight and heat, which can be reduced by watering before transplanting and providing early shade.
ga: Transplant shock baa kɛji shishifãi lɛ efite loo hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa trukaa lɛ kpe. Abaanyɛ aba enɛ shi kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa dani aduɔ lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa mra lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my crops to suddenly wither and die even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po?

english: Sudden wilting during rainy periods is usually caused by waterlogged soil damaging the roots or fungal root rot diseases that block water from moving up the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni haaa nu aya ŋwɛi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ baa.

english: How can I stop my crops from dying off when a sudden dry spell hits my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbo beni hɔmɔ ba trukaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around plants with organic mulch like dry grass keeps the soil cool and conserves moisture, helping plants survive dry periods between rains.
ga: Mulching around Dumɔ kɛ organic mulch, tamɔ jwɛi ni egbi, koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ.

english: Why are my crop flowers falling off before producing any fruit or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii loo amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flower drop usually happens when crops suffer severe heat or water stress during their delicate flowering phase, causing the plant to shed flowers to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ yɛ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhi shi.

english: Is it normal for the bottom leaves of my crop to die off while new leaves are growing at the top?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ baagboi yɛ be mli ni baai heei miida yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, as plants grow taller, older bottom leaves get shaded, and the plant naturally transfers nutrients from those lower leaves to nourish new leaves and fruits at the top.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ tsei lɛ dara babaoo Babaoo ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ daraa lɛ, babaoo ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ni tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ nakai baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛha baai heei kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen or cassava plants are planted too close together, the plant spends all its energy developing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo aduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why are there tiny holes in my young maize leaves and green worms hiding inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani akɛtee gɔŋ lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that burrows into the funnels of young maize plants to feed on the leaves, which slows down plant growth if not treated early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli koni eye baai lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines to climb tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maye mabua sweet potato wain tso ko ni ekwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum exposure to sunlight to create food that builds the big tuber underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni feɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts or beans on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients and weakens the land. Legumes like groundnuts and beans absorb nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring natural fertility for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni akɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it better to water my vegetable garden early in the morning rather than in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ mli nu lɛ leebi fe hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Watering in the mid-day heat causes water to evaporate before the crop roots can drink it, and wet leaves in scorching heat can scorch the plant and encourage fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli yɛ gbi teŋgbɛ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu. Baai ni efɔ yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ ni ewo tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in a open, clear field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse, ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. They require partial shade from nurse crops like plantains to retain soil moisture and shield their leaves during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni amɛbu amɛtso lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees snap or fall over easily right when the fruit bunch starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ fãa loo egbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be weakened by root pests or poor soil structure. When the heavy fruit bunch grows, strong winds push the tree over unless it is supported with wooden fork stakes.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Kɛji aduawai akuu lɛ da Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa tsei ashwie shi ja tso ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn yellow and grow slowly even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiida blɛoo be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and compete aggressively for the nutrients, space, and fertilizer in the soil, taking food away from your crops and starving them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛyeɔ niyenii, he ko, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni amɛheɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my farm when the ground is dry and there is no rain coming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve into the soil. Applying fertilizer to dry soil concentrates chemical salts around the roots, which can scorch and destroy the roots rather than feeding the plant.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsofai ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbe amɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, severe lack of water, or when there are no beneficial insects like bees around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. nu efo mli waa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow mainly due to a lack of nitrogen in the soil or poor drainage causing waterlogging. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost early in the growing stage helps the leaves stay green and photosynthesize properly.
ga: Nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ ni abɛi baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ, ni no haa nu shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he kɛjɛ shishijee be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ fotosintɛsis jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from losing more water, and it usually recovers as the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbo be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni elaaje lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do crop leaves curl up tightly when we have long periods without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up to reduce the surface area exposed to direct sunlight and wind. This is a natural survival defense that minimizes water loss through evaporation until the plant receives water again.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa lɛ shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ hebuu ni haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ naa nu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the young pods dropping off my cocoa trees before they can mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Early cocoa pod loss, known as cherelle wilt, happens when the tree is under stress from drought, nutrient shortages, or pest attacks like capsids. Providing adequate shade, soil organic matter, and proper nutrients reduces this pod loss.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni laajeɔ mra Ale lɛ hu akɛ Cherelle Wilt, ni ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ shishi. Niyenii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids, shade, kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni niyenii kpakpa baaye abua ni pod ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Regular watering and light shading during extreme heat spikes help flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ejaaa loo kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cashew trees produce plenty of flowers but very few cashew nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi cashew ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Low fruit setup in cashews is often caused by sap-sucking insects damaging the flower clusters, or by inadequate pollination. Protecting the flower panicles from pests during early bloom helps convert flowers into nuts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi akui lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ yibii ni baa shi yɛ cashew ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa mli Kɛ́ abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even when the leaves are lush and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: When soil has excessive nitrogen, cassava puts most of its energy into growing big top leaves instead of storing starches in the roots. Balanced soil nutrients and avoiding heavy nitrogen applications encourage energy to flow down into the tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo woɔ ebaai wuji lɛ anɔ shweremɔ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa kɛ nitrogen ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ baawo hewalɛ hewalɛ ni eho kɛya shi kɛya bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why does planting plantains next to my young cocoa seedlings help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni aduɔ dumɔwui yɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that create temporary shade and keep the air cool and humid, which helps young cocoa trees survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad for my crop yield if I plant my seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting too closely forces crop roots and leaves to compete fiercely with each other for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and moisture. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong stems and produce bigger harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulutsoo ni faaa Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa baakwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does burning my bush before planting harm my soil over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii ni ashãa dani aduɔ lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ awui yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the living organisms in the soil and burns off organic matter that holds moisture. Over time, it leaves the topsoil hard, dry, and easily washed away by heavy rains.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ wala ni eshãa nibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli wa, egbiɔ, ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ lɛ oya.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct, harsh sunlight during their first few years. Without shade trees or plantains grown nearby to block the heat, the hot sun scorches the tender leaves and turns them yellow.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni amɛtsi latsaa lɛ naa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baashã baai bibii ni eha amɛfee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my maize stalks fall over easily whenever a strong wind or rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ baa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over, a problem known as lodging, when their roots are too shallow or damaged by underground pests. Planting seeds at the right depth and mounding soil around the base of the stems helps anchor the roots firmly.
ga: ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shi Enɛ ji naagba ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ shĩa. Beni eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa kɛ sũ ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: My cassava plants are growing very tall with plenty of big leaves, so why are the tubers under the ground so small?
ga: Mi yucca tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ waa ni eyɛ baai wuji waa. Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich organic matter, they spend all their energy growing tall stems and bushy leaves above ground instead of sending energy down to develop thick roots and big tubers.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo nɔ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli tse kɛ bulbs agboi aba.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is an imbalance of nutrients. Without steady moisture and moderate warmth, the plant drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ejaaa lɛ Kɛji hulutsoo be ni tamɔ ekome kɛ hulutsoo ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ baashɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help my soil grow better crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cowpea ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means their roots work with helpful bacteria in the soil to trap nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into food. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds the neighboring maize plants.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsɔ niyenii. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing green shoots even while sitting in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ be mli ni mita ŋmɔ lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living organisms that naturally wake up from dormancy after a few months. Heat and moisture signal to the yam that it is time to sprout, so keeping them in a cool, dry, and well-ventilated barn delays sprouting.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji bɔɔ nii ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i tsɔɔ sweet potatoes akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ asɛɛ afo.

english: Weeds have wild, aggressive root systems and hard seeds that stay alive in the soil for years. They are naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops can.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei, ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛ dumɔwui ni wa ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. Amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden eggs curling up and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛfite lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding underneath and sucking the sap out of the leaves. These insects can also spread plant diseases that cause the leaves to grow deformed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shishi ni amɛnuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ baanyɛ agbɛ tsei ahe helai ni haa baai ni efite lɛ hu ashwã.

english: Why is my plantain tree producing small bunches after growing many young shoots around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ miikwɛ̃ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni adu tsei bibii ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When a plantain plant produces too many young shoots, known as suckers, they all compete with the mother tree for nutrients and water. Pruning away extra suckers leaves more energy for the main plant to build heavy bunches.
ga: Beni plantains woɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo tsɔ, ni ale amɛ akɛ suckers. Amɛkɛ tso nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ tsei akui ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves droop and wilt during the afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can suck water from the ground. Adding dry grass or mulch around the root zone keeps the soil cool and moist longer throughout the day.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani akpaa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is a key nutrient for leaf greenness and growth, and when it is deficient, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has to the newer, upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ ŋmãa baa lɛ shishi ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baa lɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ, ni kɛ́ ebɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ kɛ nitrogen fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ yaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: If I apply a lot of chemical fertilizer to my crops at once, why do the leaves start looking burnt?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ fata he yɛ be kome mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: Applying too much fertilizer causes a high concentration of salts in the soil, which pulls moisture away from the roots instead of feeding them. This causes the leaf edges to dry out and look burnt.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmei babaoo aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, humid conditions. Rain splash spreads the fungus, causing pods to darken, decay, and dry up.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli Nugbɔ haa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ duŋ, amɛgboɔ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground if I leave them past the normal harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni sa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Over-mature cassava tubers left in waterlogged or heavy soils are easily attacked by fungal and bacterial root rots that break down the roots when soil oxygen is low.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni eda ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ helai, ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ faaa lɛ, tutuaa amɛ oya.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin with weak stems when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ waa lɛ, kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the seedlings compete for sunlight. They stretch upward rapidly to get light before their neighbors do, resulting in tall but thin and weak stems.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya koni amɛmɔ kane lɛ dani amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ shi eyɛ mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my young crops to stay small and look pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal essential soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your crops, effectively starving the main crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates sharply. High heat causes stress and damages pollen, preventing the flower from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ haomɔ baa ni efiteɔ pollen. Ehaa fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ awo yibii

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their small fruits before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed young fruits when they experience erratic watering, sudden heat stress, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips that damage the flower stem.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baawo yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛji akɛ afɔɔ amɛ nu be fɛɛ be. trukaa latsaa he haomɔ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, ni fiteɔ fɔfɔii ahe tsei lɛ atuatsemɔ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry hot spell. If seeds germinate during this break in the rains, the young roots will dry out and die due to lack of sustained soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ hejɔɔmɔ be mli lɛ Shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Can I grow foreign vegetables like cabbage and lettuce successfully during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu maŋsɛɛ aduawai tamɔ kaabe kɛ lettuce yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Yes, foreign crops can grow well in the dry season if you provide reliable irrigation, protect them from intense midday sun using shade nets, and manage common pest attacks.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛji akɛ okɛ nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ha. Buu tsei ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋshɔŋlooi ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. ni akwɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fɔɔ baa lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant takes food from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Tsei lɛ heɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves but give me very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or is planted too close together, it spends all its energy growing branches and leaves above ground instead of storing food below in the roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Ebaahe ebe fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ niji kɛ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ ashishi lɛ

english: What is eating small ragged holes inside the leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli lɛ yeli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central funnel of the corn plant. They eat the tender leaf tissue before it opens up, which can stunt the plant if not controlled early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baa bibii amli fãji dani egbeleɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plants without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the afternoon air is too hot or when the soil lacks water. High heat destroys the pollen inside the flower, so the plant sheds the flower to save its energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shwane kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kpataa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds from around my crop plants while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Mi tsei lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they steal sunlight, soil nutrients, and water from your crops. When crops are young, weeds grow faster and can starve your plants before they get established.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛjuɔ hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni jɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli Beni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ Jwɛi lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaaha hɔmɔ aye otsei lɛ dani amɛma shi.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil, but leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, restoring the soil's fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Koni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha okwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I remove all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct, harsh sunlight. Big shade trees protect young cocoa from scorching heat and conserve moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni eda ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: How can I tell if my plantain bunch is fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantain tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Plantain fruits are ready for harvest when individual fingers become full, plump, and lose their sharp green corners. The dried flower ends on the tips of the fruits will also easily snap off when touched.
ga: Plantain aduawai lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni inchi fɛɛ inchi eyi, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eshishigbɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ efo mli lɛ. Fɔfɔi ni egbi ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ anaa lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ ata he.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up or droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curling leaves is a natural survival defense. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, preventing water from evaporating out of its leaves too quickly.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ amɛhe kɛhaa amɛwala. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I plant fail to sprout out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are planted too deep in the soil, if the ground is completely dry, or if soil insects eat them. Seeds need air, warmth, and just enough soil moisture to wake up and start growing.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ. Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, dɔlɛ, kɛ fɛ̃i ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛte shi ni amɛbɔi dalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong sunlight burns their delicate leaves. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or bananas next to them protects the seedlings until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo banana, ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Enɛ baaye abua ni abu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellowing in the middle of maize leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is the main food crops need to build green leaves, so applying an NPK or urea fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid putting dry fertilizer directly touching the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem concentrated chemicals that burn the plant's skin and roots. Fertilizer should be placed a few inches away from the stem in a ring or shallow hole so the roots can draw it in safely.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni shãa tso lɛ hewolo kɛ shishifãi lɛ woɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋwɛi ŋta loo bu ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbala ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli shweshweeshwe.

english: Look at the small buds on the cassava stick where leaves used to grow; these buds must point upward toward the sky. Planting cassava upside down makes it hard for the roots to push down and severely lowers your harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaatsi kɛya shi ni ehaa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do my crops give smaller harvests when I plant many seeds very close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong and yield big fruits or ears.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni faaa Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hewalɛ baawo yibii loo yibii wuji.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves and powdery dust inside the leaves at the center?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ ni sũ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: This leaf damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf funnel and eats the growing tip. Catching them early and spraying targeted neem extracts or approved pesticides prevents crop loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii akafite.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of green leaves but drop their flowers before setting fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo baai eŋɔli babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ woɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. High nitrogen forces the plant to focus on growing leaves rather than keeping its flowers to make tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ Nitrogen ni fa babaoo nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaato fɔfɔii ahe gbɛjianɔ koni amɛkɛfee tomato.

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground using tall stakes allows the leaves to capture maximum sunlight to produce energy. This energy travels down into the ground to feed and grow large yam tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ tsu nii kɛwo sweet potato wain tsei anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Hewalɛ nɛɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eyaye sweet potato ŋmeii agboi lɛ niyenii ni ekwɛ amɛ.

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the same specific nutrients from the soil each season and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up in the field. Rotating with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I keep my soil from drying out too fast when the rains stop for a short period?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi oya tsɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kukuoo ko?

english: Covering the bare soil around your crops with dried grass, maize stalks, or leaves—a method called mulching—traps moisture in the ground, prevents the sun from drying out the root zone, and keeps soil cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni okɛbaabɔle ohe lɛ nɔ Okɛ jwɛi, ŋmãa tsei, loo baai aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe, gbɛ ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Etsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekaha shishifã lɛ he lɛ agbi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: Why do my young maize leaves keep turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are starving for nitrogen, which is their main food, or the root area is soaked in too much water. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji eniyenii titri lɛ. aloo shishifã lɛ he lɛ ebote nu mli tsɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava needs loose, well-drained sandy or loamy soil where its roots can expand easily into big tubers. If your soil is heavy clay that holds too much water, the cassava roots will rot before you can harvest them.
ga: Cassava he miihia shikpɔŋ ni ŋã loo ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛfee bulb agboi oya. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli. Cassava shishifãi lɛ baagboi dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed, usually by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist and balanced helps the flowers stay attached and produce fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often a sign that tiny pests like whiteflies have attacked the plant, or that the plant is trying to protect itself from hot, dry conditions. Providing shade and controlling pests early keeps the leaves open and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ miitutua tso lɛ. Aloo etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitao ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ he. Mra be mli hulutsoo kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ mli tseɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it better for me to water my crops early in the morning or in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because it allows the crop roots to drink before the sun gets hot. Afternoon watering leaves foliage wet overnight, which encourages crop diseases and mildews to spread.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ shwane mli lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ woɔ tsei ahe helai kɛ downy mildew hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and look dead during hot afternoons even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egboi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: During very hot hours, crops lose water from their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the soil. They wilt temporarily to protect themselves from burning, but they usually perk up again by evening as the air cools.
ga: Yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, Dumɔwui fiteɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagboi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he. Shi amɛfɔɔ shitee ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: If maize seeds are planted too closely, the plants end up fighting each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. This causes thin, weak stalks that yield tiny cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei wuɔ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ loo amɛwoɔ ŋmeii kwraa lɛ baa.

english: Why do some farmers plant cowpeas or beans inside the same farm with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ ŋmãa duɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special crops that capture nitrogen food from the air and put it into the soil. Planting them with maize naturally feeds the maize and gives you two different food harvests from the same piece of land.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen nibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli abele duɔ lɛ haa abele lɛ niyenii ni ehaa onine shɛɔ niyenii srɔtoi enyɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why must I remove weeds while my crops are still small instead of waiting until they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ moŋ fe ni mamɛ ni etsɔ agbo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and steal their sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your young crops get all the food they need to grow strong enough to withstand pests.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei bibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid on maize leaves by moths. They hide in the central funnel of the plant to eat the soft leaves, so treating the central leaf funnel early protects the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ ŋmãa baa nɔ lɛ amli. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, atsaa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tsɔne lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow taller and produce fruit faster inside a greenhouse compared to my open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ akɛto miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ he lɛ?

english: Inside a greenhouse, plants are shielded from harsh wind, heavy rain, and direct pest attacks. The controlled environment keeps warmth and humidity steady, allowing the crops to use all their energy for growing and producing fruit quickly.
ga: Yɛ greenhouse lɛ mli lɛ Abuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ahe. Shihilɛ ni akudɔɔ lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi daa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii oya.

english: Why are my vegetables wilting inside the greenhouse during the hot afternoon even after I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho yɛ greenhouse lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa mli beni awo amɛ nu po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Greenhouses trap heat easily. If the structure does not have proper ventilation or shading, the temperature inside gets too high for the plants, causing them to lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can pull water from the soil.
ga: Greenhouses lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ oya. Kɛji akɛ tsũ lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo hulutsoo ni sa lɛ, Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baafee nɔ ni nɔ kwɔ tsɔ kɛha tso lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some greenhouse structures build up too much heat and ruin crops in Ghana while others work well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsũi komɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa hulutsoo fe nine baa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ Ghana lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni greenhouse tsɔnei komɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ,.

english: Because Ghana has a hot climate, greenhouse designs must have high ceilings and side vents to let hot air escape. Low or completely sealed designs trap hot air inside, which heat-stresses the crops instead of protecting them.
ga: Ejaakɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa. No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni afee greenhouse lɛ aha lɛ biɔ ni atswa ŋwɛitsu ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ sɛɛgbɛ ŋwɛitsu koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ anyɛ ajɛ mli. Nɔ ni afee ni aŋã loo eba shi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo haomɔ baa tso lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cucumber plants produce flowers but no fruits inside a closed farm structure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kukumba tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo aduawai yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni agbe naa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Most crops need insects like bees to carry pollen from flower to flower so fruit can form. Inside a covered greenhouse, bees cannot enter, so you must either use special self-pollinating seeds or gently shake the plants to help pollen spread.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ pii biɔ ni koolooi, tamɔ wuobii, aŋɔ pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ koni aduawai aba. Yɛ greenhouse ni aha nɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii nyɛŋ abote mli No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi ni haa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii loo okɛ tso lɛ akpokpo blɛoo. Koni eye ebua ni egbɛ pollen lɛ eshwa

english: How do I know if the fertilizer or chemicals I buy for my crops are good quality?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni miheɔ kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good quality fertilizers dissolve smoothly in water without leaving thick dirt at the bottom, come in properly sealed bags with clear label instructions, and are purchased from registered agricultural dealers rather than unverified sellers.
ga: Nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu mli ni eshiuuu muji ni mli edɔ yɛ shishigbɛ. Okɛwo kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa jogbaŋŋ ni gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli. kɛ nihɔɔmɔ kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ Yɛ nihɔɔlɔ ni akwɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my crops turn yellow after using cheap fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara waaa tsu nii?

english: Low-quality or improper fertilizer mixes can burn delicate plant roots or alter the soil's balance, preventing the crop from absorbing essential nutrients like nitrogen, which causes the leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni ehiii loo ni akɛfutuɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ loo etsake bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛhe niyenii ni he hia tamɔ nitrogen, ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛ gboiɔ.

english: Why is feeding crops through drip water pipes better than spreading solid fertilizer on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akɛ niyenii haa kɛtsɔ hose ni hoɔ nu mli lɛ nɔ lɛ hi fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni akɛaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Liquid plant food mixed into drip irrigation delivers small, precise amounts of nutrients directly to the roots along with water. The plant absorbs it immediately without waiting for rain to break down dry fertilizer pellets.
ga: Tso niyenii ni ji nu ni akɛfutuɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii bibii ni ja pɛpɛɛpɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛfataa nu he. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛmɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ koni ekɛgbala ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ amli.

english: Why is it necessary to test my borehole water before using it to water greenhouse crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aka nu ni yɔɔ nubu ko mli lɛ akwɛ dani akɛtsu nii kɛwo tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nu lɛ?

english: Water containing high amounts of salt, iron, or bad chemicals can clog small drip irrigation pipes and build up in the soil, eventually poisoning delicate crop roots and stunting their growth.
ga: Nu ni ŋoo, dade, loo tsofai krokomɛi ni ehiii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ paipii ni akɛshwieɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ amli lɛ naa. ni ebua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ naagbee ni ehaa amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why are my crops still getting sick with pests even though they are inside a covered structure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hela lolo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai eyɛ mli akɛ amɛyɛ tsũ ko ni akɛha nɔ ko mli moŋ?

english: Tiny insects and fungal spores can easily enter on a farmer's clothes, shoes, or tools, or through dirty soil brought from outside. Once inside, the warm greenhouse environment helps the pests multiply rapidly if strict sanitation is not maintained.
ga: Kplukai bibii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ abote okwaafonyo atadei, tokotai loo nitsumɔ dadei amli mlɛo. aloo kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji ni akɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ kɛba lɛ nɔ Kɛji ebote mli pɛ Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaye abua ni kooloi ni yeɔ wala lɛ aya hiɛ oya. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ hetsemɔ ni mli wa nɔ

english: Why are my crops failing even though I spent a lot of money installing a modern farming system?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifite eyɛ mli akɛ mifite shika babaoo kɛwo ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛjianɔtoo ko mli moŋ?

english: Expensive equipment alone cannot guarantee a good yield. Crops require daily monitoring, correct watering schedules, and proper feeding, which require practical training and experience in managing the specific system you are using.
ga: Nibii ni jara wa pɛ nyɛŋ aha yibiiwoo kpakpa aba. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ mli daa gbi. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni ja kɛ niyenii ni sa Enɛ biɔ tsɔsemɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii kɛ niiashikpamɔ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo pɔtɛɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ mli.

english: Can cocoa trees grow successfully on land that was previously dug up for illegal mining?
ga: Ani cacao tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ ajie kɛha shika tsuru ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, but the land needs restoration first. Mining strips away the fertile topsoil and damages the soil structure, so you must add compost, poultry manure, or plant cover crops to rebuild nutrients before replanting cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ehe miihia ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dã. Shikpɔŋ ni atsaa lɛ jieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni ekɛsaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ dani okɛ kookoo hee adu.

english: Why are my newly planted cocoa seedlings dying after I cleared and dug up the top layer of my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ gboi beni mifo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mifo mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Deep digging removes the nutrient-rich topsoil where plant roots feed. Without topsoil, young cocoa roots cannot access essential plant food or hold enough moisture, causing the seedlings to dry up and die.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ jieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli ni tsei shishifãi yeɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ bɛ lɛ, kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ naaa tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How long does a new cocoa tree take to start producing pods after being replanted?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tsei heei jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii beni adu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties take about 3 to 5 years to bear fruit, while improved hybrid varieties can start producing pods in 2 to 3 years if given proper shade, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi amli kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani ewoɔ yibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hybrid cocoa henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔtɔi feemɔ yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji amɛná hulutsoo, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa.

english: What can I add to damaged soil to help my young crops recover and grow strong?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛfata shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ he koni eye ebua mitsei bibii lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛdara waa?

english: Adding organic matter such as well-rotted chicken manure, compost, or cocoa pod husks helps rebuild soil structure. Planting leguminous cover crops like Mucuna also helps fix natural nitrogen back into degraded soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ tsina ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ekoŋŋ. Legume ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ Mucuna lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa plants turn yellow and burn when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to strong sunlight and heat. Without shade trees or food crops like plantain to block direct sun, their leaves burn and cannot produce the energy the plant needs to grow.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains bɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Amɛbaai lɛ shãa ni amɛnyɛɛɛ amɛha hewalɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni eda.

english: Are there quick crops I can grow alongside new cocoa trees to earn money while waiting for the cocoa to mature?
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ oya yɛ ni manyɛ madu yɛ kookoo tsei heei komɛi ahe. Koni oná shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Yes, you can intercrop with plantains, cassava, or maize. Plantains provide vital shade for the young cocoa trees, while crops like maize and vegetables harvest quickly to give you early income.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ plantains, ŋmei loo ŋmei akwɛ tsei. Plantains haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa. Yɛ be mli ni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ aduawai oya koni eha oná shika oya.

english: Why does rain water collect on top of my cleared farm instead of sinking into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeefo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy digging and movement on the land compact the subsoil into a hard layer. You need to break up this hard layer with a pickaxe or hoe and mix in organic manure so water can drain freely to plant roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni atsaa kɛyaa he kroko lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa. Esa akɛ okɛ spade loo shɔvel akumɔ nɛkɛ fã ni wa nɛɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ afutu mli koni nu lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli oya kɛya tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: If old cocoa trees were completely uprooted from my farm, can I plant new seedlings in the exact same holes?
ga: Kɛji ajie kookoo tsei momo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwu hee yɛ bu kome mli?

english: It is best to dig fresh holes slightly away from old ones. Fill the new holes with fresh topsoil mixed with compost so the young roots can spread easily without struggling in compacted, depleted root zones.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsa bu hee ni kɛ bu momo lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo. Okɛ sũ hee ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii efutu mli lɛ awo bu hee lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni amɛkafee nɔ ko yɛ shishifãi ni eyi obɔ kɛ hei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds grow very fast on my cleared land, but my cocoa seedlings struggle to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikwɛ̃ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni nɔ ewo muji lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara.

english: Weeds have wild, hardy root systems adapted to poor and disturbed soils. Cocoa seedlings have sensitive feeder roots that require shade, consistent moisture, and rich organic topsoil to compete against wild weeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni efite lɛ nɔ. Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni biɔ hulutsoo. hulutsoo ni tamɔ amɛhe kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baaha ekɛ koo mli jwɛi lɛ abɔ he akaŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland is safe enough for crops after chemical digging activity happened near it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii? Beni tsofai ni akɛtsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ba yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Look for natural signs like healthy weed growth and earthworms in the soil. If the soil smells unusual, appears greasy, or crops refuse to germinate, ask an extension officer to test the soil safety before planting.
ga: Taomɔ adebɔɔ mli okadii, tamɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ srɔto, etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ fɔ, loo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpoo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ Bi extension officials lɛ ni amɛka shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe shihilɛ amɛkwɛ dani amɛdu.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when planted in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and small roots that cannot handle full, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a living canopy that protects the cocoa from heat and keeps the soil moist until the trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ latsaa he lɛ baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers from an old farm to start my new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Select 'sword suckers'—these are young shoots with broad bases and narrow, sword-like leaves. They carry strong energy from the main root system and grow faster into high-yielding plantain trees compared to broad-leafed 'water suckers'.
ga: Halamɔ ‘klante tso’, ni ji tso bibioo ko ni shishigbɛ lɛ mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ klante. Amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ ni mli wa kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛdaraa oya kɛfeɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto 'nu mli tsei' ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing starting at the tip and moving down the middle of lower maize leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Maize requires plenty of nitrogen to build healthy leaves, so applying compost, manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will restore green growth.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyaa shi yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni eha baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my corn leaves and green waste inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ jwɛi eŋɔli ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing funnel of the maize plant. Catching them early and applying targeted treatments, such as neem seed extract or approved sprays, stops them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ agbɛi lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra ni okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii tamɔ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Ehaa amɛkafiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why does paddy rice grow much better when there is standing water on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ be mli ni nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Standing water suffocates weeds that would otherwise compete with rice for light and fertilizer, while keeping soil temperatures even and nutrients easily accessible to the rice roots.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi ni baanyɛ atswa akaŋ kɛha la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ yaa nɔ daa, ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ ahe oya.

english: Why do I need to heap soil into high mounds before planting yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ sũ ni nɔ kwɔ ato dani odu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yam tubers grow straight down and need loose, soft soil to expand without obstruction. Mounds also protect the seed tubers from rotting in waterlogged soil during heavy rains and make harvesting easier.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa jaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia amɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ. Gɔŋ lɛ hu buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo

english: Which direction should the buds point when I cut cassava stems for planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oofo ŋmei tso ko koni odu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmei lɛ atsɔɔ?

english: Always plant cassava stem cuttings with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes shoots to grow downwards first, weakening the plant and delaying growth.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, dumɔ ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ. Ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa edalɛ baa shi.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my maize improve the soil for next season?
ga: Te ŋmei ni mikɛ mi ŋmei lɛ baadu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the plant roots decay, this nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as free natural fertilizer for crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi amli. Kɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ fite Nitrogen nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when plants experience stress from intense heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Giving plants consistent water and shade during peak afternoon heat helps flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa tsei yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward to reduce water loss during hot, dry periods, or as a response to whiteflies spreading leaf curl viruses. Keeping soil moist through mulching and controlling whiteflies keeps leaves healthy.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ mli koni nu ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Aloo eji hetoo ni akɛhaa ŋmeii yɛŋ ni gbɛɔ leaf curl hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ whitefly nɔyeli nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. As the plant grows, it pulls nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed new upper growth, signaling that your soil needs nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Beni tsei lɛ daraa Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: How can I tell if my field's soil has lost its strength and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your crops are growing very slowly, look pale green instead of dark green, and produce smaller harvests than in past years despite getting enough rain, your soil has run low on key nutrients.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo waa Ha efee tamɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo fe afii ni eho lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Shi niyenii titrii ni he hiaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sun. Planting shade crops like plantains or cassava next to cocoa seedlings creates a protective canopy that keeps them cool and retains soil moisture until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ cocoa dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhaa amɛhe jɔɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds very close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete with one another for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. This results in thin, weak stalks with small or poorly filled ears of corn.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii loo ni ehiɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to spread their leaves to catch as much sunlight as possible to grow big tubers under the ground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, reducing diseases and helping the plant produce energy faster.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa helai baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when we get heavy rain for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. When rain leaves standing water in the field for too long, the roots drown and rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu hiɔ ŋmɔji amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ gbee shi ni amɛgboi. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli.

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plant roots can soak up moisture before the heat of the day. Watering in the hot afternoon causes much of the water to evaporate into the air before the plant can use it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi maŋkpa koni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aba. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛtsu nii.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by extreme afternoon heat, uneven watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Maintaining consistent moisture around the roots can help keep the flowers on the plant.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ hao amɛ yɛ shwane mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ yeɔ egbɔ lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Holes in the center leaves of young corn are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide deep inside the growing leaf funnel during the day and feed on the soft leaf tissues.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ amli fãji.

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal the nutrients, water, and root space meant for your crops. Even with good rain, crops suffer if weeds are taking their food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi Dumɔwui hu naa amanehulu kɛji jwɛi ye amɛ niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the exact time of year I should start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ maje midumɔwui lɛ ashishi?
