english: Planting timing depends on the main rainy season in your region of Ghana, usually starting around March or April in the south. Planting right after the first steady rains ensures your seeds get enough moisture to sprout and establish strong roots.
ga: Be ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ damɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri ni yɔɔ nyɛ Ghana kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ejeɔ shishi yɛ March loo April aaafee yɛ anaigbɛ. Kɛ́ odu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa odumɔwui lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why is March often recommended for starting the major planting season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, ajieɔ March yi akɛ eji ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be titri lɛ shishijee yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: March marks the beginning of the early rainy season in many southern and central parts of Ghana. Planting in March helps fast-growing crops like maize take advantage of early rainfall before mid-year dry spells set in.
ga: March ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee yɛ Ghana wuoyigbɛ kɛ teŋgbɛ. Dumɔ yɛ March mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ ŋmãa, náa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ he sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ afi lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: What will happen to my seeds if I plant them in March but the rain delays for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni baa midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ March mli ni nugbɔ lɛ ha amɛba sɛɛ otsii fioo komɛi?

english: If seeds sit in hot, dry soil without follow-up rain, they can fail to germinate, dry up, or get eaten by birds and insects. It is usually best to wait until the ground has received a few reliable heavy rains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃, amɛgbi, loo okpoi kɛ koolooi baaye amɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ.

english: Why do I need to prepare my seeds and chemicals weeks before the planting season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masaa dumɔwui kɛ tsofai otsii babaoo dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Having your inputs ready early prevents late planting. If the rains start and you are still searching for seeds or chemicals, your crops will miss the best soil moisture and grow weaker.
ga: Nibii ni haa anáa nii lɛ ahe saamɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akadu nii yɛ sɛɛ mli. Kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ni otaoɔ dumɔwui loo tsofai lolo. Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ.

english: What do agriculture workers mean when they talk about crop 'medicines', and why do my plants need them?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni okwaayeli nitsulɔi tsɔɔ kɛ amɛmiiwie ŋmɔshi nibii ‘tsofa’ he ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi tsei lɛ?

english: Crop 'medicines' refer to agrochemicals like fertilizers, pesticides, and weedicides. Fertilizers feed nutrients to the crop, while pesticides and fungicides protect plants from insects, weeds, and diseases that steal your yield.
ga: Tso "tsofa" tsɔɔ okwaayeli tsofai tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi, kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi, jwɛi, kɛ helai ni juɔ onibii lɛ ahe.

english: Should I apply farm medicines before planting or after my crops start growing?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu loo beni tsei lɛ ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ?

english: It depends on the product. Weed killers are often applied during land preparation before planting, whereas fertilizers and pest control sprays are applied after seeds germinate and reach specific stages of growth.
ga: Edamɔ nibii ni afee lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi tsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani aduɔ nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ woɔ mli beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni amɛshɛ he ko ni amɛdara lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can applying too much crop medicine or spray harm my plants instead of helping them?
ga: Ani tsofa loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye mitsei lɛ awui moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ?

english: Yes, using too much chemical or spraying at the wrong strength can burn plant leaves, damage roots, and reduce yield. Always apply the correct dosage recommended for your specific crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã, shishifãi lɛ afite, ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi. Kɛ yibɔ ni sa ni atsɔɔ kɛha onibii pɔtɛɛ lɛ atsu nii be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale yellow even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant lacks nutrients, especially nitrogen, or that pests are damaging the roots. Applying the right fertilizer or pest treatment helps restore deep green, healthy leaf growth.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai. titri lɛ nitrogen loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miifite shishifãi lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ aku sɛɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I buy certified seeds instead of using seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mihe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Certified seeds are specifically selected to resist common diseases, survive short dry spells, and produce bigger yields. Seeds saved from past harvests slowly lose these strengths over time.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Ebaanyɛ ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli. ni amɛwo babaoo Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Nɛkɛ hewalɛi nɛɛ laajeɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I tell if my plants are struggling because of pests or because they lack water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahewɔ loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ mitso lɛ miitswa lɛ?

english: Drought-stressed plants droop or curl during hot hours but recover slightly at night. Pest-damaged plants show visible signs like eaten leaves, holes, sticky fluid, or bugs living under the leaves even when the ground is wet.
ga: Tsei ni hɔmɔ emɔ amɛ lɛ baagbee shi loo amɛbaabɔle amɛhe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Shi ehiɛ baa shi fioo gbɛkɛ. Tsei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai efite lɛ baajie okadii ni anaa tamɔ baai ni aye, bu, nu ni shwieɔ shi. Aloo kooloi bibii ni hiɔ baai ashishi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why are my maize yields getting smaller every year even though I put in the same hard work on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ miiba shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii waa nakai nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the soil every time you harvest. If you grow the same crop year after year without replacing those nutrients or letting the soil rest, the land becomes exhausted, leading to smaller harvests despite your physical effort.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa amɛ. Kɛji odu tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni otsakeee nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaho. Nɔ ni jɛɔ enɛ mli baa ji nikpamɔ bibioo kɛji akɛ okɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo tsu nii po.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and stop growing after just a few months in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo pɛ ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal that the crop is starving for vital soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is too hard and poorly drained for the roots to breathe and feed properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ yɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ sũ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni nu shwieee shi jogbaŋŋ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amɛmu ni amɛye niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct sunlight and intense heat. They need fast-growing shade crops like plantains planted beside them to act as living umbrellas, keeping the air cool and soil moist until the cocoa roots mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiisumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any fruit develops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat or erratic watering. This is the plant's natural self-defense mechanism to save energy when it feels too stressed to support growing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni ejaaa mli. Enɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ he beni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my main crop help the soil and plants grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and other legumes have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the earth. This naturally fertilizes the surrounding soil and feeds neighbor crops without extra effort.
ga: Peanuts kɛ legumes krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii ni mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kroko fataaa he.

english: How does rotating the crops I plant on my land keep my field healthy over time?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mikɛtsakeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔji lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Different crops take and give different nutrients to the soil, while also disrupting pest populations. Switching crops each season prevents soil depletion and stops crop-specific pests from building up in the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi heɔ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ ni amɛhaa lɛ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, egbaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ hu anaa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is there a cover crop I can plant to stop weeds from taking over my field so I don't burn out weeding manually?
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa miŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ yɛ ni manyɛ madu koni jwɛi akaye miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ. Bɔni afee ni mikɛ mihe akawo jwɛi mli?

english: Planting cover crops like Mucuna or cowpeas spreads a dense carpet over the ground. This blocks light from weed seeds so they cannot sprout, saving you from constant clearing and weeding by hand.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ Mucuna loo cowpeas ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ kapɛti ni mli edɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ la ni jɛɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Ehereɔ bo kɛjɛɔ nine ni okɛbaatsu nii kɛjie jwɛi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops wilt so quickly during short dry spells even when it rained heavily a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ waa gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ moŋ.

english: Bare soil loses moisture rapidly to the sun through evaporation. Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves creates mulch, which holds water in the soil much longer after a rainfall.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛyaa hulu lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Mulching ni okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi baabɔle Oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baaha afee mulch. ni haa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ

english: Why are my older oil palm trees producing smaller fruit bunches compared to when they were younger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso ni egbɔ lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: As palm trees grow taller, they require larger amounts of nutrients to transport food all the way up. Without adequate fertilizer, light access, and regular pruning of old fronds, the tree produces smaller bunches to conserve strength.
ga: Beni ŋmei tso lɛ da lɛ Amɛmiitao niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛkɛ amɛ niyenii lɛ aya ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni akɛbaashɛ la he kɛ fern tsei niji momo lɛ ahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ daa lɛ Tso lɛ baawo ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. koni ehiɛ hewalɛ mli

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so fast in the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot quickly if they suffer small cuts during harvest or are kept in warm, stagnant air. Proper handling, curing the skin in the shade, and storing tubers on raised, well-ventilated racks stops rot fungi from attacking.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ amɛ fioo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ shi. Nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa Hewolo lɛ tsamɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ni akɛtoɔ shĩa ni nɔ kwɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni akatutua rot fungus lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, giving the cocoa seedlings the necessary shade and soil moisture to survive their first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings rot and die when I stick them upside down in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava niji lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems have small growth buds that must point upward. Planting them upside down forces the new roots and shoots to grow in the wrong direction, causing the plant to burn its energy under the soil and rot.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi Dumɔ ni akɛ ŋwɛi shishi lɛ baaha shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shãa hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy for the plant. Staking holds the leaves up off the dark ground, allowing them to catch maximum sunlight, which results in bigger and healthier yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba tso lɛ nɔ. Staking hiɛɔ baai lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ nɔ. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to grow leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer around the roots will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the daytime heat gets too intense or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet. Providing regular watering and light shade during extremely hot weeks helps the flowers stay on to produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the sap from under the leaves. Spraying the plants with soapy water or neem oil can clear these pests and let healthy leaves grow back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ. ni eha baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves become soft and droopy during the hot afternoon sun even when the dirt is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In the hot afternoon, cabbage leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can drink it up. Wilting is the plant's natural way of resting to save water, and the leaves usually firm back up once the cool evening arrives.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Cabbage baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Withering ji tso adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejɔɔ ehe koni ekɛbu nu he. Ni baai lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛfee ais ekoŋŋ kɛ́ gbɛkɛ shɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajie midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and food from the mother plant. Removing the weak ones and leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant produces a thick stem and a heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ ashishifãi ni mli tse kɛ plantains babaoo.

english: Why do my tall maize stalks fall flat on the ground whenever strong rain and winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ lɛ? Ani minɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa?

english: Maize falls over when its roots are shallow or when the base of the stem is weak. Heap soil high around the bottom of the maize stalks when they are knee-high to build a sturdy anchor against strong wind and rain.
ga: Abele baagbee shi kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli ejɔ. Okɛ sũ lɛ abɔle ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ he beni amɛshɛɔ aaafee amɛnaji ahe lɛ koni efee ŋmãa ni wa ni baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ naa.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it inside their roots. When the crop is harvested and its roots rot in the ground, that stored nitrogen stays in the dirt as natural food for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight and high soil temperatures. Tall shade trees or quick-growing plants like plantains act as natural umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist while protecting young cocoa leaves from scorching until the trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ naa. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashi tso lɛ daa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually indicates that the soil is running out of nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to grow leaves and stems. The plant moves nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed newer upper growth, signaling that it needs compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miiho. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni afee ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my field make my maize grow better in the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special microscopic organisms in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil. This naturally enriches the soil with plant food for the next crop planted in that spot.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shweremɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ tsei niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni adu yɛ nakai he lɛ.

english: Does it matter which way up I insert cassava stem cuttings into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ, ani akɛ ŋmei niji lɛ baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ko nɔ loo akɛwooo mli?

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the small bud nodes pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the stems to grow downward into the soil before turning up, weakening the plant and drastically reducing tuber yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani efoɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why is it bad to plant my crop seeds very close together in a dense cluster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ kui ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants compete heavily with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing plants properly gives each root system enough room to gather nourishment so the plants produce larger fruits and tubers.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ hulu la he akaŋ waa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ Niyenii kɛ Nu Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa shishifãi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbua niyenii mli hewalɛ naa. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ awo yibii wuji kɛ bulbs.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with wooden stakes instead of letting them spread flat on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei ni akɛfee tsei lɛ afi mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high off the hot ground into sunlight and fresh air, allowing the leaves to make maximum food for the plant while preventing leaf decay caused by direct soil contact and humidity.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii kwraa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ baai ni fiteɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛkpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli baa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without producing any fruits during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat combined with dry air causes severe stress to tomato plants, causing their pollen to dry out so flowers fail to form fruit. Providing light shade and regular watering keeps the plant cool enough to set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni fata kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ he lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa tomato tsei amli muji lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo yibii. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do black patches spread so quickly on my cocoa pods during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains create moist, humid conditions that encourage fungal organisms, like black pod disease, to multiply rapidly. Water droplets splashing off infected pods easily carry these fungal spores to healthy pods across the field.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii tamɔ black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Nu ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmeii nɛɛ aya ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and making the plants stunt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni eha tso lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these pests early stops the curling and restores healthy plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ nibii lɛ ni amɛnuɔ kɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ekpaa ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce smaller yields even if I water my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are often stronger than cultivated crops, so they actively steal nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your crops, leaving the crop plants starving despite regular watering.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni bei pii lɛ amɛhe wa fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji akɛ afɔ amɛ nu daa po.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make leaves green and healthy. It can also happen when the ground stays waterlogged for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is extremely hot or when the soil dries out completely while the plant is blooming. Giving the plants consistent water helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi be mli ni tso lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ha tso lɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my cassava roots are ready for harvesting under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause so much damage to my crops if they are all just plants growing in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miifite miŋmɔshi nii babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ ji amɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than regular crops and aggressively steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your crops, which starves your main harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ daa lɛ ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ waa. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye okpamɔ titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Ragged holes inside the growing leaves of maize are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the center whorl of the plant and eat the tender leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmeii baai ni miida lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Why is it bad to apply fertilizer right on top of dry soil during the heat of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaawo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve into the ground where roots can reach it. Applying it on hot, dry soil causes the fertilizer nutrients to evaporate into the air or burn the plant roots.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo eshã tsei shishifãi.

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and food from the soil, while also allowing air to flow between plants to prevent fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden early in the morning or in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil can absorb the water before the hot afternoon sun causes it to evaporate, giving the plants strength for the day.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ aha etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli

english: Why do my tomato plants grow lots of thick leaves but produce very few tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baa lɛ mli tse waa shi tomato fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes tomato plants focus all their energy on producing green leaves instead of flowers and fruits. Switching to a balanced fertilizer richer in phosphorus helps the plant produce more flowers and yield more fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tomato tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai eŋɔli ni amɛbaafee lɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo kɛ aduawai babaoo.

english: What makes some tomato plants grow tall like vines while others stay short like bushes?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato tsei komɛi daa tamɔ wain tsei? Yɛ be mli ni tomato tsei komɛi yɛ kuku tamɔ jwɛi lɛ?

english: Tomatoes naturally come in two main types: bush varieties (determinate) that grow to a set size and produce all their fruit at once, and vining varieties (indeterminate) that continue growing tall and producing fruit over a longer period.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, tomato henɔi titrii enyɔ yɔɔ: shrubby (determinate) henɔi ni daa kɛyashɛɔ dalɛ pɔtɛɛ ko mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii shikome; kɛ wain tsei srɔtoi (ni aleee) ni baada ni amɛwo yibii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellow and curling leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like whiteflies are attacking the plant or spreading a virus. Treating the crop early with safe pesticides or insecticidal soaps can protect your plants.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ koolooi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, miitutua tso lɛ loo amɛmii gbɛ hela ko amɛshwã. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ abu otsei lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather becomes extremely hot, when soil dries out, or if the plant lacks nutrients. Ensuring regular watering during hot days helps the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa, be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi, loo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and soft while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo beni edara lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often made worse by irregular watering. Watering your farm consistently and adding calcium or lime to the soil prevents this rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ mli baa Ni bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa hela lɛ he okadii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ehiii kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Okɛ nu awo oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ calcium loo lime awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekafite.

english: What causes my tomatoes to crack open while they are still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato mli gbalaa be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they suddenly take in too much water after a long dry spell, causing the inside to grow faster than the skin. Keeping soil moisture steady with regular watering prevents skin cracking.
ga: Tomato baatswa trukaa. Amɛnáa nu babaoo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Ehaa tomato daa oya fe hewolo lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akagbala.

english: Why do my tomato plants need much more water once they start producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa mi tomato tsei lɛ beni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Tomato fruits are made mostly of water. Once the plant sets fruit, it pumps large amounts of water and nutrients into them to make the tomatoes plump, juicy, and healthy.
ga: Nu ji nɔ ni akɛfeɔ tomato babaoo. Kɛ tso lɛ wo yibii Ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo woɔ mli koni eha tomato lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Will planting tomatoes on the exact same piece of land every year affect my harvest?
ga: Ani tomato ni miduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ baaná mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, planting tomatoes in the same soil repeatedly allows crop-specific diseases and pests to build up in the soil. Rotating tomatoes with crops like maize or beans keeps the soil healthy and protects your harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, tomato ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ. Ebaaha helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ tsei anɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake tomato. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebuɔ onibii ahe.

english: Why do extension officers recommend tying my tomato plants to wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ tomato tsei akpɛtɛ tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Staking keeps stems upright so heavy tomatoes don't rest on wet soil, which prevents rot, soil-borne diseases, and pest damage while making harvesting much easier.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ damɔɔ shi bɔni afee ni tomato ni tsii lɛ akajɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite. helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ nibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to pick my tomatoes so they don't spoil before selling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa tomato koni ekafite dani ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Tomatoes are ready for market when they change from solid green to a light pink or reddish tint. Harvesting them at this 'mature green' or early pink stage allows them to ripen fully without getting damaged during transport.
ga: Tomato efee klalo kɛha jarayeli kɛji ejɛ eŋɔli ni mli wa mli kɛtee pinki loo etsuru ni mli tse mli. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ yɛ ‘eŋɔli’ loo mra be mli pinki mli lɛ, ehaa amɛshwereɔ kwraa ni amɛfiteee yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ.

english: Why should I clear my land without burning the grass before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oshãaa jwɛi lɛ dani odu nii lɛ?

english: Clearing without burning allows organic plant matter to decay naturally into the soil. Burning destroys vital soil nutrients, kills beneficial micro-organisms, and leaves the soil exposed to dry out quickly under the sun.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ashãaa lɛ, ehaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fãa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekpãtãa nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya yɛ hulu lɛ shishi.

english: Why will my maize produce smaller cobs if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛji midu ŋmeii lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete heavily with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to build strong stalks and full ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ hulu la he akaŋ waa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmãa toi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thin leaves when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai bibii kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava requires direct sunlight to convert light into food and store energy in its underground roots. Under heavy shade, the plant uses all its energy stretching upward toward the light instead of developing large tubers.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛtsake la lɛ ewo niyenii mli ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. shishi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ni ekpãa kɛyaa la lɛ he lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee tsɔnei wuji.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during hot afternoons as a natural defense mechanism to reduce moisture loss. If the leaves stay curled or turn yellow, it indicates heat stress or irregular watering.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ mli yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni haa fɛ̃i ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi. Kɛji baai lɛ ebɔle loo etsɔ ŋmɔŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell. If you plant too early, the young seedlings will germinate but quickly dry up and die from lack of continuous soil moisture before the main rains settle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi oya ni amɛbaagboi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ ehiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ baa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: How do I know if my farmland needs animal manure before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ashikpɔŋ ni miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia dani adu nii?

english: If your previous crops grew slowly, had pale yellow leaves, or if the soil feels very hard and sandy, adding manure or compost restores missing nutrients and helps the soil retain water.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ dara blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ewa ni eyɛ ŋã babaoo Kɛ́ akɛ ŋã loo ŋã fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nu mli.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crops right after I apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that absorb nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds before applying fertilizer ensures your crops get the food rather than feeding the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ dani awoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa anáa niyenii yɛ jwɛi lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cassava on the same piece of land three seasons in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ bei etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava heavy feeds on soil nutrients each season. Planting it repeatedly without rotating crops depletes the soil and allows cassava-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Cassava yeɔ niyenii mli nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ daa afi. Nibii ni aduɔ shii abɔ ni atsakeee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off the lower branches of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɛ bo akɛ ofolɔ kookoo tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning lower branches improves airflow and allows sunlight to reach the lower trunk. This keeps the tree dry and prevents fungal diseases like black pod from spreading in damp shade.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ agbɛ ashwã hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and curling up across my whole farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava Mosaic Disease is caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. It moves quickly from plant to plant, so removing infected plants early stops the sickness from spreading to the rest of your field.
ga: Virus ko ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ kɛ Cassava mosaic hela baa. Efãa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa hei krokomɛi. yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, wet conditions and damp air. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air to dry the pods, which prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Blɔfo hela jɛɔ ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ fɛ̃i. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are my tomato plants suddenly wilting and dying even when the soil is completely wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kwraa moŋ lɛ?

english: Soil bacteria or tiny worms called nematodes can attack the root system and block the plant's internal water tubes, causing the plant to starve for water even when the ground is damp.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ atutua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛtsi tso lɛ mli nu paipii lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa nu shwieɔ tsei amli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Maize plants roll their leaves when the sun is very hot to trap moisture inside and stop water from evaporating too fast. It is the plant's natural way of saving itself from drying out.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu lɛ miitso koni ekɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehereɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ mli.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die when I clear away all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Taller shade trees or plantain plants act like living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the cool shade and moisture it needs to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space ensures it gets enough food to produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly on my field even after I spend days clearing them by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikwɛ̃ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ miniji shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ gbii babaoo moŋ.

english: Weed seeds lie hidden in the soil and sprout whenever rain and sunlight hit the open ground. Planting cover crops like leguminous vines shades the ground and stops weed seeds from receiving the light they need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni hulu la baashɛ he ni atse lɛ. Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ legume wain ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ aná la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops yield less food when I plant the exact same crop on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naaa niyenii babaoo beni miduɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Every crop pulls specific nutrients out of the soil. Planting the same crop repeatedly drains those exact nutrients, so rotating different crops gives the soil a chance to rest and rebuild its strength.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ komɛi afite. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa hegbɛ ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ ehewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees take several years before they start producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees must build a deep root system and strong trunk before they can support heavy pods. The tree focuses all its initial energy on becoming strong enough to survive and bear fruit for decades.
ga: Esa akɛ cacao tsei lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ maa amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ nɔ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer off the soil surface or pushes it too deep into the ground before the roots can drink it up, wasting your money and effort.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Eji shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ fitemɔ.

english: Why are my crops producing poor yields even though I am working just as hard on my farm as I used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Crop yields do not depend only on your hard work; they depend heavily on the health of your land and changing weather patterns. Over time, soil loses its nutrients, so understanding your soil's current condition is key to bringing back good harvests.
ga: Jeee nitsumɔ ni wa ni otsuɔ lɛ pɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ damɔ. Amɛdamɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ waa. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Sũ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baafite. No hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ shishinumɔ ji nɔ titri ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai aku sɛɛ aba.

english: What does it mean to get my farm soil tested, and why should I do it?
ga: Mɛni shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa ni afeɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee nakai?

english: Soil testing is like taking your land to a doctor for a health checkup. It reveals what nutrients your soil is missing so you know exactly how to treat it and help your crops grow strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa tamɔ okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ yaa datrɛfonyo ŋɔɔ koni ekwɛ mli. Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpo. No hewɔ lɛ ole bɔ ni ooofee okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ ni oye obua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How often am I supposed to test the soil on my farm?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ maka shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ?

english: It is good practice to test your soil before every new cropping season. Soil nutrients change after each harvest, so testing regularly ensures your land is ready for the next crop.
ga: Eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ oooka oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii heei fɛɛ aba. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii tsakeɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kaa ni ooofee daa lɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the rainy seasons on my farm becoming so unpredictable compared to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: The climate is constantly changing and developing over time, leading to unexpected changes in rainfall and temperature. Farmers must monitor these shifts and adjust their planting schedules and soil care accordingly.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ miitsake ni eetsake be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ latsaa tsakemɔi ni akpaaa gbɛ baa. Esa akɛ okwaafoi akwɛ tsakemɔi nɛɛ anɔ ni amɛtsake amɛdumɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli yɛ nakai gbɛ nɔ.

english: Why do crops grow very well on one part of my field but struggle on another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli shi amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ fã kroko lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soil quality is not uniform across an entire farm. Different spots in your field can have different nutrient levels or soil conditions, which is why testing soil from various parts of your land is helpful.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su lɛ jeee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ muu fɛɛ mli. Hei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛi srɔtoi. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni no hewɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hei srɔtoi lɛ akaa lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ

english: How do I take a soil sample from my farm to give to an extension officer for testing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maŋɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni extension nitsulɔ aka lɛ akwɛ?

english: You dig up small amounts of soil from several spots across your planting field, clear away surface weeds, mix the collected soil together, and bring a small bag of that mixture for testing.
ga: Ofoɔ shikpɔŋ bibii kɛjɛɔ hei srɔtoi yɛ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ fɛɛ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Okɛ shikpɔŋ ni abua naa lɛ afutu mli. ni okɛ nɔ ni akɛfutu lɛ awo kotoku bibioo ko mli koni oka lɛ okwɛ

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow even when I irrigate them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa tso lɛ daa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean the soil is lacking essential plant nutrients or that the land has become too acidic. Checking your soil's health will tell you which specific nutrient your crops are missing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tso lɛ loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsɔɔ bo niyenii ni haa otsei lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Can the weather changing over time permanently affect how my crops behave?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni tsakeɔ yɛ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aná miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ajeŋba nɔ hewalɛ daa?

english: Yes, long-term changes in local climate alter heat and water levels in the soil, which changes how crops grow, flower, and bear fruit. Adapting your soil management helps crops withstand these shifts.
ga: Hɛɛ, he ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ kɛ tsakemɔi baa dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ saa tsei adalɛ, fɔfɔi, kɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ tsakemɔ baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛŋmɛ tsakemɔi nɛɛ anaa.

english: Why is adding fertilizer without testing the soil first sometimes a waste of money?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ eji shikafitemɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni akaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: If you do not know what your soil lacks, you might add the wrong fertilizer or the wrong amount. Testing your soil acts like a doctor's prescription so you only spend money on what your land actually needs.
ga: Kɛji oleee nɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ he ehiaaa. Ekolɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa loo falɛ ni ejaaa wo mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa tamɔ tsofa ni datrɛfonyo ŋma. No hewɔ lɛ, nɔ ni he hiaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ pɛ he ofiteɔ shika.

english: How does knowing my soil's health help me choose the right crop to plant this season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ ni mile lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni mihalaa tsei ni sa ni madu yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Different crops require different soil nutrients and soil types to yield well. Knowing your land's health helps you select crops that naturally thrive in your current soil conditions.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi srɔtoi koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai. Kɛ́ ole bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ nɔ amrɔ nɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why do many cocoa farmers in Ghana plant plantains on the same farm with young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ duɔ kookoo tsei yɛ ŋmɔji ni amɛduɔ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and produce broad leaves that shade young cocoa plants, protecting them from extreme heat while providing food and early income.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ be mli ni ehaa niyenii kɛ shika oya.

english: Do plantain trees need full sunlight to grow well?
ga: Ani hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia dumɔwui koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, plantains require direct sunlight to grow strong stems and produce heavy fruit bunches, which is why they are often planted in open spaces before cocoa trees grow tall enough to shade them.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la he miihia plantains tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni amɛwo yibii ni tsii. Yɛ yiŋtoo nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, aduɔ amɛ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ dani kookoo tsei lɛ ashɛɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaa hulutsoo.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are ripe and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cocoa pods change color when fully ripe, turning from green to yellow or red to orange. You should cut them off the tree when they change color rather than waiting for them to fall naturally.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa. Tsakemɔ kɛjɛ eŋɔli kɛya ŋmɔŋ loo etsuru kɛya akutu. Esa akɛ ofo amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛ́ amɛtsake amɛhe su moŋ fe ni ooomɛ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: How can I tell if my plantain bunch is ready to be cut down?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ plantains kuu ko efee klalo akɛ abaafolɔ?

english: A plantain bunch is ready for harvest when the individual fruits look full and plump, the sharp ridges on the sides become rounded, and the top leaves of the tree begin to turn yellow.
ga: Plantain ŋmɔji lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko eyi obɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe. ni tsei lɛ anɔ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Should I cut off old or dry leaves from my plantain trees?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni egbɔ loo ni egbi kɛjɛ mi-plantain lɛ mli?

english: Yes, pruning dry or yellowing leaves prevents diseases from spreading and reduces pest hiding spots, allowing more sunlight and nutrients to reach the main stalk and fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni egbi loo ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã, ni ebaaha hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ niyenii babaoo shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ aduawai lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my plantain plant grow many young stems around its base, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shishi tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo babaoo ebɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, ni ani esa akɛ majie amɛ?

english: Those young stems are called suckers. You should remove most of them and leave only one or two healthy ones so they do not steal water and food from the main fruiting stalk.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai tsei bibii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Esa akɛ ojie amɛteŋ babaoo kɛjɛ ohe ni oshi eko loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ ji koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ aduawai titrii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are some of my cocoa pods turning black and rotting before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in excessive moisture and shade. Pruning overhead branches to improve air flow and harvesting ripe pods quickly helps prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ shade mli fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni yɔɔ yiteŋ ni aaafolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ oya lɛ ni akpaa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: What causes some cocoa trees to produce small pods while others grow big, healthy ones?
ga: Mɛni haa cacao tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu daraa ni amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Pod size depends on soil nutrients, water availability, and plant health. Proper weeding, fertilizer application, and pruning out dead branches give the tree the energy needed to grow large pods.
ga: Pod lɛ dalɛ damɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. nu ni yɔɔ kɛ tsei ahewalɛ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ ahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know the right time of year to start clearing land for planting crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi he ni tsei yɔɔ lɛ shwiemɔ?

english: In Ghana, land clearing is typically done during the dry season (December to February) so the vegetation dries out and can be cleared before the main rainy season begins in April or May.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ajieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. (December kɛyashi February) koni tsei lɛ agbi ni anyɛ ajie amɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi yɛ April loo May mli.

english: Should I start planting my seedlings at the exact same time my neighbor starts planting theirs?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui akwɛmɔ yɛ be kome too mli ni akutsoŋbii lɛ jeɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ shishi lɛ?

english: While observing experienced neighbors is helpful, planting time depends on when the rains become consistent in your specific area and whether your soil has absorbed enough moisture.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ eyeɔ ebuaa akɛ oookwɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ moŋ, Shi be ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ damɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Ni ani oshikpɔŋ lɛ miihe nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready to pick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ?

english: Cocoa pods change color as they mature. Green pods turn bright yellow and reddish pods turn orange-yellow when they are fully ripe, indicating that the seeds inside have developed properly for harvesting.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii tsuji lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛha nikpamɔ.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn yellow when they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: As a cocoa pod matures, the chlorophyll that makes it green breaks down, revealing yellow pigments. This color change is natural and signals that the sugars inside the pod have developed and the beans are ready.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa Chlorophyll, ni haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, fiteɔ Ejieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kpo Nɛkɛ su tsakemɔ nɛɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ sugars ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ etsɔ hiɛ ni kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo.

english: What will happen if I leave ripe yellow cocoa pods on the tree for too long?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ ashi kookoo ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree too long leads to over-ripening, which can cause the beans inside to start germinating or rot. Overripe pods also attract pests like squirrels and insects, ruining your crop yield.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ hu gbalaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii. ni fiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibii lɛ

english: Why does cocoa money only come at specific times of the year in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo shika baa yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi pɛ amli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees flower and produce pods according to rainfall patterns. In Ghana, this creates two distinct harvest periods: the main crop season (October to February) and the minor light crop season (May to June).
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ naa. Yɛ Ghana lɛ, enɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ bei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ baa: ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be titri (October kɛyashi February) kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ (May kɛyashi June)

english: How can I earn income from my farm while waiting for the cocoa harvest season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná shika yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni mimɛɔ kookoo ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ?

english: You can practice intercropping by planting quick-yielding food crops like plantains, cassava, or vegetables alongside cocoa trees. This gives you regular food and income throughout the year while waiting for cocoa season.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛtsɔ niyenii ni woɔ yibii oya tamɔ plantains, cassava, loo cocoa tso mli aduawai ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa anáa niyenii kɛ shika ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni emɛɛɔ kookoo be lɛ.

english: What work should I be doing on my farm during the period before the cocoa pods ripen?
ga: Mɛɛ nitsumɔ esa akɛ matsu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani kookoo ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Before harvest, focus on farm maintenance: weed regularly, prune excess tree branches to allow airflow, remove diseased pods, and apply fertilizer so the tree has enough energy to ripen healthy pods.
ga: dani akpa kpamɔ Gbalamɔ ojwɛŋmɔ kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli saamɔ nɔ: Jwɛi lɛ daa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha tso lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa.

english: Are regions like Eastern and Volta suitable for growing high-yielding cocoa?
ga: Ani kpokpai tamɔ Bokagbɛ kɛ Volta lɛ sa kɛha kookoo ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ adumɔ?

english: Yes, areas in the forest zones like Akyem in the Eastern Region and Ho or Dodi Papase in the Volta/Oti region have suitable tropical weather, adequate rainfall, and fertile soils ideal for cocoa cultivation.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooi amli hei tamɔ Akyem ni yɔɔ Bokagbɛ Kpokpaa lɛ nɔ kɛ Ho loo Dodi Papase ni yɔɔ Volta/Oti Kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni sa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Does direct sunlight help cocoa pods turn yellow faster, or does it hurt the tree?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ oya? Aloo efite tso lɛ?

english: Balanced sunlight helps pods mature, but too much direct sun without shade trees burns cocoa leaves and stresses the plant. Cocoa needs partial shade from taller trees like plantain or forest trees to thrive.
ga: Hulu la ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Shi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsɔ ni tsei ahe hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ baashã kookoo baai lɛ ni eha tso lɛ aná haomɔ. Cocoa he miihia ni ená hulutsoo fioo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei amli koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are some of my young cocoa pods turning black and shriveling before they ever turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Young pods often turn black due to fungal infections like Black Pod disease or natural physiological thinning (cherelle wilt). Regular pruning and spraying with recommended fungicides help protect young pods until maturity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii ahe helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji hela loo adebɔɔ mli gbɔmɔtsoŋ ŋmeii (wilt) hewɔ. Kɛ́ atse tsei lɛ ahe daa ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baabu ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: What is the best thing to do with my cocoa pods right after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: After picking ripe yellow pods, gather them together and break them open within 5 days to collect the beans. Then, heap the beans under banana leaves to ferment for 5 to 6 days before drying them in the sun.
ga: Kɛji ogbala ŋmeii ni egbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Bua amɛnaa ni ogbala mli yɛ gbii 5 mli koni obua dumɔwui lɛ anaa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ ŋmeii lɛ ato banana baai ashishi koni etsɔ gbii 5 kɛyashi 6 dani egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do some traders ask me to pick my tomatoes or peppers while they are still green instead of fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nihɔɔlɔi komɛi biɔ mi akɛ mafolɔ tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Harvesting produce while green allows it to survive long transport to market without getting crushed or rotting. Green produce ripens slowly over time, giving traders a longer period to sell before it spoils.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa yɛ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛyaa jara nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni atswaaa loo egbooo. Nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ blɛoo. Beni be hoɔ lɛ Enɛ haa jarayelɔi lɛ náa be babaoo ni amɛkɛhɔ̃ɔ dani egboɔ.

english: Is it better for me to separate my green produce from the ripe ones after harvesting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafo mi-green lɛ mli kɛjɛ mi-green lɛ mli beni mikpa nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, ripe crops release natural gases that cause nearby green crops to ripen faster. Sorting them helps you manage which crops reach the market immediately and which ones can be saved for later sales.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ni haa tsei eŋɔli ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ shwereɔ oya. Nibii ni ahala lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni shɛɔ jara nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni mɛɛ tsei abaanyɛ akɛto koni akɛhɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli?

english: How does putting my harvested vegetables in a fridge or cold room make them stay fresh longer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ aduawai ni akpa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ friji loo he ko ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛhi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Cold temperatures slow down the crop's natural breathing and decay process. This locks in moisture and prevents bacteria from growing, keeping your vegetables crisp and high in quality for days.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ waa lɛ haa tsei lɛ adebɔɔ mli mumɔ kɛ amɛfitemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ baa shi. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaaa muawai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Ehaa o-vegetables lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ gbii babaoo.

english: Does freezing fresh farm produce spoil its quality, or does it keep it strong?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli nibii heei ni akɛwoɔ fɛ̃i mli lɛ baaha nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba shi loo ebaaha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Deep-freezing stops all decay immediately and preserves the strength, flavor, and nutrients of the produce. As long as it stays frozen, its quality and potency remain as high as the day it was picked.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa fitemɔ fɛɛ kpaɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ehaa hewalɛ, ŋmɔlɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hiɔ shi. Shii abɔ ni ebaaya nɔ efee fɛ̃i lɛ Ehilɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ baakã he ahi shi tamɔ gbi ni akɛto lɛ.

english: Why do my fresh leafy vegetables wither so quickly when I leave them under the sun after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmɔji heei lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, vegetables can no longer draw water from the soil. The hot sun causes them to lose their remaining moisture rapidly through transpiration, making them limp and soft.
ga: Kɛji akpa Aduawai lɛ nyɛŋ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ. Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa amɛshwieɔ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ oya kɛtsɔ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ nɔ. Ehaa hewolo lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I pack my produce neatly in crates instead of carrying them loosely in big sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi aduawai kɛ aduawai lɛ awo adekai amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛwo kotoku agbo mli mlɛo lɛ.

english: Neat packaging protects delicate crops from being crushed under their own weight. It preserves the fine appearance and quality of your produce so you can sell them to high-paying buyers.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli fɛfɛo lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsiimɔ akakumɔ amɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ oha mɛi ni heɔ nii babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do my peppers rot faster when I tightly pack them into plastic bags right after picking them in the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛwo plastic kotoku mli beni mikpa amɛ shwane mli nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Harvesting in heat traps warm moisture inside sealed bags, creating hot and humid conditions where rot-causing fungi thrive. It is best to cool crops in the shade before packing them.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa mli mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ baanyɛ adara yɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tso lɛ afee fɛ̃i yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani okɛwo tsɔne mli.

english: How can preserving the natural potency and freshness of my produce help me get better prices at the market?
ga: Te adebɔɔ mli hewalɛnamɔ kɛ ehee ni mikwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná jara kpakpa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Buyers pay higher prices for produce that retains its full flavor, firm texture, and rich nutrients. Keeping freshness high gives your crops a better shelf life, making them more desirable to town markets.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kɛha nibii ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe ŋmɔlɔ fɛɛ lɛ. Texture ni mli wa kɛ niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ Kɛ́ oha onibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Ni eeefee nɔ ni ataoɔ babaoo yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ.

english: Can proper cold storage help me make more money during the harvest season when market prices drop?
ga: Ani he ko ni sa ni akɛ nibii ni mli ejɔ toɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná shika babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli beni jara nɔ nibii jara baa shi lɛ?

english: Yes, using cold storage or freezing allows you to hold back your fresh crops without losing quality during market gluts, so you can sell them later when supply drops and prices rise.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛ nibii ni mli ejɔ loo fɛ̃i ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ nibii heei ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko fiteee yɛ be mli ni akɛhaa fe nine lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ amɛ sɛɛ mli beni nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa ni amɛjara hu yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do fruits like bananas and plantains ripen all at once when kept together in a covered container?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai tamɔ banana kɛ plantains shwereɔ yɛ be kome mli kɛ́ akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni akɛ nɔ ko eha he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Ripening fruits produce a natural gas called ethylene. When enclosed together, this trapped gas signals all surrounding fruits to ripen at the exact same time.
ga: Yibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene. kɛji akɛ atswa amɛhe Gas ni emɔ lɛ nɛɛ tsuɔ okadi kɛyaa aduawai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ. Amɛ fɛɛ amɛhoo yɛ be kome mli.

english: When is the best time of year for me to plant my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei?

english: Cocoa seedlings should be planted at the start of the major rainy season, usually around April or May in Ghana. Planting early in the rainy season gives young roots enough water and time to grow strong before the dry season arrives.
ga: Esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli. Bei pii lɛ, aduɔ enɛ yɛ April loo May aaafee yɛ Ghana. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaadara dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why should I treat or clear my farm land before planting cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ loo mafo mli dani madu kookoo lɛ?

english: Clearing and treating the soil before planting removes hidden pests, dangerous fungi, and weeds from the dirt. This gives your young cocoa seedlings a clean and healthy environment to grow without competing for soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni atsu he nii dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Fung kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ oshara ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ baaha o-cocoa dumɔwui bibii lɛ aná shihilɛ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛkaaa akaŋ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn yellow when planted in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily and lose water fast in direct sunlight. They need shade crops, like plantains or shade trees, to protect them from harsh sun heat during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ he.

english: Is it better to spray my crops with farm medicine early in the morning or in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ tsofa leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning when the weather is cool and winds are calm. In the hot afternoon, heat causes the spraying chemical to evaporate too fast and can burn tender leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu efee kpoo. Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Dɔlɛ lɛ haa tsofai ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ ni eshãa baai bibii lɛ.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in wet, humid conditions. Heavy rainfall splashes fungal spores from the soil onto the pods, which causes them to rot if not sprayed with protective cocoa medicine.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashwieee kookoo nɔ koni ekɛtsi enaa.

english: If wild plants on the land grow slowly or have pale yellow leaves, the soil is likely low in nutrients like nitrogen. Adding fertilizer restores soil strength, helping your new cocoa plants grow faster and yield more pods.
ga: Kɛji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daraa blɛoo loo amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa ekoŋŋ. Ye obua o-cacao tsei heei lɛ ni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crop plants and choke them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛmiitsi amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to steal sunlight, water, and soil food away from crops. Keeping your farm weed-free ensures that all water and nutrients go directly into growing healthy cocoa trees.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ aya kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to cut off extra branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata kookoo tso ni eda lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cutting dead or overcrowded branches, known as pruning, allows fresh air and light to move through the tree canopy. This keeps dampness away, reduces fungal diseases, and helps the tree produce more cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ Atsɛɔ lɛ pruning. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ la boteɔ tsei lɛ ayiteŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ baaa, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi babaoo.

english: What is causing small dark spots and dried patches on my cocoa stems and leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ nii kɛ ŋmeii ni egbi yɛ mi-kookoo tsei kɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: These spots are usually caused by sap-sucking insects like mirids or 'akate'. They bite into soft stems and leaves to drink the sap, causing plant tissues to dry up and die if insecticides are not applied.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids loo 'akate' kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ tsei bibii kɛ baai koni amɛnu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei amli fãji lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Why is it important to measure and leave specific spaces between cocoa plants when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni asusu ni ashi gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ adu lɛ?

english: Leaving proper space prevents cocoa trees from fighting each other for water and soil nutrients underground. It also leaves enough space above ground for air flow, which keeps the cocoa canopy dry and reduces pod diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ ato tsei lɛ ahe gbɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi cacao tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkawuu amɛhe kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Eshiɔ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa hu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ, ni ehaa helai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin but fail to give big cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi amɛwooo toi wuji lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and nutrients. The plants stretch high up to reach light instead of using energy to grow thick stems and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛmiitswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ lɛ, tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ la lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaafite hewalɛ ni amɛkɛmiida ŋmãa ni mli tse kɛ ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers usually fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme sun heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. The plant drops its blossoms to conserve water and survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la ni mli edɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi.
