english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up away from moist soil, preventing leaf rot and allowing maximum sunlight absorption.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni eŋɔ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I use the seeds saved from my hybrid maize harvest for the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa ŋmãa ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred from selected parent plants to give high yields. The seeds harvested from those crops lose that special vigor, leading to uneven growth and low yields if planted again.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ fɔ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tsei ni ahala koni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ nakai tsei lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛji akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to prevent water loss through evaporation. The plant goes into a resting state to keep its roots alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni laajeɔ lɛ akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Tsei boteɔ hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. The pepper plant rolls its leaves to shield itself from strong sunlight and trap moisture inside so it does not dry out.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni amɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my farmland make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that fix nitrogen gas from the air into the soil through their roots. When the plant decays, it leaves behind natural nitrogen fertilizer that helps the next crop grow strong.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmei tso ko ni tsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ ekɛ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ fite Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are my sweet potato tubers small and stringy instead of fat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ fiber yɛ sweet potato najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes need loose, well-drained soil to expand properly. If the soil is hard or tightly packed, the tubers cannot push through to expand, resulting in thin, stringy roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia atomo koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo ebɔle ehe lɛ Anyɛɛɛ ajie yitso lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ kpãi.

english: Why do plantain suckers take longer to bear fruit if I leave many of them on one stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii kɛji mishi babaoo yɛ tso kome nɔ lɛ?

english: All suckers attached to the main plantain stool share the same underground food supply. Leaving too many stems creates competition for nutrients, slowing down fruit production for all of them.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei fɛɛ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ plantain sɛi wulu lɛ he lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi niyenii jɛɛhe kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii. Kɛ́ ashi tsei babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii aba kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa yibii ni anáa lɛ baa blɛoo kɛha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my young cocoa plants turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often indicate that the plant is not getting enough nitrogen from the soil or that the roots are standing in too much water, preventing them from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ naaa nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Ehaa amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to harsh sunlight and dry winds. Keeping larger shade trees like plantains or timber trees protects the young cocoa leaves from burning and helps the soil hold onto moisture.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he waa. Kɛ́ akwɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ plantain loo tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi

english: Why does my plantain farm yield smaller bunches if I leave all the young shoots growing around the main plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: The small shoots (suckers) compete directly with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Pruning away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, allowing the plant to direct all its energy into growing a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso bibii (tso lɛ) kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up before the corn is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani abele lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to stay green and healthy, so when soil nutrients run low, the plant pulls food from its lower leaves to feed the growing cob.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmei ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting beans or groundnuts in my field make the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth. When the plants finish growing, they leave that extra plant food in the soil for future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ gbe ekwɛ̃ naa Amɛshiɔ tso niyenii ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Black pod is caused by a soil fungus that thrives and spreads in wet, humid condition. Rain splashes the fungus onto lower pods, and dense foliage traps moisture, making it easy for the disease to attack the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Nugbɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Ni baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ helai baatutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the undersides of the leaves, or by a virus carried by those insects. The feeding damages the leaf tissue, causing it to wrinkle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ hiɛɔ lɛ nɔ Niyenii fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Cassava roots need well-draining soil to breathe. When excess rainwater stays on the land without draining away, it drowns the root system and allows soil fungi to cause root rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines and keep them off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ tso nɔ ni mikɛhaaa amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on tall stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture energy. This energy travels down into the soil to build a much larger tuber.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. Hewalɛ nɛɛ yaa shi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efeɔ ŋmei ni da kwraa.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden changes in water supply. The plant drops flowers to conserve its strength until conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ nɔ ko tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ tsake trukaa lɛ kpe. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it better for me to water my garden early in the morning instead of the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu woɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli leebi moŋ fe shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering in the morning gives roots time to drink before the sun gets hot, whereas afternoon heat causes most water to evaporate into the air before the soil can absorb it.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ nu dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shwane mli latsaa lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ eŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: If I am clearing my land to plant crops, should I burn the weeds and brush after clearing?
ga: Kɛji miitsumɔ shikpɔŋ koni mikɛdu nii Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi ni mikɛ brɔshi atsu nii beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ?

english: Burning might seem quick, but high heat destroys useful soil nutrients and beneficial organisms. Instead, leave the cut weeds to dry and rot naturally on top of the soil as mulch; this keeps moisture in the ground and feeds the soil.
ga: Ekolɛ ebaafee tamɔ nɔ ni shãa oya. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ kpataa sũ mli niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baatsu nii lɛ, ha jwɛi ni afo lɛ agbi ni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Is it better for me to plant my whole land at once or start with a small plot first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo mabɔi kɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Starting small allows you to test how your chosen crop performs on your soil without risking much money. Once you learn the correct care, pest management, and fertilizer timing on a small scale, you can expand across all your land with confidence.
ga: Kɛ́ oje shishi bibioo lɛ, ebaaha oka bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni ohala lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ okwɛ ni okɛ shika babaoo wooo oshara mli. Kɛji okase bɔ ni ooofee okwɛ Pest management kɛ be ni sa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ gbɛ bibioo nɔ lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ hekɛnɔfɔɔ agbɛ ogbɛhe muu lɛ fɛɛ oshwã.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is starving for nitrogen, which helps leaves grow big and green. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help the plants recover their dark green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yes, cassava and maize grow well together because maize grows fast and is ready for harvest in three months, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the space after the maize is removed.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni eshɛɔ he ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eŋɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do I know the exact time to sow my seeds when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the soil underneath may still be dry. Wait until you receive two or three good rains so the soil has enough deep moisture to keep the seeds growing continuously.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo. Mɛɛ ni ona nugbɔ kpakpa fioo ko koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ aya nɔ akwɛ̃.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically selected and treated to resist common local diseases and yield higher harvests. Saved seeds lose their vigor over time, resulting in weaker plants and smaller yields.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ pɔtɛɛ ni atsaa amɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my crops mostly at night or early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo gbɛkɛ loo leebi lɛ?

english: Pests like armyworms hide inside crop leaves or soil during the hot afternoon sun to avoid drying out. They come out to feed when the air is cool, so checking your field early in the morning is the best time to spot and manage them.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ tsei ahe baai loo shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkagbi. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbatao niyenii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli leebi maŋkpa lɛ, no ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ ona amɛ ni okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop during the hot afternoon even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plant leaves lose water into the hot air faster than their roots can pull it up from the soil. As long as the root zone has moisture, the leaves will stand back up automatically once the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ shishifã lɛ he lɛ Baai lɛ baate shi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ beni hulu la lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields every year even though I plant the exact same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the same specific nutrients from the soil year after year. Rotating your main crop with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it critical for me to clear weeds during the first month after my crops sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are weak and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for water, sunlight, and fertilizer. Keeping your farm clean during the first four weeks gives your crop the best chance to grow tall and strong.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ ashi akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Can strong gas or chemical fumes blowing across my farm actually kill my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani lasu ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ, loo tsofai ni tswaa kɛtsɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbe mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, cocoa trees are sensitive to toxic fumes. If bad gas or harsh chemical smoke drifts across your farm, it can poison the leaves and kill your cocoa trees.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cacao tsei lɛ nuɔ lasu ni yɔɔ gbeyei ahe waa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii loo tsofai ni mli wa ni mli wa lɛ shwieɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ Ebaanyɛ ekɛ poison awo baai lɛ amli ni egbe o-cacao tsei lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves wither when there is heavy chemical spraying or burning happening near my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni mli wa shwie nɔ loo ashã yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Harsh gases and airborne chemical drifts can poison cocoa plants on contact, causing the leaves to wither and potentially destroying the entire tree.
ga: Gas ni mli wa kɛ tsofai ni hoɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbe cacao tsei lɛ kɛji amɛshɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebaanyɛ efite tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to spread treatments on my cocoa trees after three months have passed?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofa baawo cacao nɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, once three months have passed, you should avoid spreading unapproved substances or chemicals on your cocoa trees, as improper application at this stage can harm or kill the crop.
ga: Dabi, beni nyɔji etɛ eho lɛ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ okpa nibii loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ ni ooogbɛ ashwã o-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui loo efite.

english: What happens if I apply fertilizers or chemicals to my cocoa crop at the wrong time?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai tsu nii yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ be ni esaaa mli?

english: Applying or spreading improper materials on your cocoa past the recommended three-month mark can burn the plants, damage developing pods, and reduce your yield.
ga: Kɛ akɛ nibii ni esaaa tsu nii loo akɛwo kookoo nɔ fe nyɔji 3 ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ ashã. Efiteɔ pod ni miiya hiɛ lɛ. ni ebaanyɛ eba nibii ni anáa lɛ shi

english: What key mistakes should I avoid when applying inputs to my cocoa crop after a few months of growth?
ga: Mɛɛ tɔmɔi titrii esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ he kɛ́ mikɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ amli lɛ miitsu nii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: A major mistake is spreading unrecommended substances on the crop after three months has passed, as well as leaving heaps of farm waste sitting close to the trees.
ga: Tsɔne wulu ko ji nibii ni esaaa akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ ni fata he ji ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋtayaai amli yɛ tsei ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I stack harvested cocoa pods in big piles inside my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ toɔ ŋmeii wuji amli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Piling up cocoa pods inside your farm creates rotting heaps that trap heat and release harmful gases, which can spoil the soil and kill nearby healthy cocoa trees.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni okɛtoɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ ni mɔɔ dɔlɛ ni ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpo. Enɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ lɛ ni efite kookoo tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Can leaving heaps of old cocoa pods in the field destroy my standing cocoa crop?
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii momo ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ Ani eshi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite mikookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni damɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving pods piled up in the farm generates bad localized rot and fumes that can easily spread disease and kill surrounding cocoa trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi pods ni ebɔle ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ he ko kɛ lasu gbonyo aba. Enɛ baanyɛ agbɛ helai ashwã oya ni egbe kookoo tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ.

english: What is the proper way to handle cocoa pod waste after harvesting to protect my living trees?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni ashwieɔ yɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ he nii koni akɛbu mi tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ ahe?

english: Cocoa pods and crop waste should be removed or spread out properly rather than piled up inside the farm, preventing toxic rot and gas buildup around living trees.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie kookoo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaabua amɛnaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Enɛ ji koni akɛtsi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anaabuamɔ naa. tso ni hiɛ kã

english: How does improper piling of plant waste affect the overall health of my farm?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni abua naa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔ lɛ fɛɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When farm waste or cocoa pods are tightly piled together, the decay creates harsh localized fumes and harbors diseases that can stress and kill active cocoa plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔ mli jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anaa lɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ haa lasu ni naa wa baa, ni ekɛ helai ni baanyɛ ahao kookoo tsei ni miitsu nii lɛ aná haomɔ ni egbe amɛ lɛ baa.

english: What common farm management practices can unexpectedly kill my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi ni afɔɔ feemɔ baanyɛ afite mi-cacao tsei lɛ trukaa?

english: Cocoa trees can die if toxic gases drift over the farm, if unapproved substances are spread on them after three months, or if cocoa pods are left stacked in piles inside the farm.
ga: Cacao tsei baanyɛ agboi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei shwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nibii ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ eshwa yɛ nyɔji etɛ sɛɛ Aloo kɛji akɛ ashi kookoo ŋmeii yɛ ŋtayaa mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Officer, why are the leaves on my young maize turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe. Applying the right amount of nitrogen-rich fertilizer after clearing standing water will help the leaves turn green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Nitrogen ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli beni ajie nu ni ekã shi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Officer, why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Agent Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in excessive moisture and shade during the rainy season. Pruning extra tree branches to let light in and removing affected pods quickly prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ahe koni la abote mli, ni ojie ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do I need to keep clearing weeds around my cassava when cassava is already a strong plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Mi ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ Be ni ŋmei ji tso ni mli wa momo?

english: Weeds compete with cassava roots for underground space, water, and soil nutrients. Keeping the field clean early in the season lets the cassava roots expand freely into big, heavy tubers.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmei shishifãi yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi he ko, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha he lɛ he tse yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Officer, why should I measure and plant my seeds in straight lines instead of scattering them randomly?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu ni madu dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ? Yɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ trukaa lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Planting in measured lines ensures each crop gets equal access to sunlight and soil nutrients without crowding. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and walking through your farm much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ linei ni asusu he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli nyiɛmɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and dropping off during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl to conserve moisture when the sun is very hot and the soil is dry. Mulching around the base of the plant with dry grass helps hold moisture in the soil and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli edɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Officer, if I put double the amount of fertilizer on my crops, will they grow twice as fast?
ga: Onukpa: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo mli lɛ toi enyɔ lɛ, ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya shii enyɔ?

english: No, putting too much fertilizer can scorch the roots and burn your crops, causing them to dry up. Every crop has a recommended procedure and amount that helps it grow safely.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã ni eshã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ etsɔɔ gbɛi kɛ tsofai ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is my plantain shoot taking so long to bring out a fruit bundle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mi plantains lɛ jieɔ aduawai akui lɛ?

english: When too many small sucker shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they steal food from the main mother plant. Removing the weaker extra suckers allows the main plant to fruit faster and produce bigger bundles.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii miida yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ Amɛbaaju niyenii kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tsei krokomɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo yibii oya ni etsɔ kui wuji.

english: Officer, why shouldn't I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant again next season?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Hybrid seeds lose their high yield and pest resistance after the first harvest. Planting saved hybrid seeds produces weaker stalks and smaller cobs, so getting fresh certified seeds each season gives you a better harvest.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ amɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ ni amɛyeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Hybrid dumɔwui ni ato ni aduɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ onine shɛ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ anɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oná ŋmaa kpakpa.

english: Why do older farmers tell me to plant plantains on the same land as my newly planted cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko kɛɛ mi akɛ midu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu kookoo ehee lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide tall, broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants from the harsh sun until they are mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai kakadaji ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shɛɛɛ kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshɛɔ shweremɔ he.

english: Officer, how can I tell that my yams are completely ripe and ready to be dug out of the soil?
ga: Amralofoi, te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ko eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Yams indicate they are mature when the green leaves and vines above the ground dry up and turn brown at the end of the rainy season. Harvesting at this stage ensures the tuber is full of starch and will store well.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsɔɔ akɛ amɛdara kɛji baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gĩ ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bulb lɛ eyi kɛ starch ni akɛtoɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and have large broad leaves that provide vital shade and hold soil moisture, helping young cocoa trees survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do people spread dry grass around the base of crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwereɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwieɔ tsei ashishi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass around crops is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating quickly under hot sun, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my crops when the major rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Wait until the ground gets 2 to 3 steady rains that soak deep into the soil rather than planting after the very first light shower, which can trick seeds into germinating before drying out.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii 2 kɛyashi 3 ni baabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, duɔ ngɛ kekleekle hiɔmi ɔ se, nɛ lɔ ɔ ma nyɛ maa sisi duwu ɔmɛ konɛ a kwɛ̃ loko a gbo.

english: Leaves turning yellow from the tips down usually means the soil is running out of nitrogen, which the plant needs to build green foliage. Applying manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishi kɛyaa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei lɛ he hiaa koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same field drains specific soil nutrients and lets crop-specific pests multiply in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpea or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hoɔ, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to create food for growing large tubers underground. Elevating the vines on stakes maximizes light intake and keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa la lɛ jeɔ kpo babaoo. ni etsĩɔ baai anaa koni amɛkajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ Koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli aba

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my young maize central funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ funnel lɛ mli baai lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, pests that hide inside the central funnel of young maize plants to chew fresh leaves before they unfold. Detecting them early allows for targeted bio-pesticide or recommended sprays.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei dani amɛje kpo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. mra mli ni anaa Enɛ baaha anyɛ akwɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or viruses they transmit. Controlling these insects early protects new leaves from crippling damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, whiteflies, loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebuɔ baai heei ahe kɛjɛɔ nibii ni fiteɔ ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants suffer from extreme heat or irregular watering, which disrupts pollination. Keeping soil consistently moist and planting during moderate weather helps fruit set normally.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. ni tsiɔ pollination naa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ dumɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa mli lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ ama shi bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting if I leave them in the soil during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains soak the soil and cut off air to the cassava roots, causing underground fungal rotting. Harvesting mature roots on time or planting on raised mounds prevents waterlogging around the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũuɔ ni efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ akpa shishifãi ni edara lɛ yɛ be naa loo adu yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu akabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing crops like plantains provide shade with their large leaves, keeping the young cocoa plants cool and moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ haa baai agboi ni yɔɔ hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I get smaller maize cobs when I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, their roots and leaves compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leaving less energy for the plant to produce big ears.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náaa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaafee toi wuji.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stems at an angle instead of burying them flat in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slanting 45-degree angle helps the roots grow deeper and spread out evenly, which produces larger tubers and makes them easier to dig up during harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu cassava tsei yɛ 45-degree angle mli lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaafo amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why is it necessary for me to stick wood poles in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high up to catch sunlight to make food. Staking keeps the vines off the damp soil to prevent rot and allows the plant to put more energy into swelling the tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛhoo nii. Staking haa wain tsei lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ koni amɛkafite, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ jie

english: Too many shoots around one mother plant compete for food and water. Pruning away the extra ones leaves only one or two strong suckers, which helps the main plant produce a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi babaoo ni ebɔle Tso kome ni ji nyɛ kome lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afo tso ni fa fe nine lɛ mli lɛ, tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa, ni no haa tso titri lɛ woɔ tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential food they need to build green leaves, or that the soil is waterlogged and the roots cannot take up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for the next season's crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha be ni baa lɛ mli dumɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have tiny bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ helai bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ ni heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly when the weather is very wet, cool, and humid, especially if the farm canopy is too thick and has very little airflow.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ, edɔ, ni edɔ waa, titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo pɛ tsɔɔ mli.

english: Why are the blossom ends of my green tomatoes turning dark and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering or dry spells while the fruit is forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo shihilɛ ni mli egbi be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lay asleep in dry dirt for months. The first rain wakes them all up at the same time, giving them moisture and warm soil to grow rapidly before crops can cover the ground.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kã shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo. Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ tee amɛ fɛɛ shi yɛ be kome mli, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũ ni edɔ oya dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight during the dry season. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa gives them cover, keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tso lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn purple and grow very short in some parts of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ purple ni amɛfeɔ kuku waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks phosphorus, an important nutrient for root growth and plant energy. Adding phosphorus-rich fertilizer or composted animal manure helps the roots expand and turns the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ fɔsfɔs ni fa babaoo loo kooloi ashishifãi fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big leaves above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen from chemical fertilizers or overly rich soil, it spends all its energy producing leaf foliage instead of storing starch in the roots. Using balanced nutrients and wider planting distances encourages larger tuber formation.
ga: Beni ŋmãa naa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli loo shikpɔŋ ni ŋmãa yɔɔ mli tsɔ lɛ mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baato shishifãi lɛ amli. Niyenii mli nibii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ he ni aduɔ lɛ babaoo lɛ baawo bulbs wuji afeemɔ he hewalɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my young corn leaves with sawdust-like dirt inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn baai lɛ miifee bu bibii? Ni muji tamɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides and feeds inside the central whorl of the maize plant. Spraying approved neem-based biopesticides or recommended insecticides into the whorl early in the morning kills the pest before it ruins the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ji neem ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when soil moisture is irregular or when hot winds dry out the blossoms before pollination happens. Mulching around the base of the plant with dry grass keeps the soil cool and moist, helping the flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ha fɔfɔi lɛ egbi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo amɛhe ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and put wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni majie tsei koni mikɛdu sweet potato wain tsei lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight on their leaves to make food that builds the tuber below ground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet soil, preventing fungal decay and ensuring maximum exposure to sunlight for bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni hiɛ yitsei wuji lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo

english: How do groundnut plants make the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tsei aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have special nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil plant food. When groundnut roots rot in the field after harvest, they release this natural fertilizer into the ground for the next maize crop.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids that carry plant viruses. Removing severely affected plants and spraying insecticidal soap or neem oil stops the insects from spreading the disease to healthy plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni hiɛ hela ko yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni akɛ samla loo neem fɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi lɛ akagbɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra young shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Allowing too many shoots (suckers) to grow forces them to steal water and nutrients from the main tree, resulting in small plantain bunches. Pruning extra suckers to leave only two or three healthy stems ensures heavy, large fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ suckers (tso) babaoo gbɛ ni amɛdara lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantains lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ koni ashi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha aduawai ni tsii ni dara.

english: Why do my corn seeds fail to sprout when I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain after a long dry spell often heats up the parched ground without soaking deep enough into the soil. If a dry period follows, the seeds dry out and rot under the hot ground before they can fully germinate.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ haa hei ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ehaaa sũ lɛ mli awo mli bɔ ni sa. Kɛji hulutsoo be ko yɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kwraa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing sunlight and air to pass through the tree. This air circulation prevents fungal diseases like black pod and encourages the tree to focus its energy on producing healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɛɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pod blackening naa ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ ama pod ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ feemɔ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of the plant usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or compost gives the crop the energy it needs to grow deep green leaves and strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-abele lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with many leaves but small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei lɛ kɛlɛ waa, ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or water, the cassava plant puts all its strength into growing leaves above ground instead of food underground. Planting in loose, well-drained soil with balanced nutrients encourages tuber growth.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi niyenii najiaŋ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni niyenii mli nibii ni ja yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tuber lɛ ada.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Keeping soil moist and using shade can help flowers stay on the plant and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔii ahi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛto tomatoi lɛ ama shi.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or whiteflies sucking sap from the leaves and transmitting plant viruses. Spraying plants with neem oil or soapy water helps clear these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛhaa helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ajie amɛhe.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and weak when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Seeds planted too close together fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing allows the roots and stalks to grow thick and produce full ears of corn.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwo ŋmãa toi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yam vines naturally want to climb toward the sun to collect light and make food for the tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground where insects and mold can rot them.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛbua la naa ni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akadamɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ afite.

english: Why should I remove small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajie midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Having too many shoots causes them to steal water and food from the mother plant. Leaving only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce big bunches of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ amɛye ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, amɛbaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo plantains babaoo.

english: Why do my vegetable crops turn yellow and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much standing water around roots drowns them by cutting off oxygen, causing root rot. Growing vegetables on raised soil mounds or beds lets excess water drain away safely.
ga: nu ni ebɔle amɛhe Shishifãi babaoo tsɔ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo saatsoi ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up tightly during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves roll up tightly as a natural defense mechanism to protect themselves from intense heat and sunshine, reducing the amount of moisture the plant loses through its leaves.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la he. Enɛ haa nu ni tso lɛ fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing huge leaves on top but giving me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji yɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is extremely rich, the cassava plant spends all its energy developing heavy stem and leaf growth above ground instead of storing starch in its roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ nii babaoo. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ tsei kɛ baai ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ starch ato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are a sign that the plant is hungry for nitrogen or that too much water around the roots is preventing the plant from taking up food from the soil.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo nu ni ebɔle ehe. Shishifãi babaoo haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my farmland produce less maize every year even though I plant at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Planting the same crop continuously without adding compost, manure, or fertilizer exhausts the essential nutrients in the soil, leaving it too weak to support good yields.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ edu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will planting cowpeas together with my maize steal food away from the maize plants?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu lɛ baaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli?

english: No, cowpeas actually feed the soil by taking nitrogen from the air and trapping it in their roots, which helps nourish the neighboring maize while giving you two crops from one piece of land.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. ni baaye abua ni eha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aná niyenii Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmãa enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: What is making tiny ragged holes in my young corn leaves and leaving sawdust-like dirt in the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ baa? ni eshiɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central stem of the young corn plant and eats the delicate leaves before they unfurl.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ.

english: Why does Striga weed always attach itself near my corn roots and stop the corn from growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ ŋmɛɔ mi ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ ahe be fɛɛ be ni etsĩɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed whose roots grow directly into the corn plant's roots to steal water and food, which starves the corn and keeps it stunted.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei ashishifãi amli koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni ehaa egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why did some of the maize seeds I planted last week fail to sprout out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni midu yɛ otsi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ejeee kpo kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if the soil was too dry, if they were planted too deep for the shoot to reach the surface, if insects ate them underground, or if the seeds were old and damaged.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ Kɛji kooloi yeɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ ni efite.

english: How do I know the soil is wet enough to start planting my maize when the early rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Dig down into the soil to about the depth of your hand; if the dirt easily forms a moist ball that stays together without dripping water, the soil has enough steady moisture to sprout seeds safely.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aaafee bɔ ni onine lɛ mli kwɔ ha. Kɛji muji feɔ bɔɔlu ni mli efɔ ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi lɛ mlɛo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa be fɛɛ be ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my stored corn turn into powder with tiny insects inside after a few months in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ tsɔɔ powda kɛ kooloi bibii? Ehi mli beni ehi tsu lɛ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ.

english: Grain weevils bore into corn kernels that were stored with too much moisture inside, eating the inside of the grain and multiplying rapidly in unsealed or untreated storage spaces.
ga: Seed weevil lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni akɛ nu babaoo ewo mli lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ dumɔwui amli nibii ni amɛshwereɔ oya yɛ hei ni akɛ nibii toɔ ni atsĩii naa loo atsuuu he nii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from bigger trees or shade crops like plantains because direct sunlight dries out the soil and burns tender leaves before the young root system is fully established.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ, ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni eshãa baai bibii lɛ dani shishifãi bibii lɛ agbeɔ naa.

english: Pruning removes weak, dead, or overcrowded branches so the tree can direct its water and plant nutrients into growing healthy cocoa pods rather than feeding useless foliage.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni egboi, loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii kɛya kookoo ŋmeii ni miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooye baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ niyenii

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right after the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains create high humidity that allows the Black Pod fungal disease to spread quickly; keeping weeds down and pruning tree canopy allows air to flow and keep pods drier.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa, ni no haa black pod fungal hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli ni afoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How can using the wrong chemical spray ruin my cocoa farm within a single year?
ga: Te tsofa ni ejaaa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baafite mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ afi kome mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Applying incorrect pesticides or using wrong doses can burn plant foliage, destroy beneficial insects needed for pod development, and cause long-term damage to the tree's health.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ejaaa tsu nii loo akɛ falɛ ni ejaaa tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashã. Efiteɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni he hiaa kɛha pod lɛ shweremɔ. ni ekɛ naagbai ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ nɔ.

english: When maize is planted too close together, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and small or missing cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo ni bɛ mli baa.

english: Cassava root rot usually happens when water settles in heavy soil due to poor drainage, creating damp conditions where harmful soil fungi can multiply and destroy tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. ni kɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa Biɛ ji he ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Removing extra suckers stops them from stealing vital water and nutrients from the main mother plant, ensuring the main plant produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaaa amɛju nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛ tso titri ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo dumɔwui wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil has run out of nutrients for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa miduɔ nii?

english: When soil loses its fertility, crop leaves often turn pale yellow, plants remain stunted and weak, and overall harvest yields decrease significantly season after season.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Tso lɛ kã he eji nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ. ni nibii fɛɛ ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi waa yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Early weeding stops aggressive wild plants from stealing light, soil food, and moisture while your young crop seedlings are still vulnerable and building roots.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju la, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni odumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why is it bad practice to apply fertilizer right before a heavy rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli dani ahum baa lɛ akɛ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes granular fertilizer off the surface soil into drainage paths before the crop's roots have time to absorb the nutrients, wasting your money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ hiɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa nu homɔ gbɛi anɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Ehaa ofiteɔ oshika.

english: Why do cassava and plantain prices go up so much during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jara yaa hiɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: During the dry season, the ground hardens and crops receive less water, making them harder to harvest and less abundant. Because supply drops while people still need food to make fufu, market prices go up.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ais ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa nu fioo. Enɛ haa nikpamɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa, ni ehaaa ŋmɔshi nibii hu aya hiɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ miiba shi yɛ be mli ni niyenii he miihia gbɔmɛi lolo koni amɛkɛfee fufu lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ jarayeli jara lɛ etee ŋwɛi.

english: What can I do to keep my crops from dying when the dry season comes and there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni miŋmɔshi nibii akagboi beni hɔmɔ eba ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dried leaves or straw (mulching) to trap moisture, and use simple drip irrigation or watering buckets early in the morning to keep the soil damp.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni okɛ drip irrigation loo nu ni akɛwoɔ baagi mli lɛ atsu nii leebi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How should I prepare my land before planting so my crops grow well?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu nii koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good land preparation involves clearing weeds, breaking up hard soil, and creating mounds or ridges. This creates loose, fertile soil where crop roots can easily breathe, catch water, and spread.
ga: Nɔ ni fata shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kpakpa he ji jwɛi ni ajieɔ. shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ hiɛkpatamɔ kɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni afeɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baa nii baa. Tso lɛ shishifãi baanyɛ amu, amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo.

english: What is the best method to plant yams to get a big harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ sweet potatoes koni aná yibii babaoo?

english: Yams grow best when planted on high soil mounds made of loose, rich earth. This gives the tubers plenty of soft space underground to expand into large, healthy yams.
ga: Sweet potatoes daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baa nii babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ naa hegbɛ babaoo ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii agboi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants need wooden stakes in the ground to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the tubers growing under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛha niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why is it so much harder and tiring to harvest cassava and yams when the soil is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe waa akɛ abaakpa ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ?

english: When rain stops, the soil dries up and turns hard like cement around the tubers. This requires much more physical effort to dig, which exhausts you and damages tools.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ewaa tamɔ simenti ni bɔleɔ bulb lɛ he, ni ebiɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo dani anyɛ atsa. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni efiteɔ dɛŋdade lɛ.

english: How can I reduce physical exhaustion when harvesting heavy tuber crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã gbɔmɔtsoŋ tɔlɛ aba shi kɛ́ mikpa shishifãi ni tsii?

english: Try harvesting early in the morning when the air is cool, use proper digging tools like sharpened cutlasses and pickaxes, and harvest shortly after light rains when the soil is soft.
ga: Bɔɔmɔdɛŋ ni okpa nii lɛ leebi maŋkpa be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Kɛ tsumɔ nibii ni sa tamɔ kaklai ni naa wa kɛ shɔvel atsu nii. ni akpaa yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ, beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops lose weight and quality if rain fails close to harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ baaa kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Crops rely on water up until maturity to stay plump and healthy. If water drops suddenly before harvest, the plants draw energy back from their roots, causing tubers to shrink.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa koni amɛya nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛji nu lɛ ba shi trukaa dani akpa ŋmaa lɛ Tsei lɛ heɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: What does proper farm planning mean and why is it important before I start planting?
ga: Mɛni ŋmɔ mli gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa tsɔɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa dani aje dumɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Farm planning means deciding what crops to plant, how much land to prepare, and when to plant based on expected rains. It prevents you from wasting money and labor on crops that might fail.
ga: Okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoo tsɔɔ nibii ni abaadu lɛ ahe yiŋkpɛɛ. He ni esa akɛ asaa he kɛ be ni esa akɛ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ ebaanɛ lɛ naa. Etsiɔ bo gbɛ koni okafite shika kɛ nitsumɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baanyɛ afite lɛ ahe.

english: How can I plan my farm calendar so I harvest food when market prices are high?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato miŋmɔ mli kalanda lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni makpa niyenii be mli ni jara nɔ jara wa lɛ?

english: By adjusting your planting dates slightly earlier or using water conservation methods, you can harvest during the early dry season when produce is scarce and buyers pay higher prices.
ga: Kɛtsɔ gbi ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ ni aaatsake mra fioo loo gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okpa nii yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli, be mli ni yibiiwoo lɛ faaa ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ jara babaoo lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their leaves lose moisture faster than their small roots can absorb water. They need temporary shade crops, like plantains, to shield them while they build strong root systems.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. ni baanyɛ aŋɔ nu Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛmaa shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ.

english: When maize lacks nitrogen in the soil, it pulls stored nitrogen from its older lower leaves to nourish the new leaves at the top, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Kɛji nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejieɔ nitrogen ni ato kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually a reaction to tiny sucking pests like thrips or mites feeding on leaf sap, or a virus carried by insects that disrupts normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni tsiɔ baa lɛ adalɛ naa bɔ ni sa lɛ.

english: When too many suckers grow around the main plantain stem, they compete with it for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning extra suckers directs all the plant's energy into growing one large fruit bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ he lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, nu lɛ mli, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo aduawai akuu agbo kome mli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. In flooded soil, water fills all the air spaces, suffocating the roots and allowing rot fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ mli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my yam plants produce bigger tubers when I make the vines climb up wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ hiɛ bulbs wuji beni mihaa wain tso lɛ kwɔɔ tso ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking exposes yam leaves to direct sunlight so they can perform photosynthesis efficiently, creating the sugars required to build large underground tubers.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛha fotosintɛsis lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa sugar ni he hiaa koni akɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without forming any fruits when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures damage tomato pollen, preventing flowers from getting fertilized. When fertilization fails, the plant sheds the useless flowers to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ tomato ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ afɔ. Kɛji fɔmɔ nii lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why does my land yield less maize every year when I plant maize on the exact same plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil, leading to lower yields over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why did my crops turn yellow and stop growing after I sprayed weedkiller near their base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpa shweremɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie eshishitoo lɛ he lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weedkillers can harm main crops if sprayed too close, as the plant roots absorb the chemicals from the soil. Approved weedkillers must be applied carefully at correct distances and doses to avoid injuring the crop.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye tsei titrii lɛ awui kɛji akɛ afɔse amɛ ashwie amɛhe tsɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei shishifãi gbalaa tsofai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni sa kɛ bɔ ni sa koni akapila tso lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods catch black pod disease more easily when the trees are planted very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black pod hela lɛ yeɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ oya beni adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting cocoa trees too close together blocks sunlight and wind, creating a damp, dark environment under the leaves where fungal spores thrive and spread rapidly between pods.
ga: Kɛ́ adu kokoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ baa baai lɛ ashishi. he ni fungal spores lɛ daa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya yɛ pods lɛ ateŋ lɛ

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different farm chemicals together in the same sprayer tank before spraying my maize?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai enyɔ baafutu yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ kome mli dani mikɛ ŋmãa afɔ ŋmãa nɔ?

english: Mixing unapproved chemicals together can cause a harsh reaction that ruins their power or creates a mixture that burns your crop leaves. Always check labels or ask an extension officer before mixing different products.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛfutuɔ he lɛ baanyɛ aha nɔ ko ni mli wa waa aba aahu akɛ efiteɔ hewalɛ loo ekɛ nɔ ko ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni shãa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai baa. Kwɛmɔ nɔ ni aŋma yɛ nɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be loo bi mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ dani okɛ nibii srɔtoi afutu.

english: Will spraying insect medicine directly onto my fruit trees while they are flowering harm the young fruits?
ga: Ani tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni mikɛshwieɔ mi aduawai tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ baaye aduawai bibii lɛ awui?

english: Spraying chemicals during full flowering can damage delicate flower blossoms and scare away beneficial insects like bees that pollinate your trees, leading to fewer fruits forming.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ, ni etsi kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ anaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibii fioo komɛi ni afɔɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow and burn a few days after I apply chemical sprays?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf burning usually happens when the chemical mixture is too strong, applied during hot sunshine, or when spray drift accidentally lands on sensitive parts of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ baa shãa. Kɛtsu nii yɛ hulutsoo be mli. aloo kɛ́ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ gbee tso lɛ hei ni he hiaa waa lɛ anɔ yɛ oshara mli.

english: If I add more water than the instruction says when mixing my crop medicine, will it still kill the pests on my farm?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo fata he fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ mikɛwo mli beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ futuɔ lɛ hu? Ani ebaagbe kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ lolo?

english: Adding too much water dilutes the chemical, making it too weak to control pests. Weak doses can also teach pests to become resistant to the medicine over time.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu babaoo fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ afee mlɛo. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ ehiii kwraa. Tsofa bibioo ni akɛhaa lɛ hu baanyɛ atsɔɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsofa lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛye tsofa lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do chemical fertilizers imported from abroad sometimes fail to give good yields on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsofai ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ haaa yibii kpakpai aba miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Imported fertilizers are made for general soil types. If your local Ghanaian soil lacks organic matter or has high acidity, the soil cannot absorb the fertilizer nutrients properly until soil health is improved.
ga: Afeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ baa kɛhaa shikpɔji fɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ Ghana shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ nɔ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo eyɛ acid babaoo lɛ, Kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Do crop seeds brought from foreign countries require more chemical sprays than our local traditional seeds?
ga: Ani tsei ahe dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ biɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ babaoo fe wɔ maŋ tsei ahe dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Many foreign seed varieties are bred for high yield but lack natural resistance to local pests and diseases found in our climate, often requiring more careful protection and chemical management.
ga: Akwɛ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui babaoo koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi ebɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni ekɛteɔ shi ewoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni anaa yɛ wɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ biɔ ni abu he jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii.

english: How can I know if a farm chemical sold in the store is actually meant for my specific type of crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ ji miŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni miduɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Every registered chemical has a label specifying approved crops and target pests. Using a chemical on an unapproved crop can poison the plant or leave harmful chemical residue in your harvest.
ga: Tsofa fɛɛ tsofa ni aŋmala awo wolo nɔ lɛ yɛ nɔ ko ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ. Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ agbo loo eshi tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara yɛ okpamɔ lɛ mli.

english: Does putting chemical treatments directly into the soil weaken my fruit trees over time?
ga: Ani tsofai ni mikɛbaafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha mi aduawai tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Overusing harsh chemical treatments in the soil can kill friendly soil organisms like earthworms and good bacteria, which naturally help tree roots absorb water and nutrients.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ sũ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbe sũ mli nibii ni yɔɔ naanyo tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai kpakpai. Nɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛŋɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are my young fruits dropping off the tree prematurely even after I applied chemical treatments?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibii bibii lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ oya beni mikɛ tsofai etsu nii po lɛ?

english: Fruit drop can happen if the tree is stressed by incorrect chemical dosage, or if the tree lacks fundamental needs like water and proper soil nutrients, which pesticides alone cannot solve.
ga: Yibii baanyɛ afite kɛji tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Aloo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ shishijee hiamɔ nii tamɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi pɛ nyɛŋ atsu he nii.

english: Is it true that spraying my crops during the hot afternoon sun can spoil the plants?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ kɛ́ akɛ tsofa shwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛgboi?

english: Yes, high afternoon heat causes liquids on leaves to evaporate quickly, leaving concentrated chemical spots that can scorch leaves and reduce the chemical's effectiveness.
ga: Hɛɛ, shwane mli la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya. Shi tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baanyɛ ashã baai ni eha tsofa lɛ nitsumɔ aba shi lɛ yɛ sɛɛ.
