english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and turn brown when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from larger trees or plantains because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil before their root systems can grow deep enough to reach groundwater.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he.

english: Why does covering the bare soil around my tomato plants with dry grass help them grow during dry hot days?
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ Tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, creating a protective blanket over the soil that blocks sunlight from evaporating water, keeps root temperature cool, and prevents soil moisture loss.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Feemɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli fɛ̃i lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ

english: Pale yellow leaves are usually a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to build green leaves and produce food for growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛfee niyenii kɛha dalɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my main crops improve my soil?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni miduɔ nii titri yɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally adding essential plant food back into the soil for companion crops to use.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Ekɛ tsei niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni tsei ni fata ehe lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops when I plant maize in the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ baa beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same soil nutrients every season and creates a permanent home for specific crop pests and diseases to multiply.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aaaya nɔ akwɛ lɛ baaha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ajɛ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni afee shĩai ni baahi shi daa aha kooloi komɛi ni yeɔ tsei kɛ tsei ahe helai koni amɛshwere.

english: Too many young shoots compete directly with the main mother stem for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which results in smaller bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ nyɛ tso lɛ titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms onto the ground without growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛduuu tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insects like bees to pollinate the flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni aduawai aba.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide inside the center leaves of my young corn plants and eat holes through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer feeding inside the central leaf whorl of young corn because the tender leaves offer both food and shelter from sunlight and predators.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye nii yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ ejaakɛ baa bibii lɛ haa niyenii kɛ wɔɔhe kɛjɛɔ hulu kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my mature cassava roots spoil and rot underground if heavy rain falls right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa dani akpa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains soak the soil completely, leaving no air for root respiration, which causes stagnant water to harbor rot-causing bacteria and fungi that attack wet cassava tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nuɔ kwraa. ni eshiuuu kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni shishifãi lɛ amu Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ hiɛɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ni tutuaa ŋmei shishifãi ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from last season's harvest produce a smaller yield compared to certified store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nyɛsɛɛ be ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ahe kɛjɛ shwapoi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred for high vigor, disease resistance, and uniform growth, whereas seeds saved repeatedly over time lose their genetic strength and yield potential.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha hewalɛ, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. yɛ be mli ni akɛ dumɔwui lɛ toɔ shii abɔ Beni be hoɔ lɛ, ebɛ fɔmɔ su mli hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ yibii.

english: I heard about a crop called taro; will it grow well on the wet, swampy parts of my land where other crops rot?
ga: Minu tso ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ taro lɛ he. Ani ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ, he ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi miifite yɛ lɛ?

english: Taro loves moisture and naturally thrives in wet or swampy soils where crops like maize would rot, making it ideal for low-lying areas on your farm.
ga: Taro sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni edaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa baafite yɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does rainwater roll off taro leaves like drops of oil instead of soaking into them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ shwieɔ taro baai lɛ anɔ tamɔ fɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ mli lɛ?

english: Taro leaves have a natural waxy coating and microscopic surface bumps that repel water, protecting the leaf from fungal rot and shedding excess water quickly.
ga: Taro baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli waxy ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe kɛ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ bibioo waa ni shwieɔ nu. Ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe ni ejieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ oya.

english: Does taro need full sunlight all day, or can I plant it in the shade under taller crops?
ga: Taros biɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ loo abaanyɛ akwɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ tsei kakadaji ashishi.

english: Taro is naturally shade-tolerant, which means it can grow successfully under the canopy of taller crops like plantains or trees while still producing tubers.
ga: Taro ji tso ko ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ebaanyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantain loo tsei ashishi. Be mli ni eyɔɔ yitso lolo lɛ

english: How can I tell that my taro tubers are mature and ready to harvest under the ground just by looking at the leaves?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ taro shishifã ko ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: When taro reaches maturity, its leaves will naturally begin to yellow, shrink, and droop because the plant stops growing leaves and shifts its remaining energy into the underground tuber.
ga: Kɛ́ taro lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Ebaai lɛ baaje shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ, amɛbaagbɔjɔ, ni amɛbaagbee shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei kpaɔ baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni amɛjieɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever heavy wind and rain hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni naa wa baatswa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that stay near the top layer of the soil rather than deep taproots, making the tall, heavy trees easy for strong winds to push over unless supported.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa tsei kakadaji ni tsii lɛ, ja mɔ ko fiɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why do small shoots keep growing around the base of my main plantain stem, and should I leave them all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ɔ ebɔleɔ Mi plantain shishitoo titri lɛ he Ni ani esa akɛ mashi fɛɛ yɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plantains naturally produce side shoots called suckers to reproduce. Leaving too many suckers forces them to compete with the main tree for food and water, which reduces your final yield.
ga: Plantains woɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii koni amɛkɛfɔ bii. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo ni nuɔ nu lɛ, ebaanyɛ amɛnɔ ni amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha onaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: How do I propagate new plantain crops if the tree does not produce seeds like maize or vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ magbɛ plantain tsei heei ashwã? Kɛji tso lɛ wooo dumɔwui, tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai

english: Plantains do not grow from seeds; instead, farmers plant young side shoots called suckers or cut up the healthy underground root bulb (corm) to sprout new plants.
ga: Plantains jɛɛɛ dumɔwui amli ekwɛ̃ɔ. Okwaafoi baadu tsei bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots loo amɛbaafolɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli wa (corms) koni amɛkwɛ tsei heei.

english: Why do the trunk stems of my plantain trees feel soft and wet inside when I cut them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ kɛ́ afo lɛ?

english: Plantains are not woody trees but giant herbaceous plants, and their trunks are made of tightly wrapped leaf layers that store vast amounts of water to fuel fast leaf and fruit growth.
ga: Plantains jeee tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo. Shi eji tso wulu ko ni ji jwɛi. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ji baai ni akɛwo mli shiŋŋ koni nu babaoo ahi mli koni eha baai kɛ aduawai lɛ adalɛ oya.

english: I have a lot of dead plantain leaves and cut stems piling up after harvest; how do these crop remains behave if I leave them on the soil?
ga: Miyɛ plantain baai ni egboi kɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi babaoo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Te nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ baafee amɛnii amɛha tɛŋŋ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Plantain stems and leaves hold water and break down slowly, creating a thick organic cover (mulch) that keeps the soil cool, holds moisture, and turns into nutrient-rich compost for future crops.
ga: Plantain tsei kɛ baai lɛ toɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ fiofio. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eji ŋmɔshi nibii (mulch) ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my plantain plant turn yellow and dry up as new leaves come out at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni baai heei jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: This is a natural shedding behavior where the plant directs nutrients from older, outer leaves to nourish new top growth and the developing fruit cluster.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli tso lɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ subaŋ ni tso lɛ heɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kponɔgbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee kɛ aduawai akui ni miiya hiɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: If I move my farm to a new piece of land, how can I quickly tell if the soil is good for crops?
ga: Kɛji mijie miŋmɔ lɛ kɛtee he hee Te mafee tɛŋŋ male oya kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: You can look at what is naturally growing on the land. Dark soil with earthworms and deep-rooted, healthy green weeds usually means high fertility. You can also squeeze damp soil in your hand—if it holds shape loosely without turning into hard clay, it will hold moisture and food well for crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona nibii ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ jwɛi eŋɔli yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ ebaawo fɔmɔ babaoo. Obaanyɛ okɛ sũ ni mli efɔ hu awo oniji amli. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli mlɛo ni efeee shikpɔŋ ni wa Ebaahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant the exact same crop in the same soil every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of the specific food that crop needs and allows pests and diseases that like that crop to build up in the ground. Switching crops, especially planting beans or groundnuts, rebuilds soil fertility and starves crop pests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tamɔ tsei baanyɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni tsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii Titri lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ. ni hɔmɔ aye ŋmeii lɛ anɔ

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in an upside-down 'V' pattern, it usually means the maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for green growth. Adding fertilizer or compost and ensuring proper soil drainage helps fix this problem.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ni ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves but give me small cassava roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ cassava shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava plants focus energy on leaves instead of roots if the soil has too much nitrogen or if they receive too much shade. Clearing nearby bush to give them full sunlight helps the plant store its energy underground in the tubers.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo enáa hulutsoo babaoo. Kɛ́ afo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe babaoo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: On hot or windy days, crops lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it up from the ground. This daytime wilting is a natural defense to protect against heat, and plants usually recover in the evening when temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo be mli ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Ni tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing any peppers when it gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa kɛji edɔ lɛ?

english: Extremely high heat causes pepper flowers to dry out and fall off before fruit can form. Watering the soil around the base early in the morning and providing light shade during peak sun helps the plant keep its flowers and make fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he nu leebi, ni aha lɛ hulutsoo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive and easily get burned under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as living shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist for its first couple of years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa ni amɛshãa oya. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off without turning into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ anɔkwa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off if the trees suffer from dry soil, direct hot sun, or if there are no tiny insects (midges) to pollinate them. Maintaining shade trees on the farm keeps the air humid and creates a good environment for these helpful insects.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ na tso lɛ he amanehulu. hulu la ni mli edɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) bɛ ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ, tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tseɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ kpakpa baa kɛha kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and drying during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl to shield themselves from losing water in intense sun, or because small sap-sucking insects like whiteflies are attacking them. Mulching the soil with dry grass and spraying organic neem oil can help protect the leaves.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ he. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies lɛ miitutua amɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie nɔ ni akɛ organic neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Yam plants make food for underground tubers through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so the leaves get maximum sunshine, good air movement, and stay away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ebaai ni hulu la tsuɔ nii lɛ feɔ niyenii ehaa eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ jɛmɛ. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ ahe

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Keeping some shade trees or planting plantains around them provides a cool canopy that protects the cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Tso lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni baabu kookoo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to give my yam vines long wooden sticks to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji kakadaji he hiaa mi lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves high up to capture sunlight and make food for big tubers. Staking keeps the leaves dry and healthy, preventing rots caused by wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ hulu la ni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ bulb agboi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ haa egbiɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow from the tip inwards, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build strong leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plant its green color back.
ga: Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛtee mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why did my plants wither after I placed chemical fertilizer directly against their main stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that draw moisture out of the stem if touched directly, burning the tissue. Fertilizer should always be applied a few inches away from the stem in a ring or hole so roots can absorb it safely.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli kɛji akɛ amɛkpe tɛ̃ɛ. Ebaaha fãji lɛ ashã. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be fɛɛ be yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi 2-3 yɛ ring loo bu lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year when I keep planting maize in the exact same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi beni miyaa nɔ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same spot continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills nitrogen into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaakɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are small worms hiding inside the center leaves of my young maize plants and chewing holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the tender young leaves inside the heart of the maize plant. Spraying safe pesticides or neem extract into the leaf funnel early in the morning destroys the worms before they ruin the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tswaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem mli nu lɛ shwie baai lɛ amli leebi lɛ, ebaakpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛbaakpãtã tso lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling upwards and looking crumpled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the leaf sap and spreading viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem spray or recommended insecticides stops the leaves from crumpling.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baa mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ baa. Akɛ neem spray loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe nii mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. Mulching the soil with dry grass and watering regularly keeps the roots cool and helps the plant hold onto flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi wo tso lɛ nɔ ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi ebaawo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the soil during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on flat land for a long time, the roots drown and decay, so planting cassava on raised ridges allows extra water to drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete for soil food, water, and sunlight. Giving each plant proper space ensures every stalk gets enough food to build large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nu lɛ mli, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa amɛ fɛɛ amɛnáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the crowded plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow tall and weak trying to reach the sun, leaving them with very little energy to grow large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni mli wa lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ amɛmiitao ni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛnáa hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it necessary for me to pull out some healthy seedlings after my seeds germinate?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: Removing extra seedlings, known as thinning, creates enough space, airflow, and soil food for the remaining crops. If too many seedlings remain crowded in one spot, none of them will receive enough nutrients to grow into strong plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni fa fe nine lɛ ajiemɔ Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ thinning. baaha kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle ŋwɛi ni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui babaoo eyi he kome lɛ, Tso ko bɛ ni baaná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eda ni efee tso ni he wa.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Tall shade trees or plantain plants shield the young cocoa from intense heat and dry winds, keeping the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei loo dumɔwui ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yam vines produce leaves that need direct exposure to sunlight to feed the tuber growing underground. Staking lifts the vines off the shaded, damp ground toward the light, preventing leaf decay and helping the yam produce bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ baai ni he hiaa hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni eye ebua bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa la lɛ he. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ agbo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potato lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my pepper farm produce plenty of big green leaves but very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ baai agboi babaoo shi pepper fioo pɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or plants are too crowded, the crop puts all its energy into growing thick stems and leaves instead of flowers and fruits. Pruning excess leaves helps redirect the plant's energy toward producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo tsei lɛ ebɔi tsɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo tsei kɛ baai ni mli tse yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Baai ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai afeemɔ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves on my tomato plants turn yellow and fall off as the plant grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni tso lɛ miida lɛ?

english: As tomato plants get taller and bushier, upper leaves shade the lower ones from sunlight. Deprived of light, the lower leaves can no longer produce food for the plant, so the tomato drops them to focus its energy on growing new leaves and fruit at the top.
ga: Beni tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ yitsɔi lɛ, Ŋwɛi baa lɛ haa shishigbɛ baa lɛ he feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Kɛji la bɛ lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii aha tso lɛ dɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tomato lɛ shiɔ lɛ koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai heei kɛ aduawai ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than my cassava even when I plant them at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mi-cassava lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, aggressive roots that absorb water and fertilizer much faster than cultivated crops. If you do not clear them early, they crowd out the slow-growing cassava plants and steal the food needed for root expansion.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji ojieee mli mra lɛ, Efoɔ ŋmei tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ amli ni ejuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do fungal diseases spread so fast when my garden bushes become thick and overgrown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya nɛkɛ be mli ni tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ?

english: Overgrown crops block breeze from flowing between the branches, trapping moisture and heat around the stems. This damp environment allows fungal diseases to multiply quickly and spread easily from leaf to leaf when plants touch.
ga: Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ateŋ lɛ naa. Akɛni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ mɔ̃ɔ tsei lɛ ahe hewɔ lɛ, nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ nɛɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ baa kome nɔ kɛyaa baa kroko nɔ kɛ́ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe kpe.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl inward like small tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli tamɔ jwɛi bibii yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves curl up during intense heat as a natural defence to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun. This helps the plant trap moisture inside and prevent water loss through evaporation until the weather cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ koni akɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ baa shi lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ni ehaaa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ naa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose smaller yields when I plant them on the same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yibiiwoo fioo pɛ kɛ́ adu yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop on a field continuously exhausts the specific nutrients that plant needs from the soil. Over time, the soil becomes depleted, causing crop yields to shrink unless you rotate with legumes or let the land rest.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be. Be ni be shwieɔ mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baa shi. Ja okɛ ŋmeii tsake loo oha shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe.

english: Why can't I just plant my seeds very close together so I can harvest more crops from a small land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ he ko bibioo lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. This makes all the plants grow weak and thin, producing smaller yields than if they were given proper space.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo fioo fe kɛji akɛ aha he ko ni sa.

english: Why do I need to make soil mounds or ridges before planting my cassava and yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ dani madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei?

english: Mounds loosen the soil so tubers have soft ground to grow big and long. Loose soil also helps rainwater drain properly so the tubers under the ground do not sit in water and rot.
ga: Gɔji lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha bulb lɛ afee shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛdara ni amɛdara. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii lɛ akabote nu mli ni amɛkafite.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant are usually a sign of nitrogen hunger. The plant is pulling nitrogen from its old lower leaves to feed the new top leaves. Adding fertilizer like urea can restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen hɔmɔ miiye amɛ. Tsei miihe nitrogen kɛmiijɛ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni efee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people tell me not to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ mikadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize eats a lot of the same nutrients from the soil every season. Planting it in the same spot repeatedly drains the ground and causes crop pests to multiply. Swapping maize with cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ babaoo daa be. Dumɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu atsɔ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo baa Kɛ́ akɛ tsina loo ŋmei tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava have very leafy green stems above ground, but small roots when I dig it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tsei ni baai eŋɔli babaoo yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii yɛ kɛji atsa?

english: If soil has too much rich manure or nitrogen, or if the plants get too much water, the cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems instead of storing food in the underground roots.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo nitrogen babaoo loo kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ akwɛmɔ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Tomato flowers drop without forming fruit when weather gets too hot, when water supply is irregular, or when tiny pests bite the flower stems. Keeping soil moist and managing pests helps the flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ŋmɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni etsɔɔ tomatoi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking juice from under the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by these insects. Spraying early with neem water or soapy water helps clear them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Neem nu loo samla nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ mli atse.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. If your seeds sprout during that heat wave, the young shoots will dry up and die. It is safer to wait until the rains are regular before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baanɛ dani odu.

english: Does leaving weeds on my farm really affect my harvest, or can I wait until harvest time to clear them?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ aloo manyɛ mamɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli dani majie jwɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops. If you leave weeds to grow alongside your crops during the early weeks, your crops will get stunted and yield far less harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee mlɛo ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Why are so many farmers around here switching from growing maize to planting cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ nɛkɛ he nɛɛ miitsake kɛmiijɛ ŋmãa dumɔ mli kɛmiiya kookoo dumɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a reliable cash crop that commands a high market price and provides a steady income for many years once established, helping farmers earn significantly more than they usually make from seasonal food crops.
ga: Cocoa ji shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni jara wa waa ni ekɛ shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ha afii babaoo beni ato shishi lɛ. Ehaa okwaafoi naa shika babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaaná kɛjɛ niyenii ni amɛduɔ yɛ be mli lɛ mli.

english: Should I use the seeds saved from my father's old harvest or buy new seeds for my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ mitsɛ kpamɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii loo mahe dumɔwui heei kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: New hybrid seeds are specifically bred to grow faster, resist common diseases, and produce more cocoa pods compared to old seeds saved from previous generations.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛdara oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ekɛ kookoo ŋmeii babaoo baa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui momoi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛ yinɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field with full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under harsh, direct sunlight; they need shade from temporary nurse crops like plantains or big trees to retain moisture and survive their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei wuji amli. Koni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How can I feed my family while I wait for my newly planted cocoa trees to start making money?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ miweku lɛ yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ kookoo tsei heei ni adu lɛ koni amɛje shika ni amɛná lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: You can intercrop short-term food crops like plantain, cassava, or cocoyam alongside young cocoa trees; these food crops mature quickly to provide food and extra cash while providing natural shade for the cocoa.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii ni heɔ be kuku tamɔ plantain, cassava loo cocoa yɛ cocoa tsei bibii ahe. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ miiya hiɛ oya akɛ niyenii kɛ shika kroko ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kookoo lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo.

english: How many years will it take after planting cocoa before I can start harvesting pods and selling them?
ga: Kɛ́ adu kookoo sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa ŋmeii lɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa trees usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties take 5 years or longer to yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo tsei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo tsei ni etsɛ waa lɛ heɔ afii 5 loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do cocoa trees drop their flowers and leaves when the dry harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ afɔfɔi kɛ baai lɛ fiteɔ beni Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: During the dry harmattan season, cocoa trees naturally drop flowers and leaves to conserve precious water in their stems and protect themselves from drought stress.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ Cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi kɛ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛto nu ni jara wa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ he. ni obu ohe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ he

english: How can I tell if the soil on my land in the Bono region is good for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Bono kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cocoa thrives best in dark, deep, well-drained loamy soil that retains moisture without holding stagnant water, and where plant leaves easily rot into rich organic compost.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehiɛɛɛ nu mli Ni hei ni tsei ahe baai lɛ miifite yɛ lɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa nii oya.

english: Will growing cocoa on the same piece of land for many years destroy the soil for future crops?
ga: Ani kookoo ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii babaoo lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ ni akɛbaadu nii yɛ wɔsɛɛ be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa takes specific nutrients from the soil over time, but keeping shade trees, returning empty pod husks to the ground, and using proper fertilizers maintains soil fertility for decades.
ga: Cocoa nine shɛɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Shi tsei ni aaaha amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo mli lɛ Kuu pod shwiili ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: What is this Black Pod disease that people warn me about, and how does it hurt my cocoa?
ga: Mɛni ji black pod hela ni mɛi babaoo miibɔ mi kɔkɔ yɛ he lɛ? Ni te eyeɔ mikoo lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Black Pod is a fungal infection that spreads fast during heavy rains and cool shade, turning healthy green cocoa pods black and rotting the beans inside, making them unsellable.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ehaa kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa anyɛɛɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my healthy cocoa trees when they are growing so big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ekomɛi amli be mli ni amɛmiida waa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches so air and sunlight can reach the tree, which prevents diseases from taking hold and encourages the plant to produce bigger pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haaa hela aba tso lɛ nɔ, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tso bibioo lɛ shã ni egbo beni mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their leaves are tender and burn easily. Keeping shade trees or planting plantains around them creates a cool shelter that holds soil moisture and protects the young plants until they are strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Tsei lɛ feɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebuɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ amɛhe waa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and curling up in the dry heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo la ni mli egbi mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing water during hot spells, and yellowing usually means the plant is starving for nitrogen in the soil or lacks enough water to absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ feɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye lɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by extreme hot weather, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to conserve energy for survival instead of producing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ haomɔ ba Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei baawo yibii lɛ, amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even though the leaves above ground are tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ?

english: When soil has too much leafy fertilizer (nitrogen) or too much shade, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing tall stems and thick leaves instead of sending food down into the tubers below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ baai amli ŋmɔshi nibii (nitrogen) babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai bibii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛya shi kɛya ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do my orange trees produce heavy fruits this year but yield almost nothing the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange lɛ wo yibii babaoo afi nɛɛ shi afi ni baa lɛ ewooo yibii kwraa lɛ?

english: Orange trees can exhaust all their stored energy producing a huge harvest. If they do not get enough water and manure after harvest, they rest the following year to regain their strength before bearing heavy fruit again.
ga: Akutu tso lɛ baanyɛ ashã hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ kwraa. nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibii babaoo Kɛji amɛnáaa nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ Amɛbaajɔɔ amɛhe yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ dani amɛwo yibii ni tsii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees take so long to produce bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantain trees are planted too close, their large leaves block sunlight from reaching each other and their roots fight for the same food in the soil, which slows down their growth and delays fruiting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso lɛ baai wuji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha edalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha aduawai lɛ aba sɛɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help my crops yield better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ haa mi ŋmãa lɛ yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the ground through their roots. This acts as a natural soil builder that nourishes the maize next to it while covering the ground to keep the soil moist.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ tswalɔ ni haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii. be mli ni ekɛ mulching tsuɔ nii koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die within days even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a disease in the ground that clogs the water pipes inside the plant stem, preventing water from reaching the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Ehaa nu nyɛɛɛ abote baai lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds make my vegetable crops look pale and thin if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji mijieee jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most vegetables, so they steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil before your crop can get them, leaving your vegetables hungry and weak.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe aduawai babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anine shɛɔ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye o-vegetables lɛ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so quickly after I dig them out of the earth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if their skin gets scratched during digging or if they are stored in hot, unventilated places. Small cuts allow germs and fungi in the air and soil to enter and spoil the flesh.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafite oya kɛji akɛ atsɔ amɛhewolo nɔ yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli ni edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nibii bibii ni afolɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie helatsɛmɛi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ sũ mli ni efite loo lɛ.

english: Lower maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient it pulls from the soil to stay green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its color and strength to produce good ears.
ga: Abele baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii mli hewalɛ ko ni he hiaa ni tsei gbalaa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli. Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa su kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ koni amɛwo toi kpakpai.

english: Why does placing chemical fertilizer directly against my plant stem burn it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ shãa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts that pull moisture out of the plant's stem and delicate roots. Leaving space between the stem and the fertilizer prevents tissue damage while allowing roots to feed safely.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ashi gbɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ehaa fãji lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ yeɔ nii shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and cool soil moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my yam plants produce bigger tubers when I stake them with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko tswa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need maximum sunlight to make food for their tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, improving sunlight exposure and preventing leaf rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo koni amɛha amɛ bulbs lɛ niyenii. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites living under the leaves. Their feeding weakens the plant and can spread viruses that stop new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Amɛ niyenii lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni haa tsei heei daa lɛ eshwa.

english: Why do fall armyworms target the deep center of young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Armyworms feed inside the inner tender leaves (the whorl) of young maize because those leaves are softest to chew and protect the insects from hot sun and predators.
ga: Asraafoi akuu lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli baai bibii (rings) lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ baai nɛɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ ni anyɛɔ ayeɔ, ni ebuɔ kooloi ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants face extreme heat, lack water, or miss out on insect pollination. Keeping soil moisture consistent and protecting plants during heat waves helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu bɛ ehe, loo kooloi fɔfɔii lɛ shɛɛɛ amɛhe. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ tsei ahebuu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni shwereɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of thick leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai lɛ mli tse waa shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When cowpea plants receive too much nitrogen, they put energy into growing green leaves instead of flowers. Balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to produce flowers and healthy pods.
ga: Kɛji cowpea tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo baai eŋɔli yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does weedicide spray accidentally hurt my main crop even if I target weeds?
ga: Te tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ awui yɛ oshara mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ mihe miiwo jwɛi lɛ amli moŋ?

english: Weedicides absorb into plant tissues. If drift or overspray touches crop leaves, the active chemical can stunt plant growth, yellow leaves, or kill the crop along with nearby weeds.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ boteɔ tsei lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ aerosols loo sprays ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ tsei ahe baai lɛ kpe Tsofai ni tsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ahi shi, baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ, loo amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn watery and rot after heavy rains flood the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ náa nu ni fiteɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni eha ŋmɔji lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When fields stay flooded, oxygen is blocked, causing roots to drown and fungal rot to spread quickly underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu eyi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli lolo lɛ, abaatsi Oxygen naa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Ni ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning brown and withering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees wither when they do not get enough water, when exposed to high heat, or when their roots are damaged. Keeping heat sources away and ensuring proper moisture helps keep the leaves green.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ gboɔ kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba mli loo shishifãi lɛ efite Kɛ́ hulutsoo jɛɛhe lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi ŋmɔŋ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa tree is dying or just needs water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi cacao tsei lɛ miigboi loo nu kɛkɛ he miihia amɛ?

english: If a tree is just thirsty, its leaves will droop and dry up, but giving it clean water around the base will help it recover within a few days as long as the trunk and roots are still healthy.
ga: Kɛji kumai ye tso lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ Ebaai lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagbi. Shi nu ni mli tse ni akɛhaa kɛbɔleɔ The base lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli, kɛji akɛ eshishifãi lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ yɛ hewalɛ.

english: Can a cocoa tree recover after its leaves have completely dried up?
ga: Ani cacao tso lɛ baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ beni baai lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: If the dry leaves are caused by temporary heat or lack of water, prompt watering and removing the cause of stress can bring the tree back to life, provided the roots are not dead.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni baa be kukuoo mli loo nu ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbi lɛ ba Nu ni awoɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ajieɔ nɔ ni kɛ haomɔ baa lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aba wala mli ekoŋŋ. ni shishifãi lɛ gbooo

english: Can I keep my motorized spraying machine or generator right next to my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ loo tsɔne ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ama cacao tsei lɛ ahe?

english: No, running machines or exhaust engines near cocoa trees generate heat and fumes that dry out the soil and scorch nearby leaves, causing the tree to wither quickly.
ga: Dabi, tsɔnei loo tsɔne mli la ni hoɔ yɛ cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ lasu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni shãa baai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ gbɔɔ oya.

english: What should I do if I notice a cocoa tree next to my farm machinery is starting to dry up?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina akɛ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli tsɔnei ahe lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔ?

english: You should immediately move the machine away from the tree. Leaving heat-producing equipment next to a cocoa tree for even a few days can cause permanent damage or kill the tree.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie tsɔne lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ashi tsɔne ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo tso nɔ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite tso lɛ daa loo egbe lɛ.

english: Does exhaust heat from farm engines affect the soil around my crops?
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli tsɔnei amli lɛ saa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ he. Miŋmɔshi nibii loo daabi?

english: Yes, continuous heat from engine exhausts bakes the soil, evaporating all the natural moisture that the tree's roots need to drink.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, la ni tsoɔ be fɛɛ be kɛjɛɔ tsɔne lɛ mli la lɛ mli lɛ baashã shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ni adebɔɔ mli nu fɛɛ ni he hiaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How much water do I need to mix with my fertilizer before applying it to cocoa?
ga: Nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mikɛfutu kookoo mli?

english: Fertilizers must be diluted with the exact amount of water recommended on the package; using too little water creates a solution that is too strong and will burn your tree's roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ nu ni atsɔɔ yɛ tsɔne lɛ nɔ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Nu fioo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha tsabaa ko ni mli wa tsɔ aba ni ebaashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Is it safe to apply fertilizer to a cocoa tree that is already dry and withered?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaawo kookoo tsei ni egbi ni egbo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: No, applying fertilizer to an already thirsty or heat-stressed tree can make the dry conditions worse. You must give the tree clean water first before applying chemical nutrients.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shihilɛ ni mli egbi lɛ aya hiɛ waa. Esa akɛ oha otsei lɛ nu ni mli tse dani okɛ tsofai ni haa mɔ hewalɛ awo mli.

english: Why did my cocoa tree start withering after I applied liquid fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi beni mikɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ewo mli lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the fertilizer solution was mixed with too little water or applied in intense heat, causing the solution to draw moisture out of the plant instead of feeding it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ akɛ nu fioo ko pɛ futu ŋmɔshi nibii amli loo akɛwo he ko ni mli edɔ waa. Enɛ haa tsofa lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeekɛwo mli.

english: Can I use any water I find on the farm to mix my chemical fertilizers?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni anaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afutu tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: You should use clean water in the correct quantity to mix fertilizer, ensuring there are no oils or engine chemicals mixed into it that could harm the cocoa roots.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ nu ni mli tse ni sa atsu nii kɛ́ oofutu ŋmɔshi nibii. Kwɛmɔ akɛ tsɔne mli fɔ loo tsofai komɛi efutu mli ni baanyɛ aye kookoo shishifãi lɛ awui.

english: Should I cut down all the big trees on my land before I plant my cassava?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani madu ŋmei?

english: You do not need to cut down every tree. While cassava needs sunlight, leaving selected mature trees provides shade, preserves soil moisture, and protects the land from strong winds and erosion.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni ofo tso fɛɛ tso. Eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la he miihia ŋmei moŋ Shi tsei wuji ni ahala lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ baaha ená hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he.

english: Do big forest trees steal all the water and nutrients away from my food crops?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ miiju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ mi niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ mli?

english: Large trees mostly feed from deep underground using deep taproots, while food crops like cassava and plantain feed from the upper soil level. When spaced properly, big trees and shallow crops can share the land without competing heavily.
ga: Tsei wuji babaoo naa niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ anɔ. yɛ be mli ni ayeɔ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ plantain kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Beni gbɛ ni jɛkɛ lɛ sa Tsei wuji kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ekɔɔɔ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛja he ni akaŋshii babaoo bɛ mli.

english: Can I plant food crops like plantain together with long-term trees on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii, tamɔ plantains, ni tsei ni etsɛ waa yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, planting food crops alongside trees is a good strategy. Fast-growing crops like plantain provide food and early shelter, while long-term trees grow slowly and protect the soil for years to come.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ tsei ahe lɛ ji ŋaa kpakpa. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantain lɛ haa niyenii kɛ wɔɔhe oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ daa fiofio ni amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ afii ni baa lɛ amli.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with many leaves but producing tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi shishifãi fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much shade or too much nitrogen in the soil, it directs its energy into growing tall stems and leafy foliage instead of storing food in the underground tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ebaakudɔ ehewalɛ lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ baai. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose water rapidly under direct heat. During dry spells, the leaves turn yellow and dry up as a self-defense mechanism to save water in the stem.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai agboi ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ wo mli tɛ̃ɛ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ amɛhe koni akɛbu nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the ground. When the soil becomes soft from rain and the plant bears heavy fruit bunches, strong winds can pull the roots out.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ fee blɛoo kɛjɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli ni tsei lɛ wo aduawai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: Does cassava grow better in loose soil or hard, packed soil?
ga: Ani ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse loo shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ?

english: Cassava needs soft, well-drained soil so its roots can expand easily underground. Hard soil restricts root expansion, leading to small and crooked tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia cassava. bɔni afee ni eshishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi oya. Shikpɔŋ ni wa haaa shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ ji bibioo ni ebɔle ehe.

english: Will keeping a crop plantation on the same land for ten years make the soil infertile?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii nyɔŋma lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni wooo nii?

english: Continuous farming can reduce soil nutrients, but if trees are left on the farm, their falling leaves rot and naturally feed the soil, keeping it fertile over many years.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Shi kɛji akɛ ashi tso lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei ahe baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ yibii afii babaoo.

english: How long can a perennial tree crop farm stay productive before the yield starts dropping?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmɔ ni ŋmɔ mli nibii ni yeɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii dani nibii ni aduɔ lɛ aje shishi eba shi?

english: With proper weed control, soil management, and pruning, many perennial tree crop plantations can remain productive for 20 to 30 years or more.
ga: Kɛtsɔ jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ, shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Tsoji babaoo ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii afii 20 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: How do I know when my old farm trees are too old and need to be replaced?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni atsake amɛ?

english: When trees stop producing healthy new leaves, show signs of severe rot or disease, and produce low yields continuously despite good rainfall, they have reached the end of their productive life and should be replanted.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ kpa baai heei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ feemɔ Ejieɔ fitemɔ loo hela ni naa wa he okadii kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi be fɛɛ be yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baashɛ esɛɛnamɔ shihilɛ naagbee ni esa akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to plant my cucumber seeds directly in the main field or nurse them first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu kukumba dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo makwɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Nursing seeds in small trays or protected nursery beds allows them to sprout safely away from heavy rain, pests, and severe heat. Once they sprout and become strong seedlings, you can safely transplant them into your main growing area for a higher survival rate.
ga: Aduɔ dumɔwui yɛ tsɛnsii bibii amli loo tsɛnsii ni abuɔ he lɛ amli koni eye ebua ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛbatsɔ dumɔwui ni he wa Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ aya he titri ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe koni amɛhi shi babaoo.

english: How do I know when my young sprouted seedlings are ready to be moved to the main farm area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni midumɔwui bibii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings are ready for transplanting when they have grown strong roots and developed their first set of true leaves, usually a few weeks after sprouting. At this stage, they are sturdy enough to handle being moved without dying.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaadu kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa ni amɛjie amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ baai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ kpo. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu nii kɛji ajie amɛ ni amɛgbooo.

english: How can I protect my fragile young seedlings from dying when I am transplanting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbo kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo he kroko?

english: Always water the nursery tray before moving seedlings so the roots stay moist. Lift them gently by the root ball or leaf rather than squeezing the main stem, and plant them immediately into moist soil so the roots do not dry out.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ha nu awo dumɔwui lɛ amli dani okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo he kroko. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, okɛ shishifã bɔɔlu loo baa awo nɔ blɛoo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomimɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ni odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Koni shishifãi lɛ akagbi.

english: I hear about farmers growing crops inside plastic domes or greenhouse structures; how does that help my plants?
ga: Minu okwaafoi ni duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ plastic dome loo greenhouse mli. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ no yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ?

english: Growing crops inside a dome protects them from harsh weather, scorching sun, heavy downpours, and outdoor pests. It creates a controlled environment where crops grow faster and produce clean, healthy yields all year round.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ dome mli lɛ buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe. Hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kponɔgbɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Feɔ shihilɛ ko ni akudɔɔ He ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do climbing crops like cucumbers need physical support structures or ropes inside the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɔɔ tamɔ kukumba he hiaa gbɔmɔtsoŋ yelikɛbuamɔ nibii loo kpãi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Climbing crops need support to grow off the ground. Lifting the stems onto ropes or stakes keeps the leaves and fruits clean, prevents soil-borne fungal diseases, increases air circulation, and makes harvesting much easier.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔɔ lɛ he miihia yelikɛbuamɔ bɔni afee ni amɛda kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ awó tso lɛ shishi yɛ kpã loo tso nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa kɛ aduawai lɛ ahe tseɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ anaa ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ Ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Where should I get my cucumber seeds to make sure my farm yields well?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mahe kukumba dumɔwui yɛ koni maná ŋmaa kpakpa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to purchase certified seeds from approved agricultural dealers rather than using saved seeds. Certified seeds have high germination rates, sprout uniformly, and are bred to resist common crop diseases.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ dɛŋ. Yɛ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ waa. Ekwɛ̃ɔ daa ni efɔɔ kɛha tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ahe shitee-kɛ-woo

english: What is a fertigation system, and how does it work on a crop farm?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔtoo? Ni te etsuɔ ​​nii ehaa tɛŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli?

english: Fertigation is a modern farming method where liquid plant nutrients are mixed into the water supply and delivered directly to the crops through a network of pipes. This allows plants to drink and feed at the same time.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛ ko. Ekɛ tsei amli niyenii ni ji nu lɛ futuɔ nu mli ni ekɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ paipii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Ehaa tsei nuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why is using a network of pipes better for watering my crops than carrying buckets of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ paipii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ hi fe baagi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ?

english: Pipe networks deliver water steadily directly to the root zone of each plant. This saves you heavy daily labor, uses water efficiently without waste, and keeps crop leaves dry to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Paipii ni yaa nɔ etsɔɔ nu lɛ gbɛ kɛyaa tso fɛɛ tso shishifã he. Enɛ haaa otsu nitsumɔ ni tsii daa gbi. Kɛ nu atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni okɛfiteee. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei ahe baai lɛ agbiɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Do crops growing inside covered dome structures still need regular watering and feeding?
ga: Ani tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋwɛitsu ko mli lɛ he miihia lolo ni afɔ amɛ nu kɛ niyenii daa?

english: Yes, because covered domes block natural rain, crops inside rely completely on you for water and food. A pipe system must be used daily to supply the exact moisture and plant food they need to grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ dome ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ teeɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ damɔ onɔ kwraa kɛha nu kɛ niyenii. Esa akɛ akɛ paipii gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ atsu nii daa gbi koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ aha amɛdalɛ.

english: What are the key things cucumber plants need to produce large, healthy fruits?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii titrii ni he hiaa kukumba tso koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Cucumbers need consistent moisture at their roots, balanced plant food, warmth, and upright support so the heavy fruits do not touch wet soil and rot before harvest.
ga: Kukumba he miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi eshishifãi lɛ amli be fɛɛ be. Tso niyenii ni sa, dɔlɛ kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ koni aduawai ni tsii akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he ni egbo dani akpa.

english: Yellow and curling leaves are often caused by a plant virus, which acts like a sickness in crops. Tiny insects carry these viruses from plant to plant, stopping them from growing strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ tso mli helai kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli Kplukai bibii hiɛɔ nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko mli. koni ekɛtsi amɛhewalɛ naa.

english: Can crops get sick with viruses just like human beings do?
ga: Ani tsei baanyɛ aná helai ni gbeɔ mɔ tamɔ adesai?

english: Yes, plants can get infected by viruses just like people do. While plant viruses cannot harm human health, they make crops weak, stunt their growth, and reduce the amount of food they produce.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei baanyɛ aná helai ni gbeɔ mɔ tamɔ adesai pɛpɛɛpɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yeee adesa hewalɛnamɔ lɛ awui moŋ, Shi amɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. etsĩɔ dalɛ naa ni ehaa niyenii ni anáa lɛ baa shi

english: How can I tell if my maize leaves are dry because of sun or because of a disease?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ egbi kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli loo hela emɔ amɛ?

english: Sun heat causes leaves to wilt in the afternoon and recover at night, but disease usually creates strange spots, yellow lines, or patches that stay on the leaves even after heavy rain.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli, ni ehaa amɛhe feɔ fɛo gbɛkɛ. Shi bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ baa. No hiɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa po sɛɛ.

english: If one crop on my farm gets sick, will it spread to all my other crops?
ga: Kɛji hela mɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eko Ebaagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi amli. Mi fɛɛ?

english: Many plant sicknesses spread quickly through wind, farm tools, or insects moving from sick plants to healthy ones. Removing and destroying sick plants early protects the rest of your farm.
ga: Tsei ahe helai babaoo gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ. okwaayeli he nibii loo kooloi ni fãa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra kɛ amɛhiɛkpatamɔ Ebaaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why should I worry about tiny whiteflies if they are not eating big holes in my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahao yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe lɛ? Akɛni amɛyeee buji wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Even small insects like whiteflies cause major damage because they carry plant viruses in their bodies and inject them into healthy crops while feeding.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ whiteflies po baanyɛ afite nii waa ejaakɛ amɛhiɛɔ tsei amli helai yɛ amɛgbɔmɔtsei amli ni amɛkɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Is it safe to plant new crops in the exact same spot where my last harvest got diseased?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu tsei heei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ ha hela lɛ ba yɛ lɛ?

english: It is risky because viruses and plant diseases can live on in leftover roots and soil, ready to infect new seedlings of the same crop as soon as they sprout.
ga: Oshara yɛ ejaakɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ tsei ahe helai baanyɛ ahi shishifãi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ lɛ mli. Ni efee klalo akɛ ebaatswa tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ dumɔwui heei kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and stunted even though I give them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops can look weak despite water if a plant virus or root disease is preventing the crop from absorbing food and nutrients properly from the soil.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ afee tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu po. Kɛji tso mli hela ko loo shishifã hela ko tsi tso lɛ naa koni enyɛ eŋɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some seed varieties handle diseases better than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi komɛi nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ helai ahe nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Improved seed varieties are specifically bred by agricultural researchers to have natural strength against common local crop viruses and pests.
ga: Okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi efɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛná adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni amɛkɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers turning out small and hard inside instead of big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe wa moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Small, hard tubers are often caused by viral infections like cassava mosaic disease, which steals energy from the leaves so the plant cannot form rich roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli, tamɔ cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ yitsei bibii ni wa baa. ni juɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli, ni ehaaa tso lɛ aná shishifãi babaoo.

english: Are there crop varieties specially made to survive the common plant viruses found in Ghana?
ga: Ani tsei srɔtoi komɛi yɛ ni afee amɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ tsei amli helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ amli?

english: Yes, local Ghanaian agricultural research institutes continually develop improved crop varieties that are naturally resistant to common local plant viruses and suited to local soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, Ghana maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔhei lɛ miifee ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be. Amɛhe wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha maŋ lɛ mli tsei ahe helai, ni amɛhi kɛha maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil or are receiving too much water, which prevents their roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo amɛmiiná nu babaoo. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when the temperature gets too high, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil causing the plant to produce leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ehaa tsei woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: When crops get too much water, the soil stays constantly soggy, causing the plant roots to rot, the leaves to turn yellow and droop, and overall growth to stop.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be. haa tso shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. ni dalɛ fɛɛ baakpa.

english: What will happen to my pepper plants if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the crops compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin, weak plants with very low fruit yields.
