ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo faaa kwraa lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to clear all the weeds before I plant my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will quickly steal water, manure, and sunlight from your cassava stems, causing the young cassava to grow weak and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, ŋmei, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ o-cassava tsei lɛ amli oya. Enɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and crisp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up when they receive direct, strong sunlight without shade trees around to protect them from heat and moisture loss.
ga: Kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ blɔfo ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mli wa ni tsei ahe hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ shɛ amɛhe koni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafite.

english: Why should I cut off some of the side branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe niji komɛi ni yɔɔ afã lɛ?

english: Removing side branches helps the tomato plant direct its energy into growing bigger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on extra leaves and stems.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tomato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the leaves of my cabbage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These worms are caterpillars hatched from eggs laid by moths. They feed heavily on cabbage leaves to grow, which damages the head of the cabbage if not controlled early.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii fɔɔ lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ kaabɛji baai babaoo koni amɛshwere. Enɛ baafite kaabe yitso lɛ kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ lɛ mra.

english: Maize usually needs fertilizer twice: first about two weeks after germination to help early leaf growth, and a second time when the plants reach knee-height to support stem strength and grain formation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ awo ŋmãa mli. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ ji aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ koni eye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛdara oya. kɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛnaji ahe koni eye ebua tso lɛ shishi hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui afeemɔ.

english: How can I tell that my yams are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are ready to harvest when the green leaves and vines start turning yellow and dry up naturally, showing that the plant has finished feeding the underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crop turning yellow and drying up in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tip down the middle vein, it is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is a key food for plants, and when the soil does not have enough, the plant pulls it from the older bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaagbee kɛtee amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei yeɔ. kɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do the roots of my cowpea plants have small round bumps on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Those small bumps are root nodules where friendly soil bacteria live. They pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food, which actually enriches your soil instead of damaging the plant.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji shishifãi ni sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ su yɔɔ mli. Amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii, ni no haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ moŋ fe ni eeefite tsei.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Raindrops splash the tiny fungal spores from the soil or infected trees onto healthy pods, causing them to turn black.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ duŋ mli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores bibii anɔ. kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛtee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ diji.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly upward and becoming thick and brittle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho kɛmiiya ŋwɛi ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies, or by extreme heat and water stress. The plant curls its leaves to reduce water loss or as a reaction to the insect damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu mli haomɔ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi loo akɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ kɛji kooloi fiteɔ nii.

english: Yam is a vine crop that needs light to make food in its leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward the sun and prevents them from rotting on wet soil, which allows the plant to grow bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni he hiaa la koni amɛfee niyenii yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he, ni ebaaha amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kwɛɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If too many suckers grow around the mother plantain tree, they steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from it. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong followers, ensuring the main tree produces a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu lɛ he lɛ, tso nyɛ lɛ baaju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni he wa ahi shi. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ plantains babaoo.

english: Why do groundnut flowers bend down and bury themselves in the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfuɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have a unique way of growing where the flower gets fertilized above ground, and then grows a long stem called a 'peg' that pushes into the soil so the actual nut can safely develop underground.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛdaraa. he ni fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ aya hiɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as very hot temperatures, too little water, or a lack of nutrients. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy to stay alive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo be ni naa wa kpe. nu fioo tsɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaahi shi lɛ ato.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: You can tell cassava is maturing when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the ground directly around the base of the plant begins to crack as the thick tubers swell beneath the surface.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei ko miida kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. Ni ashiɔ tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why does swamp rice survive in flooded water while my maize rots if water sits on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔŋ ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nu afua lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni damɔ shi yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special hollow tubes inside their stems and roots that act like tiny straws, allowing oxygen to travel from the air above water straight down to the roots under water, whereas maize roots suffocate without air in the soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii bibii. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ nu lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu lɛ shishi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi nyɛŋ amu kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight and heat. Without shade trees or plantain plants to protect them, the hot sun scorches their leaves and dries out the soil moisture faster than their roots can drink it.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same soil where I plan to plant maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛdu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛto gbɛjianɔ akɛ amɛbaadu ŋmã yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil so that hungry crops like maize have plenty of food to grow big and strong later.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ aná niyenii babaoo ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves at the bottom of my maize plants turning yellow while the plant is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen or water. When a plant does not get enough food from the soil, it pulls nutrients out of its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Egbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni eda lɛ amli koni ekɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest without digging up the whole farm to check?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii koni mikwɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest around 9 to 12 months after planting. Look for lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and check if the soil right around the base of the main stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Taomɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Ni kwɛmɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ loo ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside funnel of my maize leaves, and how can I stop them from ruining my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-abɛi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafite midumɔ nii lɛ?

english: Those worms are Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on the soft growth center of maize plants. You can control them by spraying approved remedies early in the morning when the caterpillars come out to feed.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni daraa lɛ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni oooshwie nɔ leebi be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ eje kpo kɛmiitao niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested beans get full of holes and turn to dust after storing them in sacks for just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kɔfi ŋmɔji ni mikpa lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ sũ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ ni mikɛwo kotokui lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The holes are caused by tiny pests called weevils that lay eggs inside the seeds. Drying your beans under the sun until they are completely hard before storing them in airtight containers stops these insects from multiplying.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils ni woɔ wɔji yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa dani akɛwo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akafee babaoo.

english: Why should I make raised soil mounds or ridges to plant my yam seeds instead of just planting them directly on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni mikɛdu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: Mounds create loose, soft soil that makes it easy for yam tubers to expand deep into the ground. Raised soil also allows heavy rainwater to drain away so the yams do not sit in excess water and rot.
ga: Gɔji feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni awó nɔ lɛ hu haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akabote nu babaoo mli ni amɛkafite.

english: Why is it better to place fertilizer in a small hole near the crop roots rather than throwing it loosely all over the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo bu bibioo mli lɛ? Ebɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ ehi fe ni oooshi ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Placing fertilizer right near the roots ensures that your crop drinks up the nutrients directly. If you scatter it across the open field, rainwater washes it away or weeds consume it before your crop can get it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa niyenii kpakpai tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji ogbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ Nugbɔ nu baaho lɛ loo jwɛi baaye lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one small area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he bibioo kome lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and food to build large, heavy ears of maize.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmãa toi wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as extremely high heat, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps protect the flowers so fruits can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle intense heat and sun. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantain to cover them and keep the soil moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new upper growth when nutrients in the soil run out.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii kɛ́ sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant cassava stem cuttings at an angle instead of straight up and down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmei niji yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a 45-degree angle encourages roots to develop evenly along one side near the soil surface, making the tubers grow bigger and easier to harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ 45 degree angle mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ekomefeemɔ yɛ fa kome ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni ekpamɔ waaa.

english: My tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers, but why do the flowers keep falling off without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather gets too hot or water supply is uneven. High heat damages pollen, so the plant sheds unpollinated flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yam leaves need to climb high to catch sunlight to manufacture food for the growing yam stem underground. Without stakes, leaves rot on the wet ground, resulting in very small tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii amɛha sweet potato tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, yitso lɛ ji bibioo kwraa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants look very healthy with big leaves, but fail to produce any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ waa ni eyɛ baai wuji shi ebɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Tiny insect pests like thrips often eat cowpea flower buds before pods can form. Even if leaves look healthy, pests destroy the flowers unless protected during the blooming stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips yeɔ tsina ŋmeii dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ Shi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hu fiteɔ fɔfɔii. ja abu he yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli

english: Why should I cut off extra suckers growing around my main plantain tree instead of letting all of them grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ. Mohu ɔ, ha nɛ a pee kake kɛ wa.

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plantain for food and water. Pruning down to one main stem allows all plant energy to go into making one big, heavy bunch of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni ashi tso lɛ shishifã titri kome pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ daa ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward like small cups and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? ni okpa tso lɛ dalɛ

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or mites that spread viruses. This weakens the plant and stops new leaves and fruit from developing.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ekpaa baai kɛ aduawai heei akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Removing old fronds lets sunlight reach lower leaves and makes harvesting fruit bunches easier. It also prevents nutrients from being wasted on dead parts of the tree.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai momoi lɛ, hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe, ni ehaa aduawai akutsei lɛ akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo. Etsĩɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni elaaje kɛyaa tso lɛ fãi ni egboi lɛ amli lɛ hu naa.

english: Why does paddy rice grow better when there is standing water in the field during early growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli lolo yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli ŋmãa lɛ shishijee be mli lɛ?

english: Standing water smothers weeds that compete with young rice for space and light, while keeping soil temperature steady so young rice plants can establish quickly.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni egbeɔ jwɛi ni kɛ ŋmãa bibii yeɔ akaŋ kɛha he ko kɛ la lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ ahi shi daa bɔni afee ni ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ama shi oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in an open field without big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei wuji bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and heat. Shade trees and temporary shelter crops like plantains protect young cocoa seedlings from intense sun, conserve soil moisture, and prevent the leaves from burning before the root system matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa diɛŋtsɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni otsi baa lɛ shãa naa dani shishifãi lɛ adara.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black, rot, and smell bad during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ, egboɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, dark, and excessively humid conditions. Clearing farm weeds, pruning overcrowded branches to let in sunlight and air, and spraying approved fungicides helps stop the disease from destroying your harvest.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, duŋ, kɛ hulutsoo be fe nine. Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Tsei ni egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ afolɔ Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: My cocoa trees produce hundreds of small flowers, but why do most of them fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mi-cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii ohai abɔ, shi mɛni hewɔ amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers require tiny beneficial insects called midges for pollination. High temperatures, lack of rainfall, or chemical sprays that kill good insects prevent successful pollination, causing flowers to drop off naturally.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afeɔ pollination. He ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ, loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kpakpai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha fɔfɔii amli ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ akaye omanye. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Will cutting off branches from my healthy cocoa trees reduce the number of pods I get?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ niji ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: No, proper pruning actually increases your harvest. Removing unnecessary shoots, diseased branches, and dead wood allows the tree to direct its water and nutrients to forming big, healthy cocoa pods while improving airflow and sunlight.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni afoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa onibii ni owoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ nine ni hela emɔ lɛ Ni tso ni egbo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its power to grow heavy cocoa pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ kookoo ŋmeii babaoo dɔŋŋ?

english: If your mature cocoa trees have pale yellow leaves, thin canopies, or produce very few pods despite good rainfall, the soil lacks key nutrients. Applying recommended fertilizers or compost restores soil strength and boosts pod growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso ko ni edara lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha pod lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What is the difference between the older cocoa varieties my grandfather planted and the modern hybrid cocoa?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo henɔ momo ni mitsɛkwɛ̃ du lɛ kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfee ekome lɛ teŋ?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties take 5 to 7 years to yield fruits, while modern hybrid cocoa varieties begin producing pods in just 2 to 3 years, resist diseases better, and yield significantly more bags per acre.
ga: Kusum kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛwoɔ yibii, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli. Helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛnɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni ewoɔ baagi babaoo kwraa yɛ acre kome mli.

english: Can I plant cassava closely alongside my young cocoa trees to harvest food while waiting for the cocoa to mature?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ? Ani abaanyɛ akpa cacao tsei bibii kɛha niyenii yɛ be mli ni amɛmiimɛ ni cacao lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cassava is not recommended near young cocoa because its aggressive roots steal water and nutrients from the cocoa, and its dense foliage blocks out the sunlight cocoa needs to develop properly. Plantain or cocoyam are safer companion crops.
ga: Akɛ tapioca tsuuu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo ni mli jɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo lɛ mli. Ni ebaai ni mli tse lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa kookoo koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa. Plantain loo cocoa ji nanemɛi tso ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: What causes the leaves and young shoots on my cocoa trees to look burnt and curled up as if hot water was poured on them?
ga: Mɛni haa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni ebɔle amɛhe, tamɔ nɔ ni afɔse nu ni mli edɔ awo cacao tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is caused by mirids (commonly called capsids), which are sucking insects that feed on sap from young stems and pods. Spraying target insecticides during peak capsid seasons protects your crop canopy from dying back.
ga: Mirids (ni afɔɔ amɛ tsɛmɔ akɛ capsids), ni ji kooloi bibii ni yeɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni capsid lɛ fa babaoo lɛ baaye abua ni ebu otso lɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ he koni ekagbo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods stop growing and turn shriveled and hard during the dry Harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwaa yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is known as cherelle wilt. During severe dry spells, cocoa trees reduce water loss by naturally shedding or drying up young pods so that the main tree can survive the drought.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi. yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei haa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛshwieɔ loo amɛshwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni kookoo tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to pluck cocoa pods from the trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa pods are fully ripe when their outer skin completely changes color from green or dark red to bright yellow or orange. Plucking green pods leads to unfermented, flat beans, while leaving pods too long can cause beans to germinate inside.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛji akɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsake su kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse waa. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔɔɔ lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ kpo nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantains on the same land with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko kɛɛ mi akɛ midu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand strong, direct sunlight when they are small. Plantain trees grow very fast and have wide leaves that shield the cocoa from intense heat while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ kɛ́ amɛji bibii. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during drought to save water and stay alive. As long as the stem remains green, the plant will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ baahi shi akɛ eŋɔli lɛ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers, but no fruit is growing on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: When the weather gets too hot, or if the soil has too much chemical fertilizer, the plant gets stressed and drops its flowers before they can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ baaná haomɔ ni ebaagbee shi dani ebatsɔ tomato.

english: Why is my maize turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow maize leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil, or the ground is flooded with water, which prevents the roots from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curl is caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from under the leaves. Spraying with neem water or insect soap helps clear them.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu loo kooloi ahe samla shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi lɛ afee faŋŋ.

english: Why does my yam vine dry up and die off completely above the ground when harvest time comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When the vine dries out, it shows that the plant has finished sending all its food and energy underground into the yam tuber, signaling that the yam is fully mature and ready to dig up.
ga: Beni wain tsei lɛ egbi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ emaje shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtee sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda ni esa akɛ atsa.

english: If I plant my maize right after the very first rain of the year, why does it sometimes die off?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ egboɔ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry hot spell before the main rainy season starts. Planting too early causes the young seedlings to dry up when that gap in rainfall happens.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ he ko yɛ.

english: Weeds steal the water, sunshine, and soil food meant for your crops. When weeds crowd the field, your crops starve and cannot grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ jwɛi eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my garden egg fruits crack open on the plant before I can pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ fãa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ mafolɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Fruits split when water supply is irregular, such as heavy rain following a long dry period. The inside of the fruit swells up faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to split.
ga: Yibii lɛ mli gbalaa kɛji nu ni ejaaa ba, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Yibii lɛ amli fũuɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛre. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Can planting marigold flowers around my cabbage garden keep insects away?
ga: Marigold tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani kaabe abɔɔ baanyɛ ashwie kooloi bibii?

english: Yes, marigold flowers produce strong scents and root chemicals that confuse and repel many damaging insects and soil worms naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, marigold tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa kɛ tsofai ni jɛɔ amɛshishifãi amli ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ futuɔ kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow from the bottom before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a vital nutrient for leafy growth. When soil lacks nitrogen, the plant pulls nutrients from older leaves to feed young growth, causing bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei jieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei bibii lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why is my cassava plant growing very tall with thick leaves, but the tubers underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or manure, cassava puts all its energy into growing big stems and leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers. Using balanced soil nutrients helps redirect energy to root growth.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shishifã lɛ dalɛ nɔ.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass or leaves help them grow better?
ga: Mulching around Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai aha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It blocks harsh sunlight from drying out the soil, keeps plant roots cool, and breaks down over time to enrich the soil.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he Etsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni efiteɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their small flowers before they can turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Mɛi enyiɛ dani ebatsɔ pod?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they do not receive enough water, shade, or natural insect pollinators. Maintaining shade trees and protecting soil moisture helps the cocoa tree retain its flowers until pods develop.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛnáaa nu, hulutsoo loo adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ tso lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be mli ni obu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baa.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to manufacture food. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into the sun, which increases food production that gets stored below ground as big, healthy tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli. Enɛ haa niyenii ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo.

english: Why should I cut away extra suckers growing around my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers compete directly with the main plantain tree for water, sunlight, and soil food. Pruning suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring maximum food goes into growing a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsobii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni niyenii babaoo aba kɛha dumɔ wulu ko.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves, or by viral diseases spread by bugs. Controlling insect pests keeps leaves flat so they can catch sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Pest control ji ni afee baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark brown and rot before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Dark, sunken spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when plants cannot absorb calcium properly due to dry or irregular soil watering while fruits are growing fast.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo ni afɔɔɔ nɔ nu yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves get scorched and turn brown when I cut down all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are delicate and scorch easily under direct equatorial sun. Retaining tall shade trees creates a cool environment that blocks excessive light and shields fragile cocoa leaves from drying winds.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ equatorial hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tso lɛ ni akɛaaha he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni tsiɔ la ni fa fe nine naa lɛ baa, ni ebuɔ kookoo baai ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops die shortly after sprouting if I plant right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboiɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ kɛji akɛ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain after a long dry season often tricks seeds into sprouting, but the soil underneath remains dry. If dry weather returns for a week, young sprouts quickly dry up and die. It is best to wait until rains become frequent.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ lakaa dumɔwui koni amɛkwɛ̃. Shi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli egbi lolo. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ku osɛɛ otsi kome. Tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ shii abɔ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen. The maize plant moves nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top, showing that the soil needs manure or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling upwards and turning pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by heat stress, irregular watering, or tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus. Keeping the soil evenly moist and controlling sucking insects helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ he haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni ejaaa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Yam vines need full sunlight on all their leaves to produce energy. Lifting the vines on stakes allows maximum exposure to sunlight, which helps the plant feed and grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la koni amɛshɛ baa fɛɛ baa he koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ awó wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naa niyenii ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I space my maize plants far apart instead of planting many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ato he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ Ha dumɔwui lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe.

english: When crop seeds are planted too closely, their roots fight for water and soil nutrients while their leaves block sunlight from each other. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough resources to form big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tso agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop to the ground without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop when the tree is stressed by intense heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. Maintaining shade trees and keeping soil moist helps the flowers convert into healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛ́ okɛ otsei lɛ wo hulutsoo mli ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them for too long, encouraging fungal growth. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa ŋmeii shwereɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their fruits while the peppers are still small and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni pepper lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Small pepper fruits fall off when the plant suffers from sudden dry spells, extreme heat, or damage from pests like thrips. Maintaining consistent soil moisture and checking for pests prevents early fruit drop.
ga: pepper aduawai bibii Amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na amanehulu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa, latsaa ni naa wa, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ thrips ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ baaye abua ni atsi yibii lɛ ni shwieɔ shi mra lɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily once the bunch starts growing heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ miitsii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that pests like nematodes or stem borers can weaken. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the top-heavy stalk easily tips over unless supported with bamboo props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Kɛji akɛ aduawai akuu lɛ batsɔ tsii lɛ, ewaaa akɛ tso ni tsiimɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baagbee shi. ja akɛ ŋmei nibii fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop plants right after I clear the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that are naturally adapted to sprout quickly and survive on very little. They aggressively consume the water and soil nutrients before young crops can establish their roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛhi shi yɛ gbɛ bibioo nɔ. Amɛyeɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ miishɛɛ dani tsei bibii lɛ baanyɛ afee shishifãi.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the early rains start coming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu nii kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: It is best to wait until the rains become consistent and moisture penetrates deep into the soil for several consecutive days. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ anɛ shi ni nugbɔ lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ba.

english: How do I know when my maize is ready to harvest for soft green corn instead of dry grain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋmã lɛ efee klalo akɛ akpa koni maná ŋmãa bibii ni ji ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Maize for green corn is ready when the silks turn dark brown and pressing a kernel releases a milky juice, usually around 8 to 10 weeks after planting. If the liquid is clear, it is too early; if it is hard, it has passed the green stage.
ga: Abɛi kɛha abɛi eŋɔli lɛ efee klalo beni siliki lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ́ onyɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ, nu lɛ jeɔ kpo. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee otsii 8 kɛyashi 10 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji nu lɛ mli tse lɛ, no lɛ etsɛ tsɔ. Kɛji ewa lɛ, no lɛ otsɔ green stage lɛ nɔ momo.

english: How long after planting my plantain suckers should I expect to harvest the first bunch?
ga: Beni midu nii sɛɛ lɛ, etsɛɛɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ makpa mi klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants usually produce a flower stalk about 8 to 11 months after planting, and the bunch takes another 3 to 4 months to mature fully, making total time to harvest around 11 to 15 months.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui woɔ fɔfɔii aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 11 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Ni tso lɛ baahe nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 krokomɛi dani eda kwraa. Enɛ haa be fɛɛ ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ feɔ aaafee nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 15.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young cassava plants turning yellow and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Losing lower leaves is often a natural way cassava manages water during dry spells, but if it happens rapidly in good weather, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen fertilizer or the plant is infected with cassava mosaic virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni laajeɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni ŋmei tsɔɔ nɔ ekwɛɔ nu nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Shi kɛji eba oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa mli. Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. loo tsei ni ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ emɔ amɛ

english: What causes my pepper plant leaves to curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper tsei lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips, mites, or aphids hiding under the leaves, or by a leaf curl virus spread by whiteflies. Neem oil spray or insecticidal soap helps control the pests early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips, mites loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛtsɔ leaf curl hela ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ kooloi lɛ mra.

english: Brown dry edges on cocoa leaves mean the leaves are scorching from receiving too much direct sunlight without enough shade trees, or the young roots are not getting enough soil moisture.
ga: Baai ni egbi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo baa lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ baa lɛ miitswa kɛmiijɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ mli ni tso lɛ haaa hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa. loo shishifãi bibii lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures are extremely high, when watering is uneven, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer which causes the plant to produce leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ejaaa loo kɛji akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why are my young watermelon fruits rotting from the bottom while still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon gbekɛ lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ? Ani eji bibioo lolo?

english: This rot at the tip of the fruit is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often brought on by irregular watering where the soil gets too dry between waterings.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ fitemɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ naagbee lɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni haaa sũ lɛ mli agbi tsɔ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: How close to my crop stems should I apply granular fertilizer so I don't damage the roots?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ awo tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he tɛŋŋ koni ekafite shishifãi lɛ?

english: Place fertilizer about 5 to 10 centimeters away from the plant stem in a small ring or hole, and cover it with soil. Putting fertilizer directly against the stem will burn the plant.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli sɛntimitai 5 kɛyashi 10 kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ ŋwɛitsu bibioo ko mli loo bu mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ shikpɔŋ aha nɔ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees like plantain alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun and need soft light. Fast-growing plantain plants provide broad leaf shade and cool moisture for the first two to three years until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi, ni amɛbiɔ kane ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa baa lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my yam vines drying up and dying early before the rainy season ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines is usually caused by yam anthracnose disease, a fungal infection that turns leaves black, or by yam beetles feeding on the tuber under the soil and cutting off nutrients to the vines.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni ji anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya. Fungal hela ni kɛ baai diji baa loo kɛtsɔ sweet potato ŋmeii ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni amɛfoɔ niyenii ni haa wain tso lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that create shade, acting like living umbrellas to protect young cocoa plants until they grow strong enough to handle direct sunlight.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Kɛyashi tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni hulu la lɛ baaná tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops even when the crops are already much taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe, kɛji tsei lɛ ekwɛ fe jwɛi lɛ momo po?

english: Even when crops are taller, weeds under the soil steal water and nutrients that your crops need. Clearing weeds leaves all the food and moisture in the soil for your main crop to grow bigger yields.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ da po lɛ, jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ hu juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for green growth. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn healthy green so the plant can make larger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but give me only small roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi shishifãi bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or water, it spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of fat tubers below. Trimming excess stems helps direct the plant's energy down into the roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ najiaŋ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ shishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves to slow down water loss in extreme heat. It is the plant's natural way of saving moisture until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni hoɔ yɛ latsaa be mli lɛ akafee mlɛo. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers fall off the plant without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Legume flowers often fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or a sudden dry spell. The plant drops its flowers to save water and stay alive until moisture conditions improve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo amɛgbi trukaa. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ baaya hiɛ.

english: Why are there sticky white spots under my pepper leaves and small flies buzzing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ ashishi kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni fãa kɛbɔleɔ he

english: Those white spots are small insects like whiteflies that suck sap from your pepper plant's leaves. Spraying the underside of the leaves with mild soapy water or organic neem extract washes them off and protects your harvest.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ ji kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ, ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ o-pepper baai lɛ amli lɛ. Ni akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ. Aloo organic neem mli nu lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ nu lɛ afɔ mli ni ebu onibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my yam leaves developing brown spots and drying out long before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Early browning of yam leaves is often caused by leaf spot fungi or dry soil heat. Covering the soil around the plant base with dry grass or mulch keeps the soil cool and stops diseases from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa mli ŋmei loo dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ sũ ni egbi mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ mra be mli atomɔ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why does my pepper farm produce plenty of green leaves but very few flowers and peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi fɔfɔi kɛ pepper fioo pɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes pepper plants produce bushy leaves while delaying flowers. Adding nutrients rich in phosphorus or wood ash encourages the plant to start flowering and producing fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha pepper tsei lɛ afee baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha fɔfɔi lɛ asɛɛ afo. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ fɔsfɔs loo tso sũ fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ebɔi fɔfɔii ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines spread everywhere on the ground if I do not trim them back?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mifolɔko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sweet potato vines like to spread out and take root at every point they touch damp soil. Trimming the extra vines forces the plant to concentrate its food into making a few large tubers near the main stem instead of tiny roots everywhere.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛwo shishifãi yɛ he fɛɛ he ni amɛbaakpe shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Wein tso ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa niyenii nɔ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji enyɔ loo etɛ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ. Yɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ he fɛɛ he lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How do I know when my maize crops actually need water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni nu he hiaa mi-abele lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Maize leaves start to curl inward like narrow tubes during the day when they are thirsty. If the leaves remain curled early in the morning before the sun gets hot, it means the soil is dry and the crops need water right away.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfoɔ kɛyaa mli tamɔ paipii bibii. Yɛ gbi lɛ mli beni kumai yeɔ Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lolo leebi dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baa No tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Can I give too much water to my tomato plants, or is more water always better?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahã mi-tomato tsei lɛ nu fe nine? Aloo ani nu babaoo hi be fɛɛ be?

english: Too much water is harmful because roots need air to breathe just like they need water. Overflowing the soil with water drowns the roots, causes them to rot, and turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nu lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. kɛ fitemɔ baa ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my cabbage leaves droop in the afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ nu ha amɛ leebi lɛ, kaabaji baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: During hot afternoon hours, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground. They droop temporarily to protect themselves from the heat, but if the soil stays moist, they bounce back when evening comes.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaahi hulu lɛ he yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he. Shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo Ebaaku esɛɛ kɛji gbɛkɛ shɛ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during prolonged dry spells to save water and keep its underground tubers alive. It is the plant's natural self-defense mechanism until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my garden egg plants look stunted and stop growing during the dry harmattan wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni ekpaa dalɛ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ?

english: The dry harmattan wind strips moisture from leaves very fast, forcing the plant to slow down its growth to preserve water until humid conditions return.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa fioo koni amɛbu nu he kɛyashi be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or the roots are getting too much water. The plant sends its remaining nutrients up to the young, new leaves at the top to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi lɛ miiná nu babaoo. Tso lɛ kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ majeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist prevents flower drop and helps fruit set.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi, ni ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and weak when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete with neighboring leaves for sunlight. They stretch upward quickly to catch the sun, resulting in tall, skinny stems that can easily fall over.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ baai ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛgbala amɛhe oya kɛtee ŋwɛi koni amɛyamɔ hulu la lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves creates a protective blanket called mulch. It prevents the hot sun from evaporating water out of the soil, keeps root zones cool, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: How does controlled watering directly at the base of my crops help them yield more food than waiting for rainfall?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni akudɔɔ ni akɛhaa mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii babaoo fe nugbɔ ni amɛmɛɔ lɛ?

english: When crops receive consistent water right at their roots, they expend less energy searching deep underground for moisture and can focus all their energy into producing healthy leaves, flowers, and heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ nine shɛ nu nɔ daa kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛtao ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee baai, fɔfɔii, kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in a field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect their delicate leaves and keep the soil moist while their roots grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei koni amɛbu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves all the plants weak and reduces the total amount of food you harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii mli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni niyenii fɛɛ ni okpaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the ground is waterlogged and preventing the roots from breathing and absorbing food.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛmɔmɔ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even after waiting many months to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ nyɔji babaoo ni mikɛmɛ koni akpa amɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay thin if the soil is too hard and compact for the roots to expand, or if the soil lacks nutrients because crops have been grown on the same land without rest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafee bibioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ aduɔ tsei yɛ he kome ni amɛhiɛɛɛ shi.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to eat holes inside the fresh growth of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ tsei heei ni eda lɛ amli?

english: These are pests known as fall armyworms. Moths lay eggs on the leaves, and the hatched caterpillars crawl into the central leaves of the plant to feed on the tender stem.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ale amɛ akɛ cutworms. Kplukai fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, dark conditions when cocoa trees are too thick and don't let air or sunlight pass through.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela, ni jɛɔ ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni yɔɔ duŋ kɛji kookoo tso lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo hulu la atsɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so that heavy rain does not waste my money?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafite shika?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp but not flooded, and bury or cover it with a little soil so rain does not wash it off the farm before the roots absorb it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ nɔ. ni akɛ sũ fioo ko aha loo aha nɔ koni nugbɔ akaho kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: How do weeds reduce my crop yield even if I put fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and will drink the water and absorb the fertilizer you applied before your crops get the chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tso titri lɛ. Ni ebaanu nu lɛ fɛɛ ni ebaaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why does putting dry grass or crop leaves around my vegetable plants help them during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi tsei lɛ baanyɛ aye abua yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass acts as a mulch that shades the soil from the hot sun, preventing water from evaporating quickly and keeping root moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu shwieɔ oya ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: If one of my cassava plants looks sick, should I cut it down immediately or leave it to see if it recovers?
ga: Kɛji hela mɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ eko Ani esa akɛ mafo lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo mashi yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ koni mana kɛji ebaatsa?

english: You should remove and safely destroy sick plants right away. Leaving a diseased plant in the field allows pests or diseases to spread to healthy neighboring plants and ruin future harvests.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ loo hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. ni efite nibii ni abaafee wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or is getting too much water. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: If my tomato crop dies from a disease this season, can I plant tomatoes in that exact same soil next season?
ga: Kɛji mi tomato tsei lɛ gboi yɛ hela mli yɛ be nɛɛ mli Ani manyɛ madu tomato yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ yɛ be kroko mli?

english: No, because disease organisms can survive in the soil between seasons. You should practice crop rotation by planting a different family of crops, like maize or beans, to break the disease cycle.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ helai ahe nibii baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ bei lɛ ateŋ. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsakemɔ atsu nii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ wekui srɔtoi amli, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Koni akɛkpa helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ

english: If I see a black, rotten pod on my cocoa tree, should I pluck it off or leave it to fall on its own?
ga: Kɛ mina ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ko ni egbo yɛ kookoo tso nɔ Ani esa akɛ majie loo mashi ni egbee shi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You must pluck off and destroy rotten pods immediately. Leaving them on the tree allows fungal diseases like black pod to spread to healthy pods nearby through rain splash.
ga: Esa akɛ otsi ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji lɛ agbɛ ashwã tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli kɛtsɔ nugbɔ nɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees taking so long to produce pods even though they have plenty of big leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ ŋmeii eyɛ mli akɛ eyɛ baai wuji babaoo moŋ?

english: Excess nitrogen makes trees grow big leaves but delays pod production. Cocoa trees need balanced sunlight, proper branch pruning, and soil nutrients like phosphorus to trigger flowering and pod formation.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa baai wuji shi ehaa pod lɛ feemɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Hulu la ni sa he miihia kokoo tsei. ŋmɔlɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, koni ekɛha fɔfɔii kɛ podi afee.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before they can turn into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ebatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Flower drop usually happens when plants suffer from extreme heat, dry soil, or pest attacks. Keeping the soil moist and protecting young plants from harsh sun helps flowers develop into peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ miipiŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni abuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I sow many seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why does my land yield smaller harvests when I plant yam on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo beni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Yam draws heavy nutrients from the soil. Planting it continuously in the same place drains those nutrients and builds up soil pests; alternating with leguminous crops like cowpeas restores soil richness.
ga: Sweet potatoes gbalaa niyenii ni tsii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ hoɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes holes in the leaves of my cabbage plants, and will the crop survive?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji baa mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli? Ni te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi?

english: Holes are caused by insect pests like caterpillars feeding on the leaves. If caught early, applying recommended organic sprays or biological controls will stop the pests so the cabbage can form firm heads.
ga: Buji jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ amɔ lɛ mra lɛ, akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛkwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ koni kaabe lɛ aná yitsei ni wa.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young plantains with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, retains moisture during hot dry periods, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from competing with your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa koni fɛ̃i ahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi kɛ onibii akaye akaŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear all the tall trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sunlight. Tall trees act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs until its leaves grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei kakadaji tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Amɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i kɛyashiɔ be mli ni baai lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa.

english: Can I grow vegetables like tomatoes inside a plastic shelter instead of an open field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai tamɔ tomato yɛ plastic ŋtayaai amli? Ani abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii moŋ fe ni aaadu yɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: Yes, growing crops in a protected greenhouse structure keeps heavy rains and destructive insects away from the plants, allowing them to grow faster and yield healthier fruit all year round.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋwɛitsu ni abuɔ he lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach it, or weeds take it up first.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Aloo jwɛi lɛ baaŋɔ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ midu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants are natural soil builders. They pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil and helps neighboring crops like maize grow bigger without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanut tsei ji adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ tswalɔi. Amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii babaoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ni amɛdaraa ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the field for too long without draining, it smothers the roots, allowing fungus to grow and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli lɛ, egbeɔ shishifãi lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with weak, skinny stalks that produce tiny cobs or no corn at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni feɔ ŋmeii bibii. loo ŋmãa ko bɛ kwraa

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch sunlight for food making. Keeping leaves off the damp earth also prevents leaves from getting rot and diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ fiteɔ kɛ helai baaa.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they get too stressed, especially from sudden heat spikes or lack of water. The plant drops flowers to save its own energy so it can survive the harsh weather.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛhao tsɔ. titri lɛ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ trukaa loo nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do armyworms suddenly attack and eat the center leaves of my maize during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutua mi ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ trukaa ni amɛye amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Warm, dry weather causes armyworm eggs to hatch quickly in large numbers. The caterpillars crawl into the tightly wrapped center of young corn leaves to hide from the sun while eating the softest part of the plant.
