ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi lɛ haa ŋmeii babaoo fɔɔ oya. Kplukai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni akɛwo amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ateŋ koni amɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to pour water on my crops in the middle of a hot sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mafɔse nu yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Watering under hot sunlight causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before reaching the roots. Drops of water left on leaves can also magnify sun heat and scorch tender crop leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai anɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ aha hulu lɛ mli dɔlɛ aya hiɛ ni eha tsei ahe baai lɛ ashã.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. They hide in the central growing leaf (the whorl) and feed on young tissue, but applying targeted pest control early prevents them from destroying the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ni miida yɛ teŋgbɛ (whorls) lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Shi kɛ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ lɛ tsu nii mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early keeps the plant healthy so it can grow normal leaves and fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhe wa No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akwɛ baai kɛ aduawai bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when the dry Harmattan wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ tswa lɛ?

english: Dry winds make cocoa trees lose water rapidly. Dropping leaves is the tree's natural way to survive drought, but planting shade trees and keeping soil covered with mulch helps protect the cocoa from severe drying.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Shi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo lɛ he koni ekagbi waa.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves wilt and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants curl or droop their leaves in intense afternoon sun to reduce the amount of surface exposed to heat, which saves water until temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Bush bean tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni naa wa lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni ajie hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ shi Enɛ haa nu sɛɛ foɔ kɛyashiɔ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees snap and fall over easily during heavy rains and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain stems are filled with soft, water-rich tissue rather than hard wood, making them top-heavy when bearing fruit. Supporting the fruiting stems with strong wooden poles stops wind from blowing them down.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ amli eyi kɛ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli fe tsei ni wa. Ehaa tso lɛ tso lɛ mli tsiiɔ kɛ́ ewo yibii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛ shi.

english: Why are flowers falling off my tomato plants without setting any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollinators can cause tomato blossoms to drop before forming fruit. Keeping soil evenly moist and planting at the right season helps flowers produce tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Loo pollinators ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato fɔfɔi lɛ agbo dani aduawai aba. Kɛ́ okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be ni odu yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-tomato lɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi.

english: Why do my cashew trees bloom with many blossoms but produce very few nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Hot winds and sap-sucking insects often damage tender cashew flowers before they can form nuts. Protecting blossoms during early flowering improves nut formation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ fiteɔ cashew fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi mra lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing leafy branches above ground instead of storing starch in root tubers underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛkwɛɔ tsei niji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ ngmlɛfia ɔ kɛ woɔ tso ɔ sisi fã ɔmɛ a mi ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer on my crops when the ground is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi?

english: Fertilizers need soil moisture to dissolve so crop roots can absorb them. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry ground can burn roots and waste expensive nutrients under the hot sun.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã ni niyenii ni jara wa afite yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Covering soil with dried grass, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, holds water in the soil longer during dry days, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Will my maize give me a bigger harvest if I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Ani mi-ŋma lɛ baawo yibii babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni fa fe ekome? Ha dumɔwui lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and small cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and nutrients to produce a larger, healthier yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni ŋmeii lɛ hu yɛ bibii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting plantains alongside them provides living shade and retains moisture in the soil, protecting the delicate cocoa trees until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Buu kookoo tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada ni ená hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my crops so the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nugbɔ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a light rain, rather than right before a heavy downpour or during extreme dry spells. Covering the fertilizer lightly with soil also prevents heavy rains from washing it off the field.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Mohu ɔ, mo wo lɛ loko hiɔmi nɛ wa nɛ wawɛɛ aloo be mi nɛ hwɔɔ ngɛ wawɛɛ ɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli fioo lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How does spreading dry grass or leaves around my crops help them survive during hot days?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry organic material around your plants, known as mulching, acts as a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly. Over time, the dry leaves also break down and enrich the soil.
ga: Ale nibii ni egbi ni akɛshwãa otsei lɛ ahe lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, baai ni egbi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants showing ragged holes and white patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes and light patches on maize leaves are common signs of Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the plant. Checking the central funnel of the plant early helps you catch and manage them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Buji ni ekumɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ahe lɛ ji okadii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli mra. Enɛ baaye abua bo ni omɔ amɛ ni okwɛ nɔ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips, aphids, or mites, which can also spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with soapy water or appropriate sprays prevents the leaves from twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites, ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ hu ashwã tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ nu ni sa ni akɛ saamɔ fee loo spray ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and cannot drain away, creating conditions where fungal diseases thrive. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ efo kɛya. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli, ni ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plants without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or a shortage of plant nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting shade crops nearby during very hot periods helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli ni adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow even when I am watering them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant lacks nitrogen or that the soil is waterlogged. Too much water suffocates the roots, making it impossible for the plant to absorb nutrients from the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu babaoo baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What does fertilizer actually do to my soil and crops when I put it in the ground?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ mishikpɔŋ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ? Mɛɛ be mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for the soil and plants. Just like human beings need proper food to grow strong and fight sickness, fertilizer gives the soil essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus so crops can grow healthy and produce bigger yields.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ. Taakɛ niyenii ni sa he hiaa adesai koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwu amɛshi helai lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Koni tsei lɛ adara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is starving for specific nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or the soil is holding too much water around the roots, which chokes them and prevents them from taking up food.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko, tamɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo, shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa amɛtsiɔ amɛhe ni ehaaa amɛye nii.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my crop roots with dry grass or fallen leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbo loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ awo tsei shishifãi ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like an umbrella for the soil. It traps moisture so the hot sun doesn't dry the ground out quickly, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: When crops are planted too close to one another, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and light to produce full, healthy corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant beans or cowpeas together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas are special plants that grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them with maize helps naturally feed the maize and keeps the soil healthy without buying extra chemicals.
ga: Legumes tamɔ beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni ooodu lɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ abele yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ohaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe tsofai krokomɛi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive and burn under full, direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting plantains provides shade and humidity, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle the sun.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei kakadaji ni ashiɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la.

english: Why shouldn't I grow maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot every year drains the exact same nutrients from the dirt until the soil becomes exhausted. Rotating crops gives the soil time to recover and breaks the cycle of pests living in the dirt.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ sũ lɛ mli aahu kɛyashi sũ lɛ mli baaho. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ, ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: How do weeds hurt my main crops if I leave them in the farm for too long?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight directly away from your crops. Leaving them too long leaves your crops weak, stunted, and vulnerable to pest attacks.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ oshi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ, amɛhe afee shoo, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baatutua amɛ.

english: Why do I need to trim or cut off some leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo loo majie mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Trimming extra leaves allows sunlight and air to flow through the plant, keeping leaves dry and preventing diseases. It also forces the plant to direct its energy into producing large tomatoes instead of growing unnecessary leaves.
ga: Baai krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa helai baaa. Enyɛɔ tsei anɔ hu koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo tomatoi wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ

english: Why do insects seem to attack my crops much more during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, wild bushes dry up, so insects move to green farm crops searching for moisture and food. Heat also causes insect eggs to hatch faster, leading to larger numbers of pests.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Koo lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ mli egbi. Kɛkɛ lɛ, kooloi bibii yaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli koni amɛyatao ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii. Dɔlɛ hu haa kooloi awɔlɔi fɔɔ oya. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ.

english: How do I know the correct amount of chemical or fertilizer to apply to my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Applying too much chemical can burn plant roots and ruin your soil, while applying too little will not protect or feed the crop. Following precise measuring guidelines ensures crops get just enough inputs to grow healthy without damaging the land.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni nɔ fioo tsɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ebuuu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe loo ehaŋ lɛ niyenii. Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi pɔtɛɛ ni kɔɔ susumɔ he lɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: What happens to my soil if I put too much chemical on my farm every season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai babaoo wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi?

english: Overusing chemicals can kill the beneficial organisms in the ground that naturally build soil fertility. Over time, the soil becomes hard, overly acidic, and unable to hold water, making it harder for future crops to thrive.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ agbe shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ. Be ni be shwieɔ mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. ni enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ nu Enɛ haa ewaa waa kɛhaa tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃.

english: Can I spray weedkiller on my crops right before the rain falls?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ?

english: Rain washes the chemical off the plant leaves into the soil before the crop or weed can absorb it. This wastes your money and can cause the chemical to wash away into nearby water streams instead of working properly.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tsei loo jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Nakai feemɔ baaha ofite shika, ni ekolɛ ebaaha tsofai lɛ atsɔ nu gbɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How should I mix chemicals with water so I do not burn my crop leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ tsofai afutu nu mli koni tso lɛ baai lɛ akashã?

english: Always measure both the water and chemical carefully using standard containers rather than guessing. Mixing the chemical thoroughly in a small amount of water first before filling your knapsack sprayer prevents concentrated pockets that burn plant leaves.
ga: Susumɔ nu kɛ tsofai fɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsɛnsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ooosusu he. Okɛ tsofa lɛ afutu nu fioo ko mli jogbaŋŋ dani okɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ awo mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ akashã.

english: Why is it important to space my crops properly instead of planting seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ hei ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ ato he jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and ground water, resulting in thin stalks and small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough air and room for its roots to spread.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How deep should I dig the hole when planting my seeds in the farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo bu lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni kɛ́ midu dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, the young sprout uses up all its energy trying to push through the dirt and dies underground. If planted too shallow, birds eat them or the sun dries them out, so planting at a depth about two to three times the seed's size gives them the best start.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɔ Tso bibioo lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ Okpoi baaye amɛ loo amɛbaagbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ toi 2-3 lɛ, ehaa amɛjeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or that the soil is too waterlogged around the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich manure or fertilizer and clearing drainage pathways helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he ni ajie nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the plant hold its flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield when I plant the same crop on the same land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to recover. Rotating different crops, such as planting beans or cowpeas after maize, puts natural nutrients back into the dirt.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil become very hard and dry shortly after the rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbi beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens quickly when it lacks organic material like decayed leaves, compost, or animal manure to bind the soil particles. Adding organic matter helps the soil act like a sponge, holding moisture longer for crop roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa oya kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo kooloi ashishifãi ni baakpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii bibii lɛ ahe. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tso shishifãi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I clear all the tall trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei kakadaji kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade to survive because direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving some mature trees or planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain keeps the young cocoa cool and moist until it grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ ni ajieɔ loo aduɔ hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ baaye abua ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food source for plants. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure around the plant roots will help them turn green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri lɛ. Nitrogen ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛfataa he lɛ Tso shishifãi yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: What is eating small holes in the middle leaves of my corn plants and leaving green dust behind?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ni mishiɔ sũ eŋɔli yɛ sɛɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant. Spraying recommended insecticides early in the morning or late evening when the worms come out to feed will help kill them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi lɛ eje kpo amɛmiitao niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe amɛ.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots are ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves start turning yellow and dropping off. You can also dig up the soil carefully around one stem to check if the tubers are thick enough before harvesting the whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa sũ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ hu. Tso kome ni akɛkwɛɔ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa dani akpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Do I really need to put sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makɛ niji afata he koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, lifting yam vines off the ground on sticks allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight to feed the plant. Staking also prevents the leaves from rotting on damp soil, which results in much larger yam tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ okɛ niji wo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛfi tso lɛ sɛɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ agboi babaoo.

english: Why are my plantain bunches small when many small suckers are growing around the main plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ be mli ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he.

english: When too many young suckers grow around the main plant, they steal water and nutrients away from it. You should cut off the extra suckers and leave only one or two strong ones so the main stem gets enough food to make big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ plantain tso agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Is it helpful to plant groundnuts or beans together in the same field with my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Yes, crops like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil for your maize crop and increases your total farm harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a shade blanket. It keeps the soil cool, stops water from drying out quickly in the heat, and prevents stubborn weeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa hulu tsoɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekagbi oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi ni yitsoŋ wa lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a soft rain, but avoid doing it right before a heavy downpour. Always cover or bury the fertilizer slightly with soil so it stays close to the plant roots.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi kaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa. Esa akɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo loo afu bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before any small tomatoes appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop without forming fruit when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the plant lacks nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under strong heat. They need partial shade from companion crops like plantain or cassava to keep the soil cool and moist while their root systems establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains loo yucca lɛ adɛŋ. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ maa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the maize plants fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Proper plant spacing gives every maize plant enough room and nutrition to grow thick stalks and large ears.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Abɛi tsei wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmãa ni mli tse kɛ toi wuji.

english: Why do I need to use wooden poles to lift my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso atsu nii koni mikɛwo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on wooden poles allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight needed to generate energy for building big underground tubers. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, protecting them from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Too much rain fills up the air spaces in heavy soils with standing water, suffocating the cassava roots and causing fungal rot. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa nu shwieɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farmland after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize pulls a large amount of nitrogen fertilizer out of the ground. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it back into the soil through their roots, naturally restoring field fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply fertilizer to my farm right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli dani ahum baa lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Heavy rainstorms wash away loose fertilizer from your field before your crops have a chance to absorb it. Applying fertilizer when the soil is damp, rather than right before a downpour, ensures the plant roots take in the nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooowo dani nugbɔ anɛ Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when plants suffer from drought, or when there is poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from extreme heat helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni tsei nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ gbɛ loo be mli ni pollination ni ehiii lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni abuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: These caterpillars, known as Fall Armyworms, hide inside the central funnel of young maize plants to feed on tender leaves. Controlling them early with appropriate organic or chemical sprays prevents them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni ale amɛ akɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Amɛ nɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ organic loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ amɛbaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to give poor yields even when I plant good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa miŋmɔshi nibii amli eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kpakpai moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, soil moisture, and fertilizer away from your plants. Clearing weeds early in the growing season ensures your crops get all the food they need to produce high yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la. shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ ahe waa. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do the crops I grow from my saved maize seeds produce smaller harvests than the original hybrid seed I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni miduɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe shishijee ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed to produce a single generation of exceptionally high yields. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special genetic traits, resulting in smaller and less productive plants in the next season.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ futuɔ amɛhe yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo waa yɛ yinɔ kome mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai fɔmɔ sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and look burnt when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni eshã beni mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle mihe lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, intense sunlight. Without taller trees or shade plants like plantains to block the harsh heat, the leaves get sunburned, which slows down the plant's growth and damages its tissue.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei kakadaji loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains bɛ ni baatsi hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ naa. Hulu baashã baai lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ baa shi ni efiteɔ efãji lɛ.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts in the same farm help my maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow, so the legumes act as a natural fertilizer for the maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa kɛha ŋmãa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with bushy green leaves, but the tubers under the ground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ jwɛi ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa tsɔ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen compared to other nutrients like potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending food down to grow thick roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nine kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ potassium he lɛ, ŋmei tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaatsu niyenii kɛya shi koni shishifãi ni mli tse lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: If I leave fallen leaves and leftover crop waste to rot on my field, will it damage the next crop or help it?
ga: Kɛji mishi baai ni egbee shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni egbo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani ebaaya nɔ efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo eye ebua lɛ?

english: As long as the leftover crop was not infected with diseases, letting plant material decay on your soil acts as natural manure. It adds organic matter, retains soil moisture, and feeds the crop you plant next.
ga: Shii abɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ bɛ hela lɛ Tso mli nibii ni ashiɔ koni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. add organic matter Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, dry soil, or a sudden imbalance in water. When the plant feels stressed, it drops flowers to save energy and protect itself.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni ejaaa trukaa lɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato ni ebu ehe.

english: Why do some of my tiny baby cocoa pods turn black and shrink before they ever grow into big pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibi cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi wuji lɛ?

english: This is often 'cherelle wilt,' which is the cocoa tree's natural way of thinning itself out when it has produced more pods than it has energy and water to feed, though fungal diseases like black pod can also cause it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ ‘cherelle wilt’, ni ji cacao tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ egbɔjɔɔ ehe yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni eyɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ nu ni ekɛyeɔ nii lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods hu baanyɛ aha amɛba moŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and droop in the middle of the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛjeee nakai moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In the hot sun, pepper leaves lose water through breathing faster than their roots can suck water from the soil. Curling up reduces the leaf area exposed to the sun to prevent the plant from drying out.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ mumɔ ni amɛmuɔ lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ abɔle tso lɛ he lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi koni tso lɛ akagbi.

english: Why does my harvested maize start growing mold and rotting so quickly when I store it in my shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto mi-abele lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize rots in storage if it is harvested while still holding too much water or if stored in a humid place without air movement. Grains must be thoroughly sun-dried until dry and hard before storage.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ akpa yɛ be mli ni nu babaoo yɛ lolo loo kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ tsiii ehe. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaagbi ni ewa dani akɛto.

english: Why do my harvested ripe tomatoes become soft and spoil within just two days after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni mikpa lɛ?

english: Once harvested, ripe tomatoes continue to 'breathe' and release heat and ethylene gas, which speeds up their softening and decay, especially when kept packed together in hot conditions.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa Tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baaya nɔ ‘emu’ ni ejie dɔlɛ kɛ ethylene gas kpo. ni haa tomato lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efiteɔ oya lɛ. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ akɛto he kome yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and die early before the yam tubers in the mound have grown big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ oya dani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines usually dry prematurely due to fungal diseases like anthracnose or damage from underground pests attacking the root system, preventing water and food from reaching the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose loo shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ahewɔ. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight during their first couple of years. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a sunshade, keeping the air cool and protecting the cocoa leaves from burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Nibii ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ hulutsoo he lɛ Etsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo tsei Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa kookoo baai lɛ ashã.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land is suitable for growing maize before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ko nɔ sa akɛ adu ŋmãa dani adu?

english: Good land for maize has dark, loose soil that drains well after rain without staying flooded. If water sits on top of the soil for many days, or if the ground is mostly hard stone, maize roots will rot or fail to spread.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ji sũ ni mli edɔ. Ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Nu shwieŋ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ji tɛi ni wa babaoo Abɛi shishifãi lɛ baagboi loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why does my cassava grow huge stem leaves above the ground, but gives me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ baai wuji yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi eshi mi kɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or is planted too close to other crops, it spends all its energy producing leaves instead of storing energy underground in the tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei krokomɛi tsɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: When should I plant my crop seeds after the long dry season ends in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ madu dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ eba naagbee yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: You should wait until two or three heavy, steady rains have thoroughly soaked deep into the ground. Planting after just the very first light shower can cause the seeds to sprout and then die if the sun comes back strong.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji hulu lɛ mli wa waa.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow better when I plant beans in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it inside the soil through their roots. This acts like natural fertilizer that nourishes neighboring plants growing beside them.
ga: Beans kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Egbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small balls and preventing fruits from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bɔɔlu bibii ni amɛmiitsi yibii anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny, invisible insects like aphids or thrips that suck the juice out of the leaves and spread plant sicknesses. Clearing the pests with proper farm care fixes the new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli ni egbɛɔ tsei ahelai eshwaa Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni asaa shweremɔ hee.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn weak and pale even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal food, soil nutrients, and sunlight directly away from your crops' roots. Even with plenty of rain, your crops will starve because the weeds take the nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ niyenii. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ Hɔmɔ baaye onibii po ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ baaye niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I place chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer behaves like strong salt when it touches plants directly. If it touches the stem, it burns the skin and roots of the crop; it must be placed a few inches away in moist soil so the roots can safely reach for it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ŋmeii ni mli ewo muji kɛ́ amɛkɛ tsei kpe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ eta tso lɛ shishi lɛ Ebaashã ŋmɔshi nibii ahewolo kɛ shishifãi. Esa akɛ akɛ amɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe.

english: Why am I supposed to snap off the extra small shoots that grow on my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli lɛ? Ajie nɔ ni yaa hiɛ babaoo yɛ mi tomato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Removing extra branch shoots forces the plant to send all its water and nutrients into growing larger, healthier tomato fruits instead of wasting energy on making useless extra leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaabi ni tso lɛ ajie nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ koni ekwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni okɛfee baai krokomɛi ni he ehiaaa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops look like they are dying after heavy rains flood my farm for three days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛ waa ni ekɛ nu eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii etɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the air to breathe, just like humans do. When water covers the soil completely for days, the roots suffocate underwater, causing the leaves to turn yellow and drop off.
ga: Tse shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛmu. Taakɛ adesai sumɔɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Kɛ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ nu shishi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that give the cocoa plants the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa kookoo tso lɛ hɔɔŋ kɛ fɛ̃i koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines up toward the sun and keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli ni ehaaa baai lɛ akajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or when the soil has too much trapped water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or improving drainage helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji nu babaoo ni sũ lɛ emɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does putting dry grass on the soil around my tomato plants help them stay healthy?
ga: Akɛ jwɛi fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi tomato tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly in the hot sun. It keeps the soil cool and moist while preventing weeds from taking nutrients away from your tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa, ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ tomatoi lɛ amli.

english: When cassava plants are spaced too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives the root system enough room to expand into large, thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ yitso agbo ni mli wa.

english: Trimming extra leaves and weak branches helps the plant direct its water and nutrients into producing bigger, healthier tomato fruits instead of wasting energy on excess leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afo baai ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei niji bibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ewo tomato yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of soil nutrients. Regular watering and nutrient-rich soil help the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do seeds saved from my last maize harvest produce smaller yields than certified store seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred for maximum strength, uniform growth, and high yield. Saved seeds lose these strong traits after the first generation, resulting in smaller and less reliable harvests.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ odaseyeli mli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo. Dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ feɔ bibioo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly if I delay weeding my farm during the early growing stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ shwiemɔ be sɛɛ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and aggressively steal sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crops get everything they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni mli wa Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii titri lɛ aná nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and dry even after I applied fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo ŋmɔ lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often point to nitrogen deficiency. However, if fertilizer was applied, the soil might be too acidic, flooded, or dried out, which prevents the crop's roots from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Shi, kɛji akɛ awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee acid tsɔ, nu abɔ he loo egbi tsɔ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my neighbor getting a much bigger harvest than me when we planted on the same day and used the same farm size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe mi beni wɔduɔ nii yɛ gbi kome nɔ ni wɔkɛ ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ kome tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Yield differences usually come down to soil fertility levels, the quality of seeds used (such as high-yielding hybrid seeds versus saved seeds), crop spacing, and how early weeds were cleared.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli lɛ damɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe hilɛ (nɔkwɛmɔnɔ, dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni akɛ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ), ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ kɛ bɔ ni afeɔ ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishijee mli

english: Why are my pepper plants suddenly wilting and dying off even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by soil-borne fungal or bacterial diseases like root rot. Excessive water blocks oxygen to the roots, allowing harmful microbes to damage the plant's internal water transport system.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ trukaa lɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli loo helatsɛmɛi amli, tamɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ nu ni akɛyaa tsei lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees developing strange swollen stems and yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni efuu ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ? ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi

english: This is a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is transmitted by tiny insects called mealybugs. Infected trees lose productivity over time and must be removed to prevent the virus from spreading across the farm.
ga: Enɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ he okadi. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baafite amɛyibii yɛ be ni sa mli. ni esa akɛ ajie koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Yam rot underground is caused by poor soil drainage, waterlogging, or soil nematodes and fungi invading wounded seed yams. Planting on high mounds with good drainage helps protect the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ, nu ni hoɔ, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni baa ŋmeii ni epila lɛ anɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu bulb lɛ he.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the leaves and leaves' cores of my young maize plants so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miiye mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a aggressive pest that attacks maize. They multiply rapidly and can destroy crops unless detected early and managed with recommended control methods or biological treatments like neem extracts.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni tutuaa ŋmãa. Amɛshwereɔ oya ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii. ja ana mra ni akɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ hela lɛ loo tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem mli nu lɛ tsu he nii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and drop off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves and curl remaining foliage during severe dry spells to conserve water. This is a natural survival behavior that allows the plant to stay alive underground until rain returns.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni baai ni eshwɛ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala su ko ni haa tso lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their blossoms without growing any actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii ko diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes shed flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why did many of the cowpea seeds I planted fail to shoot out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if planted too deep, if the soil is too dry or flooded, or if insects and poor storage damaged the seed embryo before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ loo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ fiteɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ dani aduɔ.

english: Why does planting plantains alongside my young cocoa trees make the cocoa grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, hot sunlight. Plantains grow fast and possess wide leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting young cocoa from scorching heat.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why does the weather keep changing every year, and how should it affect when I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yaa nɔ daa afi lɛ? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Weather patterns are shifting due to climate changes, which alters rain schedules. Instead of planting on fixed calendar dates, you should monitor rainfall stability or ask local extension officers when the rains have truly settled before putting seeds in the ground.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi miitsake. ni haa nugbɔshiimɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsakeɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaadu yɛ gbii pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ taakɛ kalanda lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ. Esa akɛ okwɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ nɔ loo obi maŋ lɛ mli nitsulɔi ni kwɛɔ nugbɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ baakpa diɛŋtsɛ. Ni dani ebaadu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do some farmers clear their land as early as January when the rains are not yet here?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ amɛshikpɔji lɛ anɔ yɛ January shishijee mli be mli ni nugbɔ bako lɛ?

english: Clearing land in January gives you enough time to clean the farm, allow cleared bush to dry, and prepare the soil without rushing so your field is completely ready when the first main rains arrive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ooojie yɛ January mli lɛ baaha oná be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛsaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ha tsei bibii ni ajie lɛ lɛ agbi. ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni okɛ oyaiyeli tsuuu nii Koni oŋmɔji lɛ afee klalo kwraa kɛ́ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ wulu lɛ ba.

english: How do I know if a crop will take four months or longer before I can harvest it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baahe nyɔji ejwɛ loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani abaanyɛ akpa?

english: Every crop and seed variety has a specific growth cycle. You can find out the maturity time by checking the seed package details or asking an extension officer about the exact variety before planting.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ kɛ dumɔwui fɛɛ yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko ni amɛdaraa. Obaanyɛ ona be ni dumɔwui lɛ baatsɔ mli lɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli saji lɛ amli fitsofitso lɛ nɔ loo obi mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ nɔ pɔtɛɛ ni ji dumɔwui lɛ dani odu.

english: Why do farmers in places like Bawku and the northern areas have shorter farming seasons than us?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ hei tamɔ Bawku kɛ kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ okwaayeli be lɛ faaa fe wɔ lɛ?

english: Northern regions experience a single, shorter rainy season compared to other parts of Ghana. Because the rains start late and end early there, farmers must use fast-growing crops that finish before the dry season starts.
ga: Kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku pɛ kɛ akɛto hei krokomɛi ahe. of Ghana Ejaakɛ nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi sɛɛ mli ni egbeɔ naa mra yɛ jɛmɛ. Esa akɛ okwaafoi adu nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi.

english: Which crops should I plant if my area receives rain for only a short period?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ madu kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ be kukuoo pɛ?

english: In areas with short rainy seasons, you should plant fast-maturing crops like groundnuts, cowpeas, or short-duration maize varieties that can complete their life cycle within two to three months.
ga: Yɛ hei ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo yɔɔ lɛ Esa akɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei, loo ŋmei srɔtoi ni yeɔ be kukuoo ni baanyɛ agbe amɛwala be lɛ naa yɛ nyɔji enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli.

english: Why are groundnuts recommended for areas where the rains stop quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmeii atsu nii yɛ hei ni nugbɔ lɛ kpaa oya lɛ?

english: Groundnuts grow relatively fast and form their pods underground, allowing them to produce a good harvest even with limited water and a short rainy season.
ga: Peanuts daa oya ni pods feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmaa kpakpa yɛ nu ni faaa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: What should I do if I clear my land early but the rains delay longer than expected?
ga: Ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya shi nugbɔ lɛ nɛ sɛɛ mli fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ. Mɛni esa akɛ mafee?

english: If rains delay after clearing, hold off on planting so your seeds do not burn in dry soil. You can also switch to short-duration seed varieties that need less time to mature once the rains finally start.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ sɛɛ Kpa dumɔ koni dumɔwui lɛ akashã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ otsake kɛya dumɔwui ni yeɔ be kukuoo hu anɔ, ni biɔ be fioo dani ekwɛ̃ beni naagbee lɛ nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi enɛɔ lɛ.

english: What is the difference between a short-season crop variety and a long-season crop variety?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo kɛ tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ateŋ?

english: A short-season variety matures quickly (usually in 2 to 3 months) to beat early dry weather, while a long-season variety takes 4 months or more to harvest and requires steady rain over a longer period.
ga: Be kukuoo mli henɔi lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya (bei pii lɛ yɛ nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 mli) koni amɛye shihilɛi ni mli egbi mra lɛ anɔ kunim. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo be mli ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ heɔ nyɔji 4 loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani amɛkpaa ni amɛbiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: What happens to my four-month crop if I leave it in the ground after it matures?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii ni eye nyɔji ejwɛ lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi yɛ shikpɔŋ mli beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving mature crops in the ground past their harvesting time exposes them to pest damage, mould, and rotting, which ruins the quality of your yield.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛho kpamɔɔ be lɛ he lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ amɛ. Enɛ baaha nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe afee fɛo.

english: If I clear my land months before planting, will the soil lose its nutrients before seeds are planted?
ga: Kɛji mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ nyɔji babaoo dani midu Ani niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite dani midu dumɔwui?

english: If soil is left completely bare for months under hot sun, it can dry out and lose topsoil to wind. It is best to leave a light cover of dry cleared grass on top to protect the moisture until planting time.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɔji babaoo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu baanyɛ agbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi jwɛi ni egbi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ nɔ koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi dumɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to have my fertilizer ready before the end of March?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee mi-fertilizer lɛ klalo dani March aba naagbee lɛ?

english: March marks the transition into the main rainy season in many parts of Ghana. Having your fertilizer ready ahead of time ensures you can apply it as soon as the rains start and the soil becomes moist enough for your crops to absorb the nutrients.
ga: March ji tsakemɔ kɛmiiya nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli yɛ Ghana hei babaoo. Kɛ́ osaa o-fertilizer lɛ he kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ obaanyɛ okɛwo mli kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni onibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I buy my farming supplies early instead of waiting until planting day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe okwaayeli he nibii mra? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi dumɔ gbi lɛ nɔ?

english: Buying inputs like fertilizer and seeds early prevents delays caused by high market prices or sudden shortages when all farmers are rushing to buy supplies at the start of the rainy season.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dumɔwui ahemɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ sɛɛkuu ni jarayeli jara ni nɔ kwɔ loo nibii ni faaa trukaa lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa. Beni okwaafoi fɛɛ kɛ oyaiyeli yaahe nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ

english: Why does my maize turn light green or yellow early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient that fast-growing plants like maize quickly use up from the soil during their early stage of growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei ni daa oya tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Can I apply dry fertilizer to my crop fields when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi atsu nii yɛ midumɔi lɛ anɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: No, crop roots cannot absorb dry fertilizer without water. The fertilizer needs moisture from rainfall or irrigation to dissolve into the soil so the roots can drink in the nutrients safely without getting burned.
ga: Dabi, tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi kɛji nu bɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe miihia nugbɔshiimɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli koni etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛshãaa.

english: What actually happens inside the plant when I feed it with fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni baa tso mli kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ha lɛ?

english: Fertilizer dissolves in soil water, and the plant roots suck it up like food. These nutrients help the plant build stronger stems, greener leaves, and eventually larger grains or fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. ni shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ lɛ tamɔ niyenii. Niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛ naa tsei ni wa, baai eŋɔli, kɛ naagbee lɛ dumɔwui loo aduawai wuji.

english: Why do crops grow so fast right after the first heavy rains after the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya nɛkɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ hɔmɔ be ko sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rains wake up beneficial soil organisms and release a sudden flush of natural nutrients stored in the warm soil, giving plants an immediate boost of energy to grow rapidly.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ teɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ shi ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ trukaa lɛ mli lɛ kpo. Ehaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛdara oya.

english: How do my crops know when it is time to start growing after the long dry spell?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ leɔ be ni esa akɛ amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds and plant roots react to the increase in moisture and drop in soil temperature caused by the early rains, which signals to the plant that conditions are safe to grow.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ tsei shishifãi tsuɔ hulutsoo ni yaa hiɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ ni baa shi ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra be mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he nii. Enɛ haa tsei leɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha dalɛ.

english: Why do some of my crops need fertilizer applied more than once while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi amli ŋmɔshi nibii fe shikome beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Crops need different amounts of nutrients at different stages. Early fertilizer helps build roots and leaves, while a second application later gives the plant energy to make fruits or grains.
ga: Tsei biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ srɔtoi yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa shishifãi kɛ baai. Yɛ be mli ni sɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ yibii loo dumɔwui.

english: How does applying fertilizer early help my crops survive if the rain suddenly stops for a week?
ga: Ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli mra Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa otsi kome?

english: Well-fertilized plants build deeper, stronger root systems early on, allowing them to reach water stored deeper in the soil when the surface dries out.
ga: Tsei ni awo amɛ fɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa baa mra. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ashɛɔ nu ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ he kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is ready for me to plant after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: Your soil is ready when the first rains have soaked in deeply enough to make the dirt soft and crumbly to touch, but not so wet that it forms sticky mud that chokes seeds.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ebote mli shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni eha muji lɛ afee blɛoo ni efo kɛji eshɛ he lɛ. Shi jeee ni edɔ tsɔ bɔ ni efeɔ muji ni shwieɔ shi ni fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How do I know if my maize crop is performing well before harvest time comes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miiya nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ?

english: Healthy maize that is performing well stands tall with strong, dark green leaves, sturdy stems, and uniform growth across the field without yellowing or signs of pest damage.
ga: Abɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ baai ni tsuɔ nii waa. tso ni mli wa kɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ ni ŋmɔŋ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ he okadi ko bɛ mli.

english: What makes a maize crop produce an abundant harvest in some seasons and very little in others?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa woɔ ŋmaa babaoo yɛ bei komɛi amli, ni ewoɔ fioo yɛ bei krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Abundant maize yields depend on a combination of using good certified seeds, planting with proper spacing, applying fertilizer at the right growth stages, and getting adequate rain.
ga: Abɛi babaoo ni anáa lɛ damɔ dumɔwui kpakpai ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli Woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa

english: How can I prepare my land properly so that my maize plants grow strong and stand tall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni mi-abele tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ?

english: Clearing weeds, plowing or loosening the soil, and adding compost or organic manure creates a rich, loose root environment that helps maize anchor firmly and absorb water and nutrients.
ga: jwɛi ŋmɔmɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo humus fataa he lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Is it good to farm the same piece of land every year, or will the soil stop producing well?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaatsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ baakpa yibiiwoo?

english: Farming the same soil repeatedly without adding nutrients depletes its fertility over time; rotating crops with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients to keep harvests high.
ga: Okwaayeli ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ Kɛ́ okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he lɛ, fɔmɔ ni oyɔɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni aduɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts fata he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to leave space between my maize seeds instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing gives every maize plant enough room to receive full sunlight, spread its roots, and feed on soil nutrients without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa he lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo, egbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa, ni eŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ.

english: What happens if I plant too many maize seeds in one small area on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he ko bibioo? Ekome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Overcrowded maize plants compete heavily for light, water, and food, causing them to grow thin, weak, and produce small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Abɛi tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu kɛ niyenii he akaŋshii mli waa, ni no haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii. loo cob ko bɛ kwraa

english: Why do the leaves on some of my maize plants turn pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil, meaning the plant lacks the key nutrient required to grow leaves and produce healthy foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii ni he hiaa koni ebaakwɛ̃ ni ewo baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: When is the best time to give fertilizer to my growing maize plants?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-abele tsei lɛ amli?

english: Maize usually needs fertilizer twice: a starter application shortly after germination when leaves appear, and a second application (top-dressing) when plants reach knee height to support cob formation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa he hiaa ni akɛ ŋmãa awo mli shii enyɔ: ŋmãa lɛ jeɔ shishi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ beni baai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ. kɛ be ni ji enyɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli (Top fertilizing) beni tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛnaji ahe koni eye ebua cob feemɔ.

english: Why does removing weeds early in the season help my maize produce bigger cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-ŋmã lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from young crops; removing them early ensures all the goodness in the soil goes straight into making your maize strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli. Ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha nibii kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aha o-ŋmã lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes maize stalks to fall down easily when heavy rain or wind comes?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli?

english: Maize falls over easily when its roots are shallow, when stalks are weakened by insect pests like stalk borers, or when plant rows are planted too closely together.
