ga: Abɛi gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Beni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ stem borers lɛ egbɔjɔ tsei lɛ ahe, loo be mli ni adu tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow prematurely usually due to a lack of nitrogen in the soil or improper watering. Nitrogen acts as plant food for green foliage; without enough of it, the plant steals nutrients from older lower leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmãa baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya lɛ baa. Nitrogen tsuɔ nii akɛ tso niyenii kɛha ebaai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ. Kɛji akɛ eshɛɛɛ Tso lɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eye ebua dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience heat stress, irregular watering, or a shortage of nutrients like phosphorus. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ, kɛ́ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli Ebaashi fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the main stem starts to crack. You can harvest one test plant to see if the tubers are full, firm, and mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ he lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. Obaanyɛ okpa kaa tso kome koni ona kɛji bulbs lɛ eyi, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edara.

english: Why do my groundnuts start to sprout under the ground if I wait too long to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmeii lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani mikpa lɛ?

english: Groundnut seeds naturally enter a growing phase once they reach full maturity. If matured pods stay in damp soil for too long, the moisture tricks the seeds into breaking open and sprouting new stems while still buried.
ga: Peanut dumɔwui lɛ boteɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ be mli beni amɛshɛɔ dalɛ he lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni edara lɛ hi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Fɛ̃i lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ atswa ni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii heei be mli ni afu amɛ lolo lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads during wet and humid weather. Moisture allows fungal spores to multiply on the skin of the pod, which rots the shell and spoils the cocoa beans inside.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Fɛ̃i haa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɛ pod lɛ hewolo nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ kookoo yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: What makes my tomato plants suddenly wilt and collapse during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni haa mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Excess rain causes waterlogging in the soil, which smothers plant roots by cutting off oxygen. Damp soil also encourages waterborne fungi and bacteria that rot the roots and block water from moving up the stem, causing quick wilting.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ fiteɔ tsei shishifãi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ hu woɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛtsiɔ nu naa koni ekaya ŋwɛi tso lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa oya

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant cowpeas alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. This enriches the ground with free food for the maize while covering the soil to reduce weed growth.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmli ni amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛwoɔ mli koni jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread easily.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ ahe.

english: Why does witchweed keep coming back to damage my sorghum even after I clear the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abɛi yaa nɔ ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa koni ebakpata mi-sorghum lɛ hiɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii moŋ

english: Witchweed, or Striga, is a parasitic weed whose microscopic seeds can live underground for over ten years. When sorghum roots grow nearby, they release chemical signals that tell the weed seeds to sprout and attach to the crop's roots.
ga: Witchweed loo Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui bibii waa ni baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi nɔ ni fe afii nyɔŋma. Kɛji ŋmãa shishifãi kwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ejieɔ tsofa okadii ni kɛɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ kpo.

english: Plantains have shallow roots carrying a very heavy upper stem and fruit bunch. Pests like banana weevils or microscopic root worms often damage the roots underground, leaving the heavy tree without a strong anchor.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋwɛi tsei lɛ tsii kɛ aduawai akui. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ banana ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ekɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsiiɔ ni ebɛ sɛkɛ ni wa.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed animal manure helps make the leaves green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us to plant cowpea or groundnuts before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu tsina loo ŋmei dani wɔdu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting maize after these crops allows the maize to feed on this natural soil fertilizer and grow bigger yields.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ asɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni aha abele lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and adding wood ash or agricultural lime to the soil helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo okwaayeli mli sũ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the leaves of maize plants. Spraying recommended treatments like neem leaf extract or targeted pest control early in the morning or late evening kills the caterpillars.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ koni akɛgbe ŋmeii lɛ ashwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and getting small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the plant's juices, or by a virus they spread. Spraying the plants with soapy water, neem oil, or appropriate pesticides helps keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli edɔ, neem fɔ, loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long because the roots cannot get air underwater. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aná kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ nu shishi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are flowers falling off my cocoa trees without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree lacks water, nutrition, or shade, or when tiny insects like mirids attack them. Providing adequate shade trees and protecting the farm from insects helps the flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nu, niyenii loo hulutsoo, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ ashwishwɛi tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo ni sa ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong stalks and big maize cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji baakwɛ̃.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground where they get more sun and stay safe from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Staking baaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ebaaná hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ, ni ehi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: How do weeds reduce my crop yield even when I give my plants enough water?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa mitsei lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on the farm by taking away water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures your main crop gets all the nutrients it needs to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ onibii amli lɛ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and yellow when I plant without adding fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants need proper food to grow strong, just like humans. Without fertilizer or compost, the soil quickly runs out of vital nutrients like nitrogen, causing leaves to turn yellow and plants to stay small and weak.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ faaa oya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ.

english: How does fertilizer actually help my maize plants produce bigger cobs?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmãa wuji tɛŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer provides essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. These feed the roots and leaves, giving the maize plant enough energy to build larger, healthier cobs full of grain.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasium. Enɛɛmɛi haa shishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmãa wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni dumɔwui eyi mli obɔ.

english: Will my crops die if I put too much fertilizer on them at one time?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagboi kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli shikome?

english: Yes, applying too much chemical fertilizer can burn the roots and pull moisture away from the plant, causing the leaves to wither and potentially killing the crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ni ejie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gboɔ ni ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and drop off before the fruit is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often mean the plant is short on soil nutrients, lacking enough water, or suffering from a root fungal disease, which stops the plant from getting the energy it needs to sustain its leaves.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛye ebua ebaai lɛ.

english: Why do cassava plants stay green and produce food even when the dry season is very harsh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwoɔ niyenii yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa po mli lɛ?

english: Cassava is a naturally hardy crop with deep root systems that store water and nutrients deep underground, allowing it to survive hot weather far better than crops like maize or vegetables.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa ehiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow faster than my main crops after I spread fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that quickly steal the fertilizer and water meant for your crops. You must clear the weeds around your crops before applying fertilizer so the crops get the food first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ oya. Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ dani awoɔ ŋmɔshi nii koni tsei lɛ aná niyenii klɛŋklɛŋ

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of moisture in the soil, or an improper balance of soil nutrients like too much nitrogen.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa ha tsei lɛ miihao. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni sa, tamɔ nitrogen babaoo.

english: Why do crops fail to yield good food during prolonged hot weather in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛɛɛ awo niyenii kpakpa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli edɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Without enough rainfall or irrigation, crops cannot absorb nutrients from the soil, causing their leaves to dry out and preventing flowers from turning into fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ loo nu shwieee shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ ni etsĩɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui.

english: What makes farm fields in places like Agogo yield higher harvests than fields with poor soil?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hei tamɔ Agogo lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe ŋmɔji ni sũ ehiii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Areas with rich, fertile soil hold more natural moisture and essential organic matter, giving crops a steady food supply to grow larger leaves, roots, and heavier harvests.
ga: Hei ni shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni baa nii yɔɔ lɛ hiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nu babaoo kɛ nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ baai, shishifãi, kɛ nibii ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is too poor to grow crops before I even plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ehiii kwraa ni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu dumɔwui lɛ po?

english: Soil that is very hard, pale in color, sandy, or where wild weeds grow small and yellowish usually signals low fertility that requires compost or fertilizer before planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa waa, ni mli tse, ni ŋã yɔɔ mli loo hei ni koo mli jwɛi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɔɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa, ni no biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii dani adu.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen in the soil, or the ground is too soaked with water, preventing roots from breathing and feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn the grass and weeds on my plot before planting my next crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: While burning clears the land fast, it burns away valuable organic matter and kills small living organisms in the soil that keep your earth fertile and able to hold water.
ga: Beni shãa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya lɛ Eshãa nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu lɛ.

english: Why do my small cocoa seedlings wither and die during the hot, dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ Ani minɔ lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and tender leaves that burn easily in full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a sunshade, keeping them cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaatsu nii tamɔ hulutsoo tsei. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to put my cassava cuttings into the soil after the early rains start?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the rains become regular for about two weeks so the soil stays deep-moist, which prevents your cassava sticks from drying out before they form strong roots.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ bɔ ni sa, aaafee otsii enyɔ, koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ agbi dani amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why are small holes appearing in the funnels of my young maize leaves with tiny worms inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu lɛ ji bibioo lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating tender crop leaves. Catching them early with recommended bio-pesticides or neem oil prevents them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei bibii ahe baai lɛ. Mɔ amɛ mra. Kɛtsɔ bio-insecticide loo neem fɔ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the dark brown bottoms of my growing tomatoes turning soft and squishy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi ni midu lɛ ashishi lɛ ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, which happens when irregular watering prevents the tomato plant from absorbing enough calcium from the soil while forming fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ tsiɔ tomato tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas or groundnuts between my rows of tall maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpeas trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally feeds the maize and improves your harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ ni ehaa okpamɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when plants suffer stress from severe heat, sudden dry spells, or too much water, causing the plant to abort its blossoms before fruit can set.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Trukaa hulutsoo be loo nu babaoo ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Will watering my vegetable bed under the hot afternoon sun damage my plants?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛwoɔ mi aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baafite mitsei lɛ?

english: Watering in strong heat causes the water to evaporate before roots can drink it and can shock hot leaves. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: Nu ni akɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anu. ni ebaanyɛ eha baai ni mli edɔ lɛ akpokpo Esa akɛ awo nu lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing green shoots while sitting inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃mɔ be mli ni mita mi shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break their resting period when room temperatures and air moisture rise, forcing the tuber to use up its stored food reserves to sprout leaves.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafite amɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ beni tsu lɛ mli latsaa kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ bulb lɛ atsu niyenii fɛɛ ni ato lɛ he nii koni ekwɛ baai.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them provides the shade and humidity young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why am I finding small holes in my maize leaves and worms inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baa mli ni ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young maize foliage. Early detection and spraying recommended organic or chemical treatments into the central whorl of the leaf helps protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Akɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ ana tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsaa hela lɛ mra ni akɛshwie nɔ. kɛbote baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava performs best in deep, well-draining sandy loam soil that allows its roots to expand into tubers. Clay soils that hold too much water cause the cassava roots to rot before harvest.
ga: Yucca tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ bulbs. Shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly damp conditions. Pruning tree branches to let in light and clearing infected pods away from the farm stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni edɔ tsɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tsei ni afolɔ koni la aba mli kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my maize field?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer is usually applied in two stages: a first application about two weeks after germination to boost root and leaf growth, and a second application around five to six weeks when the plant starts developing tassels.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ajaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli awoɔ fãi enyɔ mli: Klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ dara lɛ. ni fɔmɔ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ ji aaafee otsii enumɔ kɛyashi enumɔ beni tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Can I grow pepper and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping pepper with maize works well because maize grows tall while pepper stays low, allowing both crops to share nutrients and sunlight without crowding each other out.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ kɛlɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hulu la ni amɛtsiii amɛhe kɛjɛɛɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my main crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds naturally have aggressive root systems adapted to grab water and soil nutrients instantly. Removing weeds early prevents them from stealing essential food and sunlight from your young crop plants.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni haa nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need stakes to lift their leaves off the ground toward sunlight. Exposure to full sun helps the leaves create energy, which feeds the growth of large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shishitoo mla ni ji amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la lɛ nɔ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji ni daraa lɛ hewalɛ

english: What causes my tomato plant leaves to curl up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward to protect themselves and reduce water loss during hot, dry conditions. Mulching the soil around the base with dry leaves helps retain soil moisture and reduce plant stress.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli koni amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛha nu ni amɛlaajeɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi shwie shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ ahi shi ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe haomɔ baa shi.

english: How do I tell when my maize is fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer husks turn dry and papery brown, and pressing your thumbnail into a kernel no longer leaves a wet dent, showing the grain has hardened.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, egbi ni efee tamɔ wolo. Ni kɛ́ okɛ o-thumbnail lɛ nyɛ dumɔwu lɛ nɔ lɛ, eshiŋ he ko ni efɔ dɔŋŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli ewa.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct sunlight and burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa provides living shade and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe. Ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to stay green and healthy. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and supports bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why does planting groundnuts before maize make my maize grow better without adding extra fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ dani awoɔ ŋmei lɛ haa mi ŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmei kroko fataaa he lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested, that trapped nutrient stays in the soil and feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Niyenii nibii ni amɔmɔ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce food. Staking lifts the foliage, helping the leaves capture maximum light so the tubers underwater can grow big.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ bɔni afee ni nu shishi tsɔne lɛ anyɛ adara.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for limited sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Giving plants enough space allows roots to spread and stems to grow thick and strong.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la fioo, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ni eshishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Excessive water fills up air pockets in the dirt, suffocating the roots and causing rot-causing fungi and bacteria to attack the crop.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by severe heat or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist during hot days helps the plant hold onto flowers so they can form fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ fe nine loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the undersides of young leaves, or by a virus transmitted by these pests. Controlling small insects early stops leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kplukai bibii anɔyeli mra Ehaa baa lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why should I trim off the bottom dry leaves from my oil palm trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ashishi baai ni egbi lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pruning dead fronds prevents pests from nesting in the tree and stops the palm from wasting energy on dying leaves, directing food straight into developing fresh fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni egboi lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee amɛ shĩa yɛ tso lɛ mli. ni etsĩ ŋmei tsei anaa koni amɛkafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni miigboi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, niyenii lɛ tsɔɔ aduawai heei akui ni baa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops stop growing even when I water the farm well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha midumɔwui lɛ miikpa kwɛ̃mɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water and fertilizer from the soil much faster than young crops can. Removing weeds eliminates this competition so your crops get all the nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii baanyɛ afee. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa akaŋshii ni yɔɔ otsei lɛ fɛɛ ahe lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and can easily get scorched. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them protects the cocoa leaves from harsh sun rays and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaabu kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crops turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually show that the plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or decomposed animal manure gives the crop the energy it needs to grow green leaves and large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔlii kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my vegetable crops grow much bigger when I mix dried poultry manure into the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daraa babaoo waa kɛ́ mikɛ kooloi ashishifã ni egbi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Poultry manure improves the soil's ability to hold water and slowly releases essential nutrients that vegetable roots need to build strong stems and produce large fruits.
ga: Kooloi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli babaoo, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa aduawai shishifãi koni amɛná tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji lɛ kpo fiofio.

english: How do I know which end of a cassava stem cutting should face upward when I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ naagbee ni esa akɛ ekwɛ ŋwɛi beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Look closely at the small leaf buds along the cassava stem. The buds must point upward toward the sky; planting them upside down causes delayed sprouting and reduces your final tuber yield.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Nyiɛmɔ ŋmei tso lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni oootsɔ hiɛ lɛ baaha kwɛ̃mɔ asɛɛ afo ni ebaaha onaagbee bulb yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Which type of plantain sucker is best for me to dig up when starting a new farm?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui sucker henɔ sa akɛ mafo beni mijeɔ ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Choose 'sword suckers', which have narrow, spear-like leaves and a large base. They grow faster, establish stronger roots, and produce bigger bunches than 'water suckers' that have broad leaves.
ga: Halamɔ ‘Sword Bud,’ ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi kɛ shishigbɛ agbo lɛ. Amɛ daa oya. Tsɔɔmɔ shishifãi ni wa ni ofee fɔfɔi agbo fe ‘tso ni nuɔ nu’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant faces water stress from dry soil or severe heat. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots helps the flowers stay attached and form healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo latsaa ni naa wa mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cucumber plants yield better when I lift the vines off the ground using wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kukumba tso lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai kɛ́ mikɛ tsei ni akɛfee tsei wo wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting cucumber vines off the ground improves airflow around the leaves and keeps the fruits away from wet soil. This prevents rot and fungal diseases, allowing the plant to produce clean, healthy cucumbers.
ga: Kukumba wain tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ akashɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Koni akafee ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ kukumbai ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for growing large tubers underground. Staking raises the leaves off the hot ground and spreads them out to catch more sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my main season maize after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije ŋmãa dumɔ shishi yɛ be titri lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plant after the first two or three steady rains have deeply soaked the soil. Planting in dry soil after just one light shower can cause the seeds to dry up and fail to germinate.
ga: Dumɔ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why do the center leaves of my young maize plants look chewed up with small holes and powdery dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni atsɔ mli ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ hu yɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding inside the central leaf funnel of the maize. Applying approved organic or chemical control early in the morning helps protect the growing tip of your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa loo tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi ahe.

english: If a factory agrees to buy my tomatoes, why do I need to follow a strict planting schedule?
ga: Kɛji nitsumɔhe lɛ kpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ ebaahe mi-tomato lɛ Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ tomato dumɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa nɔ?

english: Factories can only process a set amount of fresh tomatoes each day. Following a planting schedule spreads out your harvest so the factory can receive your tomatoes when they are fresh, rather than letting them spoil while waiting in line.
ga: Nitsumɔhe lɛ baanyɛ atsu tomato hee ko pɛ he nii daa gbi. Kɛ́ onyiɛ dumɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo ko sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha onifeemɔi lɛ afee srɔtoi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aná otomatoi lɛ beni amɛji ehee lolo lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha o-tomato lɛ agbo beni omɛɔ yɛ line mli lɛ,.

english: Does a tomato processing factory accept any type of tomato I harvest, or do I need specific seeds?
ga: Ani nitsumɔhe ni feɔ tomato lɛ kpɛlɛɔ tomato srɔtoi fɛɛ ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ? Or do I need specific seeds?

english: Factories usually require specific processing varieties that have thicker skins, firmer flesh, and deep red color. Planting the seeds approved by the factory guarantees your crop meets their standards for paste or canning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nitsumɔhei biɔ nibii pɔtɛɛ ni atsu he nii ni hewolo lɛ mli wa, loo ni mli wa, kɛ su tsuru ni mli kwɔ. Dumɔwui ni nitsumɔhe lɛ kpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha ona nɔmimaa akɛ onibii lɛ baashɛ shishitoo mlai ni kɔɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli loo ni akɛwoɔ tsinsii mii lɛ ahe lɛ he.

english: How do I know the best month to plant tomatoes so they don't get ruined by heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nyɔŋ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu tomato? Bɔni afee ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafite lɛ?

english: Tomatoes grow best when planted toward the tail-end of the major rainy season or under irrigation during the dry season. Too much rain washes away flowers and spreads fungal diseases on the leaves.
ga: Tomato daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee loo yɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ ni egbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ eshwaa baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young tomato plants wilt in the afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In high heat, leaves lose water faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to shade itself and reduce water loss, and it will bounce back once the sun sets as long as the soil remains moist.
ga: kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ baagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛha hulutsoo ni amɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Ni ebaaku esɛɛ kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi pɛ, be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Flowers fall off when temperatures are too high or when the plant is stressed from sudden dry spells. Keeping the soil evenly damp and planting shade crops nearby can help lower the heat around the flowers so they set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ aba shi koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very tall with big green leaves, but no fruits are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Adding too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the crop focus all its energy on leaf growth instead of flowering. Balancing nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to stop making extra leaves and start producing tomatoes.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ baaha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi. Nitrogen kɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkpaa baai krokomɛi ni amɛfeɔ lɛ ni amɛjeɔ tomato feemɔ shishi.

english: What happens to my tomato plants if I put the seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Crowded crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin stalks and smaller fruits. Good spacing allows breeze to pass through, keeping the leaves dry and preventing plant diseases.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ aduawai bibii baa. He ni jɛkɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa tsei ahe helai aba.

english: This condition, known as blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture consistent prevents the fruit bottoms from drying out and rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baatsi aduawai ashishi lɛ anaa koni ekagbi ni ekafite.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often a defense against intense heat, or a sign that tiny insects like whiteflies are sucking sap from the leaves. Inspecting under the leaves and using proper pest controls protects the foliage so the crop can feed its fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ni abɔleɔ he lɛ ji nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo ni fe nine lɛ he. Aloo eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies miinu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi ni okɛ tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu baai lɛ ahe koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii.

english: How can I stop my harvested tomatoes from turning soft and going bad before I take them to market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tomato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafee blɛoo ni efite dani mikɛya jara nɔ?

english: Harvest tomatoes early in the morning while temperatures are cool, pack them gently in ventilated plastic crates instead of deep sacks, and keep them shaded to stop heat build-up and bruising.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tomato leebi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ lolo lɛ. Okɛ amɛ awo plastic adekai ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli blɛoo moŋ fe kotokui ni mli kwɔlɔ. Ni ha ehi he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli koni hulutsoo akabua ehe naa ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: What is hand pollination in cocoa, and why should I consider doing it on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nine ni akɛwoɔ kooko mli lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe?

english: Cocoa flowers need pollen to turn into pods. While insects do some of this naturally, hand pollination means manually transferring pollen from flower to flower to ensure almost every flower turns into a healthy cocoa pod, greatly increasing your total harvest.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ biɔ pollen koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi feɔ enɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa moŋ, shi nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ niji shwieɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. Enɛ haa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi tsɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing so many flowers, but very few of them turn into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi tsei fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed flowers if there aren't enough insect pollinators or if the tree lacks water and nutrients. Assisting pollination by hand and feeding your trees ensures more flowers successfully grow into full pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ faaa loo kɛji nu kɛ niyenii ni haa tso lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Ni ayeɔ abuaa kɛ nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ fɔfɔi ni eyi obɔ babaoo.

english: How do I know when my cocoa farm is producing enough to start investing time in hand pollination?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi be kɛ nitsumɔ yɛ nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli?

english: Once your farm enters full production and gives you a steady harvest—such as 10 or more bags per season—the trees are mature and strong enough to support the extra pod load that hand pollination creates.
ga: Beni oŋmɔ lɛ yaa nitsumɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ekpaa nii daa, tamɔ kotokui 10 loo nɔ ni fe nakai yɛ be mli. Tso lɛ baadara ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmeii ayibɔ ni yaa hiɛ ni nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ feɔ lɛ.

english: How many years does a newly planted cocoa tree take before it starts bearing fruit?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years to yield their first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ be mli ni kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does my neighbor get double the number of cocoa bags from the same size of land as mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ miiná kookoo kotokui ni fa fe mi nɔ lɛ toi enyɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ mi nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yield differences usually come down to soil fertility, proper pruning, shade management, and disease control. Giving your trees enough sunlight, fertilizer, and pest protection allows each tree to produce maximum pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli lɛ damɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ fɛo ha lɛ nɔ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ helai anɔkwɛmɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ha lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso awo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ.

english: What is the best way to scale up my farm if I want to produce significantly more cocoa in the future?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ? Kɛji akɛ esa akɛ kookoo feemɔ aya hiɛ waa wɔsɛɛ

english: To scale up successfully, reinvest profits from your current yield into improved high-yielding hybrid seeds, practice proper tree spacing, and maintain strict pest and disease control schedules.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni okɛ omanyeyeli atsu nii lɛ, no lɛ, okɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni onáa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ amrɔ nɛɛ amli lɛ awo dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ yibii babaoo mli ekoŋŋ. Tsɔɔmɔ gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ he nii. ni amɛkwɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa ni akɛbaatsu tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do cocoa prices set by the government change from one season to another in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo jara ni nɔyeli lɛ toɔ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ be kome mli kɛyaa be kroko mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Cocoa prices are set by COCOBOD based on global supply and demand, international market rates, and exchange rates, aiming to give farmers a fair, guaranteed farmgate price each main crop season.
ga: COCOBOD ji mɔ ni toɔ cocoa jara yɛ jeŋ muu fɛɛ nibii ni akɛhaa kɛ nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ nɔ. Majimaji ateŋ jarayeli mli jara kɛ shika tsakemɔ Oti ni ma hiɛ ji ni aha okwaafoi lɛ aná ŋmɔ mli jara ni ja ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be titri fɛɛ be mli.

english: What steps must I take during harvest to ensure my cocoa beans get the best price at the buying depot?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii esa akɛ mafee yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ mi-kookoo lɛ ná jara ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: To get top grade and maximum payout, you must ferment your fresh beans properly in plantain leaves for 5 to 6 days and thoroughly sun-dry them until they have a low moisture content and rich brown color.
ga: Koni anyɛ ana ŋmeii heei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni fe fɛɛ. Ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ plantain baai amli lɛ awo mli jogbaŋŋ gbii 5 kɛyashi 6 ni okɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi be mli ni amɛhe baajɔ ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How long can a cocoa tree remain productive and give me good harvests before it gets too old?
ga: Be enyiɛ cacao tso baanyɛ awo yibii ni ewo yibii dani egbɔ tsɔ?

english: A well-cared-for cocoa tree can remain healthy and produce good yields for 25 to 30 years or more before its production naturally begins to slow down.
ga: Cacao tsei ni akwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani yibiiwoo lɛ aje shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet and dark conditions. Pruning excess shade trees, clearing weeds, and spraying approved fungicides will protect your pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ duŋ mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo fe nine lɛ ni ooofolɔ, jwɛi ni ooojie, kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu o-pods lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an important nutrient for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves stay green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why does my groundnut farm produce plenty of green leaves but very few nuts under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants need soft, loose soil so the flower stalks can easily push into the dirt to form nuts. Hard or compacted soil, or using too much nitrogen fertilizer, forces the plant to grow leaves instead of nuts.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia ŋmei tsei. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ ashɛ fɔfɔi ahe tsei awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni efee ŋmeii. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii Enɛ baaha tso lɛ akwɛ baai yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil cool, protecting the young cocoa trees during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I alternate planting maize with beans or groundnuts on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize pests to multiply. Rotating with beans or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ feɔ babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, ehaa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to start sowing seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain, as the soil underneath remains dry. Wait until you get two or three heavy rains that soak the ground deep enough to keep the seeds hydrated for continuous growth.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli egbi lolo. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo wu bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: What causes my watermelons to split open on the farm before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-watermelon lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani eshɛɔ shweremɔ he?

english: Watermelons split open when they receive a sudden surge of heavy water or rain after a long dry spell. The inside of the fruit expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to burst.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛji nu afua loo nugbɔ ni naa wa ba trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai lɛ amli fãmɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling up and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of the leaves. Spraying early with natural neem oil or appropriate treatments keeps these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Neem fɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ mra Loo tsofafeemɔ ni sa baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather conditions are too hot, when the soil dries out completely between waterings, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like calcium.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ loo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily and prevents root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya, ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that absorb nutrients and water faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing light, water, and food from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la, nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to loosen hard soil before planting my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie shikpɔŋ ni wa dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Loosening hard soil creates a soft path for young shoots to break through easily and allows roots to spread safely. If the ground is too hard, the seed struggles to push through and can die underground before sprouting.
ga: Gbalamɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɔ koni ŋmeii bibii lɛ abote mli mlɛo ni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shweshweeshwe. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛbote mli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What will happen to my crop seeds if the soil dries out completely right after planting?
ga: Mɛni baa midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ kwraa beni adu lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Seeds need continuous moisture to wake up and start growing. If the soil dries out completely right after planting, the seed stops developing inside the ground and will die before it ever sprouts.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu daa koni amɛte shi ni amɛbɔi dalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakpa shweremɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaagboi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young vegetable plants wilt and die during a short dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants have shallow roots and depend heavily on topsoil moisture. Without enough water, the plant cannot carry food from the soil to its leaves, causing it to weaken and die quickly.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛdamɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ waa. Kɛji nu faaa lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya baai lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egboɔ oya.

english: Is it dangerous to stop watering my pepper plants when they start producing flowers?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ oookpa ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu kɛji amɛbɔi fɔmɔ?

english: Yes, flowering plants need extra water to form healthy fruits. If you do not provide water during this stage, the plant gets stressed, drops its flowers, or produces small, ruined fruits that dry up early.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia nu kroko koni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji ohaaa nu yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli Tso lɛ baaná haomɔ, fɔfɔi ni baagbee shi loo aduawai bibii ni baagboi ni baagbi oya.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my crops help them stay alive in heat?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛyeɔ hulutsoo be lɛ nɔ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass, or mulching, acts like a protective shade over the dirt. It stops hot sunlight from evaporating soil moisture, keeping the ground damp so your crops can drink even on hot days.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baatsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni baabu he kɛjɛ muji he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni onibii lɛ anu nu yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ po amli.

english: What causes tomato fruits to rot at the bottom while still on the stem?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato aduawai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the plant experiences sudden dry periods without water. Irregular watering prevents the plant from absorbing key soil nutrients, causing the growing fruit to spoil before it ripens.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo be trukaa ni nu bɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa lɛ haaa amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai ni miida lɛ fiteɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are my nursery seedlings dying before I can move them to my main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ gboiɔ dani ajieɔ amɛ kɛyaa miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Baby seedlings in a nursery are very delicate. If they do not get enough water and shade, they dry out rapidly and die in their seedbeds before growing strong enough for field planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ waaa kwraa. Kɛji onine shɛɛɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa nɔ lɛ, Amɛgbiɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings fail to sprout when I plant them in dry ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings need moisture in the soil to stimulate root growth. Planting them in dry soil without watering causes the stem to dry out completely and die inside the soil before roots can form.
ga: Cassava tsei ni afolɔ lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ koni eha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni awooo nɔ nu lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbi kwraa ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why should I clear weeds away from the base of my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water and plant food directly from the soil surrounding your crop. Clearing them ensures your young plant gets all the water and nourishment it needs to survive and grow.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha otsei bibii lɛ aná nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara.

english: How can I keep my young cocoa plants from dying during their first dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagboi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa trees dry out easily in direct sun. Planting plantains alongside them provides shade and holds moisture in the soil, protecting the tender cocoa plants so they do not die from heat and thirst.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Buu kookoo tso ni mli tse lɛ he Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kumai amli.

english: Why should I tie a red cloth or ribbon on my plant when it starts flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ mama tsuru loo tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ akpɛtɛ tso lɛ he beni tso lɛ jeɔ fɔmɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Tying a bright cloth or ribbon on the plant marks the exact day flowering begins, making it easy to visually record when fruit development started without needing to write down dates.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ mama loo tsɔne ni mli tse fĩ tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha gbi ni fɔfɔi lɛ baawo lɛ afee faŋŋ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaaŋɔ hiŋmɛi akwɛ be ni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni aŋmala gbi ni eba lɛ awo shi.

english: Why is it important for me to keep track of the day flowers first appear on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ makwɛ gbi ni fɔfɔii lɛ jeɔ kpo klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: The emergence of flowers marks the start of the final stage of crop growth. Knowing the exact flowering date allows you to count the required months until the harvest is fully ripe.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni jeɔ kpo lɛ kadiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ naagbee fã lɛ shishijee. Kɛ́ ole gbi pɔtɛɛ ni fɔfɔi lɛ baawo lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okaneɔ nyɔji ni he hiaa lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kpamɔ lɛ baashɛ shi kwraa.

english: How do I know when my crops will be ready for harvest after they start flowering?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛbɔi fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Each crop variety requires a specific number of months to develop after flowering begins. By adding that fixed time to the date your flowers first appeared, you can predict your harvest day.
ga: Tso srɔtoi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko biɔ nyɔji babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ beni eje fɔfɔii ashishi lɛ sɛɛ. Be pɔtɛɛ ko ni okɛbaafata gbi ni ofɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ kpo klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ he. Obaanyɛ otsɔɔ gbi ni obaakpa nii lɛ.

english: What is the best simple way to mark key growth dates on my farm if I cannot write them down?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ makadi gbii ni he hiaa ni mikwɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji minyɛɛɛ maŋmala amɛ?

english: Using colored rags, cloth strips, or stakes tied to representative plants in your field is a practical way to physically flag important events like the start of flowering.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsɔji, atadei ni akɛwoɔ mli, loo tsei ni akɛfi tsei ni damɔ shi kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eji gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akadiɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni tee nɔ lɛ, tamɔ fɔfɔii ashishijee.

english: How can I tell that my crop has shifted from growing leaves to making fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ etsake kɛjɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ kɛtee yibiiwoo nɔ?

english: The appearance of the very first flower on your plant is the clear sign that it has finished its leafy growth phase and is starting to produce fruits or pods.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi ni jeɔ kpo yɛ otso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ egbe ebaai lɛ adalɛ be lɛ naa. ni ejeɔ shishi ewoɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii

english: How does knowing the specific crop variety I am growing help me manage my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ ni miduɔ lɛ ni mileɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni makwɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Different varieties have different lifespan requirements—some take 5 months while others take longer. Knowing your specific variety allows you to plan your labor and market sales accurately.
ga: Srɔtoi yɛ wala be he taomɔ nii srɔtoi. Mɛi komɛi heɔ nyɔji 5, yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi hu heɔ be babaoo. Osrɔtoi pɔtɛɛ ni ole lɛ haa otoɔ onitsumɔ kɛ jarayeli nibii ahe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my crops taking a different amount of time to harvest compared to my neighbor's crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ be ni yɔɔ srɔto fe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: You and your neighbor are likely growing different varieties of the crop. Certain improved varieties mature faster, such as in 5 months, while traditional varieties may take longer.
ga: Ekolɛ bo kɛ okutsoŋbii lɛ duɔ tsei srɔtoi. Henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekomɛi shwereɔ oya, tamɔ yɛ nyɔji 5 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema henɔi lɛ baanyɛ ahe be babaoo.

english: How long does a typical medium-duration crop variety take from flowering to harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ tso ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ be mli lɛ heɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔii ni ewoɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ekpaa nii lɛ nɔ?

english: Depending on the specific variety you plant, many standard improved varieties take around 5 months from the initial flowering phase to full maturity.
ga: Edamɔ tso pɔtɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ. Henɔi srɔtoi babaoo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji enumɔ kɛjɛɔ shishijee fɔfɔii kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: What happens if I harvest my crop before its specified maturity period is complete?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani be ni ato lɛ ho?

english: Harvesting before the crop completes its required maturity period results in underdeveloped, light-weight, or poor-tasting produce that brings low prices at the market.
ga: Nikpamɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛ shweremɔ he lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo ni ŋɔɔ waa lɛ aba. ni haa jarayeli jara lɛ baa shi

english: What key information should I ask an extension officer about a new seed variety before I plant it?
ga: Mɛɛ saji ni he hiaa esa akɛ mabi mi-extension officer lɛ yɛ dumɔwui heei ahe dani madu amɛ?

english: You should ask for the exact duration the variety takes to mature—such as whether it is a 5-month crop—and how to identify key stages like flowering.
ga: Esa akɛ obi be pɔtɛɛ ni tso henɔ ko heɔ dani edaa, tamɔ kɛji eyɛ wala be ni ji nyɔji 5, kɛ bɔ ni ooofee oyoo fãi ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why does my farm soil dry up so quickly even after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ po lɛ?

english: Soil loses water quickly when it lacks organic matter like dried leaves or compost, and when direct sunlight hits bare ground without trees or shade crops to protect it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi loo ŋmɔshi nibii. Ni beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni tsei loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni baabu he lɛ bɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: What simple steps can I take to restore dry, worn-out soil on my farm?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mikɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni efite ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves (mulching), adding animal manure, and planting shade trees helps soil hold water and brings nutrients back to dead land.
ga: Akɛ baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching), ni akɛ kooloi aŋmei fata he. Ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ.

english: What causes tiny bugs to attack my cocoa trees and ruin the pods?
ga: Nɔ ni haa kooloi bibii ni Ba lɛ tutuaa mi-cacao tso lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Insects like mirids (capsids) feed on cocoa stems and pods, leaving small black spots that drain the plant's food and dry out young pods before they can mature.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ mirids (capsids) yeɔ kookoo tsei kɛ ŋmeii. ni ehaa ŋmeii bibii diji lɛ hoɔ tsei aniyenii amli ni ehaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ agbiɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa leaves are dying from pest damage or just heat from the sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo baai lɛ miigboi yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahewɔ loo hulutsoo kɛkɛ hewɔ?

english: Pest damage leaves small holes, sticky liquid, or dark spots on leaves and stems, while heat damage causes leaves to curl, dry, and droop evenly across the farm.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kɛ buji bibii baa. nu ni shwieɔ shi loo eyɛ ŋmeii diji yɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa yields decreasing every year even though my trees are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ni mifeɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni mi-kookoo tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, the soil loses essential nutrients, and hidden pest infestations or lack of shade can weaken trees, reducing the number of pods they produce.
ga: Kɛji kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo hɔnɔ ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni afee lɛ ayibɔ ba shi.

english: Why is my neighbor getting a heavy cocoa harvest while my farm in the same village produces very little?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ woɔ kookoo babaoo yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ akrowa kome mli lɛ woɔ kookoo fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Differences in soil quality, proper pruning, timely pest spraying, and the amount of shade on a farm can cause big variations in cocoa yields even in the same town.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli Ni hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ baanyɛ afee srɔto kwraa yɛ kookoo yibiiwoo mli yɛ maŋ kome mli po.

english: Why do some cocoa pods on my farm turn yellow and mature while others on the same tree stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiidara lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii komɛi ni yɔɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ kã he amɛfee eŋɔli.

english: Pods ripen at different times depending on how much direct sunlight they receive and how well nutrients travel to each specific branch on the tree.
ga: Pods lɛ shwereɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Edamɔ bɔ ni hulu la ni amɛnáa lɛ fa ha kɛ bɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa tso lɛ niji lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do shade trees keep my cocoa trees healthy during the dry season?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Shade trees block burning sunlight, lower the ground temperature, and keep humidity high around cocoa trees so they do not dry out during hot months.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ baa shi Ni ehaa latsaa yaa hiɛ yɛ cacao tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ nyɔji ni latsaa lɛ amli.

english: Why is it necessary for me to prune extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni jɛ kookoo tso mli lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to let in fresh air and sunlight, which reduces humidity where pests breed and directs energy into growing healthy pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi yɛ hei ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ yɛ lɛ, ni etsɔɔ hewalɛ gbɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni daraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will planting food crops like cassava or yam near my cocoa trees harm them?
ga: Ani niyenii nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ cacao tsei ahe lɛ baaye tsei nɛɛ awui?

english: Heavy feeding food crops like cassava can steal nutrients and groundwater from cocoa roots if planted too close, so they should be spaced far enough from young cocoa.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei baanyɛ aju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛjɛ kookoo shishifãi amli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ he ko ni kɛ kookoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ahi shi bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need to be planted under plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ dumɔwui ashishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong sunlight and can easily dry out and die. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce broad leaves that create protective shade, giving the cocoa seedlings the moist, cool environment they need in their early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. ni ebaanyɛ egbi ni egbo oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hɔɔŋ baa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives during cool, rainy weather. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to reach the pods, which dries them out and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmei lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry spells to save water and protect its root system underground. Once the rains return, the stem will sprout new green leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it necessary for me to heap soil into high mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibuaa sũ naa yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ dani miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yams need loose, soft, and well-drained soil so the roots can expand wide and long underground. Mounds prevent water from sitting around the tubers, which stops them from rotting before harvest.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛfee shɔŋŋ ni amɛlɛ. Gɔŋ lɛ tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle bulb lɛ he, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkafiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning purple and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ purple ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is lacking phosphorus in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure or phosphorus-rich fertilizer helps the roots grow deep and restores the natural green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛha amɛ adebɔɔ mli su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I get very small maize cobs when I drop three or four seeds into a single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mináa ŋmãa bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ ŋmãa bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When multiple seeds grow in the same hole, the plants compete with each other for water, sunlight, and plant food. Planting just one or two seeds per hole gives each stalk enough space and nutrients to grow big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii he akaŋ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ pɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifã lɛ eko fɛɛ eko aná he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmei agbo ko akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough water. Mulching the soil with dried leaves keeps the soil cool and moist, helping the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Curling leaves on tomato plants are usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Clearing weeds around your plot and protecting young beds helps keep whiteflies away from your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ajiemɔ Oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ saatsoi bibii ahebuu Enɛ baaye abua ni whiteflies lɛ akaje oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Planting the same crop continuously removes the same nutrients from the soil over and over, while attracting specific pests. Rotating your crop with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility and starves pests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni ayaa nɔ akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi hu. Nibii ni akɛduɔ nii kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ hɔmɔ baagbe kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do I find tiny insects eating holes inside my stored cowpea seeds after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Cowpea dumɔwui ni akɛto beni akpa ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yeli.
