english: These are cowpea weevils, which lay eggs on the pods while the crop is still in the field. Drying your cowpeas thoroughly under the sun and storing them in airtight containers or specialized bags suffocates the insects and protects your seeds.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji tsina ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsina ŋmeii egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku krɛdɛɛ ko mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebu odumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: How many years does it take for a new cocoa seedling to start bearing fruit?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwui heei woɔ yibii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting if properly maintained, whereas older traditional cocoa varieties take about 4 to 5 years to mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand strong direct sunlight because their roots are shallow and their leaves lose water faster than they can absorb it. They require shade crops like plantains during their early years to protect them from heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbaa lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he

english: Why does Ghana have two separate cocoa harvest seasons in a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Ghana yɛ kookoo kpamɔ bei srɔtoi enyɔ yɛ afi mli lɛ?

english: The two harvest seasons are driven by Ghana's rainfall cycle. The Main Crop season (October to March) comes after the heavy rains and gives larger yields, while the Mid Crop season (May to June) comes after smaller rains and produces fewer, smaller pods.
ga: Ghana nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni tsirɛɔ kpamɔ bei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Nikpamɔ be titri (October kɛyashi March) lɛ baa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ ni ehaa yibii babaoo baa. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ yɔɔ teŋgbɛ (May kɛyashi June) lɛ baa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo kɛ pod yibii bibii ni baa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many pods one year and then very few pods the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli, ni ewoɔ fioo yɛ afi kroko mli lɛ?

english: This natural behavior is called alternate bearing. A tree uses up most of its stored nutrients to produce a bumper crop, leaving it exhausted and needing the next year to rest and rebuild its energy.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ tsakemɔ. Tsei kɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ niyenii ni amɛto lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ehe hiaa ni ekɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their flowers before pods can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Trees shed excess flowers naturally when they do not have enough water or nutrients to support them all into full pods, or when insects like capsids damage the delicate flower stems.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛ fɛɛ amɛhi fɔfɔi ni eyi obɔ mli. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why are some of the pods on my tree small and withered while others grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ekomɛi ji bibii ni egbo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu dara lɛ?

english: Small, withered pods are often a result of cherelle wilt, a natural process where the tree intentionally sacrifices younger pods to conserve water and nutrients for the larger, healthier pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cherel ni egbo lɛ ji nɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni egbo lɛ amli baa. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei jɛɔ amɛtsui mli amɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii shaa afɔle koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly when the air is cold and very wet. High moisture on the pods allows the fungus to grow and destroy the crop.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ waa ni edɔ waa. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and fall off during the dry Harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their leaves during dry conditions as a survival defense to prevent water loss through the leaves when soil moisture is low.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots and side branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ esɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-producing branches that steal nutrients from the main trunk, while allowing sunlight and air to move freely through the canopy to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Niji ni wooo yibii ni juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ niji lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli bɔ ni sa koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ akamɔ bo.

english: Why do weeds in my farm reduce the number of pods my trees yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiba ŋmɔtɔ ni mitsei lɛ woɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from the roots of your cocoa trees, starving the crops and leaving them with too little energy to produce healthy pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa waa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ehaa hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli ni ekɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What changes will I see in my cocoa trees if I apply fertilizer during the main season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsakemɔi baaba kookoo tsei anɔ kɛji akɛ awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be titri lɛ mli?

english: Applying fertilizer during the main season helps the trees recover nutrients used to produce pods, leading to darker green leaves, stronger branches, and better flower development for future yields.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be titri lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli. Niji lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa. kɛ fɔfɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛbaatsu nii wɔsɛɛ lɛ afeemɔ

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm soil lacks nutrients and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your cocoa leaves turn pale or yellow, the trees produce small or very few pods, or flowers drop off easily, your soil is likely tired and needs fertilizer to replenish its nutrients.
ga: Kɛji o-cocoa baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ Tso lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ loo bibii loo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ etɔ ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer when the ground is dry or after rain has fallen?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is always best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a rain. Water helps dissolve the fertilizer so the roots can absorb it safely without burning the plant.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Nu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛshãaa tso lɛ.

english: When is the best time of year to start applying fertilizer to my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ aje kookoo tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii awomɔ shishi?

english: In Ghana, fertilizer is usually applied at the start of the rainy season, around May or June, so that the trees have plenty of water to break down and absorb the nutrients.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, bei pii lɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Aaafee May loo June Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaafite ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees start producing new shoots and flowers around February?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ fɔfɔii heei yɛ February mli lɛ?

english: Around February, early light rains and changing sunshine trigger the tree to wake up from its dry-season rest period, causing it to push out new growth and early flowers.
ga: Aaafee February mli lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra kɛ hulu la ni tsakeɔ lɛ teɔ tsei lɛ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛ hɔmɔ be mli wɔɔhe lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ehee ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi oya.

english: What is the difference between the main cocoa harvest season and the minor season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ shishijee kɛ nɔ ni ji enyɔ nɔ ni akɛkpaa kookoo yɛ Ghana lɛ teŋ?

english: The main season brings heavy rainfall which results in large pods and high yields, while the minor season has less rainfall, producing smaller pods and a lower total harvest.
ga: Nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ be titri lɛ mli, ni no haa ŋmeii wuji kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo baa. Yɛ be mli ni be ni ji enyɔ lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo lɛ. Enɛ haa pods lɛ feɔ bibii ni nɔ ni afeɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow much faster right after the dry season ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya waa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: During the dry season, plants store up energy. As soon as the first rains arrive, water unlocks nutrients in the soil and triggers rapid leaf and branch growth.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei baato hewalɛ. Kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ba pɛ kɛkɛ Nu gbeleɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa ni ehaa baai kɛ tsei aniji daa oya.

english: How should I prepare my farm before the main cocoa season begins?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ masaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani kookoo be titri lɛ aje shishi?

english: Before the main season starts, clear away weeds around the tree bases, prune dead or overcrowded branches, and remove diseased pods so sunlight and air can reach the trees.
ga: Dani be titri lɛ baaje shishi Jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ni ofolɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni egbɔjɔ fe nine lɛ. ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ he.

english: Why do many flowers on my cocoa trees fall off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers can drop due to poor soil nutrients, dry weather, or pest damage. Proper weeding, pest control, and balanced fertilizer help keep flowers attached long enough to form pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi baanyɛ agbee shi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni bɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ he nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni sa Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ja yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: How quickly after applying fertilizer should I expect to see improvements in my crops?
ga: beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli lɛ sɛɛ Te esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaya hiɛ oya ha tɛŋŋ?

english: You will usually start seeing visible changes, like darker green leaves and new shoots, within two to four weeks after applying fertilizer, provided there is enough moisture in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ obaaje shishi ona tsakemɔi ni anaa, tamɔ baai eŋɔli ni tsuɔ kɛ tsei heei. Yɛ otsii enyɔ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ Esa akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. As the plant grows, it moves available nitrogen to newer top leaves, causing older bottom leaves to starve, which you can fix by applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Beni tsei lɛ daraa Ejieɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baa heei anɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ baaye hɔmɔ. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young corn leaves overnight and leaving dark powder inside the center fold?
ga: Niyeli bu bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli Mɛni tɔmɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaashi powda ni tsuɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana. They hide inside the center whorl during the day and eat leaves at night, so applying approved insecticides directly into the central whorl early in the morning or late evening controls them effectively.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai gbɛkɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaakudɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land without damaging either crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mifiteee ŋmãa enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and maize works very well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in 3 to 4 months, while cassava grows slower and takes longer to mature. As long as you maintain proper planting distances, the maize will yield well without disturbing the cassava.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmãa daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa daa blɛoo ni eheɔ be babaoo dani edaa. Shii abɔ ni obaakwɛ he ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, Abele baawo yibii kpakpai ni egbaaa ŋmei lɛ naa.

english: Is it better for me to use poultry manure or chemical fertilizer for my vegetable farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Both have unique benefits: poultry manure improves soil structure, organic matter, and water holding capacity over the long term, while chemical fertilizer provides fast, concentrated nutrients for quick plant growth. Using well-decomposed manure to build the soil alongside targeted chemical fertilizer yields the best results.
ga: Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ srɔto: kooloi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni mli wa oya koni tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii kɛma shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up with yellowish-green patches and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral infection spread by tiny whiteflies or through infected stem cuttings. Because infected plants cannot recover, you should uproot affected stems and plant certified disease-resistant cassava varieties in the future.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Virus hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛŋ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ. Esa akɛ ojie tsei ni ena hela lɛ ni odu yucca henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and collapse during the daytime even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting in wet soil is typically caused by bacterial wilt or root rot. Excess water causes roots to rot or allows harmful bacteria to block water tubes inside the stem, so ensuring good raised beds for drainage prevents roots from suffocating.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Nu babaoo baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo loo ebaaha helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsĩ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ anaa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ owó saatso lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni nu atsɔ mli lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant for the next farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu okwaayeli be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed to deliver high yields only in their first generation. If you replant saved seeds from a hybrid harvest, the resulting crops will yield significantly less, grow unevenly, and lose their strong resistance to pests and diseases.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ tsɔɔ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji akɛ odu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ hybrid ŋmaa mli lɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baaha yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa. shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛteɔ shi ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni naa wa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops immediately after the major rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds produce thousands of resilient seeds that lie dormant in the soil during the dry season and germinate instantly with water. Because wild weeds adapt better to natural conditions than domesticated crops, weeding early within the first three weeks gives your young seedlings a head start.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ woɔ dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni nyɛɔ efoɔ ni ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ nu. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, koo mli jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛi amli fe shia tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ lɛ mli lɛ baaha odumɔwui bibii lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Flower drop in pepper plants happens when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer that forces leaf growth over fruit growth. Providing steady soil moisture and balanced fertilizers keeps flowers attached so fruit can develop.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be Loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa baai lɛ daa fe aduawai lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: When is the right time for me to clear my farmland before the first rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ dani klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi?

english: The best time to clear land is 2 to 4 weeks before expected major rains begin, typically around late February or March depending on your region. Clearing early allows slashed weeds to dry into organic matter and gives you time to prepare mounds or ridges before heavy rainfall turns soil muddy.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie jɛmɛ ji otsii 2 kɛyashi 4 dani nugbɔ ni naa wa lɛ aje shishi. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee yɛ February loo March naagbee gbɛ. Edamɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ Mra be mli ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni afoɔ jwɛi lɛ ni etsɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Ni ehaa onáa be ni okɛsaa gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are soft and burn easily under the hot sun. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act like umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist so the young cocoa can survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa, ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plants the strength they need to turn dark green and grow healthy ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni amɛdu ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small when I plant the stems very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots fight each other underground for space, water, and food. Giving them enough distance allows each root to spread out and swell into big cassava tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifã fɛɛ shishifã gbɛɔ eshwaa ni etsɔɔ ŋmei ŋmei agbo ko.

english: Why must I build high mounds of soil before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose earth to stretch long and thick underground. Mounding breaks up hard soil so the yam tuber can grow without hitting tough ground, while also helping extra water drain away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato koni ekɛ ehe agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Gɔji gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa nu lɛ hu ni etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts make my land better for maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmeii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are special plants that pull nitrogen food from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest the groundnuts, that leftover soil food feeds the maize crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okpa ŋmei No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmei tsei ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and looking sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Curled, sticky leaves are caused by tiny insects called aphids sucking the water out of your plants. Spraying the leaves with soap water or neem oil removes the insects and helps the leaves open up again.
ga: Kooloo bibii kɛ baai ni ekɔ, ni wa lɛ baa. Atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ aphids ni miimu nu kɛjɛ tsei lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi bibii lɛ, ni ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛgbele ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee tomato lɛ?

english: When the sun is too hot and the soil is dry, tomato plants drop their flowers to save water and protect themselves. Regular watering and covering the soil around the plant with dry leaves keeps them cool enough to make fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi ha tso lɛ he daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ mli ajɔ bɔ ni sa ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my young crops while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and will drink up all the water and soil food meant for your young plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the strength to grow tall without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni ebaanu nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or get insects inside the storage bag so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya loo ŋmeii yɔɔ kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If maize is stored while it is still slightly wet, mold grows and insects are attracted to the moisture. Drying your grains completely under the sun until they are hard before bagging keeps them fresh for a long time.
ga: Kɛji okpa ŋmãa be mli ni edɔ fioo lolo lɛ, Mold daa ni ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋmãa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi amɛhe wa dani okɛwo kotoku mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off the dry and excess branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni egbi kɛ nɔ ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning dead or crowded branches lets sunlight and fresh air pass through the tree. This stops moisture from trapping fungal diseases like black pod while helping the tree focus its energy on growing pods.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ akamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ diji, yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmɔtɔ ni miida lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or by plant viruses spread by those same insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni nakai kooloi bibii lɛ nɔŋŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot, when the plant experiences water stress from drying out too much, or when there are no insects around to pollinate the blooms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei naa nu he haomɔ kɛjɛɔ gbimɔ ni fe nine mli loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ amɛhe ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow so much faster than the food crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe niyenii tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to the local soil, so they quickly steal sunlight, water, and plant nutrients before your cultivated crops can get established.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ oya dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which the plant needs in large amounts to grow healthy green leaves and big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ he miihia tsei babaoo koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ toi wuji.

english: Why is it bad to pour chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaafɔse tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Concentrated fertilizer directly touching the plant stem or roots will burn the living plant tissues; it needs to be placed a few inches away so the roots can absorb it safely through the wet soil.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akɛ tso shishifãi loo shishifãi kpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã tso lɛ mli fãji ni hiɛ ka lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ amɛ ato he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in a wide, clear field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains grown beside them to provide cool cover and moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough for full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni ekɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aha kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yam leaves need to climb up so they can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the plant, while keeping leaves off the damp ground prevents wet fungal diseases from rotting them.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ hela ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ akafite.

english: How many suckers should I leave growing around one main plantain stem?
ga: Esa akɛ mashi tsei bibii enyiɛ mabɔle plantain tso titri kome he?

english: You should only keep one or two strong suckers beside the main plantain tree, because leaving too many causes all of them to fight for nutrients, resulting in small, thin plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi plantain wulu lɛ masɛi, ejaakɛ kɛ́ oshi babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛwu amɛtao niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantain lɛ ji bibii ni eyɛ mlɛo.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long hot dry spell that bakes seeds in the soil; waiting for steady, regular rainfall ensures seeds get enough moisture to germinate and survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni mli edɔ ni shãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa, ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mɛmɔ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: How do I know if my cassava is ready to harvest since the tubers are hidden under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa? Ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ ehiɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: You can tell cassava is mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, the soil around the base of the stem cracks, and the plant has reached about 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ yucca ko eda kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli egbɛ eshwa. Ni tsei lɛ baahi shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer can restore the soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha niyenii mli hewalɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them after maize naturally replenishes the soil nutrients without needing expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei Ebuaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside them protects the tender seedlings from sunburn and retains soil moisture.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my plantain mats produce smaller bunches of fruit after two years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain mat lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii yɛ afii enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When too many young shoots grow around the main plantain stem, they compete for nutrients and water. Cutting back excess shoots and leaving only two or three strong ones allows the main stem to produce larger bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii dara kɛbɔle Plantain tsei wuji babaoo tsɔ Ebaatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii 2-3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii titri lɛ afee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Does tying my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes actually make the yam tubers grow bigger?
ga: Ani mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni mikɛaawo tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ adara?

english: Yes, staking keeps the leaves spread out toward the sunlight. Sunlight helps the vine produce food, which is then stored underground to build larger, healthier yam tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa wain tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni no sɛɛ lɛ akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni akɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it better to plant my cassava stem cuttings flat in the soil or slanted standing up?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei niji yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ loo yɛ koŋ nɔ?

english: Planting stem cuttings at a slant helps roots grow deeper into the ground to withstand dry weather, whereas flat planting keeps roots shallow, which can cause them to rot in heavy rain.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool under direct sunlight, stops water from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: How do weeds lower my crop yield even when I apply fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ aba shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most cultivated crops and consume the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops, starving your plants before they can mature.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ, ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ dani amɛshɛɔ shweremɔ he.

english: Why are my tomato leaves twisting and curling upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miitsi amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a virus or by irregular watering. Spraying neem oil or controlling pest insects early stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be Neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo mra be mli ni agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny dark specks inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni ŋmeii diji bibii yɛ nɔ. Yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The worms hide inside the young leaves and eat the plant from the inside; applying recommended controls early inside the leaf center protects the crop.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Kpɔŋɔi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai bibii amli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli. Nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing fewer pods every year even when I give them fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past their prime, their internal transport systems become less efficient at taking up nutrients and forming fruits. Even with fertilizer, older trees naturally decline in productivity, showing it is time to gradually rehabilitate or replant the farm.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ ye afii pɔtɛɛ ko lɛ, kookoo tso lɛ mli gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli ni ewoɔ yibii. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po lɛ, tsei ni edara lɛ haa amɛyibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ okɛtsu nii blɛoo. Atsake loo adu ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is my maize plant producing flowers when it is still very short and young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi be mli ni amɛji kukuji ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: When crops experience early stress, such as a short drought or poor soil fertility, they get triggered to flower early as a survival response. The plant prioritizes reproducing before it dies, resulting in short stalks and small ears.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ haomɔi kpe mra, tamɔ hɔmɔ ni baa be kukuoo mli loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ, atswaa tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi mra akɛ nɔ ni haa amɛhiɔ shi. Tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa fɔmɔ nɔ dani amɛgboi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ kuku kɛ toi bibii.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my cassava in batches a few weeks apart instead of planting the whole field on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei kui otsii fioo komɛi kɛjɛ amɛhe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Staggering your planting dates creates a continuous sequence of crop development. This ensures you do not face a single peak harvest that rots before sale, and it protects your overall yield if a dry spell hits at a specific growth stage.
ga: Gbii ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ ni oootsake lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ okɛ okpamɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ mli yitso kome po kpeŋ dani ahɔ̃ɔ. Ni ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii fɛɛ ahe kɛji hɔmɔ shihilɛi ba yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: If my young pepper plant starts bringing out flowers early, should I remove them or leave them to grow?
ga: Kɛji mi-pepper tsei bibii lɛ bɔi fɔfɔii mra Ani esa akɛ majie loo maha ekwɛ̃?

english: It is best to pinch off early flowers on very young plants. Removing them allows the plant to focus its energy on growing strong roots and branches first, which will later support a much bigger harvest.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi fɔfɔi ni fɔɔ mra yɛ tsei bibii waa lɛ anɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi kɛ niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ baaye abua nikpamɔ ni da kwraa yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight over sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. As a result, the plants grow tall and thin with poor strength, producing smaller tubers or fewer grains overall.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni ená hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ kpakpa. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii loo amɛdumɔwui faaa.

english: If some of my corn seeds fail to sprout after planting, can I plant new seeds in those empty spots?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ hu? Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui heei yɛ nakai hei lɛ?

english: Yes, this practice is called supplying or beating up. Replanting empty spots within a week of the first sprouts ensures the new plants get enough space and sunlight before the main crop grows too tall and shades them out.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ procuring loo bashing. Kɛ́ atsake he ni etse lɛ yɛ otsi kome mli kɛjɛ be mli ni tso lɛ eje kpo klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso hee lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulu la. Dani tso titri lɛ baashɛ tsɔ ni etsĩ kane lɛ naa.

english: Why should I plant cowpea on my land after harvesting my maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil during growth. Legumes like cowpea take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring fertility for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ mli aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing big green leaves but no flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo aduawai bɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil encourages plants to focus purely on leaf and stem growth instead of reproduction. Reducing nitrogen and ensuring balanced nutrients encourages the plant to start flowering and setting fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baa kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ pɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ fɔmɔ. Nitrogen ni abaaba shi ni ana niyenii ni sa lɛ baawo tsei hewalɛ ni amɛje fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: How do I know when my oil palm trees are too old to keep taking care of?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-oil palm tso lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni minyɛɛɛ makwɛ nɔ?

english: When palm trees reach an advanced age, their trunk height makes harvesting difficult and yield drops significantly regardless of rain or care. At this stage, the return on investment drops, signaling it is time to clear and plant new seedlings.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ dara lɛ Tso lɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ haa nikpamɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa ekɔɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ loo bɔ ni atsuɔ he nii ahaa lɛ he. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli nyɔmɔwoo lɛ baa shi. Okadii akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ajie ni adu dumɔwui heei.

english: Why do my crops perform poorly if I plant them towards the end of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Crops need steady moisture during their main growth and flowering phases. Planting late means the rains may stop while the plant is still maturing, causing it to dry out before filling its pods or seeds.
ga: Tsei lɛ hia nu ni mli edɔ daa yɛ amɛdalɛ kɛ fɔfɔii titrii lɛ amli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ baanyɛ akpa be mli ni tsei lɛ miida lolo lɛ. Enɛ haa egbiɔ dani akɛ ŋmeii loo dumɔwui lɛ woɔ mli.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing holes right through the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely armyworms, which target the soft, growing funnel of the maize plant. They hide deep inside the central whorl because it provides both rich food and shelter from the hot daytime sun.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni miida lɛ anɔ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛhaa niyenii babaoo kɛ he ko ni amɛhiɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli.

english: How come armyworms seem to appear suddenly overnight and destroy large parts of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ je kpo nyɔɔŋ kome mli ni amɛfite miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Armyworms travel in large groups and feed mostly at night or early morning to avoid heat and predators. Because they feed while farmers are resting, the damage looks like it happened overnight.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii fãa gbɛ yɛ kui wuji amli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii babaoo gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛyeɔ nii yɛ be mli ni okwaafoi lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe lɛ. Etamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ni efite lɛ ba nyɔɔŋ kome mli.

english: Why do armyworms move from one farm to another so quickly in large numbers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fãa oya yɛ yibɔ babaoo mli kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli lɛ?

english: When armyworms finish eating all the greenery on one field, they march together across the ground in search of fresh green crops, acting like an invading army.
ga: Beni cutworms yeɔ tsei eŋɔli fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ. Amɛnyiɛɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛyatao ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Feemɔ onii tamɔ asraafoi ni tutuaa amɛ

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upwards into tight cups during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl inward during extreme heat to reduce leaf surface area exposed to the sun, helping the plant save water and keep from drying out.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba baai lɛ anɔ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he, ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out. High temperatures stress the plant and prevent proper pollination, so the plant sheds its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa tsei haoɔ ni etsĩɔ pollination ni sa naa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen or water. Maize moves available nutrients from old bottom leaves to support new leaves and cob formation at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Abɛi tsiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛ baa heei kɛ cob ni feɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aba.

english: Why do the leaf tips of my young maize plants look brown and burned at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eshãa yɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Burned leaf edges happen when crops lack sufficient soil moisture during dry spells, or when chemical fertilizer is applied too close to the stem, drawing water out of the plant.
ga: Baai ni shãa lɛ ahe baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. aloo kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ wo tso lɛ shishi tsɔ Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why does my young maize grow tall and thin with weak stems when planted under large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Maize needs direct sunlight to make food. When shaded by big trees, the plant stretches upwards rapidly searching for light, making the stem thin, weak, and easily blown over by wind.
ga: Abɛi he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ehoo. Kɛ́ eyɛ tso agbo ko shishi Tso lɛ tsɔɔ ehe oya koni etao la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, egbɔjɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ lɛ oya.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I get more cobs at harvest time?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná ŋmãa babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak plants with tiny cobs or no cobs at all, reducing your overall yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ baa. loo cob ko kwraa bɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii fɛɛ ni afeɔ lɛ nɔ ni baa shi.

english: Why do my sweet potato plants produce lots of thick green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ miiwo baai ni mli tse ni eŋɔli babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes sweet potatoes to put all their energy into leafy top growth above ground, leaving very little energy to develop thick tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛ ni ekɛbaafee yitso ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: How do I make sure my maize crop yields enough so my family can eat and I can still sell the rest for income?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ baawo yibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni miweku lɛ baanyɛ aye, ni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ lolo koni maná shika?

english: To get a high yield for both home use and the market, space your maize seeds properly, apply fertilizer at the right growth stages, and keep weeds out early. Healthy plants produce larger cobs, giving you extra grain beyond what your household consumes.
ga: Koni aná yibii babaoo ni akɛtsu nii yɛ shia kɛ jara nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ awo mli jogbaŋŋ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ be ni sa ni edaa lɛ mli. ni ojie jwɛi lɛ mra. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmaa babaoo yɛ nɔ ni oshia lɛ yeɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn plants turning yellow, and will this reduce my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni ani ebaaha mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the corn lacks nitrogen in the soil or is getting too much water. If left untreated, the plant won't develop big cobs, leaving you with very little grain to eat or sell at the market.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Tso lɛ efeŋ ŋmei agbo. Enɛ haa onáa dumɔwui fioo ko pɛ ni obaanyɛ oye loo ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Why do some of my harvested corn cobs have missing grains on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Missing grains occur when dry weather or heat disrupts pollination while the corn is flowering. Planting in compact blocks rather than long single rows helps pollen spread better, filling every cob with complete grains.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollination naa be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi. Dumɔ yɛ blɔki bibii amli Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaadu yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kakadaŋŋ mli Eyeɔ ebuaa pollen ni egbɛɔ eshwaa jogbaŋŋ. Ha cob fɛɛ cob aná dumɔwui ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Will adding fertilizer to my rice crop help me harvest extra grain to sell at the market?
ga: Ani mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ni makpa ŋmaa babaoo ni mikɛbaahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Yes, applying recommended nitrogen and phosphorus fertilizers at the right times encourages rice plants to grow more stems and heavier grain heads, significantly boosting your final harvest for sale.
ga: Hɛɛ, nitrogen kɛ phosphorus ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii babaoo kɛ dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii. Ehaa naagbee nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: Which type of corn seed should I plant if I want to harvest quickly to feed my home and sell the extra?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmãa esa akɛ madu kɛji miitao nikpamɔ oya koni mikɛha mishia lɛ niyenii ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ?

english: Early-maturing hybrid maize varieties grow fast—usually ready in about 90 days—and yield high amounts of grain, allowing you to secure food for your home quickly and sell the remaining surplus.
ga: Abɛi ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni shwereɔ mra lɛ daa oya—bei pii lɛ, efeɔ klalo yɛ aaafee gbii 90 mli—ni ewoɔ ŋmãa babaoo. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ niyenii toɔ shia oya ni ohɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ.

english: Why does rice require so much more water to grow well compared to corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa biɔ nu babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in shallow water or flooded fields because their roots are adapted to absorb nutrients in wet soils. Steady water prevents weeds and helps the plant produce full heads of grain.
ga: Omɔ tsei daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ loo hei ni nu afua baanyɛ aba. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni anáa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ jwɛi anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmaa ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does maize grow better during the rainy season than during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Maize needs continuous soil moisture to germinate, build strong stalks, and form full grains. The rainy season provides natural, regular water that rain-fed crops need to produce maximum yields without irrigation.
ga: Abɛi he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni ekwɛ̃. Bɔɔ tso ni mli wa ni obɔ dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nu ni he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni nugbɔshiimɔ bɛ mli lɛ haa.

english: How do I keep my harvested corn from spoiling before I can sell the surplus portion?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite dani manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ?

english: Corn must be thoroughly dried in the sun until the grains are hard before storing. Storing dry grains in airtight bags or well-ventilated granaries protects them from mold and pests, keeping them ready for food or sale.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani akɛto. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmaa ni egbi lɛ wo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmaa lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha niyenii loo jarayeli.

english: Why is it necessary to dry my harvested maize before taking it to the market to sell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ dani mahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Wet corn rots quickly and develops dangerous molds that buyers reject. Market traders pay higher prices for well-dried, clean corn because it can be safely stored and processed into food without spoiling.
ga: Abɛi ni efɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui baa, ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ kpooɔ enɛ. Jarayeli jarayelɔi woɔ ŋmãa ni he tse ni egbi lɛ jara babaoo. Ejaakɛ abaanyɛ akɛto shweshweeshwe ni afee lɛ niyenii ni efiteee.

english: Why are tiny insects destroying my stored rice grains, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa amɛ?

english: Grain weevils lay eggs inside dry grains and eat them from the inside out. Drying your rice properly and storing it in sealed, airtight hermetic bags suffocates pests and protects your crop for both eating and selling.
ga: Dumɔwui ŋmei lɛ woɔ wui yɛ dumɔwui ni egbi mli ni eyeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaabu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛha niyeli kɛ jarayeli fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil is lacking nitrogen, which is essential plant food. Applying fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the plants will help restore their green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ wo Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha amɛ su eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my crop field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔji amli?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied when the soil is moist and the plants are actively growing, typically a few weeks after germination or at the start of the rains, so roots can easily take up the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ tsei ni miida waa lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee otsii 2-3 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ mlɛo.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus they spread. Spraying recommended pest controls early helps prevent this damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni haa chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ mli Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ helai ni gbeɔ helai lɛ afɔse mra Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are insects attacking my cowpea flowers before the pods even form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ po feɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers attract pests like thrips because they are soft and full of nectar. Protecting the crop with insect control right as flowering begins allows the blossoms to develop into full, healthy pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ gbalaa kooloi tamɔ thrips ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ blɛoo ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ wuo. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ bu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ je shishi pɛ lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need taller shade plants growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa tsei kakadaji ni haa hulutsoo baa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and easily scorched by strong sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa from heat stress and keeps the soil moist while they establish deep roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cocoa tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch sunlight efficiently. Staking keeps the leaves dry, reduces fungal diseases, and allows the plant to produce larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Staking baaha baai lɛ agbi, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi, ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo bulbs wuji.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to support their heavy stems and fruit bunches. Supporting the stem with a wooden prop fork helps keep the tree upright until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi amɛshishifãi ni tsii kɛ aduawai akui lɛ asɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and nutrients directly from your crop roots. Clearing weeds early removes this competition so your main crops get all the nourishment they need.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ajie akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛya. Bɔni afee ni onibii titri lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off without making fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when the plant doesn't get consistent water. Regular watering during dry hot periods helps the plant hold onto its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu daa. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai amli.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from an agent instead of just saving seeds from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ nitsulɔ ko dɛŋ? Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ je ngma kpami nɛ be ko nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ kɛ to.

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred for high yield, fast growth, and disease resistance. Saving seeds from past harvests causes the crop to gradually lose these good traits, leading to smaller yields and weaker plants over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛha yibiiwoo babaoo, dalɛ oya kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ. Dumɔwui ni ato he kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa fiofio. Sui kpakpai nɛɛ baaje odɛŋ Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close together on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the young crops end up fighting each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. This competition leaves you with thin, weak stalks and very small ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii toi bibii waa.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry conditions as a survival trick to keep water inside their stems and roots. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛ nu ato amɛshishi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without forming fruit when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: High temperatures heat up the flower blossoms and damage the pollen inside, preventing fertilization. When a blossom isn't fertilized, the plant drops the flower to save its water and strength.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ ni efiteɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔmɔ nyɛŋ aba. Kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fɔ lɛ, amɛwooo fɔmɔ nii. Tso lɛ baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my maize field much harder when a short dry spell comes after early rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ waa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ bei yɛ lɛ? Ani eba yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ mra lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Hot, dry weather speeds up the hatching cycle of pest eggs, while the dry spell stresses young maize plants, making them less capable of defending themselves against insect feeding.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ fɔmɔ be lɛ yaa oya. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni mli egbi lɛ maa ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ mi. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ni amɛyeɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do some farmers plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land with their maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas out of the air and put it back into the soil as plant food. The maize feeds on this extra nitrogen, helping both crops produce a better harvest without depleting the soil.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni ekɛha tsei lɛ niyenii. Akɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ haa ŋmãa. Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai ni amɛfiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds always seem to sprout faster than my crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are already sleeping in your soil by the thousands and are adapted to wild conditions, so they wake up immediately with the first water drops. Cultivated crops take longer to absorb water and push through the dirt.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui akpei abɔ ewɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ momo. ni ekɛ ehe ewo koo mli shihilɛi amli No hewɔ lɛ amɛteɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nu lɛ shwie shi klɛŋklɛŋ. Tsei heɔ be babaoo dani amɛmɔɔ nu ni amɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shi.

english: How can I tell if my soil needs extra food or manure just by looking at my growing crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi kɛtsɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikwɛɔ lɛ pɛ nɔ?

english: If your plants look pale green or yellowish instead of deep green, grow very slowly, or have thin stalks, your soil is running low on essential nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ, edaa blɛoo waa, loo eyɛ ŋmeii bibii Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains creates living umbrellas that shelter young cocoa until they grow sturdy roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my yams rot so quickly in storage if heavy rain falls on my field right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Too much water in the soil right before harvest forces the mature yam tubers to soak up excess moisture, creating perfect wet conditions for rotting bacteria and fungi to multiply inside the tuber.
ga: Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli dani akpa ŋmaa lɛ baaha sweet potato ŋmeii ni eda lɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mli edɔ baa kɛha helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry up so fast after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When bare soil is exposed directly to the sun and wind, moisture evaporates very quickly. Planting cover crops or broad-leafed plants shields the ground from direct heat, helping the soil retain rainwater longer instead of letting it dry out.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ shɛɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Fɛ̃i lɛ baaho oya. Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tsei ni baa babaoo lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ moŋ fe ni eeeha egbi.

english: How can planting certain crops help keep water in my soil after it rains?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cover crops like groundnuts or cowpeas spread across the surface of your farm, creating a natural shield over the soil. This shade stops direct sunlight from evaporating the rainwater, allowing the moisture to stay in the ground where your crops can reach it.
ga: Ha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni egbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ nɔ. koni ekɛfee adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekafee nugbɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why does bare soil lose water faster than soil covered with plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nu fiteɔ oya fe shikpɔŋ ni tsei ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: Without plants to shade the earth, the intense sun beats down directly on the ground, causing rainwater to evaporate into the air rapidly. Plant leaves block the sun while roots help trap moisture in the dirt.
ga: Kɛji tsei komɛi bɛ ni baaha je lɛ nɔ Hulu ni naa wa lɛ ba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Tso baai tsiɔ hulu la naa be mli ni shishifãi yeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ nu yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Will planting crops closer together help my soil stay wet longer during dry days?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaye abua ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Yes, planting crops close enough to let their leaves touch creates a plant canopy. This canopy acts as a blanket that shades the soil, reducing water loss from heat and keeping the ground damp for longer.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bɔ ni sa ni baai lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ feɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta. Nɛkɛ ŋwɛitsu nɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la mli lɛ aba shi. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do my main crops survive heat better when I plant creeping plants like groundnuts around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei titrii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ gbɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsei ni shwereɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Creeping plants act as a living mulch over your soil. They completely cover the bare earth, keeping the ground cool and locking in rainwater so nearby crops continue to get moisture during hot days.
ga: Tsei ni shwereɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɛ ka yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ekɛ nugbɔ nu toɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anyɛ ana ŋmɔtɔ lolo yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: How can intercropping help my cassava farm hold moisture during short dry spells?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli yɛ be kukuoo mli nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting ground-covering crops like cowpeas between your cassava rows shades the soil surface. This coverage prevents the sun from drying out the ground, preserving trapped rainwater for your cassava roots.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ tsina ŋmei, ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei ŋmeii ateŋ lɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ nɛɛ baatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. ni obua nugbɔ nu ni emɔ lɛ naa kɛha o-cassava shishifãi lɛ.

english: How can I prevent the hot sun from drying out my maize roots after it rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ agbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ?

english: You can plant low-growing legumes like beans between your maize rows. These companion plants shade the earth around the maize stalks, stopping the heat from evaporating water out of the root zone.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmeii ni shwereɔ fioo, tamɔ ŋmeii, yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ. Nɛkɛ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe yeɔ tsakpaa nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ekɛtsi dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: What types of crops should I plant to prevent rainwater from just washing away from my field?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ madu koni nugbɔ nu akashwie miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ?

english: Planting fast-spreading cover crops like beans or Mucuna helps slow down water movement. Their roots bind the topsoil and their leaves protect the ground so rainwater soaks deep into the soil instead of washing over the surface.
ga: Dumɔ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Amɛshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can cover crops help my young cocoa farm hold onto water during the heat?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo lɛ ni ehiɛ nu mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, planting cover crops around young cocoa trees creates a dense protective layer over the dirt. This layer blocks hot winds and sun, allowing rainwater to soak in deeper and stay in the root zone longer.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ Young cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulu la naa. Enɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shishifãi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does leaving low plant cover on my land keep rainwater in the ground?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ ni baa shi ni ashi lɛ ahi nugbɔ nu lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Low plant cover forms a barrier between the sun and the soil surface. This barrier traps moisture underneath, making sure rainwater remains stored in the soil for your crops rather than escaping into the air.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ haa gbɛtsii nii ko baa hulu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ gbɛtsii nii nɛɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ la kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply fertilizer to my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so roots can safely absorb it. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the roots and damage the crops.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings get scorched easily by strong sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and provide wide leaves that shield the cocoa trees until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni buɔ kakao tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa bɔ ni sa ni enine shɛɔ hulu la ni fa nɔ.

english: Why will my maize yield smaller cobs if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving every plant weak and produce small.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Groundnuts form their seed pods underground. After the flower is pollinated above ground, the stalk naturally bends downward and buries itself in the dirt so the nuts can grow.
ga: Peanuts feɔ dumɔwui ŋmɔji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛfuɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Extreme heat or lack of water causes stress to tomato plants, making them drop their flowers to save energy rather than growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa tomato shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ aduawai.

english: Why do I need to clear away extra leaves and branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie baai kɛ niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ cacao tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming extra branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the main stem, which prevents fungal diseases like black pod and encourages the tree to produce bigger pods.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji anaa ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji.

english: Why should I use tall wooden stakes to support my yam vines instead of letting them crawl on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ tsuɔ nii kɛfiɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã amɛkpãtã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground gives the leaves maximum sunlight to build large tubers underground, while keeping leaves away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni awoɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni amɛfeɔ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ baai anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ kɛjɛ helai amli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Cassava roots cannot breathe when soil remains flooded for too long, which creates space for harmful fungi to infect and rot the roots underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa gbɛ haa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ koni amɛye shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛfite.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster right after I clear my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa beni mijie he ko yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Clearing the field exposes weed seeds hidden in the soil to direct sunlight and rainwater, causing them to germinate all at once.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ shikome

english: How do I know if my land is good for planting mango trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha mango ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Mango trees need well-drained soil and a distinct dry season to flower and set fruit properly. If your land floods frequently, the roots will rot, but in warm, sunny areas with moderate rainfall, mangoes do very well.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ be ni mli tse koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nu afua yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagboi, shi yɛ hei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ babaoo yɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ, Mango lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ waa.

english: Where can I find reliable planting seeds or grafted seedlings that will yield well in my region?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana dumɔwui ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ loo dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli ni baawo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ?

english: You should source seeds or grafted seedlings from certified nurseries, government agricultural offices, or established, successful farms in your district rather than unverified local markets.
ga: Esa akɛ oyahe dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli loo dumɔwui bibii kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe ko ni aŋmɛ gbɛ. Nɔyeli Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe loo ŋmɔ ko ni ato ama shi ni eye omanye yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Moŋ lɛ, eji maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe ko ni akwɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long does a newly planted mango tree take before it starts producing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mango tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Grafted mango seedlings usually start producing fruit in 3 to 4 years, whereas trees grown directly from raw seeds can take 7 to 10 years or longer to bear fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahe afii 7 kɛyashi 10 loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani amɛwo yibii.

english: When is the best time of the year to plant young tree seedlings in my field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui bibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant seedlings is at the start of the main rainy season. This allows the roots to grow deep into the moist soil and establish strong support before the dry season begins.
