ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ dumɔwui ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: How should I prepare my land before planting permanent fruit crops?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu tsei ni woɔ yibii ni baahi shi daa lɛ?

english: You should clear the land of big weeds and heavy brush, dig wide planting holes mixed with rich topsoil or compost, and mark out proper spacing so mature trees do not crowd each other later.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi wuji kɛ tsei bibii ni mli tse lɛ. Tsɔmɔmɔ dumɔ bu ni mli kwɔ ni okɛfutu shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo mli. ni okadi he ni sa koni tsei wuji akafee ekome sɛɛ mli.

english: Is it a good idea to plant short-term food crops between my young mango trees?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ madu niyenii ni yeɔ be kukuoo yɛ mi mango tsei lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, planting short-term crops like legumes or vegetables between young trees provides early food and income while suppressing weeds, as long as you keep a clear radius around the young tree trunks.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmeii loo aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ dumɔwui ateŋ lɛ baaha niyenii kɛ shika oya yɛ be mli ni ejieɔ jwɛi kɛyaa. Shii abɔ ni obaahiɛ radius ni mli ka shi faŋŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli. tso bibioo ko shishi

english: What should I do if my crop leaves start wilting during a hot, dry period?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Wilting is a plant's natural defense to reduce water loss. You can protect your crops by applying a layer of dried grass or mulch around the base of the plants to retain soil moisture.
ga: Wilting ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe koni ekɛba nu ni efiteɔ lɛ shi. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ooogbɛ ashwã amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are my young fruit trees growing very slowly even though I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ daa blɛoo waa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Plants need soil nutrients as well as water. Hard-packed or poor soil stops root expansion, so adding organic manure or balanced fertilizer around the root area will help kickstart faster growth.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ he miihia tsei. Shikpɔŋ ni edɔ loo ehiii lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa afata he abɔle he. He ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni eda oya.

english: Why do my crops drop their flowers before forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Flower dropping is usually caused by pest attacks, sudden prolonged dry spells, or a lack of essential nutrients in the soil during the critical flowering stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli. Be kakadaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ trukaa loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ mli.

english: Do I need to trim or cut the branches of my fruit trees as they grow?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafolɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ aniji loo mafolɔ amɛhe be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yes, light pruning helps remove dead or diseased branches and opens up the tree canopy to sunlight and air, which keeps the tree healthy and increases fruit production.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei niji ni afolɔ fioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. ni amɛgbele tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛwoɔ nibii babaoo.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tight like tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl inward to protect themselves from intense heat and reduce water loss through evaporation. It is the plant's natural survival mechanism during dry spells.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli koni ekɛtsi la ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ naa ni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants shrinking and curling upward at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus spread by aphids. Their feeding damages the leaf tissues, stopping them from expanding normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni aphids gbɛɔ eshwaa Amɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. Enɛ haaa amɛgbɛ amɛshwã bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know if my cassava tubers are rotting underground before I dig them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mafo amɛ?

english: When cassava roots begin to rot underground, the leaves at the top of the stem often turn yellow and fall off early, and the base of the stem near the soil level may feel weak or soft.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi je shishi amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya. Ni tso lɛ shishi ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ anu he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ loo eyɛ bɔdɔɔ.

english: Why are there small holes and brown powdery dirt inside the heart of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Kɛ muji ni tamɔ powder ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ

english: This is caused by fall armyworm caterpillars feeding on the soft leaves inside the whorl. The brown powder is the insect's waste, showing that pests are actively feeding on the plant's growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Pauda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji kooloi amli jwɛi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ miiye tsei ni eda lɛ.

english: Why are the young leaves on my new cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off during the dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso hee lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Without shade from taller food crops or trees, the plant sheds leaves to reduce water loss and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ niyenii tsei loo tsei kakadaji ahe hulutsoo bɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when extreme heat or inconsistent watering stresses the plant. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni eyaaa nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why do my cowpea plants keep growing lots of leaves without producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baa babaoo ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ?

english: If cowpea soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or excess water, the plant uses all its energy to grow stems and green leaves instead of triggering flower and pod production.
ga: Kɛji cowpea shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen fertilizer loo nu babaoo lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Mohu ɔ, e haa nɛ fɔfɔi kɛ fɔfɔi ɔmɛ peeɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to capture maximum sunlight. Sunlight helps the leaves manufacture energy, which is sent down to feed and expand the yam tuber underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛjieɔ hewalɛ ni atsuɔ kɛyaa shi koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is my plantain stem leaning over and falling down before the fruit bunch fully matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi banana tso lɛ miiho shi dani ŋmeii lɛ eda kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can easily weaken from wet soil or root pests. As the bunch grows heavier, the plant loses balance unless supported by a strong wooden prop.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ loo shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ oya. Kɛji tso lɛ kuu lɛ da Ja tso ni mli wa ko fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni sɛɛ efooo.

english: Why do groundnut flowers bloom above the ground but the nuts develop inside the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fɔfɔii fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmei shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they grow long stalks called pegs that bend downward and push themselves into the soil, where the nuts can safely grow protected from heat and animals.
ga: Beni ashɛre ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. He ni ŋmeii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe, ni abu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ahe.

english: What happens to my maize if I plant it during the dry or off-season period?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo be ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ mli?

english: Planting maize off-season requires extra water management because rainfall is unpredictable. While crops can still grow if watered properly, they may mature at a different speed and dry out much faster on the field due to higher heat.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ biɔ nu he gbɛjianɔtoo krɛdɛɛ ko. Ejaakɛ anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lolo kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu jogbaŋŋ moŋ. Tsei baanyɛ adara oyaiyeli srɔtoi ni amɛgbi oya yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ dɔlɛ ni fa babaoo lɛ hewɔ.

english: Can I harvest corn multiple times a year if I change when I plant?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmãa shii abɔ yɛ afi mli kɛji mitsake dumɔ bei?

english: Yes, if you have access to irrigation or a reliable water source, you can grow and harvest corn outside the main rainy season. Planting off-season can often fetch higher market prices because fewer farmers are harvesting at that time.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ oyɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Obaanyɛ odu ni okpa ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ baa. Ejaakɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, okwaafoi kpaaa nii babaoo.

english: Why does my land dry out so quickly when I plant crops outside the main rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ sɛɛ?

english: During the off-season, temperatures are higher and air moisture is lower, causing water in the soil to evaporate rapidly. Using mulch like dry leaves around your plants helps keep the soil cool and retains water longer.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ hu baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Kɛ akɛ mulch tamɔ baai ni egbi ni bɔle Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni nu lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my corn is fully ready to be harvested from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Corn is ready to harvest when the outer leaves surrounding the cob turn brown and dry like paper, and the grains become hard. Leaving it too long can attract pests, but harvesting too early causes the wet kernels to rot.
ga: Abɛi efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ dara. Cob lɛ tsɔɔ blɔfo ni egbiɔ tamɔ wolo. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa Kɛ́ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Shi kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni efɔ lɛ agbo.

english: Why do some farmers leave mature corn stalks standing in the field instead of harvesting them right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shiɔ ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Farmers often leave mature corn in the field so the natural sunlight can dry the grains directly on the plant. This saves the labor and expense of drying the corn manually at home.
ga: Bei pii lɛ okwaafoi shiɔ abele ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli koni hulu la ni jɛɔ mli lɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha okɛ nitsumɔ kɛ shika ni okɛbaatsu nii kɛgbi ŋmãa bo diɛŋtsɛ yɛ shia lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Is it safe for me to keep my harvested corn on the farm instead of bringing it home immediately?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mikɛbaa shia amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Storing harvested corn on the farm carries risks such as theft, moisture damage, and insect attacks. However, during dry off-season periods, some farmers keep crop piles on the field temporarily if they lack immediate transport or dry home storage.
ga: Abele ni akpa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ biɔ osharai tamɔ juu, ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ nii, kɛ kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ. Shi, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛɛɛ lɛ, Okwaafoi komɛi baato ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛji akɛ gbɛfaa loo shĩa ni mli egbi ni akɛtoɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Will my harvested maize spoil if unexpected rain falls on it while it is stored on the farm?
ga: Ani mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ baafite kɛji nugbɔ nɛ trukaa be mli ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, water causes harvested maize to grow mold, rot, and even sprout prematurely. If you must store corn on the farm, keep it raised off the ground and covered with a waterproof tarp.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu haa ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ shwieɔ, egboɔ, ni ekwɛ̃ɔ po oya. Kɛ ehe bahia ni okɛ ŋmãa ato ŋmɔ lɛ mli Wo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni okɛ tarp aha nɔ.

english: Why do pests attack my crops more heavily when I harvest during the dry off-season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ́ mikpa amɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: During the off-season, there are fewer green plants available in surrounding farms. Insects and wild animals will naturally concentrate on and attack whichever fields still have ripe crops or stored grains.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ŋmɔji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli tsei fioo pɛ yɔɔ, ni kooloi bibii kɛ koo mli kooloi gbalaa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lolo loo dumɔwui ni ato lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why are crops left on remote farm fields more likely to be stolen during the off-season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aju yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ lɛ?

english: Food is generally scarcer and more expensive in local markets during the off-season, making mature crops or stored grain left unattended on distant farms an easy target for theft.
ga: Niyenii namɔ wa ni ejara wa yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei yɛ be mli ni niyenii lɛ bɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda loo ŋmaa ni ato lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ amli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ. Efee mlɛo akɛ ebaatsɔ juu he otii.

english: Why do my corn kernels become very hard and shrink while sitting on the dry farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ wa ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ beni mita ŋmɔ ni egbi mli lɛ?

english: As mature corn sits under heat and dry air, the moisture inside each kernel evaporates. This shrinks the kernel slightly, hardens it, and makes it easier to shell from the cob.
ga: Abɛi shwereɔ yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ mli agbɔjɔ fioo, ni eha ewa, ni ebaaha efee mlɛo akɛ abaajie ŋmei lɛ.

english: If I use a tractor to clear and plow my land in the Central Region, how does that help my crop roots grow better?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ trakta tsu nii kɛjie shikpɔŋ ni mikɛtsu nii yɛ kpokpaa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Plowing breaks up hard soil layers, making it loose and airy. This allows young roots to easily spread deep into the ground to find water and nutrients for stronger crop growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baagbala shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli. Ha efee mlɛo ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu ahi mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ oya koni amɛtao nu kɛ niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ daraa waa.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my maize seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes the plants to fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. As a result, the stems grow weak and thin, producing very small cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni efeɔ mlɛo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen fertilizer or the soil has too much trapped water, which chokes the roots and stops them from feeding the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo ni ato Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ baa ni ehaaa amɛha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa seedling leaves dry up and fall off when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and easily damaged by direct sunlight. Without tall trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh heat, the leaves lose water too fast and burn.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Kɛji tsei kakadaji loo tsei bibii bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ Koni hulutsoo ni naa wa akafee lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya tsɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: Why do my tomato plant leaves roll up tightly during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defense mechanism during extreme heat. The plant curls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and hold onto its moisture.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of dark leaves, but the tubers underground are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen or leaves are heavily overgrown, the plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo baai lɛ dara tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaato niyenii yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Will my cassava crops yield well if I plant them under the deep shade of big forest trees?
ga: Ani mi-cassava lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ashishi?

english: Cassava needs direct, bright sunlight to manufacture food through its leaves. Growing them under heavy tree shade starves the plant, leading to poor tuber development.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni enyɛ etsɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ ená niyenii. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tsei ni tsii ashishi lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye tso lɛ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as sudden hot spells, lack of soil moisture, or insect pests feeding on the delicate stem joints.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi kpe, tamɔ hulutsoo ni baa trukaa fe nine. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni baaye nii yɛ tso lɛ he

english: Why is my young maize crop producing flowers when the stalk is still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ yɛ kukuji lɛ?

english: Early flowering happens when a crop suffers severe water or soil stress. The plant panics and tries to produce seeds quickly before it dries out completely.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni baa mra lɛ baa kɛji nu loo shikpɔŋ nɔ haomɔ ni naa wa ko ba tsei anɔ. Tso lɛ he feɔ gbeyei ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo dumɔwui oya dani amɛgbi kwraa.

english: How do weeds growing near my crop roots actually affect how my crop behaves?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ subaŋ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal vital water, fertilizer, and root space directly from your crops, effectively starving your plants and slowing down their growth.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hia, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ ni ehaa edalɛ baa shi.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow mainly when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to grow green and strong. It can also happen when too much rain stays in the soil and suffocates the plant roots.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ babaoo kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ nɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha tsei shishifãi lɛ shwie shi.

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets maize-specific pests and diseases multiply in the ground, leading to poorer harvests over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be ni ehaa abɛi pɔtɛɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop all their small flowers without producing any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ ni feɔ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from water stress during hot, dry periods, or when tiny beneficial insects called midges are not present to properly pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna nu he haomɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni nu hɔmɔ bɛ lɛ. Aloo beni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ Etamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ haaa fɔfɔii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over when even a small wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko po tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that hold heavy tops. Underground pests like banana weevils or microscopic worms can also eat through the roots, weakening the plant's grip on the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni fiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni tsii lɛ anaa. Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ banana ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii hu baanyɛ atsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛye nii. Enɛ haa bɔ ni tsei kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to lift up my yam vines with wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Letting them stay on the ground exposes leaves to diseases from damp soil and results in smaller yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la ni ekɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ashi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha baa lɛ aná hela kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yams bibii.

english: Cassava roots rot in the ground mostly because water settles in clay or hard soil for too long, creating damp conditions where harmful fungi can attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli babaoo ejaakɛ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni wa mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. ni kɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ atutua ni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper blossoms dry up and fall off during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli hɔmɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes the pollen inside pepper blossoms to dry out before fruit can form. When the plant senses too much heat stress, it sheds blossoms to save water and keep itself alive.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ pepper fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo. Kɛ tsei na dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni fe nine lɛ Ewoɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi.

english: Why do my tomatoes crack open on the sides right before they get fully red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi dani amɛfeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they get a sudden heavy wash of water after a dry spell. The inside of the tomato expands quickly with the sudden water, bursting through the skin before it can stretch.
ga: Tomato baatswa kɛji akɛ aha lɛ nu babaoo trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya beni nu lɛ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ hewolo lɛ mli oya dani egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea crop much more aggressively than my cereal crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ waa fe mi-cereal tsei lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants produce sweet flowers and pods that are very high in protein, making them an attractive food source for insects compared to tough, fibrous grain leaves.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ ni protein babaoo yɔɔ mli waa. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ niyenii ni ŋɔɔ kɛha kooloi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ahe baai ni wa ni yɔɔ fiber lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have faster-growing, aggressive roots that drink up water and steal the fertilizer nutrients out of the soil before your crop roots have a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa. Enɛ haa nu hoɔ ni ejuɔ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: How often can I cut the leaves from my cocoyam plant for kontomire without killing the plant?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ mafo cacao tso ko baai kɛha myrtle ŋmeii ni migbeee tso lɛ?

english: You should only harvest one or two of the older, mature outer leaves per plant at a time, leaving the center leaves so the plant can continue making food and growing tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ, ni ji kponɔgbɛ baa lɛ yɛ be kome mli. Shi baai lɛ yɛ teŋgbɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ ahoo ni ekwɛ̃ bulb ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my fresh cocoyam leaves cause an itchy feeling when handled or eaten, and how do I stop it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai heei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ ata he loo aye lɛ? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Cocoyam leaves contain natural tiny crystals that irritate the skin and throat; harvesting mature leaves and thoroughly boiling or cooking them breaks down these crystals and makes them soft and safe.
ga: Cocoyam baai lɛ amli kristalo bibii yɛ. Ehaa hewolo kɛ tsitsi lɛ mli fuɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Kɛ́ ajie baai ni edara lɛ ni ashã loo ahoo lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, efiteɔ nɛkɛ kristalo nɛɛ ni ehaa efeɔ blɛoo ni ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it better to cut cocoyam leaves when they are young or wait until they are full size?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo baai lɛ beni amɛji bibii lolo loo mamɛ ni amɛshɛ amɛdalɛ he?

english: Harvesting medium to fully expanded green leaves gives you the best balance of good tender leaf texture without weakening the main plant's growth.
ga: Baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ kɛyashi egbɛ eshwa kwraa lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha oná baa ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ he mfoniri ni hi fe fɛɛ. ni ekɛ tso titri lɛ dalɛ baa shi

english: Why do some sweet potatoes become very soft when boiled while others stay hard and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato komɛi feɔ blɛoo waa kɛ́ ahoo amɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi kã he amɛfee shiŋŋ ni amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Different varieties of sweet potato have different starch and water contents; orange-fleshed types tend to boil softer and smoother, while white or yellow types stay firmer.
ga: Sweet potato henɔi srɔtoi yɛ ŋmeii kɛ nu babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ srɔtoi. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni yɔɔ futafuta loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ fa babaoo.

english: How do I know when my sweet potatoes are ripe enough to dig up from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Sweet potatoes are usually ready about three to four months after planting, when the leaves start turning yellow and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ayeɔ yɛ nyɔji 3-4 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Does cutting off the sweet potato vines above ground help the sweet potatoes grow bigger underneath?
ga: Ani sweet potato wain tsei ni afoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ shishigbɛ?

english: Cutting off too many vines starves the plant because leaves make food for the roots, but light trimming right before harvest makes digging easier without hurting crop size.
ga: Kɛ́ afo wain tso lɛ mli babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aye hɔmɔ, he ni baai lɛ ji niyenii kɛha shishifãi lɛ. Shi kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ fioo dani akpa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋmɔmɔ feɔ mlɛo ni enaaa tsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I grow sweet potato and cocoyam together in the same farm plot?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu sweet potato kɛ cocoa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, sweet potatoes spread along the ground to cover the soil and block weeds, while cocoyam grows taller, allowing both crops to share space as long as they get adequate water.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii baagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa. yɛ be mli ni kookoo baakwɛ̃ babaoo Enɛ haa tsei henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ jaa he ko kɛji amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Do I need seeds to grow sweet potatoes, or can I just use pieces of the vine?
ga: Ani dumɔwui he miihia mi koni mikɛdu ŋmeii? Aloo manyɛ mikɛ wain tso lɛ atsu nii yɛ fãi amli kɛkɛ.

english: You do not need seeds; sweet potatoes grow easily by planting healthy vine cuttings directly into mounded or ridged soil.
ga: Dumɔwui he ehiaaa bo. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ aaadu sweet potato kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ gɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ ŋmeii amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoyam plants turn yellow before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛkpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks water, lacks nitrogen nutrients in the soil, or is receiving too much direct sunlight without enough soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli.

english: What kind of soil moisture do cocoyam plants need to give me thick, healthy green leaves?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he hiaa cacao tso ko koni ebaakwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Cocoyams need consistently damp, rich soil with good drainage; if the soil gets too dry, the leaves will stay small, tough, and dry out quickly.
ga: Cocoa he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni baa nii ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lɛ, baai lɛ baafee bibii, amɛhe wa ni amɛbaagbi oya.

english: Can I use clean borehole water to irrigate my crops, and will it affect how they grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni mli tse ni jɛɔ nubu mli lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ? Ni ani ebaana tsei adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ loo enaŋ?

english: Yes, clean borehole water is safe for crops because it is free from the pests and disease-causing germs often found in surface river water. Using clean groundwater helps crops grow strong without exposing them to waterborne diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni mli tse ni jɛɔ nubu mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ ni bei pii lɛ anaa yɛ nu ni yɔɔ faai amli lɛ mli lɛ bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa jogbaŋŋ ni helai ni jɛɔ nu mli baa lɛ bɛ oshara mli.

english: Is river water always safe to pour directly on my vegetable crops?
ga: Ani faa mli nu lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe be fɛɛ be akɛ aaafɔse mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: River water can carry dirty runoff, chemicals, or bacteria from upstream that might make your vegetable crops sick or contaminate food that is eaten raw. Filtering the water or letting sediment settle first makes it safer for crops.
ga: Faa mli nu baanyɛ aŋɔ nu ni hoɔ, tsofai, loo helai ni baa mɔ mli ni baanyɛ aha o-vegetables lɛ aná hela loo efite niyenii ni ayeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu lɛ shwie shi loo oha ŋmeii lɛ shwie shi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha efee shweshweeshwe aha otsei lɛ.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the moisture before the sun gets too hot. Watering during a hot afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the plant's roots can take it in.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops curl up and turn yellow during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to trap moisture and stop water from evaporating off their surfaces. The leaves turn yellow because the crop cannot absorb soil nutrients like nitrogen without enough water.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekajɛ amɛyiteŋ. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their lower leaves when the rains stop for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shwieɔ eshishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its lower leaves as a survival strategy to reduce the amount of water it loses during a drought, focusing all its energy on keeping the underground tuber alive until water returns.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ shi akɛ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi koni ekɛba nu ni laajeɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ shi. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nu lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn brown and dry up on the tree when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need steady soil moisture to support growing pods. When soil dries out, the tree discards or dries up young pods to save water and keep the main tree alive.
ga: Cacao tsei biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni eye ebua ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbi lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ loo egbiɔ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛbu tso titri lɛ he.

english: What happens to my tomato plants if heavy rain suddenly falls after a long dry period?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛgbɔjɔ trukaa? Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: A sudden rush of heavy water after a drought causes tomato plants to take up water too fast, which can make the skin on the growing fruit split open or cause the roots to suffocate if water collects around them.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya tsɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha hewolo ni yɔɔ aduawai ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ akumɔ loo efo shishifãi lɛ amli kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa.

english: How does dry, hardened soil affect the growth of my yam and cassava tubers?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wa lɛ saa mi-sweet potatoes kɛ cassava shishifãi lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Hard, dry soil acts like a solid wall that prevents root tubers from expanding freely, resulting in small, bent, or stunted crops that cannot store food properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo ni wa ni tsiɔ shishifãi ahe ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã amɛhe. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii, ni ebɔle loo ni egbɔjɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ato niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: How can I check if my soil has enough moisture for my crops without buying expensive tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni miheee nibii ni jara wa?

english: Dig down a few inches and squeeze a handful of soil into a ball. If it holds its shape without dripping water or falling apart into dust, your soil has good moisture for your crops.
ga: Tsɔmɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli inchi fioo komɛi ni okɛ sũ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ afee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ehiɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli ni nu shwieee shi loo efoŋ ni etsɔɔɔ sũ. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ hu yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do crops grow faster and stay greener on land close to a riverbank?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ faa lɛ naa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil near riverbanks stays naturally moist for longer and is full of rich nutrient deposits washed down from upstream, giving crop roots constant water and food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ faa lɛ naa lɛ hiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni niyenii mli hewalɛ nii babaoo ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ faa lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ eyi mli obɔ. Ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ náa nu kɛ niyenii daa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their root systems are not yet deep enough to absorb enough water. They need shade trees or temporary plantain plants grown beside them to shelter their leaves from heat until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo be kukuoo mli tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni ekɛbu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to stick wooden poles into the soil for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce food for the tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, preventing leaf rot and allowing the leaves to catch as much sunlight as possible.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni oha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni abaanyɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves during the hottest parts of the day as a defense mechanism to reduce water loss through evaporation. Once the sun goes down or rain falls, the leaves naturally uncurl and expand again.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi loo nugbɔ nɛ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛdaraa ekoŋŋ.

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and lie dormant in the soil throughout the dry season, ready to sprout instantly with the first rainfall. Clearing them in the early weeks gives your crops the nutrients and light they need to grow without competition.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Efee klalo akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ. Amɛjiemɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli Ebaaha otsei lɛ niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with many green leaves, but leaves small cassava roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo lɛ? Shi? Cassava shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or moisture, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and lush leaves above ground rather than storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my maize crops yield better when I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the farm first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their root nodules. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on this stored nitrogen to grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye nɛkɛ nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ koni etsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the soil to be moist before putting solid fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Solid fertilizer requires moisture to dissolve into a liquid form that crop roots can absorb. Placing fertilizer on dry soil during hot weather can burn plant roots or cause the chemical nutrients to evaporate into the air.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni wa lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ nu ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ wo mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo eha tsofai ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the stems before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi dani etsɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: High heat and dry winds can cause tomato pollen to dry up, preventing fertilization so the flowers fall off. Irregular watering and excessive nitrogen fertilizer can also cause the plant to shed its blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi baanyɛ aha tomato pollen lɛ agbi. Tsi fɔmɔ naa kɛyashi fɔfɔii lɛ baagbee shi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli be fɛɛ be kɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small suckers growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plantain tree for water, soil nutrients, and light. Pruning all but one or two strong suckers allows the mother tree to focus its energy on producing a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi lɛ kɛ plantain wulu lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni afolɔ mli ja tso kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ nɔ koni efee tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why are small, ragged holes appearing in the center whorl leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Small holes in the center leaves are a classic sign of early Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding. Checking the center of young plants early allows you to treat the caterpillars before they destroy the growing tip of the stalk.
ga: Buu bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii yeɔ nii yɛ fɛ̃i be mli. Kwɛmɔ dumɔwu lɛ teŋgbɛ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ.

english: How many times am I supposed to spray my rice crop before it is ready for harvest?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ nu dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: Most protective or yield-boosting sprays for rice only need to be applied once at a specific growth stage. Spraying too often wastes money and can leave harmful chemical residues on the rice grains when you cook and eat them.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he loo ni haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ lɛ ateŋ babaoo atsu nii shikome pɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ dalɛ be ko mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ shii abɔ lɛ, eji shika fitemɔ, ni ebaanyɛ eshi tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ ŋmaa lɛ nɔ kɛ́ ohoo ni oye.

english: Is it safe for my family to harvest and eat vegetables immediately after spraying them with pest medicine?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ miweku lɛ baakpa aduawai ni amɛye amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ efɔ amɛnɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, every farm chemical has a required waiting period after spraying, known as a pre-harvest interval. You must wait a specific number of days so the chemical can break down safely before the crop is harvested for cooking.
ga: Dabi, tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ ni amɛmɛ be mli ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ale lɛ hu akɛ be ni tsɔ ŋmaakpamɔ hiɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ omɛ gbii babaoo dani tsofai lɛ afite shweshweeshwe dani okpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni okɛhoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize plants need to grow green and healthy. Adding compost or a nitrogen fertilizer early in the season will restore the plant's green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ he afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikɛ amɛ po shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil retains too much water during heavy rains. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Does my rice farm always need to stay flooded with water for the crop to grow well?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni nu atsɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be koni tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: While rice loves moisture, flooded water is mainly used to suppress weeds. Keeping the soil muddy and wet is enough for healthy growth, and letting the field dry out slightly near harvest time makes harvesting much easier.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ moŋ Shi akɛ nu afua lɛ mli nu lɛ babaoo gbeɔ jwɛi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee muji ni edɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa. Ni kɛ́ oha ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi fioo beni ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ, ebaaha nikpamɔ lɛ afee mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there is strong sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are very delicate and lose water quickly under direct hot sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa creates a living umbrella that protects them until their roots grow strong.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe waaa waa, ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ aba kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper space ensures they grow big and yield more harvest overall.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ni sa lɛ, ebaaha eda ni ewo yibii babaoo yɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and soft dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant. Spraying an approved crop protector directly into the plant funnel early in the morning kills the pest before it ruins the yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmɔshi nibii dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist and plants are actively growing, typically a few weeks after planting. Applying fertilizer during heavy rainfall will just wash the plant food away into the drains.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ nu lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster and stronger than my crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to steal water and food from the soil quickly. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures your crops receive all the rain and soil nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: How do I know when it is the right time to start clearing my land for the main planting season in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ shishi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be titri ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: In Ghana, the major planting season usually starts around March or April with the arrival of the first continuous rains. You should clear your land just before these rains begin so that your planted seeds can take immediate advantage of the moist soil.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, bei pii lɛ, be titri ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ March loo April aaafee. Nugbɔ baanɛ be fɛɛ be klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa. Esa akɛ ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ koni dumɔwui ni adu lɛ anyɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ he sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers in my community harvest crops multiple times a year while I only harvest once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ kpaɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii shii abɔ yɛ afi mli yɛ be mli ni mikpaa shikome pɛ lɛ?

english: Harvest frequency depends on crop type and rainfall patterns. Ghana has both a major rainy season and a minor rainy season. Farmers who plant fast-growing crops like vegetables or maize can plant and harvest across both seasons, yielding multiple harvests in a single year.
ga: Nikpamɔ shii abɔ lɛ damɔ tso henɔi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Ghana yɛ shishijee nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji enyɔ fɛɛ. Okwaafoi ni duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ aduawai loo ŋmãa Abaanyɛ adu ni akpa yɛ bei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ ewo yibii shii abɔ yɛ afi kome mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water around their roots. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure will help restore their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsu nii. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni ji eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ kpakpa aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my pepper plants before any peppers actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ dani ŋmɔtɔ lɛ daa diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from high heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and using mulch to cool the ground helps the plants hold onto their flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsu nii ni okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai amli.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil remains too wet for too long, especially during heavy late-season rains. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava is very effective. Maize grows quickly and is harvested after three to four months, while cassava grows more slowly and takes over the space after the maize is removed, giving you two harvests from one plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa dumɔ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ sɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he ko beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii shii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller crops every year even though I plant in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ he kome moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crops—such as planting beans or cowpeas after maize—helps restore nitrogen and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ. Enɛ baaha niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black and shriveling up during the rainy period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and damp conditions. Pruning dense branches to allow sunlight and air to pass through your farm reduces moisture and prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei lɛ amli babaoo koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do I see tiny insects clustered under the leaves of my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Abua naa yɛ mi-aduawai lɛ baai ashishi?

english: These insects are likely aphids or whiteflies that suck sap from your plants, causing leaves to curl and stunt growth. Spraying them early with neem oil mixed with mild soapy water is a simple way to control them.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛdaraaa. Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Okɛ samla kɛ nu ni mli ejɔ afutu mli. Eji gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ.

english: How deep into the soil should I push my maize seeds when I am planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ matsi mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Maize seeds should be planted about 2 to 5 centimeters deep. Planting them too deep prevents the shoot from reaching the surface, while planting them too shallow leaves them exposed to birds and hot surface soil.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimita 2 kɛyashi 5. Kɛ́ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaya ŋwɛi. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha okpoi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ aná amɛ.

english: Why does my rice crop need so much water compared to my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ he hiaa nu babaoo fe mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in wet conditions or flooded soils because their roots are adapted to pull nutrients from saturated ground, which also prevents weeds from choking the young plants.
ga: Omɔ tsei daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ akatsi tsei bibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why is it important to plant my rice in straight rows instead of just scattering the seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni aaadu dumɔwui yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting rice in straight rows gives each plant enough space and sunlight to grow strong, while making it much easier for you to weed, fertilize, and harvest.
ga: Omɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why does my rice crop turn yellow and stop growing when the field gets full of weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa shweremɔ be mli ni jwɛi eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with rice plants for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When weeds take over, the rice cannot get enough food, causing the leaves to turn yellow and stunt growth.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmãa tsei yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Beni jwɛi lɛ ye nɔ lɛ, Rice nyɛɛɛ eye niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know when my rice crop is fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Rice is ready for harvest when about 80 percent of the seed heads turn from green to golden-yellow, and the grains feel hard when you bite into them.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei aaafee oha mlijaa 80 tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ akɔmɔ amɛ.

english: Why do I need to dry my freshly harvested rice grains before storing or milling them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa ehee lɛ dani mikɛto loo mafolɔ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested rice contains moisture. If stored wet, it will rot, grow mold, or spoil quickly. Proper drying keeps the grain hard, clean, and safe for milling and selling.
ga: Omɔ ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ akɛwo nu mli lɛ, ebaagbo, ebaaná ŋmɔtɔ, loo ebaafite oya. Kɛ́ agbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa, ehe tseɔ, ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa kɛ jarayeli.

english: What does rice processing involve after I harvest the crop from my field?
ga: Mɛni kɔɔ ŋmãa nitsumɔ he beni mikpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Processing involves threshing to remove grains from stems, drying to reduce moisture, parboiling (optional steaming), and milling to remove the outer husk so you get clean rice ready to sell or cook.
ga: Nɔ ni fata he ji ni atswa ŋmãa lɛ koni ajie dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Nibii ni agbiɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ aba shi, ŋmɔtɔ (kɛji oosumɔ) kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛjieɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ haa onáa ŋmãa ni he tse ni esa akɛ ohɔ̃ɔ loo ohoo.

english: Why are improved local rice varieties better to plant in Ghana than random imported seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana fe dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba trukaa lɛ?

english: Improved local varieties like AGRA rice are specially developed to resist local diseases, tolerate local weather conditions, and give higher yields in local soils.
ga: Afee maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ AGRA ŋmãa, yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛte shi ewo maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo baa shikpɔji ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ

english: How much rice yield can I expect to get from one hectare of land if I care for it well?
ga: Shikpɔŋ hectare kome mli ŋmãa yibii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ kɛji mikwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: With good land preparation, proper seed spacing, correct fertilizer use, and adequate water, one hectare of land can yield between 3 to 5 metric tonnes of paddy rice.
ga: Kɛji akɛ asaa shikpɔŋ jogbaŋŋ He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni ka dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni sa tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ hectare 1 baanyɛ aha ŋmãa ni shɛɔ mɛtrik tɔn 3 kɛyashi 5.

english: How can an agricultural extension officer help me improve my rice farm?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni aha ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: An extension officer visits your community or farm to teach you best practices in seed selection, field preparation, planting methods, pest management, and post-harvest handling.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi baasara akutso loo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛtsɔɔ nifeemɔi ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ dumɔwui ahalamɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ he saamɔ, dumɔ gbɛi, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ kwɛmɔ

english: What happens if I plant my rice seeds directly on unprepared land without clearing and tilling?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni asaaa nɔ ni mikɛtsuuu nii ni mikɛtsuuu nii?

english: Unprepared soil makes it hard for young rice roots to spread and find nutrients, leading to poor germination, weak seedlings, and heavy competition from wild weeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaaa he lɛ baaha ewa aha ŋmãa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛna niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii. Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Ni esa akɛ koo mli jwɛi lɛ atswa akaŋ waa.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily whenever a strong wind hits my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over when their roots are not deep enough in the ground to hold them firm. Planting seeds at the correct depth and pulling soil up around the base of the plant (ridging) helps the roots stay grounded and support the heavy stalk.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛmɔmɔ amɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa ni agbalaa sũ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛbɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he (ni ajieɔ) lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi yɛ sũ lɛ he ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni tsii lɛ.

english: How do I know if the ground on my farm is too hard for my crops to grow properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If it is difficult to push a stick into the ground when it is wet, or if water collects on top without sinking in, the soil is too hard. Hard soil stops roots from spreading down to find water and food, which slows plant growth.
ga: Kɛji ewa akɛ aaatsi tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni edɔ Aloo kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ nɔ ni efoŋ shi. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã shi koni amɛyatao nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but only produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? shi eyɛ yitso bibioo Shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer or grow in heavy shade, they put all their energy into reaching up toward the sun to grow leaves. Balancing the soil food helps the plant send its energy down to expand the roots into large tubers.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei baafite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛshɛ hulu lɛ he koni amɛkwɛ baai. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni amɛshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cowpea plants fold their leaves in extreme heat to protect themselves. By making their leaves smaller target areas for the hot sun, they save water and keep from drying out until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ la ni naa wa lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni afee lɛ bibii yɛ he ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha nu akafite, ni ebaaha egbiŋ kɛyashi be mli ni ebaajɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my yam vines turn yellow and dry up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani kpamɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves naturally dry up at the end of the rainy season because the plant is finishing its growth above ground and storing all remaining food deep in the tuber for safety during the dry season.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, sweet potato tso lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ toɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni ekɛtsu nii shweshweeshwe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do we heap up soil into big mounds to plant yams instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔbuaa muji agboi anaa koni wɔkɛdu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds build a soft, loose structure of soil above the hard ground. This makes it easy for the yam tuber to expand freely down and sideways, while also protecting the roots from sitting in excess water after heavy rain.
ga: Gɔji feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishi kɛ amɛsɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ akabote nu ni fa fe nine mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ.

english: Why does the top of my soil turn into a hard crust like concrete after it rains and dries in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa tamɔ kɔnkrit beni nugbɔ enɛɔ ni egbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Soil with very little organic material breaks down under heavy raindrops and bakes hard in the sun. Adding dried grass, manure, or compost keeps the soil crumbly so young shoots can easily sprout through.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fioo pɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni hulu lɛ shã lɛ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ anyɛ ajie amɛhe kpo oya.

english: How often do I need to walk through my cocoa farm to check on the pods?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ kookoo ŋmɔ mli koni makwɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: You should check your cocoa trees at least once a week. Walking through regularly allows you to catch early signs of black pod disease or insect attack so you can remove bad pods before the damage spreads to healthy trees.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ o-cocoa tsei lɛ amli shikome yɛ otsi mli. Kɛ́ oya jɛmɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona black pod hela loo kooloi bibii ni baatutua bo lɛ ahe okadii mra. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ ojie ŋmeii gbohii lɛ dani nɔ ni efite lɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I protect my harvested maize from insects eating it inside the storage room?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ lɛ yɛ mi-nitoohe lɛ ahe?

english: Insects enter stored maize when there is moisture and open space. Drying your maize until the grains are completely hard and sealing it inside airtight bags acts like locking the door against pests, preventing them from surviving.
ga: Kplukai boteɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hei ni agbele. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa kwraa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ akɛwo vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ shinaa naa ŋmɛlɛ ni tsiɔ ŋmeii anaa. Koni amɛkahi wala mli

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and die suddenly even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil happens when harmful organisms in the ground attack the plant's underground stem and roots. Once the roots are ruined, the plant can no longer draw up water to the leaves, causing it to collapse.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ agbala nu kɛya ebaai lɛ amli dɔŋŋ. ha efo mli

english: Why are my crop leaves growing so slowly and thin instead of bushy and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛfee mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Slow and thin leaf growth usually happens when plants lack essential nutrients like nitrogen or suffer from poor water supply. Adding well-rotted manure or balanced fertilizer helps plants develop thick, healthy leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni daa blɛoo lɛ baa be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo amɛnaaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my neighbor's crop look much bigger than mine even though we planted them at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eda kwraa fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔdu lɛ yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Crops planted at the same time can grow at different rates depending on soil fertility, weed competition, seedling quality, and how much sunlight or water each farm receives.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ baanyɛ adara yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Jwɛi ahe akaŋshii Dumɔwui lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ kɛ hulu la loo nu ni ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ nine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ falɛ

english: Why are my plants growing very tall but refusing to bear any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ miida shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much shade or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing tall stems and leaves instead of flowering and producing fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ maa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni kwɔlɔ ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii lɛ

english: Should I keep a tree on my farm if it has stayed small for years without producing anything?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makwɛ tsei anɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Ni kɛji akɛ tso lɛ efee bibioo afii babaoo ni ewooo yibii hu?

english: If a tree remains severely stunted and non-productive for years despite good care, it may have diseased roots or weak genetics, and replacing it with a fresh, high-quality seedling is usually best.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ tee nɔ egbɔjɔ waa ni ewooo yibii afii babaoo yɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Tsei lɛ hu baanyɛ aná shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ loo amɛhe waaa yɛ amɛfɔmɔ su mli. Ni bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛbaato najiaŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops keep stretching straight upwards instead of spreading out wide?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jajeɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã babaoo lɛ?

english: Plants stretch straight up when they are planted too close together or shaded by bigger trees because they are competing with each other to reach direct sunlight.
ga: Tsei lɛ baatsɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ tsei wuji ashishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know if my young tree is mature enough to start producing high yields?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Tree crops show maturity through physical signs such as a thick main trunk, a fully developed canopy of leaves, and the regular appearance of healthy flower clusters.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli lɛ jieɔ dalɛ kpo kɛtsɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii tamɔ tso lɛ shishifã ni mli wa kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni eda kwraa lɛ nɔ. kɛ fɔfɔii akui ni mli wa ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ akpojiemɔ

english: Why are the new shoots on my plants turning pale yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale green or yellow leaves are a sign that the soil is low in nutrients, especially nitrogen or iron, which plants need to make food and grow properly.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen loo dade ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ

english: What causes flowers to drop off my crops before fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔii shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii?

english: Flowers fall off prematurely due to extreme heat, insufficient soil moisture, insect damage, or poor pollination, preventing the plant from setting fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii, loo pollination ni ehiii. Ehaa tsei wooo yibii

english: Can applying too much fertilizer prevent my crops from producing food?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo niyenii?

english: Yes, using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to overgrow its leaves and stems while delaying or completely stopping flower and fruit formation.
ga: Hɛɛ, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná baai kɛ ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai afeemɔ baa shi loo ekpaa kwraa.

english: Why do some of my crops take longer to establish shoots after planting than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi heɔ be babaoo fe ekrokomɛi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings establish at different speeds depending on the health of their root systems at planting, how deep they were placed in the soil, and soil moisture levels during the first few weeks.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ toɔ tsei ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli ni damɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahewalɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni mli edɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with deep root systems and seeds that can lie dormant in the soil for years. When you clear the bush, you expose the soil to direct sunlight and rain, which triggers these weed seeds to germinate much faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni baanyɛ aya wɔɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ Obaahã hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui nɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya kwraa fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: How do weeds actually reduce the final yield of my maize crop if I leave them in the field?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ aha mi-ŋmãa lɛ naagbee yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Weeds act like aggressive competitors in your field. They steal water, sunshine, and soil nutrients directly from your maize roots, causing your crops to grow weak, turn yellow, and produce small or empty cobs.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akaŋshilɔi ni mli wa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ha onibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛwo ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko nɔ ko.

english: How does covering my bare farm soil with dry grass or leaves after clearing help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai shwie miŋmɔ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering the soil, which is called mulching, blocks sunlight from reaching weed seeds so they cannot sprout. It also traps moisture in the ground and keeps the roots of your crops cool during hot days.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ hu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why did my crop seeds fail to sprout after I planted them right after burning the cleared bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ beni mishã jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Burning generates intense heat that dries out the moisture in the topsoil and destroys useful soil microbes. The ash can also form a hard crust when rain falls, making it difficult for weak sprouts to push through.
ga: Shãa haa dɔlɛ ni naa wa baa, ni no haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ ni efiteɔ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Ashwishwɛ hu baanyɛ afee ŋshɔŋloo ni wa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Ha bean sprouts lɛ afee blɛoo Ewa akɛ oootsɔ mli

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems close together to get more plants on my small plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together, their underground roots compete for growing space and nutrients. Instead of getting large, thick tubers, you will end up with many thin, woody roots that have little food value.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná he ko kɛ niyenii ni haa amɛdaraa. Yɛ yitso agbo ni mli wa najiaŋ lɛ Ebafee akɛ shishifãi komɛi yɛ. ni fa babaoo lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ

english: Cowpeas are legumes that absorb nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant grows, it releases this natural nitrogen into the soil, which acts like free fertilizer for your maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei dara Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni damɔ shi ekome kɛhaa o-corn lɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa saplings die when I plant them in a fully cleared, open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse, ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in direct sunshine. Without taller shade plants like plantains or shade trees to shelter them, the intense sun dries out their leaves faster than their small roots can take up water.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo ni nɔ kwɔ, tamɔ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo tsei bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni naa wa baaha baai lɛ agbi oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. ni baanyɛ aŋɔ nu

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers as a natural survival mechanism when exposed to excessive heat or water shortage. The plant sacrifices its blossoms to conserve energy and keep the main stem alive.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi akɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi kɛji amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine loo nu ni faaa lɛ he. Tsei kɛ fɔfɔi shaa afɔle koni amɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛha tso lɛ yitso lɛ ahi wala mli.

english: Why are my sweet potato plants growing very thick green leaves but almost no tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse waa shi eshwɛ fioo ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen, the plant focuses all its energy on growing long vines and leaves above ground. As a result, it forgets to send energy down into the roots to develop big potato tubers.
