ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ wain tsei kɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe nii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛhiɛ kpaa nɔ akɛ amɛbaatsu hewalɛ kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plant roll up into tight tubes during the sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the maize plant's natural defense against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the leaf area exposed to the sun, which stops water from evaporating out of the plant too quickly.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baa lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ ebaa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akajɛ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or animal manure will help restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava rots underground mostly due to poor water drainage or excessive rainfall that waterlogs the soil, allowing fungal diseases to attack the roots. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps drain extra water away.
ga: Cassava fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni bei pii lɛ, nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ nu lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atutua shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early using recommended sprays or neem oil prevents the virus from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Mra be mli whitefly nɔkwɛmɔ Neem spray loo fɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Plantain trees fall over because small underground pests like nematodes or banana weevils damage their root systems, leaving the heavy tree with no firm support against strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii nyɛɛɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa.

english: What are these small caterpillars eating holes into the central leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that feeds on young maize leaves. Early spraying with approved insecticides or applying neem leaf extracts directly into the plant funnels helps destroy them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ shi mra Loo ni akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni efite amɛ.

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas with maize is beneficial because cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps your maize grow better without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward the sun and prevents fungal diseases from spreading from damp soil onto the leaves.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he ni ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa baai lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: How does adding dry animal manure help my soil grow better crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Decomposed animal manure acts like a sponge that holds water in the soil during dry days and slowly releases natural nutrients, keeping the soil soft and rich for crop roots.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji, ni ehiɛɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli, ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fiofio. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni tsei shishifãi babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from stress caused by harsh sunlight, dry weather, or insect attacks. Planting shade trees nearby protects the cocoa flowers from drying out in the sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ Tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ akagbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Is it better to water my pepper plants in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water in the early morning so plants can absorb moisture before the sun gets hot. Watering during a hot afternoon causes water to evaporate too quickly and can heat up the leaves, damaging the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi koni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ adɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ. ni ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ adɔ. ni baanyɛ afite tsei

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tight like straws during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing water when the sun is intense. By curling, the leaves reduce the surface area exposed to heat, helping the plant save moisture until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛhaa he ni hulutsoo baa lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ mli ni hulutsoo baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants shrinking and twisting up into tight curls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking sap from young leaves, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies. The damaged leaves cannot expand normally, so they twist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Baai ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ ashwã bɔ ni sa, no hewɔ lɛ amɛhe ejɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cowpea beans fold up and droop when night falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Many bean plants naturally fold their leaves at night to reduce moisture loss and protect themselves from nighttime cold. This normal plant behavior is called 'sleep movement' and does not mean the crop is diseased.
ga: Bean tsei babaoo shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa gbɛkɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi, ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ fɛ̃i ni baa gbɛkɛ lɛ he. Atsɛɔ tso lɛ subaŋ ni sa nɛɛ akɛ ‘Wɔhe nyiɛmɔ’ ni etsɔɔɔ akɛ hela emɔ tso lɛ.

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering or long dry spells while the fruit is growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo be kakadaŋŋ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but most of them fall off without growing into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi amɛteŋ babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers if they don't get pollinated by tiny insects, or if the tree lacks enough water and nutrients to feed all the young pods at once.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Aloo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ shikome.

english: Why do my groundnut plants look green and healthy, but the shells under the soil are completely empty when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyɛ hewalɛ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli efolo beni mikpa lɛ lɛ.

english: Empty groundnut pods (often called 'pops') happen when there is not enough calcium in the soil while the pods are expanding. Without calcium, the inner nut fails to develop inside the shell.
ga: Peanut pods ni bɛ nɔ ko (ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘pops’) baa kɛji calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni pod lɛ miigbɛ eshwa. Kɛji calcium bɛ Nut ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereŋ yɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with bushy leaves, but the tubers underground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich organic matter, the plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves and stems instead of transferring food down into the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli loo eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai kɛ ŋwɛi tsei lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of growing flat on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso koni ekwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu lɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into full sun so they can capture more light to feed the underground tuber. It also keeps the leaves off damp soil, which prevents fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la ni fa bɔni afee ni amɛná la babaoo ni amɛkɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: When plants are overcrowded, they shade each other out. Each plant stretches upward as fast as it can to reach sunlight, resulting in tall, weak stems that fall over easily.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaafee amɛhe hulutsoo. Tso fɛɛ tso ŋmɛɔ ehe oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni enine ashɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Why do my mature maize stalks break and fall over near the ground when a small wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni eda lɛ fãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ masɛi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko pɛ tswa lɛ?

english: Stalk breaking (lodging) usually happens because stem borer pests have eaten the inside of the stalk, or because the plant roots were planted too shallow to support the heavy corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni ekumɔ (wɔɔhe) baa ejaakɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ mli. Aloo akɛni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua ŋmãa ni tsii lɛ hewɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for leafy growth. It can also happen when the soil is too wet and waterlogged, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem with leaves mostly at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmei lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baa ko egbɔ kɛji baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso lɛ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni eyɛ baai babaoo yɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they get stressed, usually by extreme afternoon heat, lack of water, or prolonged dry spells. High temperatures prevent effective pollination, causing the blossom to dry up and fall off without forming fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛhao. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shwane dɔlɛ, nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso mli, loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have naturally adapted to survive harsh soil and weather over centuries. They germinate quickly, produce thousands of seeds, and aggressively steal water and light from your crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔji ni mli wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli afii ohai abɔ. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya. Ewoɔ dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu kɛ la kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting beans or cowpeas together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that can capture nitrogen gas from the air and put it back into the soil as natural plant food. Planting them with maize helps feed the soil, reduces the need for expensive fertilizer, and covers the ground to hold moisture.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛku sɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii. Abele ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Tsɔɔmɔ bɔ ni ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa atsu nii aha lɛ shi. ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no plantain trees near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui ko bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: The first rain of the season can be a false start, leaving the ground hot and dry if rain does not fall again for weeks. Sowing too early causes seeds to dry out and rot in the hot soil before the steady rains fully arrive.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni egbiɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ ekoŋŋ otsii babaoo. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ aba kwraa.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids hiding under the leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaf curling from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall trees and use stakes to lift up my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ amli ni mikɛ sɛɛfimɔ tsei awo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need plenty of sunlight to make energy and grow large underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves toward the light and keeps them off the wet soil, preventing rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji. Staking baaha baai lɛ akwɛ la lɛ hiɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Why is it bad to put chemical fertilizer on dry soil when there is no rain coming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water so plant roots can absorb it safely. Placing fertilizer on dry soil during hot weather causes the nutrients to evaporate into the air or burn the plant roots directly.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛre shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and protect soil moisture, helping the young cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows their leaves to capture more sunlight to make food. It also prevents leaves from rotting on damp soil, directing more energy into growing larger roots.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa ebaai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo kɛha nihoomɔ. Ehaa baai hu shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa akɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni akɛha shishifãi lɛ adara.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans together with my cassava help my land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and fixes it into the soil. This naturally enriches the soil with food for nearby crops like cassava.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii, ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛhaa ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to compete aggressively for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing vital resources away from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛkɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nibii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen or sitting in waterlogged soil. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or adding compost helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off before producing any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ pepper ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant is stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. Keeping soil consistently moist and mulched helps the plant hold onto its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni awo nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai amli.

english: What causes tiny holes in the center leaves of my maize, and why is it dangerous?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? ŋmãa baa teŋgbɛ Ni mɛni hewɔ eyɛ oshara lɛ?

english: Tiny holes and chewed edges in central maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. If left unchecked, they destroy the plant's growing point, drastically lowering your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ebaakpata he ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches indicate Cassava Mosaic Disease, spread by tiny whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Nɔ ni tsɔɔ cassava mosaic hela ni ŋmeii bibii loo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Why should I wait for two or three good rains before planting my seeds at the start of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fioo dani madu dumɔwui yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: The very first rain only wet the surface, and the hot ground below can scorch new seeds. Waiting for several steady rains ensures the soil holds enough deep moisture for seeds to sprout safely.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nuɔ pɛ. Ni he ni edɔ yɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui heei. Nugbɔshiimɔi babaoo ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mɛmɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Concentrated fertilizer placed directly on a stem can burn the plant's skin and roots like chemical heat. It should always be applied a short distance away in a ring or line so roots safely absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Nakai eji yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ la mli lɛ hu he. Esa akɛ akɛwo mli be fɛɛ be yɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ kuku lɛ amli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: This usually happens when the plant lacks nitrogen or water. Nitrogen makes leaves green and healthy, so when the soil runs low, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo nu. Nitrogen haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ eshwɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas on my land before I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize on that same land next season, the maize feeds on that natural fertilizer and grows much stronger.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baaye adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni ebaatsɔ hewalɛ babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce smaller harvests when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants end up competing with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving them proper space ensures every plant gets enough food to grow big.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni adu lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaadara.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up into the sunlight so they can make more food for the growing tuber underground. It also keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii babaoo amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni baai lɛ akajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the fruit bunch gets large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that do not go deep into the soil. As the heavy fruit grows at the top, strong winds can easily push the plant over unless you prop it up with a strong wooden pole.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni aduawai ni tsii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ashɛre tsei kɛba shi mlɛo. Ja okɛ tso ni wa miitsu nii kɛmiifi sɛɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting in the soil before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Root rot happens when excess water sits around the roots for too long, especially in heavy or poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rain water drain away safely.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ fitemɔ baa kɛji nu ni fa fe nine ta shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does keeping shallow water in my rice field help control weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ jwɛi lɛ?

english: Most land weeds cannot breathe or grow underwater and will drown. Rice plants are naturally adapted to grow in standing water, so flooding acts as a natural weed controller.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ nu shishi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ nu mli. Omɔ tsei lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, nu afua tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli jwɛi akudɔmɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to stress, such as sudden hot dry weather, too little water, or excess fertilizer. Regular watering during the flowering stage helps flowers stick and form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔi, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ kpe. nu fioo tsɔ loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo afata he Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli daa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ shi.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often a defense against heat and water loss, or a sign of a virus spread by tiny whiteflies. Mulching the soil to hold moisture and protecting plants from insects helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni akɛwoɔ tomato nɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ he koni dɔlɛ kɛ nu akafite. Aloo eji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi? Mulching ni akɛbaakwɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko ni ebu tsei ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa plants can build strong roots and leaves without drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, cacao tsei bibii baanyɛ aná shishifãi kɛ baai ni mli wa ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why does my plantain crop yield smaller bunches when I plant the suckers too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ́ midu ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too closely, their broad leaves block sunlight from reaching each other, and their roots fight for nutrients and water in the soil, leading to smaller trunks and smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ aduawai akui bibii baa.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge bushy leaves above ground but very small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients like potassium, the plant puts all its energy into growing green leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ potassium he lɛ, tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my maize plants turn yellow in a V-shape and die early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the leaf tips in a V-shape indicate nitrogen deficiency. The maize plant moves limited nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naagbee yɛ V su mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Abɛi tsei jieɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans work with beneficial soil microbes to take nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground, naturally enriching the soil for crops like maize that need a lot of feeding.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei Ekɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni biɔ niyenii ni tsii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or sudden dry spells. The plant aborts the blossoms to save energy and water to survive the hot weather.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my maize plants more aggressively during the early rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-abele tsei lɛ waa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The warm air and soft, green shoots that appear right after the first rains create the perfect environment for pests like Fall Armyworm eggs to hatch and feed rapidly.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ kpo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛfɔ oya ni amɛye nii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during hot, dry weather to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun and slow down water evaporation, helping the plant retain moisture.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Koni hulu la ni baa yɛ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi ni eha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines start to wither and rot when water sits on my field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ ni egboɔ kɛ́ nu ta miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Yam roots and tubers need air in the soil to breathe. Standing water suffocates the roots and creates wet conditions where fungal diseases rapidly rot the underground seed tubers.
ga: Sweet potato shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ baa ni ŋmeii helai fiteɔ dumɔwui ayitsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ oya.

english: Why do my cabbage plants open up their leaves wide instead of forming a solid round ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ miigbele amɛhe waa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cabbage plants fail to form tight heads when temperatures are too hot or when water supply is irregular, causing the leaves to grow outward rather than wrapping tightly around the central core.
ga: Kaabaji tsei nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli tsɔ loo be mli ni nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ daa kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabɔle ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ he waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and shriveling up in the strong sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow root systems that cannot handle direct, intense heat. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ naa.

english: The small shoots, known as suckers, compete with the main plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing most of them allows the main stem to direct all its energy toward producing larger, heavier bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ajieɔ mɛi babaoo lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yitso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ plantains wuji ni tsii.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are mature enough to dig out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When cassava is ready for harvest, the lower leaves on the stem naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stalk with a small tuft of leaves at the top. You can also test maturity by carefully scraping away soil at the base to inspect the thickness of the tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Tso lɛ yitso lɛ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni eyɛ baai bibii komɛi yɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ oka ehewalɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ sũ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni oootsi lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ona bɔ ni ŋmei lɛ mli edɔ ha lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of just trailing along the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso koni ekwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooonyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture food for the growing tuber under the ground. Staking also lifts leaves off the damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and rotting.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni amɛbai lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii haa bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa.

english: Why are my sweet potato plants growing very thick green leaves but only tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa shi ŋmeii bibii pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen, sweet potato plants put all their energy into growing leafy top stems instead of storing food in the roots. Using less nitrogen fertilizer encourages the plant to direct its energy into expanding the tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaato niyenii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baawo tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo bulbs.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a V from the tip inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiya mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves in a V-pattern indicate that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen. The plant is pulling nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to feed the young, developing upper leaves and grain head.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ V lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Tso lɛ miihe nitrogen kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmaa yitsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my corn plants look wilted and curled up in the afternoon even when the ground feels damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi ni amɛbɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: In the intense afternoon heat, maize leaves roll up tightly to reduce surface area and minimize water loss through evaporation. As long as the soil has moisture, the leaves will relax and open up again when the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛha nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeleɔ ekoŋŋ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ.

english: How does growing groundnuts in my field make the soil better for my next corn planting?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with helpful soil microbes to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant roots decompose after harvest, this nitrogen stays in the soil as free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ beni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before any tomatoes start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off without forming fruit when temperatures are too high or when the plant experiences sudden drought or water stress. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, preventing fertilization.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ tsei kɛ hɔmɔ loo nu he haomɔ kpe trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper bushes twisting and curling tightly together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-hot pepper bush lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsi amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or whiteflies sucking the sap from young shoots and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat, broad, and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛmli atse, ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess rain washes away essential soil nutrients like nitrogen from the root zone and waterlogs the soil, preventing roots from breathing and absorbing food properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. ni ehaa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like calcium and phosphorus needed to support fruit development.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium kɛ phosphorus ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai lɛ adalɛ ni bɛ.

english: Is it better for me to plant cassava on raised mounds or flat ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ?

english: Planting on mounds creates loose, well-drained soil, which allows cassava roots to expand easily into large tubers and prevents them from rotting in wet soil.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji. ni ehaaa efite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak plants that yield very little harvest.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in humid, shady conditions when rainfall is high and farm air circulation is poor.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu eyaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions, allowing them to absorb water and soil nutrients much more aggressively than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: How can I keep my garden crops from dying during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagboi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil around plants with dried grass or leaves (mulching) holds moisture in the ground and shields the plant roots from the burning heat.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato leaves look wilted in the afternoon heat even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ?

english: In intense sun, water evaporates from the leaves faster than the roots can pull water from the soil, causing temporary wilting to protect the plant from drying out.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha tso lɛ agbi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekagbi.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over easily when it starts carrying a big cluster of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi ŋmeii wuji shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots, so the extra weight of a heavy fruit cluster can pull the weak root system right out of wet soil unless supported by a prop stick.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ja tso ko yɛ ni baaye abua lɛ

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my maize so it doesn't rot during storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Koni ekafite yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Maize is ready when the outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and the grains become hard enough that your fingernail cannot easily dent them.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ batsɔ ŋmãa ni egbi kwraa. Ni dumɔwui lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaŋ otsitsii lɛ atsɔ mlɛo.

english: If I run completely out of food and need something to harvest quickly to feed my family, what crop should I plant?
ga: Kɛji niyenii fite mi ni ehe bahia ni makpa oya koni mikɛha miweku lɛ niyenii Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ madu?

english: Short-duration crops like sweet potatoes or early-maturing maize varieties can be harvested in just two to three months. Fast-growing leafy vegetables like kontomire (cocoyam leaves) or okro also start producing food within a few weeks to keep your household fed while longer crops grow.
ga: Abaanyɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ mra lɛ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ mli. Aduawai ni yɔɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ kontomire (kokoo baai) loo okro hu jeɔ niyenii feemɔ shishi yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli koni ekɛ niyenii aha oshia lɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Which food crop is safest for me to plant if the rains are unpredictable and I am worried about drought?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha mi akɛ makwɛ kɛji nugbɔ baanɛ ni mihaoɔ yɛ hɔmɔ he?

english: Cassava is the most resilient crop during dry spells because its tough root system can store water underground for long periods. Even if its leaves dry up during severe hot weather, the roots remain safe and edible in the soil until you are ready to harvest them.
ga: Cassava ji tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ ateŋ ekome. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ baanyɛ ato nu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ebaai lɛ baanyɛ agbi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli moŋ, Shi shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni obaafee klalo akɛ obaakpa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea around the base of the plants will help them turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni yɔɔ nitrogen, tamɔ urea fata tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to a family of crops called legumes that take invisible food (nitrogen) from the air and trap it in tiny balls on their roots. When the plant dies after harvest, that trapped food stays in the soil as free natural fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata tsei akuu ko ni atsɛɔ amɛ legumes lɛ he. Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni anaaa (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ amɛ shishifãi bibii amli kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Niyenii ni ekã lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves during the dry season, and are they dead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ fite yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli ni egbo lɛ?

english: The cassava plants are not dead; dropping leaves is their natural way of saving water and surviving hot, dry weather. Once the rain returns, the plant will push out fresh green leaves and keep growing without losing the food stored in its tubers.
ga: Kasava tso lɛ gboko lolo. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he ni ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyaa nɔ edaa ni niyenii ni ato yɛ bulb lɛ mli lɛ laajeee.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Giving your tomato plants regular watering at the base and adding compost will help the flowers stay attached and swell into healthy fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Numɔ tomato tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni eye ebua tomato fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwere ni amɛfee aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding on the underside of leaves and sucking out the plant's juices. You can fight them by spraying the leaves with simple soap and water solutions or appropriate neem oil treatments.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ awuu kɛtsɔ samla kɛ nu ni oookɛshwie baai lɛ anɔ loo kɛ neem fɔ ni sa ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings fall over and die at the stem right after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil is kept too wet, allowing tiny fungi to rot the soft stem near the ground—a condition called damping-off. To stop this, water your nursery bed lightly in the morning instead of the evening and ensure seedlings have good air flow.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Ha ŋmɔtɔ bibioo lɛ Young stems ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ masɛi. Enɛ ji shihilɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ damping. Koni akpa enɛ Nu lɛ awo gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ blɛoo. leebi moŋ fe gbɛkɛ Ni kwɛmɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa.

english: Why must I place dry leaves or grass on top of my newly planted yam mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi woɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni adu ehee lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering yam mounds with dry plant material (mulching) acts like a blanket that shields the seed yam from baking under the hot sun. It keeps the soil cool and moist so the yam sprout does not dry up and rot before it can grow above ground.
ga: Kɛ akɛ tsei ni egbi (mulching) ha sweet potato ni ato lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ blanket ni buɔ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Enɛ ji koni sweet potato tsei lɛ akagbi ni amɛkafite dani amɛdara yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better for my land if I plant only one crop in my field or mix different crops together?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi kome pɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli loo mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi futu mli?

english: Mixing crops like maize, cassava, and beans together (intercropping) protects your land and secures your food supply. Different crops draw nutrients from different depths of the soil, and if a pest or dry spell damages one crop, you will still have other crops to harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmãa (nibii ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmãa) yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he ni ehaa niyenii ni oyɔɔ lɛ hiɔ shi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ srɔtoi amli. Ni kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo hulutsoo be fite ŋmɔshi nibii kome? Obaaná ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lolo ni obaakpa.

english: Why should I try growing sweet orange potatoes instead of sticking only to my usual cassava and maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka ŋmei ni ji orange sweet potatoes lɛ akwɛ yɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Diversifying your farm with sweet orange potato reduces your financial risk if maize or cassava crops fail. It grows quickly—maturing in just 3 to 4 months—and provides essential nutrients like Vitamin A to keep your family healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji orange sweet potatoes wo oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shika he oshara ni oyɔɔ lɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ o-corn loo cassava lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. Edaa oya—eshɛɔ dalɛ he yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 pɛ mli—ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ vitamin A haa koni oweku lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are health workers saying that sweet orange potato is better for my family than the white sweet potato?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helatsamɔ he nitsulɔi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji orange lɛ hi kɛha miweku lɛ fe ŋmɔtɔ ni ji white lɛ?

english: The bright orange color in the potato comes from beta-carotene, which your body converts into Vitamin A. This helps prevent blindness in children and boosts the immune system, unlike white potatoes which mainly provide starch.
ga: Nɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ jɛɔ beta-carotene mli. ni ogbɔmɔtso lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ vitamin A Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa gbekɛbii shwilafo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nii ni gbeɔ helai lɛ yaa hiɛ Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ, ni ji ŋmɔtɔ titri lɛ he.

english: How do I properly plant sweet orange potato vines so that I get big tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ sweet potato wain tsei ni ji orange lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni maná bulbs wuji?

english: Sweet orange potatoes need loose soil to expand, so you should heap the soil into mounds or ridges. Plant vine cuttings about 20 to 30 centimeters long at an angle, burying at least three nodes under the soil where the roots will form.
ga: Orange sweet potato biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa. Esa akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ato gɔji loo ŋmeii ahe. Dumɔ wain tso lɛ kɛtsɔ eshishinumɔ ni ooofo yɛ koŋ nɔ, ni elɛɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimitai 20 kɛyashi 30 nɔ, ni kɛ hoo lɛ, ŋmeii etɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi he ni shishifãi lɛ baafee lɛ nɔ.

english: Can sweet orange potatoes handle areas with short rainy seasons or dry spells?
ga: Ani sweet orange yams baanyɛ akpee hei ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo loo nugbɔshiimɔ bei yɔɔ lɛ anaa?

english: Yes, sweet orange potatoes are naturally quick-maturing and drought-tolerant. Because they harvest in 90 to 120 days, they can produce a good yield even when rains are short or unpredictable.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, sweet potatoes ni ji orange lɛ shwereɔ oya ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Akɛni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ gbii 90 kɛyashi 120 mli hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ewo yibii kpakpai kɛji nugbɔ enɛ fioo loo anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba po.

english: Why do sweet potato vines spread all over the ground, and should I cut them back while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ mafo amɛ be mli ni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: The spreading leaves cover the soil like a blanket to retain moisture and block weeds from growing. You should not cut the vines back, because the leaves trap sunlight to manufacture energy that feeds and expands the tubers underground.
ga: Baai lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ kuntu koni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni eha jwɛi akakwɛ̃. Esaaa akɛ ofoɔ wain tsei ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ hulu la lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa amɛmli shwereɔ lɛ baa.

english: How can I protect my sweet potatoes from pests that attack them under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmeii ahe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni tutuaa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe?

english: Pests like sweet potato weevils burrow through cracks in dry soil to reach the roots. You can protect them by 'earthing up'—piling fresh soil over the roots to keep cracks covered and soil moist.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ sweet potato moth lɛ baatsɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli ŋmeii amli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ. Obaanyɛ obu amɛhe kɛtsɔ ‘shikpɔŋ’ ni oookɛwo amɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ sũ hee ni oookɛto shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni eha sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I turn my sweet orange potato harvest into bread or pastries to make extra income?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔ mi-orange sweet potato ni mifeɔ lɛ nɔ matsɔ blodo loo nibii ni ashãa koni maná shika kroko?

english: You can boil and mash the potatoes into a smooth purée or dry them into flour, then mix it with wheat flour. This reduces how much wheat flour you need to buy while making rich, naturally sweet bread that sells well at the market.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ afɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse loo ogbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ ŋmaa ashikiŋsha afutu mli. Enɛ haa ŋmaa ashikishaŋ ni ehe hiaa ni ohe lɛ baa shi beni ofeɔ blodoo ni mli ŋɔɔ, ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni ahɔ̃ɔ waa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ.

english: How should I store my sweet orange potatoes after harvest so they do not rot quickly?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ato yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ koni amɛkafite oya?

english: After harvesting, let the tubers sit in a warm, shaded area for a few days so skin cuts can heal, then store them in a cool, dark, well-ventilated room on dry straw or sand to keep them fresh for months.
ga: kpamɔ sɛɛ Ha tuber lɛ ahi he ko ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi koni hewolo ni afo lɛ lɛ atsa. Kɛkɛ lɛ, akɛtoɔ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ jwɛi loo ŋã ni egbi nɔ koni amɛhi shi nyɔji babaoo.

english: Does growing sweet orange potato drain all the nutrients out of my soil like heavy crops do?
ga: Ani ŋmɔtɔ ni ji orange ni aduɔ lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii baafee lɛ?

english: Sweet orange potato takes moderate nutrients from the soil compared to heavy feeders like yam. Mixing compost or well-rotted animal manure into the mounds before planting keeps your soil fertile for future crops.
ga: Orange sweet potatoes lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛto ŋmɔtɔ ni tsii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo okpɔŋɔ lɛ mli dani odu lɛ, ebaaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo kɛha nibii ni obaadu wɔsɛɛ.

english: How do I keep sweet orange potato vines alive for the next planting season during the dry period?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã wain tsei ni ji orange sweet potato lɛ ahi shi kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Since sweet potato vines dry up without water, you can keep a small nursery plot near a water source or shady backyard area during the dry season so you have fresh, healthy vine cuttings ready when the main rains return.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, sweet potato wain tso lɛ mli egbi ni nu bɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe bibioo ko ato. Yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe loo yɛ sɛɛgbɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Bɔni afee ni oná tsei niji heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni asaa he kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ku esɛɛ aba.

english: Extreme heat and direct sunlight can dry out cocoa leaves and burn the plant, causing the leaves to turn brown, curl up, and fall off if the farm lacks proper shade cover.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo baai lɛ agbi ni eshã tso lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, amɛkpãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ bɛ hulutsoo ni sa.

english: How does intense sunshine affect the number of cocoa pods my tree can produce?
ga: Te hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ saa kookoo ŋmeii ayibɔ ni mitso lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Too much direct sunlight causes heat stress, which makes cocoa trees drop their flowers and young pods early, resulting in a much lower harvest.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi kɛ amɛbii bibii lɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ enɛ mli baa ji kpamɔ bibioo kwraa.

english: What is this thick grease treatment people use on damaged cocoa trunks, and what does it do?
ga: What is it about people who apply this thick grease to damaged cocoa trees? Ni mɛni etsuɔ?

english: Farmers often use protective pastes or chemical sealants—referred to as 'grease'—on cuts, wounds, or diseased parts of a trunk to seal out pests and prevent infections from killing the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi kɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he loo tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘grease’ lɛ woɔ tso lɛ fãi ni afo, pilamɔi loo hela emɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni ekɛtsi helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa koni ekagbe tso lɛ.

english: How do I properly apply medicine to my cocoa trees so I don't ruin the plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ tsofa awo cacao tsei amli jogbaŋŋ koni ekafite cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Medicines and protective treatments should be applied carefully to the affected parts using clean tools during cooler hours of the day, strictly following recommended steps so the crop can heal properly.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ tsofai kɛ tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ awo hei ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ nibii ni he tse nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ anɔyeli pɛpɛɛpɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ atsa jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees still dying even after I spray them with farm chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ miigboi lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Spraying chemicals only stops pests or diseases; if the main cause of damage is severe sun burn or heat stress, the crop will still suffer unless you provide shade or heat-protection remedies.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela loo hela lɛ kpaɔ pɛ. Kɛji akɛ nɔ titri ni kɛ fitemɔ lɛ baa ji hulutsoo ni naa wa loo dɔlɛ mli haomɔ. Ebaaya nɔ ena ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ ja okɛ hulutsoo loo gbɛ ko ni oootsɔ nɔ obu ehe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he.

english: Can cocoa seeds or varieties brought from countries like Brazil grow well in Ghana?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmeii loo henɔi ni akɛbaajɛ maji tamɔ Brazil lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana?

english: Varieties from tropical countries like Brazil can grow well in Ghana because of similar climate conditions, but they may need careful management and shade to adjust to local weather.
ga: Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni jɛ maji ni mli edɔ tamɔ Brazil lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana yɛ amɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni tamɔ amɛhe lɛ hewɔ. Shi ekolɛ ebaabi ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni aha lɛ hulutsoo koni ekɛ ehe akpã gbee ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do new crop varieties brought from outside sometimes struggle with the weather on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei srɔtoi heei ni akɛbaa kɛjɛɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ naa naagbai yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Crops bred in other regions may be sensitive to different soil types or stronger sunshine, requiring extra water, shade, and protective care until they adapt to local conditions.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni sũi srɔtoi yɔɔ mli. aloo eyɛ hulu la ni naa wa fe tsutsu lɛ Ebiɔ nu, hulutsoo, kɛ hebuu krɛdɛɛ kɛyashi ebaatsake ehe ewo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree is dying because of the sun or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hulu loo hela miigbe mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Sun damage mainly affects leaves exposed to open sky by turning them dry and burnt, whereas disease usually causes dark spots, rotting pods, or fungal growth even on shaded parts of the tree.
ga: Hulu ni fiteɔ nii lɛ saa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe titri kɛtsɔ amɛgbimɔ kɛ shãa nɔ. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. ŋmeii ni egboi loo ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ Yɛ tsei lɛ ahe hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ po

english: What causes mature cocoa trees to suddenly start dying off in large numbers?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ trukaa babaoo?

english: Sudden dieback in mature cocoa is usually caused by a combination of harsh heat waves, lack of shade, and fungal diseases spreading through damaged bark or open wounds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo ni naa wa, hulutsoo ni bɛ, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii ni efite loo pilamɔi ni agbele naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ gbele ni baa trukaa yɛ kookoo ni eda lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: What steps should I take to save my farm when my cocoa trees start dying from intense sun?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni maye mabua miŋmɔ lɛ beni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: To save surviving trees, prune away dead branches, apply protective pastes to tree wounds, and plant temporary shade crops like plantains to shelter the cocoa from direct heat.
ga: Bɔni afee ni abu tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe lɛ Afolɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ amli. Okɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ awo tso lɛ pilamɔ lɛ he. kɛ tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛ latsaa tɛ̃ɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need shade plants around them when I first plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe bahia ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo abɔle mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ he beni midu lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are easily burned and dried out by direct, intense sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or cassava next to them acts like a sun canopy, keeping the young trees cool and the soil moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii ni amɛgbiɔ. Dumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo tsɔne Ehaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa tree falling off without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by drought, poor soil nutrients, or insect pests like mirids. Ensuring your soil stays moist, keeping the farm shaded, and managing pests early helps the flowers stay on the tree and turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hɔmɔ ha tso lɛ hao. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen Kwɛmɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ nɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which thrives in cool, overly damp environments. Pruning excess branches to let sunlight and wind pass through the farm helps dry out the trees and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei lɛ aniji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why am I advised to cut off the small side shoots growing at the bottom of my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi.

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers or chupons, waste the tree's food and energy. Removing them forces the tree to direct all its water and nutrients to the main branches where the cocoa pods grow.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi lɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo chupons. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii kɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ amɛ lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ enu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ majeɔ tso lɛ niji titrii ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Cocoa seedlings should ideally be planted about 3 meters apart. Proper spacing prevents the trees from competing with each other for soil nutrients and leaves enough room for air to flow, which reduces disease spread.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cocoa dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe aaafee mitai 3. Kɛ́ ato tsei lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni oshi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Can I grow rice on dry land, or do I always need a flooded field?
ga: Ani obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ? Aloo esa akɛ nu atsɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli be fɛɛ be?

english: You can grow rice on dry land if you use upland rice varieties, which rely mainly on regular rain. Lowland rice varieties, on the other hand, require wet or flooded soil like river valleys to give a good yield.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ gɔŋ nɔ, ni damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ waa lɛ tsu nii. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ faai amli jɔɔ lɛ, koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why are the leaves of my young rice plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your rice plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea at the right time helps the leaves turn green and feed the growing plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-rice tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni eha tso ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds harm my rice crop more quickly than my other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ oya fe tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Rice plants have shallow roots and thin leaves, making it hard for them to compete with fast-growing weeds for light, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early in the crop's life keeps the rice from being choked out.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ baabɔ he akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ shihilɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa akamɔ.

english: How can I tell when my rice is fully ripe and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Rice is ready for harvest when most of the grains on the head turn from green to a hard, golden-yellow color, and the leaves at the bottom of the plant begin to dry out.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni ŋmaa ni yɔɔ eyitso lɛ nɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ ni wa mli lɛ. ni baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops if I plant the same crop on it every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating crops gives the soil a break and breaks the life cycle of farm pests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ gbalaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce fruit after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains need a strong foundation before fruiting. It usually takes about 9 to 12 months for a plantain stalk to mature and flower, and another 3 to 4 months for the fruit bunch to fully fill out for harvest.
ga: Shishitoo ni wa he miihia plantains dani amɛwo yibii. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani plantain tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi, ni eheɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 krokomɛi hu dani aduawai akui lɛ eyi obɔ kɛkpamɔ.

english: Why does my mango tree produce a huge harvest one year and then almost no fruit the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli shi afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ, eshɛɛɛ eko kwraa lɛ?

english: This is a natural behavior called alternate bearing. Producing a heavy harvest exhausts the mango tree's stored food reserves, so it spends the following year resting and gathering energy instead of making fruit.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ nɔ kroko ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli. Nikpamɔ ni tsii haa mango tso lɛ niyenii ni ekɛtoɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛjɔɔ he ni abuaa hewalɛ naa yɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ.

english: Why are some of my pawpaw trees flowering heavily but never producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw trees have different sexes. Male pawpaw trees produce flowers on long dangling stems to release pollen, but only female or hermaphrodite trees can actually develop fruit.
ga: Pawpaw tsei lɛ yɛ bɔlɛnamɔi srɔtoi. Pawpaw tsei hii fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tsei kakadaji ni shwieɔ shi ni jieɔ pollen. Shi tsei ni ji yei loo tsei ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ yakayaka nii lɛ pɛ baanyɛ awo yibii.

english: Why do my mango flowers keep falling off before small fruits can even form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai bibii baa lɛ?

english: Mango trees drop excess flowers naturally, but heavy flower drop is usually triggered by dry spells without water, pest attacks like thrips, or fungal diseases that attack during the flowering period.
ga: Mango tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Shi bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ jɛɔ hulutsoo be ni nu bɛ mli, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ thrips, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa mɔ yɛ fɔfɔi afeemɔ be mli lɛ mli.

english: Should I cut off the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ani ajie mi plantain shishifãi lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving too many suckers causes them to steal food and water from the main tree. You should trim them away and leave only one or two strong suckers to take over after you harvest the main stem.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ oshi suckers babaoo ni amɛgbele lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ofolɔ mli ni oshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni oye yɛ egbɛhe beni okpa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my ripening pineapples burn and develop soft spots on one side while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shã ni eyɛ he ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ efã kome beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Pineapples are sensitive to harsh afternoon sun as they ripen. Farmers shade the growing fruits by tying their leaves over the fruit or covering them with dry grass to block direct heat.
ga: Pineapple nuɔ shwane hulu la ni naa wa he kɛji ekwɛ̃. Okwaafoi haa aduawai ni miida lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ baai ni amɛkɛfiɔ aduawai lɛ anɔ loo amɛkɛ sũ ni egbi haa nɔ koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the oil palm is lacking key nutrients like potassium or nitrogen in the soil, or that it is struggling to get enough water during dry seasons.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ potassium loo nitrogen bɛ mu tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo naagba ni enaa yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Can I plant the leafy top cut from a pineapple fruit to grow a new pineapple plant?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tso nine ni baai yɔɔ mli kɛjɛ ŋmei tso ko mli koni makwɛ ŋmei tso hee?

english: Yes, the top leafy crown of a pineapple fruit can be trimmed and planted directly into well-drained soil, where it will root and grow into a full new producing plant over 18 to 24 months.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ afo anana baa yiteŋgbɛ ni adu tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Ebaawo shishifãi ni etsɔ tso ni woɔ yibii kwraa yɛ nyɔji 18 kɛyashi 24 mli.

english: How do I know the right time to pick my pawpaws so they don't spoil on the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa? Koni ekafite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Pawpaws are ready to harvest as soon as yellow or orange streaks start showing near the base of the green fruit. Leaving them to turn completely yellow on the tree attracts birds and fruit flies.
ga: Pawpaws lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ je shishi amɛje kpo yɛ aduawai eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ pɛ. Ha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ kwraa koni ekɛgbala okpoi kɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii.

english: How far apart should I space my oil palm seedlings when planting them on my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo oil palm dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Oil palms grow very wide leaves and deep root systems, so they need about 9 meters of space between each plant in a triangular pattern to avoid shading each other out.
ga: Mu tsei yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ waa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ mu tso lɛ aná sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni ji triangular aaafee mitai 9 yɛ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ koni amɛkatsi amɛhe naa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their foliage is soft and sensitive. Shade trees act like umbrellas that keep the soil cool and moist, protecting young seedlings until they grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can harvest more food on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and nutrients in the soil, while their leaves block sunshine from reaching one another. Proper spacing allows every plant to grow thick, healthy, and produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa, amɛhe wa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks essential food like nitrogen, or that water is sitting around the roots for too long. Feeding the soil with compost or proper fertilizer gives plants the strength to stay green and produce big tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu eta shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why am I supposed to cut off the extra branches and suckers growing at the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine yɛ kookoo tso shishi lɛ?

english: Suckers and crowded branches drain water and energy away from the main trunk without producing good pods. Cutting them away lets sunlight and fresh air reach the tree, which encourages more flowers and healthy cocoa pods to grow.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii kɛ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ jieɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli ni amɛfeee ŋmeii kpakpai. Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ he. Enɛ baawo fɔfɔi babaoo kɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans in the same field help my main crops grow better?
ga: Te ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ titri lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?
