english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which naturally captures nitrogen from the air and feeds it into the soil. As they grow, they enrich the soil naturally, helping neighboring crops like maize grow faster without needing as much commercial fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ amɛdara lɛ Amɛbaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ni amɛdaraa oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ jarayeli ŋmãa babaoo awo mli.

english: Black pod is caused by a small water-loving fungus that spreads rapidly when the farm is damp and dark. Clearing weeds and pruning crowded leaves allows air and sunlight to dry out the trees, preventing the fungal moisture from destroying the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa ji ŋmei bibioo ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ. Etsiɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ naa koni ekafite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my vegetable crops drop off rapidly during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The Harmattan brings extremely dry wind that pulls water directly out of plant leaves faster than roots can absorb it from dry soil. To preserve water, the plant sheds its leaves so it does not dry out completely and die.
ga: Harmattan kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi waa baa koni ekɛgbala nu kɛjɛ tsei ahe baai amli tɛ̃ɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. koni akɛbu nu he Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkagbi kwraa ni amɛgboi.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the soil. It holds moisture near the plant roots for many days, suppresses weed growth, and turns into rich soil food as it rots.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe gbii babaoo. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ebafeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ kɛji egbo.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor soil fertility. Regular watering during warm periods and balanced plant food help the flowers stay on the stem until fruit forms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ kɛ tso niyenii ni sa yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I buy certified hybrid seeds instead of just planting seeds saved from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Seeds saved from past harvests lose their strength over generations, growing into uneven plants that yield less grain. Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local diseases, handle short rains, and yield much more food per farm acre.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni wooo yibii babaoo. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai. Kpee nugbɔshiimɔi kukuji anaa ni owo yibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli acre kome mli

english: Why do my maize leaves still have holes even after I sprayed them with chemical pesticide?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli bu yɔɔ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ moŋ?

english: Pesticides might fail if they are washed away by rain, sprayed at the wrong time of day, or mixed incorrectly. Also, some pests like the fall armyworm hide deep inside the maize leaves where light spraying cannot reach them.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni tsuuu nii kɛji nugbɔ shwie amɛ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni esaaa mli loo ni akɛfutuɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Kɛfata he lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui komɛi, tamɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ, teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmei baa mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why does the weedkiller I bought leave some stubborn weeds alive in my farm while killing others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mihe lɛ shĩɔ jwɛi ni mli wa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni egbeɔ jwɛi krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Different weedkillers target specific types of plants. Some only kill broad-leaf weeds while others target grasses. Using the wrong chemical, or spraying when weeds are already mature and strong, makes the chemical ineffective.
ga: Tsofai srɔtoi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ. Mɛi komɛi gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo pɛ, yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi hu kwɛɔ jwɛi anɔ. Tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii Loo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ beni jwɛi lɛ edara kwraa ni ehe wa lɛ. Ebaaha tsofai lɛ akatsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties is the best protection.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Agbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmei bibii yɛŋ nɔ. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa.

english: Why are the roots of my yam plants rotting underground before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when the soil holds too much water without proper drainage, or when tiny soil pests called nematodes bite the tubers, allowing rot-causing fungi to enter.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Atsɛɔ amɛ akɛ yitsoŋ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ abote mli.

english: I applied chemical fertilizer to my tomato farm last week, so why are the plants not growing any faster?
ga: Mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo mi tomato ŋmɔ lɛ mli otsi ni eho lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ edaaa oya lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need moisture in the soil to dissolve so the roots can absorb them. If the soil is too dry, or if the fertilizer was placed too close to the stem without being covered with soil, the plant cannot feed on it properly.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi tsɔ ni okɛhaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei hu nyɛɛɛ amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants look strong in the morning but wilt completely during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ leebi lɛ? Shi egbo kwraa yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli?

english: Hot afternoon weather causes leaves to lose water faster than dry roots can collect it from the soil. Covering the soil around your plants with dry grass (mulching) helps keep the soil cool and wet.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ abua naa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their young pods before they even grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ eshishifãi bibii lɛ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods drop (a condition called cherelle wilt) when the tree is stressed by a lack of rainfall, insufficient shade, poor soil nutrients, or attacks from insects like mirids.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ baagbee shi. (Shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ wilt) baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Shade ni fa bɔ ni sa Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen tutuamɔ.

english: My garden egg plants are flowering plenty, so why are the flowers falling off without producing fruit?
ga: Eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of water, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees. Heavy use of harsh insect sprays during flowering can also drive away beneficial insects.
ga: Fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa, nu ni bɛ, loo nibii ni haa fɔfɔi tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ ashwie kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ manyɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. Ani minɔ ni?

english: Planting too close makes the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This creates tall, thin plants with very small corn ears or no ears at all. Proper spacing produces healthier plants and bigger yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ baaha tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa toi bibii waa loo toi ni bɛ kwraa lɛ aba. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from my last maize harvest produce smaller crops than the packaged seeds I buy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛwo kotoku mli ni mihe lɛ?

english: Many commercial seeds are hybrid varieties bred specifically for high yield in their first planting. Seeds saved from those crops lose that high yield power in the next generation, resulting in weaker plants.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni atsɔse amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ ni haa yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning yellow and drying up now that the weather has become very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme sun and high heat cause plants to lose water faster than their roots can draw it from the ground. When heat gets intense, plants burn and drop leaves to conserve water to stay alive.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ haa tsei lɛ nu fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa lɛ Tsei lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu koni amɛhi shi.

english: How can I protect my soil from drying out too fast during the hot season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mishikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dry grass, straw, or leaves, a method called mulching. This layer blocks direct sunlight from the ground, trapping moisture in the soil and keeping roots cool.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Akɛ jwɛi, jwɛi loo baai duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, gbɛ ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ.

english: Will planting taller trees around my farm protect my delicate vegetables from severe heat?
ga: Tsei kakadaji ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani miŋmɔ lɛ baabu mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he?

english: Yes, planting trees like plantains or shade trees around your farm creates living barriers that lower ground temperatures and shade sensitive plants from intense sun and drying winds.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ adumɔ. Oŋmɔ lɛ baafee gbɛtsii nii ko ni hiɛ ka ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ aba shi ni eha tsei ni hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ nuɔ he lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to water my crops when the weather is extremely hot?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ nu awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening is best because lower temperatures allow the soil to absorb moisture. Watering during the hot afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before reaching the roots.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulutsoo ni baa shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu. Kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop in the afternoon heat even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During peak afternoon heat, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can replace it, causing temporary wilting. As long as the soil stays moist, the plants will bounce back once the evening air cools down.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa fe fɛɛ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ Tsei fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ atsake lɛ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa kɛji gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my crops when the ground is dry and hot?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni edɔ lɛ?

english: No, applying fertilizer to hot, dry soil can cause 'fertilizer burn' on the crop's roots. Always ensure the soil is well-moistened before applying fertilizers so the plant can safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Dabi, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ‘ŋmei ashã’ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Kwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my seeds taking so long to sprout after I plant them in dry, warm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need both consistent moisture and cool soil to break open and grow. Extremely hot, dry soil hardens the earth and starves seeds of water, slowing down germination or preventing it completely.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni mli ejɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa ni hɔmɔ baaye nu dumɔwui lɛ. Ehaa kwɛ̃mɔ baa shi loo ehaaa ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why are flowers falling off my pepper plants without growing into fruit during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: High temperatures stress plants, causing them to drop their blossoms to save energy and water. When it gets too hot, plants focus on surviving rather than producing new fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ agbee shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ baama wala nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii heei.

english: Which basic crops can I plant that survive best when the dry season heat becomes severe?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee tsei manyɛ madu koni manyɛ mahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli wa waa?

english: Crops like cassava, cowpeas, millet, and sorghum have deep roots and tough leaves that tolerate heat and dry soil much better than soft leafy vegetables.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ cassava, cowpea, millet kɛ sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni wa ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi naa babaoo fe aduawai ni baa yɔɔ blɛoo.

english: Why do I see more insects attacking my crops whenever the weather suddenly becomes very warm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ trukaa lɛ minaa kooloi bibii babaoo ni tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ? Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa.

english: Insects multiply much faster in warm weather, and heat stresses crops, making plants weaker and less able to fight off pest attacks.
ga: Kplukai fɔɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Ni latsaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide the necessary shade and keep the soil moist during the cocoa plant's first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ cacao tso lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same piece of land every farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be mli lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills the soil with nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai shwereɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni ebaafite ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure will help your maize regain its dark green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni eda waa.

english: What is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my crop during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp, but avoid doing it right before a heavy downpour so the rain does not wash the nutrients away. Applying it early in the morning or late afternoon gives the best results.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi kaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa aba koni nugbɔ lɛ akajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii leebi loo shwane lɛ, ehaa nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with dark dust inside the center leaf?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ni sũ diŋŋ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ.

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the whorl (heart) of the plant. You can control them by applying recommended insecticides early in the morning or late evening when the worms come out to feed.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ whorl (tsui) lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okudɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi lɛ eje kpo kɛmiitao niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings for planting is the best way to prevent this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Ni akɛ ŋmeii niji ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ́ adu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green sweet peppers turning dark and rotten while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi green bell peppers lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping your soil consistently moist helps the plant transport calcium properly to the developing peppers.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkɛ calcium lɛ aya ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does leaving cleared grass on top of my soil help or hurt my crops during hot weather?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa loo eyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awui yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Leaving cleared vegetation on top of the soil acts as mulch. It protects the soil from direct heat, traps moisture, stops weed growth, and eventually breaks down to enrich your soil.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni ajie yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi Ekpaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready for harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, the main stem turns woody brown, and the ground around the plant root cracks slightly. You can carefully dig up one test plant to check root size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ tsɔɔ blɔfo. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ efo fioo. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa tso kome ni akaa lɛ akwɛɔ koni okwɛ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ dara ha.

english: Why do my stored maize grains get destroyed by tiny insects even when kept in closed bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii bibii fiteɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ kɛ́ akɛto kotokui ni aŋã mli po lɛ?

english: Insects like grain weevils often lay eggs on the maize before harvest or survive inside damp grains. Fully drying your maize until the grains make a sharp cracking sound when bitten, and storing them with approved storage dust or hermetic bags, will keep insects out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmaa ŋmeii woɔ ŋmaa nɔ dani akpaa loo amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmaa ni mli efɔ mli. Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ baatswa kɛji akɛ amɔ lɛ. ni akɛtoɔ sũ loo kotokui ni awo mli ni awo he odase lɛ amli. Ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akabote mli.

english: Why is it raining heavily in January when it is usually dry Harmattan season, and how will this affect my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ January mli lɛ? Akɛni bei pii lɛ eji Harmattan be ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ. Ni te enɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Unseasonal rains in January happen due to changing climate patterns. While the moisture helps crops survive dry spells, sudden rains can trick crops into flowering early or create wet conditions that lead to fungal rot if drainage is poor.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ January mli lɛ baa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli moŋ, shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afɔlɔ mra loo eha shihilɛi lɛ afee fɛ̃i waa bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔtɔ agbo kɛji nu ni hoɔ lɛ ehiii.

english: If rain falls heavily early in the year, should I start planting my maize immediately?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli Ani esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Not immediately. Early rain in January or February can be a false start. If the dry weather returns right after, your planted seeds will dry up in the soil and fail to germinate.
ga: Jeee amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ January loo February shishijee gbɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, ku osɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni adu lɛ baagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow when it rains almost every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Too much daily rain fills all the small air spaces in the soil with water. This suffocates the plant roots, preventing them from taking up essential nutrients like nitrogen, which turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo daa gbi lɛ haa nu yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Etsiɔ enaa koni ekaná niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why are weeds growing much faster than my main crops during these unexpected rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have wild, deep root systems that react instantly to moisture. They absorb water and nutrients faster than cultivated crops, taking advantage of unexpected rain to grow rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni ji adebɔɔ mli shishifãi ni tsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ba. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Amɛkɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ tsu nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: What happens to the fertilizer I applied on my farm if heavy rain falls right after?
ga: Mɛni baaba ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ no sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away fertilizer from the soil surface before the plants can absorb it. To prevent this, apply fertilizer when light rains are expected, or dig small holes to bury the fertilizer near the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ enɛ naa Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni akpaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ baanɛ fioo. aloo atsa bu bibioo ko ni okɛfu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ

english: How can I prevent heavy rainwater from washing away the good soil on my sloping farmland?
ga: Matsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekahoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ. Yɛ mi okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Building soil ridges across the slope rather than down the hill slows down flowing water. This forces the rainwater to soak into the ground instead of carrying your rich topsoil away.
ga: Kɛ́ ama ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ yɛ gɔŋkpɔ ko nɔ yɛ gɔŋkpɔ lɛ nɔ shi moŋ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Enɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground before harvest time during wet weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when soil stays waterlogged for too long. If rain falls continuously without proper field drainage, oxygen cannot reach the roots, allowing decay-causing bacteria and fungi to thrive.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be ni nu kpakpa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Oxygen nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, muawai kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ baanyɛ ada.

english: Why do dark spots and rot appear on my cocoa pods when wet weather lasts longer than normal?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ beni hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Continuous wet and humid weather encourages Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in water droplets. Pruning excess tree branches lets sunlight and air flow through to keep pods dry.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ eha blackpod hela eba, ni ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nu mli ŋmeii amli lɛ kɛbaa. Tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants when heavy rain hits the farm every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa leebi lɛ?

english: Heavy raindrops physically beat fragile flowers off the plant and wash away pollen before fertilization occurs. Planting living windbreaks around your plot can reduce the impact of driving rain on tender crops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni efoɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli dani fɔmɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aba. Kɔɔyɔɔŋ ŋmɔji ni ooodu yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: How can I safely dry my harvested corn when it rains every day and there is no sunshine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ shweshweeshwe beni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa gbi ni hulu bɛ lɛ?

english: When sunshine is scarce, store harvested corn elevated off the ground inside a well-ventilated shed, spread them out thin to avoid mold, and cover them with tarpaulins only when rain is actively falling.
ga: Kɛ hulu la faaa lɛ Too ŋmãa ni akpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli, ni okɛgbɛ ashwã mli fioo fioo koni ŋmã akafee nɔ ko. Ni kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa pɛ kɛkɛ ni okɛ tarpaulin aha he.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build healthy green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and get light green patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Curling leaves with yellowish patterns are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny white insects called whiteflies.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and look dead during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni gboi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops droop their leaves in intense afternoon heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps them save water from evaporating too fast until the air cools down.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings dying when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender roots and leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight; they need shade from crops like plantain to hold moisture around them until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. kɛyashi ebaada kwraa

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering, which prevents the flowers from pollinating and setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, cloudy weather when moisture stays on the pods for too long.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ atatu yɔɔ. he ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ.

english: When water sits in the soil without proper drainage, it starves the roots of air and allows soil fungi to multiply, causing the tubers to rot.
ga: Beni nu yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu haa kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwereɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni egbo

english: Why do my maize stalks fall over easily whenever a light wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its root system is weak due to shallow planting, soil packed too tightly, or pest damage inside the stem that makes the base brittle.
ga: Abɛi baagbee baai lɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ yɛ dumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ mli, ni no haa shishigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does my pepper plant stop bearing new peppers after I harvest the first ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ pepper heei feemɔ beni mikpa mi klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants exhaust their energy and soil nutrients to mature the first fruit batch, so they require extra compost or fertilizer after harvest to produce a second flush.
ga: Pepper tsei kɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii ni ji enyɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines grow very thick with lots of leaves but give me small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ehaa yitso bibioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant focus all its energy on growing leaves above ground instead of transferring food down into the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei ahe tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaatsu niyenii kɛya bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I just take palm nuts from my neighbor's high-yielding tree to plant on my own land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miheɔ ŋmei dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ mikutsoŋnyo tso ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Palms grown from ordinary harvested nuts (F2 seeds) often revert to wild, low-yielding types with thick shells and very little oil. Certified seedlings are specially bred hybrids (Tenera) produced under strict controls to guarantee high oil production and uniform growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni afɔɔ kpamɔ (F2 dumɔwui) amli lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa koo mli tsei ni wooo yibii babaoo lɛ amli. Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ fɔ fioo ko pɛ. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ji tsofa krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛfee tsofa (Tenera) ni afee yɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa shishi koni ekɛha mu babaoo aba ni ekwɛ̃ daa.

english: Is there an official government body in Ghana that regulates where farmers get oil palm planting materials?
ga: Ani nɔyeli nitsumɔhe ko yɛ Ghana ni kudɔɔ he ni okwaafoi lɛ náa mu ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ yɛ?

english: Yes, regulatory bodies like the Tree Crops Development Authority (TCDA) oversee the oil palm industry in Ghana to ensure that nurseries only distribute certified, disease-resistant seeds and prevent the spread of unapproved, low-quality planting materials.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛjianɔtoi ni kudɔɔ nibii tamɔ Tsei Ahe Nibii Ahe Nitsumɔhe (TCDA) lɛ kudɔɔ mu ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ Ghana lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ jaa dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ pɛ. ni atsĩ nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni bɛ odaseyeli ni bɛ he odaseyeli lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ naa.

english: Why do raw palm seeds take so long to sprout when I put them directly into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei dumɔwui heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Oil palm seeds have a thick, hard shell and a natural dormancy mechanism that protects the embryo. They require controlled heat treatment and specific moisture conditions in a professional nursery setting to break dormancy and sprout evenly.
ga: Oil palm dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni wa, kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni buɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Amɛbiɔ ni akwɛ amɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ tsɔne ni akɛkwɛɔ kooloi amli lɛ mli koni amɛha amɛwɔ shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ po.

english: Why do my young oil palm trees produce plenty of flowers but no fruit bunches form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Oil palms bear separate male and female flowers on the same tree. If there are not enough pollinators (like pollinating weevils) or if the tree is stressed by drought, female flowers fail to get pollinated and dry up without forming fruits.
ga: Mu tsei yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi yɛ tso kome nɔ. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ faaa (tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ) loo kɛji hɔmɔ miigba tso lɛ naa lɛ, Fɔfɔi yei lɛ nyɛŋ afee pollen ni amɛgbi ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Why does it take three to four years after planting for my oil palm tree to start producing harvestable fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu mu tsei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eheɔ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ dani ajeɔ nibii ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ afeemɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Oil palms use their first few years to build a deep root system, a sturdy trunk, and strong leaves. This foundation is necessary so the tree can support heavy fruit bunches consistently over its 25-to-30-year productive lifespan.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ dani amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. tso lɛ shishitoo ni wa kɛ baai ni wa Shishitoo nɛɛ he miihia bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ afii 25 kɛyashi 30 ni ekɛfeɔ nii lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my oil palm trees grow very tall quickly but only yield small, light fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ekomɛi daa oya shi amɛwoɔ yibii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: When palm trees are planted too close together or given excessive nitrogen fertilizer, they stretch upward competing for sunlight instead of building a thick trunk and storing energy for large, oil-rich fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo aha amɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo tsɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaama tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii kɛha aduawai wuji ni mu eyi mli obɔ lɛ, ŋmei tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ.

english: How far apart should I space my oil palm seedlings when I plant them in the field?
ga: Beni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ He enyiɛ esa akɛ makɛ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ awo mli?

english: Oil palms should be planted about 9 meters apart in a triangular pattern. Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough sunlight for its wide leaves without shading neighboring palms, which is essential for maximum yield.
ga: Esa akɛ adu mu tso lɛ yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 9, ni efee triangle. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha efoji ni mli kwɔ lɛ anɔ ni etsĩii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anaa. ni he hiaa koni anyɛ atsu nii babaoo

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or maize between my oil palm trees while the palms are still young?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mu tsei lɛ ateŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping with short-term food crops is beneficial during the first two to three years. However, tall or aggressive crops should be kept at a safe distance from the seedling so they do not block sunlight or steal nutrients from the young palm.
ga: Hɛɛ, be kukuoo mli nanemɛi ni akɛ niyenii tsei duɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni he baaba sɛɛnamɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ akɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ loo ni yɔɔ basabasa lɛ ato shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahe. Enɛ ji koni akatsi hulu la lɛ naa loo akaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young oil palm turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nutrients like potassium or nitrogen in the soil, or water stress during the dry season. The palm moves available nutrients to its newer top leaves to stay alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium loo nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. loo nu he haomɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: How does heavy rain affect how my oil palm trees grow and bear fruit?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa mu tsei lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛyibiiwoo he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Adequate rainfall gives oil palms the water needed to swell fruit bunches and absorb nutrients from the soil. However, prolonged heavy rain with low sunlight can reduce pollinator activity, temporarily slowing down fruit set.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ haa mu tsei lɛ náa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛgbala aduawai akui amli ni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ kɛ hulu la fioo pɛ baanyɛ aha pollinator nitsumɔ aba shi. ni ehaa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ be kukuoo mli

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees burn and turn yellow when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantain nearby creates a living umbrella that gives young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara lɛ baa.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds very close to each other to squeeze more onto my field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛmi dumɔwui babaoo awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close forces your maize to fight for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This competition leaves you with thin, weak stalks and small or empty cobs instead of a bigger harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ kɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ baaha oná tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei bibii loo ni bɛ nɔ ko yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni da fe no najiaŋ.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air to catch full sunlight with their leaves. Getting plenty of sun helps the plant make food and feed the tuber expanding under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni hulu la lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ amɛtso lɛ he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni efeɔ niyenii ni ehaa bulbs ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil. This natural food strengthens your soil and helps nearby maize grow greener and stronger without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ŋmãa ni ehe wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmãa kroko kɛfata he.

english: Why are my cassava tubers growing out small and woody instead of big and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot expand easily if planted in hard, packed soil or left too long in nutrient-poor ground. Loosening the soil well before planting gives the tubers room to grow fat and tender.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ alɛɛ mli oya kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ. aloo ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani adu lɛ, ebaaha bulb lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: When is the best time for me to put chemical fertilizer on my crops so it doesn't waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛkafite?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist right after a moderate rain, but not during heavy downpours that wash it away. Putting it close to the roots when crops are growing fast gives them maximum strength.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛwo shishifãi lɛ ahe beni tso lɛ miida oya lɛ, ebaaha ená hewalɛ babaoo.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops right after I clear my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie sleeping in the soil and sprout instantly when exposed to sunlight and rain. Clearing weeds early in the first few weeks gives your main crop a head start before weeds choke them.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛ. Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli jwɛi ni oookpa lɛ baaha onibii titri lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ dani jwɛi lɛ agbe lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves have tiny holes and light brown powder inside the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni powda ko ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on your crop. Spraying recommended treatments directly into the leaf center early in the morning or late evening kills the caterpillars before they destroy the cob.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛkpãtã tso lɛ ŋmei lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rot right before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering and a lack of calcium in the soil. Giving your plants a steady supply of water and adding compost or lime to your soil stops the fruit bottoms from blackening.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Okɛ nu awo tsei lɛ amli ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo lime awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni aduawai lɛ ashishi akafee ediŋŋ.

english: Why should I wait for regular rains to start fully before planting my seeds instead of planting after the first single rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ aje shishi dani madu dumɔwui moŋ fe ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first isolated rain can trick seeds into sprouting, but if a dry period follows immediately, your young shoots will dry up and die. Waiting for continuous rains ensures your sprouted seeds survive.
ga: Mra mli lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he kroko lɛ baanyɛ alaka dumɔwui ni amɛkwɛ̃. Shi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, Oshishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi. Nugbɔ ni yaa nɔ nɛɔ lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha odumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants keep dying when I plant them near certain big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ tsei wuji komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Some large trees have aggressive root systems that steal all the water and nutrients from the soil, while others release natural chemicals through their roots or fallen leaves that stop crops like cocoa from growing well.
ga: Tsei wuji komɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Mɛi krokomɛi hu jieɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ anɔ ni haaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if a shade tree on my farm is harming the crops underneath it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ awui?

english: If the crops directly beneath a specific tree are stunted, have yellow leaves, or dry up much faster than crops in other areas, that tree is likely competing too heavily for water, light, or soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ tso ko shishi lɛ egbɔjɔ, amɛbaai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ, loo amɛgbi oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ hei krokomɛi lɛ, Tso lɛ sumɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe awo nu, la, loo niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii mli.

english: Which trees are safe to keep on my farm to provide shade for my cocoa?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni esa akɛ mahi miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛha mikoo lɛ he ŋmɔlɔ?

english: Beneficial shade trees like Albizia or Terminalia (Emire) drop nutrient-rich leaves that feed the soil and have root systems that do not fight aggressively with cocoa for water.
ga: Tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ Albizia loo Terminalia (Emire) lɛ jieɔ baai ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni kɛ kookoo he tawuu kɛhaaa nu.

english: Do young cocoa plants need full sunshine or shade to survive?
ga: Ani hulu loo hulutsoo be babaoo he miihia kookoo tsei bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi?

english: Young cocoa plants need gentle, filtered shade because full sunlight burns their young leaves and dries out their shallow roots before they have a chance to grow deep into the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo ni mli jɔ, ni mli tse. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaa bibii lɛ ni eha shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ aba. Egbiɔ dani enáa hegbɛ ni edaa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings dry up right after the rainy season ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Without enough shade cover or organic matter in the soil, the sudden heat of the dry season causes young seedlings to lose water faster than their weak roots can draw it from the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Latsaa ni baa trukaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbala amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is stressed by too much harsh sunlight, poor root health from bad soil, or a lack of essential nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ mli

english: Should I cut down all the wild trees on my land before I plant cocoa?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ koo mli tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani madu kookoo?

english: No, clearing all trees leaves your land exposed to severe heat and soil erosion. It is better to keep select beneficial shade trees to maintain a cool, moist climate for young cocoa.
ga: Dabi, tsei lɛ fɛɛ ni ooojie lɛ baaha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli adɔ waa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Esa akɛ ato tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ koni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ aha kookoo bibii lɛ.

english: If a cocoa seedling dies on my farm, can I plant a new one in the exact same spot?
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ gboi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani manyɛ madu tso hee yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: You can replace it, but you should first correct the problem that killed the first plant—such as adjusting the shade level, digging out old dead roots, or enriching the soil with compost.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsake. Shi esa akɛ osaa naagba ni gbe klɛŋklɛŋ tso lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ, tamɔ bɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ tsakemɔ. Shishifãi ni egboi lɛ ni aaakumɔ loo aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo

english: What is the best time of year for me to replace dead crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaato ŋmɔshi nibii ni egboi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: The best time to replace dead plants is at the start of the main rainy season so the new seedlings get plenty of water to establish strong roots before the dry harmattan season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ atsake tsei ni egboi lɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui heei lɛ aná nu babaoo ni amɛkɛma shishifãi ni wa dani harmattan be ni egbi lɛ aba.

english: What should I add to the soil when I am replacing a dead seedling?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mikɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui ni egboi lɛ miitsake?

english: Mix rich topsoil with well-rotted compost or animal manure inside the planting hole to give the replacement plant extra nutrients and help the soil retain moisture during dry spells.
ga: Okɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ afutu ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔ bu lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii krokomɛi aha tso ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli

english: Why does choosing the right tomato variety matter so much for my farm in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato henɔ ni sa ni mihalaa lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: Different tomato varieties are bred for specific weather conditions, pest resistance, or crop uses. Choosing a variety adapted to local heat, heavy rains, or local market preferences prevents crop failure and ensures higher profits.
ga: Akwɛ tomato henɔi srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ naa. Nibii ni fiteɔ nii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii Tsei srɔtoi ni ahalaa ni kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee yɛ maŋ lɛ mli latsaa, nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa, loo maŋ lɛ jarayeli nibii ahe lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii akafite ni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔi babaoo aba.

english: Can I plant any tomato seeds inside a greenhouse, or do I need special seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tomato dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli? loo esa akɛ ekɛ dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi atsu nii

english: Greenhouse farming works best with special greenhouse varieties that grow tall continuously and thrive in controlled shade, whereas many open-field varieties grow like short bushes and do not produce well indoors.
ga: Greenhouse okwaayeli tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ greenhouse henɔi pɔtɛɛ ni yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akudɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi babaoo ni agbele naa lɛ daa tamɔ tsei bibii ni amɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shia mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a vegetable variety is good for planting during the rainy season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji akɛ aduawai srɔtoi lɛ sa akɛ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli loo esaaa?

english: Rainy season varieties are specially bred to resist leaf diseases, fungal rot, and flower loss caused by excessive rain and high humidity.
ga: Akwɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli tsoi srɔtoi yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo baa helai. fungal rot hela kɛ fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛbaa lɛ.

english: Why do some of my crops have shallow roots while others root deep into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Root depth depends on the crop type, how hard the soil is, and watering habits. Hard or compacted soil and frequent light watering keep roots near the surface, while loose soil and deep watering encourage roots to grow deep.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ amlibotemɔ damɔ tso lɛ henɔ nɔ. Te shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ha tɛŋŋ? kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ sui Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ fioo Bei pii lɛ enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ abɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ nu ni mli kwɔ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ.

english: How do shallow roots affect how often I should water my tomato plants?
ga: Te shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ saa shii abɔ ni esa akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ nu lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops with shallow roots cannot reach deep soil moisture, so they dry out quickly in the sun and need smaller, more frequent watering to stay healthy.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ. ni ebiɔ ni afɔ lɛ nu fioo kɛ shii abɔ koni ená hewalɛ kpakpa.

english: How deep do I need to clear and plow my soil before planting vegetable seedlings?
ga: Te ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni mafo mli dani madu aduawai dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: Loosening soil 20 to 30 centimeters deep allows tender young roots to easily spread out, gather nutrients, and firmly anchor the plant against heavy winds.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Bua niyenii mli hewalɛ naa ni okwɛ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he

english: What causes the roots of my crop to rot, and how do I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni haa midumɔ nii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: Root rot occurs when water sits in the soil for too long without draining, suffocating the roots. Adding organic matter and ensuring proper soil drainage keeps roots healthy and strong.
ga: Shishifãi fitemɔ baa kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it better to water my crops lightly every day or deeply a few times a week?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu fioo daa gbi loo ooowo nu babaoo shii fioo komɛi yɛ otsi mli?

english: Deep watering a few times a week encourages roots to stretch deep into the soil searching for water, making the crop stronger and more drought-resistant than daily shallow watering.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli shii fioo komɛi yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛtao nu. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe wa ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ hɔmɔ fe nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ daa gbi.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how can it protect my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-vegetables lɛ ahe?

english: A greenhouse is a plastic or mesh frame structure that shields delicate crops like tomatoes from harsh direct sunlight, heavy downpours, and destructive pests, creating a safe climate for better yields.
ga: Greenhouse ji plastic frem loo ŋshɔŋloo ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he waaa, tamɔ tomato, kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe. Bɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha nitsumɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In intense midday heat, leaves lose water faster than shallow or young roots can pull it up from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself until temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ loo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baagbo be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are foreign buyers so strict about buying only healthy, clean cocoa from Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ mli wa waa yɛ kookoo ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ni amɛheɔ kɛjɛɔ Ghana lɛ he lɛ?

english: Foreign buyers treat cocoa not just as sweet food, but as a healthy product and medicine that helps prevent serious diseases like cancer. Because people consume it for health benefits, buyers insist on strict quality standards to ensure it is clean and safe.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ buɔ kookoo akɛ jeee niyenii ni ŋɔɔ kɛkɛ. Shi eji hewalɛnamɔ he nibii kɛ tsofa hu ni yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai ni mli wa tamɔ kansa naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, gbɔmɛi yeɔ kɛhaa amɛhewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ bɔ ni nibii lɛ hi ha lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ehe atse ni ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cocoa get rejected if I dry the beans near smoke or dirty places?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpooɔ mi-kooko lɛ kɛji migbi mi-kooko lɛ mli yɛ he ko ni lasu loo he ko ni muji yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa beans act like a sponge and easily soak up bad smells, chemical fumes, and dirt. Because cocoa is processed into food and medicine for consumers abroad, any bad smell or dirt ruins its quality and makes it unsafe to eat.
ga: Cocoa yibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni eŋɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ gbonyo, tsofa lasu, kɛ muji oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, afeɔ kookoo niyenii kɛ tsofa kɛhaa mɛi ni yeɔ yɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ehiii loo muji No hewɔ lɛ, nɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi ni ehaa ebɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ayeɔ.

english: Why do extension officers warn me against using just any chemical pesticide on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ bɔɔ mi kɔkɔ akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi akatsu nii yɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Chemicals sprayed on cocoa can soak into the beans inside the pod. Since cocoa is consumed as food and medicine, chemical residues can cause harm to human health, leading international buyers to reject the crop.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kookoo nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ kɔfe yibii ni yɔɔ tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, akɛ kookoo tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛ tsofa. No hewɔ lɛ tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye adesa hewalɛnamɔ awui. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, maŋsɛɛ jarayelɔi miikpoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What does it mean when buying companies say they want to track where my cocoa beans came from?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ ooohe nitsumɔhe ko ni ekɛɛ amɛmiisumɔ ni amɛkwɛ he ni mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ jɛɔ lɛ?

english: International buyers use special tracking systems to follow cocoa beans from the exact farm where they were grown to the final country buying them. This proves to health-conscious consumers that the cocoa was grown safely without harmful chemicals or illegal forest clearing.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ gbɛjianɔtoo krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛtaoɔ nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ni aduɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashi naagbee maŋ ni amɛheɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ maa mɛi ni yeɔ nii ni kwɛɔ amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ mi akɛ, aduɔ kookoo shweshweeshwe ni tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ fataaa he.

english: How does careful handling during harvest make my cocoa beans more valuable?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ tsu nii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa waa?

english: Careful harvesting keeps the pod free from dirt, fungus, and damage. Healthy pods produce pure, high-quality beans rich in natural health properties, which commands better interest and prices from international buyers.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa muji, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. Pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii krɔŋŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli. ni enine eshɛ miishɛɛ kɛ jara babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their leaves and produce small pods when the sun is too severe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ni amɛmiiwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni hulu la lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ

english: Cocoa trees naturally thrive under shaded, humid conditions. When the sun is too strong, the plant drops leaves to save water, leaving it with less energy to nourish and grow big cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ hulu la lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ ni akɛbaakwɛ kookoo ŋmeii wuji lɛ anɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does black pod disease spread so fast across my farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a water-loving fungus. Rain drops splash the fungus from infected pods and wet ground onto healthy pods, so proper pruning is needed to let air in and keep the pods dry.
ga: Fungi ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni afolɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do I need to ferment my cocoa beans under plantain leaves for several days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ plantain baai ashishi gbii babaoo dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Fermentation kills the life inside the bean so it does not sprout, and it unleashes the rich chocolate flavor and beneficial natural nutrients that make the cocoa valuable to health-food makers.
ga: Fermentation gbeɔ wala ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Ehaa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔ waa kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ hu. Enɛ haa kookoo he hiaa mɛi ni feɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ.

english: Over many years, cocoa trees pull nutrients out of the soil to build pods. If the soil is not refreshed with proper organic matter or nutrients, the soil becomes tired, causing the tree to yield fewer pods.
ga: Afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ, Cacao tsei jieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo niyenii ni sa nɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ etɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why is it unsafe to store my dried cocoa beans in the same room where I store fertilizer or fuel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ebɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ baato tsu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo fuɛl toɔ lɛ?

english: Dried cocoa beans contain natural oils that quickly absorb strong chemical vapors from diesel or fertilizers. Storing them together spoils the flavor and destroys the clean, medicinal value of the cocoa.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli fɔji ni shwieɔ tsofai ni mli ewo wu ni jɛɔ diesel fuel loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ oya yɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ to he kome lɛ, efiteɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo mli lɛ, ni efiteɔ tsofa ni he tse ni yɔɔ kookoo mli lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my crops so they reach the big size buyers in the market prefer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Koni ashɛ jarayelɔi wuji ahe yɛ jara ni ataoɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops show clear physical signs when mature, such as yellowing leaves for cassava or drying silks for maize. Waiting for these full maturity indicators ensures your tubers or grains reach maximum weight and size, which commands higher prices from Ghanaian market women.
ga: Tsei jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛha ŋmei. loo siliki ni egbi kɛha ŋmãa Nɛkɛ nibii ni tsɔɔ akɛ eda lɛ ahe mɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni o-bulbs loo dumɔwui lɛ ashɛ shwiili kɛ dalɛ ni fe fɛɛ he. Enɛ haa yei ni yɔɔ Ghana jarayelihe lɛ jara yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow so much faster after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya waa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer supplies essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that act as food for the plant. Just like good food helps children grow strong, fertilizer enables crops to develop thick stems, broad green leaves, and roots faster.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa tsei. Taakɛ niyenii kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa gbekɛbii ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ, Fertilizer yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa ŋmeii ni mli wa. baai eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi oya

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they face heat stress, lack enough water, or suffer from nutrient imbalance in the soil. Without consistent moisture and balanced feeding, the plant self-protects by discarding flowers it cannot afford to turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejaaa ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ni hulutsoo be fɛɛ be kɛ niyenii ni ja bɛ Tsei buɔ amɛhe kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni anyɛɛɛ atsɔ aduawai ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my pepper leaves to curl up, and how can I tell if my plant is sick?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela mɔ mitso lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from under the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies. You can identify the problem by inspecting the underside of leaves for small moving spots or sticky residue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Obaanyɛ ona naagba lɛ kɛtsɔ baa lɛ shishi ni oookwɛ koni ona hei bibii ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Aloo muji ko ni shwieɔ shi yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Why are insects eating holes in my cabbage leaves, and how does it affect the crop's growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te enáa tsei adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Pests like the diamondback moth caterpillar feed on leaves, which are the plant's food factories. When leaves are destroyed, the crop cannot capture sunlight effectively, leading to stunted heads or total crop failure.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ diamondback ŋmeii yeɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii nitsumɔhei lɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ fite lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ amɔmɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ kwraa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shading the young cocoa trees and retaining soil moisture while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce tiny tubers when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight over limited soil nutrients, water, and space. Giving cassava enough distance allows the root system to expand freely and absorb enough food to develop thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ he ni faaa lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha ŋmei lɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛŋɔɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee ŋmei ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds make my maize plants turn yellow and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your maize roots. Without enough nutrients, the maize leaves lose their deep green color and cannot grow to full height.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-corn shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Abɛi baai lɛ hu fiteɔ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhe.

english: During intense afternoon heat, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can pull water from the soil. The leaves temporarily droop to conserve moisture, but they will bounce back once the sun sets if the soil has enough deep water.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Shi ebaaku esɛɛ kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting quickly after I dig them out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rotting usually happens when yam tubers get scratched or bruised during digging, creating openings for fungi and bacteria to enter. Storing them in warm, unventilated spaces speeds up this decay, so careful harvesting and cool, airy storage are essential.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii baa kɛji akɛ atswa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ loo atswa amɛ yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ. Enɛ haa gbɛ ko gbɛɔ kɛhaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ koni amɛbote mli. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo he ko ni hulu tsoɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛfite oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia.

english: How do I know if the insects on my crop are actually harming my plants or helping them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ miiye mitsei lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ loo amɛmiiye amɛmiibua amɛ?

english: Not all insects are bad; some like ladybugs eat harmful pests. You know pests are damaging your crop when you see chewed leaves, tiny holes, sticky spots, or curling leaves.
ga: Jeee kooloi bibii fɛɛ ehiii. Kooloi komɛi, tamɔ ladybugs, yeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara. O le kaa koolohi nɛ a gbeɔ ní ɔmɛ ngɛ o ngmlɛfia ɔmɛ a hɛ mi kpatae ke o na tsohi nɛ a ngma, bu nyafii, hehi nɛ a ngma, aloo tsohi nɛ a ngma.

english: Why are my pepper leaves rolling up and shrinking instead of spreading wide?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mites or aphids feeding under the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in overly shady, wet, and humid conditions during the rainy season.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine, hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why are the roots of my okra plants forming big swollen knots under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni efuu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Swollen knots on roots are caused by tiny microscopic worms in the soil called nematodes that attack the plant's roots, making it hard for the crop to drink water and absorb food.
ga: Kpoji bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni efuu lɛ baa. ni tutuaa tsei ashishifãi Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaanu nu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food, or that excessive water in the soil is suffocating the roots so they cannot feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛna niyenii.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my farm than my young cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe mi-cassava tsei lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally aggressive and spread quickly, so they steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before your slow-growing cassava crop gets a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ mli wa waa yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani o-yucca ni daa blɛoo lɛ náa hegbɛ ni ekɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay soft and loose instead of forming tight, firm balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee bɔɔlu ni mli wa ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form firm heads if they are planted too close together, face intense hot weather, or do not get enough water and nitrogen food during their main growth stage.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni wa kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ waa kpeɔ loo nu kɛ nitrogen niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni enine shɛɛɛ nɔ yɛ dalɛ be lɛ mli

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant before they can turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot and dry, or when the plant is stressed by hot winds, poor water supply, or insect attacks.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Aloo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tswa tomato tsei lɛ. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ ehiii. loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ

english: What makes my watermelons crack open right before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-watermelons lɛ fãa dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: Watermelons crack when they receive a heavy burst of water or rain after a long dry spell, causing the sweet inside of the fruit to swell faster than the outer skin can stretch.
ga: Watermelons tswaa kɛji akɛ amɛbote nu loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ. Enɛ haa tso yibii lɛ mligbɛ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why are my orange trees dropping young green fruits onto the ground before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ miifɔ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ashwie shikpɔŋ dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop young fruit as a reaction to severe water shortages, lack of proper soil food, or damage from fruit flies laying eggs inside the green oranges.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii akɛ hetoo kɛha nu ni faaa waa. Niyenii ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nɔ ni jɛɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ citrus tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Officer, why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow from the bottom up while the crop is still young?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your plant is hungry for nitrogen fertilizer or is stressed by waterlogging. The plant moves nitrogen from older leaves to feed the new top leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, otso lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo eyɛ haomɔ kɛjɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight because their leaves are tender and burn easily. Shade trees act as living umbrellas that keep the seedlings cool, conserve soil moisture, and protect them until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni obu he kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa

english: What causes my pepper plant leaves to curl up tight and stop growing flowers?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper tsei lɛ miibɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛmiikpa fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or thrips that feed on the sap, or by a viral disease they transmit. When plants lose sap, the leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ mli Kɛ́ tsei amli nu lɛ fite lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nutrients from the soil, especially nitrogen. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally restores nutrients to the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Legumes tamɔ tsina kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.
