english: Why shouldn't I spread my chemical fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ashwieɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain downpours wash away loose fertilizer off the topsoil before plant roots have time to soak it in. It is better to apply fertilizer after light rain when the soil is damp so it dissolves directly near the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛŋɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe

english: I noticed my cassava plants grew very tall green leaves, but why are the tubers underneath so small when I harvest?
ga: Miyɔse akɛ mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni kɛlɛ waa. Shi mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or given too much nitrogen, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems competing for sunlight instead of storing food in the underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo aha lɛ nitrogen babaoo Tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛye hulu la he akaŋ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I need to make high mounds in the soil before planting my seed yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee gɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to expand downward easily. Mounding softens the ground, allows water to drain so tubers do not rot, and gives the root plenty of room to grow big and thick.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa kɛya shi mlɛo. Muji ni abua naa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo. Ehaa nu hoɔ kɛjeɔ kpo. No hewɔ lɛ, yitso lɛ fiteee. Ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ babaoo koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping all their flowers onto the ground instead of growing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ amɛshwie shikpɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when they face heat stress, extreme dry soil, or excessive humidity. Without the right balance of water and mild temperatures, the plant cannot complete pollination and drops the blossoms to survive.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, loo fɛ̃i babaoo kpe. Kɛji akɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo be ni esaaa lɛ bɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Tsei nyɛŋ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwie fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does seed maize saved from my last harvest give me smaller cobs than the certified seeds I buy from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi naagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred for strength and high yields in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose that special vigor, resulting in weaker plants and smaller cobs in the next planting season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster on my farm than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive in harsh conditions with very deep roots and thousands of dormant seeds hiding in the soil. When you clear the land, sunlight triggers these wild seeds to germinate faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ waa kɛ dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ shi ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Hulu la lɛ haa nɛkɛ koo mli dumɔwui nɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Officer, why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying when I plant them in a field with no tall trees around?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to heat and full sunlight. Without shade trees or food crops like plantains to block direct sun, the leaves burn easily and the soil dries out faster than the roots can absorb water.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains ni baatsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa bɛ lɛ. Baai lɛ shãa oya ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them earlier in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi maŋkpa moŋ?

english: During the hottest parts of the day, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it up from the ground. As long as the soil remains moist, the plant usually recovers in the late afternoon when the temperature drops.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ he baajɔ amɛ yɛ shwane mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that grows big tubers under the soil. Staking holds the leaves high off the damp ground where they get more sun and airflow, which also protects them from rotting.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. he ni amɛnáa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo yɛ Enɛ hu buɔ baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green foliage. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient out of the topsoil, or waterlogged soil can prevent the roots from taking it up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nɛkɛ niyenii kpakpa nɛɛ he kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbala niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: My cassava plants have tall stems and lots of big leaves, so why are the tubers under the ground so small?
ga: Mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai wuji waa. Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or rainfall early on, it uses most of its energy to grow leaves and stems above ground. Because all energy went into foliage, very little was left over to build thick, starchy roots.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen loo nugbɔ babaoo nɔ yɛ shishijee mli Ekɛ ehewalɛ babaoo baatsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa baai lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ eshwɛ ni baanyɛ afee shishifãi ni mli tse ni mli edɔ.

english: What is causing ragged holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the center leaves of my growing maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the central funnel of the plant. They feed on tender young leaves during the day, leaving behind ragged holes and waste as the leaves unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii yɛ gbi mli. Amɛshiɔ bu ni etsilɛ kɛ sũ ni efite beni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why are the fresh leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mites, thrips, or whiteflies feeding on the underside of the leaf. It can also be a sign of a viral infection carried by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii, thrips, loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Ebaanyɛ efee hela ko ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɛ lɛ he okadi hu.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before producing any actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or irregular watering. When stressed by severe weather, the plant drops its blossoms to conserve energy and water for survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ nɔ. Kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii nyɛ amɛnɔ lɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does my main plantain stem give me small bunches if I leave all the young shoots growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? kɛha mi kɛji mishi tsei bibii fɛɛ ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ.

english: The young shoots, or suckers, share the root system with the main plant. When too many suckers grow at once, they compete with the main stem for food, light, and water, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii loo tsei bibii kɛ tso titri lɛ jaa shishifã gbɛjianɔtoo kome. Beni ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ Amɛkɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, la, kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do my bean pods turn moldy and rot on the farm if I don't harvest them before heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean pods lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji mikpaaa amɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Bean pods need warm, dry conditions to dry naturally on the plant before harvest. Rain during the drying stage gets inside the dry shells, creating moisture that causes the seeds to mold, sprout early, or rot.
ga: Bean pods biɔ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi koni egbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa dani akpa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be mli ni egbiɔ lɛ boteɔ ŋshɔŋloo ni egbi lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya loo amɛgboiɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to build strong green leaves. It can also happen if heavy rains have washed the nutrients too deep into the soil for the roots to reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni aná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsi niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I place chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is full of strong salts that will burn and damage the plant stem and sensitive surface roots if placed directly against them. It is best to place fertilizer a few inches away in a circle or line where feeder roots can safely reach it.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baashã ni efite ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ eyi ŋmeii amli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo he ko ni kɛ jɛmɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi yɛ kooyigbɛ loo line mli he ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker when I plant the exact same crop on the same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests and diseases that prefer that specific crop to build up in your land.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ nakai tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I do not leave bigger shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji mishiii tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under full, direct sunlight. Taller shade trees protect the seedlings from high heat, keep the soil moist, and shield them from strong winds while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ baaye abua ni ebu dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he beni eji bibioo lolo lɛ.

english: Curling and wrinkled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap underneath the leaves, which stresses the plant and stops normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ekpaa baai lɛ adalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my yam vines yield bigger tubers when I train them to climb up wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ naa bulbs wuji beni mitsɔseɔ amɛ koni amɛkwɔ tso tso ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking raises the yam leaves higher off the ground so they catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make more food, which is then sent down into the ground to grow a larger tuber.
ga: Staking baawó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ nɔ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii babaoo. No sɛɛ lɛ, atsuɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ koni efee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I need to cut away extra suckers growing around my plantain stool?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Stool lɛ miije kpo.

english: If too many suckers grow at once, they compete with the main plantain stem for food and water. Removing extra suckers ensures that all nutrients go toward producing a large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida shikome lɛ, Amɛkɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ yaa ni ewoɔ aduawai wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the heat is too high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. This stress prevents the flower from pollinating correctly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ la lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollin jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil and helping neighboring crops like maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele lɛ, ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, usually between 9 and 12 months after planting depending on the variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ daa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni eshiɔ tso ni nɔ ko bɛ mli Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my young maize seedlings die right after sprouting out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ gboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Millipedes hide in damp soil and chew through the tender stems of young sprouts at night, cutting them off at the soil line before the leaves can grow.
ga: Millipedes kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ ni amɛyeɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛkɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani baai lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do I see small round holes and nibble marks on my cassava tubers when I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? Ni ŋmɔtɔ he okadii ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ beni mifoɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Millipedes burrow into the ground during wet periods to feed on soft root tubers, leaving small holes that cause the roots to rot early.
ga: Millipedes lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ edɔ koni amɛye shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. ni ekɛ buji bibii ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya lɛ baa

english: Why is overwatering my vegetable patch harmful to the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni mikɛwoɔ mi aduawai tsei lɛ amli fe nine lɛ yeɔ mi tsei lɛ ashishi awui lɛ?

english: Consistently wet soil creates an ideal damp environment that attracts millipedes, which gather around plant bases and begin feeding on wet crop stems.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mli ejɔ ni gbalaa millipedes koni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛje shishi amɛye tso lɛ shishifãi ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I see so many small coiled worms crawling around my crop roots when the soil stays wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Mɛi babaoo shwieɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ.

english: Those are millipedes, which thrive in moist soils; while they usually eat decaying plant matter, heavy soil moisture makes them multiply and start attacking healthy plant roots.
ga: Amɛji millipedes ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ bei pii lɛ amɛyeɔ tsei amli nibii ni egboi moŋ, Shi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ni amɛjeɔ tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ tutuamɔ shishi.

english: Why should I clear away dead plant debris and old bush cuttings before planting my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei ni egboi kɛ tsei aniji momoi dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Decaying vegetation creates a breeding ground for millipedes, so clearing land reduces their population before your new crop seeds start to sprout.
ga: Tsoi ni efite lɛ bafeɔ he ni millipedes lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha gbɔmɛi ayibɔ aba shi dani dumɔwui heei aje shishi akwɛ̃.

english: Why is it unsafe to heap thick leaf mulch directly touching the stems of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ebɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaato ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa ni mli tse ni kɛ tomato tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Thick wet mulch right against stems provides daytime shelter for millipedes, allowing them to easily nibble and damage the plant stems at night.
ga: Mulch ni mli ewo fɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ masɛi lɛ baaha millipedes lɛ aná he ko yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛbaaye tsei ashishifãi ni amɛfite amɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea seeds fail to germinate when I mix un-rotted plant manure directly in the seed holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ tso mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteee lɛ futuɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Undecomposed plant matter attracts millipedes to the planting hole, where they eat the soft, germinating seeds before they can push through the soil.
ga: Tso mli nibii ni efiteee lɛ baagbala millipedes kɛba dumɔ bu lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ dani amɛshwieɔ amɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my groundnuts get eaten under the soil if I wait too long after they mature to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ayeɔ mi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ beni amɛdara sɛɛ dani mikpa amɛ?

english: Leaving mature pods in damp soil invites millipedes to pierce the pods and feed on the soft nuts inside.
ga: Ni aaashi ŋmeii ni eda yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ Enɛ baaha millipedes lɛ atsɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛye ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my sweet potatoes develop black spots and rot while still growing in the soil mounds during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potatoes lɛ náa ŋmeii diji ni amɛgboɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli lolo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain drives millipedes into crop mounds, where they nibble on sweet potato skins, creating wounds that allow moisture and rot to set in.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ tsirɛɔ millipedes kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Amɛyeɔ sweet potato lɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa pilamɔi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ boteɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my seed yams get small bites on their skin before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ amɛhewolo nɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Millipedes feed on the tender skin of growing yam tubers underground, especially when organic matter in the soil runs low.
ga: Millipedes yeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahewolo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I have to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking holds the yam vines up so the leaves can catch maximum sunlight to build a large tuber underground, while keeping the foliage off damp soil reduces disease.
ga: Akɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ aaawo tso mli bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ koni efee shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni eye ebua ni helai aba shi.

english: Allowing too many shoots to grow causes them to steal food and water from the main plant. Pruning extra suckers ensures the main plant produces large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives crops their dark green color and energy to grow, so applying top-dressing fertilizer can solve this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: How does planting cowpeas help make my farm soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground through their roots. When the plant decomposes after harvest, it leaves natural fertilizer in the soil.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ tsei fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp, but avoid applying it right before a heavy rain, as heavy downpours will wash the plant food away before the roots can take it in.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni ooowo amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ he. Enɛ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ laaje dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: How can I tell if Fall Armyworms are destroying my maize leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ Fall Armyworms miifite mi ŋmãa baai lɛ?

english: Look for ragged holes on the leaves and a sawdust-like material inside the central leaves of the plant. If you look closely, the caterpillars also have a light inverted 'Y' mark on their head.
ga: Taomɔ buji ni etse yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ nibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ. Kɛ okwɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ hu yɛ ‘Y’ okadi ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ eyitso nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies. Controlling these insects early stops them from spreading viruses that deform the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ helai ni haa baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ amɛshwã.

english: What makes my cassava roots rot in the soil before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifo amɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them without draining away properly. Planting on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to run off and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. ni enyɛɛɛ ejie nu jogbaŋŋ Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when the soil gets too dry, temperatures become extremely hot, or the plant lacks key nutrients. Regular watering helps protect the blooms.
ga: Tomato baafɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. He ni mli edɔ waa loo tsei bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi ahe.

english: Why should I leave dried grass and crop leaves on top of my field instead of burning them before I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi jwɛi kɛ baai yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ dani madu?

english: Covering the soil with dried plant materials, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, traps moisture so your crops do not dry out quickly, and slowly turns into organic matter that feeds your soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Eŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni onibii akagbi oya ni fiofio lɛ etsɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize immediately after the very first rain of the year falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often a false start followed by hot, dry weather. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout and then dry up and die before the real rainy season begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ji amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baa.

english: Can I plant cowpeas between my rows of maize, or will the cowpeas steal food from my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ? Aloo tsina ŋmeii baaju niyenii kɛjɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: Planting cowpeas with maize actually helps your farm. Cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and release it into the soil, which feeds the maize plants and improves their growth.
ga: Cowpeas ni akɛ ŋmãa baadu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua oŋmɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa tsei ni ehaa amɛdalɛ yaa hiɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I cut down all the large shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are easily burned by strong direct sun. They need shade trees or plantain plants above them to protect them from heat and keep the surrounding air moist while they grow.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo drapei ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he, ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why should I trim off the broad top leaves of a new plantain sucker before I plant it in my garden?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ dumɔwui heei lɛ anɔ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ dani madu amɛ yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Trimming the large leaves reduces the amount of water the plant loses into the air, allowing the fresh sucker to focus its energy on growing strong roots in its new home.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ baai wuji lɛ, ehaa nu ni tso lɛ shwieɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa suckers heei ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida yɛ amɛshia hee lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops suddenly full of ragged holes with small worms hiding inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ eyi kɛ buji ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that feeds on the central leaves of maize. Identifying it early helps you treat it before it destroys the growing point of the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ. mra be mli ni ayɔseɔ Enɛ baaye abua bo ni otsa lɛ dani efite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn dark brown and rot away during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called late blight, which thrives in wet, cool weather. Spacing your plants wider allows wind to dry the leaves faster and slows down the disease.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blight kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i mli Kɛ́ ashi gbɛ babaoo yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aha baai lɛ agbi oya ni ebaaha helai aje shishi.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my maize so that the heavy rains do not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mawo ŋmãa koni nugbɔ ni naa wa akanɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not flooded, doing the first application about two weeks after planting and a second top-dressing when the plants reach knee-height.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ aaafee otsi enyɔ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli shii enyɔ nɔ beni tsei lɛ eshɛ amɛnaji ahe lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up with yellow patches, and why are the tubers under the ground so small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ?

english: Your cassava has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. The virus weakens the leaves so they cannot produce enough food to grow large tubers.
ga: O ŋmei lɛ yɛ ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Virus lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to use tall wooden stakes to guide my yam vines up off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mikɛjie mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves into the air using stakes exposes more of the leaves to sunlight. Sunlight helps the leaves produce energy, which goes back down into making bigger, heavier yam tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tso ko wo sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛtee kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. Enɛ yaa sɛɛ kɛyaa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the young pods on my cocoa tree turning black and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly during rainy and humid weather. Clearing bush around the trees and removing infected pods helps keep air moving and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ latsaa be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ yaa nɔ etsɔɔ mli ni ehaa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ kpaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves the strength to turn green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara oya.

english: How does planting groundnuts help improve my soil for next season's crop?
ga: Te ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts are special legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. After harvest, that left-behind nitrogen feeds the next crop you plant, like maize or cassava.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmei krɛdɛɛ ko ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. kpamɔ sɛɛ Nakai nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Covering the soil, which is called mulching, keeps the hot sun from drying out the ground too quickly. It holds moisture near the roots, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa, ni atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ haaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa ni ebɔle amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the sap. Spraying the undersides of the leaves with neem oil mixture helps drive these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nu lɛ numɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ ni akɛfutu mli lɛ shwie baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eshwie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight with their leaves. Sunlight helps the leaves produce food, which travels down to swell and grow large yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaji lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi kɛbaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato tuber agbo ko

english: What causes holes in the middle leaves of my corn and tiny droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa baa teŋgbɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibioo ko ni shwieɔ shi yɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar eating the growing center of the corn. Dropping a little clean sand or applying safe neem extract into the leaf funnel early in the morning controls them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Okɛ ŋã ni he tse fioo loo neem mli nu ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe awo baai lɛ amli leebi koni okɛkudɔ enɛɛmɛi.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other in a row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stems and tiny or empty corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the crop is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for growth. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or planting leguminous crops like cowpeas in the soil beforehand helps keep the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri kɛha dalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he loo odu ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani be shɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my yam farm produce tall vines with many leaves but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ wain tsei kakadaji ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: Giving yams too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of tubers below. Using a balanced fertilizer rich in potassium and staking the vines properly encourages bigger tuber growth.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen wo sweet potato mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii ni akɛwo wain tso lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii wuji lɛ adara.

english: Why do my groundnut plants grow well even when I do not add heavy chemical fertilizers to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ? Ni mikɛ tsofai ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fataaa he?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can pull nitrogen directly from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. They naturally make their own food, so they require very little added fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni etsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhooɔ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and getting yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting improved, disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings recommended by extension officers prevents this disease from destroying your yield.
ga: Enɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi, ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava niji ni asaa ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ taakɛ extension nitsulɔi lɛ wo ŋaa lɛ baaye abua ni hela nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are under stress from dry weather or when damaged by pests like mirids (capsids). Protecting the farm with shade, retaining soil moisture, and spraying against mirids helps the flowers mature into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ miihao amɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ efite lɛ, ebuɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛ hulutsoo Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi Ni pollen ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains turn into fine powder after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ batsɔ powda kpakpa beni mikɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grain weevils bore into stored maize to lay eggs, and their young eat the inside of the grains. Thoroughly drying your maize in the sun and storing it in airtight bags or treating it with safe storage dust protects the grain from insects.
ga: Dumɔwui ŋmeii shwieɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli koni amɛwo wɔji. ni amɛbii lɛ yeɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli. Gbimɔ ŋmãa kɛtsɔ hulu ni oooha egbi lɛ nɔ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ okɛwo vacuum kotoku mli loo okɛto he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. Muji lɛ buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds and heavy rain come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches at the top, making them top-heavy. Mounding soil around the base of the plant (earthing up) and supporting the main stalk with a strong wooden prop stick keeps them standing.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ panicle ni mli wa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. make it top heavy Shikpɔŋ ni abɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi (shikpɔŋ) kɛ tso ni wa ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔɔ shi.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my young crops when the weeds are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛdarako kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients your crops need to survive. Clearing weeds early stops them from strangling the young plants during their critical early growth phase.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa amɛkagbeɔ tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mra be mli dalɛ bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli.

english: Why does the soil around my garden plants dry out so fast even after I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ daa leebi po lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water quickly to evaporation under direct sunlight. Covering the bare soil around your crop plants with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool and traps moisture longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni okɛwoɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) atsu nii koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark, rotten spots on the bottom end before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering and a lack of calcium in the soil. Maintaining steady soil moisture and applying agricultural lime to the soil prevents these black spots from forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa kɛ calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ okwaayeli mli ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ duŋ nɛɛ akafee.

english: If I spray pest chemicals on my cabbage or tomatoes today, how many days must I wait before harvesting them to sell or eat?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie kaabe loo tomato nɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ, Gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ nikpamɔ lɛ koni ahɔ̃ɔ loo aye?

english: Chemicals need time to break down inside the plant so they do not harm consumers. This waiting time is called the withdrawal period, and respecting it ensures your crops are safe to eat and meet market standards.
ga: Tsofai ahe miihia be dani amɛfite yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ koni amɛkaye mɛi ni heɔ lɛ awui. Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ mɛmɔ be nɛɛ akɛ be ni akɛjieɔ nii. Ni bulɛ ni oooha be nɛɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ ni eshɛ jarayeli he mlai lɛ ahe.

english: What happens to my crops if I spray strong chemicals on them when they are not actually sick?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni mli wa shwie nɔ be mli ni amɛshwieee nɔ? Ni akɛ tso lɛ hela mɔɔɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Misusing or applying chemicals unnecessarily can scorch crop leaves, kill beneficial insects that protect your field, and cause pests to become resistant to the chemical so it will not work when a real disease strikes.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ loo ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni he ehiaaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ahe baai lɛ ashã. Gbemɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni buɔ oŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nyɛɔ tsofai ahe No hewɔ lɛ, etsuuu nii kɛ́ hela diɛŋtsɛ ko yɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning pale white and yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tseee kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When crop leaves lose their green color and turn white or yellow, it usually shows that the plant lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or it is suffering from a fungal disease that stops it from making food.
ga: Beni tso baai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ ni amɛtsɔ eyɛŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo eyɛ fungal hela ko ni haaa eye niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and stop growing during the warm season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa dalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is typically caused by tiny pests like whiteflies sucking sap from the leaves, or a virus spread by those insects when the plant is stressed by hot and dry weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmei mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmei mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ miigba tsei anaa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die if I cut down all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mifo tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. They require partial shade from larger trees or nurse crops like plantains to keep their tender leaves cool and preserve moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni kwɛɔ nɔ, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛha baai bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into narrow tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rolling leaves is a plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss through evaporation during intense heat, helping the crop survive short dry spells.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ shi kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli ni hulu lɛ egbi.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing huge green leaves but failing to give me any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewooo pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to put all its energy into growing tall stems and leafy foliage instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Why do traders at the market reject my harvested tomatoes even though they are big and red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ jara lɛ nɔ lɛ kpoo tomato ni mikpa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛdara ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ?

english: Traders reject crops that are harvested too soft or treated with chemicals right before market because they rot quickly during transport and can carry chemical residues that make buyers unsafe.
ga: Jarayelɔi kpooɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa beni amɛdarako tsɔ loo akɛ tsofai ewo mli dani amɛshɛɔ jara nɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛ amɛ tee gbɛfaa mli, ni ekolɛ tsofai ni eshwɛ ni haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ bɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ yɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to heap my harvested cocoa beans and cover them with plantain leaves for a few days before sun-drying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibuaa kookoo yibii ni akpa lɛ anaa ni mikɛ plantain baai haa nɔ gbii fioo komɛi dani mikɛwoɔ hulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering cocoa beans allows them to undergo natural fermentation, which develops the chocolate flavor, changes the bean color from purple to brown, and ensures buyers accept the crop.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii amli. ni haa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔ lɛ Seed su tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ purple kɛyaa brown mli. ni eha nɔmimaa akɛ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ baakpɛlɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does planting beans or groundnuts in the same farm make my maize crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa mi-abele lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and lock it into the soil, acting as a free natural fertilizer for neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: If I secure a land lease for 20 years, which crops make the most sense to plant for long-term profit?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ ha afii 20 lɛ, mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu koni maná sɛɛnamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ?

english: Perennial tree crops like cocoa, oil palm, or cashew are ideal for long-term leases because they take a few years to mature but will yield continuous harvests for decades, giving you maximum return on your long-term land investment.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ afii babaoo tamɔ cocoa, oil palm loo cashew nuts lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be kakadaŋŋ mli nibii ni akɛhaa ejaakɛ amɛheɔ afii fioo pɛ dani amɛdaraa. Shi ebaaya nɔ ewo yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Enɛ haa onáa shika ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Can I plant short-term food crops like plantain or cassava alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii ni yeɔ be kukuoo, tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava or plantain with young cocoa helps maximize land use in the early years. The plantains provide necessary shade for the young cocoa trees, while food crops give you income before the cocoa starts producing.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei loo plantain ni akɛ kookoo bibii duɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii babaoo yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. Plantains haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ haa onáa shika dani ajeɔ kookoo feemɔ shishi.

english: Why do my crops stop producing heavy yields after several years on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛhi shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Crops continuously pull nutrients out of the earth. Over time, the soil becomes depleted, so without adding organic manure, fertilizer, or letting the land rest, crops will naturally produce less fruit.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baawo yibii fioo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does my maize look green and healthy in one area of my field but yellow and weak in another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fã ko mli lɛ? Shi eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ he kroko.

english: Soil quality and water retention vary across a single farm. Yellowing usually signals a lack of nitrogen or waterlogging, showing that different parts of your land require tailored soil care.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ nu ni ahiɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ loo nu eyi mli obɔ. ni tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ fãi lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do crops grow much better when I till the land deeply before planting instead of dropping seeds into hard soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ dani midu yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Tilling breaks up hard ground so crop roots can easily spread out, access oxygen, and absorb underground water and nutrients required for strong early growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. nine shɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa nɔ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha gbɔmɔtso lɛ dalɛ kpakpa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shishijee mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under full direct sun. They need shade trees or fast-growing plantains above them to act as living umbrellas and maintain moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni daa oya yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Wild weeds are naturally adapted to quickly claim bare soil and full sunlight. Crops need dedicated clearing, weeding, and initial care because they require more resources to establish themselves.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ ni ajie amɛ, ajie jwɛi, kɛ shishijee kwɛmɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná nibii babaoo koni amɛkɛto amɛhe shi.

english: Why do my crops drop their flowers and stop fruiting during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Severe dry winds and heat cause plants to shed flowers to preserve internal water and survive. Mulching the soil and providing shade helps crops hold moisture through the dry period.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ haa tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ toɔ nu amɛmli ni amɛhiɔ shi. Mulching kɛ shade yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing sunlight and air to circulate freely through the tree. This prevents fungal diseases and directs the plant's energy into growing pods instead of excess leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii ahe helai anaa ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli moŋ fe baai ni fa fe nine lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crop is suffering from too little water versus too much water in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli, ni nu hu fa tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When crops lack water, their leaves wilt, curl, and dry up. When soil has too much standing water, leaves turn yellow and stems become soft or rotten because the roots are suffocating from lack of air.
ga: Beni nu bɛ tsei ahe lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo. Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shishifãi lɛ baafee blɛoo loo amɛbaafite ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient, or the soil has become waterlogged from heavy rain, which stops the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kpaa mumɔ kɛ niyenii yeli.

english: What is eating small holes into the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa gbekɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing center (funnel) of the maize plant and feed on soft new leaves before the plant can fully develop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei (cones) lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa, ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii heei dani tsei lɛ daraa kwraa.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water during long rainy periods. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away and keeps the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up into the light and keeps them off the damp soil where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ la he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ni jɛmɛ ji he ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot and dry or when the plant lacks consistent water. Without enough moisture and mild temperatures, the flowers cannot set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu daa Kɛji hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi ni esaaa bɛ jɛmɛ. Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the leaves. They transmit plant viruses that cause the leaves to wrinkle and stunt overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛ tsɔɔ tsei amli helai ni haa baai shwieɔ shi ni amɛ tsiɔ dalɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my vegetable crops grow thin and weak if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, forcing them to stretch tall and weak instead of growing strong.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ waa.

english: The dry Harmattan wind pulls moisture out of cocoa leaves faster than the roots can pull water from the dry soil. The tree drops its flowers and young pods to conserve water and survive.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha wala ahi shi.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas work with friendly soil bacteria to take nitrogen from the air and trap it in their roots. When the plant dies, that trapped nitrogen fertilizes the soil naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔmɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nitrogen ni emɔ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my mature plantain plants easily fall over during heavy rains and winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots carrying a heavy stem. If soil pests like microscopic worms (nematodes) or root weevils damage those roots, the plant loses its anchor and topples easily.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tsei ni tsii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii bibii (nematodes) loo shishifãi amli ŋmeii fite nakai shishifãi lɛ. Tsei baanyɛ afite amɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ oya ni amɛkumɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow even though I give them plenty of water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa lɛ nu babaoo daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Just like people can drink too much, crops can get overloaded with water. Too much water drowns the roots by blocking oxygen in the soil, which leads to root rot and turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Taakɛ gbɔmɛi baanyɛ anu dãa babaoo lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ekolɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hu yɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Nu babaoo baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: If I double the amount of chemical fertilizer I put on my tomato plants, will they grow twice as fast?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ falɛ toi enyɔ wo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, Ani mi-tomato tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya fe tsutsu lɛ shii enyɔ?

english: No, crops have a strict limit on how much nutrient food they can process at one time. Adding too much fertilizer burns the roots and hardens the soil, which stunts growth or kills the plant.
ga: Dabi, tsei yɛ husui ni mli wa yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu he nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaashã shishifãi lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ akpa dalɛ loo ebaaha tso lɛ agbo.

english: How do I know the correct percentage of chemical to mix with water when spraying my cassava field for pests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofai oha mlijaa 100 ni sa ni esa akɛ akɛ nu afutu mli kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ miifɔ ŋmɔji amli?

english: Chemical sprays work within safe limits. If the mixture percentage is too low, the pests will not die; if it is too high, the chemical will burn the plant leaves and ruin the harvest.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ husui ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe mli. Kɛji akɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mlijaa oha mlijaa 10 lɛ faaa tsɔ lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ gbooo. Kɛji etee ŋwɛi tsɔ lɛ, tsofai lɛ ba shã tso lɛ baai ni efite ŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I clear away all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle intense direct sunlight. They need temporary shade from trees or crops like plantain to protect them from heat and conserve soil moisture during their early growth.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my yam seeds very close together so I can fit more on my small plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi koni manyɛ makwɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ?

english: Crops need a set amount of space to feed. Planting too close forces roots to fight over water and soil nutrients, resulting in smaller, weaker tubers.
ga: He ko he miihia tsei koni amɛye nii. Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ bafeɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra green leaves from my tomato plants if they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo baai eŋɔli ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli kɛji amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ?

english: When a crop grows too many leaves, it spends all its food energy maintaining the greenery instead of growing fruit. Pruning extra leaves helps direct nutrients into producing larger tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ tso ko yɛ baai babaoo tsɔ Ekɛ eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii. Baai ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa niyenii mli hewalɛ koni ewo tomatoi wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and drying out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni egbi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural stress response when tiny insects like aphids or thrips feed on the sap underneath the leaves, stealing the plant's food and moisture.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli beni kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. Koni amɛju niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tsei amli

english: Why do weeds in my maize field make my main crop look thin and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha mi ŋmãa titri lɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively for the same water, light, and soil nutrients as your crops. When weeds take over, your main crop starves because its supply of essentials is stolen.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ kɛ nu, la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii he akaŋ waa tamɔ bɔ ni otsei lɛ feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ jwɛi ye Oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ anɔ hɔmɔ ejaakɛ aju nibii ni he hiaa waa.

english: Why do my crops refuse to grow in one part of my farm even when I add fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpooɔ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: The soil in that spot may be too acidic or sour. When soil acid crosses a certain limit, roots are unable to absorb fertilizer nutrients until agricultural lime is added to balance the soil.
ga: Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nakai he lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ loo edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ acidity ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fe husu lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli niyenii kɛyashi be mli ni akɛ lime baafata he koni ekɛha sũ lɛ afee ekome.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the ground if I plant immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain usually wets only the top layer while the deep soil stays hot and dry. Seeds need steady, continuous soil moisture to sprout, otherwise they get trapped in the dry heat and decay.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ pɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni egbi. Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni eyaa nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baakã la lɛ mli, amɛbaagbi ni amɛbaafite.

english: If I notice disease on just a few branches of my cocoa tree, why is it recommended to cut or uproot the whole tree?
ga: Kɛji mina hela ko yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ niji fioo komɛi pɛ anɔ lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ afolɔ kookoo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ loo ajie kɛjɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus spread throughout the entire system of the tree long before symptoms appear everywhere. Uprooting the infected tree prevents the disease from traveling through root contact or insects to infect surrounding healthy trees.
ga: Helai tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ mli fɛɛ be saŋŋ dani okadii lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ he fɛɛ he. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haaa hela lɛ atsɔ shishifãi ni akɛtswaa amɛhe loo kooloi bibii anɔ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: Will new cocoa seedlings get sick if I plant them in the exact same spot where infected trees were removed?
ga: Ani hela baamɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ni ajie kookoo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, new seedlings can easily get sick if infected roots or pests remain in the soil. You need to clear out all old root fragments and let the land rest before planting fresh seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui heei baanyɛ aná hela oya kɛji shishifãi loo kooloi ni yeɔ hela lɛ tee nɔ amɛhi sũ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ojie shishifãi momo lɛ fɛɛ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe dani odu dumɔwui heei.

english: How can I tell if a new disease that I have never seen before is attacking my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela hee ko ni minako dã miitutua miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Watch out for strange symptoms like swollen stems, unusual leaf discoloration, or pods rotting faster than usual. When you see strange patterns that regular farm care does not fix, contact an extension officer to inspect it early.
ga: Kwɛmɔ okadii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ tamɔ tso lɛ yibii ni efuu kɛ baai ni su tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ. Aloo ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ. Kɛji ona nibii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ daa lɛ nyɛɛɛ asaa lɛ, Na o-extension officer lɛ ni ekwɛ mra.

english: What key habits should I practice on my farm so I do not lose my crops to disease outbreaks?
ga: Mɛɛ sui titri esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Bɔni afee ni mikafite miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hela ni je shishi lɛ hewɔ?

english: Regularly inspect your crops, clean your farm tools so you do not carry sickness from tree to tree, remove diseased pods immediately, and clear thick weeds to keep airflow open.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli daa. Tsumɔ oŋmɔ mli nibii ahe koni okɛ helai akajɛ tso kome mli kɛya tso kroko mli. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni ojie jwɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: How do I protect my newly planted cocoa seedlings so they do not catch sickness while they are small?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-kookoo dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ ahe? Bɔni afee ni hela akamɔ amɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: Plant food crops like plantains alongside young cocoa to provide shade and reduce sun stress. Also, leave a barrier space between your new cocoa seedlings and any old cocoa farms nearby.
ga: Dumɔ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains yɛ cocoa tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni eha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi. Kɛfata he lɛ, shi gbɛ yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei kɛ kookoo ŋmɔji momo lɛ ateŋ. bɛŋkɛ

english: How do crop diseases move from my neighbor's farm into my own farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai jɛɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ mli?

english: Diseases travel through insects like mealybugs, wind, rain splashing off infected plants, contaminated tools, or even on farm workers' boots and clothes as they walk between fields.
ga: Helai tsɔɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ nugbɔ ni shwieɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. nibii ni mli ewo muji loo ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi atadei kɛ atadei po beni amɛnyiɛɔ ŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ.

english: How long should I wait after destroying sick cocoa trees before it is safe to plant fresh cocoa again?
ga: Beni mifite kookoo tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makwɛ kookoo hee shweshweeshwe ekoŋŋ?

english: It is best to wait several months to a year after clearing infected roots completely. Growing temporary non-cocoa crops during this waiting period helps break the disease cycle.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nyɔji babaoo kɛyashi afi beni ojie shishifãi fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Nibii ni jeee kookoo ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ mɛmɔ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ akumɔ.

english: What simple signs on my cocoa trees tell me that a disease is starting to take over?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mi akɛ hela miije shishi eba?

english: Look for yellowing leaf veins, red banding on young leaves, wilting during wet conditions, or unusual swellings on twigs and shoots. Early spotting allows you to take action before it spreads.
ga: Taomɔ kaadi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ mli linei. Ayɛ ŋmeii tsuji yɛ baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Egboɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. aloo fũu ni ejaaa yɛ tsei lɛ aniji kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ Mra ni anaa Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ofeɔ nɔ ko dani egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why does keeping my cocoa farm clear of tall weeds help prevent tree diseases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni jwɛi kakadaji ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akabote tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Tall weeds trap moisture and create a dark, warm environment where fungi and insect pests thrive. Keeping the farm clean allows sunlight and air to keep trees dry and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi kakadaji lɛ mɔɔ nu ni amɛhaa shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli edɔɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa yɛ. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why is it risky to plant new cocoa seedlings right next to an old, declining cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji momoi ni miibafite lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Old or dying cocoa trees often harbor hidden pests and viruses. Planting young seedlings right next to them makes it easy for pests to jump over and infect the young trees before they mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei ni egbɔ loo ni egboi lɛ hiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baatsɔ nɔ ni amɛye tsei bibii lɛ anɔ hela dani amɛdara.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa plants shaded and the soil cool while they get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa, ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa kookoo tso lɛ náa hɔnɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves near the bottom of maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which it needs to stay green. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen away from roots, so applying fertilizer like NPK or well-decomposed manure will keep the plant healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni esa akɛ ehi shi eŋɔli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves in dry weather to save water so they do not dry out completely. The plant is not dead; it rests until rain returns and then quickly sprouts fresh green leaves from its stems.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he koni baai lɛ akagbi kwraa. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ebaajɔɔ ehe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba. Ni baai eŋɔli heei lɛ kwɛ̃ oya.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get extremely hot or when the soil dries out completely. Ensuring your plants get regular watering and placing mulching grass around the base helps keep soil cool so flowers can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Kɛji okwɛ koni okɛ nu awo otsei lɛ amli daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground, catching more sunshine and preventing leaves from rotting on wet soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Egbalaa hulu la babaoo ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking leaf juices. Spraying infected plants early with recommended neem extracts or mild soapy water controls the insects and lets leaves grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Ni akɛ neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛshwieɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ mra loo nu ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ. Ebaaye kooloi bibii anɔ ni eha baai lɛ ada bɔ ni sa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them in heavy, soggy soil for too long. Planting your cassava on raised dirt mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily and keeps roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni efɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋmei nɔ lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ oya ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why do groundnut plants produce flowers above the dirt, but the actual nuts grow under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ, shi ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Once yellow groundnut flowers are pollinated, they grow long stalks called 'pegs' that bend downward and push themselves into the soil. The pods then grow safely under the dirt where they are protected from heat and birds.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei fɔfɔi ni ji yellow lɛ ebɔi pollination lɛ Fɔfɔi tso kakadaŋŋ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘peg’ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ebaakoto shi ni ekɛ ehe awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ adara shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ okpoi ahe lɛ shishi.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing loose, open leaves instead of forming hard, tight heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tso lɛ baa ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni agbeleɔ naa yɛ yitsei ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cabbage fails to form hard heads when planted too close together or given too much nitrogen fertilizer all at once. Proper spacing lets cool air circulate around each plant so a firm head can close up.
ga: Cabbage lɛ baafee ais kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ loo aha lɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ bɔleɔ he fɛɛ he. Tso fɛɛ tso baanyɛ No hewɔ lɛ yitso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ baanyɛ aŋmɛ.

english: Why does my cowpea crop produce plenty of bright flowers but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni kpɛɔ babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Tiny insects called flower thrips often attack and damage cowpea buds before pods can form. Inspecting flowers early and using proper pest control ensures the flowers turn into full pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ flower thrips lɛ tutuaa cowpea ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii. Fɔfɔi lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni kɛ akɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ fɔfɔii ni eyi obɔ.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars inside the central funnels?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ yɛ gbɛjegbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young maize leaves and growing points. Applying recommended bio-pesticides or organic solutions like neem oil early into the funnel destroys the pest before it destroys the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ neem fɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite kooloi lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites, or a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects with appropriate sprays early stops the leaf damage and allows new leaves to grow healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites, loo helai ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Okɛ tsofai ni sa akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra. Ehaa baa lɛ fiteɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa baa heei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth and green leaf development. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ kɛ baai eŋɔlii lɛ akwɛmɔ.
