Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that work with soil bacteria to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant harvested, those roots break down and naturally enrich the soil with free fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpa tsei lɛ Nakai shishifãi lɛ baakumɔ ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yes, cassava stems have growth buds that must point upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the shoots struggle to grow upward, which drains the plant's energy and results in a very poor tuber yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei tsei yɛ hiŋmɛii ni esa akɛ amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ hiɛ shi lɛ, Shoots lɛ baaná naagba yɛ amɛdalɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ hewalɛ afite. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii ni baa shi kwraa.

english: Why should I remove extra shoots or suckers growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie suckers loo shoots fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: Extra suckers compete with the main stem for water, light, and soil nutrients. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main stem gets maximum food to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantain.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yitso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii babaoo ni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when the Harmattan weather starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ harmattan kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are vulnerable to direct, scorching sunlight and dry winds. During severe heat or dry seasons like Harmattan, the plant drops its leaves to conserve water unless given shade from temporary nurse crops like plantain or shade trees.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ waa. Yɛ hɔmɔ loo hulutsoo be ni naa wa tamɔ Harmattan lɛ mli lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Ja amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves receive maximum sunlight. More sunlight allows the leaves to make more food, which travels down into the ground to feed and swell the developing yam tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛbai lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo mli. Hulu la babaoo haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo. ni gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ akɛ niyenii ni ehaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ mli lɛɛɔ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the roots pull calcium steadily up into the fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛya nɔ amɛgbala calcium kɛbote aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my newly sprouted vegetable nursery seedlings fall over and die right at the soil level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ miigboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is called 'damping-off,' a fungal disease that attacks tender stems at soil level when nursery beds are overwatered or poorly drained. Reducing watering and giving seedlings good airflow helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ ‘Damp’, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ beni nu eyi tsei akwɛmɔhei lɛ amli fe nine loo nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ ni aaatsi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni tsɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and thin roots that dry out easily. They need shade from taller plants like plantains to protect them from intense heat and conserve soil moisture during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like tubes during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl inward as a natural protective response to reduce their surface area, which slows down water loss and protects the crop from heat stress when the sun is very strong.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu hetoo koni ekɛba ŋwɛi he lɛ shi. Enɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛ́ hulu la lɛ mli wa waa.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge green leaves on top, but very small roots underneath the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy developing leaves and stems instead of storing food in the underground tuber roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why does planting beans in my field make my maize crop grow stronger in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmei lɛ daa waa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When the beans are harvested, this natural nitrogen stays behind to nourish nutrient-hungry crops like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shi koni ekɛha tsei ni niyenii he hiaa amɛ, tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing tall and thin instead of spreading out and making pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the seedlings compete with each other for sunlight. They stretch upward quickly to reach the light, making them tall, weak, and less able to produce healthy fruit pods.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut away the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie Plantain shishitoo lɛ

english: These extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for water and soil nutrients. Removing most of them ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Amɛkɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds make my young yam plants grow so slowly in their first few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young yam shoots and quickly steal essential sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before the yam roots can establish themselves properly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe sweet potato bibii. ni ejuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni he hiaa lɛ oya dani sweet potato shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ama shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off without forming fruits when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there are not enough insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ bɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up after tiny white insects appear underneath them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ kooloi bibii yɛŋ miibɔle amɛhe lɛ? lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ shishigbɛ

english: Tiny insects like whiteflies feed on the sap under the leaves and pass on viral diseases that distort leaf growth, stopping the pepper plant from developing food normally.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ whiteflies yeɔ baa mli nu ni amɛkɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni fiteɔ baa lɛ dalɛ baa. Enɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are fully mature and ready to be dug up from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves begin to turn yellow and dry up, and the inside shell of the pods develops dark brown or black spots.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Ni pod lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ.

english: If a crop variety was bred in a distant country like Thailand, will it still grow well on my farm here in Ghana?
ga: Kɛji akɛ afɔ tso henɔ lɛ yɛ maŋ ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ tamɔ Thailand Ani ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lolo yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Not always. Crops behave according to the climate, sunlight, and soil where they were bred. A seed bred in Thailand might struggle in Ghana unless our local weather, rainfall, and soil matches where it came from.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Tsei feɔ amɛnii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni adu amɛ yɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ Thailand lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni wa yɛ Ghana. ja jɛmɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ kɛ he ni ejɛɔ lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: If I get imported seeds brought in from Kenya, why might they grow differently on my land compared to local Ghanaian seeds?
ga: Kɛji minine shɛ dumɔwui ni akɛba kɛjɛ Kenya lɛ anɔ. Mɛni hewɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto Ghana dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Kenya has different land elevations, rainfall patterns, and temperatures compared to Ghana. Seeds react to these environmental factors, so an imported seed might flower at the wrong time or suffer from local pests that don't exist in Kenya.
ga: Kenya yɛ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ waa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ bɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ yɛ srɔto kɛ akɛto Ghana he. Dumɔwui tsuɔ shihilɛ mli nibii nɛɛ ahe nii. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ baanyɛ afɔlɔ yɛ be ni esaaa mli loo amɛná maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni bɛ Kenya lɛ.

english: What does it mean when an officer tells me a seed variety has been 'bred' for specific traits?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ maŋ onukpa ko kɛɛ mi akɛ ‘afɔ’ dumɔwui kɛha su pɔtɛɛ ko?

english: Plant breeding is like choosing the best animal parents for strong offspring. Scientists cross a plant that survives dry weather with one that produces large fruits so the new seed gets both good qualities.
ga: Tsei afɔmɔ tamɔ kooloi afɔlɔi ni hi fe fɛɛ ni ahala kɛha seshibii ni he wa. Jeŋ nilelɔi fɔɔ tsei ni nyɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa lɛ kɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii wuji. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui heei lɛ aná su kpakpai enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ

english: Why should I buy high-quality seeds when I can just get free seeds or save seeds from my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Mɛɛ be manyɛ maná dumɔwui ni aheee nɔ ko loo makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Free or saved seeds may lose their strength over time, yielding smaller harvests and catching diseases easily. Quality certified seeds are tested to give higher yields, grow uniformly, and resist pests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni bɛ nɔ ko loo ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo ni faaa kɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ oya. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛɔ koni ana yibii babaoo. shweremɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ nyɛmɔi ni teɔ shi ewoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ

english: Why do some free seeds given to us by programs fail to produce good yields on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni nitsumɔ lɛ kɛhaa wɔ ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ ekomɛi wooo yibii kpakpai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Free seeds are sometimes general varieties that are not matched to your specific soil type or local rainfall. They may also need special fertilizers or watering schedules that were not explained to you.
ga: Bei komɛi lɛ, dumɔwui ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ baanyɛ afee srɔtoi ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ kpãaa gbee. Ekolɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni atsɔɔɔ mli ahaaa lɛ he baahia amɛ.

english: Why do some crop varieties resist bugs easily while other varieties of the same crop get destroyed by pests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe oya yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ lɛ?

english: Certain bred varieties have natural traits—like thicker skins, bitter leaves, or tiny hairs—that deter insects, while unimproved varieties lack these built-in defenses.
ga: Henɔi komɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli sui tamɔ hewolo ni mli tse, baai ni mli edɔ, loo yitsɔi bibii. ni baanyɛ atsĩ kooloi bibii anaa yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni asaaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ bɛ hebuu ni akɛwo mli lɛ.

english: What makes crops grown for European export different from the ones I sell in our local market?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ni aduɔ koni akɛya maŋsɛɛ yɛ Europa lɛ afee srɔto yɛ tsei ni mihɔ̃ɔ yɛ wɔmaŋ jarayelihe lɛ he?

english: Export markets require strict uniformity in fruit size, shape, color, and zero chemical residues, whereas local markets are usually more flexible about minor cosmetic spots and varying fruit sizes.
ga: Jarayeli nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ biɔ ni aduawai lɛ adalɛ, amɛhefɛo, amɛhe su kɛ tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ akafee nɔ kome. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli hei lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ nibii bibii ni akɛsaa mɔ he kɛ aduawai adalɛi srɔtoi ahe.

english: How do I choose between a seed variety that yields heavily and one that buyers prefer for foreign export?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛkɛya maŋsɛɛ lɛ ateŋ?

english: A high-yielding local variety guarantees more crop weight to sell nearby, but export varieties sell at higher prices if you have a guaranteed export buyer and can meet their strict quality rules.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ haa anáa tsei tɔni babaoo ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ. Shi ahɔ̃ɔ srɔtoi ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ. Kɛji oyɛ mɔ ko ni baahe nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ ni obaanyɛ onyiɛ mlai ni mli wa ni kɔɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does the same seed variety grow tall and healthy on my neighbor's farm but remain small on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa ni ehiɛ wa yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli shi ehiɔ shi bibioo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops react strongly to micro-differences in soil nutrients, organic matter, shade, and water drainage. Even neighboring farms can have completely different soil quality that changes plant performance.
ga: Tsei feɔ amɛnii waa kɛji amɛna srɔtofeemɔi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ mli niyenii, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, hulutsoo, kɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ mli. Ekolɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ po yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa ni tsakeɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ.

english: Why do some seeds sprout quickly after planting while others take a very long time or die underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ́ adu lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi heɔ be kakadaŋŋ waa loo amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Seeds need the right balance of soil moisture, warmth, and planting depth to break open. Planting seeds too deep, using old seeds, or having dry soil stops the seed from having enough energy to sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ni amɛná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i, dɔlɛ kɛ dumɔ mlibotemɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ Dumɔwui momoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii Loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni yɔɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akaná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why should I clear the small trees and bushes on my land before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii lɛ? Yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Small trees and wild bushes compete with your planted crops for underground food, water, and sunlight. Clearing them gives your young crops enough space, light, and soil nutrients to grow strong.
ga: Tsei bibii kɛ koo mli tsei bibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ehaa otsei bibii lɛ náa he ko, la, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara waa.

english: Is it helpful to leave my farmland to rest for a full year before planting crops on it again?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mahã midumɔi lɛ ajɔɔ amɛhe afi muu fɛɛ dani madu amɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, leaving land to rest allows the soil to naturally rebuild its lost plant food and moisture from previous harvests, which helps your next batch of crops yield much better.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ahaa ejɔɔ ehe lɛ haa enyɛɔ etswaa tsei aniyenii kɛ nu ni elaaje kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baaye abua ni onibii ni obaakpa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ aba yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: What happens to my seeds if I plant them in hard soil without breaking it up first?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ ni mikɛ amɛ tswaaa klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Hard soil makes it very difficult for young plant roots to push through and search for water and food. Loosening the soil helps roots spread easily and grow deep.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei bibii ashishifãi akɛ amɛaabote mli ni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ.

english: Why is it better to start tree crops in a nursery before moving them to my main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe dani mikɛ amɛ aya miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A nursery protects weak young seedlings from harsh sun, strong winds, and hungry pests while they are small, ensuring only healthy and strong plants get moved into your main farm.
ga: He ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, kɛ kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa oŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to move my young seedlings from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ majie dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: It is best to transplant early in the morning or late in the evening when the sun is cool. This stops the young plants from losing too much water and wilting in the heat.
ga: Esa akɛ adu amɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulu la lɛ mli ejɔ. Enɛ baatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite nu babaoo ni amɛkagbo yɛ latsaa be mli.

english: Why do my young tree seedlings die when I plant them in full sunshine without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young tree seedlings have small roots and delicate leaves that burn and dry out quickly under direct hot sun. They need temporary shade from larger plants or leaves while their roots establish.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei loo baai wuji adɛŋ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ tswaa amɛhe lɛ.

english: What will happen if I plant my crops too close together on the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight with each other for sunlight, rain, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with tall, skinny plants that produce very little yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nugbɔ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crops turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are lacking vital food from the soil like nitrogen, or the soil has too much trapped water that is suffocating the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli, loo akɛ sũ lɛ emɔ nu babaoo mli, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ.

english: Why do extension officers cut off extra small branches from growing fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ shwieɔ tsei niji bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ani okpa tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ adumɔ?

english: Cutting off extra or weak branches helps the tree direct all its energy and soil nutrients into making big, healthy fruit rather than feeding unnecessary leaves.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ewo yibii wuji ni mli wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooye baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ

english: Why do my crops wilt when I water them in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering under hot afternoon sun causes the water to evaporate quickly before roots can absorb it, and hot water near the topsoil can shock the tender roots. It is better to water early in the morning.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpokpo shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Ehi akɛ oooha nu leebi.

english: Why are my mango trees dropping so many of their flowers before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Mango trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but they drop them if they experience stress from prolonged dry spells, heavy rains, or attack by tiny insect pests like thrips. Ensuring consistent soil moisture and protecting flowers from insects helps more blossoms turn into healthy fruit.
ga: Mango tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi amɛbaa shi kɛji amɛna haomɔ ni jɛɔ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips mli baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ tsɔɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my mango tree give me a massive harvest one year, but almost no fruits the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei woɔ yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ afi kome mli lɛ? Shi afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, eshwɛ fioo ni nɔ ko kwraa baajɛ mli aba?

english: This pattern is called alternate bearing. Producing a huge load of fruits exhausts the tree's stored food energy and nutrients, causing it to rest and rebuild its strength the following year before it can produce heavily again.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ style nɛɛ akɛ bearing ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ. Tso lɛ yibii babaoo ni ewoɔ lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni tso lɛ eto lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni etswaa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli dani enyɛɔ ewoɔ yibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender like babies and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Leaving taller shade trees or planting plantains provides shade and keeps the moisture in the soil, which helps the young cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao bibioo lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ tamɔ gbekɛ nɔ, ni eshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ oshi tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when I leave many shoots growing around the main stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ feɔ bibii bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: The extra shoots, or suckers, fight with the main plantain tree for nutrients and water in the soil. Pruning away the extra suckers allows the main tree to get all the food it needs to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei ni fa lɛ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo tsei agboi ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are a sign that the crop is hungry for nitrogen fertilizer or that the soil is holding too much stagnant water. Giving the plant nitrogen or draining excess water helps leaves turn green and produce healthy maize ears.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmãa loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ha tsei lɛ loo ajie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ebaaha ŋmãa toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my land make my next crop of maize grow much stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa waa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans have special root systems that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth. When the cowpea leaves and roots decay, they leave this natural fertilizer in the soil for the next crop to feed on.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛ ko ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji cowpea baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aye.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves high into the air to catch sunlight, which the plant uses to make food and grow large tubers underground. Vines left on the ground stay shaded, get wet, and are easily attacked by pests and diseases.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi koni amɛyamɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ. Akɛ tsei lɛ hoɔ nii ni amɛduɔ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Wein tsei ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baafee hulutsoo, ŋmɔtɔ, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baatutua amɛ oya.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings sprout quickly while others rot in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekomɛi daa oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings need healthy nodes and moist, soft soil to sprout. Stems cut from old, weak, or diseased plants, or stems planted upside down, cannot draw nutrients properly and rot before sprouting.
ga: Yucca tsei ni afo lɛ he miihia fãji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Afolɔ tsei ni egbɔ, ni bɛ hewalɛ, loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli tsei, loo ni akwɛ̃ɔ amɛyitso. Amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfite dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the air gets excessively hot or when the plant suffers from sudden dry soil. Without consistent moisture and moderate heat, the flowers dry up before insects or wind can help them form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi trukaa lɛ, tso lɛ naa amanehulu. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni tamɔ ekome kɛ dɔlɛ ni sa bɛ. Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni ato tomatoi lɛ ama shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly and stopping the plant from growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath. Controlling these insects early allows the plant to stretch out its leaves and resume normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛbaai lɛ jajeɔ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I avoid applying fertilizer on my farm when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers must dissolve in water for roots to safely absorb them. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil concentrates the chemicals, burning and damaging the crop's tender root tips instead of nourishing them.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shweshweeshwe. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baaha tsofai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eshãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ ni efiteɔ amɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it harmful for me to water my crops in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ehiii kɛhaaa mi lɛ?

english: Watering under strong afternoon heat causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before reaching the roots. Droplets left on the leaves under intense sun can also cause leaf burn or encourage plant fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli edɔ waa wo mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai anɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã loo ewo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large broad leaves that act as natural shade, protecting the young cocoa plants and keeping the soil cool and moist during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ oya. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen away from the root zone, so applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shishifã lɛ mli lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot rapidly drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii komɛi oya. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ shwereɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do I need to use bamboo stakes to lift my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋmei tso awo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to catch light; lifting the leaves off the ground exposes them to maximum sunlight so the plant can produce more food, which results in much larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná la. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ fe fɛɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves in dry weather to save water and protect themselves from drought. This is normal behavior, and the plant will grow new leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Enɛ ji subaŋ ni afɔɔ feemɔ. ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do groundnut plants need soft, loose soil after they flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he hiaa ŋmei tsei beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they form growing stems called 'pegs' that bend down and push into the soil. Loose soil allows these pegs to bury themselves easily to form the underground nuts.
ga: Beni afee ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ pollen sɛɛ lɛ, Efeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa ewaa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baafu amɛhe, ni amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off due to stress caused by high temperatures, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulching to keep roots cool helps the flowers stay on.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ haomɔ ni hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings suddenly collapse and die at the soil level in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ gbee shi trukaa ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This collapse is caused by a fungal disease called 'damping-off,' which thrives when seedbeds are kept too wet and crowded. Spacing out your seeds and avoiding overwatering will protect the young stems.
ga: Nɛkɛ gbeekpamɔ nɛɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Damping’ lɛ mli, ni ehiɛɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛji he ni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ni aaaha amɛtse amɛhe ni ajie nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni akatsi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why are weeds so damaging to my crops during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop sprouts are weak and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures all available food in the soil goes straight to your young crop.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yaa otsei bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to be dug up, and what happens if I leave it in the ground too long?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ? Ni mɛni baaba kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months when lower leaves yellow and shed. If left in the ground for too long, the roots turn hard, woody, and lose their starch quality.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ, be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛbaafee tsei, ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: When the lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, the crop is lacking nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the younger top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara, ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for next season's crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas work with beneficial bacteria in the soil to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil naturally when the plants decay.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni tsei lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or sudden dry spells. The plant discards the flowers to conserve energy and save its own life.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhere amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Plantains grow fast and wide, providing living shade umbrellas that protect cocoa plants during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo nɛɛ ji nɔ ni buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines onto tall wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants store food in underground tubers by catching light through their leaves. Lifting the leaves up on poles helps them catch maximum sunlight, which results in larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ niyenii toɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛtsɔ la ni amɛmɔɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ yɛ tso ko nɔ lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ naa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ agboi.

english: Why do my crops stay thin and weak when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, while their leaves fight for sunlight, causing all of them to stay small and yield less.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ miitswa akaŋ Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii baa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Too much rain fills all the air spaces in the soil with water. Without air, the cassava roots drown, starve of oxygen, and become vulnerable to fungal rot organisms in the soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ baagboi, amɛnaŋ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa, ni amɛbaafee oshara akɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaje mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants turn dark and dry up right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: High humidity and rain create ideal conditions for fungal diseases like late blight. Raindrops splash microscopic fungus spores from the soil onto the lower leaves, causing them to turn black and die.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. ni haa efeɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ.

english: Why am I finding ragged holes in my young maize leaves and small caterpillars inside the central funnels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni etse yɛ ŋmãa bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ? yɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm. The adult moths lay eggs on young leaves, and the caterpillars crawl into the central funnel of the plant to feed where it is hidden and safe from heat.
ga: Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akpɔlɔi ni eda lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai bibii anɔ. Ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛyatao niyenii yɛ hei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni hulutsoo lɛ bɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my main crops after a fresh rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ hee sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with aggressive root systems naturally adapted to the local soil. They absorb available water and fertilizers faster than cultivated crop varieties.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ koo mli ni eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni ekɛ ehe ebɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ he. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya fe tsei srɔtoi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my mango tree flowers fall off without turning into full fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango fɔfɔi lɛ shwieee shi lɛ?

english: Mango flowers drop mainly because of pest attacks like thrips, fungal diseases caused by wet weather, or a lack of moisture in the soil. Pruning the tree to let in sunlight and watering at the base during dry snaps helps keep the blossoms intact.
ga: Mango fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi titri yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ thrips, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ tutuamɔ hewɔ. aloo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni hulu la aba mli, ni awo lɛ nu yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I stop small worms from ruining my mangoes while they are still on the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ ŋmeii bibii ni mifiteɔ mi mangoi lɛ anaa be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Those worms come from fruit flies that lay eggs under the skin of young mangoes. Setting up local fruit fly traps using plastic bottles and lures, or destroying fallen fruits immediately, stops the flies from spreading to healthy crops.
ga: Maggots lɛ jɛɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ mango bibii ahewolo shishi lɛ amli. Akɛ plastic tsinsii kɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛmɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli aduawai amli ŋmeii. loo efite aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing big leaves but not forming a hard round head in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi ebɛ yitso ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form heads when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer or during periods of extreme heat. Balanced feeding and making sure the crop gets steady moisture helps the leaves curl tightly into a head.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ afee yitsei kɛ́ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli loo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Niyenii ni ja ni akɛaaha tso lɛ ni akwɛ koni tso lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ po lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ abɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa.

english: What is eating tiny round holes into my cabbage leaves and how can I stop it naturally?
ga: Mɛni ye bu bibioo ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? yɛ mi-cabbage baa lɛ nɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Those holes are made by caterpillars like the diamondback moth larvae. Spraying a mixture of ground neem seed water mixed with a little soapy water onto the leaves acts as a natural deterrent that keeps worms away.
ga: Nakai buji lɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii, tamɔ diamondback ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ neem dumɔwui amli nu kɛ nu fioo ni akɛ samla efutu mli lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Why are the bottoms of my young tomatoes turning dark brown and soft before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom end rot, which happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and adding compost prevents this problem.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly upward during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often the plant's way of conserving water when it is hot and dry, but it can also be a sign of a virus carried by whiteflies. Mulching the soil and managing whiteflies helps keep tomato plants stress-free.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni abɔleɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Shi ebaanyɛ efee hela ko ni whiteflies hiɛɔ lɛ he okadi hu. Mulching kɛ whitefly nɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni tomato tsei lɛ akafee nɔ ni haoɔ amɛ.

english: Is it better to start my moringa farm using seeds or by cutting branches from an old tree?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaaje moringa ŋmɔ shishi kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo tsei momoi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ amli?

english: Moringa grows easily from both. Branch cuttings grow much faster and produce leaves sooner, but plants grown from seeds develop deeper roots that survive harsh dry seasons much better.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ aaakwɛ Moringa kɛjɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ daa oya kwraa ni amɛwoɔ baai oya. Shi tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yeɔ hɔmɔ ni naa wa lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: How should I cut my moringa leaves so that the tree keeps producing fresh leaves quickly?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mafo Moringa baai lɛ koni tso lɛ awo baai heei oya?

english: Prune the main stem and side branches when they reach shoulder height instead of plucking individual leaves. Cutting branches encourages the plant to branch out and produce double the fresh leaf shoots.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ esɛɛ niji lɛ kɛji amɛshɛ tsitsi nɔ moŋ fe ni ooojie baai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko. Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ niji ni ewoɔ ŋmeii heei ni fa fe tso lɛ shii enyɔ.

english: Why are my vegetable crop leaves turning pale yellow even though I water them every single morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean you are giving too much water, which smothers the plant roots and prevents them from taking up plant food from the soil. Let the surface soil dry slightly between waterings so roots can breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ooha lɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii. Ha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi fioo yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why is it a bad idea to plant tomatoes in the exact same spot where I harvested cabbages last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ aaadu tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikpa kaabe yɛ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy feeding crops like cabbage strip specific nutrients from the soil and leave behind pests. Rotating your beds by planting leguminous crops or root crops after leafy vegetables gives the soil a rest and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tsei ni awoɔ amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, tamɔ kaabe lɛ, baajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli ni amɛshi tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kɛ́ atsake saatso lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ asɛɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he jɔɔ lɛ ni ehaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct tropical sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out the topsoil. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or leaving selected canopy trees provides protection and holds soil moisture until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo tsei bibii ni ahala lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he ni ehi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: How do I know the proper spacing to leave between my maize plants during planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni kã ŋmãa tsei ateŋ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each maize plant gets enough sunlight, soil moisture, and nutrients. When planted too close together, crops compete for food, resulting in thin stems and small, poorly filled corn cobs.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa he lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa hulu la. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛji adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baatswa niyenii he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli tseee ni ŋmãa lɛ mli tsei lɛ hu ji bibii ni ekɛ amɛhe wooo mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without turning into hot peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop mainly due to extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of beneficial insects like bees to pollinate them. Consistent watering and encouraging pollinators near your farm helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa kɛha pollination. Nu ni oooha amɛ daa ni owo pollinators ni bɛŋkɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Can manually transferring pollen between flowers help me get more produce from my farm?
ga: Ani pollen ni mikɛ niji tsɔɔ fɔfɔi ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni minine shɛɔ nibii babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, hand pollination ensures that female flowers are fully fertilized, especially when wild insect pollinators are scarce. Doing this regularly can significantly increase the total count and size of fruits harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ haa fɔfɔi yei lɛ fɔɔ fɔmɔ kwraa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Kɛ́ ofee enɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha yibii ni obaakpa lɛ ayibɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields when I plant maize on the exact same plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Maize continuously drains specific nutrients, particularly nitrogen, from the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and keeps the land fertile.
ga: Abele shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi be fɛɛ be. Titri lɛ, nitrogen ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii.

english: Why are my cassava tubers small and woody even though the leaves look large and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii ni amɛji tsei eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: Excessive foliage usually means the soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium. Potassium is the specific nutrient crops require to expand their underground tubers and roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai babaoo tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo shi potassium faaa. Potassium ji niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛ amɛshishifãi.

english: How can I tell if my cassava crops are infected with cassava mosaic disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ emɔ cassava mosaic hela?

english: Infected cassava plants show twisted, curled leaves with patches of yellow or light green. The disease stunts plant growth, leading to very low tuber yields.
ga: Cassava tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni ebɔle amɛhe ni ji ŋmɔŋ loo eŋɔli ni mli tse. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa. Enɛ haa tuber yibiiwoo baa shi waa.

english: Why are my tomato plants suddenly wilting and dying even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by fungal or bacterial wilt in the soil, which blocks the plant's internal tubes so water cannot reach the stems and leaves, regardless of soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo muawai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni tsiɔ tsei amli paipii lɛ anaa Nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ahe. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji

english: Why do certified hybrid seeds give better harvests than seeds I save from my previous crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsu nii tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred for higher yields, uniform growth, and disease resistance. Saved seeds lose these strong traits over time, resulting in weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. shweremɔ ni tamɔ ekome kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: What causes my yam tubers to rot in the ground right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Yam rot in the ground is usually caused by waterlogged soil that traps excess water around the tubers, allowing soil-borne fungi and bacteria to multiply and decay the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa, ni no ŋmɛɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ he kɛbɔleɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe, ni no haa ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong sunlight or heat on their own. They need shade from nurse crops like plantains to keep the soil moist and cool until the trees are mature enough to handle full direct light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa loo dɔlɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná la tɛ̃ɛ fɛɛ.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers from my field to plant in a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Look for 'sword suckers' that have narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad base. These grow much faster and produce stronger bunches than 'maiden suckers' which have broad leaves right from the start.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante tu’ ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ. Enɛɛmɛi daa oya kwraa ni amɛwoɔ panicles ni he wa fe ‘tso bibii’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ.

english: Staking gets the leaves up off the hot ground into the air and light. This allows the yam leaves to catch maximum sunlight to make food for the roots, while preventing leaf diseases caused by damp soil.
ga: Staking haa baai lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ he ni edɔ lɛ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la mli. Enɛ haa sweet potato baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛha shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ baa helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and tiny green droppings inside the shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai amli ni ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on your maize. They hide inside the center whorl of the plant during the day and eat the soft leaves, which weakens the stalk and reduces corn yield.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ miiye o-corn lɛ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads through excess water droplets and high humidity. Pruning thick foliage and removing infected pods early helps air flow through and stops it from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji black pod hela, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nu ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo nɔ. Baai ni mli tse ni afoɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni ebaatsi enaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot and smell bad underground before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fite ni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi dani mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long without draining away, or from soil-borne fungi. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain so the roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is low on food for my crops without taking it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli nibii ni haa miduɔ nii lɛ faaa ni mikɛyaaa laboratori?

english: If older leaves at the bottom of your crops start turning pale yellow while the top leaves stay green, or if crop stalks remain thin and stunted, your soil is running low on essential nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. aloo kɛji tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni egbɔjɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the first rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit naturally in the soil for months waiting for moisture. They have adapted to sprout instantly with the first rain and take nutrients quickly, which is why early weeding is needed to give your crop seeds a head start.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo, ni amɛmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ba pɛ kɛkɛ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni oha odumɔwui lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into any fruits during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, the pollen inside tomato blossoms dries out and dies before it can fertilize the flower. Providing shade or adequate watering during extreme heat helps keep flowers intact.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔ. Kɛ́ aha fɔfɔi lɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni sa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do I harvest smaller corn cobs when I plant my maize seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaa ŋmãa bibii lɛ be mli ni adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each crop plant enough personal space to grow strong stalks and full cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why should I test my soil before planting my crops every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka mishikpɔŋ lɛ makwɛ dani madu tsei daa afi lɛ?

english: Testing your soil before every planting season tells you what nutrients are already in the ground, so you don't waste money buying the wrong fertilizer or adding too much.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ baatsɔɔ bo niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni ofite shika ni okɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo mli.

english: When is the best time for me to take soil samples from my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ maŋɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to take soil samples is right before you prepare the land for a new planting season, so you know the exact nutrient state of your soil before putting seeds in the ground.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko atsu nii ji dani osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be hee lɛ. Enɛ ji koni ole niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shihilɛ pɔtɛɛ dani okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do I correctly collect soil from my farm to check its nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabua sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ koni makwɛ kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli?

english: You take small samples of soil from different spots across your field before planting, mix them together, and test that sample to see the average nutrient levels in your farm.
ga: Obuaa shikpɔŋ bibii anaa kɛjɛɔ hei srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ dani oduɔ nii. Futumɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni oka nakai nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ okwɛ koni ona niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mlijaa mlijaa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields when I plant maize on the same field again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients. When you harvest corn, it takes those nutrients out of the ground, leaving less food in the soil for the next crop unless you replace it.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okpa ŋmãa lɛ, ajieɔ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ. ja okɛto najiaŋ

english: Does planting corn take away nutrients from my soil?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, growing and harvesting corn absorbs significant nutrients from the ground, which reduces the natural fertility of your soil before the next season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ kɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ baa shi dani be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why does my crop look weak even though I applied fertilizer during the previous season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo amɛmli yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli moŋ?

english: The crops you harvested earlier used up those nutrients to grow, meaning last season's fertilizer may be completely depleted before your new crop starts growing.
ga: Tsei ni okpa tsutsu lɛ kɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwo mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baaho dani otsei heei lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do I know the exact amount of fertilizer to buy for my farm this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ mahe kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: By testing your soil to see what nutrients remain after your last harvest, you can calculate the exact amount of extra fertilizer needed for your new crop.
ga: Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akaa lɛ akwɛɔ koni ana niyenii mli nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ naagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ obu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni he hiaa kɛha onibii heei lɛ ahe akɔntaa.

english: Can I assume there is enough fertilizer left in the ground from my last harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ mamu sane naa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli?

english: No, because the previous crop absorbed nutrients while growing, leaving unknown amounts behind that must be tested before planting again.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ tsutsu lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Enɛ haa ehe hiaa ni aka bɔ ni aleee bɔ ni fa ha lɛ akwɛ dani adu ekoŋŋ.

english: How can checking my soil's nutrients save me money on chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni okɛ shika ato tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Knowing what food is already in your soil prevents you from buying unnecessary fertilizers, allowing you to pay only for the specific nutrients your land actually lacks.
ga: Kɛ́ ole niyenii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi bo gbɛ koni okahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni he ehiaaa. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ owoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ pɛ he nyɔmɔ.

english: Is it necessary to test my soil every time I plant if I farm twice in a year?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni maka shikpɔŋ lɛ makwɛ be fɛɛ be ni madu nii kɛji mitsu okwaayeli shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli?

english: Yes, because every crop harvest removes nutrients from the soil, changing the land's fertility level between the first and second planting seasons.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmaakpamɔ fɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ teŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain trees or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from harsh heat and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Dumɔwui loo shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli shade. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enáa hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: What benefit do I get by covering the soil around my pepper plants with dry palm fronds or grass?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔi maná kɛji mikɛ ŋmei loo jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the soil water. It keeps the roots cool, stops weeds from growing, and eventually rots into good manure for your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛfiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape while the crop is growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the tip mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to stay green and build large ears. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the crop's life restores health to the leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni ewo toi wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts take air from the atmosphere and fix it into the soil as plant food through their roots. This naturally feeds neighboring crops like maize, keeping your soil fertile without spending extra money on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ tsei aniyenii kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ aná niyenii. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ni ofiteee shika yɛ tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so that I can get more plants on my small farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crop roots fight each other for water, food, and sunlight. This results in tall, thin plants that easily fall in strong winds and produce very tiny ears or no corn at all.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa lɛ baa shi oya. ni amɛwoɔ toi bibii waa loo amɛwooo ŋmãa ko kwraa

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant is stressed by severe hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of insects to move pollen inside the flower. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ pollen lɛ yaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do the center leaves of my young corn look chewed up with dirt like sawdust inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ yɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the growing whorl of the plant during the day to eat soft leaves. Applying safe treatments like neem leaf extract or recommended insecticides directly into the funnel kills the caterpillar before it ruins the whole crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ni miida lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster and greener than the crops I planted on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ be fɛɛ be fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally tough and have deep roots designed to drink water and soil food faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early gives your main crops full access to the soil nutrients they need to outgrow wild grass.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ wa yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni afee koni enu nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ haa tsei ni okwɛɔ amɛ lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛdara oya fe koo mli jwɛi.

english: How do I know if the ground has enough water for me to start sowing my seeds at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okɛdu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Dig a small hole hand-deep and squeeze a handful of the soil into a ball. If the soil holds together in a lump without dripping excess water, the ground has the right moisture for seeds to sprout safely without rotting.
ga: Okɛ oniji atsa bu bibioo ko ni okɛ sũ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ afee bɔɔlu. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni nu ni hoɔ fe nine bɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sũ lɛ yɛ nu ni sa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe ni amɛfiteee.

english: Can I leave my cassava tubers in the ground after they mature, or will they rot right away?
ga: Kɛ́ ekwɛ̃ lɛ, ani obaanyɛ oshi ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli? Aloo ebaagbo amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Cassava tubers store safely under the ground for several months after maturing, acting like a natural food store. However, leaving them in the soil for too long can cause them to become woody, hard, and lose their starch content.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei shishifãi toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Amɛtamɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii shwapoi. Shi, kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛtsɔmɔ tsei, amɛwa ni amɛmli starch lɛ akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ mli.

english: Why should I spray my crops with chemicals when I do not see any pests or diseases on them yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ? Be mli ni minako tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai komɛi lolo?

english: Spraying before pests appear is called preventive spraying. It acts like a protective shield for your crops, destroying invisible fungus spores and early pest eggs so they cannot damage your farm later.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ dani tsɛŋemɔ helai baaje kpo lɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hela naa. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ gãimlibii ni buɔ onibii ahe. Efiteɔ fungal spores ni anaaa kɛ mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai akui. Bɔni afee ni ekafite oŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Can I use the same chemical to kill insect pests and cure spots on my plant leaves?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai nɛɛ nɔŋŋ agbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni majie baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: No, different farm chemicals perform different jobs. Insecticides kill insects, while fungicides cure fungal diseases; using the wrong chemical will waste your money and leave your crops unprotected.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔ mli tsofai srɔtoi tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ gbeɔ kooloi. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsaa ŋmeii helai. Tsofai ni ejaaa ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ baaha ofite shika ni ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akabu he.

english: How do I know the correct amount of chemical to mix with water for spraying my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofai abɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ nu afutu mli koni mikɛshwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Chemicals come with specific instructions based on farm size and crop type. Agricultural extension officers help you measure the exact dosage so you do not burn your crops with too much chemical or waste money using too little.
ga: Tsofai baaba kɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi pɔtɛɛ ni damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahenɔi anɔ. Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he nitsulɔi baanyɛ aye abua bo ni osusu shika pɔtɛɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ he. Enɛ ji koni okɛ tsofai babaoo akashã oŋmɔshi nibii. aloo shika ni afiteɔ kɛtsɔ nɔ fioo ni akɛtsuɔ nii tsɔ nɔ

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because the weather is cooler and the wind is calm. High afternoon heat can cause chemicals to evaporate quickly or burn plant leaves in direct sunlight.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu mli ejɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai lɛ atsɔ oya loo eha tsei ahe baai ashã yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli.

english: How long should I wait after spraying my farm before it is safe to enter and work?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani mabote mli shweshweeshwe ni matsu nii?

english: Every chemical has a re-entry period, usually between 24 and 48 hours. Waiting allows the sprayed chemical to dry properly and prevents skin contact or breathing in toxic fumes.
ga: Tsofa fɛɛ tsofa yɛ be ni ekɛboteɔ mli ekoŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yaa nɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 teŋ. Mɛɛmɔ baaha tsofa ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ. ni otsi hewolo lɛ he loo lasu ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni amuɔ lɛ naa

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellow and curling leaves are a sign of stress, usually caused by tiny insects sucking the plant sap, a plant disease, or a lack of key nutrients in the soil.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji haomɔ he okadi. Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ tsei amli nu, tsei ahelai, loo niyenii kpakpai ni he hiaa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the dry afternoon heat even when I watered the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Plants wilt in strong heat because their leaves lose water faster than their roots can draw it from the ground. It can also happen if pests or disease have damaged the root system.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli ejaakɛ baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji kooloi loo helai fite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall green leaves but producing very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen from fertilizer without enough phosphorus or potassium, they focus all their energy on growing tall leaves instead of forming healthy, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni phosphorus loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kakadaji ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ cob nɛ ngɛ he wami nɛ e he wa.

english: How can an agricultural extension officer help me start my farm correctly as a beginner?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mije miŋmɔ lɛ shishi yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ kɛjɛ shishijee?

english: Extension officers provide direct training on land preparation, seed selection, correct chemical mixing, and crop protection methods tailored to your local environment.
ga: Nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ tsɔsemɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ mli lɛ he hewalɛ. Dumɔwui halamɔ Tsofai kɛ tsei ahebuu gbɛi ni sa kɛha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni akɛfutuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Seeds usually fail to sprout if they are buried too deep, planted in dry or waterlogged soil, or damaged by soil insects and birds before they can germinate.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. aloo kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ lɛ dani enyɛɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is even ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani abele lɛ po feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to grow strong. It can also happen if the soil has too much water around the roots or if weeds are stealing the plant's food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha tso lɛ dalɛ kpakpa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe loo kɛji jwɛi ju tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that loves to hide in the tender central leaves of young corn plants and eat them before the cob can form.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni sumɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe awo ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni eyeɔ nii dani ŋmãa lɛ baa.

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree does not get enough water, when there are not enough tiny insects like midges to pollinate them, or when the tree is stressed by too much direct sun and heat.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ mli loo be mli ni hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ tsɔ.

english: How should I put my cassava sticks into the ground so I get large tubers?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ afuɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli koni aná ŋmei wuji?
