english: Planting cassava stems at a slant or horizontally under soft, loose soil gives the roots space to spread out easily and grow into bigger tubers compared to planting them straight up in hard soil.
ga: Aduɔ cassava tsei yɛ he ko ni etse ehe loo etse ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egbɔjɔ shishi. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná gbɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ dumɔ tɛ̃ɛ he

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their little fruits before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii lɛ? Dani ebaada agbo?

english: Peppers drop young fruits when the plant experiences stress from irregular watering—like going from very dry soil to heavy rain suddenly—or when the temperature gets too hot for the plant to feed the fruit.
ga: Chili peppers jieɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ekɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli, tamɔ tsakemɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ kɛyaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. aloo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni tso lɛ nyɛŋ aha aduawai lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and drying out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes can be the plant's way of protecting itself from losing water in hot weather, but it is often caused by leaf-curl viruses spread by tiny whiteflies.
ga: Baai ni akɛshwieɔ tomato nɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Shi bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni haa baai shwieɔ shi, ni whiteflies bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: What happens to my crops when the dry Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan air pulls water out of plants and soil very fast, causing leaves to dry up, flowers to fall off, and crop growth to slow down unless you cover the soil with dry grass or water them regularly.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei kɛ sũ mli oya. gĩ baai ni fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ni tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi Ja okɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie nɔ loo okɛ nu wo nɔ daa.

english: Why do my crops grow much faster when I mix dried chicken manure into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya waa kɛ́ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Chicken manure contains natural nitrogen and rich organic matter that improves the soil's ability to hold water while feeding the plants the necessary nutrients to build leaves and stems.
ga: Nitrogen ni ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni sũ lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ yaa hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ haa tso lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when a heavy wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that stay near the surface, making them top-heavy when bearing bunches. Tiny root-damaging worms in the soil can also weaken their grip on the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ kɛ́ amɛfee kui. Kplukai bibii ni fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hu baanyɛ aha amɛhe ni amɛmɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee mlɛo.

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots fight over the same water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunshine from reaching one another, resulting in smaller plants and lower harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua tsei anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei bibii feɔ bibii ni akpaa nii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings experience transplant shock and are sensitive to direct, intense sunlight. They require shade trees or temporary crops like plantains to shelter them, along with steady soil moisture while their roots get established.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui naa amanehulu kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ dumɔwui koni amɛkɛha amɛhe. Enɛ fataa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ he beni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense heat and direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that act like natural shade umbrellas, protecting young cocoa plants and keeping the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Curled leaves with yellow patterns on cassava are typically caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is transmitted by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties and removing infected plants stops the disease from spreading across your field.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmei nɔ Bei pii lɛ ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa Okɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã he ni oyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting under the soil before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when the soil holds too much water or lacks proper drainage, allowing soil fungi and bacteria to attack the tubers. Planting yams on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away and keeps the tubers healthy.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ bɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing starting from the tips of lower maize leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires nitrogen to stay green and grow strong, which can be corrected by applying balanced fertilizer or well-rotted manure.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce leafy green vines but very few pods underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miiwo wain tsei ni baai eŋɔli lɛ? Shi pods fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Groundnuts need adequate phosphorus and calcium in the soil to form strong pods and nuts. Excessive nitrogen in the soil makes the plant focus all its energy on growing leaves instead of developing underground pods.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmeii kɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ shishi pods lɛ

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when daytime temperatures get extremely hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is an imbalance in nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulched helps protect the flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is my cashew tree producing plenty of flowers but very few nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Low nut formation in cashew trees often occurs due to poor pollination or damage from sap-sucking pests like cashew bugs during flowering. Protecting beneficial insects like bees and managing flower pests early helps turn blooms into nuts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fioo komɛi ni baa cashew tsei amli lɛ baa yɛ pollination ni ehiii loo nɔ ni ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ hewɔ. Koolooi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ wuobii ahebuu kɛ fɔfɔii awuiyelɔi akwɛmɔ mra. It will help turn the flowers into nuts.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to build a sturdy stem and support large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛma tso lɛ shishi ni wa ni ekɛfiɔ tso agbo ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I tell when my maize crop is fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves turn brown and dry, the silks at the tip of the cob turn dark brown, and a small black spot forms at the base of the corn kernels when you scrape them off the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi. Siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ naagbee lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii Ebaa yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi beni okɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide the necessary shade and moisture to protect young cocoa trees during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni akɛbu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is essential for green leaf growth, so applying fertilizer like NPK or urea can help restore the plant's health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable farm early in the morning or under the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the soil can absorb moisture before the sun gets too hot, preventing fast evaporation and leaf burning.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Etsiɔ la ni hoɔ oya kɛ baai ni shãa lɛ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cassava on the exact same spot on my land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients in the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating cassava with legumes like cowpeas helps restore soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Cassava ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ cowpea tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Staking raises yam leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight. More sunlight allows the leaves to make more food, resulting in larger yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la babaoo haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Flowers drop off mainly due to heat stress, irregular watering, or insect attacks. Keeping the soil consistently moist and controlling pests ensures flowers stay attached and produce tomatoes.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ amɛhe ni tomatoi lɛ hu awo yibii.

english: Why do certified seeds from agro-dealers yield more than seeds I collect from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aŋmala he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred for high yields, disease resistance, and local climate tolerance, while saved seeds lose those beneficial traits over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe kɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe tsuishitoo. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nakai nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why does my stored maize turn into fine powder after a few months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Storage insects like weevils bore into the dry grains to feed on them, reducing them to powder. Using airtight storage bags or approved grain preservatives keeps weevils out.
ga: Picker kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii baafo dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ amli koni amɛye amɛ. tsake amɛ amɛfee powda Kɛ akɛ vacuum kotokui ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe loo nɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛbuɔ dumɔwui ahe lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ ŋmeii anaa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce much smaller yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni jieɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave recommended space between my pepper plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ pepper tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting peppers too close causes them to overcrowd each other, blocking air and light. Giving them space reduces disease spread and allows each plant to produce bigger peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ekome tsɔ. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la naa He ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ baa shi. ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso woɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow strong and green. Applying fertilizer like NPK or well-decomposed animal manure will help feed the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does spreading dry grass and leaves around my crop stems help them survive hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai awo he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from taking nutrients away from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ agbala niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from young leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or recommended sprays helps keep the plants growing normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo spray ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the soft center leaves inside my young maize plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms that prefer eating the tender central leaves (the whorl) because they are soft and full of nutrients. Checking your field early and applying targeted bio-pesticides or ash can help protect the leaves.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo (rings) lɛ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ. Odumɔi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo sũ ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: What causes my cowpea leaves to become covered in tiny sticky white insects?
ga: Mɛni miiha ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ miiha mi-cowpea baai lɛ ahe?

english: These sticky insects are aphids or whiteflies that feed on plant sap and release a sweet substance that attracts black mold. Washing them off with soapy water solution or spraying neem extract can keep them under control.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ shi nɛɛ ji aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛjieɔ nɔ ko ni ŋɔɔ ni gbalaa ŋmeii diji kɛbaa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ tsu nii loo okɛ neem mli nu shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why should I plant plantains in the same field with my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ ni adu kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the cocoa seedlings the shade and humidity they need during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: When soil gets soaked with too much standing water, roots cannot breathe and harmful water-loving fungi grow rapidly, causing the tubers to rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away safely.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Ni ŋmei ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ daa oya. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before they can turn into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, sudden dry spells, or too much water. Maintaining consistent soil moisture and providing slight shade can keep the flowers attached.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa loo hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa lɛ he. aloo nu babaoo yɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔlɔ fioo aha lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ he.

english: Why does my maize grow tall and thin with very tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they compete for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting with proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough resources to form large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔ ni akɛ gbɛ ni sa kpãa gbee lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha efee ŋmei agbo ni eyi obɔ.

english: How can I tell that my yam tubers are mature and ready to harvest without digging them up first?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛtsuuu nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines naturally begin to yellow and dry up. This sign shows that the plant has finished storing all its energy down in the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eye omanye ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because their leaves burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them provides living shade and keeps the soil cool and moist during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aaadu yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ shishijee bei ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Is it better to plant my cassava stem cuttings straight up or slanted in the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei niji ni ja loo ni atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slant (about 45 degrees) helps the roots spread out closer to the surface, making it easier to harvest the tubers later while still giving the plant good stability.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ (aaafee digrii 45) lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lolo.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on young maize leaves inside the central whorl. Catching them early and applying recommended pesticides or neem-based treatments helps protect your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ okɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Alternating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant receives uneven amounts of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do weeds growing near my crops cause them to stay small and yield less?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops don't have to compete for the food they need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa onibii lɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdu lɛ akaŋ.

english: When is the right time to put fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil while crops are actively growing, usually a few weeks after germinating. Applying it on dry soil or right before heavy downpours causes the fertilizer to evaporate or wash away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ebaaho.

english: Why do my saved maize seeds get destroyed by tiny insects while stored in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ? Be mli ni mikɛtoɔ mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weevils attack stored seeds if the seeds are not fully dried or if they are stored in open containers. Drying seeds thoroughly under the sun and storing them in airtight containers or with ash keeps insects away.
ga: Weevils baatutua dumɔwui ni ato lɛ kɛji amɛgbiko kwraa loo akɛto tsɛnsii ni agbele mli. Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la shishi ni okɛto nɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli loo okɛ sũ awo mli koni ekɛshwie kooloi bibii.

english: How can I keep my farm soil from drying out too fast when the rain stops for a few weeks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akagbi oya tsɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi?

english: Covering the bare soil around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or crop residues—a method called mulching—traps moisture in the ground and shields the plant roots from heat.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ni ebɔle oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This happens when the plant lacks nitrogen, a major plant food. The crop moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves, signaling that the soil needs organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji amɛ niyenii titri lɛ. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow plenty of big leaves but very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: When pepper plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing leaves instead of fruits. Reducing nitrogen and ensuring plants get enough sunlight helps them shift into producing flowers and peppers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Amɛbaakɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ama baai ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai. Nitrogen ni abaaba shi kɛ nɔmimaa akɛ tsei lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsake kɛya fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, they leave this natural fertilizer in the soil, which feeds the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite Eshiɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni haa niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and develop yellowish patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems for planting prevents the virus from taking over your farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmei bibioo lɛ ji nɔ ni hiɛɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Kɛ okɛ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ odumɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do tiny insects get into my stored maize grains and turn them into powder after harvest?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii boteɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ amli ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ powda yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Maize weevils lay eggs inside damp grains while crops are drying. If grains are stored before drying completely, the eggs hatch into larvae that eat the grain from the inside out.
ga: Abele ŋmeii woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmaa ni mli efɔ mli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmaa lɛ to dani egbi kwraa lɛ, Ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop many of their small young pods before they can mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? Mɛi enyiɛ dani eda?

english: This is a natural process called cherelle wilt, where the cocoa tree drops extra pods it cannot support due to limited water, light, or nutrients in the soil.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherelle wilt, he ni cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ yɛ nu, la loo niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni faaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves fold up and hang down during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmatta be ni nu egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves droop and split in hot, dry weather to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant conserve water and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbalaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do the bottoms of my fresh green tomatoes turn dark and soft before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani etsɔɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant carry calcium to the fruits.
ga: Enɛ ji fɔfɔii lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ, ni calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium yaa aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my rice plants grow tall and thin with empty heads when I sow seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛyitsei lɛ efee efolo beni adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded crops fight for sunlight and soil nutrients. This leaves them weak and unable to produce full, healthy grains.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dense crops kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmaa ni hi jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: How do I know that my yams under the ground are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: When the yam vines and leaves start turning yellow and drying naturally above ground, it shows the plant has finished sending energy into the tuber and the yam is fully mature.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛmajeɔ bulb lɛ naa. Ni yams lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does adding dried chicken manure to my farm soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Chicken manure adds rich organic matter and essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus to the soil, while helping the ground hold moisture better during dry spells.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he, yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce small yields when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves compete with each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing weak growth.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: Why should I cover the ground around my plantain suckers with dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle banana tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool and moist, stops weeds from growing, and breaks down into natural soil food over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efite akɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that expands the tubers underground, and keeping leaves off the damp ground protects them from fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I allow weeds to grow tall around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ kɛbɔleɔ cacao tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Tall weeds steal water and nutrients from the cocoa roots, and they create a dark, humid environment that encourages black pod disease.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi amli. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli edɔ ni woɔ black pod hela lɛ he hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off without producing peppers when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper baaa beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes heat stress in pepper plants, drying out flower pollen and forcing the plant to drop flowers to save water and survive.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa pepper tsei amli. egbiɔ pollen lɛ ni enyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie fɔfɔi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much rain fills soil air pockets with water, suffocating the cassava roots and creating wet conditions where rotting fungi thrive.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ ada yɛ mli lɛ aba.

english: What causes small caterpillars to hide inside the funnel leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewoɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni ji cone lɛ amli?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, destructive pests that lay eggs on maize leaves and feed on the soft growing center of young corn plants.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ nii ni woɔ ŋmãa baa nɔ ni eyeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ ateŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the cut tips of my fresh cassava cuttings rot instead of growing roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi heei lɛ miifite yɛ shishifãi ni miida lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are cut with blunt tools or planted in poorly drained soil, fungi enter the open cut easily. Using clean, sharp cuts on mature stems helps the growing tip form healthy white root buds quickly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ nibii ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ miifo ŋmei tsei loo oodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmei boteɔ hei ni agbele naa lɛ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni eda ni he tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ naagbee ni miida lɛ ni efee shishifãi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ futafuta oya.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen or waterlogged, which prevents roots from absorbing nutrients. Applying nitrogen-based fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛ nitrogen fee, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Will spraying strong crop medicine burn the soft growing tips of my plants?
ga: Ani tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baashã mitsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: Yes, using too much chemical mixture or spraying during hot afternoon sun can scorch delicate growing tips and leaves. Always follow the correct water mixture ratio and spray early in the morning or late afternoon.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Nyiɛmɔ nu ni akɛfutuɔ nii amli lɛ mlijaa ni ja lɛ sɛɛ be fɛɛ be. ni okɛshwie nɔ leebi loo shwane mli

english: How long do strong weed-killing chemicals stay in my soil after I spray?
ga: Be enyiɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baahi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Certain chemical weed killers can remain active in the soil for months or even years, which can stop new crop seeds from sprouting. It is important to know if a weed killer works only on contact with leaves or stays long in the ground.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ekomɛi baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji loo afii babaoo. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ dumɔwui heei akwɛ̃mɔ naa. Ehe miihia ni wɔkadi akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii pɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkɛ tsei ahe tsei lɛ kpe loo amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How many years can a cocoa tree keep producing good pods if I look after it well?
ga: Afii enyiɛ cacao tso ko baawo ŋmeii kpakpai kɛji mikwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: A well-cared-for cocoa tree can produce good harvests for 20 to 30 years or more, provided you prune shade trees, remove diseased pods, and keep the soil healthy with nutrients.
ga: Kookoo tso ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai afii 20 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai, kɛji akɛ ofo tso lɛ he koni eha hulutsoo aba. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. ni ekwɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the days are too hot, water is irregular, or there is too much nitrogen in the soil, which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ. Nu ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee yɛ jɛmɛ. aloo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ awo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do the delicate white roots of my pepper seedlings die after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi yɛŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gboiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo he kroko lɛ?

english: White root tips die if they dry out in the hot sun during transplanting or are forced into hard soil. Keeping roots moist and transplanting late in the day when the sun is down protects them.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi yɛŋ lɛ baagboi kɛji amɛgbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni aduɔ amɛ lɛ loo anyɛ amɛnɔ amɛwo shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ. Kɛ́ oha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni otsi ohe yɛ gbɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe.

english: Yam tubers twist or stop growing when they hit hard, compacted soil or rocks underground. Building high, loose mounds gives the tubers soft soil to grow deep and straight.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ loo amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Gɔŋ kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: What is causing the white powdery stuff under the leaves of my garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni kɛ powda yɛŋ ni yɔɔ eggplant baai lɛ ashishi yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: That white coating is often caused by mealybugs or powdery mildew fungus. These suck the plant's juices, causing leaves to curl and reducing the size and quality of your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo powdery mildew fungi ji nɔ ni kɛ nakai ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ baa. Enɛɛmɛi shwieɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ dalɛ kɛ amɛhe kpakpa baa shi.

english: Why do my young sweet orange trees drop their small green fruits early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop small fruit early when there is a sudden dry period or a lack of nutrients like potassium. Watering during dry spells and applying balanced fertilizer keeps the fruit attached.
ga: Citrus tsei woɔ yibii bibii oya kɛji hulutsoo be ko ba trukaa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium bɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen or getting too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or compost gives the plant the nutrient boost it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows maize pests to build up in the field. Rotating with legumes like beans or cowpeas refills nitrogen into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii atsakeɔ Ekɛ nitrogen baafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or cassava grown beside them during their first two years to block harsh heat and keep the environment moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni akafee hulutsoo fe nine ni eha shihilɛ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunshine to make food for the growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight, leading to much bigger yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ bafee wuji babaoo.

english: Too many extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and food from the main plant. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to focus its energy on producing larger, heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei babaoo loo tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantains wuji ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with small brown droppings inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the plant. Spraying approved treatments early in the morning or late evening when the worms come out to feed helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ yeɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow poorly even after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that act like thieves, drinking up water and taking in fertilizer before your crops can reach it. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients you provide.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi. Nuu nu ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani onibii lɛ abashɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni okɛhaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants dropping off before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are too high or when water supply to the soil is irregular. Keeping the soil consistently moist by mulching with dry grass helps prevent flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ejaaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ ahe tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: In intense afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil, causing temporary wilting. Covering the soil around the plants with dry leaves keeps the roots cool and saves soil water.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi shwie tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akafitemɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to make green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the roots or when water settles in the field for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ afee eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli loo kɛ́ nu shwie ŋmɔ ko mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air is too hot or when the soil gets too dry. When a plant feels stressed by extreme heat or lack of water, it drops its flowers to save energy so the plant itself can stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ amɛmiihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: How do I know which direction to push a cassava stem into the ground when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni esa akɛ matsi ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Look closely at the small bumps (nodes) where leaves used to grow on the stem; those small buds should point upward toward the sky. Planting the stem upside down forces the new shoots to grow downward first, making the plant weak and reducing root growth.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii (nodes) ni be ko ni eho lɛ baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yitso lɛ hiɛ shi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ shi klɛŋklɛŋ. Ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cool, overly shaded, and damp conditions. Moisture helps the fungus spread quickly from pod to pod, especially during the heavy rainy season.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ Shade babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus carried by those insects. As they feed, they cause the leaves to wrinkle, twist, and stunt the plant's overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ hiɛɔ beni amɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ nɔ Amɛhaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas together with my maize helps the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du tsina ŋmãa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that have special bacteria in their roots capable of pulling nitrogen from the air and putting it into the soil. This acts as a natural food source that neighboring maize plants can feed on to grow stronger.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi ni baanyɛ agbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my yam vines and leaves dry up and die off near the end of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: When yam leaves turn yellow and dry up at the end of the season, it is a natural sign that the plant has finished its life cycle and stored all its energy inside the tuber underground. It tells you the yam is mature and ready for harvesting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe ewala shihilɛ naa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto shikpɔŋ shishi. Ekɛɛ bo akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do my crops wilt and droop even when there is plenty of water sitting in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like they need water. When soil stays flooded or overly wet for too long, the roots drown and begin to rot, preventing them from taking up water and causing the plant to wilt even in wet dirt.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛje shishi amɛgboi. Enɛ haaa amɛnu nu, ni ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ po nɔ.

english: Cassava sheds its leaves during dry periods as a self-defense mechanism to prevent losing moisture through its leaves. The plant rests underground during the drought and will quickly sprout new green leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ehe koni ŋmɔtɔ akatsɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Tso lɛ baajɔɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli, ni ebaakwɛ baai heei eŋɔli oya kɛji nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do crops planted near muddy, polluted river water grow poorly and have stunted roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ faa mli nu ni mli ewo muji ni mli ewo muji lɛ masɛi lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Muddy water loaded with heavy sediment and pollutants chokes the soil, blocking air from reaching the roots and damaging the soil's natural nutrients. Healthy crops need clean water and clean soil so their roots can breathe and absorb food easily.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji ni ŋmeii ni tsii kɛ mujiwoo eyi mli obɔ lɛ baatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa. Etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni efiteɔ sũ lɛ mli niyenii kpakpai. Nu ni mli tse kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii mlɛo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dry when the sun gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts like a living umbrella, protecting them from excessive heat and conserving soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔ ni hiɛ ka. Ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and turn small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early with neem oil spray or recommended insecticides stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaatsi baa lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves in maize usually means the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green growth. Applying fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the boost it needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiamɔ nii aya hiɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows corn pests to build up in the earth. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi baaje shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young corn leaves and caterpillar droppings in the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmãa mli ŋmãa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana. Spraying approved insecticides or neem leaf extracts into the central funnels of the maize plants early in the morning helps get rid of them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water during heavy rains or when waterlogging causes fungal infections. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away and keeps the tubers healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa mli loo kɛji nu eyi mli obɔ, ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plants do not get consistent water. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulching around the plants helps reduce heat stress so fruits can set.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu daa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ he ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ baaha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi koni eha aduawai lɛ ashɛ shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains right when the bunches start getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni jwɛi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and become top-heavy as the fruit bunch grows. Propping the main stem with a sturdy, forked wooden pole prevents strong winds from blowing the tree over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ be mli ni kuu lɛ daa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ fĩ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekatswa tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Yes, staking yam vines lifts the leaves toward the sunlight so the plant can make more food, resulting in much larger tubers. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, reducing fungal diseases.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he koni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ feɔ agbo kwraa. Etsiɔ baai hu anaa koni amɛkaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ aba shi

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce small yields when I sow seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing allows the roots and leaves to spread out and grow strong.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara waa.

english: How do I know if I am planting my cassava stem cuttings the right way up in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni afo lɛ miidu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Look closely at the stem for the small buds or 'eyes' where leaves grow out. These buds must point upward toward the sky; if planted upside down, the crop will struggle to sprout and will yield very little.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ koni ona ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu tsei lɛ ahiɛ shi lɛ, ebaawa akɛ amɛakwɛ̃, ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food for leaf growth, or that the soil is holding too much water around the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps turn them green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo tsɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks regular water, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering and providing light shade during extremely hot weeks help the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni sa loo kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni ashwieɔ amɛ daa ni amɛhaa amɛ hulutsoo be fioo. Otsi kome ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up to protect the plant from losing water too quickly in strong sunlight, but curling can also be caused by tiny insects sucking the juice from the leaves. Watering regularly in the morning and checking under leaves for tiny pests can stop this.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ebu tso lɛ he koni nu lɛ akafite oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shi kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aha curling aba. Nu ni oooha amɛ daa leebi ni okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii komɛi yɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ akpa naagba lɛ.

english: What is making small ragged holes in the middle leaves of my maize crops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Nɛgbɛ ji mi ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ?

english: These holes are usually made by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the young center leaves of the maize plant. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended treatments or neem liquid into the leaf funnel stops them before they ruin the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai bibii amli lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ buji nɛɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii loo neem nu lɛ awo tso lɛ baa lɛ mli. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani ŋmɔ lɛ akumɔ.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting in the ground before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifolɔ amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when water collects around them in heavy soil or when diseased seed yams were planted. Planting on high mounds in well-drained soil prevents water from sitting around the tubers and soaking them to death.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu shwie shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ loo kɛ́ adu sweet potato ni hela emɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nu ni ebɔle bulb lɛ he lɛ naa ni ekɛ amɛ shwie shi kɛyashi amɛgboi.

english: When is the exact right time for me to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer is best applied when plants are actively growing, usually two to three weeks after planting and again when they start flowering. Always apply fertilizer when the soil is moist so the roots can soak it up without burning.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ miida waa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2-3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu kɛji fɔfɔii je shishi Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ni amɛshãaa.

english: Does leaving grass and weeds between my crops really hurt my yield?
ga: Ani jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, weeds act like stolen mouths at the family table—they steal light, water, and soil fertilizer away from your main crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops all the food and room they need to grow strong and yield big.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ naabu ni aju yɛ weku okpɔlɔ lɛ nɔ—amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha onibii lɛ niyenii kɛ he ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How can I easily tell if my soil is healthy enough to support good crop growth?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Healthy soil feels soft, looks dark, smells fresh, and holds moisture well after rain. If your soil feels like hard clay, looks pale, or dries out instantly, mixing in animal manure or compost will make it rich and soft for root growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ nii, ni eŋɔɔɔ ehe. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa Efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo egbi trukaa Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ futu mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee blɛoo kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves burn and drop off when the dry season sun gets strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitswa waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need soft shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out their small roots faster than they can absorb water. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby keeps the air humid and protects young cocoa trees from heat stress.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo fioo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi bibii aba. Egbiɔ oya tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eŋɔ nu. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy winds and rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees naturally have shallow root systems that struggle to hold heavy bunches, especially if tiny soil pests or root borers have eaten their roots. Mounding extra soil around the base of the plant and supporting heavy bunches with wooden poles helps keep them standing upright.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛmɔ panicles ni tsii lɛ amli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ yɛ. eat its roots Laying additional soil around The base of the tree and supporting the heavy branches with wooden stakes help keep the tree upright.

english: I noticed tiny caterpillars inside the center leaves of my young maize plants eating holes through them. What is happening to my crop?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmei bibioo ko. Yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ, buji miiho kɛmiitsɔ amɛmli. Mɛni ba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: This is likely the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that burrows deep inside the middle leaves of maize to eat the young shoot. Checking your farm early in the morning and applying recommended biopesticides or ash into the leaf centers can control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni eye ŋmãa bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo sũ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ wo baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye amɛnɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plants without turning into fruits when the weather is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely hot, the pollen inside tomato flowers dries up, preventing the flower from forming fruit, which causes it to drop. Watering your crops early in the morning and providing light shade helps keep the plants cool enough to form fruits.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ Pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ baagbi. Tsĩ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo yibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi Nu ni awoɔ tsei amli leebi kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛhe jɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Choose mature, healthy stems from cassava plants that are 8 to 12 months old and show no signs of rot or insect damage. The middle section of the stem sprouts fastest and produces the strongest roots, so cut pieces from that part rather than the soft top or dry bottom.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni jɛ ŋmei tsei ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni ejieee ŋmei loo kooloi ni efite lɛ ahe okadii akpo lɛ amli. Tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ daa oya fe fɛɛ ni ewoɔ shishifãi ni wa fe fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔ nakai fã lɛ kɛjɛ nakai fã lɛ mli. Mohu ɔ, moo po hiɔwe fã nɛ ngɛ blɛoo ɔ loo sisi fã nɛ e gbi ɔ.

english: Yam vines produce tubers underground by capturing sunlight through their leaves above ground. Staking lifts the leaves into the air for maximum sunlight and keeps them away from damp soil, which prevents leafy diseases and allows the underground tubers to grow much bigger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛmɔɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. ni etsĩɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Is it good for my soil if I plant groundnuts or cowpeas between my rows of maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, planting leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas enriches the soil because these plants naturally pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food. This feeds your current maize crop and leaves nutrients in the soil for future plantings.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nɛɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii. Enɛ baaha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni okwɛɔ amrɔ nɛɛ aná niyenii ni eshi niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my maize farm so it does not go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni mikafite nii?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied twice: first about 10 to 14 days after planting when roots begin to take in nutrients, and second when the maize reaches knee-height. Applying fertilizer when the soil is moist prevents it from burning the roots or evaporating.
ga: Kɛ akɛwo mli shii enyɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ ji aaafee gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ beni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai. kɛ shi ni ji enyɔ lɛ beni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ akashã loo amɛkatsɔ la.

english: Why does spreading dry bush leaves on top of the soil help my crops stay green during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii ni egbi ni mikɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Spreading dry leaves or grass on top of the soil (mulching) acts like a blanket that blocks direct sunlight from evaporating soil moisture. It keeps the roots cool, retains groundwater longer, and slowly decays into rich organic compost.
ga: Baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Ehiɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and yellow even when I planted on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be naa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal light, water, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the first four weeks after planting gives your crops full access to everything they need to grow tall, green, and strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara, amɛfee ŋmɔji, ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why should I build a strong fence around my seedling nursery before I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa gbogbo ni wa mabɔle he lɛ? Nursery dani adu?

english: A sturdy fence acts as a guard that keeps farm animals, rodents, and pests from entering your nursery and destroying delicate young seedlings before they are ready for transplanting.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni wa tsuɔ nii akɛ bulɔ ni tsiɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote o-nursery lɛ mli ni amɛfite dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaadu amɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under full sun. Planting shade crops like plantains around them protects the tender seedlings from heat stress until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaabu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baadara waa.

english: How does placing lines of stones around my crop beds help my plants grow better?
ga: Tɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli Te mi dumɔ saatso lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Placing stones around your crop beds creates a protective boundary that traps rainwater in the soil, prevents heavy rains from washing away topsoil, and keeps moisture concentrated around plant roots.
ga: Tɛi ni okɛbaabɔle odumɔ saatsoi lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ husu ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli

english: Why should I avoid allowing runoff water from neighboring farms to flow into my crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ he koni eho kɛya miŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Runoff water coming from outside can carry weed seeds, dangerous fungal spores, and chemical residues directly into your field, contaminating your healthy crops and soil.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ kponɔgbɛ kɛbaa lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ jwɛi dumɔwui. Fungal spores ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ baanyɛ abote oŋmɔji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. ni fiteɔ onibii kɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do crop diseases move from neighboring lands into my clean field?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ nɔ kɛyaa miŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli?

english: Diseases enter your farm through blowing wind, flowing surface water, infected insects, or dirty tools brought in from outside. Creating clear borders around your farm helps block these outside threats.
ga: Helai boteɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ nɔ. nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni hela emɔ amɛ loo nibii ni he tseee ni akɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ aba Husui ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni ooofee yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ kponɔgbɛ gbeyeishemɔi nɛɛ anaa.

english: How does clearing the wild grass around my farm edges protect my vegetables from insects?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ ni mafolɔ lɛ baabu mi-aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe?

english: Clearing a wide border around your farm removes the breeding grounds where insect pests like armyworms hide, preventing them from crawling into your main crop area.
ga: Nibii ni afeɔ lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ Yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ajieɔ hei ni ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ ahi amɛhe yɛ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkabote he titri ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and curling up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl and yellow under heat stress because the plant cannot absorb enough water and nitrogen from dry ground. Mulching the soil around the base helps retain water and restores leaf color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaa baa lɛ su baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers during extreme heat to conserve water and protect the main stem from drying out, acting as a natural defense mechanism against heat stress.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa koni ekɛhiɛ nu mli ni ebu tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he koni ekagbi. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when the soil feels wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes wilt when soil-borne bacteria or root pests enter through root damage and block water movement inside the stem. Isolating infected beds prevents the disease from spreading to healthy plants.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ shi kɛji sũ mli helai loo shishifãi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai bote mli kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni efite lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsi nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Kɛ́ ajie saatsoi ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot inside the soil before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Cassava roots rot when trapped water collects around them for too long. Planting on raised mounds or stone-bordered ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the roots safe underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni emɔ mli lɛ bua ehe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen or is struggling from drought. Applying fertilizer or manure early in the season gives the plant the food it needs to stay green and grow healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha niyenii tamɔ nitrogen loo ekɛ hɔmɔ miiwuu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, dark environments. Pruning extra branches from your trees lets sunlight and air flow through the farm, drying out moisture so the fungus cannot grow.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ duŋ yɔɔ. Afolɔ tsei aniji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ akakwɛ̃.

english: How do I know when my cocoa trees are hungry for fertilizer?
