ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni hɔmɔ miiye mi-kokoo tsei lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cocoa trees show hunger through pale yellow leaves, slow growth, and producing very few pods. Feeding the soil with fertilizer or organic manure at the start of the rainy season helps the roots absorb food when they need it most.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ amɛ hɔmɔ lɛ kpo kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛdalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo kɛ amɛ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛná niyenii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ waa lɛ.

english: Why does planting beans or groundnuts make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil as natural food for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off before growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant lacks water and nutrients. Giving the plants steady water at the roots and protecting them from extreme heat keeps the flowers healthy so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting inside after just a few weeks in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ mligbɛ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during harvest or stored in hot, unventilated spaces. Storing them in a cool, raised yam barn with plenty of moving air prevents rot from developing.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Kɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni awó nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekafite.

english: Why are witchweed plants constantly growing around my sorghum and destroying my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abɛi tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi sorghum lɛ yaa nɔ ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Witchweed, or Striga, is a parasitic weed that attaches itself to crop roots to steal their food and water. Rotating your farm with cowpeas or groundnuts starves the Striga seeds and clears the soil over time.
ga: Witchweed loo Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ tsei shishifãi ahe koni eju niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ okɛ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔ lɛ, ebaaha Striga dumɔwui lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Planting cassava stems too close makes them compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants with small tubers. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to form large, healthy roots.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei komɛi yɛ yitsei bibii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi wuji ni wa baa.

english: Cassava cuttings should be planted with the buds or stem eyes pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new sprouts to grow downward first, exhausting the plant before it reaches the surface.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa dumɔwui heei daa kɛyaa shishi klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ dani amɛshɛ nu lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants droop during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants fold or droop their leaves in strong sunshine to reduce water loss. If they bounce back in the cool evening, it is natural stress protection, but if they remain droopy, the crop needs immediate watering.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ loo amɛjieɔ amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛ amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛɔ haomɔ he. Shi kɛji amɛtee nɔ amɛgboi lɛ, ehe miihia ni afɔ Dumɔwui lɛ anɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is an essential plant food, or the soil is holding too much water. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or improving farm drainage helps them turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa tsɔ Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛfataa he loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady. Planting after just one rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a week-long dry spell follows.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji hɔmɔ ni heɔ otsi kome nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by long dry spells, insect attacks, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping soil moist with shade trees and protecting flowers from insects allows pods to develop.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when heavy fruit bunches start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ aduawai babaoo bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that cannot support heavy fruit during strong winds. Propping the main stem with a strong bamboo or wooden pole supports the weight until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ yibii ni tsii nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛfi tso lɛ shwiili lɛ sɛɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long during heavy rains. Planting on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in full sunlight to make energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases and encouraging growth.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ aha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tsi helai anaa ni oha dalɛ aya hiɛ

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids sucking plant juice from under the leaves. Using neem water spray or organic pest control helps remove them and restores leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni nuɔ tso nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ ni ebaaha baai lɛ adara ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my tomato leaves and make them dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato baai anɔ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Dark spots are caused by fungal diseases that spread fast in wet conditions. Leaving space between plants for airflow and watering only the soil instead of the leaves helps prevent this fungus.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black spot baa. Kɛ́ ashi gbɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli, ni akɛ nu awo shikpɔŋ lɛ pɛ nɔ yɛ baai lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ ŋmei nɛɛ naa.

english: Fertilizer works best when the soil is already moist and crops are actively growing. Applying fertilizer on dry soil can burn plant roots and waste your money.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo ni ŋmɔshi nibii miikwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shika.

english: Why should I buy packaged seeds from a store instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo mli yɛ shwapo mli moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Store-bought certified seeds are specially bred to resist local diseases, grow evenly, and yield much more crop, giving you a better return on your investment compared to old saved seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai. shwereɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ewoɔ babaoo Enɛ haa shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo ni hi fe dumɔwui momo ni ato lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow when the plants are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tsei lɛ darako lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. It can also happen when too much water stays around the roots, preventing the plant from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haaa tso lɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or dry spells. The plant discards the flowers to save energy and water until conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ nu lɛ haaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tso lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and look limp during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves in intense afternoon heat to reduce the amount of water lost through transpiration. It is the plant's natural self-defense mechanism to stay hydrated.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli koni nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ latsaa mli lɛ nɔ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni nu akafite gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and bent instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, well-drained, and loose soil in high mounds to grow straight and deep. If the soil is hard or compacted, the tubers cannot easily expand and end up deformed.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ amli koni amɛkwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛmli kwɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo ebɔle ehe lɛ Yitso lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã ni efite mlɛo.

english: Why are my young cocoa leaves scorching and turning brown when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are shade-loving crops that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them protects their delicate leaves from sun damage while they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii ji tsei ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ hulu lɛ masɛi Enɛ baaye abua ni ebu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting and showing green and yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This pattern is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral infection spread by tiny whitefly insects or infected stem cuttings. It stops the leaves from making food efficiently, leading to smaller tubers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ su nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ afolɔ Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkahoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo.

english: Why do my crops grow so poorly and turn pale whenever Striga weeds appear nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni Striga jwɛi lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Striga, also known as witchweed, is a parasitic weed that attaches its roots directly to crops like maize and sorghum, stealing water and vital nutrients straight from the host plant.
ga: Striga, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ Witchweed lɛ ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ajuɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are white powdery spots spreading on my bean leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni tamɔ powda ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is powdery mildew, a fungal disease that thrives in high humidity and warm temperatures. The white coating blocks sunlight from reaching the leaf surface, slowing down the plant's growth.
ga: Enɛ ji powder mli ŋmei. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ futafuta lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ehaa tsei daa blɛoo.

english: Why do armyworms destroy my maize foliage so rapidly compared to other pests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fallworms fiteɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ oya kɛ akɛto tsɛŋemɔ helai krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms hatch quickly in large numbers and feed aggressively on the soft inner leaves of young maize plants. Warm weather speeds up their growth cycle, allowing them to strip a field in days.
ga: Autumn cutworms lɛ fɔɔ oya yɛ yibɔ babaoo mli ni amɛkɛ ekãa yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli baai bibii lɛ. Kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ yaa oya. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, abaanyɛ akumɔ jɛmɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why is it dangerous for me to buy and plant uncertified crop seeds brought in from across the border?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛha mi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni bɛ he odaseyeli ni jɛ husu lɛ naa lɛ ni madu lɛ?

english: Uncertified seeds from other regions can carry hidden fungal spores, viruses, or foreign pests that are not yet common in your local area, which can spread quickly and ruin entire harvests across your community.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni jɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ baanyɛ ahi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ, loo maŋsɛɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni bɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ lolo. Enɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yɛ akutso lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to stay green and grow, and when there isn't enough in the soil, the plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed its young top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda. kɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha eŋwɛi baa bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my maize cobs sometimes come out half-empty with missing grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi-abele lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ fã bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize cobs miss grains when pollination fails. If the weather is too dry or hot when the silk flowers appear, the pollen dies before fertilizing the cob, leaving empty gaps where grains should have grown.
ga: Abɛi ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmaa lɛ nɔ kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. Kɛji siliki fɔfɔii je kpo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi tsɔ loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ Pollen baagbo dani ekɛ fɔfɔi awo ŋmei lɛ mli. Enɛ haa gbɛ shwieɔ he ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes and brown powdery dirt inside the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ sũ ni tsuɔ yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the fall armyworm, a small caterpillar that hides in the central leaf fold (whorl) of maize plants and eats the leaves before they open.
ga: Fall armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli (rings) ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ.

english: How do groundnut plants produce nuts underground when their yellow flowers bloom above ground?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tsei woɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: After the flower pollinates, it grows a long stem called a 'peg' that bends down and pushes into the dirt. Once underground, the tip of this peg expands to form the groundnut pod.
ga: Beni afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen sɛɛ lɛ Eyɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘peg’ ni shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. kɛji akɛ eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Pin nɛɛ naagbee lɛ baagbɛ eshwa kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmei ŋmei.

english: Why is it harmful to weed around my groundnut field once the plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ No hewɔ lɛ ani mi-peanut ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ oshara beni tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi lɛ?

english: Weeding late can cut or crush the delicate stems (pegs) growing from the flowers down into the dirt, preventing the pods from forming underground.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ blɛoo lɛ baanyɛ afo loo akumɔ tsei bibii (pins) ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haaa pods afee shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow plenty of bushy green leaves but very few flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo shi fɔfɔi loo aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes plants put all their energy into leafy growth, which prevents them from developing flowers, cobs, or nuts.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai ni miida lɛ ahe. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ afee fɔfɔi, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii.

english: Why do my seedlings become tall, thin, and weak instead of growing strong stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadara ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Seedlings grow tall and skinny when they do not get enough direct sunlight. They stretch upwards rapidly in an effort to reach more light.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji amɛnaaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛgbala amɛhe oya kɛtee ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha la babaoo abote mli.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller harvests when I plant seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves crowd each other, forcing them to compete for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, which shrinks their overall yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Akɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ miimɔ amɛhe. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshi akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. ni haa nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ baa shi

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a sudden lack of moisture, causing the plant to abort fruit production.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ trukaa lɛ. Ehaa tsei kpaɔ aduawai.

english: Waterlogged soil prevents air from reaching the roots, causing cassava tubers to suffocate and rot from fungal decay under wet conditions.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei ni fiteɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow fast. Applying animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help your maize regain its dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller harvests every year when I keep planting the same crop in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Beni miyaa nɔ miduɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil until it becomes exhausted. Rotating different crops, such as planting beans after maize, helps rebuild soil nutrients naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ kɛkɛ lɛ ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni etswa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that create natural shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa and keeping the soil moist during their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why must I tie my yam vines to tall wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much direct sunlight as possible to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high up in the sun and off the damp ground, which also prevents leaves from rotting.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ejɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ hu baaye abua ni baai lɛ akafite.

english: If you leave too many suckers growing around the main stem, they will steal water and nutrients from it. Removing extra shoots leaves just one or two strong suckers, allowing the main plant to produce a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle tsei babaoo ahe lɛ Amɛbaaju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ nakai tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ dumɔwui wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds when the rains start after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting after the very first rain is risky because the hot sun can return and dry up the soil, killing young sprouts. It is best to wait until two or three heavy, regular rains have thoroughly soaked the soil before sowing.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii lɛ agbele. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot inside the ground if I leave them in the soil during heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ sũ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ sũ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the soil stays soaked with excess water for too long, air cannot reach the roots. Waterlogged soil causes fungal rot, which quickly destroys mature cassava tubers before you can harvest them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nu ni fa fe nine ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ ŋmei shishifãi ni eda lɛ oya dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: What makes the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tight like small cups?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites that hide on the undersides of leaves and drink the sap. Spraying with neem oil solution or suitable insecticide helps control these pests.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni kɛ ehe teeɔ baai ashishi ni enuɔ mliki Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni sa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before they turn into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛtsɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is extremely hot, when the plant lacks water, or when there are no insects to pollinate them. Consistent watering and mulching around the roots helps keep flowers on the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni nu bɛ tsei ahe loo be mli ni kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ lɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow slowly even when I plant good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kpakpai moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that grow faster than your crops, stealing the water, soil nutrients, and sunlight your crops need. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to food and light.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni daa oya fe onibii ni oduɔ lɛ, ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii kɛ la kwraa.

english: I planted mango seedlings this year, but why will it take up to three years before I can harvest any fruits?
ga: Afi nɛɛ midu mango. Shi mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii etɛ dani akpaa yibii lɛ?

english: Perennial tree crops like mangoes use their first two to three years to establish strong root systems and sturdy branches. This setup phase is essential so the tree becomes strong enough to support heavy fruit yields in later years.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ mango lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ dani amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ niji ni mli wa. Nɛkɛ hesaamɔ gbɛ nɛɛ he hiaa koni tso lɛ mli awa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ afii ni baa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings need extra shade during their first two years in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ he hiaa ni amɛná hulutsoo kroko yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that dry out easily under full tropical sun. Shade protects them from heat stress and preserves soil moisture while their roots settle deep into the ground.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Shade lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ boteɔ sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Can I grow quick food crops like cassava or plantain on the same farm while waiting for my main tree crops to mature?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii oya tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli be mli ni mimɛɔ ni mi ŋmei titri ni yeɔ daa lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Yes, intercropping with fast-growing crops provides natural shade for young tree seedlings and gives you food and income during the initial setup years before your main crop starts bearing fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni akɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ duɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui bibii lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. ni eha bo niyenii kɛ shika kɛha shishijee afii komɛi dani oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Why should I pick off the flowers that appear on my fruit trees in their very first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ fɔfɔi ni jeɔ kpo yɛ mi yibii tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If a young tree carries fruit in its first year, it wastes energy that it needs for growing big branches. Removing early flowers encourages the tree to build a strong frame for bigger harvests in the future.
ga: Kɛji tso bibioo lɛ wo yibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ Ebaafite hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ niji wuji lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mra lɛ, ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛma gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ wuji wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why are my citrus trees dropping their small fruits before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii lɛ? Dani ebaada agbo?

english: Trees shed young fruits when they experience water stress, lack essential soil nutrients, or when the tree realizes it does not have enough energy to mature all the fruit it produced.
ga: Tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ ekɛ nu he haomɔ kpe. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo be mli ni tso lɛ yɔseɔ akɛ ebɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ yibii fɛɛ ni ewoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my fruit trees stop growing and drop their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ kpaɔ amɛdalɛ ni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, low humidity and dry soil force trees into a protective survival mode. Shedding leaves helps the plant conserve internal water so it does not dry out.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo be ni baa shi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ nyɛ ehi shi. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaaa egbi.

english: Why do my crops grow plenty of green leaves but take a long time to start producing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi eheɔ be babaoo dani ebɔi fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil encourages leaf and stem growth instead of flowering. Crops require a balance of nutrients, particularly phosphorus and potassium, to trigger flower and fruit development.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa baa kɛ tsei lɛ daraa yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa jogbaŋŋ he miihia tsei. titri lɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium Koni eha fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ

english: Why is clearing weeds so critical during the first two years of establishing a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi akudɔmɔ he hiaa waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ ni akɛjeɔ ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from young plants. Keeping the farm clean during the early setup years ensures your seedlings get everything they need to grow strong rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli waa. Ni oooha ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli Established plant lɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ náa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why does planting my fruit trees too close together reduce my total harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai tsei ni miduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa miyibii fɛɛ ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Overcrowded trees block sunlight from each other and compete underground for food, leading to tall, weak trees with fewer fruits. Proper spacing ensures every tree gets maximum sunlight and root space.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ niyenii he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei kakadaji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa hulu la kɛ shishifãi babaoo.

english: How do I ensure the fruits I harvest will be suitable for fruit processing factories to buy?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ aduawai ni mikpaa lɛ baafee nɔ ni sa kɛha aduawai ahe nitsumɔhe ni mahe yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Factories look for specific fruit varieties with uniform size, good juice content, and no disease damage. Using recommended seeds and proper field care ensures your crop meets factory buying standards.
ga: Nitsumɔhei taoɔ aduawai srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ ni amɛdalɛ tamɔ amɛhe. Good amount of juice and without damage from disease Using recommended seeds and proper site care help ensure your crops meet factory-purchased standards.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain saturates the soil and stops the roots from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛkaye niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow small and produce small harvests when I plant my maize and cassava very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daaa fioo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ beni miduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots fight under the soil for water and nutrients, while their leaves block sunlight from reaching one another. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and light to grow big.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and wilt in the afternoon heat even when the soil still feels moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it from the soil. The plant wilts on purpose to protect itself from losing more water, and it will normally stand back up when the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ shi yɛ yiŋtoo ko hewɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ amɛhe lɛ he. Ni bei pii lɛ, tsei teɔ shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃i ba.

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer on my crop after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo midumɔ nii lɛ amli beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer is best applied when young plants have already grown roots strong enough to eat the food, usually two to three weeks after planting. Applying it too early can burn tiny roots or waste the fertilizer before the plant can use it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye nii. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee otsii 2-3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Using it too quickly can cause small roots. Eshãa loo efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛtsu nii.

english: Flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. When night temperatures are too high, tomato plants also struggle to set fruit from their flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ, kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ gbɛkɛ. Tomato tsei hu baaná naagba yɛ yibii ni amɛwoɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I clear away all the large shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikpaa cacao tsei wuji lɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Shade trees act like living umbrellas that shield young cocoa from sunburn, keep the air humid, and prevent the soil around the cocoa roots from drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. Kwɛmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni otsi shikpɔŋ ni bɔle kookoo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ naa koni ekagbi.

english: Cassava roots need loose, uncompacted soil so they can easily expand into thick tubers. If the soil is too hard, or if the soil lacks potassium, the plant cannot store enough food in its roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni enyɛ eda ni etsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ato niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my plantain trees turn brown and dry up while the fruit is growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Plantain plants naturally direct their energy away from older lower leaves to feed the growing top leaves and fruit bunch. However, if many leaves dry up at once, it could mean the plant needs more water or is affected by leaf spots.
ga: Plantains lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai kɛ aduawai akui ni miida lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai babaoo gĩ shikome lɛ, Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo he miihia tso lɛ loo baa he ŋmɔtɔ enaa enɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my groundnuts so much more than other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa mi-peanuts lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ babaoo fe tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and quickly steal food, water, and sunlight from groundnuts. Groundnuts also need clean, soft soil around them so their flowering pegs can push down into the ground to produce nuts.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ oya. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ hu he miihia ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni anyɛ ashɛ efɔfɔi lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ ŋmeii aba.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba?

english: Heavy rain can wash granular fertilizer off the field or push it too deep into the soil where plant roots cannot reach it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after rain so it can dissolve safely near the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji granular fertilizer lɛ kɛjɛ saatso lɛ nɔ loo ekɛshwie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ koni enyɛ efo shweshweeshwe yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside your cocoa creates a living umbrella that keeps the young plants cool, moist, and protected.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i, ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe.

english: Which side of the cassava stem cutting should point upward when I plant it in the field?
ga: Kasava tso lɛ fã ni afo lɛ fã ni esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛji akɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: The small buds or nodes on the stem must always point upward toward the sky. Planting cassava stems upside down forces the shoots to grow backward, leading to weak plants and very small tuber yields.
ga: fɔfɔii bibii loo nodes Esa akɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kasava ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya sɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Is it really necessary to erect tall sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni ato tsei kakadaji ahe gbɛjianɔ koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, staking yam vines lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the growing underground tubers, while also preventing leaf rot diseases.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ baa ni fiteɔ lɛ hu naa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps bring back the green color and improves growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ nitrogen. ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil richer for my next maize crop?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen from the air and traps it in their roots. When the plant roots decay in the soil, they release that stored nitrogen for the next crop to feed on.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛjieɔ amɛ nitrogen ni amɛto lɛ koni tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aye.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer onto dry soil when there is no rain expected?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko lɛ?

english: Fertilizers must dissolve in water before plant roots can drink them in. Applying fertilizer to dry soil during hot weather can burn the crop's roots or cause the fertilizer to evaporate into the air.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the center funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides in the central leaf whorl of corn. Applying recommended bio-pesticides or a neem leaf extract mixture directly into the center funnel early in the morning will clear them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii ateŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ wo tsɔne ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaha tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baaje mli.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids hidden under the leaves. Spraying your crop with neem oil or insecticidal soap removes the pests so normal leaves can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi lɛ koni baai ni sa lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch around the base of the plant helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba daa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Should I trim off the extra shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Ani ajie plantain tsei titrii lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving too many suckers causes them to compete with the mother plant for food and water, leading to smaller bunches. It is best to keep only one mother plant, one medium sucker, and one small follower per stand.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii babaoo ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa amɛkɛ tso nyɛ lɛ yeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii baa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ kome pɛ, tso lɛ shishifã kome ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ, kɛ sɛɛnyiɛlɔ bibioo kome yɛ shidaamɔhe fɛɛ shidaamɔhe.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the crop the energy it needs to grow green leaves again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my field when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Plant roots can only drink in nutrients when there is water in the soil. Applying fertilizer to dry earth leaves the chemical resting on top where it can burn the plant roots or blow away before rain comes.
ga: Tse shishifãi baanyɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ pɛ kɛji nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baashi tsofai ni eshwɛ yɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã loo kɔɔyɔɔ atswa dani nugbɔ lɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun and lose moisture quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy that protects the seedlings while their roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi, ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baa yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ ema shi lɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava stems when setting up a field?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ he tɛŋŋ kɛ́ adu shikpɔŋ ko?

english: Cassava stems should be planted about one meter apart from each other. This space allows the underground tubers enough room to spread out and grow big without competing with neighboring plants for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe aaafee mita kome. Nɛkɛ he nɛɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ etswaaa akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why is it important to support my yam vines with wood stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei ni akɛfee tsei lɛ afi mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce energy. Lifting the leaves off the ground with stakes helps the plant catch sunshine, which makes the underground yam tubers grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ wuji babaoo.

english: What causes ragged holes in my corn leaves with tiny worms hiding inside?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-abele baa lɛ mli ewo bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii? ni akɛtee mli

english: This damage comes from the Fall Armyworm, a pest common across Ghana that eats young corn stems and leaves. Spragging approved biological treatments or neem water early in the morning when the caterpillars are active helps clear them out.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ jɛ Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ Ghana fɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii kɛ baai lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛ neem nu wo mli leebi be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miitsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits rot and turn black before turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato aduawai ashishi lɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani etsɔɔ etsuru lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, happen when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular water. Keeping the soil evenly damp and adding lime or organic manure prevents the fruit tissue from breaking down.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo amɛnáa nu be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ lime loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ehaa aduawai amli fãji lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crop plants right after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that naturally react faster to water and steal plant food from the soil before your crops can. Clearing weeds early ensures all the rain and soil nutrients go directly into growing your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛfeɔ oya kɛji amɛnu nu he, ni amɛjuɔ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ afee nakai. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛduɔ onibii.

english: Why do flowers drop off my pepper plants without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme sun heat, dry soil, or a lack of friendly insects like bees to transfer pollen. Regular watering during hot periods helps the plant hold onto its blossoms so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hulu la ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo kɛji kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo tamɔ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ajie fɔfɔi lɛ aha tso lɛ bɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Having too many suckers causes them all to fight for the same food and soil moisture, resulting in small plantains. Keeping only one strong stem alongside the mother tree ensures all nutrients go into producing one large, heavy bunch.
ga: Shikpɔŋhosomɔi babaoo haa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa amɛfeɔ plantains bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to nyɛ lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii lɛ fɛɛ afee tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and crisp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle full, direct sunlight. They need shade trees or food crops like plantain planted beside them to shield their delicate leaves from sun damage until their roots are well established.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛdu tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei, tamɔ plantains, ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni akɛbu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatswa shi shiŋŋ.

english: When plants are crowded, they stretch upward to fight each other for sunlight instead of using their energy to grow strong stems and large fruits or roots.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Ebaakpã mli koni ekɛ hulu la atswa akaŋ moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛdu tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai loo shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines off the ground using tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ atsu nii ni mikɛdu mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking holds yam leaves up toward the sun so they can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the underground tubers, while also keeping the leaves off damp soil where diseases spread.
ga: Hiɛ staking lɛ kɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ni okwɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ koni onine ashɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ ni okɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ he ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and soft during the heavy rainy season around August?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ August mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain and high dampness create ideal conditions for a fungal disease called black pod to thrive and spread rapidly across damp cocoa pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ aya hiɛ ni egbɛ eshwa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce smaller cobs when I plant them late in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Maize needs steady soil moisture while developing cobs. Late-planted maize runs out of water before the cobs finish growing because the main rains stop too early.
ga: Abɛi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be be mli ni ŋmei lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ. Abɛi ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ nu lɛ baaho dani ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ nugbɔ titri ni nɛɔ lɛ kpaɔ mra tsɔ.

english: Why do cassava roots rot in the ground if heavy rain floods the farm for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Waterlogged soil blocks oxygen from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate and rot underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ naa. ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year when I farm on the same land without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ mitsu okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Every crop harvest removes essential nutrients from the soil. Continuous planting without adding manure, fertilizer, or leaving the land to rest exhausts these food reserves.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo he ko ni akɛjɔɔ he fataaa he. Ebaaha niyenii ni ato nɛɛ afite.

english: Why do the center leaves of my young maize plants look shredded with leaves full of holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by caterpillars like fall armyworms, which crawl inside the central shoot during the day and eat the soft growing leaves from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ cutworms ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Efoɔ ehe kɛboteɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni eyeɔ baai bibii lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by hot, dry weather or a lack of water to conserve energy and survive the heat.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi hao amɛ. aloo nu ni bɛ ni akɛbaakwɛ hewalɛ nɔ ni akɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop seedlings right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have deep, wild roots that soak up water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated seedlings, which is why early clearing is needed so your crops aren't choked.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe dumɔwui ni adu. Nɔ ni haa ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ mra lɛ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbɔjɔ.

english: Why is it important to measure the distance between my maize plants instead of just scattering the seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masusu bɔ ni mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ he moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Proper spacing gives each maize plant enough room, sunlight, water, and nutrients from the soil to grow strong. If seeds are planted too close together, they fight for nutrients and produce very small ears.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa he lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ ni ehaa toi bibii waa baa.

english: What happens if I plant my pepper seedlings too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu pepper dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, air cannot pass between them easily, which creates a humid environment where diseases and mold spread quickly, reducing your harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ tsei nɛɛ ateŋ mlɛo. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa ni helai kɛ ŋmeii gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I drop only two seeds per hole when planting cowpea?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui enyɔ pɛ yɛ bu kome mli kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmei?

english: Dropping two seeds ensures that if one seed fails to germinate, the second one will sprout. Leaving more than two seeds causes the young plants to crowd each other out.
ga: Dumɔwui enyɔ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha kɛji eko kwɛɛɛ lɛ, Dumɔwu ni ji enyɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ oshi dumɔwui ni fa fe 2 yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ afee ekome.

english: How do I know the right amount of fertilizer to give to my crops so I do not destroy them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni mikafite lɛ?

english: Crops need balanced nutrients to grow properly. Using too much fertilizer can burn the crop's roots and kill the plant, while using too little will not boost growth, so measuring the right dose based on your field size protects your plants.
ga: Niyenii ni ja he miihia tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso shishifãi lɛ ashã ni amɛgboi. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haaa tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ lɛ, kɛ́ osusu bɔ ni sa lɛ he yɛ bɔ ni oduɔ nii lɛ da ha lɛ naa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my farm soil feel hard and dry even after a short rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ewa ni egbi yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Hard soil usually lacks organic matter such as compost or decomposed manure. Organic matter acts like a sponge in the soil to trap and hold rainwater for plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ ahi tsei shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves during heavy rain usually mean the soil is waterlogged, which chokes the roots and prevents them from taking up essential nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen.

english: Flowers often drop when the crop suffers from heat stress, a sudden lack of water, or insufficient pollination, preventing the plant from forming fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihe dɔlɛ. nu ni faaa trukaa loo pollin ni fa bɔ ni sa Haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii.

english: Why does my local variety of maize take longer to mature than the hybrid seeds bought from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ ŋmãa srɔtoi lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ fe dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to grow fast and mature early within a specific number of weeks, whereas traditional varieties naturally follow a longer growth cycle.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛdara oya yɛ otsii pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni kusum mli henɔi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛdaraa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are getting too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo tsɔ?

english: When tomato plants receive excess water, their leaves start to curl downward, look pale or yellowish, and the skin of the fruit may crack open before ripening.
ga: Kɛji tomato tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Ebaai lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni tso yibii lɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ atse dani ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to quickly absorb water and nutrients under tough conditions, while cultivated crops grow more slowly and need protection from weeds to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni adu lɛ daa blɛoo, ni ehe miihia ni abu he kɛjɛ jwɛi ahe koni amɛshwere.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their young leaves burn and dry out quickly. Leaving a few tall shade trees or planting plantains beside them creates a cool environment that protects the young trees until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ lɛ Dumɔ tsei fioo komɛi loo dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings rot in the soil while others grow into strong plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu miida ni amɛmiifee tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings rot when they are planted upside down or cut from diseased plants. Planting healthy, mature cuttings right-side up with the growth buds pointing toward the sky allows the plant to take root properly.
ga: Yucca tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ atsɔ hiɛ atsɔ hiɛ loo afolɔ kɛjɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ adu tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda ni amɛkwɛ ŋwɛi ni amɛshishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etswa shishifãi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my young crops when the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ be mli ni nugbɔ jeɔ shishi?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and will steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients your crops need to start strong. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food available in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛje shishi jogbaŋŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to make green leaves. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn dark green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni edara oya.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flower stems down into the ground after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ashishi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants form their pods underground rather than on the branches. Once the flower is pollinated, the stem grows downward and pushes into loose soil where the peanut pod can safely expand.
ga: Peanut tsei lɛ feɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ fe tsei lɛ aniji anɔ. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔi pollin lɛ Tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shishi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ mli. ni ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã shweshweeshwe

english: Why should I prune some of the shoots growing around the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they all compete for the same food and water in the soil. Removing all but one or two strong shoots allows the main plant to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tso kome ŋmeii fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii mli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the undersides of the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or recommended sprays keeps new leaves growing flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ tso lɛ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua baai heei ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in dark, overly wet, and humid conditions. Pruning extra shade branches to let sunlight and air pass through your farm helps dry out the pods and prevents the fungus from taking over.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ. too wet and has humidity Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo ni oookpa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaaha ŋmeii akaye nɔ.

english: Why do I see ragged holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the funnels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu ni etse ehe yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ? ni akɛtee yɛ kɔni lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the center of the maize plant to eat tender leaves. Applying recommended treatments directly into the central funnel of the plant destroys the caterpillars before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaakpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets too hot or lacks water during the flowering stage. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots during dry spells helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ mli dɔ tsɔ loo nu faaa yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow root systems that lose water quickly under harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy that protects the young trees from sun damage and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize on the same field at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly and takes up to a year. This allows you to harvest two crops without them competing heavily for sunlight and space.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo ni ekɛ afi tsuɔ nii lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ hulu la kɛ ŋwɛi akaŋ waa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient plants need to produce green leaves and grow strong. Applying compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer can help restore healthy leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my vegetable plants help them survive dry periods?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te mi-aduawai lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass, known as mulching, acts as a protective shield. It traps moisture in the ground, reduces water evaporation from sunlight, and keeps the soil cooler so the roots stay healthy during hot weather.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ jwɛi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Etsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ehaa nu ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ baa shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli

english: Why do my sweet potato plants produce long green vines but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ miiwo wain tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes sweet potato plants to put all their energy into leafy top growth rather than underground tubers. Using balanced soil nutrients with higher potassium encourages the plant to store energy in the roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli moŋ fe shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ mli niyenii ni ja ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa trees to turn black and dry up?
ga: Mɛni miiha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungal infection that thrives in damp, shaded conditions with poor air movement. Pruning shade trees and cocoa branches lets in light and airflow, while removing affected pods prevents the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ aya jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Shade tsei kɛ kookoo niji ni afoɔ lɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and showing tiny insects underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni kooloi bibii yɔɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like whiteflies or aphids feeding on the leaves. Spraying the plants with a mixture of water and neem seed extract or mild soap solution can naturally control these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni yeɔ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu kɛ neem dumɔwu mli nu loo samla ni mli ejɔ ni akɛfutuɔ tsei ahe. Abaanyɛ akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need to spread their leaves in full sunlight to produce energy for tuber growth. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground, preventing leaf diseases and allowing maximum sunlight exposure for bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulb lɛ dalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tso helai anaa ni ehaa hulu la ni fa babaoo baa bulb wuji lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before growing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani eduɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience environmental stress, such as extreme heat, lack of water, or sudden nutrient imbalances. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying mulch reduces plant stress and helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ trukaa lɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe haomɔ aba shi, ni ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Cassava is generally ready for harvest when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can carefully test one plant by digging up a single root to check if it has grown thick and starchy before harvesting the rest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ oka tso kome okwɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ shishifã kome ni oootsi koni ona kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ dani okpa nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds sprout back so quickly right after I finish clearing my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya nɔŋŋ beni akpa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds produce thousands of seeds that hide in the soil. When you clear the bush, sunlight and air reach the ground, which signals those buried seeds that it is time to germinate and grow.
ga: Jwɛi woɔ dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji otsi jwɛi lɛ mli lɛ Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ be ni nakai dumɔwui ni afu lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛdara.

english: Is it better for my crops if I burn the cleared bush or leave it to rot on the farm?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mishã jwɛi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ loo miha amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Leaving cleared plant material to decompose on your farm creates mulch. Mulch keeps the soil moist during hot days, prevents weeds from growing, and rots into natural plant food, whereas burning destroys useful nutrients.
ga: Tso mli nibii ni ajie lɛ ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛfite yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Mulch yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efite ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ be mli ni shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize turning yellow instead of healthy dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually show that your crop is missing nitrogen, a main plant nutrient. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen too deep into the ground where young roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri ko bɛ otso lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do some of my crops grow tall and strong on one part of my farm while the same crops stay stunted on another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? yɛ be mli ni nakai ŋmɔshi nii lɛ nɔŋŋ kã he ehi shi yɛ fã kroko mli lɛ?

english: Soil nutrition and depth change across different spots on the same land. Areas with stunted plants usually have harder ground, higher water pooling, or fewer nutrients than the fertile parts.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ emlibotemɔ tsakeɔ yɛ hei srɔtoi. yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ Hei ni tsei ni egbɔjɔ yɔɔ lɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa fe tsutsu lɛ nɔ. Nu jɛɛhe ko ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. aloo eyɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo fe fã ni woɔ fɔ lɛ

english: If I plant my seeds very close to each other, will I harvest more crops from my small land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. Ani manyɛ maná mi nɔ babaoo?

english: No, planting too close forces plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak stalks and very small or empty fruits instead of a large harvest.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli yɛ ŋmaa babaoo najiaŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and curl up in the hot afternoon even when the ground feels damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ

english: On very hot afternoons, leaves lose water to the hot air faster than roots can drink it up. Curling leaves is the plant's way of shrinking its surface to save water until the sun cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu. Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛfoɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu nu he kɛyashi hulu lɛ baajɔ.

english: In dry weather, wild plants die off, so hungry insects travel to your farmed crops for moisture and food. Warm temperatures also cause insect eggs to hatch faster.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, koo mli tsei gboiɔ, ni kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ yaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ amli koni amɛyatao ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii. Dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ hu haa kooloi awɔlɔi fɔɔ oya.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting while they are still attached to the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ he lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in heavy shade and high humidity. Pruning overgrown tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry the farm and reduce fungal rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is my farm producing smaller harvests every year even though I plant the exact same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the earth time to recover. Rotating different crops restores balanced soil strength.
