ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ ni ja lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed their flowers before setting any seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani edu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops flowers when affected by heat or lack of moisture. This is normal plant behavior and does not reduce your yield, as cassava stores its main harvest underground in the roots.
ga: Cassava baajie efɔfɔi lɛ kɛjɛ ehe kɛji dɔlɛ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ ná enɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ ji tso lɛ subaŋ ni yaa nɔ daa ni ebaahaŋ onibii ni owoɔ lɛ aba shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei kɛ eŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my young maize plants are getting enough water and food from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miiná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy maize plants have broad, dark green leaves that stand firm in the morning. If the leaves start curling up, turning pale green, or showing yellow tips, it means the crop is suffering from a lack of water or key soil nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Abɛi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ, ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ nii waa, ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ leebi. Kɛji baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔ Eji eŋɔli ni mli tse. loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing bright yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kpɛɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are clear signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. This sickness weakens the plant and prevents it from growing large roots underground.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela lɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaaa shishifãi wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up when I clear all the shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive under strong direct sunshine. Without shade trees or food crops like plantains to protect them, the intense sun burns their soft leaves and dries out the soil around their roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains bɛ ni baabu tso lɛ he lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle eshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ agbi.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of plant food in the soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist and well-fed helps the flowers stay on and turn into healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei amli ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be ni eyeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy and ready for planting before the rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu nii dani nugbɔ aje shishi nɛ?

english: Healthy soil is dark, feels soft and moist when you squeeze it, crumbles easily, and has earthworms living in it. Hard, pale, or cracked soil lacks organic matter and needs compost or manure mixed in before planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ su ni tsuɔ. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ amɔ lɛ, efoɔ oya ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii. Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli tse, loo ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afutu mli dani adu.

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so that plant roots can drink it in. If you apply fertilizer to hot, dry soil, it will burn the roots and evaporate into the air, wasting your effort and money.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni tso shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛji okɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi wo mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baashã ni amɛbaatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ shika fitemɔ baa.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin, weak stalks that fall easily in strong winds and produce small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛnáa tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ, amɛgbeeɔ shi oya ni amɛfeɔ tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when there are weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo be mli ni jwɛi ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the light, water, and plant food intended for your harvest. Clearing weeds early allows your crop roots to absorb all the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaakpa lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I know that my groundnuts are ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ efee klalo akɛ makpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the leaves begin to turn yellow and dry up. You can test dig two or three plants—if the inside of the shell has dark brown spots and the nuts are full, it is time to harvest.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Obaanyɛ oka tsei fioo komɛi okwɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ eyi lɛ, no lɛ be eshɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: When is the right time to heap soil for my yam mounds after the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ ato shikpɔŋ kɛha sweet potato yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should make your yam mounds immediately after the first steady rains fall, while the soil is soft and workable. Planting seed yams in moist mounds gives the roots a head start before the heavy rains come.
ga: Esa akɛ ofee sweet potatoes akuu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ lolo ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii. Sweet potato dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi dani nugbɔ ni naa wa baa.

english: Why do my crops grow well on some parts of my land but die on the sandy parts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hei komɛi shi amɛgboiɔ yɛ ŋã hei lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has large spaces between its grains, so water and nutrients wash away quickly before plant roots can drink them. Richer ground contains fine organic matter that holds onto moisture and plant food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛjegbɛi wuji yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ oya dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ nibii kpakpai ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei amli niyenii mli hewalɛ hiɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land is fertile enough for me to plant food crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ baa nii bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu niyenii?

english: Good agricultural land usually has dark, soft soil that crumbles easily in your hand and holds moisture well, showing that it is packed with decomposed plant matter that feeds your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni fiteɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tsei ni egboi ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ.

english: Is it harmful to burn the bush on my land before I clear it for planting?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ mashã jwɛi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani majie nɔ koni adu nii?

english: Burning kills beneficial soil organisms and destroys natural plant leaves that would otherwise rot and fertilize your land, leaving the ground dry and easy for rain to wash away.
ga: Shãa gbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei ahe baai ni baanyɛ agbo ni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbiɔ ni nugbɔ shwieɔ nɔ oya.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: When the sun is very hot, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil, causing them to temporarily droop until the weather cools down.
ga: Beni hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Plants drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients, choosing to save their energy to stay alive rather than produce fruit.
ga: Tsei baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa, loo sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Amɛhalaa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ hewalɛ nɔ koni amɛhi wala mli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have weak leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, shading the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo kɛhaa kookoo bibii kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very thin and produce small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miidara waa ni amɛmiiwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves compete fiercely with each other for light, water, and soil food, leaving no extra energy to form big fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ kɛha niyenii. Hewalɛ ko bɛ ni eshwɛ ni akɛbaafee aduawai wuji.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that bakes the ground, which will kill young seedlings before the main rains arrive to keep the soil consistently wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ gbeɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my farm than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to the local environment, making them faster and aggressive at stealing sunlight, water, and nutrients from your domestic crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ebɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ kɛjɛɔ omaŋ tsei lɛ amli lɛ mli.

english: Groundnuts have a unique way of growing where the flower pollinates above ground, and then grows a long stem called a 'peg' that burrows into the soil to form the actual nut underground where it is protected.
ga: Peanuts yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekwɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, eyɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘peg’ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efeɔ nut diɛŋtsɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he ni abuɔ he yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my harvested groundnut shells end up empty with no nuts inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi efee efolo ni ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods, often called 'pops,' usually happen when the soil lacks calcium or water while the pods are developing underground, preventing the seed inside from forming properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pea pods’ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium loo nu yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miiya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut leaves fold up tightly during the middle of the day when the sun is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants fold their leaves during hot weather to reduce water loss through evaporation, helping the plant conserve moisture and survive high heat.
ga: Peanut tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young groundnut plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-peanut dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen or iron, or that the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe and absorb food.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen loo dade. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii.

english: Does planting groundnuts in my field help make the soil better for other crops like maize afterwards?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the ground for the next crop you plant.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: How can I tell underground groundnuts are mature and ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can check maturity by pulling up a few test plants; if the inside of the pods has turned dark brown or black instead of white, the crop is mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji oyɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ kaa tsei fioo komɛi ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: What causes my groundnut pods to spoil and turn dark while they are still in the ground?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-peanut ŋmɔtɔi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ duŋ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Pods turn dark and spoil in the dirt when left in soil that is too wet for too long near harvest time, allowing soil fungi and moisture rot to destroy the pods.
ga: Pods lɛ feɔ ediŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ tsɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ebɛŋkɛ kpamɔ be lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbo ni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do companies that buy groundnuts care so much about how dry the nuts are?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsumɔhei ni heɔ ŋmeii lɛ susuɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ ni egbi lɛ he waa lɛ?

english: Buyers need well-dried groundnuts because extra wetness makes the nuts spoil fast, taste bitter, and develop dangerous molds that make food unsafe for consumers.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ miisumɔ ŋmeii ni egbi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmeii ni fa babaoo lɛ haa amɛgboɔ oya, amɛmli ŋɔɔ, ni amɛnáa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ oshara ni haa niyenii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ.

english: How does bad mold get onto my groundnuts after harvest, and why does it ruin them for buyers?
ga: Te tsɛŋemɔ hela fɔŋ baanyɛ atswa mi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ?

english: Mold grows when wet groundnuts are stored in warm, poorly ventilated places, producing a invisible poison called aflatoxin that makes the nuts toxic and unacceptable to food processing companies.
ga: Mold baanyɛ adara kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ to he ko ni mli edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsofa ko ni anaaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ aflatoxin lɛ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni nitsumɔhei ni feɔ niyenii lɛ ekpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to dry my harvested groundnuts directly on the bare dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Drying groundnuts directly on soil exposes them to dirt, moisture, and fungal spores from the ground, which lowers the quality and makes them less attractive to buyers.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, muji, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ sumɔɔɔ.

english: Officer, why do I need to plant plantain trees next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Officer Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ emasɛi? Mi kokoo tso bibioo lɛ hu?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that dry out easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide broad shade and keep the air humid, giving the young cocoa trees time to establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo babaoo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ náa be koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of big green leaves, but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess water early in the season, the cassava plant spends all its energy building stems and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ etsitsi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to grow big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ koni ekɛ bulbs agboi akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing large tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground into the light, improves air flow, and prevents soil-borne diseases from ruining the leaves.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni miida. Staking baaha baai lɛ ateshi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya la lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ Ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient, or that excessive water in the soil is suffocating the roots and preventing them from taking up plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛye tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking the leaf juices, or by a plant virus they spread, which damages the leaf structure as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ bɔ ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ha beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why are there holes in the leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the center funnels of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ bu yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which crawl into the tender inner leaves (funnel) of the maize plant to feed and leave behind their waste material.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii (cones) ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ amli lɛ ahe okadi koni amɛtao niyenii ni amɛshi jwɛi.

english: My tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but why do the blossoms dry up and drop off without forming any fruit?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgbeɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures become too high or when plants experience water stress from dry spells, which disrupts pollination before the fruit can set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei naa nu he haomɔ kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination naa dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Covering the soil (mulching) keeps the ground cool, traps moisture during dry days so roots stay hydrated, slows down weed growth, and eventually rots into food for the soil.
ga: Mulching (mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli Koni shishifãi lɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ Haa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ ni etsɔɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and stunted even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than many young crops, so they steal the fertilizer, ground water, and sunlight before your main crops have a chance to drink or eat.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei bibii. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la dani otsei titrii lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛnu loo amɛyeɔ.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to plant my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo kɛha mi akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry gap before steady rains begin. Planting right after the first rain can cause seeds to sprout and then wither away from lack of continuous water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ yaa nɔ nɛɔ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgboi yɛ nu ni bɛ ni yaa nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow and wilting even when I water them with river water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ faa mli nu shwieɔ amɛnɔ moŋ?

english: If river water contains toxic chemicals or heavy mud from upstream mining, it can damage the roots and block them from absorbing nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow and wilt despite getting wet.
ga: Kɛji tsofai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo sũ ni tsii ni jɛ faa lɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa mli lɛ yɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ Ebaanyɛ efite shishifãi lɛ ni etsi niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛji amɛfɔ po.

english: Which crops can I plant on my farm if the nearby water source dries up completely?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nu jɛɛhe ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli egbi kwraa?

english: Crops like cassava, sweet potatoes, millet, and cowpeas have deep root systems or low water requirements, allowing them to survive and produce food even when water sources are dry.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo nu ni he ehiaaa tsɔ. Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ niyenii kɛji nu jɛɛhei lɛ egbi po.

english: How does dirty, muddy water from nearby mining sites affect the way my vegetables grow?
ga: Te nu ni mli ewo muji kɛ sũ ni jɛɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ saa mi-aduawai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Muddy water coats the soil surface and root systems with fine silt, which suffocates the roots by cutting off oxygen and preventing the plant from taking up essential plant nutrients.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ, ni ehaaa tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small and tough when the soil becomes very dry and hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe wa be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi waa ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Cassava plants slow down tuber expansion in dry, hard soil because the roots cannot easily push through hard ground, and the plant spends its energy keeping its leaves alive instead of swelling its roots.
ga: Cassava tsei haa tuber lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ baa shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wa nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa mli mlɛo. Ni tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai lɛ akafite moŋ fe ni amɛaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Can I still grow good crops if the soil on my land has become hard and baked like brick?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lolo? Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli wa ni etswa tamɔ brikii?

english: Hard ground makes it difficult for young plant roots to push through and hold water. Adding animal manure, compost, or decaying plant leaves softens the soil, improves moisture retention, and restores life to the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ wa, ni no haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi akɛ amɛaatsɔ mli ni amɛhiɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishifã, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsei ahe baai ni egboi fata he lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ afee blɛoo. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ni oha wala aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into thin tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rolling leaves is a plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve water. By rolling up, the maize plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun and traps moisture inside the leaf.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he. kɛji akɛ abɔle ehe Abɛi tsei lɛ haa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I irrigate them with water that smells strange or has an unusual color?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ loo su ni yɔɔ srɔto wo mitsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Water with strange smells or colors often carries dangerous pollutants or chemicals that can burn crop roots, stunt plant growth, cause leaf spots, and make harvested produce unsafe to eat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nibii ni fiteɔ nii loo tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi yɛ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ loo su ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ mli. tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ kɛ baai lɛ ahe tsɔi baa ni ehaa nibii ni akpaa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are dying from lack of water or because the soil is damaged by chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miigboi yɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ loo tsofai efite shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Water shortage causes leaves to droop and dry evenly from the edges, while chemical soil damage often causes dark blotches on leaves, sudden leaf drop, or rotten root tips even when the ground feels moist.
ga: Nu ni bɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni tsofai fiteɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ anɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Baai lɛ gbee shi trukaa Aloo shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fite eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ moŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the ground around them dries out completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that depend on moist, packed soil to stay anchored. When the soil loses all moisture, it becomes loose and powdery, making the heavy plantain stem lose its grip and fall.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, ni mli wa nɔ kɛha ŋshɔŋlooi. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ fite lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaafee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa plantain tsei ni tsii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi.

english: Is it safe for me to plant food crops on land where gold washing or pit digging took place nearby?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni shika tsuru ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ loo bu ni atsaa lɛ bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Land near gold washing often contains heavy mud and harmful substances like mercury that can poison crops or render food unsafe. The soil needs to be tested, treated with rich organic manure, or left to recover before safe planting can happen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ hei ni afɔɔ shika tsuru he yɛ lɛ yɛ muji ni tsii kɛ nibii ni yɔɔ oshara tamɔ mercury, ni baanyɛ aha tsei awui loo eha niyenii akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. Esa akɛ aka shikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo atsu he nii. Aloo shi ni ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ dani abaanyɛ adu lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight damages their tender leaves. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains provides protection and keeps the soil moist while the young cocoa trees get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ amɛbaai bibii lɛ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he ni ehiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ amaa shi lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers during dry spells to conserve water and survive. Adequate soil moisture is needed for the tree to hold its blossoms and turn them into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia koni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Will cutting off branches from my cocoa tree hurt my pod yield?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni mifoɔ lɛ baaná mi-pod lɛ yibiiwoo lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: Proper pruning actually increases yield. Removing extra or diseased branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the middle of the tree, which prevents fungal diseases and encourages better pod growth.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa, ni ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm's soil is running out of nutrients for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa miduɔ nii?

english: If your trees grow very slowly, have pale or yellowish leaves, or produce fewer pods despite getting enough rain, the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, or potassium.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ daa blɛoo waa Ehiɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ Aloo ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo eyɛ mli akɛ no yɛ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus loo potassium.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly wet conditions when rain splashes fungal spores from the ground onto lower pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine lɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ŋmeii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: What is causing dark patches on my young branches and making the shoots dry up?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni kɛ okadii diji ni yɔɔ miniji bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ miigbi?

english: This damage is usually caused by capsids (mirids), small insects that suck sap from the branches and pods, injecting toxins that cause shoots to wither and die back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji capsids (mirids), ni ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei aniji kɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Okɛ tsofai fɔji ni haa ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ awo mli.

english: Cassava is an aggressive feeder that takes too much water and nutrients away from young cocoa roots. It is better to intercrop with plantain or cocoyam, which provide beneficial shade without suffocating the young cocoa.
ga: Cassava ji niyenii ni mli wa waa ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo ni jɛɔ kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii tsɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu plantain loo kookoo, ni haa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni ehaaa kookoo bibioo lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: How do cocoa flowers turn into pods if there are no big bees around?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii kɛji ŋmeii wuji bɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers are pollinated by tiny biting insects called midges. Keeping a layer of decomposing leaf litter on the ground provides a breeding habitat for these beneficial insects.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni shwieɔ mɔ lɛ woɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egboi lɛ eko to shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ fɔɔ yɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm give me two different harvests in a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii sɔrɔtoi shii enyɔ yɛ afi kome mli lɛ?

english: Ghana experiences two distinct rainy seasons each year. The main rainy season triggers the primary, larger harvest (main crop), while the shorter rains produce a secondary, smaller harvest (light crop).
ga: Ghana yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ bei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ daa afi. Nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ kɛ shishijee ŋmaa babaoo baa (ŋmɔshi nibii titrii), yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuji lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ lɛ baa bibioo (ŋmɔshi nibii ni waaa).

english: How do tall weeds around my trees affect my cocoa pods?
ga: Te jwɛi kakadaji ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ saa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer and water from the soil that your cocoa trees need. They also trap humidity around the trunk, creating a breeding ground for pests and pod-rotting fungal diseases.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ sũ ni he hiaa o-cacao tsei lɛ amli. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ hu shwieɔ tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ fɔɔ yɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and scorching in the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiishã yɛ latsaa be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside your cocoa provides a canopy that protects the young seedlings until they grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip and moving down the central vein usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will restore their bright green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ naagbee kɛyaa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ adara. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi lɛ aku sɛɛ afee eŋɔli ni mli tse.

english: Cowpeas and other leguminous plants have tiny organisms on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest the cowpeas and leave the roots to decay, that stored nutrient remains in the soil to feed your next maize crop naturally.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Nibii bibii komɛi yɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa tsina ŋmei ni oha shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, Niyenii ni ato lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha oŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it bad to apply chemical fertilizer to my field when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa?

english: Crop roots can only absorb fertilizer when it is dissolved in soil moisture. Placing chemical fertilizer in dry soil can scorch and burn the plant's roots, while much of the fertilizer will be wasted or blown away before the rain comes.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ etsɔ shikpɔŋ mli nu mli pɛ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa dani nugbɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater collects in flat fields and cannot drain, it drowns the roots and encourages soil fungi that cause root rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows water to drain away safely.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu babaoo buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ajie nu lɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my mature plantain plants easily fall over in strong wind before I can harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that carry heavy weight. Underground pests like nematodes or banana weevils often destroy these root anchors, making the plant weak so that even mild winds can push the whole plant over.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni tsii. Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii Bei pii lɛ, amɛfiteɔ nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛyashiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa blɛoo Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsei lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ shi.

english: My tomato plants have a lot of flowers, so why are the flowers dropping off without producing fruit?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo. Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without making fruit when the plant faces extreme heat stress or irregular watering. When soil moisture drops suddenly during hot days, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ hulutsoo haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ kpe. Kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ ba shi trukaa yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking the sap from young leaves, or transmitting a virus. Spraying your pepper field with neem oil or appropriate protective spray helps eliminate these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ shwie ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do I harvest much smaller cobs when I plant my maize seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaa ŋmeii bibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmeii dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete aggressively for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space ensures every single stalk gets enough nutrients and sunlight to produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifã fɛɛ tso lɛ naa niyenii kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting and becoming soft while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living organisms that naturally enter a sleeping period after harvest. When stored in places with light and warmth, the tuber wakes up and uses its stored starch to grow new shoots, causing the yam flesh to shrink and soften.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ shihilɛ ni bɛ mli mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni hulu tsoɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ. Bulbs lɛ teɔ shi ni amɛkɛ starch ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ ŋmeii heei. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ loo lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaafee bɔdɔɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen fertilizer, or the ground is flooded with water, which stops the roots from breathing and taking up food from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ mumɔ ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to apply chemical fertilizer right when I put the seeds in the ground or wait until they sprout?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ oodu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ooomɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: It is best to wait about one to two weeks after sprouting when the plant has developed roots to absorb the food. Putting strong chemical fertilizer directly on seeds can burn and destroy them.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ beni tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ beni tso lɛ ená shishifãi ni ekɛbaaŋɔ niyenii lɛ. Tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why is extension officers always telling me not to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ wɔkadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into your soil naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsu nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know the right time to start sowing my maize seeds after the long dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije ŋmãa dumɔ shishi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ eho lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first light rain because the ground underneath is still hot and dry. Wait until you get two or three heavy rainfalls so the soil is deeply wet, preventing the seeds from baking.
ga: Kaadu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ, ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni edɔ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ shii fioo komɛi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkashã

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground in the farm before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani manyɛ mafo amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when rain water collects around them for too long without draining, causing fungal decay. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows water to run off safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua amɛhe naa. Be kakadaŋŋ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under the scorching hot sun. Plantains grow fast with big broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, shading the cocoa and keeping the soil moist for the first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or attacks from insects like mirids. The tree drops its flowers to save energy so it can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ atatu ni tswaa lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why must I put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants for the vines to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi koni wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves out in the sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to manufacture food, which is then sent down underground to grow large yam tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la mli. Hulu la haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, atsu amɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛyadu sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight shapes and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that hide under the leaves and suck out the juices, or by viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the soil lacks calcium or when watering is uneven, which prevents the tomato plant from pushing nutrients all the way to the tip of the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji akɛ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ bɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haaa tomato tso lɛ ashɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyashɛ aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build green leaves. It can also happen when the soil is soaked with too much water, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ nu babaoo ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why does my groundnut farm produce plenty of green leaves but very few pods underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Groundnuts put all their energy into leafy growth when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. To produce strong underground shells and seeds, the soil needs phosphorus and calcium instead of excess leaf-growing fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai lɛ adalɛ mli kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia phosphorus kɛ calcium yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai amli ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moist air they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do seeds planted under big trees fail to grow tall and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni adu yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ edaaa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Seeds need direct sunlight to produce food for themselves as they grow. Big tree canopies block the sunlight and their strong roots steal water and food from the small plants growing beneath them.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii be mli ni amɛ daraa lɛ. Tsei wuji lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa ni amɛshishifãi ni wa lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii lɛ amli. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi lɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and get yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches on cassava are symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Using healthy, disease-free stems for planting stops the sickness from spreading.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni ŋmei bibioo lɛ ji nɔ ni tereɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii kɛ́ adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, wet, and cool conditions. Clearing weeds and trimming overgrown cocoa branches allows air and sunlight inside the farm to dry out the pods and prevent rot.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ duŋ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hei ni mli ejɔ kɛ black pod hela baa. Kookoo tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛtsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Why are small holes appearing all over the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by fall armyworm caterpillars feeding on the soft tender leaves inside the central funnel. Catching them early by inspecting the middle of the plant helps control them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ŋmeii bibii amli. Amɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oye obua ni okudɔ amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does spear grass keep growing back on my field even after I cut it down completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi yaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mifo fɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Spear grass has deep underground stems called rhizomes that store food even when the top leaves are cut off. To clear it completely, you must dig up the underground stems or use a targeted weed treatment.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes ni kɛ niyenii toɔ beni afo ŋwɛi baai lɛ po sɛɛ. Kɛji oosumɔ ni ojie kwraa lɛ Ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out too much. Keeping the soil constantly moist with mulching helps the plant retain its flowers so they can form pepper fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ mulching ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose, and deep soil to push downward as they expand. If the soil is hard, stony, or packed tight, the growing tuber gets bent and misshapen as it tries to push past the hard dirt.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya mli be mli ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, Tsofai ni miida lɛ baabɔle amɛhe ni amɛbaafite beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know if my planted crop is sprouting without digging it up to check?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni mikɛtsuuu nii koni makwɛ?

english: You do not need to dig up or uproot your seeds to check on them. If you leave the plant alone in the moist soil, green shoots will naturally push through the ground surface on their own when ready.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni otsa loo ojie dumɔwui lɛ koni okwɛ. Kɛji akɛ oshi tso lɛ pɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ, Eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji efee klalo.

english: Will it harm my crops if I pull them out of the soil to see if they are growing properly?
ga: Ani ebaaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui kɛji migbala amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni mana kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lo?

english: Yes, pulling up young plants damages their delicate early growth. It is best to leave them undisturbed in the soil so they can naturally shoot up without losing their hold in the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso bibioo ko ni ajieɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ fiteɔ mra be mli dalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akagbala amɛ. Enɛ ji koni amɛnyɛ amɛtu kɛya ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkafite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: How long does a seed or stem usually sit in the soil before shoots appear above ground?
ga: Be enyiɛ dumɔwui loo tsei lɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: After planting, a crop sits quietly in the soil while developing roots underneath. Shoots will naturally appear above ground once the root base is established, so patience is key.
ga: Kɛ́ adu agbe naa lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ taraa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dioo yɛ be mli ni shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ eshishi. Tsobii baaje kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji ato shishitoo lɛ ama shi pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tsuishitoo he miihia.

english: Why are my newly planted crops failing to grow well and looking weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni midu ehee lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Crops struggle to grow when they have not developed proper roots to go deep into the ground. Without strong roots, the plant cannot take in water and food from the soil to thrive.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji amɛnáaa shishifãi ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara.

english: Why is root growth so important for a crop right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ he hiaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Roots act as the feeding system for the plant. If a crop cannot push roots into the ground, everything you plant will fail to thrive because it has no way to feed itself.
ga: Shishifãi tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ niyenii gbɛjianɔtoo. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛɛɛ atswa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ Nɔ Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni oduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ ejaakɛ enyɛŋ ekwɛ ehe kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english: What happens to my final harvest if the plant struggled to develop roots early on?
ga: Mɛni baaba minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo shishifãi mra?

english: If a plant fails to establish strong roots early, it will not grow well throughout its life, resulting in a very poor yield or unusable food at harvest time.
ga: Kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ afee shishifãi ni wa mra lɛ, Edaŋ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ewala be fɛɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo ni ehiii loo niyenii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why did the crop cuttings I shared with my neighbor fail to grow after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni mikɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ jaa lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When planting materials or cuttings are moved without established roots, they struggle to survive in the new soil unless given proper moisture and time to form roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aduɔ dumɔ nibii loo tsei ni afolɔ ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ bɛ mli lɛ, Ehe baahia ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ waa koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ. Ja aha lɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛ be ni sa koni ekɛfee shishifãi.

english: Can I move a young plant to a new part of my farm before it forms roots?
ga: Ani manyɛ majie tsei bibii kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ fã hee ko dani amɛshishifãi akwɛ̃?

english: Moving a plant before it has developed roots to take hold in the ground makes it very difficult for the plant to survive. It will likely fail to thrive in the new location.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tso ko dani eshishifãi lɛ emɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa ewaa waa kɛhaa tso lɛ akɛ eeehi shi. Ekolɛ enyɛŋ eshwere yɛ gbɛhe hee mli

english: How can I make sure that stem cuttings I put in the ground actually survive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ tsei niji ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baahi shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Stem cuttings need undisturbed soil and adequate moisture so they can focus on sending fresh roots down into the earth before trying to grow leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni afoɔ lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko gbaaa naa ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli. Enɛ ji koni anyɛ akɛ jwɛŋmɔ ama shishifãi heei lɛ amajemɔ nɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani aka baai akwɛ̃.

english: Why does a crop look like it is doing nothing in the ground for days after I plant it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efeee nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii komɛi yɛ be mli ni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Even when nothing is visible above ground, the plant is working under the soil to grow roots into the dirt. Once those roots are set, the shoots will suddenly sprout and grow fast.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ anyɛɛɛ ana nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ Tsei hu tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛwo shishifãi kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nakai shishifãi lɛ wo shishifãi lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaadara oya.

english: When planting cassava, does it matter which way up I stick the stem into the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei lɛ, ani gbɛ ni otsɔɔ nɔ oduɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia?

english: Yes, direction matters a lot. Cassava stems have tiny buds or 'eyes' pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the buds must bend around to grow up, which wastes the plant's energy, delays sprouting, and leads to small, weak tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛtsɔɔmɔ he miihia waa. Cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ Esa akɛ abɔle tso lɛ yibii lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛdara. ni haa tsei lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi Ehaa amɛkwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ekɛ yitso bibioo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa

english: Young cocoa plants are like human babies—they burn and lose water quickly under full sun. Big forest trees provide shade and shelter from harsh heat and dry winds, creating the cool, humid climate cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. Amɛshãa ni amɛfiteɔ nu oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ haa hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he hɔɔŋ kɛ abobaahe. Ha kookoo lɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread across the floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground with tall stakes allows the leaves to catch direct sunlight, which the plant turns into food to feed the underground tuber. Staking also keeps leaves away from hot soil and wet mud, protecting them from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛ tsei kakadaji woɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei lɛ baatsɔ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ akabɔ. Ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, very dry soil, or a sudden lack of nutrients. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of conserving energy to stay alive until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji haomɔ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ trukaa lɛ faaa. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: The extra shoots, called suckers, act like extra mouths at a table—they steal water, food, and sunlight from the main plant. Removing excess suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring your main plant grows a heavy, high-quality bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krokomɛi ni yɔɔ okpɔlɔ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ akwɛ plantains ni tsii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crop turning yellow from the tip downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. When there isn't enough nitrogen in the soil, the plant pulls nutrients from its older, bottom leaves to feed the young leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-ŋmã lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts makes the soil better for maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni adu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmeii ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, meaning their roots work with helpful soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the dirt. When you harvest the groundnuts, that natural fertilizer remains in the soil, feeding the maize you plant next.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa ŋmei Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmei lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmei ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I put fertilizer in the soil on the exact day I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi ni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds do not have roots yet, so they cannot absorb fertilizer. Applying chemical fertilizer too early can burn the tender emerging sprouts or get washed away by early rains before the plant can use it.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ shishifãi lolo ni no hewɔ lɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo mli oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui ni miiba lɛ ashã loo nugbɔ ahoɔ amɛ dani tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato bushes curling up tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling can be a defense mechanism against hot weather to stop water loss, but it is frequently caused by tiny insects like whiteflies feeding on the sap and transmitting viruses. Check the undersides of the leaves for tiny insects.
ga: Baai lɛ ni abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ baanyɛ afee gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he koni nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ akpa. Shi bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni yeɔ latex kɛ virus ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers go soft and rot underground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When constant rain waterlogs the soil, it starves the roots of oxygen, allowing rot-causing microorganisms in the soil to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Hɔmɔ miiye shishifãi lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa he. Enɛ haa nibii bibii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: If some of my seeds are broken or cut in half, can I still plant them in my farm?
ga: Kɛji mi dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi efo loo afo mli enyɔ Ani manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo?

english: It is best not to plant broken or half seeds. A seed needs all of its internal parts intact to feed the baby plant as it sprouts. Broken seeds usually rot in the soil or produce very weak crops.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui ni ekumɔ loo ni ekumɔ fã. Dumɔwu lɛ he miihia emli nibii fɛɛ koni ekɛha tso bibioo lɛ niyenii be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akumɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kwraa.

english: Why do some of the planting seeds from the agricultural store come with a colorful powder or medicine on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ okwaayeli shwapoi amli lɛ kɛ powda loo tsofai ni yɔɔ kɔla baa lɛ?

english: That coating is a protective medicine made of fungicides or insecticides. It prevents soil insects, worms, and fungi from destroying the seed before it has the chance to sprout.
ga: Coating ji tsofa ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii feɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa koni koolooi, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akafite dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛna hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How can I test if the seeds I saved from my last harvest are still alive and good for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni esa akɛ adu?

english: You can perform a simple germination test. Wrap ten seeds in a wet cloth, keep it moist for a few days, and count how many sprout. If eight or more sprout, your seeds are good to plant.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Okɛ mama ni mli efɔ abɔ dumɔwui 10 he, ni oha amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ gbii 2-3, no sɛɛ lɛ okane dumɔwui enyiɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Kɛji ŋmeii kpaanyɔ loo nɔ ni fe nakai Tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui lɛ sa kɛha dumɔ.

english: What will happen to my crop if I plant my seeds too deep into the soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, the young shoot will exhaust all its energy trying to push through the heavy soil and die underground before reaching sunlight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahewalɛ baaho ni amɛmiitao amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ.

english: Why should I buy pure certified seeds instead of just planting seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui krɔŋŋ ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, du wuhi nɛ a he yi kɛ je ngmɔ kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ pɛ.

english: Certified seeds are specifically selected to resist diseases, grow uniformly, and yield more harvest. Saved seeds lose these strong qualities over time, resulting in smaller yields.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe. shweremɔ ni yaa nɔ daa ni ewoɔ babaoo Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Why are my seeds taking longer than expected to sprout out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ koni amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds delay sprouting when the soil lacks enough moisture, when the ground is too cold, or if they were buried too deep. They require moisture and warmth to wake up and grow.
ga: Dumɔwui haaa akwɛ̃ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ tsɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ Amɛhe miihia ŋmɔtɔ kɛ latsaa koni amɛte shi ni amɛdara.

english: What happens if I plant too many seeds together in one single hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When too many seeds grow in one hole, the young plants fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin, weak, and produce smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo, amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe for me to feed left-over seeds coated with farm medicine to my farm animals?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni akɛwo ŋmɔ mli ni eshwɛ lɛ aha miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ?

english: No, never feed treated seeds to humans or animals. The chemical coating on the seed is poisonous and meant only to protect the seed inside the soil.
ga: Dabi, kaahã adesai loo kooloi dumɔwui ni atsa amɛ kɔkɔɔkɔ. Tsofa ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ ji tsofa ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni eyɛ koni ekɛbu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe pɛ.

english: Does my soil need to be wet before I put my seeds into the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ dani mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo mli?

english: Yes, seeds require soil moisture to absorb water and swell up, which triggers the sprouting process. Planting in completely dry soil delays growth until rain falls.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni dumɔwui aná nu yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ nu ni amɛfuu. ni kɛ budding process lɛ baa Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ lɛ baaha ekwɛ̃ fioo kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Does selecting only the big, plump seeds give me better crops than using small seeds?
ga: Ani dumɔwui wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛ ni mihalaa lɛ haa mináa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe dumɔwui bibii ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ?

english: Yes, larger and plumper seeds contain more food reserves for the baby plant, giving the seedling a stronger start and a better chance of developing into a healthy crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni dara ni egbɔjɔ lɛ yɛ niyenii babaoo ni ato kɛha tso bibioo lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shishijee ni mli wa kɛ hegbɛ kpakpa ni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm take up to four years before I can start harvesting any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he afii ejwɛ dani mibɔi ŋmeii lɛ akpamɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need time to build a strong root system and sturdy trunk to support heavy pods. During the first few years, the plant focuses all its energy on growing leaves and branches before it is mature enough to produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia be koni amɛma shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ tso ni mli wa ni baaye abua ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ niji ni miida lɛ ahe nii dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Cassava plants show readiness when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the expanding tubers push outward.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii ni mli lɛɛɔ lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested plantains ripen all at once so quickly after I cut the bunch down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mifolɔ ŋmeii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, plantains release a natural gas called ethylene that speeds up the ripening process. Cutting bunches when they are fully formed but still green helps delay ripening so you have time to transport or sell them.
ga: Kɛji akpa Guts lɛ, ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ oya. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii lɛ amli beni amɛdara kwraa shi amɛji eŋɔli lolo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛshwereɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, oyɛ be ni okɛbaafã loo okɛbaahɔɔ.

english: Can I plant quick crops like maize and plantain on the same field while waiting for long-term tree crops to grow?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa oya. yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ be mli ni emɛɛɔ tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, intercropping fast-growing food crops alongside long-term crops gives you food and income during the early years, while tall plants like plantain provide essential shade for young tree seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni oookwɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ahe lɛ baaha oná niyenii kɛ shika yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. Yɛ be mli ni tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains haa dumɔwui ni he hiaa waa lɛ hɔɔ lɛ, tsei bibii.

english: Why are some yam tubers on my farm growing very large while others stay small and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi miida waa nɛkɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni sweet potato ŋmeii komɛi ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Yam size depends on soil looseness, water, and seed quality. Loose, fertile soil allows tubers to expand easily, while hard or compacted soil restricts their growth.
ga: Bɔ ni sweet potato lɛ dalɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, nu lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baa nii lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ mlɛo. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ dalɛ naa.

english: Why can I harvest cassava leaves and tubers continuously, but my maize crop dies right after one harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ manyɛ maya nɔ makpa ŋmei baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ? Shi mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ trukaa yɛ kpamɔ kome sɛɛ?

english: Maize is an annual crop programmed to complete its life cycle and die after producing seeds once, whereas cassava is a perennial root crop that can live and continue growing underground for multiple seasons.
ga: Abɛi ji tso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ daa afi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni egbe ewala be lɛ naa ni egbo beni ewo dumɔwu kome pɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei ji tso ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni baanyɛ ahi shi ni eda yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be babaoo lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that your crop lacks vital nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the plant is getting too much or too little water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo tso lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant retain its blooms to produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very tall and thin without producing big ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeee abele toi wuji lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants stretch upwards to compete for sunlight instead of building strong stems and thick ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la he akaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo ŋmãa ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: Why do cassava leaves taste bitter and produce a cloudy juice when crushed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei baa lɛ mli ŋɔɔ ni kɛ́ atswa lɛ, ejieɔ nu ni mli ewo atatu lɛ kpo lɛ?

english: Cassava produces naturally bitter compounds in its leaves and skin as a defense mechanism to deter insects and wild animals from eating the plant.
ga: Cassava feɔ nibii ni mli edɔ yɛ ebaa kɛ ehewolo mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa akɛ nɔ ni akɛbuɔ he koni kooloi kɛ koo mli kooloi akaye tso lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow fast. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure around the plants helps them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛfataa Tsei ahe lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat holes in the middle of my maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are known as Fall Armyworms. Moths lay eggs on the leaves, and when the worms hatch, they crawl into the center funnel of the plant to feed. Spraying approved insecticides or applying neem extract directly into the central funnel early in the morning or late evening controls them.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ Fall Armyworms. Kplukai lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Amɛshwereɔ kɛboteɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛyatao niyenii. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo neem mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni akudɔɔ.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees on the same field where I am starting new cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mije mi-kookoo hee lɛ shishi yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa trees until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays around them in the soil for a long time. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots, preventing them from soaking and rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkafite.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high into the sunlight to capture light and make food, which grows large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to the sun and off wet ground where diseases can attack them.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ la lɛ ni amɛfee niyenii. Tubers wuji lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la mli ni ejɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ aba lɛ. baanyɛ atutua

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding under the leaves. Controlling these insects early with soapy water sprays or recommended pesticides stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Akɛ nu ni akɛ samla eshwie nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi nɛɛ atsu nii mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akabɔle amɛhe.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Watering your plants regularly and covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool and moist so flowers stay on.
