ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa kɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛwoɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛɔ ahiɔ shi.

english: Why is it harmful if I drop chemical fertilizer directly touching the stem of my plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ akɛ tsofa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baawo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer behaves like strong salt; when it directly touches a plant stem, it draws water out of the plant and burns the tissue. Fertilizer should always be placed in a small circle or hole a few inches away from the stem.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ŋoo ni mli edɔ. Kɛ́ ekɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli ni eshãa fãji lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ kooyigbɛ bibii amli. Aloo bu lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny friendly organisms in their roots that take plant food directly from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped food stays in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nibii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni heɔ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. beni okpa lɛ Niyenii ni ekã lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I wait for a heavy rain before planting my seeds instead of planting after the first light shower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa koni madu dumɔwui? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ahum lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A light shower only wets the top layer of dirt, which dries out quickly in the sun and bakes young seeds before they can grow. Heavy rain thoroughly soaks the soil deep down, giving seeds enough moisture to sprout and push roots deep into the ground.
ga: Shawa ni mli tseee lɛ baaha muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. ni egbiɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ ni egbiɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ dani amɛdaraa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛtsi amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: When maize plants get too hot and lack sufficient moisture, they curl their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to sunlight. This is a natural defense mechanism to conserve water and prevent the plant from drying out.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni amɛbɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he ni akɛtsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkagbi.

english: Is it harmful to water my crops in the middle of a hot afternoon instead of the morning?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ oooha ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli moŋ fe leebi?

english: Watering under the hot midday sun causes much of the water to evaporate before reaching the roots. It can also cause severe temperature shock to the roots, so it is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa hu aba shishifãi lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ afee nu lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves typically indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant responds by pulling nitrogen from its older lower leaves to support the growth of new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei haa hetoo kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even when the leaves and stems above ground grow tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ waa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ, shi.

english: Cassava plants grow excess foliage at the expense of root growth when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or when plants are spaced too closely. The plant spends all its energy making leaves rather than storing food in the tubers.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ woɔ tsei ahe tsei babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ he nyɔmɔwoo mli kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato amɛ bulb lɛ mli.

english: What causes my pepper flowers to fall off the plant before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo pepper?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, dry soil, or heavy stress. The plant aborts its blossoms to conserve water and energy so it can stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛ yashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa nɔ. Tsei foɔ fɔfɔi amli koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my garden egg plants produce plenty of flowers but fail to form any actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Garden eggs require insects like bees or wind movement to carry pollen between flowers to form fruit. If pollinators are absent, or if temperatures are too high, pollination fails and the unfertilized flowers drop.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ahe miihia kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni ekɛ pollen lɛ aya fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ koni efee aduawai. Kɛji akɛ pollinators bɛ loo hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii ni fɔfɔi ni pollin bɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant my seeds too close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak stems and significantly lower fruit yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni ehaa aduawai ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Weeds are native wild plants naturally adapted to thrive in local climate and soil conditions. They aggressively absorb available water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crop varieties.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛheɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei srɔtoi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my okra plants getting sticky and curling downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi okra tso lɛ nɔ lɛ mli wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Sticky, curled leaves are usually caused by sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies on the undersides of leaves. As they feed, they excrete a sugary liquid called honeydew that leads to distorted growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni wa lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ Amɛjieɔ nu ko ni mli edɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ honeydew lɛ kpo. Enɛ kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa.

english: How can I tell if my plantain bunch is mature enough to harvest before it ripens on the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi plantain tsei lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa dani amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Plantains are ready for harvest when the top leaves naturally turn yellow and the individual fingers on the bunch lose their sharp ridges, becoming full and rounded.
ga: Plantains efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni ŋwɛi baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. ni nineshi nine fɛɛ nine ni yɔɔ kuu lɛ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ etsitsi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ koni efee nɔ ni eyi obɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree take several years to produce pods while my maize is ready in just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a long-term tree crop that must build a strong trunk and deep root system over years before it has enough energy to produce pods, whereas maize is an annual crop designed to grow, seed, and die within one short season.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ko ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ehiɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ afii babaoo dani ená hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee pods. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, abele ji daa afi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni ekwɛ̃, ewo dumɔwui, ni egbo yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Why do some of my fruit trees produce plenty of yield one year and almost nothing the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko kwraa yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is called alternate bearing. When a tree uses all its energy and stored soil nutrients to give a massive harvest in one season, it becomes exhausted and needs the next year to rest and build up its reserves again.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ sɛɛkuu bearing. Enɛ ji be mli ni tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛ niyenii ni amɛto yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkpa nibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli. Tso lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia be yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli koni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛsaa he ni ekɛto lɛ.

english: Why do my crops shed their flowers during very hot and dry weather without making any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa ni egbiɔ waa lɛ, ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough water during heat stress, dropping their flowers is a defense mechanism to save water and keep the main plant alive rather than risking energy on fruit.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Fɔfɔi ni ashwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni akɛbu nu he ni aha tso titri lɛ ahi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ awo oshara mli lɛ

english: Young cocoa leaves are very tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Shade trees act like living umbrellas that protect young cocoa from direct sun and keep the moisture in the ground.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off when heavy rains flood my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excess standing water suffocates the roots, causing them to rot, which prevents the plant from drinking water and food, making the leaves yellow and drop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ, ni no haaa tso lɛ anu nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do tomato leaves roll up tightly during the middle of the day when the sun is strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is the plant's natural way of reducing the leaf surface area exposed to the sun, which helps it trap moisture and stop water from evaporating too quickly during extreme heat.
ga: Leaf curling ji tso ko adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa ebaai lɛ anɔ he ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, aggressive roots that absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to overpower young crops early in the season.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi mli kwɔ ni amɛfeɔ basabasa. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ kunim yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: If I plant my crops very close together to harvest in bulk, will I get a bigger yield from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kɛha nikpamɔ babaoo Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting crops too close together forces them to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems, small fruits, and lower overall crop quality.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii Yibii lɛ daraaa. ni eha tso lɛ fɛɛ mlihilɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall and bushy with dark green leaves but produce very small ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔji ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ewoɔ abele toi bibii waa lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant put all its energy into growing tall stems and leafy foliage instead of forming strong ears and healthy grains.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ tsei ahe baai ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tue nɛ mi wa kɛ dumɔwuhi nɛ a ngɛ he wami.

english: How can I tell if my land is properly prepared before I start planting my seeds at the beginning of the rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ asaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ nugbɔ lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Good soil setup means the land is soft, moist, crumbly, and free from hard underground crusts so that young seed roots can easily push through and absorb water as soon as rainfall starts.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni wa bɛ mli. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni dumɔwui bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli oya ni amɛmu nu kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient responsible for healthy leaf growth. Applying well-composted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea restores the green color and helps the crop grow strong.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts on my farm will help my other crops grow better next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen stays in the ground, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo. Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the field for too long without draining, the roots suffocate and harmful fungi thrive in the wet conditions, causing the tubers to decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ejɛɛɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my young maize stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-abɛi bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are known as Fall Armyworms. They hide inside the tender central part of the maize plant where it is soft and moist, and they must be controlled early so they do not destroy the growing point of the plant.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ Fall Armyworms. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni edɔ lɛ mli. ni esa akɛ akudɔ kɛjɛ shishijee bɔni afee ni akafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted in open sunlight without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle full, direct sunlight without losing water faster than their roots can drink. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby provides essential shade and keeps the air humid while the trees establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni fa ni nu lɛ sɛɛ efooo oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba ni eye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ ama shi lɛ.

english: Seeds planted too deep struggle to push through the heavy soil before using up all their stored energy. This causes them to rot underground or produce weak seedlings that emerge late.
ga: Abaanyɛ atsɔ dumɔwui ni adu mli tsɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ dani amɛkɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ haa amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ ni jeɔ kpo fiofio.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which is then sent down to build larger, heavier tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, atsuɔ kɛyaa shi koni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the moisture in the dirt and prevents weed seeds from getting enough light to germinate and compete with your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni otsi jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akaŋ.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience extreme heat stress or when the soil gets too dry, as the plant tries to save water and energy by sacrificing its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo haomɔ kpe amɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, pepper tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛkɛshãa afɔle lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it risky to sow my seeds right after the very first rain of the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often moistens only the top surface of the dry soil. If a long hot spell follows before the main rains start, the newly germinated seeds will quickly dry up and die.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ pɛ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ ko ba dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛ Dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving bigger shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa from heat until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why should I leave my land unused for a season after harvesting crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mikɛtsuuu nii kɛyashi be kome beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Leaving land unused, or letting it fallow, allows the soil to rest and naturally rebuild nutrients, organic matter, and moisture that crops took away during the growing season.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuuu nii loo ni ashiɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ niyenii, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtee yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ emaa shi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: You should wait until the first major rains fall consistently for several days so the ground is thoroughly wet. Planting too early after just one light shower will cause seeds to dry up and die in the hot soil.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ wulu ni yaa nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up toward sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing mold and helping the plant catch full sunlight.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awó amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu lɛ aje kpo koni amɛná niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii anaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ náa hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus. These insects suck the sap out of leaves, which starves the plant of important nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náaa niyenii ni he hiaa.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or water, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa lɛ kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why do I need to dry my harvested maize grains in the sun before storing them in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Drying maize removes moisture from inside the grains. Storing wet grains causes mold to grow and attracts grain-boring insects that will spoil your entire harvest.
ga: Abɛi ni agbiɔ lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmaa ni efɔ lɛ to lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii akwɛ̃ ni ebaagbala kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ ŋmaa lɛ ni baafite onibii fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my plant wither when I place chemical fertilizer right next to the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ gboɔ kɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is very concentrated salt. Placing it directly against the stem draws water out of the plant and burns its stem tissues, so fertilizer should always be placed a few inches away from the stem where roots can reach it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei fa babaoo waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli ni eshã tso lɛ fãji lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe aaafee inchi 2-3.

english: Why do farmers plant cowpeas or beans together with maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ tsina loo ŋmeii kɛfataa ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil as natural plant food. This feeds the neighboring maize plants and keeps the soil rich.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aná niyenii, ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with deep root systems designed to quickly absorb water and food before cultivated crops can. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing vital resources from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni afee koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya dani tso lɛ anyɛ eda. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why should I spend money to buy certified oil palm seeds instead of just planting seeds from old trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika kɛhe oil palm dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makwɛ̃ kɛjɛ tsei momoi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli

english: Certified oil palm seeds are specially bred to produce significantly more palm oil and start bearing fruit much faster than uncertified seeds collected from random trees, making your farm far more profitable over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ mu tso dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛ tsofa babaoo aba ni ebɔi yibiiwoo oya fe dumɔwui ni bɛ hegbɛ ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni afee amɛ srɔtoi lɛ amli lɛ. Ha oŋmɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can a small-scale farmer like me make good profit from oil palm, or is it only successful for big plantation companies?
ga: Ani okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi lɛ baanyɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa kɛjɛ ŋmei fɔ mli? Aloo abɔɔ mli nitsumɔhei wuji pɛ baaye omanye?

english: Smallholder farmers actually cultivate most of the oil palm land in Ghana. With proper management and high-yielding seed varieties, a small farm can produce high yields and be very profitable.
ga: Okwaafoi bibii duɔ mu tsei babaoo yɛ Ghana. Kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ No hewɔ lɛ ŋmɔji bibii baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo ni amɛná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo.

english: How big is a hectare of land, and how many oil palm trees can I plant on it?
ga: Te hectare kome da ha tɛŋŋ? Ni mu tsei enyiɛ manyɛ madu?

english: A hectare is roughly the size of a standard football field. When using standard recommended spacing, you can comfortably plant about 143 oil palm trees on one hectare.
ga: Hectare kome dalɛ tamɔ bɔɔlutswaa he ko ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ. Kɛ okɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛyaa lɛ tsu nii lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ hejɔɔmɔ akwɛ mu tsei aaafee 143 yɛ shikpɔŋ hectare kome nɔ.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or maize between my oil palm trees when they are still small?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mu tsei lɛ ateŋ beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Yes, during the first two to three years before the palm leaves grow large enough to block the sunlight, you can intercrop with food crops like maize or legumes to generate income and food while your trees mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli dani tso lɛ baai lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ atsĩ hulu lɛ naa. Obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa adu niyenii. Koni oná shika kɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni otsei lɛ daraa lɛ

english: What kind of soil and environment is best for planting oil palm in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ shihilɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mu tso ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Oil palms thrive best in deep, fertile, well-drained soils in warm areas that receive plenty of consistent rainfall and abundant sunlight throughout the year.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young oil palm trees turning yellow, and what should I do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni mɛni esa akɛ mafee?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of key soil nutrients like nitrogen or potassium. Applying the right blend of fertilizer will replenish the soil and bring back green, healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛfutu mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ayi obɔ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do I need to clear a clean circle around the base of each oil palm tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie kooyigbɛ ni bɔle mu tso fɛɛ tso shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds in a ring around the stem prevents weeds from stealing water and fertilizer from the tree, and makes it much easier to collect loose palm fruits when harvesting.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ kooyigbɛ ni bɔleɔ he lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaaŋɔ ŋmei yibii ni egbee shi lɛ kɛ́ akpaa.

english: Should I cut off the old dry leaves hanging from my oil palm trees?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ baai momo ni egbi ni ŋmɛɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yes, regularly cutting away dead or diseased fronds improves air movement, reduces disease risk, and makes it much easier to see and harvest mature fruit bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ afo baai ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ha helai ni baanyɛ aba lɛ aba shi Ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ aaana aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akui ni akpa.

english: How long will it take after I plant my oil palm seedlings before I can harvest the first fruit?
ga: Kɛ́ adu oil palm dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ ebaahe dani abaanyɛ akpa klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ?

english: When using high-quality improved varieties and good farming practices, oil palms generally begin producing harvestable fruit bunches within 3 to 4 years after planting.
ga: Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsake amɛ kɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi kpakpai miitsu nii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei lɛ jeɔ aduawai akui ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ shishi.

english: How does a long dry season affect my oil palm trees and the fruit they produce?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ saa oil palm tsei kɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extended dry weather stresses the tree, causing it to produce fewer flowers and smaller fruit bunches, which lowers your total harvest several months later.
ga: Be kakadaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi fioo pɛ kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ kpɛtɛɔ he. Enɛ baaha nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ aba shi yɛ nyɔji komɛi asɛɛ.

english: What is cocoa swollen shoot disease, and how does it harm my trees?
ga: Mɛni ji kookoo bud fuumɔ hela? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ tsei awui?

english: Cocoa swollen shoot disease is caused by a virus that makes the stems and roots of cocoa trees swell up, turns the leaves yellow, and drastically reduces pod yields. Over time, it weakens the tree and eventually causes it to die.
ga: Kookoo shishifãi ni fuu hela lɛ jɛɔ hela ko ni haa kookoo tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ fuuɔ lɛ mli baa. baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa pod ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi waa. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbo.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree has swollen shoot disease before it dies?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ dani amɛgboi?

english: You can spot the disease early by looking for swollen stems or roots, red lines along the leaf veins, yellow patches on mature leaves, and pods that grow smaller or unusually shaped.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona hela mra. Taomɔ tsei loo shishifãi ni efuu. Line tsuji ni yɔɔ baa lɛ fãji lɛ ahe Hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ baa ni eda lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo amɛhe mfoniri ni ejaaa.

english: How does swollen shoot disease travel from a nearby farm to my cocoa farm?
ga: Te bud swollen hela lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli kɛyaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The disease is carried by small insects called mealybugs, which travel between farms with the help of ants, high winds, or on farm tools, clothing, and infected plant cuttings brought from other farms.
ga: Hela nɛɛ jɛɔ kooloi bibii amli. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Efãa gbɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔji ateŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo ŋmɔ mli nibii, atadei, kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ ni afolɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔji krokomɛi amli lɛ anɔ.

english: There is currently no chemical cure for swollen shoot disease inside a living tree. Cutting down the infected tree—and nearby trees touching it—is the only proven way to stop the virus from spreading and killing your entire farm.
ga: Amrɔ nɛɛ tsofa ko bɛ ni akɛtsaa tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ amli ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ni eta amɛhe lɛ ni ooofo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni ana he odaseyeli ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ni egbe oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What can I do to protect my healthy trees after removing infected ones?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mabu mitsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe beni mijie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After cutting down infected trees, clear the surrounding area of wild host plants, use disease-resistant hybrid seedlings for replanting, and create a barrier strip of crops like oil palm or citrus around your farm.
ga: Beni ofo tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, jiemɔ tsei ni hiɔ koo mli lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii ni hela nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ atsu nii yɛ dumɔwui heei amli. ni ofee gbɛtsii nii ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ mu loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ.

english: Why should I keep other big trees inside my cocoa farm instead of cutting them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ tso agbo kroko yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Big shade trees protect delicate cocoa trees from harsh direct sunlight, keep the soil cool and moist during dry seasons, and shelter cocoa from strong winds.
ga: Tsei wuji ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni ebuɔ kookoo he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he

english: Are all types of shade trees safe to grow alongside my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani shade tsei srɔtoi fɛɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni abaakwɛ̃ yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ masɛi?

english: No, certain wild tree species can act as hidden hosts for the swollen shoot virus and attract mealybugs. It is best to consult an extension officer to choose non-host shade trees.
ga: Dabi, koo mli tsei komɛi baanyɛ atsu nii akɛ gbɔi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛha bud swelling virus lɛ ni amɛgbala mealybugs. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ extension nitsulɔ ko baasusu he koni ohala tsei ni jeee gbɔi ni haa hulu tsoɔ.

english: If I cut down my diseased cocoa trees, can I plant new crops on the same land immediately?
ga: Kɛ mifo kookoo tso ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ, Ani manyɛ madu tsei heei yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, you can plant food crops like plantain or maize straight away to get food and income, but you should clear out old infected cocoa roots before planting new cocoa seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu niyenii tamɔ plantains loo ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni onine ashɛ niyenii kɛ shika nɔ. Shi esa akɛ ojie kookoo shishifãi momo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ dani odu kookoo dumɔwui heei.

english: Is it a good idea to plant plantains alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ makwɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ mi-kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade for young cocoa seedlings, protecting them from sun damage while providing early food and revenue for your household.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ. Buu dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ hulu la he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha niyenii oya ni okɛ shika aba oshiabii lɛ anɔ.

english: Can I replace my infected cocoa trees with a completely different farm crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ srɔtoi kwraa ato kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Yes, planting non-host crops like oil palm, coconut, or citrus on land affected by swollen shoot is a good strategy because the virus cannot survive in those crops, keeping your land productive.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni jeee gbɔ tamɔ oil palms, coconuts loo citrus ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ emɔ nɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kpakpa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hela lɛ nyɛŋ ahi nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ awo yibii

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key soil nutrient. Adding manure or the right fertilizer early in the growing season helps the leaves stay green so the plant can make food and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli mra yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and the soil around the base of the stem will begin to crack as the tubers grow large underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni tuber lɛ daa yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in wet, humid conditions. Pruning excess branches to let sunlight and air into your farm, along with removing spoiled pods, keeps the healthy pods safe.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Agbɛnɛ hu, jiemɔ ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ. Ebaaha pods ni mli wa lɛ afee shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil dries out too much. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering and mulching helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up tightly and turning hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the sap from underneath the leaves. Spraying the plants with an organic neem leaf solution or recommended insect spray helps protect new foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Kɛ́ okɛ neem baa mli tsofa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baa heei lɛ ahe.

english: Plantain roots do not go very deep into the soil, making the plant top-heavy once heavy fruit bunches grow. Supporting the stem with a strong bamboo or wooden pole prevents the tree from snapping or uprooting during storms.
ga: Plantain shishifãi eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsiiɔ kɛ́ aduawai lɛ dara ni amɛbatsɔ kui wuji. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akakumɔ loo eshishijee yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers come out small and twisted instead of big and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eja lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil mounds or ridges to expand properly. If the soil is hard or filled with stones, the tuber struggles to push through as it grows, leading to small or misshapen yams.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ Tubers lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ mli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Certified seeds are specially selected and tested to resist common diseases, survive drought better, and give uniform, high yields. Seeds saved year after year gradually lose their strength and produce smaller harvests.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii ni yaa nɔ daa ni fa babaoo Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi fiofio ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Is it better to water my garden crops in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha abɔɔ mli tsei lɛ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so roots can absorb moisture before the sun gets strong. Watering in the hot afternoon causes water to evaporate quickly before reaching the roots and can stress hot leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ atswa tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ebaanyɛ eha baai ni mli edɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni wa.

english: Why should I avoid burning dry weeds on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni mashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu nii lɛ he?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and friendly insects in the soil that help crops grow. Clearing weeds manually or letting cut weeds rot into compost keeps the soil rich, moist, and fertile for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ oniji shwie jwɛi loo jwɛi ni afolɔ lɛ ni oooha amɛgbo yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and soil moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I have to put long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kakadaji ahe hiaa mi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing large tubers underground. Lifting the vines off the wet soil also protects the leaves from rotting and spreading leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ kɛ baai helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my maize ears stay tiny when I plant the seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same soil nutrients and water, leaving no plant with enough energy to grow full, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha baai ni eyi obɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build strong stalks and stay dark green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa, ni amɛhe tsei lɛ eŋɔli.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops if I plant cassava on the exact same farm patch every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei fioo pɛ baa kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the earth over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ je lɛŋ yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, which keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, slows down water evaporation, and stops weeds from sprouting around your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, severe dry spells, or a lack of beneficial insects like bees to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni naa wa loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ wuobii ni baawo fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ

english: Why should I remove the small extra shoots growing out from the sides of my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tomato tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Extra side shoots steal water and plant food away from the main stem, which prevents the plant from growing large and healthy fruits.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei krokomɛi juɔ nu kɛ tso niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and weak even after I apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ bibii ni egbɔjɔ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that swallow up water and fertilizer before your crops get a chance to drink them, leaving your crops hungry.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni miɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ. ni hɔmɔ aye nyɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spray insect chemical on my crops during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Spraying during hot afternoon sun causes chemicals to dry too fast and burn plant leaves, and it also kills friendly insects like bees that help your crops produce fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ agbi oya tsɔ ni ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashã. Egbeɔ kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ hu.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees on my farm before transplanting my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mawo kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight and will easily dry up and die. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, protecting young cocoa trees while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. ni ebaagbi ni ebaagbo oya Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does a short dry period followed by sudden rain cause my cocoa trees to produce many flowers all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ feɔ kuku lɛ? Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ Haa mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shikome?

english: Cocoa trees use weather changes as a natural signal for growth. The dry spell puts mild stress on the tree, and when the rain arrives, it triggers a surge of plant hormones that causes the tree to bloom heavily.
ga: Cacao tsei kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli okadi ni haa amɛdaraa. Hɔmɔ be lɛ kɛ haomɔ fioo baa tsei anɔ, ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ehaa tsei amli tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi waa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to stay green. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does lowland rice grow better when kept in standing shallow water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kplanaa nɔ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛto nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ?

english: Shallow water naturally smothers aggressive weeds that try to steal nutrients from the crop, while keeping the root zone consistently wet, which rice needs to absorb food easily.
ga: Nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be. ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa lɛ aŋɔ niyenii lɛ mlɛo

english: Does it matter which direction I bury my cassava stem cuttings when planting them in the soil?
ga: Kɛji akɛ oodu shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ afu ŋmei niji lɛ yɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the node buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If planted upside down, the shoots waste critical energy trying to turn themselves around, leading to weak stems and poor tuber yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ oodu ŋmei niji lɛ esa akɛ odu amɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa waa ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ tuber jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil to expand downward without hitting hard ground. High mounds keep the soil soft so tubers grow large and clean, while also preventing water from pooling around the roots and causing rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shi ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ adara ni amɛhe atse. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa nu akabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or dry soil. It is the plant's survival response to save water and energy when weather conditions make it too stressful to support fruit growth.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Nɔ ni tso lɛ feɔ koni ehi shi ji ni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ato he kɛji shihilɛi lɛ bafee nɔ ni haoɔ mɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding under the leaves. They drain sap from the plant, which distorts leaf growth and can transmit crop viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Amɛjieɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai ashwã.

english: Why do my watermelons split open on the vine right before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Watermelons burst when they receive a heavy, sudden amount of water after a dry period. The inside flesh expands faster than the outer rind can stretch, causing the skin to crack.
ga: Watermelon baatswa kɛji akɛ nu babaoo ba trukaa yɛ be ko sɛɛ. Heloo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baagbɛ eshwa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my main crop make the soil richer?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When these plants grow and decay, they release this natural nitrogen fertilizer back into the soil for nearby crops to use.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli beni tsei nɛɛ daraa ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ. Amɛjieɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as plant food, or the roots are soaked in too much standing water, which prevents them from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii kɛha tso lɛ. aloo shishifãi lɛ ebote nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli tsɔ. ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa

english: If your crops are growing very slowly, have pale leaves, or produce tiny yields despite getting enough rainfall, your soil has lost its nutrients and needs manure or crop fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo waa, amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ hu baafite niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ, ni ehe baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why does cassava still produce food even when the weather is very dry and other crops die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei yaa nɔ ewoɔ niyenii eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ mli edɔ waa ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi gboi lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep root systems that reach far underground for stored moisture, and its leaves can drop to save water, allowing it to survive long dry spells.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ni ebaai lɛ baanyɛ agbee shi koni nu akafite. Ha ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains on the same land as my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ he ni mi-cocoa tso hee lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act as living umbrellas to provide shade and cool moisture for young cocoa trees.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo tsei ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ baa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are small insects rolling up the leaves of my maize plants into tubes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli amɛwoɔ tsɔji amli lɛ?

english: Pests like the fall armyworm hide inside rolled leaves to protect themselves while eating the growing point of the plant, which stops the maize from producing healthy cobs if not treated.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe be mli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ fãi ni miida lɛ. Enɛ haaa ŋmãa lɛ afee ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yams rot in the soil before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni amɛkpaa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when the soil holds too much water due to poor drainage, which allows fungal diseases to multiply underground and attack the roots.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii helai gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛtutuaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the afternoon weather gets too hot or when watering is unpredictable, causing the plant to save its energy instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shwane kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nu ni abaaha amɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kwɛɔ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves look weak and wilted in the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During very hot afternoons, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. They temporarily wilt to protect themselves and usually recover by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Amɛbaasumɔ ni amɛbu amɛhe he yɛ be kukuoo mli ni bei pii lɛ, amɛhe baajɔ amɛ kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: Planting seeds too close forces the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil food, which leaves you with thin, weak stalks and small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee bibii ni dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ afee bibii loo amɛfee efolo.

english: Why does my papaya tree flower continuously but never produce any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ papaya tso yaa nɔ efɔɔ fɔfɔi shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Some papaya trees are strictly male and only produce pollen-bearing flowers; because they lack female plant parts, they will never develop fruits.
ga: Papaya tsei komɛi ji hii pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli pɛ. Akɛni tso lɛ fãi ni ji yei lɛ bɛ hewɔ lɛ, ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english: Why do my maize crops turn yellow and die when water sits on my field for days after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Just like people, plant roots need air to breathe. When water sits on your field for a long time without draining, it pushes out all the air in the soil, effectively drowning the roots so they cannot absorb nutrients.
ga: tamɔ adesai nɔŋŋ Tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ ŋmɔ ko mli be kakadaŋŋ ni nu bɛ mli. Nu baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛje kpo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why does hard, tightly packed soil cause my yam tubers to stay small and crooked?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Hard soil has very little air space and is too tough for roots to push through. Yam tubers need loose soil rich in air and organic matter so they can easily expand downwards and grow big and straight.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. ni ewa tsɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli. Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli eyi mli obɔ lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shi oya ni amɛdara ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: If fish are dying in the nearby river where I get water, is it still safe to pour that water on my vegetable crops?
ga: Kɛji loo miigboi yɛ faa ni bɛŋkɛ he ni mináa nu yɛ lɛ Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe lolo akɛ mafɔse nakai nu lɛ yɛ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ?

english: No, dying fish are a warning sign that the water contains dangerous chemicals, heavy pollution, or toxic runoff. Using that polluted water can damage your crop roots and make your harvested food unsafe to eat.
ga: Dabi, loo ni gboɔ lɛ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara, mujiwoo ni naa wa, loo nu ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni hoɔ yɛ nu lɛ mli. Nu ni mli ewo muji ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite otso lɛ shishifãi ni eha niyenii ni akpa lɛ afee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: I want to start farming on a piece of land my brother used in the past, so how do I prepare the soil for planting cassava?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni minyɛmi nuu onukpa lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii tsutsu lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, te esa akɛ ofee tɛŋŋ osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmei dumɔ?

english: Land used repeatedly by family members often lacks fresh nutrients. Before planting, clear the weeds without burning them, mix compost or manure into the soil to bring back its strength, and turn over the dirt to let in fresh air.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni weku lɛ mli bii kɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai heei. Dani obaadu lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ ni okɛshãaa. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ. ni otsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba

english: How can I tell if a new plot of land will be good for my tomato plants before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ hee ko baafee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi tomato tsei lɛ dani mabɔi dumɔ?

english: Check if the local wild plants look green and healthy, make sure water drains easily after rain rather than forming stagnant pools, and ensure the plot gets full sunlight and has access to clean water.
ga: Kwɛmɔ kɛji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni nu lɛ atsɔ mlɛo yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofee nubu ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ Ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛ nu ni mli tse aba.

english: My elders say a bad spirit in the land is destroying my crops, but why do plants really fail in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mi onukpai lɛ kɛɔ akɛ mumɔi fɔji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miifite midumɔ nii. Shi mɛni hewɔ tsei shwieɔ shi yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Crops usually fail repeatedly in one spot due to scientific causes like hidden rock layers beneath the surface, poor soil drainage, or plant diseases trapped in the soil, rather than spiritual forces. Testing and treating the soil can fix it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei fiteɔ shii abɔ yɛ he kome yɛ jeŋ nilee yiŋtoi ahewɔ, tamɔ tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo tsei ahelai ni ekã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Yɛ mumɔŋ hewalɛ najiaŋ Abaanyɛ atsake shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa kɛ tsamɔ.

english: Why do my crops dry up faster now even when I plant during the exact same month my father always planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya eyɛ mli akɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ, miduɔ yɛ nyɔŋ ni mitsɛ du lɛ nɔŋŋ mli moŋ?

english: Weather patterns have changed over the years, making rainy seasons shorter and unpredicted heat spikes more common. Planting strictly by calendar months no longer works, so it is best to check recent weather forecasts and soil moisture before sowing.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi etsake yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Enɛ haa nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ feɔ kuku ni hulutsoo be ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ baa. Dumɔ ni akɛ kalanda nyɔŋ lɛ kpãa gbee pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ tsuuu nii dɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he adafitswaa hee kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why are wild pests and insects damaging my crops much more now than they did years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi bibii miifite miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe afii ni eho lɛ?

english: When nearby bushes and trees are cut down for wood or expansion, wild insects lose their natural homes and food sources. As a result, they migrate into crop fields to survive, feeding on cultivated farm plants instead.
ga: Beni afoɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ koni akɛtsu nii akɛ tso loo akɛgbɛɔ eshwaa. Kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ koo mli lɛ miifite amɛ adebɔɔ mli shiai kɛ niyenii ni amɛyeɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfãa kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli koni amɛyahi shi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni amɛyeɔ moŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why did my pepper plants suddenly wither and die after a chemical weedkiller was sprayed on a neighboring field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gbo trukaa ni egbo beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical weedkillers can travel through the wind as invisible mist or wash through soil water into nearby fields. The chemical roots can be absorbed by your pepper plants, poisoning them even if you did not spray them directly.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfee afua ni anaaa loo shikpɔŋ nu lɛ kɛya ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. O pepper tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ tsofa shishifãi. Ekɛ poison baa kɛji okɛ tsofa lɛ shwieee nɔ tɛ̃ɛ po.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their leaves and flowers during a very severe dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe baa kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa waa be mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves and flowers is a natural defense mechanism crops use to survive severe heat and lack of water. Planting shade trees nearby helps keep the farm cool and protects the cocoa trees from dropping their potential harvest.
ga: Baai kɛ fɔfɔi ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi wala mli yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkafee nɔ ni baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no big trees growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that get scorched by strong, direct sunlight. Planting taller crops like plantains or shade trees around them provides a canopy that protects the young cocoa plants until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la shɛɔ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni akɛwoɔ shade mli ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Kakao tso lɛ buɔ kakao tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋɔɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning light green and yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong leaves. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the legume roots decay after harvest, they leave behind rich natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji legume shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛbaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the field. Rotating with different crops gives the soil time to recover and breaks the disease cycle.
ga: Nibii komekomei ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe ni ehaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Giving each plant proper space ensures it gets enough resources to produce thick stems and good yield.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tsei ni mli tse ni ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when it rains heavily for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall in soil that does not drain well creates standing water around the roots, preventing them from breathing oxygen. This waterlogged soil encourages fungal diseases that cause the tubers to soften and rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haaa amɛmu kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ nɛɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers spread dry grass on top of the soil around their tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket over the soil. It blocks hot sunshine from drying out the earth, keeps soil cool, conserves moisture, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Hay ni agbɛɔ ashwaa, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsĩɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, too little water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Ensuring steady watering and balanced nutrients helps the plant hold onto its flowers until they develop into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa waa he. nu fioo tsɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa kɛ niyenii ni ja lɛ baaye abua ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why should I pinch off the small extra suckers growing in the branch corners of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-tomato tso lɛ niji lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Removing extra suckers stops the plant from wasting energy on unnecessary stems and leaves. This redirects the plant's food and water directly into making bigger, healthier tomato fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii krokomɛi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ nu lɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tomato yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afeɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my vegetable plants droop in the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: On very hot days, leaves lose moisture faster through the air than roots can suck it up from the ground, causing temporary wilting to protect themselves. Once the hot sun cools down in the evening, the leaves typically stand back up.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ fiteɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Egboɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ebu ehe he. Kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ teɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and drying up in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight and hot winds. They need shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as natural umbrellas, keeping the leaves cool and retaining soil moisture until the cocoa plants mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ daa.

english: What is eating small holes inside the leaves and leaves-funnels of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai kɛ funnels lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, a very common maize pest in Ghana. They hide inside the central leaves of the plant and eat the foliage, so checking your farm early and applying recommended control methods early is key to protecting your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Ghana lɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ nii lɛ atsu nii mra. No hewɔ lɛ, eji nɔ titri ni baaha obu onibii ahe.

english: How do I tell if my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and small cracks begin to appear in the soil near the base of the stem where the roots are expanding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baa ko egbɔ kɛji baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ ŋmeii bibii Amɛjeɔ shishi amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ, he ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize yields every time I plant on the same plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients. Planting it continuously on the same plot drains the soil of essential foods like nitrogen. Resting the land, adding animal manure, or rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpea will help restore the soil's strength.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ afite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛjɔɔ he ni akɛ kooloi aŋmei fataa he. Aloo ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over before the fruit bunches are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai akui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and when the heavy fruit bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy and easy for strong winds to push over. Supporting the stems with sturdy bamboo or wooden props prevents them from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Plantain lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni kɛ́ aduawai ni tsii lɛ dara lɛ Tsei lɛ tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ amɛ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee.

english: Why are weeds so harmful to my pepper plants when they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ awui lɛ? Ni eji bibioo lolo?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young pepper plants and steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crop. They also shelter harmful insects and plant diseases that can spread to your peppers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe baby pepper tsei lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Ehaa kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã o-peppers lɛ anɔ lɛ hu náa he ko amɛhiɔ.

english: How do I know when it is safe to sow my maize seeds after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best not to plant right after the very first light rain, as the ground underneath remains dry. Wait until you get two or three steady rains so the soil holds enough moisture to support seeds through germination without them drying out.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ fioo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear the ground and stake my yam vines on tall poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie he ko ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei awo tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves off the ground into direct sunlight to make energy for growing big tubers beneath the dirt. Staking also keeps leaves dry and away from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ agbiɔ ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akashɛ amɛhe.

english: Is it better for me to water my tomato crop early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the roots to absorb water before the day gets hot. Watering in the middle of the day causes most water to evaporate quickly in the heat and can stress the plants.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmuɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ mli babaoo atsɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ haomɔ aba tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Beans and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special root nodules that convert nitrogen gas from the air into plant food. When these crops finish growing, they leave rich nitrogen behind in the soil for your next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni tsakeɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ efeɔ tsei aniyenii. Kɛji tsei nɛɛ dara kwraa Ebaashi nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I use dung from local cattle to help my crops grow better on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsinai amli ŋmeii atsu nii koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cow manure is a rich natural fertilizer. It adds essential nutrients like nitrogen to the soil and helps the ground hold onto water longer, which keeps crops healthy during dry spells.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmei ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmei ni jara wa waa. Ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and green with beans planted nearby, but look weak when planted alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ? Shi etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ pɛ.

english: Beans and leguminous crops pull nitrogen out of the air and put it into the soil. Other crops growing next to them feed on this natural plant food, making them stronger and greener without extra chemical fertilizers.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi Ha wɔye niyenii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli tso nɛɛ mli. Ha tsei lɛ awa ni amɛkafite shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect themselves from intense heat. By rolling their leaves, the plants reduce the amount of surface exposed to the sun, preventing moisture from escaping into the hot air.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei haa hulu la ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje kpo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do crops planted in open cleared areas dry out much faster than those planted near trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe tsei ni adu yɛ tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Trees act as natural windbreaks and provide partial shade. In wide-open areas, strong sunlight and wind evaporate moisture from both the soil and crop leaves much quicker.
ga: Tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛhaa hulutsoo fioo. yɛ he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ faŋŋ nɔ Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tso lɛ baai fɛɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kwraa.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
