ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay very small when I plant them in heavy clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose soil to expand underground. Heavy clay soil becomes hard and packed tightly, which squashes the growing roots and stops them from expanding into large tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔji ni akɛ shikpɔŋ sũ fee ni tsii lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni miida lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds completely before sowing my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are tougher than crop seedlings. If you leave them in the field, they will drink up all the water and steal soil nutrients before your crops can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei amli dumɔwui. Kɛji oshi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛbaanu nu lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛbaaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abashɛ.

english: Why do yellow spots appear on my tomato leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tomato baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: High humidity and continuous rain create a damp environment where fungal diseases spread easily. Fungi attack wet leaves, causing yellow spots that prevent the plant from making food.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Fung lɛ tutuaa baai ni efɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni haaa tso lɛ afee niyenii lɛ baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their blossoms before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛbatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they face heat stress, lack of water, or too much nitrogen. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy to stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen babaoo mli baa lɛ kpe. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato koni ehi wala mli.

english: Why do some seeds I plant fail to come up out of the ground at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi kwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deep in the dirt, if the soil is too dry for them to sprout, or if underground insects eat them before they can break through the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ̃. Aloo kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yeɔ amɛ dani amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow at the bottom in a V-shape, the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential plant food. This usually happens when heavy rains wash nutrients away or when the soil has been used repeatedly without adding fertilizer or manure.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ V su mli lɛ, no lɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo kɛ́ akɛ sũ tsu nii shii abɔ. ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he

english: Tomato flowers fall off when heat becomes extreme or when the soil dries out quickly. The plant gets stressed by these rapid weather changes and drops its flowers to save energy rather than trying to feed developing tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ oya. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ haa tsei haoɔ oya ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha tomatoi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in heavy soil and cannot drain away properly. Excess stagnant water deprives the roots of air and encourages soil fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ efo mli jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ jieɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl and turn brown during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants curl and shed their leaves during dry conditions to reduce water loss through evaporation. The plant sacrifices older leaves to preserve moisture in its main trunk so it can survive until the rains return.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ aba shi. Tso lɛ kɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ shaa afɔle koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he koni enyɛ ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yam vines climb so their leaves can reach maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to make food and swell the tubers underground. Keeping leaves off damp soil also protects the crop from leaf rot and soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo he. ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ hu buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my bean plants grow very tall with many leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Bean plants produce excessive foliage instead of flowers when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. High nitrogen forces the plant to spend energy on leaf growth rather than shifting into its flowering and fruiting stage.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ baajie baai babaoo yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai lɛ adalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebote fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do young cocoa trees require shade trees when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be mli ni miduɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or permanent shade trees shields young cocoa from harsh heat and retains soil moisture during their early growth stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ shishijee be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my crops after the first rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are native to the environment and have deep seed reserves or hardy roots that absorb moisture instantly. Cultivated crop seeds take longer to absorb water, break dormancy, and establish their root systems.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi ji nɔ ni jɛ shihilɛ mli ni amɛyɛ dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ loo shishifãi ni wa ni shwieɔ nu oya. Dumɔwui ni adu lɛ heɔ be dani amɛmɔɔ nu. gbee dormancy mli ni efee shishifã gbɛjianɔtoo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ

english: How do I know when my pepper crop is fully ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-pepper lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper fruits are ready when they feel firm, look glossy, and reach their full size or shift color from green to red. Harvesting regularly encourages the plant to produce continuous blooms and new pepper pods.
ga: Pepper aduawai lɛ efee klalo akɛ ayeɔ kɛ́ enu he akɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ, etamɔ nɔ ni ekpɛɔ, ni eshɛ egbɔmɔtso lɛ he loo etsake su kɛjɛ eŋɔli kɛtee etsuru mli. Nibii ni akpaa daa lɛ woɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛya nɔ amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo ŋmeii heei.

english: Why shouldn't I grow maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and lets crop-specific pests and diseases build up in the earth. Rotating with legumes like peanuts or cowpeas refreshes the soil with natural nitrogen.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni eha tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsake shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ mli aná adebɔɔ mli nitrogen.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when I plant the seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. Spacing them properly ensures every plant gets enough food and light to stay green and grow strong cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it bad to burn the weeds and grass on my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the good organic matter and beneficial insects that keep soil healthy and hold moisture. Clearing weeds and letting them rot into the soil feeds the ground naturally like manure.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ahiɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ahãa amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aye niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa tamɔ ŋmeii.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during long dry spells to save water and keep from drying out. The plant is not dead; it stores energy in its tubers underground and will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni nu akafite ni akagbi. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: What causes small holes in the leaves and pods of my cowpea plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ

english: Holes are caused by insect pests like caterpillars or beetles feeding on the leaves and pods. Spraying neem leaf extract or safe bio-pesticides early in the morning helps protect the leaves and pods.
ga: Buji jɛɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaabu baa lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the soil is too dry, heat is too high, or too much chemical fertilizer was applied. Keeping the soil moist and adding organic compost helps flowers stay on and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. hulutsoo fe nine loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo ni akɛfataa he Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on my farmland after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of food from the soil, but groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and put it back into the earth. Planting groundnuts fixes the soil naturally for your next crop.
ga: Abele jieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Peanuts ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Grains saved from hybrid crops lose their mother-strength, leading to weak plants and small cobs next season. Buying fresh certified seed each planting season guarantees a strong harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ haa nyɛ lɛ hewalɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he hewalɛ ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ ni mli wa baa.

english: How do weeds growing around my yam plants make the tubers small?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te mi sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛhaa amɛ bulbs lɛ feɔ bibioo?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil fertilizer meant for your yam vines. Clearing weeds early gives the yam plant full energy to feed and grow large tubers underground.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛha o-sweet potato wain tso lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi mra Enɛ baaha sweet potato tso lɛ aná hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji amli ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and turning brown during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling happens when tomato plants are stressed by intense heat, lack of water, or tiny sucking insects like whiteflies. Watering in the early morning and protecting plants from insects stops the leaf curl.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji akɛ hulutsoo, nu ni faaa, loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ miigba tomato tsei lɛ anaa. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I know when my sorghum is completely ripe for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sorghum lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Sorghum is ready when the grains become hard and dry, no longer releasing milky juice when pressed between your fingers, and the leaves at the base of the plant turn brown.
ga: Sorghum lɛ efee klalo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛgbi. Ejieŋ mliki kɛji akɛ onyɛ oniji ateŋ. Ni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants naturally move available nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed newer upper leaves when nutrients are low, showing it is time to apply fertilizer like NPK or urea.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ anɔ niyenii kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea afata he.

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that have tiny organisms on their roots capable of taking nitrogen from the air and putting it into the soil. When the roots decompose, that nitrogen stays in the soil to feed your next crop naturally.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɔɔ mli. Yɛ shishifãi ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Beni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Planting seeds too close causes the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each individual plant gets enough food and light to grow strong stalks and big cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi wuji ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the vines off the ground with stakes allows the leaves to spread out in the sun, which helps the plant produce much bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa hulu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji babaoo.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young vegetables with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the soil quickly. It holds in moisture, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from popping up easily.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni jeɔ kpo oya lɛ naa

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes inside the center funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in West Africa. Their moths lay eggs on young crop leaves, and the hatched caterpillars hide inside the central leaf funnel to eat tender foliage before the corn cob forms.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Afrika Anaigbɛ lɛ. Amɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ tsei bibii ahe baai anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli koni amɛye baa bibii lɛ dani ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: Extremely hot weather stresses tomato plants and dries up the pollen inside the blossoms. Without proper pollination, the plant cannot form fruit and drops the unused flowers.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Kɛji akɛ pollination ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii ni ebaashwie fɔfɔi ni akɛtsuuu nii.

english: Why do weeds grow and spread much faster than my planted crops after heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants adapted to sprout quickly and absorb resources fast. They rapidly soak up available water and nutrients from the rain before your cultivated crops can grow deep enough roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛŋɔ nibii oya. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ ni jɛɔ nugbɔ mli lɛ oya dani tsei ni okwɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and have broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the vital shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground if I leave them after heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water in waterlogged soil removes the air spaces around mature cassava roots. Without oxygen in the wet soil, rot-causing organisms rapidly break down and spoil the tubers before harvest.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Cassava shishifãi ni eda kwraa Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize once the rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Wait until the rainfall becomes steady after two or three good rains that thoroughly soak the soil. Planting too early after just one light shower can cause seeds to sprout and then dry up if a hot dry spell follows.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji latsaa ni mli egbi ba.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves, but the tubers underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or too much water, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing upper branches and leaves instead of storing energy in the roots. Avoiding heavy nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant focus on expanding tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji kɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ amli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa bulbs ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a living umbrella that keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into tomatoes during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat paired with irregular watering causes stress to the plant, making it drop flowers to protect itself from losing too much water. Consistent watering at the root level helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ fataa he lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei lɛ anɔ. Okɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni obu ohe koni nu babaoo akafite. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ eshishifã lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why does farmland in Techiman produce much better crop yields than the land I tried farming near Accra?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Techiman lɛ woɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ fe he ni mika he mikwɛ ni bɛŋkɛ Accra lɛ?

english: Farmland in the forest transition zones like Techiman naturally contains deeper, richer organic matter and retains water better than the sandy, coastal soil commonly found around Greater Accra.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ kooi amli tsakemɔ hei tamɔ Techiman lɛ yɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo. ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋshɔnaa shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Greater Accra he lɛ.

english: Is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas or beans on the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, which naturally fertilizes the nearby maize crop and improves future soil health.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ afɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves mean the plant lacks nitrogen. When a crop doesn't have enough nitrogen in the soil, it strips the nutrient from its older bottom leaves to feed the younger top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Kɛ tsei bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to capture as much sunlight as possible to make food for growing underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light while protecting them from soil diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni oooha amɛná la ni amɛtsiɔ helai hu anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing plenty of green leaves but not producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewooo pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Using too much manure or nitrogen fertilizer encourages the pepper plant to produce stems and leaves rather than flowers. Cutting back on nitrogen and ensuring the plant gets full sunlight encourages flowering.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo pepper tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii kɛ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Nitrogen ni abaaba shi ni akwɛ koni tsei lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ baawo fɔfɔi ahe hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my young crop seedlings so much more in the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have small, weak root systems. During their first few weeks, aggressive weeds steal the water, sunlight, and soil food before the crop can establish itself, severely slowing the crop's long-term growth.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifã bibioo ni bɛ hewalɛ. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, jwɛi ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ ama shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, an essential food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the maize regain its bright green color and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-ŋmei lɛ ni ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil traps too much water around them, preventing air from reaching the roots and allowing fungal diseases to grow. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mɔ nu babaoo ebɔle ehe, ni no haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. kɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni akɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ shwereɔ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by too much harsh sunlight, lack of water, or damage from sap-sucking insects like mirids. Planting shade trees nearby and protecting the cocoa with the right spraying routine helps the tree hold its flowers until they grow into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu la babaoo shɛ amɛnɔ, nu efo amɛmli, loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pollen lɛ efite amɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ni akɛ tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ abuɔ kookoo lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ ahi efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi ebaada ni etsɔ ŋmeii.

english: This sudden wilting is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that blocks the tubes inside the plant stem so water cannot reach the leaves. Since infected plants cannot be cured, removing the sick plants and planting non-vegetable crops in that area for a few seasons starves out the bacteria.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, anyɛɛɛ atsa tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ ni adu tsei ni jeee aduawai yɛ jɛmɛ be fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye helatsɛmɛi lɛ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to a plant family that pulls natural nitrogen food from the air and traps it in the soil through their roots. When you plant them together with maize, they feed the soil naturally and help your maize grow bigger without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata tsei aweku ko ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ okɛ ŋmãa du Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua oŋmãa lɛ ni eda ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé ŋmãa kroko.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever a small wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko baa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily because they have shallow roots, or because invisible worm-like pests called nematodes are eating their roots underground. Mounding soil high around the base of the stem and planting clean, disease-free suckers keeps the roots strong and firmly anchored in the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Aloo akɛni ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ miiye amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni aaabɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crop yield so small if I leave them on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm, quickly drinking up the soil water, stealing the plant food, and blocking the sunlight your crops need. Clearing weeds early in the crop's life ensures all the soil nutrients go directly into growing your main harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛnuɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. ju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli ni otsĩ hulu la ni otsei lɛ taoɔ lɛ naa. Jwɛi ni ogbeɔ yɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves are tiny solar panels that need maximum sunlight to manufacture food, which then gets stored underground as a big tuber. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light while keeping them safe from leaf diseases caused by moist soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai ji hulutsoo be mli nibii bibii ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni ekɛfee niyenii. ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi akɛ ŋmeii wuji Staking baaye abua ni awó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo atsɔɔ la mli yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ baai helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛbaa lɛ hu he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating large holes in the central leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ buji wuji ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that hides inside the center whorl of young corn plants to eat the soft leaves. Spraying recommended treatments directly into the center funnel of the corn plant early in the morning destroys the worms before they ruin the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ shwie ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ekpataa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do certified seeds bought from agro-dealers grow better than the seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are carefully bred in plant laboratories to resist common local diseases, survive dry conditions, and yield maximum fruit. Seeds saved from your own farm lose these strong protective traits over generations, making them weaker and less productive.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei ahe nitsumɔhei koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ebaanyɛ ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli ni ekɛ yibiiwoo babaoo aha Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ mli lɛ baafite nɛkɛ hebuu nibii ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ ni wooo yibii babaoo baa.

english: Why should I plant my crops inside plastic nursery bags instead of straight into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ plastic ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ fe ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting in bags helps retain soil moisture, protects young root systems from soil diseases, and allows you to easily care for delicate young plants before they mature.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ kotokui amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Ebuɔ shishifãi bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. ni ehaa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ dani amɛdaraa.

english: How should I pack soil into my planting bags so the crops grow properly?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mawo sũ awo mi-grow bag lɛ mli koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Fill the bags with rich topsoil mixed with organic manure, pressing gently so the soil stays firm enough to support the plant but loose enough for water to drain and roots to spread.
ga: Okɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli efutu mli lɛ awo kotoku lɛ mli, ni okɛmii shi blɛoo bɔni afee ni sũ lɛ afee shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eye ebua tso lɛ shi efee mlɛo bɔ ni sa ni nu lɛ atsɔ mli ni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why is it important for me to set up my crop bags during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masaa dumɔ kotoku yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Setting up bags during the rains ensures the soil stays naturally wet, which gives the young crops the continuous moisture they need to establish roots without drying out.
ga: Baagi lɛ ni akɛtoɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu ni he hiaa amɛ be fɛɛ be koni amɛshishifãi lɛ atswa shi ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why do my young crops need a lot of water right after I put them in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa mi dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo baagi mli lɛ?

english: Newly bagged plants need plenty of water to help their roots settle into the fresh soil and to absorb nutrients so they do not suffer from stress or wilting.
ga: Tsei heei ni awo amɛ kotoku mli lɛ he miihia nu babaoo koni eye ebua amɛshishifãi lɛ ni amɛhi shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ. kɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ atsu nii Koni ekɛtsi ehe kɛjɛ haomɔ loo shwiemɔ he

english: What does crop 'forcing' mean, and why would I need to do it on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ‘anyɛɔ mɔ nɔ’ lɛ shishi? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Forcing is a practice where you trigger plants to start flowering and fruiting at a specific time, allowing you to control your harvest period and get uniform produce.
ga: Nɔ ni nyɛɔ mɔ nɔ ji nifeemɔ ko ni owoɔ tso ko hewalɛ koni ebɔi fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko mli. Ehaa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ nikpamɔ be lɛ ni okwɛɔ koni yibiiwoo lɛ aba daa.

english: When is the right time for me to start forcing my plants to produce fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi mitsei lɛ anɔ hewalɛ koni amɛwo yibii?

english: You should force plants only after they have grown large enough and produced enough healthy leaves to feed and support the heavy fruits that will develop.
ga: Esa akɛ onyɛ tsei anɔ pɛ kɛji amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛwo baai ni he wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ni aye abua aduawai ni tsii ni baaba lɛ.

english: Why are my crops producing plenty of green leaves but no flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo shi fɔfɔi bɛ he lɛ?

english: Some crops put all their energy into leafy growth and need a nutritional shift or chemical trigger to signal to the plant that it is time to make flowers.
ga: Tsei komɛi kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛ̃ɔ baai ni ehe hiaa ni atsake niyenii mli hewalɛ loo tsofai ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli koni ekɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ewo fɔfɔi.

english: What chemical like potassium or custo is used for forcing crops, and what does it do?
ga: Mɛɛ tsofa, tamɔ potassium loo custo? Akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛnyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ Ni mɛni etsuɔ?

english: Potassium-based chemicals like custo act as growth triggers when sprayed on mature plants, signaling them to stop growing leaves and quickly begin forming uniform flower buds.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛ potassium fee, tamɔ custo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni haa tsei lɛ daraa kɛji akɛ afɔse amɛ awo tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ. Etsɔɔ amɛ koni amɛkpa baai lɛ adalɛ ni amɛje fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ shishi oya.

english: How does applying potassium or custo chemical help me get a better harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ potassium loo custo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: It makes all the plants in your field produce flowers and mature fruits at the exact same time, making harvesting easier and allowing you to sell higher quantities together.
ga: Ehaa tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be kome mli. Ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo ni eyeɔ ebuaa nyɛ ni nyɛfeɔ ekome kɛhɔ̃ɔ nibii babaoo.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray forcing chemicals on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ tsofai ni mli wa baashwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the sun is mild so the plant leaves can absorb the chemical solution properly without getting burned.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse nɔ lɛ leebi loo shwane mli. ni ji be ni hulu la ni tsoɔ fioo lɛ yɔɔ Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ baai lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ tsofai lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛshãaa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and intense heat. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide living shade, keeping the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa plants survive their early years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ koni eye ebua kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce a lot of rich green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miiwo baai ŋmɔji babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Cowpeas naturally extract nitrogen from the air into the soil. If the soil already has too much nitrogen or fertilizer, the plant focuses all its energy on growing leafy foliage instead of producing flowers and bean pods.
ga: Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a natural survival trick maize uses to reduce surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant conserve water and prevent drying out during hot periods.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛba ehiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he, ni ehaaa amɛgbi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why does my maize turn pale yellow and grow slowly after a week of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni edaa fiofio yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa otsi kome sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash essential nutrients like nitrogen deep into the ground where young roots cannot reach them, while waterlogged soil starves the roots of air. Adding a bit of nitrogen fertilizer or organic manure after heavy rains helps them recover.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo fata he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up with yellow patches during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: While cassava sheds leaves during dry weather to save water, curling leaves with yellow patches are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, spread by small insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties prevents this.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu he moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: What is eating small holes into my cabbage leaves, and how can I stop it simply?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni yɔɔ mi kaabaji baa lɛ nɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa lɛ mlɛo?

english: Small holes are typically caused by caterpillars, such as the diamondback moth larvae. You can manage them naturally by spraying a liquid mixture made from crushed neem tree leaves and mild soapy water on the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ daimondback ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ otsa amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa kɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛ saamɔ fee lɛ ni oookɛshwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Consistent watering and adding compost helps the flowers stay on to produce peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi koni amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular, as tomato plants need a steady water supply to carry calcium from the soil into the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ he miihia nu ni yaa nɔ daa koni ekɛ calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my yams so they don't rot underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii? Koni ekafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Yams are mature and ready to harvest when the leaves and vines above ground turn yellow and dry up completely. Harvesting after the top foliage dies ensures the tuber is fully developed and safe to store.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ eda ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa. Nikpamɔ beni baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gboi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtoɔ.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land is fertile enough for maize without buying soil testing equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ni miheee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni akɛkaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Look at the natural vegetation growing on the fallow land; dark brown or black soil that grows tall green weeds like wild sunflower indicates fertile soil with good moisture retention suitable for maize.
ga: Naa adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋa lɛ nɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ ni jwɛi eŋɔli kakadaji, tamɔ koo mli hulutsoo tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii, ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmãa.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because their delicate leaves scorch easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving large shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby provides the shelter and moisture young cocoa needs during its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni aaashi loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ebaaha tso bibioo lɛ aná he ko ni ehi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to climb tall stakes so their leaves can catch sunlight easily to make food for growing big tubers underground. When vines lie on the damp ground, weeds can choke them and leaf rot diseases spread much faster.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛjie amɛhe tsei lɛ akpo yɛ hulu la mli koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs ni miida lɛ. Kɛ wain tso lɛ kã shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ Jwɛi baanyɛ agbe amɛ ni baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baagbɛ eshwa oya kwraa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my green maize plants turning yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually show that your maize crop is lacking nitrogen, which is a major food source plants need to grow strong. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the base will help the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii kpakpai ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ jɛɛhe titri. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛbaabɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant beans or cowpeas in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baawo mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmãa yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and beans have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. Planting them with maize feeds the soil naturally and helps your maize crop yield better without using as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa o-abɛi lɛ yibiiwoo lɛ yaa hiɛ ni tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer directly against the main stem of my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing chemical fertilizer directly touching the stem can burn the plant's skin and damage delicate feeder roots underneath. It is safer to place fertilizer in a small ring or side pocket a few inches away from the stem so roots can safely reach for it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo ni efite tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ fɔmɔ nii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Aloo kotoku ko ni yɔɔ afã ni kɛ tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi kome pɛ. kɛha root hegbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains flooded my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe, and standing water suffocates them, leading to root rot. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away easily so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. ni nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha mɔ agbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over before the fruit bunches are fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai lɛ eda kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and become very top-heavy once a large fruit bunch grows. Supporting the tree with strong wooden Y-shaped props under the stem helps hold the weight against heavy winds until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ be mli ni kui lɛ daraa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ko ni tamɔ Y ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ fi tso lɛ sɛɛ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ekɛ etsitsinɔnii lɛ ashi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off instead of turning into small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist by mulching around the plant base with dry grass helps lower soil heat and keeps flowers attached.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ eyaaa nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ni oooha tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi, ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing deep holes inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which attack the tender growing point of maize plants. Checking your farm regularly and applying recommended botanical treatments like neem oil or mild pesticides early in the morning stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa hei ni ŋmeii tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli ni ajieɔ yi tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni waaa lɛ atsu nii leebi. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting up and curling into tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni atsɔ mli afee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips damaging the leaves as they feed. Controlling these insects early with appropriate insecticidal soap or botanical sprays prevents leaves from twisting and stunting plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni fiteɔ baai be mli ni eyeɔ niyenii Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsei ahe tsofa ni sa tsu nii lɛ, abaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ amɛhe ni amɛkafee tsei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dry when the sun comes out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle harsh direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside them acts like a canopy umbrella, protecting the young leaves from burning while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi lɛ Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai bibii ahe koni amɛkashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow so tall with lots of green leaves, but the tubers underground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the plant puts all its energy into growing stem and leaf leaves above ground instead of feeding and expanding the food-storing roots below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a yeɔ ní nɛ a haa sisifãhi nɛ a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ toɔ zugba a sisi ɔ.

english: How does spreading dry leaves and decomposed chicken dung on my farm help my soil stay wet during dry weeks?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbi kɛ tsina ŋmei ni egbo ni mikɛshwãa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi koni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Decomposed leaves and animal manure act like a giant sponge in the dirt. They trap rainwater, stop it from evaporating quickly under the heat, and slowly release moisture and nutrients to the plant roots.
ga: Baai ni egboi kɛ kooloi ashwiei tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji wuji ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Amɛmɔɔ nugbɔ nu. Etsiɔ la ni hoɔ oya yɛ la ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi lɛ naa, ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai fiofio kɛyaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli.

english: Why do I see small holes in my young maize leaves with tiny brown dust inside the leaf center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii ni sũ bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ. yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The pest burrows into the soft inner growing leaf of the maize plant to feed, which leaves hole patterns and waste droppings as the leaf unfolds.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli koni amɛye nii. Enɛ haa bu kɛ jwɛi feɔ mfoniri beni baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds close together so I can get more crops on my small plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ lɛ?

english: If maize seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other underground for food and water, while their leaves block each other from sunlight. This makes all the plants weak and leads to small or empty cob sizes.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ ehe baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa tso bibioo loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my young crops if the soil is already fertile?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni bɔle midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo?

english: Weeds naturally grow faster and drink water quicker than cultivated crops. If left untouched, weeds steal sunlight, water, and plant food from your crops, leaving them weak and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛnuɔ nu oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi ni ataa he lɛ Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Yam plants produce energy through their leaves. Staking lifts the leafy vines high into the sunshine and away from damp soil diseases, allowing the leaves to make more food that goes down to swell the yam tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ baa kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Staking woɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa hulu lɛ mli ni ekɛ ehe kpaa gbee kɛjɛɔ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo koni ekɛha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off the stem before any pepper fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani pepper yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by extreme afternoon heat or dry soil. Dropping flowers is the plant's natural way of saving energy to keep itself alive during hot spells.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni ehi wala mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during peak sun hours to expose less surface area to the heat, reducing the amount of moisture the plant loses through its leaves.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ bɔni afee ni hulutsoo be lɛ akafee nɔ ko kwraa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni tsei lɛ fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I cut off the small shoot suckers growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajie midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Extra sucker shoots compete directly with the main plantain trunk for nutrients and water. Removing excess suckers leaves the strongest shoot to get full nutrition and produce a heavy, healthy plantain bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi kɛ plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛfee plantains ŋmeii ni tsii ni he wa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and soil moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Staking lifts the yam vines off the ground and spreads the leaves out to catch direct sunlight. This helps the plant produce more energy, which leads to larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Staking baawó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen in the soil or the soil is waterlogged from heavy rain. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn dark green and grow healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nu. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows corn pests to build up in the field. Switching to beans or groundnuts restores nutrients back to the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ baajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmeii loo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I avoid spreading fertilizer right before a very heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainwater washes the fertilizer off the topsoil before the plant roots have time to drink it, wasting your money and time.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Enɛ baafite shika kɛ be.

english: Select thick, healthy stems from mature plants that show no signs of disease or holes from pests. Cuttings taken from the middle portion of the stem root faster and grow stronger than those from the soft top or old base.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eda ni bɛ hela loo ŋmeii ni jɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ amli tsei ni mli tse ni wa. Nibii ni afolɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ateŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli lɛ yaa oya ni amɛhe wa fe nibii ni afolɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi bibii loo shishifãi ni egbɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my pepper plants with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass, known as mulching, stops sunlight from drying out the earth, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu la lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: You will notice ragged, chewed holes on the young leaves and small brownish sawdust-like droppings inside the central leaf funnels where the worms hide.
ga: Obaana buji ni atse ni atsɔ mli yɛ baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ anɔ. Eyɛ baa lɛ teŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli he ni ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off mostly due to extreme hot weather, dry soil, or lack of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Spraying neem water or mild soapy water helps control these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Neem nu loo samla ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to organize a group of farmhands for harvesting instead of doing it alone over several weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee okwaafoi akui kɛha nikpamɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee lɛ otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Harvesting alone takes too much time, exposing mature crops to sun damage, pests, and rainfall. Organizing enough labor allows you to harvest quickly at peak quality, preventing severe crop losses in the field.
ga: Nikpamɔ lɛ pɛ heɔ be babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa hulu la, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ. Nitsumɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛaaha lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa oya kɛ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Tsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ naa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to start harvesting my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije ŋmãa kpamɔ shishi?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer husks turn dry and brown, and the grains become hard with a visible dark layer where they attach to the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ wa ni nɔ ko ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni anaa ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmei lɛ he.

english: Why should I avoid harvesting my produce right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ nikpamɔ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excess moisture on harvested crops creates ideal conditions for mold and fungal rot during handling and storage, and working wet soil can pack it too tightly for future planting.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ anɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ nitsumɔ baanyɛ aha efee bibioo tsɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli dumɔwui.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings burn and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense heat. They require shade crops like plantains or shade trees to shelter them until their roots grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ adamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo koni amɛha amɛhe nɔ ko kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mitso titri lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with deep root systems that extract water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to overpower your planted crops if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ koo mli ni eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ tsei ni ato ama shi lɛ anɔ kunim kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: Why must I space my maize seeds instead of planting several seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi moŋ fe ni madu babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli

english: Crowding seeds causes plants to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in tall, thin stems with small or incomplete cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni fa babaoo lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii bibii loo amɛshɛɛɛ he.

english: Why does my cassava start rotting just two days after I uproot it from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ bɔi fitemɔ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni mijie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots deteriorate rapidly once detached from the living plant because cuts and injuries trigger a natural chemical reaction that causes internal discoloration and spoilage.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fãji kɛ pilamɔi kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni haa mligbɛ su tsakeɔ kɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers rot in the storage barn after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ fite yɛ shĩa lɛ mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot in storage if they were cut or bruised during harvest, or if the barn lacks adequate shade and airflow to keep temperatures low and prevent fungal growth.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ bɛ hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha hulutsoo be lɛ aya shi ni ekɛtsi ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do small holes and white powder appear in my stored maize grains after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu bibioo ko yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni powda yɛŋ ko je kpo yɛ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ amli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: The holes and powder are caused by grain weevils and pests that feed on the inside of dried maize grains when the grains are stored without proper drying or protection.
ga: Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu kɛ sũ baa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ to ni agbiko loo abuuu he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to create energy for tuber growth. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get maximum sunlight and stay safe from soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulb lɛ dalɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo kɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Look closely at the small leaf buds on the cassava stem cutting; the buds should point upwards toward the sky. If planted upside down, the stems struggle to grow and yield fewer tubers.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Nɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmei nine nɔ Esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ewa akɛ eeekwɛ̃ ni ebaawo ŋmeii fioo.

english: Young cocoa plants get stressed easily by strong, direct sunlight and dry winds. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside young cocoa shields the tender leaves and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ haoɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: This is a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant steals nutrients from its older, lower leaves to feed new top growth, causing the bottom leaves to yellow and die.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen faaa lɛ Tso lɛ juɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil nutrients through their roots. When the plant roots decay, they leave this free nitrogen behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso shishifãi lɛ fite Amɛbaashi nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid putting chemical fertilizer right against the stems of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts that draw water out of roots and stems, causing severe chemical burns that can stunt or kill young plants. Fertilizer should always be placed a few inches away from the stem.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Ekɛ tsofai ni shãa mɔ ni naa wa ni baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aba loo egbe lɛ baa. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when air temperatures get too high or when watering is erratic. Extreme heat damages the pollen, causing the unpollinated flower to die and drop off.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni bɛ pollen lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on leaf juices, or by plant viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Why are my maize plants growing thin and producing small cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miibɔi shwiemɔ ni amɛmiiwo toi bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak stems and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa, ni akpaa nii fioo.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds early within the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli

english: Young crop seedlings grow slowly at first and can easily be choked out by weeds that grow faster. Clearing weeds early ensures the crop roots get all available water and fertilizer without competition.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ daaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbe jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ mlɛo. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ naa nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: How can I estimate how many bags of harvest I will get from my plot before I even plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmaakpamɔ kotokui enyiɛ ni mana kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu nii lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: Every crop variety has a predicted yield potential based on land size. If you follow key farming instructions like correct spacing, weeding, and fertilizing, you are practically guaranteed to reach that expected yield.
ga: Every crop has an expected yield potential based on the size of the land. Kɛji onyiɛ okwaayeli he ŋaawoi ni he hiaa tamɔ gbɛ ni sa. jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ Ayɛ nɔmimaa akɛ obaaná yibiiwoo ni otaoɔ lɛ.

english: Is there a simple step-by-step guide available that shows me how to properly care for my crop from planting to harvest?
ga: Ani gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ko yɛ ni tsɔɔ mi bɔ ni mafee makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ dumɔ mli kɛyashi kpamɔ mli?

english: Yes, extension officers provide crop manuals and production guides that give clear instructions on planting dates, spacing, fertilizer rates, and harvest times for your specific crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, Extension nitsulɔi lɛ baafee dumɔ he gbɛtsɔɔmɔi kɛ nifeemɔ he gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni haa gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni mli ka shi faŋŋ yɛ dumɔ gbii, gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ kpamɔ bei kɛha onibii pɔtɛɛi lɛ.

english: If I plant seeds saved from my previous harvest, will I get the same yield as buying certified seeds?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ Ani mana yibiiwoo ni tamɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli he lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over generations and produce unpredictable harvests. Certified seeds are specially produced to guarantee strong growth, disease resistance, and high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛha amɛdara waa, amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Will planting my crops very close together give me more baskets of produce from my small land?
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ haa mináa nibii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ lɛ tsɛnsi kome. Mihe babaoo?

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in small, weak fruits. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to give you maximum yield.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibii lɛ daraaa ni ebɛ hewalɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha oná yibii babaoo.

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the nutrients, water, and sunlight meant for your plants. Removing them early protects your crop's growth and final harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ. Amɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaabu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ kɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow plenty of green leaves but produce very few tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ tomato fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes tomato plants to grow heavy foliage instead of flowers. A balanced fertilizer containing phosphorus and potassium encourages flowering and fruit set.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná baai ni mli tse yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ja ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ haa fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ.

english: What happens to my food crop yield if rain stops right when the plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be mli ni tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi pɛ?

english: Lack of water during flowering causes flowers to drop off before forming fruits, which directly reduces the total harvest you get at the end of the season.
ga: Nu ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai jeɔ kpo. Enɛ haa ŋmaa fɛɛ ni onine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ baa shi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do I need to add fertilizer to my farm if the soil already looks dark and rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii momo?

english: Crops pull invisible nutrients out of the soil every season. Fertilizer replaces these essential plant foods so that your next crop can grow to its full potential and give expected yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni anaaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ tsei niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ najiaŋ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anyɛ adara kɛyashɛ he ni eshɛɔ lɛ ni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni okpaa gbɛ lɛ aba.

english: Why do I need to plough and loosen the ground before putting my seeds in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsu nii ni mafolɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Loosening the soil allows soft young plant roots to spread quickly, access deep moisture, and absorb nutrients necessary for producing a heavy yield.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya. Ebaanyɛ eshɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli shɔŋŋ ni eŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekɛ nibii babaoo aba.

english: How does insect damage on crop leaves affect the overall amount of food I harvest?
ga: Te kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ saa niyenii fɛɛ ni mikpaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Leaves make food for the plant using sunlight. When insects eat the leaves, the plant cannot produce enough energy to make big fruits or seeds, leading to a poor harvest.
ga: Baai kɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii amɛhaa tsei. Beni kooloi yeɔ baai lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ afee hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ ni ehiii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I remove all the shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct sunlight. Shade trees and food crops like plantain protect tender young cocoa leaves from scorching heat, hold moisture in the soil, and help the plants survive their early growth stages.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ kɛ niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ

english: This rot is caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, humid environments. Pruning excess branches and clearing weeds allows sunlight and fresh air into the farm, which dries out the pods and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Gbɔmɔ nɛɛ jɛɔ ŋmei ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Yellow leaves indicate a lack of nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs to grow strong. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new top growth, showing that the soil needs organic compost or nitrogen fertilizer.
