ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmãa dalɛ Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛye ŋmãa ni yaa hiɛ yɛ ŋmãa heei anɔ lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves and greenish dust tucked inside the shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ani sũ eŋɔli ko yɛ ni akɛtee ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the soft tender center of the maize stem. Spotting this early allows you to apply safe organic or recommended treatments directly to the center shoot to protect your harvest.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni oookadi enɛ mra Enɛ haa okɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ koni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Does it make any difference if I plant my cassava cuttings slanting or flat in the ground?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ mi-cassava niji lɛ du yɛ koŋ nɔ loo mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ?

english: Yes, planting cassava stems at a slanting angle of about 45 degrees or horizontally helps the plant grow roots close to the surface, resulting in larger tubers that are easier to harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ aaafee digrii 45 loo ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ abɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni akpamɔ waaa.

english: Why do I need to clear tall bushes around my yam vines and let them climb on wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie brɔshi kakadaŋŋ ni bɔle sweet potato wain tso ko he lɛ ni maha ekwɔ tso tso ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce food for the underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the ground where damp conditions cause leaf diseases, allowing the roots to grow bigger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akagbee shikpɔŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ aha baai hela aba lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when water sits on my farm for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain floods the land without proper drainage, the submerged roots suffocate and decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi jɛmɛ obɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce many blossoms, but the flowers fall off without growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi efoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when water supply is irregular. Keeping soil evenly moist with mulch helps maintain soil temperatures so the flowers can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking leaf sap, or by viruses spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves healthy and flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ mli waa ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my farm soil richer for the next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have beneficial bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground, naturally enriching the soil for future crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast during rainy weather. Keeping your farm weed-free and pruning branches to let in sunlight and air helps prevent water from staying on the pods and causing rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ofolɔ tsei lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu akakpɛtɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are getting sick before the whole farm gets affected?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ dani ená ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Check your leaves and pods weekly for warning signs like unusual yellowing, dark spots, or wilting shoots. Removing sick leaves or pods as soon as you see them stops disease spores from spreading to healthy trees.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli daa otsi kɛha kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii, tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ, loo ŋmeii ni egboi. Kɛ́ ojie tsei ahe baai loo ŋmeii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha helai ahe ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight or dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains next to them provides cover and keeps the soil cool and moist while the trees grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ato ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why do the tiny white flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii yɛŋ lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii?

english: Flowers fall when the tree suffers from heat stress, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping shade trees nearby and maintaining moist soil helps tiny pollinating insects do their work so flowers turn into pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai ahewɔ. Keeping shade nearby And keeping the soil moist helps small pollinating insects. Tsu nii koni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What causes small insects to make dark patches and holes on my cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi bibii shwieɔ okadii diji kɛ bu yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ?

english: These are usually sap-sucking insects like capsids or mirids that attack young shoots and pods. Spraying approved treatments at the right time of year, especially when new shoots appear, protects your yield from these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids loo mirids ni tutuaa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ ŋmeii heei je kpo. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe kɛjɛ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why does my cocoa tree look green and leafy but produces very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyɛ baai shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: A tree can have healthy leaves but lack the specific minerals needed to grow pods, like potassium and phosphorus. Adding balanced cocoa fertilizer to the soil gives the tree the food it needs to bear fruit.
ga: Tso ko baanyɛ aná baai ni hi shi ebɛ mineral pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃, tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus. Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do I need to cut off branches from a healthy cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ kookoo tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ niji?

english: Pruning removes weak branches and unwanted extra shoots so the tree directs its energy into making heavy pods. It also allows air to flow freely through the farm, which keeps diseases from building up.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni ataooo lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni tsii. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akabua amɛhe naa.

english: Why do cocoa tree sicknesses spread so much faster during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Fungi and crop diseases thrive in dark, humid, and damp conditions. Raindrops splashing off infected plants carry disease germs directly onto neighboring healthy leaves and pods.
ga: Fungal helai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwereɔ yɛ duŋ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shihilɛi amli. Nugbɔ ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛ hela lɛ yaa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Can I grow cassava on the same plot alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe?

english: Cassava is not recommended because its large roots take up too much water and food from the soil, competing with young cocoa. Plantains are better companion plants because they offer shade without robbing the soil.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei tsuuu nii ejaakɛ eshishifãi wuji lɛ heɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ kookoo ni mli tse aka akaŋ Plantains ji nanemɛi tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ehaa hulutsoo ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know when an old cocoa tree is no longer useful and should be replaced?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ cacao tso momo ko he ehiaaa dɔŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsake lɛ?

english: If a tree consistently yields very few pods for several seasons despite good food and care, or if its trunk is heavily infected with disease, it is best to remove it and plant fresh, high-yielding seedlings.
ga: Kɛji tso ko tee nɔ ewo ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɛ bei babaoo mli yɛ niyenii kpakpa kɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa fɛɛ sɛɛ, loo kɛji tso lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ hela ko ni naa wa Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaajie amɛ ni adu ŋmeii heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How many years can a hybrid crop tree continue producing before it dies?
ga: Afii enyiɛ tso ni akɛfee ekome lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii dani egbo?

english: Hybrid tree crops are bred for strong growth and long life. With good soil management and care, a hybrid tree can live and yield good crops for 70 to 80 years.
ga: Afɔ tsei ni ji hybrid lɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Hybrid tsei baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai afii 70 kɛyashi 80.

english: If I plant short or dwarf tree varieties, how long will they last on my farm?
ga: Kɛji midu tso kuku loo tso bibioo Be enyiɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Short or dwarf varieties generally have a shorter lifespan than tall hybrids. They typically remain active and productive for about 30 to 40 years before needing replacement.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, henɔi kukuji loo bibii lɛ wala be kuku fe henɔi ni kɛlɛ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛbaaya nɔ akɛtsu nii ni amɛwo yibii aaafee afii 30 kɛyashi 40 dani ehe baahia ni atsake amɛ.

english: Which type of crop variety should I plant if I want a farm that lasts for my children to inherit?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ madu kɛji miitao ŋmɔ ni mibii kɛ minabii lɛ baaná gboshinii?

english: If you want long-term productivity across generations, long-lasting hybrid varieties are ideal because they can stay productive for 70 to 80 years, compared to local varieties that age faster.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ nibii ni woɔ yibii ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ yinɔi amli lɛ Hybrid srɔtoi ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ yibiiwoo mli afii 70 kɛyashi 80, kɛ akɛto maŋbii srɔtoi ni hiɔ shi oya lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know when my local tree crops are getting too old and need to be replanted?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mimaŋ tsei lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni adu amɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Local varieties usually start losing productivity after 30 to 40 years. When yield drops significantly and the tree looks weak, it is a sign that the plant has reached the end of its natural life cycle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ afii 30 kɛyashi 40 sɛɛ, beni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa ni etamɔ nɔ ni tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eshɛ ebɔɔ wala shihilɛ naagbee.

english: What is the main difference between planting local seeds and buying hybrid seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofa kroko fee lɛ ahemɔ teŋ?

english: Local seeds come from traditional trees and usually produce plants that live 30 to 40 years. Hybrid seeds are specially developed to yield more food and last much longer, often up to 70 or 80 years.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ jɛɔ blema tsei amli ni bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ tsei ni hiɔ shi afii 30 kɛyashi 40. Afee dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni akɛye nii ni ehi shi be babaoo. Bei pii lɛ, amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ afii 70 loo 80.

english: Why do extension officers advise farmers to choose hybrid varieties over local ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ okwaafoi ŋaa koni amɛhala hybrid srɔtoi lɛ fe maŋ lɛ mli srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Hybrid varieties offer better resistance to diseases, higher production, and a much longer productive life on your farm compared to ordinary local crops.
ga: Hybrid henɔi lɛ haa helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni anáa lɛ fa babaoo Ni nibii ni anáa lɛ wala be ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ akɛto maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe.

english: Can I plant both short dwarf trees and long-lasting hybrid trees on different parts of my land?
ga: Mibaanyɛ makwɛ tsei bibii ni hiɔ shi be kuku kɛ tsei ni ji hybrid ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ fãi lɛ anɔ. lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can separate your land into sections for different varieties. This allows you to benefit from the easy harvesting of dwarf trees while building long-term security with long-lasting hybrids.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oja shikpɔŋ lɛ mli owo fãi amli. Enɛ haa onáa sɛɛnamɔi ni jɛɔ tsei bibii ni akpaa lɛ mli baa lɛ mlɛo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ koni shweshweeshwe shihilɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei ni efutu ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are some seedlings at the nursery so small compared to traditional ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ daraaa kwraa kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ahe lɛ?

english: Some varieties are bred to stay small or dwarf by nature. Even though the seedling looks tiny, it is designed to grow into a manageable, short tree that is easy to care for.
ga: Afɔ kooloi srɔtoi komɛi koni amɛfee bibii loo bibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛji bibii moŋ Shi afee lɛ koni eda ni etsɔ tso kuku, ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii, ni ekwɛmɔ waaa.

english: Are dwarf crop varieties better for an older farmer who cannot climb tall trees?
ga: Ani tsei bibii srɔtoi lɛ hi kɛha okwaafoi ni edara ni nyɛɛɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, dwarf varieties grow short and stay low to the ground throughout their 30 to 40-year life, making harvesting much safer and easier without needing ladders or climbing.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, dwarf henɔi lɛ daa kuku ni amɛbaa shi kɛyashɛɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ amɛ afii 30 kɛyashi 40 lɛ fɛɛ mli, ni no haa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ shweshweeshwe kwraa ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ atswere loo nɔ akwɔ.

english: Will a very small seedling from the nursery grow well, or is it weak?
ga: Ani dumɔwui bibii waa ni jɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ loo amɛbaafee mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ?

english: A small seedling is not necessarily weak. Dwarf and high-quality hybrid seedlings are naturally small in their early stages, but they grow into strong, healthy, high-yielding trees.
ga: Jeee akɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kwraa. Dumɔwui ni ji dwarf kɛ hybrid ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji bibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ shishijee mli. Shi ebaada ni etsɔ tso ni wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living shade trees, protecting the cocoa from intense sun and keeping the soil moist while the cocoa gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ. Buu kookoo he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Which plantain suckers are best for me to dig up and plant on my new farm?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafo ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Look for 'sword suckers'—these have narrow, spear-like leaves and strong bases. Avoid suckers with broad, wide leaves because they produce weaker plants with smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante sucker’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishitoo ni wa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe ejaakɛ enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewo yibii bibii.

english: When is the right time for me to plant my cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei?

english: Plant cassava cuttings right at the beginning of the rainy season when the soil is soft and moist. This helps the cuttings develop roots quickly before any dry spell occurs.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmei tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei niji ni afo lɛ shishifãi baa oya dani hɔmɔ shihilɛi baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the bottom going upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually show a shortage of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives plants their green color and strength, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost will help correct this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: What is eating holes into the middle leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeli?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworms. They hide deep inside the central leaf funnel (whorl) of young maize plants and feed on the tender new leaves as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ hela nɛɛ baa, ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ (rings) ni amɛyeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why are black rot spots showing up at the bottom of my green tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji ni egboi miije kpo yɛ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the soil moisture changes too drastically, preventing the plant from taking up enough calcium while the fruit is forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation during hot days, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from losing too much water when the weather is very hot and dry. It is a natural defense mechanism to conserve moisture.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do I need to put wooden poles next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso ama sweet potato tso masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to climb upwards to catch sunlight. Staking gets the leaves off the ground into maximum sunlight, which helps the leaves make food to grow large yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ akwɔ koni anyɛ ana hulu la. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off without forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences stress, such as sudden hot spells, lack of regular water, or a shortage of plant nutrients at the flowering stage.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi kpe, tamɔ hulutsoo ni fe nine trukaa. Nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli daa loo tso mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct sunlight; high heat burns their tender leaves and dries out their roots, so they need shade from taller trees or plantains to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji loo tsei bibii adɛŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to build green leaves, or that heavy rain has washed the nutrient away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same spot on my farm season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of the specific nutrients that plant needs and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ yaa nɔ amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil without proper drainage, as excess standing water drowns the roots and encourages fungal diseases.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi ni ewo tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to spread dry grass on the ground around our plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ jwɛi afɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle nitsumɔhe lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, slows down water evaporation, and turns into food for the soil as it decays.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni ebafeɔ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ́ egbo

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and poor yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my seeds burn and fail to come up if I plant right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shãa ni amɛkwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain usually only wets the surface while the deeper soil remains hot and dry, which scorches tender germinating seeds before the real rainy season starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ pɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ kã he edɔ ni egbi. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ blɛoo. Shãa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: What is eating small holes inside the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Mi ŋmãa gbekɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by fall armyworms, which hide in the central funnel (whorl) of the corn plant and eat the fresh green tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji fall worms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmãa (ring) lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa ni mli tse lɛ.

english: How does clearing weeds around my crops actually help them grow bigger fruits?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops; removing them ensures all soil nutrients go directly into making your crops produce larger yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing thick stems and lots of leaves, but dropping all their flowers without producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli tse kɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi moŋ, fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ eshwɛ ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ?

english: Giving plants too much chemical fertilizer high in nitrogen makes them spend all their energy growing leaves and stems instead of holding onto flowers and forming fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ha tsei lɛ babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛbaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Mohu ɔ, e kpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi a he nɛ e woɔ yiblii.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct, intense sunlight. Leaving some shade trees or planting plantain crops alongside cocoa creates protective shade and keeps soil cool and moist so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do older farmers cover the dirt around their crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, prevents the hot sun from drying out the dirt quickly. It traps water in the ground, stops weeds from growing fast, and turns into manure as it rots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi muji oya. Ekɛ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ oya ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji egbo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil does not have enough nitrogen food for the crop. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps feed the maize so the leaves turn dark green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛbaadu nii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa aha kooloi niyenii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant beans or groundnuts in the same farm as my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ nii titri yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts naturally grab good food from the air and store it inside the soil through their roots. Planting them feeds the soil naturally so your other crops grow better without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii mɔɔ niyenii kpakpa. kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛ nibii krokomɛi aba. Onɔ̃ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when we get too much rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain pools on the land without draining, the soil gets waterlogged, suffocating the roots and causing rot-causing fungi to attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my crop seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant proper spacing allows roots and leaves to spread wide, leading to healthier crops and a bigger harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa babaoo. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa babaoo baa.

english: Why should I remove the small side shoots coming out from the bottom of my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni jɛɔ tomato lɛ shishi lɛ mli baa lɛ

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, waste the plant's energy on growing useless leaves. Cutting them off forces the plant to send all its food and water straight into growing big, healthy tomato fruits.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ, fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa ni miida lɛ anɔ. Kɛtsɔ amɛ ni ooofo lɛ nɔ lɛ, onyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ eniyenii kɛ enu lɛ fɛɛ atsɔɔ tomato ni miikwɛ̃ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do I see small chewed holes in the middle leaves of my young maize early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Small holes inside the funnel of young maize are typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Checking crops early allows you to spray recommended controls before the caterpillars destroy the crop's growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli mra. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofa ni akɛbuɔ hela lɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii dani ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or lack of pollination. Keeping soil moist and using mulch helps the plant stay calm enough to turn those flowers into pepper fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni bɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ kpoo bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaa nakai fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ aduawai.

english: Why does leaving weeds in my farm reduce the amount of food my crops produce at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ woɔ kɛji akpa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than planted crops and steal the water, sunshine, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get full nourishment to grow big yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa niyenii ni yeɔ emuu kɛha yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: Can I plant maize and cassava together on the same field at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows fast and is harvested within three to four months, leaving space for the slower-growing cassava to expand underground over the rest of the year.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Enɛ haa gbɛ haa ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni eshwɛ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow healthy. Applying animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji bɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa babaoo adara waa. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei tamɔ urea ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to support my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, feels moist and crumbly when you squeeze it, drains water well without staying flooded, and contains signs of life like earthworms and decaying plant leaves.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. E nuɔ he kaa e ngɛ fɔ nɛ e ngɛ tsɔe ke a ngɔ lɛ. Etsɔɔ nu lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni nu shwieee nɔ. ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsei ahe baai ni miigboi lɛ ahe okadii yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Leaf curling with yellow patches is a clear sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties prevents this problem.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. Whiteflies bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: What makes the bottom of my tomatoes turn black and rot before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo dani ekwɛ̃?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by uneven watering during hot spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any peppers appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which causes the plant to grow bushy leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naa baai akui yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing many green leaves but producing very few pod beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water or over-fertilizing with nitrogen encourages cowpeas to focus all their energy on leaf production rather than flowering and making bean pods.
ga: Nu babaoo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baaha cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee baai. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni efee pea pods

english: Why is it harmful to plant my seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces the growing plants to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and a poor harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tso ni miida lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni akpaaa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell when my yam tubers are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines on top begin to dry up and turn yellow naturally, showing that the plant has finished storing food in the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni wain tso lɛ baai kɛ eyiteŋ jeɔ shishi egbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii ni ekɛtoɔ eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, harsh heat. Without shade trees or plantains to protect them, direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the topsoil, causing the cocoa tree to shed its leaves to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ bɛ ni Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kookoo tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai koni amɛhi shi.

english: Is it safe for me to put fresh cattle manure directly around my growing crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee baabɔle he? Mi ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh cattle manure is too strong and generates heat as it decomposes, which can burn plant roots. It needs to sit and decompose in a dry heap for a few weeks until it becomes cool, dark compost before you put it on crops.
ga: Tsina ŋmei hee mli wa tsɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ baa beni efiteɔ lɛ. ni baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi Ehe miihia ni eta shi ni egbo yɛ ŋtayaa ni egbi mli otsii fioo komɛi kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋtayaa ni mli ejɔ ni mli ewo duŋ dani abaanyɛ adu.

english: When maize is planted too close together, the roots and leaves compete fiercely with each other for water, sunlight, and food from the soil. This leaves the plants weak and thin, producing small or empty maize cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very leafy and tall, but the roots underground remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni kɛlɛ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich leaf manure, cassava plants put all their energy into producing green top growth instead of storing food in their underground tuber roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii eŋɔli. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tuber ɔ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Pepper flowers usually drop off without producing fruit when the weather becomes too hot, when the soil is too dry, or when lack of insect visits prevents pollen from moving within the flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni kooloi ni gbaa mɔ naa lɛ bɛ Enɛ baatsi pollen lɛ naa koni ekatsi ehe kɛya fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Is it good practice for me to plant beans inside my maize farm?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa kɛha mi?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize helps both crops. Beans naturally capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil to feed the maize, while the maize stalks give the bean vines a structure to climb on.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli. Beans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei haa ŋmãa tso lɛ náa gbɛjianɔtoo ni ekɛkwɔɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a small fungus that thrives in cold, wet weather. Rain droplets splash the fungus spores from the ground onto the pods, causing them to turn black if the tree canopy is too dark and wet.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso bibioo ko ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i shihilɛi amli ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii amli ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ ediŋŋ kɛji tso lɛ shishi edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards and turning pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often a defense mechanism caused by tiny insects like whiteflies feeding on the sap and transferring viruses, or by the plant trying to protect itself from extreme heat and lack of soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ feɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni bɛ lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: How does hard, compacted soil affect the way my yam tubers grow?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ saa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose, and well-aerated soil to expand easily. Hard soil restricts tuber growth, leading to short, twisted, or misshapen yams that do not sell well in the market.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni wa haa tuber dalɛ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kuku, ni efite loo ni efite ni ahɔ̃ɔɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Weeds are wild, naturally tough plants adapted to the local soil. Their seeds sit in the ground waiting for water and absorb nutrients much faster than cultivated seeds, allowing them to shoot up before crops fully establish.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji lɛ amli. Amɛdumɔwui lɛ taraa shikpɔŋ ni amɛmɛɔ nu ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ dani tsei lɛ daraa kwraa.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect them from harsh sunlight and heat. Leaving tall shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides living shelter that protects young cocoa leaves from burning until the plants are strong enough for full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa kɛ latsaa he. tsei kakadaji ni ashiɔ hulutsoo loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shĩa ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ he waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow tall. Applying organic manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer early in the crop's life restores green leaves and supports healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni wala yɔɔ mli loo nitrogen wo mli yɛ shishijee be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua ni toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow strong when the first rains come, but then stall after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa waa kɛ́ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ba lɛ? Shi yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, ekpa nitsumɔ?

english: Early rains trigger quick initial growth, but as crops grow larger, they rapidly consume the nutrients in the topsoil. If the soil fertility is low, adding compost or fertilizer a few weeks after planting gives crops the ongoing food they need to keep growing.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa amɛdaraa oya. Shi kɛ tso lɛ da Amɛbaaye niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ ni yaa nɔ koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why do other farmers tell me to plant cowpeas or beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi Ko ni amɛkɛɛ mi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special crops that capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground. When planted with maize, they naturally fertilize the soil, helping your maize crop grow better without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Be ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa Amɛbaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Does planting my cassava sticks very close together give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he kroko lɛ baaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba?

english: No, planting cassava sticks too close together forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each stick enough space allows the roots to expand underground and grow much larger tubers.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛkwɛɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam tubers rot when rain accumulates around their roots in heavy or flat soil. Building high mounds or raised soil ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the tubers dry, healthy, and safe from fungal rots.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ bua amɛhe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa bulb lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehiɛɔ hewalɛ ni ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: These caterpillars are likely fall armyworms, a destructive pest that hides in the center funnel of young corn plants. Checking your field frequently and applying safe neem oil or recommended insecticides early protects the growing point of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe ewoɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli. He ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ shii abɔ kɛ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce many flowers, but the blossoms drop off before making fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when soil moisture is uneven. Spreading dry grass or mulch around the base of the tomato plants keeps the soil cool and moist, helping the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ. Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii afɔ ehe. Tomato tso lɛ shishi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why are dark spots spreading across the leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ miigbɛ eshwa mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Dark spots are usually caused by plant diseases that thrive when crop leaves stay wet for a long time. Watering the soil directly around the plant base instead of splashing water over the leaves helps keep the leaves dry and stops disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso hela ko ni baa kɛji tso lɛ baai lɛ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black spot baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nu ni oooshwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ agbi ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even if I give my crop field plenty of water?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo woɔ miŋmɔji amli moŋ?

english: Weeds act like thieves in your farm by stealing the nutrients, sunlight, and moisture meant for your crops. Removing weeds regularly ensures that all the water and soil nourishment goes directly to making your crops yield well.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua onibii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade from larger trees or temporary crops like plantains to protect their tender leaves from heat damage and keep the soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛkɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ amɛhe lɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore green growth and strength to the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ adara ekoŋŋ ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have small nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop season ends, this extra nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaving too many sucker shoots causes them to fight with the main plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main stem grows strong and produces a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Nibii bibii ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baaha amɛkɛ tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ awuu koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ to he lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo plantains babaoo.

english: Yam plants make food through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground and spreads them out to catch more light, which provides the plant with the energy needed to produce large tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛfeɔ niyenii. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa koni la babaoo abote mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young crops have small, weak root systems. If weeds grow next to them, they steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight the young crop needs to establish itself, causing permanent stunt in growth.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ. Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ emasɛi Amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ aná. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dalɛ sɛɛ foɔ daa.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the leaves and central whorl of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai kɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaai lɛ anɔ

english: Ragged holes inside the central funnel of young maize plants are typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Early scouting and targeted application of approved insecticides or biological treatments prevent severe damage to the plant's growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Scout mra. Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akwɛɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni akafite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ waa.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, which feed on the leaves and can pass leaf curl viruses to the plant. Controlling these pests early helps keep the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛyeɔ baai ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ leaf curl hela lɛ aha tsei. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot inside the soil before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays too wet for long periods due to poor drainage. Excessive water starves the roots of air and allows soil fungi to infect and decompose the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Nu babaoo haa kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat or irregular watering. Consistent moisture in the soil and proper mulching help lower soil temperature and prevent flower drop.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i aba shi ni ebaatsi fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to grow strong stems and produce big yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I wait for the main rainy season to settle before planting my maize seeds instead of planting right after the first short rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui moŋ fe ni madu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ kuku lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain can be a false start followed by a long dry period. Waiting until the rainy season fully sets in ensures young seeds get continuous water to germinate and grow without drying up in the hot soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ fɛɛ mli koni dumɔwui bibii lɛ aná nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ egbiŋ.

english: Why do I need to cut away the extra shoots or suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine loo ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: Extra shoots suck water and nutrients away from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one strong shoot forces the main tree to send all its energy into producing a large, heavy bunch of plantain.
ga: Tsoi ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ ŋmei kome pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛfee ŋmei wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen or heavy rains have washed the nutrients too deep for roots to reach. Applying organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps keep the leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe kɛtee shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa yibii kpakpai baa.

english: Why does adding animal manure to my farm soil help crops survive dry spells better than chemical fertilizer alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ashishifãi ni akɛfataa sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli jogbaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli pɛ lɛ?

english: Animal manure improves soil structure like a sponge, allowing it to absorb and hold onto water longer during hot days, whereas chemical fertilizer feeds plants but does not improve the soil's ability to retain moisture.
ga: Taakɛ sponji ji lɛ, kooloi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ eŋɔɔ nu ni ehiɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii lɛ, amɛhaaa sũ lɛ anyɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted in an open, sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily scorch in direct, intense sunlight. Planting nurse crops like plantain or shade trees gives young cocoa plants the shade and cool conditions they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo shade tsei ni aduɔ lɛ haa cocoa tsei bibii lɛ naa shade kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do flowers drop off my tomato plants without turning into fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause tomato plants stress, which prevents flowers from pollinating properly. When flowers are unpollinated or stressed by high heat, the plant drops them to conserve its moisture.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi haoɔ tomato tsei. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ pollin loo hulutsoo ni naa wa haoɔ amɛ. Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why does my yam crop need tall wooden stakes for the vines to climb onto?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ he hiaa tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to produce energy. Lifting the leaves off the ground with stakes increases light exposure and prevents fungal diseases that spread on damp soil, resulting in bigger yam tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo baai anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa la lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ naa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baafee wuji.

english: Why are there ragged holes in the middle of my young maize shoots with tiny dark specks inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mi-baby corn lɛ yiteŋgbɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ bibioo ko yɛ mli.

english: Ragged holes and dark powdery specks are signs of Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the central shoot. They feed on young leaves, which slows down plant growth if not treated early.
ga: Buji ni etse kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ ahe okadii. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii, ni baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots are fully grown and ready for harvest underground without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to swell or crack due to expanding roots underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ loo egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: I want to switch from growing tomatoes to maize this season, but will maize cost me less money to farm?
ga: Miisumɔ ni matsake kɛjɛ tomato dumɔ nɔ kɛya ŋmãa nɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli. Shi ani ŋmãa baaha mi shika fioo ni mikɛbaatsu okwaayeli he nii?

english: Yes, maize generally costs less to grow than tomatoes because it requires fewer expensive chemical sprays, less intensive labor, and carries lower overall financial risk if weather conditions change.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehiaaa fe tomato. Ejaakɛ ebiɔ tsofai ni jara waaa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ. Nitsumɔ ni he ehiaaa tsɔ Ni shika he oshara fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ baa shi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ.

english: Why do tomato crops require so much more money and attention to grow compared to other crops in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei biɔ shika babaoo kɛ hiɛdɔɔ babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Tomatoes are very delicate and susceptible to many pests and diseases, especially during heavy rains. This means you must spend more money on pesticides, fertilizers, and regular spraying to keep them healthy.
ga: Tomato lɛ he waaa ni eyɛ mlɛo akɛ kooloi kɛ helai baanyɛ amɔ lɛ, titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ ofite shika babaoo yɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant beans and maize together on the same land, and how will it affect my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ? Ni te ebaaná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very good. Beans trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer that helps your maize grow tall and strong.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa. Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ni ehiɛɔ shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow while they are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni amɛmiida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen in the soil, or the ground is soaked with too much water, which prevents the plant roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ haaa tso shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: How do I know if my bean crops are getting too much water during the rainy season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-bean tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: When bean crops get too much water, their roots start to rot underground, their leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the plant stops producing flowers and pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni tso lɛ baakpa fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii feemɔ.

english: What causes my tomatoes to develop dark, rotten patches at the bottom of the fruit before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomatoi lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbo yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi dani amɛkwɛ̃?

english: This is called blossom end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering or dry spells while the fruits are forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo shihilɛ ni mli egbi yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: Why are green caterpillars so attracted to eating my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛye mibi lɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ waa lɛ?

english: Young maize leaves are sweet, tender, and nutritious. Pests like the Fall Armyworm hide inside the central funnel of the plant where it is safe and humid, eating the leaves before they can fully open.
ga: Baby corn baa lɛ ŋɔɔ, eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe kwraa.

english: How do I know when my maize is completely mature and ready to harvest from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and a small black layer or mark forms at the bottom tip of each grain on the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi kwraa. ni ŋmeii diji bibii loo okadii yɛ Ebaa yɛ ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishigbɛ naagbee yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it better for me to sell my harvested maize immediately or store it for a while?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo makɛto be fioo?

english: If you properly dry your maize and treat it against insects, storing it for a few months after harvest allows you to sell when supply is low and market prices are much higher.
ga: Kɛji ogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ojie ŋmeii kɛjɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha onyɛ ohɔɔ amɛ be mli ni nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa ni jara nɔ jara hu yaa hiɛ waa.

english: Why is there so much demand for locally grown maize and beans in Ghana right now?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mɛi biɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo yɛ Ghana amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Growing maize and beans locally reduces the amount of expensive imported food brought into the country, which keeps food prices affordable for families and provides reliable income for local farmers.
ga: Maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni jara wa ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa niyenii jara waaa kɛhaa wekui. ni ekɛ shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ aha maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi.

english: How do I make my harvested corn seeds sprout quickly before planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-abele dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ akwɛ̃ oya dani madu?

english: Maize seeds require consistent warmth and moisture immediately after processing to wake up from dormancy. Setting up a dedicated warm space allows the seeds to sprout evenly and healthy.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nitsumɔ sɛɛ koni amɛte shi kɛjɛ wɔɔ mli. He ko ni mli edɔ, ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why is warmth so important when I want my maize seeds to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulutsoo he hiaa beni miisumɔ ni ŋmãa dumɔwui akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Warmth acts as a signal to the seed that natural growing conditions are right. If the environment is too cold, the seed stays asleep; if it stays at a mild, warm level, it triggers fast sprout growth.
ga: Dɔlɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ okadi kɛhaa dumɔwu lɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ shihilɛi ja. Kɛji shihilɛ lɛ mli ejɔ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baawɔ lolo. Kɛji ehi shi blɛoo ni edɔ lɛ Ebaawo shweremɔ oya he hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell that my corn seeds have started germinating properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: When you check on your seeds daily, you will notice tiny white roots or green shoots breaking through the outer coat of the corn seed under stable conditions.
ga: Kɛji okwɛ dumɔwui lɛ daa gbi Obaana shishifãi bibii yɛŋ. aloo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ amli yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ shishi.

english: What is the best room temperature for sprouting my corn seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji tsũ mli latsaa ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmãa dumɔwui akwɛmɔ?

english: Corn seeds sprout best in a warm, controlled temperature between 20 and 30 degrees Celsius, which keeps the seed active without overheating it.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔɔ, ni akudɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni ji 20 kɛyashi 30 degrees Celsius teŋ, ni no haa dumɔwui lɛ tsuɔ amɛnitsumɔ ni amɛdɔɔɔ fe nine.

english: What happens to my corn seeds if the sprouting area gets too cold?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji he ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i tsɔ?

english: Cold conditions slow down or stop the seed's internal growth processes completely, which can delay sprouting or cause the seeds to rot before they grow.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ haa dumɔwui lɛ amli dalɛ baa shi loo ekpaa kwraa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ asɛɛ afo loo eha dumɔwui lɛ agbo dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do some farmers sprout their corn inside a controlled room instead of outside in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmãa yɛ tsũi ni akudɔ mli lɛ amli moŋ fe ni amɛduɔ yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ he ko ni mɛi yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ?

english: Inside a germination room, you can control the temperature and protect the seeds from harsh sunlight, sudden heavy rains, or extreme outdoor heat that can dry them out.
ga: Yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Obaanyɛ okudɔ hulutsoo be lɛ ni obu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa loo kpo nɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi

english: How can I regulate heat in my seed room if I don't have expensive equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makudɔ dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ midumɔwui atsu lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛ nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: You can use basic temperature regulators, simple ventilation, or shading techniques to ensure the room stays within a comfortable, warm range of 20 to 30 degrees.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shishijee tsɔne ko ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ atsu nii. tsɔnei ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli loo hulutsoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛhaa koni tsu lɛ ahi he ko ni hulutsoo be ni ji digrii 20 kɛyashi 30 lɛ mli.

english: Should I move my corn seeds to different locations after I finish processing them for sprouting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛya he kroko beni mikɛtsu nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, once processing is done, take them straight to your germination area and keep them there. Moving seeds repeatedly disrupts their growth environment and slows down sprouting.
ga: Dabi.Kɛ́ afee enɛ pɛ. Okɛ amɛ aya he ni okwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni okɛ amɛ ato jɛmɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa shii abɔ lɛ gbalaa shihilɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ mli lɛ naa, ni ehaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: How often do I need to check on my corn seeds while waiting for them to germinate?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ amli be mli ni amɛmiimɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: You should monitor your seeds regularly every day to track the room temperature and make sure the seeds are sprouting steadily without drying out.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ odumɔwui lɛ daa gbi koni okwɛ bɔ ni tsu lɛ mli dɔlɛ yɔɔ ha ni okwɛ akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Can I use sprouted corn for anything else if I decide not to plant it in the farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ atsu nii kɛfee nɔ kroko? Kɛji mikpɛ miyiŋ akɛ miduuu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Yes, sprouted corn can be processed for animal feed, brewed into local malt drinks, or used in food products, depending on your needs.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ afee ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ afee kooloi aniyenii. Akɛwoɔ maŋ lɛ mli malt dãa mli. loo abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ niyenii ni afee lɛ mli Edamɔ ohe baahiamɔi anɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their leaves scorch easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and provide broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya kɛji hulu lɛ tso tɛ̃ɛ. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which results in tall, weak stems and small cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni haa tsei lɛ tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ebɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ dumɔwui bibii.

english: Maize plants roll their leaves during hot afternoons to reduce water loss through evaporation. It is a natural self-defense mechanism to protect the plant from drying out.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why does my tomato plant produce many green leaves but very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive leaf growth with few fruits usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer. High nitrogen encourages leaf growth instead of flowering and fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine ni aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa baa lɛ daa yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I burn all the weeds cleared from my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji mishã jwɛi fɛɛ ni mijie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter in the soil that feeds crops and retains moisture. Allowing cleared weeds to decay naturally improves soil fertility.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni yɔɔ sũ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans in the field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmã yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring nutrients that heavy-feeding crops like maize removed.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni akɛ niyenii ni tsei ni yeɔ kooloi babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ ejie lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during harvest or stored in hot, poorly ventilated areas. Keeping tubers dry, unbruised, and in a cool, airy barn prevents rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛto hei ni edɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi, ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ, ni amɛhi ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Black, dried pods are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, overly shady conditions. Pruning branches to let in air and sunlight helps stop it.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni egbi baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli fe nine lɛ. Tsei ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la aba lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa enɛ.

english: Why do improved seed varieties from the agro-shop bear fruit faster than seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni jɛ ŋmɔ mli shwapo lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specially bred to grow faster, resist common local diseases, and produce flowers earlier than seeds saved over multiple generations.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛdara oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi oya fe dumɔwui ni ato kɛha yinɔi babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the key nutrient needed for green leaf growth. It can also happen when excess rain water stays in the soil for too long and stops the roots from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii.

english: Can I spread leftover wood ash from my cooking fire onto my farm soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tso sũ ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ la ni akɛhooɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ afɔ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, wood ash contains potassium and lime, which help sweeten sour or acidic soil and make plants stronger. However, you should only use light amounts because too much ash can burn tender roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, potassium kɛ lime yɛ tso sũ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ acid loo ŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli waa ni ewaa. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okɛ fioo pɛ atsu nii ejaakɛ sũ babaoo baanyɛ ashã shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I put dry fertilizer on my field when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve properly. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil can burn and damage plant roots; it is best applied when the soil is already damp after a gentle rain.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei lɛ ashishifãi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the juice out of young leaves, or by viral diseases spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: What is making large ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny brown droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli ŋmeii wuji kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli?
