english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that hides deep inside the funnel of the maize plant during the day and eats the young leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi mli ni eyeɔ baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water pools around them in wet soil for days. Excess water starves the roots of air and allows fungal rot diseases to multiply quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ gbii babaoo. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni eye ebua fungal rot hela lɛ ni egbɛ eshwa oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without tall plants around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni cacao tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a sunshade and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa is older.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ Etsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant focus on growing foliage instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my crops yield much smaller harvests when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown crops fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and ground nutrients, causing all of them to stay small and produce less.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ bibii ni yibiiwoo hu faaa.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall sticks to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe hiaa ni amɛná tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ ni amɛkwɔ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally search for sunlight. Staking allows their leaves to spread out high off the ground to capture light, which gives the plant energy to swell its underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Staking haa ebaai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔɔŋ koni emɔ la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the expensive hybrid seeds bought from the store grow faster and yield more than the seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii ni jara wa ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ kwɛ̃ oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred in controlled conditions to combine the strongest traits of two parent plants, resulting in higher yields and disease resistance. Seeds saved from your own harvest lose these special combination traits in the next generation and produce smaller, less reliable crops.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni akɛ sui ni mli wa fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tsei enyɔ ni ji fɔlɔi lɛ amli lɛ afee ekome. Enɛ haa yibii babaoo baa, ni helai hu nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ bo diɛŋtsɛ okpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite nɛkɛ sui ni akɛfee ekome nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ nɔ.

english: Why can't I plant the seeds I harvest from my high-yielding imported crops for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu dumɔwui ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Seeds harvested from imported hybrid crops do not breed true in the second generation. If you plant them, the resulting crops will grow unevenly, produce much lower yields, and lose the special qualities that the original store-bought seed had.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee srɔtoi ni akɛba maŋsɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ baafee nɔ ni shwereɔ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ odu tso lɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee nɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee. Yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa. ni amɛfiteɔ nibii krɛdɛɛi ni dumɔwui ni ahe kɛjɛ shishijee shwapo lɛ mli lɛ yɔɔ lɛ

english: Why do my crops dry up and burn when I apply too much of the strong imported fertilizer to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ ni mli ewo muji babaoo tsu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers are concentrated salts. When you apply too much near the roots, it pulls moisture out of the plant instead of feeding it, causing the leaves to scorch and the crop to wither.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛ okɛwo shishigbɛ lɛ he tsɔ Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni shãa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egboɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my maize after I apply fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-ŋmã lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have wild, aggressive root systems that swallow up nutrients from fertilizer faster than cultivated crops can. Clearing weeds before or right after applying fertilizer prevents them from stealing the food meant for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei, ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni yeɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli loo beni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ okɛbaahã onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall with thick leaves but end up producing small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or too much shade, they put all their energy into growing leaves and stems rather than forming grain, leading to tall plants with weak fruit yield.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe nii moŋ fe ni amɛaafee dumɔwui. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ kɛ yibiiwoo ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers before any fruit begins to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or poor pollination causes stress to tomato plants. To protect themselves from dying, the plants drop their blossoms instead of spending energy to produce fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ gbele he Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaawo yibii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural way of conserving water during dry spells. By reducing leaf surface area, the plant stops water from evaporating and survives on the stored energy in its underground roots until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji ŋmei adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ he ni ebaa shi lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ eshishi shishi shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantain trees planted next to them during their early years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tso bibioo ko yɛ plantain ni adu yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs to establish itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo koni ekɛ ehe awo mli lɛ haa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and stop growing even when the soil has enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or aphids that feed on the sap and spread plant viruses, which cripples the leaf's ability to grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi.

english: Insects such as grain weevils lay tiny eggs inside the dried corn. When the eggs hatch, the larvae eat the inside of the kernel, leaving behind empty husks and powdery waste.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. ŋmãa ni egbi mli Beni ŋmãa lɛ fɔ lɛ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli. ni eshiɔ ŋmeii kɛ sũ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize is short on nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow fast. Applying fertilizer or compost early in the plant's life helps fix this before it hurts your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ mli mra yɛ tso lɛ wala mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ dani ená oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are some of my maize cobs only half-filled with seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ fã pɛ eyi kɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: When a maize cob has missing grains, it usually means the plant suffered from dry weather or extreme heat while it was producing pollen and silks. Without enough water during flowering, the pollen cannot fertilize all the seeds on the cob.
ga: Beni ŋmãa lɛ bɛ dumɔwui lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ na shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo latsaa ni naa wa waa mli yɛ be mli ni ekɛ ŋmãa kɛ siliki baa lɛ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, Pollen nyɛŋ afee dumɔwui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ fɔmɔ nii.

english: What causes my maize stalks to break and fall over easily when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shi mlɛo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa?

english: Maize falls over easily if its roots cannot go deep into hard soil, or if tiny insect pests called stem borers have chewed out the inside of the stem, making it weak. Planting in well-tilled soil and protecting plants from stem borers keeps the stalks strong.
ga: Abɛi baagbee shi oya kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ abote shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni Ale amɛ akɛ trunk borers lɛ, amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli. make it weak Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ, ni abuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why does planting soya beans help improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ soybeans dumɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soya beans have natural bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the soya roots decay after harvest, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Soybean dumɔwui yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni soybean shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know when my soya beans are completely ripe for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-soybeans lɛ eshɛ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Soya is ready to harvest when the leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving brown, dry pods on the stem. If you gently shake a dry pod and hear the seeds rattling around inside, it means the soya is ready to pick.
ga: Soybean lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛji otsi ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ blɛoo ni onu dumɔwui lɛ agbɛɛmɔ ni miitswa yɛ mli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ soybeans lɛ eshɛ klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: Why are my soya bean plants growing tall with leaves, but failing to make pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai shi enyɛɛɛ efee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Adding too much nitrogen fertilizer causes soya plants to spend all their energy making leaves instead of flowers and pods. Because soya makes its own nitrogen naturally, it needs very little added fertilizer to produce pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa soybean tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, soybeans feɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ he hiaa koni aná ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of water during hot afternoons. Giving your plants steady moisture helps them hold onto their flowers until peppers form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ ha edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings suddenly fall over and die in the nursery bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ gboi trukaa yɛ ŋmɔ mli saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seedlings fall over and die when the seedbed is too wet and crowded, which creates a rot disease called 'damping off.' Giving seedlings enough room and avoiding overwatering keeps the young stems dry and healthy.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji he ni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni kɛ hela ko ni fiteɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Damping’ baa Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli fe nine lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni dumɔwui bibii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotten?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato aduawai lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often because the soil dried out completely between waterings. Keeping the soil consistently moist allows the plant to draw calcium from the ground into the fruit.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ mli baa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ teŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛgbalaa calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad practice to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year, leaving the ground weak. It also allows pests and diseases that feed on maize to build up in the soil and attack future crops.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ He kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ egbɔjɔ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct full sunlight because intense heat burns their delicate leaves and dries out the surrounding soil. Leaving shade trees provides shelter and moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ehaa enáa wɔɔhe kɛ fɛ̃i kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ he waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu lɛ naa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and catch maximum sunlight. The leaves use sunlight to manufacture energy, which is sent down into the ground to feed and swell the growing yam tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ hewalɛ. ni akɛmajeɔ shikpɔŋ koni aye niyenii ni ehaa yam ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the primary nutrient needed for healthy leaf development. Adding urea fertilizer or well-rotted poultry manure will help bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ waa Kɛ́ akɛ urea loo kooloi ashishifã ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields of corn when I plant it on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil season after season. Rotating your maize with nitrogen-fixing crops like groundnuts or cowpeas helps restore soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Okɛ tsei ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ atsake oŋmei lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava grow tall stems with many leaves but produce very tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants get too much shade, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall leaves above ground rather than storing energy in its underground root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ náa hulutsoo babaoo. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up tightly and preventing the fruits from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni ehaaa aduawai lɛ adara lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit a plant virus. Controlling these insects early prevents the virus from stunting leaf growth and fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni hiɛ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Etsiɔ helai ni haa baai lɛ daraa kɛ aduawai lɛ anaa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by prolonged dry soil, extreme high temperatures, or sudden water shortages during the flowering stage.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shikpɔŋ ni egbi be kakadaŋŋ. hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni faaa trukaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why do some plantain suckers grow into strong stems with big bunches while others produce small fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi daraa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni wa kɛ tsei wuji lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi woɔ yibii bibii lɛ.

english: Plantain suckers with narrow, sword-like leaves (maiden suckers) store more energy and establish stronger roots than suckers that develop broad, wide leaves early while still attached to the mother plant.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ klante (bamboo shoots) lɛ toɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni hi fe tsei ni woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ, ni mli kwɔ mra lɛ. be mli ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ he lolo lɛ

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the ground without sprouting when heavy rain falls right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain waterlogs soil that doesn't drain easily, it blocks oxygen from reaching the buried seeds. Without air to breathe, the seed suffocates and rots before it can germinate.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ waa. Enɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ naa koni ekashɛ dumɔwui ni afu lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni abaanyɛ amu Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow thin and weak even when I plant high-quality seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your crops, leaving your main plants starved and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii fioo ko kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii titrii lɛ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why is it dangerous to use fire to clear my farmland before the planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ akɛ la baatsu nii ni akɛjie shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ aba lɛ?

english: While burning clears weeds quickly, an unmanaged fire destroys essential nutrients in the soil, kills beneficial soil organisms, and can easily spread out of control to destroy neighboring farms.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ shãa gbeɔ jwɛi oya moŋ, shi la ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Efiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ koni efite ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: I sprayed my farm once and the pests disappeared, so why did they return worse two weeks later?
ga: Mikɛ tsofa shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ shikome ni ŋmeii lɛ laaje. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa ni ehiii kwraa yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pest control requires follow-up because chemical sprays often kill adult insects but leave behind eggs; if you stop monitoring early, those eggs hatch and quickly rebuild the population.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni eda lɛ shi amɛshiɔ amɛwui. Kɛji okpa sɛɛnyiɛmɔ mra Nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛtswaa gbɔmɛi ayibɔ ekoŋŋ oya.

english: Why do I need to completely remove and burn a single diseased crop plant if the rest of my field looks fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ majie tso kome pɛ ni hela emɔ lɛ ni mashã kɛji akɛ mihe ni eshwɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: A single infected plant acts like a spark that can infect your whole farm; leaving it there allows winds, water, or insects to carry the disease to healthy crops.
ga: Tso kome ni hela emɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ la ni tsoɔ ni baanyɛ atswa oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hela, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ, nu loo kooloi bibii gbɛɔ hela amɛshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their roots cannot absorb groundwater fast enough to replace what heat dries out from their leaves, requiring shade plants like plantains to protect them.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛye dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni egbiɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Esa akɛ amɛkɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains atsu nii kɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves dry out in the afternoon even though I watered them heavily in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ okɛ nu awo ohewalɛ mli leebi?

english: Direct heat causes rapid water loss from bare soil; covering the ground around plants with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture throughout the afternoon.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa nu ni hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli baa. Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo tso lɛ he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ shwane muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, which results in many thin, useless roots instead of large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni faaa lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni he ehiaaa lɛ baa yɛ bulb agbo ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: My tomato plants are growing many tall green branches, so why am I getting very few fruits?
ga: Mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ niji kakadaji babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ aduawai fioo ko nɔ nɛkɛ?

english: When a plant puts all its energy into growing leaves and branches, it has little energy left for flowers and fruits; trimming excess side branches directs food back into fruit production.
ga: Kɛ́ tso ko kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsu nii koni ekɛha ebaai kɛ eniji lɛ adalɛ Fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ baaná hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ afã lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa niyenii lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ewoɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my maize plants turn pale yellow when I leave weeds to grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛji miha jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds act as thieves that steal fertilizers, water, and sunlight away from your crop, leaving the maize starved of the nutrients it needs to stay green and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same crop every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi moŋ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the ground time to recover, which makes the land tired unless you rotate with nitrogen-fixing crops like beans.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Enɛ ɔ ma ha nɛ zugba a nɛ puɛ. Ja okɛ tsei ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ amɛhe.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize when the rainy season keeps changing?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli?

english: You should wait until the soil stays consistently moist for a few days after heavy rains begin, rather than planting after the very first shower. Planting after a single rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up if a hot spell follows.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji latsaa ni naa wa ba.

english: This yellowing is a sign that your crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed its new top leaves, showing you that it needs fertilizer or organic manure.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Koni etsɔɔ bo akɛ ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo humus awo mli.

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts that attract moisture. Placing it right against the stem can burn the tender plant bark and roots, so it should always be buried a few inches away from the stem where feeder roots can safely reach it.
ga: Nuŋtsɔi ni mli eyi obɔ ni gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛ́ akɛma tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, be fɛɛ be lɛ, fuu lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi inchii fioo komɛi koni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ abote mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees produce large, broad leaves that create living umbrellas, providing the vital shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo baa. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni kookoo bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around my vegetables with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts as a protective blanket. It keeps the hot sun from evaporating soil water, stops weeds from growing, and keeps the plant roots cool.
ga: Mulch ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsi jwɛi lɛ anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in flat or heavy clay soil for too long without draining, it suffocates the roots and allows rots and fungi to destroy the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Nu lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni oha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is under stress, especially from extreme afternoon heat, poor soil water, or lack of pollination. When temperatures are too high, the pollen dries up and the plant drops the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli. Titri lɛ kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli. Nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ehiii kwraa. loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots growing around the main stem of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ atso titri lɛ.

english: If you leave too many shoots growing from one plantain root, they all fight for the same soil food and water. Removing extra shoots leaves only one main stem and one small successor, leading to much larger bunches.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ kɛjɛ plantain shishifãi kome mli lɛ, Nakai ŋmeii lɛ hu baatswa niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tso titri kome kɛ nine kome pɛ, ni no haa tso nine ni da kwraa baa.

english: Why do I need to use wooden poles for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso he hiaa mi koni makwɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants use their leaves like solar panels to make energy for growing large underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight and stay safe from ground diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei ni amɛkɛfeɔ hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la ni fa ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do small insects bore holes into my harvested beans after I store them in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-kɔfi ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ amli beni mikɛwo kotoku mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: These insects are bean weevils whose eggs are often laid while the crop is still in the field. Once harvested and placed in warm storage sacks, the eggs hatch into beetles that feed on the stored seeds unless treated or stored in airtight bags.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji bean weevils, ni bei pii lɛ amɛwoɔ wɔji be mli ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa ni akɛwo kotoku mli koni edɔ. Wɔɔji lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ. ja atsu he nii loo akɛto vacuum kotoku mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer will restore their green color and help them grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ adara waa Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi a-ŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnuts make the soil richer for the maize crop I plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the groundnut leaves and roots decay, they leave behind natural nitrogen that feeds the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmei baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite Eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen akɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my plantain trees help them stay healthy during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ Mi plantain shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Spreading dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the soil so it doesn't evaporate quickly in the sun. It also keeps the roots cool and prevents weeds from taking nutrients away from your plantains.
ga: Hay ni aduɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ, mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ lɛ, efoŋ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ agbala niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ plantain lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn plants roll up into tight tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔji ni mli wa yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the corn plant's way of protecting itself from losing too much water. By curling its leaves, less leaf surface is exposed to the hot sun, which helps the plant conserve moisture until the heat cools down.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni ŋmãa tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ anɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baajɛ mli aba lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni la ni tsoɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without growing any fruit when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when high temperatures heat stress the pollen, preventing successful pollination. When the flower cannot produce seeds, the plant releases it to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni naa wa lɛ miiha pollen lɛ miiba shi. Etsiɔ pollination naa koni ekaye omanye. Kɛ fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ Tsei jieɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do my cowpeas stay green during short dry spells while my maize wilts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Beni mi ŋmãa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have long roots that go deeper into the soil to find underground water. Their leaves are also adapted to lose less water through evaporation compared to broad maize leaves.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ shishifãi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Amɛbaai lɛ hu tsakeɔ amɛhe koni nu fioo pɛ afite kɛya hulutsoo be mli kɛ akɛto ŋmãa baa ni mli kwɔ lɛ he.

english: Why should I leave adequate space between my cassava stems when planting them instead of putting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ amɛ ama amɛhe lɛ

english: Cassava tubers need room underground to expand and grow thick. If you plant them too close together, their roots fight each other for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in thin and small roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji odu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ, ni no haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their tiny young pods before they can mature into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛbii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo dani pods lɛ dara kwraa?

english: This process is called cherelle wilt, which is the cocoa tree's way of balancing its energy. If the tree has more young pods than it can support with water and nutrients, it naturally lets some die off so the rest can grow fully.
ga: Atsɛɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ cherelle wilt, ni ji gbɛ ni cacao tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ehaa hewalɛ ni yɔɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ darako tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii, Ehaa fãi komɛi gboiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni fãi ni eshwɛ lɛ anyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and turning crinkly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Upward curling and crinkling in pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites that feed on the undersides of the leaves. Removing affected leaves and spraying organic insecticidal soap or neem oil helps stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Kɛ́ ojie baai ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni okɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa amɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting in the mound before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water gathers in the mound without draining properly. Wet, soggy soil encourages fungi and bacteria to attack the tuber tissue, causing it to turn soft and decay.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ sũ gɔji amli ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, ni mli efɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ahewalɛ koni amɛtutua tuber fãji. Enɛ haa efeɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ.

english: I noticed small black spots shaped like stars appearing on my mangoes. What is causing this?
ga: Miyɔse he ko diŋ bibioo ko. Nɔ ko ni tamɔ ŋulami je kpo yɛ mi mango lɛ nɔ. Mɛni kɛ enɛ ba?

english: Those star-shaped black spots are usually caused by a bacterial disease called Bacterial Black Spot. It attacks both the leaves and the fruits, causing dark marks that can destroy the harvest if left unchecked.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackspot bacteria lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nakai ŋmeii diji ni tamɔ ŋulamii lɛ baa. Etutuaa baai kɛ aduawai fɛɛ, ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my mango trees have tiny dark spots on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mango tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii diji lɛ?

english: Dark spots on mango leaves are often an early sign of a bacterial infection. The leaves show symptoms first before the disease spreads to your fruits, making them a great early warning sign.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hei diji ni yɔɔ mango baai anɔ lɛ ji mra be mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ ko eba. Baai lɛ baajie okadii akpo dani hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã aduawai lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ eji mra be mli kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi kpakpa.

english: How can I tell if dark marks on my fruits are from insects or from a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ mi yibii lɛ anɔ lɛ jɛ kooloi loo helai amli?

english: Insect damage usually leaves small bite holes or visible sap, whereas bacterial diseases cause dark, spreading spots, star-shaped cracks, or soft rots without obvious insect holes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni amɛyeɔ lɛ baa. aloo eyɛ latɛs ni anaa Bacteria helai, yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji baa, egbɛɔ eshwaa, egbɛɔ eshwaa tamɔ ŋulamii, loo egboɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ faŋŋ bɛ mli.

english: Can a disease that starts on my mango tree leaves move to the actual fruit?
ga: Ani hela ko ni jeɔ shishi yɛ mango baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ afã kɛya tso yibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mli?

english: Yes, disease-causing bacteria easily spread from leaves to the fruit, especially through wind, splashing rainwater, or dirty harvesting tools.
ga: Hɛɛ, muawai ni kɛ hela baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ baai amli kɛyaa aduawai amli oya. titri lɛ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni shwieɔ nugbɔ nu loo ŋmaakpamɔ nibii ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ

english: What can I do to stop dark spots from spreading all over my farm?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni black spot akagbɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: To stop diseases from spreading, cut off infected leaves and twigs, clean your pruning tools after use, and bury or burn diseased fruits far away from healthy trees.
ga: Bɔni afee ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã Kpãa baai kɛ tsei niji ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ. Tsumɔ nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛji okɛtsu nii sɛɛ. ni ofu loo oshã aduawai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: If I see a few damaged mango fruits on my tree, should I pick them off immediately?
ga: Kɛ mina mango ni efite fioo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ Ani Esa akɛ Mafolɔ ni mashɛrɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, remove infected or spotted fruits right away so that rain doesn't wash the disease germs onto healthy fruits growing nearby.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ajie aduawai ni hela emɔ amɛ loo amɛhe yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni nugbɔ lɛ akajie helai ni yɔɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: What does it mean when someone says my crop has a 'bacterial' disease?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ‘bacteria’ hela lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: A bacterial disease means tiny living germs have invaded your plant's tissue. Unlike insects that bite the plant, bacteria enter through small wounds or natural openings and rot the fruit or leaves from the inside.
ga: Bacteria hela tsɔɔ akɛ helai bibii ni hiɛ ka lɛ ebote otso lɛ mli fãji lɛ amli. Muawai boteɔ pilamɔi bibii amli. loo adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ kooloi bibii ni ŋmɔɔ tsei ni no haa aduawai loo baa lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ he.

english: Why do dark spots seem to appear on my mango trees mostly during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei lɛ feɔ diji bei pii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater splashes disease germs from leaves and soil onto healthy parts of the tree, and wet weather creates the ideal warm environment for bacteria to grow fast.
ga: Nugbɔ nu gbɛɔ muawai kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ sũ mli kɛyaa tso lɛ fãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ. Ni shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha helatsɛmɛi amli helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Is it safe to sell or eat mangoes that have dark spots on the skin?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaahɔɔ loo aye mango ni hewolo nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: While light surface marks might look harmless at first, bacterial spots quickly cause the fruit skin to crack and rot, making the mango spoil fast and lose market value.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ okadii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he yɛ shishijee mli moŋ, shi Bacteria spots lɛ haa aduawai lɛ ahe tsɔi lɛ fãa ni egboɔ oya. Enɛ haa mango lɛ fiteɔ oya ni jara ni eyɔɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: How can I protect my mango fruits from diseases before they even start growing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-mango lɛ he kɛjɛ helai ahe dani amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Good farm hygiene is key: clear fallen rotten fruit from under the trees, prune crowded branches to let sunlight and air flow through, and check leaves regularly for early signs of sickness.
ga: Okwaafoi amli hetsemɔ kpakpa ji nɔ titri ni he hiaa: shwiemɔ aduawai ni egbo fɛɛ ni egbee shi kɛjɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Ni okwɛ baai lɛ amli daa kɛji hela he okadii komɛi je shishi mra.

english: Why do my crops wilt and dry up so fast whenever the rains stop for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ baakpa otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Crops need water to pull up nutrients from the soil and cool themselves down in the heat. Without regular water, the plant cells lose pressure, causing the leaves to droop, turn yellow, and eventually die.
ga: Nu he miihia tsei koni amɛgbala niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛha amɛhe ajɔɔ yɛ latsaa be mli. Kɛji nu bɛ daa Tso lɛ mli wala yibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ baa shi. ha baai lɛ egbo ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni naagbee lɛ egbo

english: How will having a constant water supply like a borehole change the way my crops grow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni anáa be fɛɛ be tamɔ nubu ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ baatsake bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A reliable water supply keeps soil moisture steady year-round. This prevents dry-season stress, allowing your crops to continue growing, flowering, and fruiting even when there is no rain.
ga: Nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni akafee haomɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛya nɔ amɛdara, amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: Why do some parts of my farm produce weak crops while other parts grow healthy crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi miiwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni hei krokomɛi miidu ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Soil holds water differently across a farm due to variations in slope or soil texture. Areas that dry out faster cause water stress to crops, leading to uneven growth across your field unless water is evenly distributed.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni ahiɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋshɔkei srɔtoi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ahewɔ. Hei ni gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. ja aja nu lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ

english: Why do my maize plants need much more water when they start flowering than when they are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ he hiaa nu babaoo kɛ́ ebɔi fɔfɔi feemɔ fe be mli ni eji gbekɛ fioo lɛ?

english: As crops mature and start flowering or forming seeds, their energy demands skyrocket. They need extra water during this critical stage to support seed growth and produce full, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ da ni ebɔi fɔmɔ loo dumɔwui Amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛtaoɔ lɛ baaya ŋwɛi. Nu kroko he miihia amɛ yɛ be ni he hiaa waa nɛɛ mli koni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Can giving my crops too much water from a powered pump harm them?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli fe nine kɛjɛɔ pɔmp ni akɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, overwatering fills up the small air spaces in the soil, effectively suffocating the roots. This leads to root rot and prevents the plant from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni awoɔ fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaaa tso lɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is underground borehole water good for my crops, or will it behave differently than rainwater?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii? Aloo ani nu baafee enii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe nugbɔ nu?

english: Borehole water is usually very good for crops because it contains natural minerals from underground. Unlike erratic rainfall, it allows you to give crops clean water on a predictable schedule.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni jɛɔ nubui amli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ejaakɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ mli. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ nu ni mli tse haa onibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Will my crops produce bigger yields if I use a mechanical watering system instead of relying on rain?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo yibii babaoo kɛji mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ tsu nii moŋ fe ni mikɛ mihe baafɔ̃ nugbɔ nɔ?

english: Yes, because consistent watering eliminates periods of drought stress. When crops don't have to stop growing to survive dry spells, they channel all their energy into producing larger fruits and seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ jieɔ hɔmɔ he haomɔ kɛyaa yɛ be ko mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii akpa amɛkwɛ̃mɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo aduawai kɛ dumɔwui wuji.

english: Can I grow vegetables like tomatoes during the dry harmattan season if I have water on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai tamɔ tomato yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ mli? Kɛji miyɛ nu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Yes, vegetables thrive in the dry season if given enough water because sunny weather reduces fungal diseases that normally attack leaves during heavy rains.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛji amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni bei pii lɛ efiteɔ baai yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crops look droopy in the hot afternoon even when there is moisture in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po.

english: In intense sunlight, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. This afternoon wilting is a protective reaction to heat, and plants usually recover once the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ shwane nɛɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ji dɔlɛ hebuu nifeemɔ. Ni tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃i ba.

english: How does supplying regular water help my crops absorb the fertilizer I apply?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni mikɛhaa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Fertilizers cannot feed a crop in dry powder form; they must dissolve in water first. Regular soil moisture allows the roots to continuously take up dissolved nutrients for fast, healthy growth.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ powda ni egbi mli. Esa akɛ atsɔ nu mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii ni mli tse daa kɛha oyaiyeli, hewalɛ dalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die when they are exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and tender roots that dry out easily under direct sun heat. Providing shade with crops like plantains or shade trees keeps the soil moist and protects the seedlings until they grow strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni akɛwoɔ hulu mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the ground using stakes allows the plant to produce more energy through sunlight, which leads to bigger and healthier tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛjie amɛbaai lɛ akpo yɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo kɛtsɔɔ hulu la nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and supports crop development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does growing groundnuts or cowpeas on my land help other crops grow better later?
ga: Peanuts loo cowpeas ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi amli. Te ooofee tɛŋŋ oda jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When these plants die and rot, they leave behind rich nutrient-filled soil that feeds future crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ gboi ni amɛfite lɛ Amɛshiɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛkɛye wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same place drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like legumes or cassava restores soil balance and reduces disease risk.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ekoŋŋ ni ehaa helai ahe oshara baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soft tuber rot happens when water accumulates in clay or poorly drained soil, suffocating the roots and allowing fungal diseases to multiply. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds helps excess water drain away from the tubers.
ga: Tuber rot baa kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii helai gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do small chewed holes appear in the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Chewed leaves in maize are typically caused by pests like Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central leaves of the plant. Applying recommended organic remedies or approved pesticides early inside the crop funnel protects the foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ baa. Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii mra yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when heavy winds blow through the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛfo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and very heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy and unstable. Supporting them with bamboo poles or wooden forks (propping) prevents them from snapping or uprooting in strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii waa. Enɛ haa efeɔ tsiimɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso loo tso ni akɛfiɔ sɛɛ (ni fiɔ sɛɛ) fi esɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem before any fruits start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant undergoes heat stress or extreme dry periods, causing it to shed flowers to save water. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ mli haomɔ loo be mli ni hulu lɛ egbi waa. Ha egbee shi koni nu akafite. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it better to water my vegetable garden early in the morning instead of at midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ leebi moŋ fe shwane mli lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows plant roots to drink fully before the heat of the day causes water to evaporate. Midday watering leads to rapid evaporation and can scorch leaves if water droplets intensify hot sunlight.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu leebi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ nu mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya, ni ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã kɛji hulu lɛ ha nu lɛ mli nu lɛ mli edɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the topsoil. Keeping larger shade trees or planting plantains alongside young cocoa protects the tender plants until their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly ensures each plant gets enough food to grow large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves toward sunlight. Staking allows the leaves to catch maximum light, which gives the plant the energy it needs to swell its underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Staking haa baai lɛ naa la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer right against the stem of my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts that can burn the stem and tender roots if applied directly against them. Placing fertilizer a short distance away allows roots to absorb it safely without damage.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii kɛ shishifãi kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli tɛ̃ɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ gbɛ kuku nɔ lɛ Haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee.

english: Why does growing cassava on the exact same spot year after year produce smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, yibiiwoo faaa lɛ?

english: Cassava draws specific nutrients from the ground every season. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts those nutrients, so rotating with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas helps restore soil health.
ga: Cassava gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni kɛ́ adu amɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii lɛ afite. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I sow all my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season can be a false start followed by a long dry spell. If seeds sprout and there is no follow-up rain, the young seedlings will dry up and die.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Tso bibioo lɛ baagbi ni ebaagbo.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any fruit during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high or water is scarce, tomato plants experience extreme stress and drop their blossoms to save energy and keep the main plant alive.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu faaa lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ baaná haomɔ babaoo ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛha tso lɛ ahi wala mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen. The plant automatically moves the limited nitrogen it has from older lower leaves to keep the young top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ nitrogen fioo ko kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni eha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ aya nɔ ada.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground during heavy rain seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and cannot drain away quickly. Excess water starves the roots of air and encourages soil fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ejɛ mli oya. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ baawo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua amɛ ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ agboi.

english: Why do small caterpillars like to hide inside the very center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which seek out the tight center funnel of young maize because it offers shade, moisture, and tender leaves for them to eat safely.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni taoɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ koni amɛná hulutsoo, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ baai bibii koni amɛye shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I know the exact right time to spray chemicals on my crops to stop insects from destroying them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni kooloi akafite amɛ?

english: You should spray at the very first sign of insect damage or pest presence, preferably in the early morning or late afternoon when pests are active and the bright sun won't burn the sprayed leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ yɛ leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tsuɔ nii. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãŋ baai ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and drying out even when I give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbi eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the plant's juice, or by a virus spread by whiteflies, rather than a lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. yɛ nu ni baa shi lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why are the leaves on my coconut trees turning yellow and falling off before producing good fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ akokoso tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Yellowing coconut leaves often signal early stages of fungal infections or nutrient deficiencies, meaning the tree's water channels are blocked and need specific spraying or soil treatment before the tree dies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko eba mra loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ atsĩ tso lɛ nu gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anaa. Ni ehe miihia ni ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo atsu he nii tɛ̃ɛ dani tso lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow tall and bushy without giving me many pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwooo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: When trees receive too much shade or are planted too close together, they put all their energy into growing leaves to reach sunlight instead of making flowers and cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baama baai ni miida lɛ anɔ koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ kookohi.

english: Why do my maize plants produce flowers at the top but fail to develop corn ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ ŋwɛi shi ebɛ abele toi lɛ?

english: Maize fails to form ears when it suffers from dry spells right at the flowering stage or when there is not enough nitrogen in the soil to support grain growth.
ga: Abɛi nyɛɛɛ afee toi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ kpe loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do young mangoes keep dropping off the tree while they are still tiny and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ? No ji nɔ bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo?

english: Young fruit drops when the tree suddenly lacks water or when fruit flies attack the flowers and tiny fruits early on, causing the plant to shed them.
ga: Yibii bibii baagbee shi kɛji nu lɛ sɛɛ fo trukaa. Aloo kɛ́ aduawai amli ŋmeii tutua fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai bibii yɛ shishijee mli, ni no haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if my cassava crop needs fertilizer or if my soil is already rich enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii bɔ ni sa?

english: If cassava leaves turn light green or yellow instead of deep green, or if the roots remain thin after several months, the soil is low in nutrients like potassium and needs fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei baai lɛ batsɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ Aloo kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo yɛ nyɔji komɛi asɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii tamɔ potassium faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Do weeds in my vegetable farm really harm my crops, or do they just share the rainwater?
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo nyɛjaa nugbɔ nu kɛkɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, light, and plant food directly from your vegetables' roots, and they also hide harmful insects that cause crop diseases.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, kane, kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ o-vegetable shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ekɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ tsei ahe helai baa lɛ hu teeɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wither and die during the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that blocks the inside of the stem so water cannot travel up to the leaves.
ga: Bacteria wilt ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ ayashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: What strange signs on my crop leaves mean I should ask an agricultural extension officer to come inspect my farm?
ga: Ani okadii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ mabi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni ekwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should ask for a farm visit if you see widespread yellow spots, strange leaf patterns, sticky substances, or dying branches that do not improve with normal watering and weeding.
ga: Esa akɛ obi ni ayasara ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji ona ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɛ eshwã, baai ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, nɔ ko ni shwieɔ shi, loo niji ni miigboi ni eyaaa hiɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing and look weak around February before the main rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ February mli dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baa lɛ?

english: February is typically the peak of the dry season in Ghana. The high heat and dry air cause plants to lose water much faster than their roots can absorb it, forcing them to slow down their growth to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, February ji be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ Ghana. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ aba amɛdalɛ nɔ fioo bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: Is it possible for me to plant and harvest maize twice on the same piece of land in one year?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ madu ni makpa ŋmãa shii enyɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ afi kome mli?

english: Yes, in regions with two rainy seasons, you can plant a major season crop early in the year and then plant a second crop for the minor season around August or September after harvesting the first.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ kpokpai ni nugbɔshiimɔ bei enyɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ Obaanyɛ odu be titri mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ yɛ August loo September he beni akpa klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I clear and clear my land in February when the ground is still dry and hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ yɛ February mli lɛ? Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Preparing your land ahead of time ensures that when the very first rains arrive, the soil can absorb the water immediately and you can plant without losing precious time in the growing season.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni asaa kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ haa kɛ́ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ba lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaŋɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ni obaanyɛ okwɛ tsei ni ofiteee be ni jara wa yɛ tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Which crops can I plant during the dry months if I want to make money before the main farming season starts?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli kɛji miisumɔ ni maná shika dani okwaayeli be titri lɛ aje shishi?

english: Short-duration vegetables like okra, pepper, and garden eggs do well near dry-season water sources like streams or dugouts and sell for higher prices in the market when produce is scarce.
ga: Aduawai ni yeɔ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ okra, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔi, kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu jɛɛhe ko masɛi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli, tamɔ faa loo ŋshɔnaa ŋshɔnaa. ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ yɛ jara nɔ kɛ́ nibii ni anáa lɛ faaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cassava turn yellow during the hot dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during dry periods mean the plant lacks enough water to pull nutrients from the soil, or it is intentionally shedding older leaves to reduce water loss and protect itself until rain comes.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo tsɔ hiɛ ojie baai momoi lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni obu ohe kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into fruit when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms so they cannot produce seeds. When a flower isn't pollinated, the plant sheds it to conserve energy for survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ enyɛŋ ebɔ dumɔwui. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ pollen lɛ Tsei jieɔ lɛ kpo koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha wala.

english: Why do my seeds fail to come up if I plant them in dry soil before the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds are inactive living organisms that require moisture to wake up, soften their outer shell, and begin growing roots and shoots. Dry soil keeps the seed dormant or causes it to dry out and die.
ga: Dumɔwui ji nibii ni tsuuu nii ni he hiaa ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛte shi. ehaa kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ebɔi shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii shweremɔ Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ yaa wɔɔ. loo eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: How does spreading dry grass or leaves around my crops help them during hot periods?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass creates a protective blanket that blocks direct sunlight, keeping the soil cool and stopping water from evaporating away quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ blanket ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my crops right after the first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weed seeds are naturally adapted to the soil and can wake up and absorb nutrients instantly from the first rain, whereas farm crop seeds take more time to establish roots.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ete shi ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ mli Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ shishifãi.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting too much water when heavy rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miiná nu babaoo tsɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa je shishi?

english: If water collects on top of the soil for days without sinking in, and your plant leaves start turning yellow and limp, the soil is waterlogged and the roots are suffocating from a lack of air.
ga: Kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli, ni otso lɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How do I know if the seeds I received are good enough to sprout properly in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Good seeds are usually heavy, uniform in size, and free from cracks or insect holes. You can test them by putting a handful in a bowl of water; healthy seeds usually sink to the bottom, while hollow or damaged seeds float to the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui kpakpai tsii. Ha dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa Ni ŋmeii loo kooloi ŋmeii bɛ mli. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni okɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛyaa shishi. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni mli ewo muji loo ni efite lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crop seeds too close to each other in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too tightly together, the young plants end up fighting each other for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves all of them weak and thin, resulting in a much smaller harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ babaoo tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ ha amɛ fɛɛ amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nikpamɔ lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa.

english: Why do my crops need fertilizer if my soil already looks dark and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo duŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ momo lɛ?

english: Dark soil can still lack key invisible nutrients like nitrogen or phosphorus that crops consume rapidly as they grow. Adding fertilizer replenishes these specific plant foods, giving crops the extra strength they need to produce abundant fruit and grain.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaaa tamɔ nitrogen loo phosphorus lolo. ni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsuɔ nii oya beni amɛdaraa lɛ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ tsei niyenii nɛɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ kroko ni he hiaa koni amɛwo aduawai kɛ ŋmaa babaoo.

english: How far away from the plant stem should I apply fertilizer so I do not damage the crop?
ga: Te esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ shishi kɛya he ko tɛŋŋ koni ekafite tso lɛ?

english: You should place fertilizer in a small ring or line about a hand-width away from the main stem. If chemical fertilizer touches the stem directly, its strong salts can burn the plant tissue and dry out the roots.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli. aloo yɛ linei ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee tso kome kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ mli fãji ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale and yellow even when I give them plenty of water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa lɛ nu babaoo daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Water helps plants move food around, but water alone does not feed the plant. Yellow leaves often mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which requires adding organic manure or fertilizer to the soil.
ga: Nu yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ niyenii kɛyaa he fɛɛ he, shi nu pɛ nyɛŋ aha tsei niyenii. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense trick maize uses to protect itself from losing water in extreme heat. By hiding its leaf surface from the bright sun, the plant holds onto moisture until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋaa ni akɛbuɔ ehe he ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ baa lɛ hiɛ ni ekɛteeɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing lots of thick green leaves but no flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ hiɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo aduawai bɛ jɛmɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer without enough phosphorus or sunlight, they put all their energy into making leafy stems instead of fruits. Balancing your fertilizer helps the plant shift its focus to producing flowers and vegetables.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ ni phosphorus loo hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ baai ŋmeii yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛjwɛŋmɔ kɛyaa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai afeemɔ nɔ.

english: How does storing my harvested vegetables in a cold facility stop them from spoiling?
ga: Te aduawai ni mikpa lɛ ni mikɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛkafite lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cold air acts like a brake on the natural aging process of harvested crops. Low temperatures slow down crop breakdown and make it difficult for rot-causing bacteria and mold to grow, keeping your produce fresh for much longer.
