ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni tsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ naa. Dɔlɛ ni baa shi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi. ni ehaa ewaa ahaa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ akɛ amɛaakwɛ̃. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni onibii lɛ ahiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my fresh crops rot so quickly if I leave them piled together under the hot sun after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi nibii heei ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋtayaa mli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi beni ajie amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested crops are still alive and give off natural heat. When piled together in the warm sun, heat and moisture build up fast inside the pile, causing the produce to sweat, soften, and rot quickly.
ga: Tsei ni akpa lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛjieɔ dɔlɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ abua naa yɛ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ buaa ehe naa oya yɛ nɔ ni ato lɛ mli. Ehaa nibii ni anáa lɛ feɔ latsaa, efeɔ blɛoo ni efiteɔ oya.

english: What happens to my harvested grain if I put it into storage bags before it is fully dried?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui ni akpa lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛwo kotoku mli dani amɛgbi kwraa?

english: Trapped moisture inside wet grain creates a perfect environment for mold to grow and heat to build up inside the bag. This ruins the quality of the grain and attracts insects that feed on damp seeds.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ ŋmaa ni efɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni shwereɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa kotoku lɛ mli lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni egbalaa kooloi bibii ni yeɔ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for green leaf growth, or when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ loo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper crop flowers drop off before making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of essential nutrients in the soil like potassium.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes inside the center shoot of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are typically Fall Armyworms. They lay eggs in the soft center leaves of young maize plants because the tender fresh leaves are easy for the young worms to feed on.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms. Amɛwoɔ amɛwui lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ehee ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ nii mlɛo.

english: Why do my groundnut leaves develop small brown spots and drop off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: This is leaf spot disease, caused by a small fungus that thrives in warm, wet weather when rainwater lingers on the leaves for long periods.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso bibioo ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, nu mli efɔ lɛ kɛ baa he sũ baa. ni nugbɔ nu ni eshwɛɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why does my cassava grow tall and thin with thin roots when I plant the stems very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ ni eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo beni miduɔ shishifãi lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close, they compete for limited sunlight and nutrients. The plant uses all its energy to grow taller toward the sun rather than developing thick tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara be mli ni amɛkwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootswa tuber ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches when I leave many shoots growing around one mother plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni mishiɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ single mother tso lɛ he lɛ

english: Multiple shoots (suckers) share the same food and water from the ground. Keeping too many suckers starves the mother plant, resulting in smaller bunches.
ga: Tsoi (tsoji) babaoo kɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii. Kɛ́ ahiɛ ŋmeii babaoo mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ hɔmɔ aye lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ bibioo

english: Why do my tomatoes split open at the bottom just as they begin to turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ tswaa yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ́ ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when watering is irregular—such as a dry period followed by heavy rainfall—causing the inside of the fruit to grow faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa, tamɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tso yibii lɛ mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni ehewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ.

english: How do weeds growing near my cowpeas hurt my crop even if they do not touch the leaves?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cowpea lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtaaa baai lɛ ahe moŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and space beneath the soil surface, leaving your cowpea plants weak and malnourished even without direct physical contact.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko. Enɛ haa tsina tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ amɛmli kɛji akɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee tɛ̃ɛ po.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted without shade trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ ni tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight; unshaded sun dries them out faster than their young roots can draw moisture from the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade ni bɛ lɛ baaha amɛgbi oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of my saved maize seeds fail to germinate when I plant them in moist soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds stored in warm or humid conditions lose their vitality or get damaged internally by invisible molds and pests, killing the embryo inside before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ baafite hewalɛ loo amɛbaaná mligbɛ naagbai kɛjɛ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni anaaa lɛ adɛŋ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gboɔ dani aduɔ.

english: Why is it important for fresh air to move freely inside my crop storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aya miŋmɔshi nibii atoohe lɛ mli yɛ heyeli mli lɛ?

english: Good air circulation removes trapped heat and moisture from harvested crops. Without airflow, crops begin to sweat, which creates a warm, damp environment where mold grows and spoils your harvest.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔ. ni haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa Biɛ ji he ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ ni ebaafite onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I keep my harvested crops locked in a room without windows or air holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ mikpamɔ lɛ toɔ tsu ko ni samfɛji loo kɔɔyɔɔ bu bɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Sealing crops in an airtight room traps the natural heat and gases they produce. This build-up creates strong, harmful fumes and speeds up rotting before you can sell your produce.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ, emɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli la ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jieɔ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ nibii ni buaa ehe naa nɛɛ haa lasu ni naa wa ni yɔɔ oshara baa. ni ehaa fitemɔ yaa oya dani obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ nibii ni okɛwo mli lɛ.

english: How does the daily hot weather in Ghana affect the crops I keep inside my storage room?
ga: Te daa gbi kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtoɔ mi-nitoohe lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: High daytime temperatures make trapped moisture inside a storage room warm up quickly. This heat causes stored crops to decompose fast and encourages dangerous fungi to grow.
ga: Gbi mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ nitoohei lɛ amli lɛ mli dɔɔ oya. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ nɛɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ oya ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: How do dangerous toxins build up in my harvested crops after I pick them?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ amli beni mikpa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When crops are stored while still damp or kept in warm rooms without air, tiny fungi grow on them. These molds release invisible poisons called toxins directly into the food.
ga: Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo loo yɛ tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli. Ayɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo ko. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nakai tsei lɛ anɔ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ jieɔ tsofai fɔji ni anaaa ni atsɛɔ amɛ tsofai fɔji lɛ kɛyaa niyenii lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my stored grains sometimes feel warm and give off strange fumes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmaa ni ato lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ ni ejieɔ lasu ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ kpo lɛ?

english: Heat and strange odors mean mold and bacteria are actively eating away at your crops. As they grow, they produce heat, moisture, and chemical fumes that show the grain is losing quality and becoming unsafe.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ miiye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ waa. Beni dumɔwui lɛ daraa lɛ, amɛjieɔ dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i, kɛ tsofa lasu ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmaa lɛ ehiii dɔŋŋ ni ebɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I tell if my stored maize or groundnuts have developed dangerous poisons?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ oshara yɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli?

english: Look out for dark spots, fuzzy mold growth, a damp feeling, or a strong, musty smell. These are signs that mold has infected the crops and likely produced dangerous toxins.
ga: Taomɔ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ. Mold dalɛ bɛ faŋŋ, enuɔ he akɛ edɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni naa wa. Enɛɛmɛi ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei ko ebote ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ oshara aba.

english: Why should I dry my harvested crops completely on a drying floor before putting them in my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mikpamɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani mikɛto mi nitoohe lɛ?

english: Drying removes the water inside the grain that mold needs to survive. Properly dried crops can be stored safely without overheating or developing dangerous chemical fumes.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ejieɔ nu ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli ni he hiaa ŋmei lɛ koni ehi shi lɛ. Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ato shweshweeshwe ni dɔlɛ ni fe nine loo tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Can eating or selling moldy crops really cause terrible human illnesses like liver cancer?
ga: Ani tsei ni ŋmei yɔɔ mli ni ayeɔ loo ahɔ̃ɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ helai ni naa wa, tamɔ mlɛbo mli kansa aba adesai anɔ?

english: Yes, moldy crops like maize and groundnuts often contain toxins that do not disappear when cooked. Over time, eating food with these poisons directly damages the liver and can cause liver cancer.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Bei pii lɛ, tsofai fɔji ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kɛ́ ahoo lɛ sɛɛ efooo lɛ yɛ mli. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Niyenii ni nɛkɛ tsofai fɔji nɛɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ fiteɔ mlɛbo lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ mlɛbo mli kansa aba.

english: How does entering a damp, poorly ventilated storage room affect my own health?
ga: Te nibii ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli efɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ baaná mihewalɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Breathing in concentrated fumes, dust, and mold spores from an unventilated storage room can cause severe chest infections, lung damage, and long-term sickness.
ga: Lasu ni mli eyi obɔ, sũ, kɛ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ nibii ni akɛtoɔ nibii amli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha mɔ aná tsitsi mli helai ni naa wa, efite fɛ̃i, ni eha mɔ he ajɔ lɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it dangerous for me to sell bad or poorly stored crops at the local market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii loo ni akɛtoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ ji oshara kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Selling toxic or spoiled crops spreads dangerous diseases to buyers in the community. It also ruins your reputation as a farmer, making traders reject your produce in the future.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ poizin loo nibii ni efite ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ gbɛɔ hela eshwaa mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ akutso lɛ mli lɛ. Efiteɔ gbɛi kpakpa ni oyɔɔ akɛ okwaafonyo lɛ hu. Ha jarayelɔi akpoo nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why should I consult an agricultural extension officer right from the start when preparing my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mayabi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Getting expert advice at the very beginning helps you choose the right crop varieties, prepare the soil correctly, and avoid costly mistakes that could ruin your farm before the crops even have a chance to mature.
ga: Kɛ́ onine shɛ ŋaawoo ni he esa nɔ kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ohala tso srɔtoi ni sa. Saamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ Ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tɔmɔi ni baanyɛ afite oŋmɔ lɛ he dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does it take about two years before I can expect to start making money from tree crops like cocoa or cashew?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe aaafee afii enyɔ dani mibɔi shika namɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo loo cashew ŋmeii amli lɛ?

english: During the first two years, young crops direct all their energy into building strong roots, thick stems, and healthy leaves rather than producing fruit. Once this foundation is solid, the crop matures and begins producing high yields that generate steady income.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, tsei bibii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ shishifãi ni wa, tsei ni mli tse, kɛ baai ni wa ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli. yɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ Kɛji shishitoo nɛɛ ama shi shiŋŋ lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ebɔi yibii babaoo ni haa shika ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is regular weeding and maintenance so critical during the first two years of planting a new crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa kɛ ekwɛmɔ he hiaa waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ ni akɛduɔ tso hee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crops have small, delicate root systems that easily lose the fight against weeds for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Keeping the field clean during these initial years gives the young plants the space and food they need to grow strong.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni haa amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi lɛ mlɛo koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛjegbɛ lɛ mli hetsemɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli Enɛɛmɛi baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither so quickly in the dry season compared to full-grown trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ akɛto tsei ni eda lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young seedlings only have shallow roots near the surface where the soil dries out fast. Fully grown trees have deep taproots that reach far underground to collect water, allowing them to withstand long dry periods.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ Tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni amɛkɛ nu ato. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ edamɔ hɔmɔ naa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is proper spacing between my young crops so important right at the planting stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛ ni sa ni kã midumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ he hiaa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ adumɔ mli lɛ?

english: Spacing gives plants enough room to expand their roots and branches as they grow over the years. Correct spacing prevents crops from blocking each other's sunlight and stealing nutrients from neighboring plants as they mature.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa amɛnáa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛniji amli be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ afii lɛ amli lɛ. He ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa. ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: If my crop starts showing flowers in its first year, should I let it grow fruit immediately?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔi fɔmɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli Ani Esa akɛ maha etsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is often better to remove flowers during the first year so the plant does not waste vital energy on early fruit. Plucking early flowers forces the crop to store energy into growing a bigger body that will produce much higher yields in later years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii fioo lɛ anɔ. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha fɔfɔi wuji ni baa lɛ. Enɛ baaha yibii babaoo aba yɛ afii ni baa lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to clear and loosen the soil thoroughly before transplanting my young seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni mafolɔ mli dani mikɛ dumɔwui bibii awo mli lɛ?

english: Soft, loose soil makes it easier for tender new roots to push through and establish themselves quickly. Good root establishment in the first few months ensures the crop stays anchored and absorbs fertilizer efficiently.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse ehe lɛ haa shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ boteɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi oya. Shishifãi kpakpai ni baa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa tso lɛ mɔɔ shi ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Do young crops in their first year need different care and fertilizer than mature, fruit-bearing crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ he miihia kwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ srɔto fe aduawai ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ?

english: Yes, young crops need nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus to build roots, stems, and leaves, while mature crops need more potassium to form flowers and fruit. Tailoring food to the crop's age ensures proper development.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei bibii lɛ he miihia niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus koni amɛfee shishifãi, ŋmeii kɛ baai, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia potassium babaoo koni amɛfee fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai. Niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ afii ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eye lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do young cocoa and plantain seedlings need shade plants overhead during their early growth stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni cocoa kɛ plantain dumɔwui lɛ he hiaa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi yɛ amɛdalɛ mra lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Delicate leaves on young plants burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Temporary shade crops protect young leaves from hot midday sun and hold moisture in the air until the crop becomes tough enough to stand full sunlight.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ buɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ he wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ.

english: Why are insect attacks much more dangerous to a crop in its first few months than when it is fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ oshara waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli fe be mli ni amɛdara kwraa lɛ?

english: A young plant has very few leaves and small energy reserves, so an insect attack can destroy all its leaves and kill it instantly. A mature tree has thousands of leaves and strong stems, allowing it to survive minor pest damage and recover quickly.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ bɛ baai fioo ko pɛ, ni hewalɛ fioo pɛ amɛyɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kooloo ni tutuaa lɛ lɛ baanyɛ akpata ebaai lɛ ahiɛ kwraa ni egbe lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Tso ni eda lɛ yɛ baai akpei abɔ kɛ tso ni mli wa. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ nibii bibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ lɛ amli, ni ehiɔ shi oya.

english: Leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to make food and stay green. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize takes nitrogen out of the soil, while cowpeas put nitrogen back into the soil through their roots. Rotating them keeps the soil fertile without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi cowpea lɛ, ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Rotation haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why does my yam farm produce very small tubers even though the leaves above ground look very big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the yam plant spends all its strength growing thick leaves above ground instead of sending energy down to build big tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Sweet potato tso lɛ baafite ebe fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or whiteflies hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juice, or from a virus spread by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly appear and eat my crops right after the early rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baa trukaa koni amɛbaye miŋmɔshi nibii beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Moths lay eggs in the weeds and soil during the dry period. When the first rains arrive, the eggs hatch into hungry caterpillars just as your seeds begin to sprout.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi lɛ fɔɔ amɛwuji yɛ jwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ba lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ be mli ni odumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my dried maize grains get full of small holes and black insects after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni kooloi diji ni akɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Weevil insects lay hidden eggs inside the maize kernels while the crop is still in the field, and these eggs hatch into beetles later when stored in warm conditions.
ga: Weevils lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui ni akɛtee ŋmãa mli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Ni sɛɛ mli lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in poorly drained soil, which suffocates the roots and encourages mold to grow underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot and dry, or when the soil doesn't get enough water, which prevents the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ awooo yibii.

english: Wait until the soil has received two or three deep soaking rains, so the seeds have enough moisture beneath the surface to stay alive even if there is a short dry gap.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shishigbɛ koni amɛhi shi kɛji akɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli egbi kuku po.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They require shade trees or plantains nearby to block direct heat and keep the soil moist until the cocoa bushes grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Amɛmiitao tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves wilt in the middle of the afternoon even when the soil still has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Ani nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo?

english: During intense afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose moisture into the air faster than the roots can pull water from the soil. This temporary wilting is a protective reaction to reduce water loss, and the leaves usually recover once the temperature cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Pepper baai lɛ fiteɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli nɛɛ ji nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Ni bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ahe baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop drop almost all its leaves during the dry season? Is it dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo efo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ? Ani eegbo?

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally during dry periods to conserve water and survive drought. The plant is not dying; it goes dormant while keeping the edible tubers safe underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Tso lɛ gbooo, eyaa wɔɔ yɛ be mli ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni ayeɔ lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when daytime temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly. Extreme weather prevents proper pollination, causing the plant to shed the blossoms instead of developing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake trukaa Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Yam vines produce leaves that need maximum sunlight to capture energy. Staking allows the vines to spread out upward, which helps the plant make enough food to develop large tubers below the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei woɔ baai ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni akɛto hewalɛ. Staking haa wain tso lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulbs agboi baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the newer top leaves, causing the older bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Abele baai lɛ ashishi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei amli. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why is it good to mix dried animal manure into my soil instead of relying only on chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni akɛ he aaafɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli pɛ nɔ?

english: Animal manure improves soil structure by helping sand or clay hold onto moisture and nutrients much longer. While chemical fertilizers feed the plant quickly, manure builds long-term soil health and feeds beneficial soil organisms.
ga: Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo kɛtsɔ ŋã loo shikpɔŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii amli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii oya moŋ, shi ŋmɔshi nibii maa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Planting maize too close together causes the plants to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks with small ears, yielding less food overall than properly spaced plants.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ toi bibii baa. Enɛ haa niyenii fɛɛ baa shi fe tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to the local environment, allowing them to absorb water and nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing essential resources from your young plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ebɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe tsei ni amɛ duɔ lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nibii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I see small holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dark droppings inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding inside the growing tip of the plant. Applying recommended remedies directly into the leaf funnel early in the infestation protects the growing point so the maize can continue to develop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni naa niyenii yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Ni akɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ baatsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ amli mra. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ he ni ŋmãa lɛ daa lɛ he koni ŋmãa lɛ aya nɔ eda.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to grow green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores this color and helps the plant grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii tso titri ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ su nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land yield less maize every time I plant it on the same plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and lets pests build up. Alternating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nutrients to the soil and stops pests from multiplying.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ afɔ.

english: Why did my crops turn brown and look burned after I applied chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛshã beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts. Applying too much fertilizer at once or putting it too close to the roots draws water out of the plant, causing the leaves to dry up and look burned.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ yɛ ŋoo babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he shikome loo okɛma shishitoo lɛ he tsɔ lɛ, ebaajie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ashã.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to produce larger, healthier yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big trees from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn under full sunlight. Keeping large shade trees or planting plantains around them creates a cool canopy that protects the young cocoa from hot sun and dry winds.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei wuji akwɛmɔ koni amɛha amɛná hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ Ehaa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout if I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain often moistens only the top layer of dry soil, which dries out quickly under the sun. Seeds need continuous soil moisture to sprout, so waiting for consistent rains prevents seeds from drying up underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ pɛ. ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la shishi Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Maintaining steady watering during dry spells helps the plant keep its flowers and make fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil during a very heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen to stay healthy. When heavy rains waterlog the soil and water cannot drain away, root drowning occurs, which causes the tubers to rot underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi he miihia oxygen koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi, shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajɛ mli, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during the hottest hours to protect themselves from losing too much water. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism against heat and temporary thirsty soil.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni kumai yeɔ lɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: How do weeds reduce my crop yield even when there seems to be plenty of space between plants?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tsei lɛ amli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and light from the soil. Clearing weeds early leaves all the available water and plant food for your crops to use.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ ni amɛkɛ ekãa juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha nu kɛ tsei aniyenii ahi shi ni otsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient for leafy growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly exhausts the specific nutrients that plant needs and allows specialized soil pests and diseases to build up, leading to poorer yields each year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ aya. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my farm when the ground is damp rather than when the soil is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ fe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ?

english: Plant roots can only drink in fertilizer when it is dissolved in water. Applying fertilizer to dry soil leaves it trapped on top and can burn the roots of your crop.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ kɛji akɛ etsɔ nu mli. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat or irregular watering. Mulching the soil keeps the roots cool and moist, helping the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant's sap and transferring viral diseases. Controlling these pests early stops the leaves from crumpling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when rain falls continuously for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them because the roots cannot breathe without air in the soil. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi nyɛŋ amu kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade trees planted next to them during their early growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu tso ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Yɛ dalɛ ni yaa oya lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in strong direct sunlight. Shade trees protect them from harsh heat and preserve soil moisture so the cocoa can establish strong roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ato shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when many shoot stems grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ feɔ kui bibii beni tsei babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɔleɔ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: The extra shoot stems, called suckers, steal plant food, water, and sunlight from the main mother tree. Pruning away extra suckers leaves more energy for the main plant to yield larger bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ tso niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfee ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting in the storage barn even without soil or water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ loo nu bɛ jɛmɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers have an internal biological clock that naturally breaks their rest period after a few months, signaling the tuber to shoot out vines in preparation for a new growing phase.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa ko ni yɔɔ mli ni yaa adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ okadi akɛ amɛbaatswa wain tso lɛ koni amɛkɛsaa amɛhe kɛha dalɛ fã hee.

english: Why do crop diseases spread much faster during the wet season than during the dry harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli fe harmatta ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fungi and bacteria thrive in high humidity and warm damp conditions. Rain splashes water from leaf to leaf, carrying disease organisms across the entire field quickly.
ga: Mold kɛ muawai yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i mli. Nugbɔ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baa kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Okɛ helatsɛmɛi oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do tiny bugs suddenly appear in my stored maize months after harvest even though the bag was tied tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ ŋmãa ni ato yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa nyɔji babaoo sɛɛ lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ akpɛtɛ kotokui lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Insects like weevils lay tiny, invisible eggs inside the grains while the crop is still in the field. These eggs remain dormant inside the grain for weeks until warm conditions cause them to hatch into adult bugs long after you have stored them.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. Anyɛɛɛ ana nakai yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ hiɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli otsii babaoo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eda ni shãa ŋmeii beni okɛ amɛ ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my stored cowpea beans end up with small holes and powdery dust inside the sack after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ lɛ tee nɔ ehi kotoku lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Bean beetles lay microscopic eggs on the seed coat before or during harvest. The eggs take time to hatch into tiny larvae that bore inside the bean, eat the food inside, and emerge later as adult insects, leaving holes behind.
ga: Pea beetles lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe dani loo yɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli. Wɔɔji heɔ be dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii. ni boteɔ ŋmei dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ Yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ejeɔ kpo akɛ kooloo ni eda, ni eshiɔ bu yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can insect eggs inside imported crop produce survive long journeys and hatch on my farm?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, many pest eggs and larvae can stay alive and dormant inside produce or feed for weeks or months during long ocean transport. When they reach local warm weather, they hatch and can spread to local crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ amɛmli ŋmeii babaoo baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo nibii ni adu loo niyenii amli otsii loo nyɔji babaoo yɛ ŋshɔ hiɛ nibii ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ amli. Kɛji maŋ lɛ mli latsaa be lɛ bashɛ Ebaafɔ ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: How can I test if seed maize I saved from last season is still alive and ready to grow before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni esa akɛ adu dani adu?

english: You can wrap a sample of 10 seeds in a moist cloth for a few days. If most seeds sprout sprouts, the batch is alive and healthy; if they remain soft or rot, the seed embryo inside is dead and will not grow.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui 10 he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ awo mama ni mli efɔ mli. gbii fioo komɛi Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ babaoo kwɛ̃ Dumɔwu lɛ baahi shi lolo ni ebaaná hewalɛ. Kɛji eyɛ bɔdɔɔ loo egbo lolo Dumɔwu lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ baagbo ni edaŋ.

english: Why do some of my vegetable seeds take several weeks to sprout after I sow them in the dry dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ heɔ otsii babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds go into a resting state called dormancy when conditions are dry. They hold their life inside until they absorb enough continuous moisture and heat to trigger sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui boteɔ shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy mli kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli egbi. Amɛmɔɔ wala yɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛheɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ dɔlɛ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii ahe hewalɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant seeds taken from food produce brought in from outside West Africa?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ niyenii ni akɛjɛ Afrika Anaigbɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ mli?

english: It is risky because imported produce seeds may carry foreign pests or diseases dormant inside them, and they may not be adapted to Ghana's rainfall patterns and soil conditions.
ga: Oshara yɛ ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni akɛbaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahi maŋsɛɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai amli. ni ekolɛ enyɛŋ ekɛ ehe awo Ghana nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ mli.

english: Why does my harvested yam start sprouting green shoots in the barn even when it is not in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living storehouses of food. After resting for a period post-harvest, the living tissue inside senses temperature changes and naturally uses its stored energy to sprout new growth for the next season.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii ji niyenii atoohe ni hiɛ ka. Beni ajɔɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, fãji ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nuɔ tsakemɔi ahe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei heei kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: How do worms get inside my pepper fruits when there are no visible holes on the outside skin?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii boteɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ amli? Be mli ni bu ni anaaa bɛ hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Parent insects lay tiny eggs on the flower or very young fruit. As soon as the egg hatches, the tiny worm enters while the fruit skin is soft, and the fruit grows around the small entry point, hiding the pest inside.
ga: Kplukai ni ji nyɛ lɛ woɔ wɔji bibii. Yɛ fɔfɔi loo aduawai bibii waa anɔ Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fɔ pɛ kɛkɛ ni ŋmeii bibii baashɛ shi yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ ahewolo lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo lolo lɛ. Ni aduawai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ shinaa bibioo lɛ he, ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ teeɔ.

english: Why do cassava leaves shed and turn yellow during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop older leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to reduce water loss through evaporation, keeping the root tubers alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ baai momoi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛba nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Ha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants do not tolerate full, direct sunlight because their leaves lose moisture faster than roots can draw it. They need partial shade from food crops like plantains to survive their early growth stage.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ shishijee dalɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning purple?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ purple lɛ?

english: Purple leaves usually mean the soil lacks phosphorus, a nutrient essential for strong roots and crop growth. Adding phosphorus-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha shishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why should I avoid burning bush leftovers on my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsei bibii ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashãmɔ he dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable nutrients and beneficial soil insects. Leaving crop remains to decompose naturally builds rich organic matter, keeps the soil moist, and protects it from drying out.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ sũ mli kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans together with my maize make the soil richer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and peas trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they release this free nitrogen into the soil, which feeds your maize plants naturally.
ga: Beans kɛ peas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛjieɔ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa tsei lɛ

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect themselves from dehydration. Planting permanent shade trees helps maintain soil moisture and protects the cocoa leaves from intense heat.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ he. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay thin and small even when the plants grow tall and leafy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ be mli ni yucca tso lɛ da ni eyɛ baai po lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are grown too close together, they compete for sunlight and soil nutrients. This causes the plant to put all its energy into growing tall stems and foliage instead of developing large tuber roots.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni kɛlɛ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee shishifãi wuji.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme dry heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining steady soil moisture during hot weather helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni mli egbi lɛ miihao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ shi.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and small dirt-like powder inside the growing center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ nibii bibii ni tamɔ muji lɛ? Yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the leaves. Early detection and applying appropriate pesticides or neem-based spray directly into the whorl can control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni abaanyɛ akudɔ tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem ni akɛshwieɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does letting weeds grow in my farm for just two weeks hurt my final yield so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli otsii enyɔ pɛ lɛ yeɔ mi naagbee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui waa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than main crops and steal water, light, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need during their critical initial growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ mra be mli dalɛ bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds when the rains start coming late?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi ebaa sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Wait until the soil receives steady rainfall for two to three consecutive days so there is enough moisture underground to sprout the seed and sustain early root growth.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni fa bɔ ni sa aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni eha shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on dry soil during a hot, sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Chemical fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so plants can absorb it. Applying it on dry soil under strong heat causes it to burn plant roots and evaporate into the air.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛtsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ la ni naa wa shishi lɛ, ebaashã tsei ashishifãi ni ebaatsɔ la kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how can it help protect my vegetable crops from extreme weather?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mitsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa waa lɛ ahe?

english: A greenhouse is a covered structure made of transparent plastic or glass that creates a controlled environment for your crops. It protects sensitive vegetables like tomatoes and peppers from harsh sunlight, heavy rainfall, and pests, allowing plants to grow stronger and produce food year-round.
ga: Greenhouse ji tsũ ko ni akɛ plastic loo glase ni mli tse fee ni haa shihilɛ ni akudɔɔ kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Ebuɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ niyenii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do crops grown inside a greenhouse tend to grow faster than those planted in my open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ greenhouse mli lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Inside a greenhouse, heat, air, and moisture stay steady, and crops are protected from sudden weather changes and heavy wind. Because the plants use less energy coping with harsh outdoor conditions and pests, they can direct all their energy into growing foliage and producing fruit much quicker.
ga: Yɛ greenhouse lɛ mli lɛ, ahãa dɔlɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi daa. Ni abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkpee kponɔgbɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa. No hewɔ lɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ awo baai ni miida lɛ amli ni amɛwo yibii oya kwraa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. When nitrogen is short in the soil, the plant moves what little it has from its older bottom leaves up to the new leaves at the top to keep growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl and droop in peak heat as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and save water. If the leaves bounce back in the evening when temperatures cool down, the plant is simply protecting itself; if they remain curled, the soil needs water.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe ni egbee shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni akɛ nu akafite. Kɛji baai lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibu ehe. Kɛji okɛ ohe ebɔ he lolo Etsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable crops early in the morning or during the middle of the day?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo gbi mli?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the cool soil absorbs water deeply before the sun heats up. Watering in the middle of the day causes water to evaporate rapidly before reaching the roots and can stress the plants.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani hulu lɛ haa edɔɔ lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ gbi mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ aná haomɔ.

english: How do I stop heat from building up too much inside a plastic greenhouse during the sunniest months?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine ni baa mi plastic greenhouse lɛ mli lɛ naa yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli?

english: You can control heat inside a greenhouse by opening side vents to allow air to flow through, using netting on top to block intense rays, and keeping the ground damp so evaporating water cools the air naturally.
ga: Obaanyɛ okudɔ dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ o-greenhouse lɛ mli lɛ kɛtsɔ sɛɛgbɛ ŋmeii ni ooogbele koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ mesh nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛtsi la ni naa wa waa lɛ naa. ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with small fruit when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots fight for water and nutrients in the soil while their leaves fight for sunlight. Proper spacing gives each plant enough light and food to grow strong stems and full-sized fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ aduawai ni fa babaoo.

english: Why should I avoid planting tomatoes in the exact same soil where I harvested tomatoes last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tomato dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa mi tomato lɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly in the same spot allows soil-borne pests and fungal diseases that target that specific crop to build up in the ground. Rotating with a different crop type, like beans or corn, breaks the disease cycle and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Nakai nɔŋŋ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsɔɔ nakai tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni aaatsake ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Enɛ haa helai baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers, but the flowers fall off before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ woɔ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. Extremely high temperatures dry out the pollen so seeds cannot form, causing the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ekɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa pollen lɛ gĩɔ. No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui efeee. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the bottoms of my growing garden egg fruits turning dark and rotting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii aduawai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi miifee duŋ ni amɛmiifite lɛ?

english: Dark, rotting spots on the blossom end of fruits are caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit while it develops. This usually happens when soil moisture fluctuates, as roots need steady water to absorb calcium properly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ baa ji calcium ni shɛɛɛ aduawai lɛ ahe beni edara lɛ ni faaa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ he miihia nu ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava cuttings when planting them in the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava niji lɛ ato he ko beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings should ideally be planted about 1 meter apart. Leaving this distance ensures each plant receives enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to grow large tubers without competing with nearby plants.
ga: Esa akɛ adu tsei ni afo lɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ he nɛɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: How many months does it usually take for improved cassava varieties to be ready for harvest?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei ni akwɛɔ lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Improved cassava varieties in Ghana typically mature between 9 and 12 months after planting. Harvesting at this time ensures maximum yield before the tubers start turning woody or rotting in the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaha yibii babaoo aba dani ŋmeii lɛ aje shishi amɛtsɔ tso loo amɛgbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a major food for crops. When nutrients are low in the soil, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has to the new top leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa ŋmãa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Beni niyenii mli nibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off the tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often fall off when the tree is stressed by prolonged dry weather, lacks sufficient soil nutrients, or has not been pollinated by beneficial insects like tiny midges. Keeping proper shade and soil moisture helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ hao tso lɛ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ midges lɛ ehiɛɛɛ amɛhe. Shade ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow and dropping even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po lɛ?

english: Yellow, dropping leaves on wet soil usually mean the pepper plants are receiving too much water. Overwatering drowns the plant roots by cutting off the air they need to breathe, causing them to rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ pepper tso lɛ miiná nu babaoo tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli fe nine lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbo kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛmu lɛ ni ebaafo mli lɛ nɔ. ha egbo

english: What causes black spots on the bottom of my tomatoes before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ?

english: Black spots at the bottom of tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which occurs when plants cannot get enough calcium or experience irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture consistent helps the plant absorb the calcium it needs.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Young crop plants have small, delicate roots that easily lose the fight against fast-growing weeds for soil food, water, and sunlight. Weeding early ensures your main crop gets all the nutrients to establish strong growth.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni kɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ wuuu oya koni amɛná niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda waa.

english: Can I plant cowpea and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting maize and cowpea together is a beneficial practice called intercropping. Cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow healthier while protecting the soil from drying out.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ ji nifeemɔ ko ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni ale lɛ akɛ intercropping. Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi.

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing fresh air and sunlight to pass through the tree canopy. This extra airflow lowers humidity around the tree, preventing black pod disease and encouraging more fruit to grow.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la atsɔ tsei lɛ ashishi. Nɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa hiɛ nɛɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa black pod hela lɛ baaa. ni eye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛdara babaoo

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops turn yellow and die when rainwater collects on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When excess water sits on the land without draining away, it drowns the roots, preventing them from taking up plant food and turning the leaves yellow.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efooo Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ niyenii ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does digging deep drainage gutters around my farm protect my crops during heavy rains?
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli ni mli kwɔ ni miifo kɛbɔle Te miŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Deep drainage gutters give excess rainwater a clear pathway to flow off your farm so that water does not settle around your crops and rot their root systems.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsɔɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni nu akabɔle ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ni eha shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when I plant them in low-lying swampy land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store food and require well-drained soil. When planted in lowlands where water constantly settles, the roots absorb too much water, rot, and spoil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi toɔ niyenii ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu damɔ shi be fɛɛ be lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo, amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Will using heavy machinery to dig large channels through our flooded farmland help our crops grow better?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni tsii ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛfo ŋshɔkei wuji kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi shikpɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni wɔŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, heavy machinery can dig wide and deep channels that lower the water level across a large area, allowing overly wet soil to dry out enough for crop roots to breathe and thrive.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni tsii baanyɛ atsa gbɛjegbɛi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni mli kwɔ koni nu lɛ aba shi yɛ hei wuji anɔ. Gbimɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ fe nine bɔ ni sa koni tso shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my crops wilt and drop their flowers when the rains stop coming for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Water carries nutrients from the soil up into the crop. Without enough rain or watering, the plant conserves its remaining strength by dropping flowers and wilting to protect itself from drying out completely.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ buɔ ehewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni ejieɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛbuɔ ehe koni ekagbi kwraa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does the water in the small pit I dug by hand dry up so fast when the weather is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni yɔɔ nubu bibioo lɛ mli Mɛi ni mikɛ mi nine tsu lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shallow pits only collect water near the surface, which evaporates quickly under direct sunlight or sinks into deeper soil levels. Digging deeper holes or shading the water source helps keep the water available longer for your crops.
ga: Nubui ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ buaa nu naa yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ pɛ. Enɛ baatsɔ la oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi loo ebaagbee shi kɛya shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ nɔ. Bu ni mli kwɔ loo nu jɛɛhe ko ni oooha lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni onáa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: If the rain fails, is it better to water my crops deeply once a week or a little bit every day?
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu shikome yɛ otsi mli loo fioo daa gbi?

english: Giving crops a deep watering less frequently encourages roots to grow deep into the soil to seek moisture, making them stronger than daily light watering which keeps roots weak near the surface.
ga: Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu ni mli kwɔ ni afɔɔɔɔ lɛ, ebaawo shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛyatao ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli waa fe nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa gbi, ni no haa shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why does rainwater sit on top of my soil instead of sinking down to where my crop roots are?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo kɛyashɛ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When soil becomes hard and compacted, water cannot easily soak through it. This causes water to settle on the surface instead of traveling down to the root zone where your crops can drink it.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ Nu nyɛŋ abote mli mlɛo. Enɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeshɛ shishi kɛya shishigbɛ he ni onibii lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetables dry out so quickly even after a brief, light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A brief rain only wets the top layer of soil, which evaporates under the hot sun before the crop's roots lower in the ground can draw water from it.
ga: Nugbɔ nɛ be kukuoo ko. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛ. ni baaho yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ. Dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu lɛ,.

english: Why do crops planted near riverbeds stay green longer in the dry season than crops planted on hills?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ faai ahe lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe tsei ni adu yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Lowland areas near water channels have a high underground water table where water settles close to the surface, allowing deep roots to keep drinking even when there is no rainfall.
ga: Hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni fa babaoo yɛ he ni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ nuɔ nu kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants keep wilting and turning brown when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot withstand full, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a living canopy that protects the young trees from harsh heat and retains soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ kwraa. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems too close to my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ tsɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete for the same water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures both the cassava and maize get sufficient room to spread their roots and produce high yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fɛɛ he lɛ haa amɛnáa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the central vein of older leaves usually indicates that the soil lacks nitrogen. Adding compost, animal manure, or a balanced fertilizer will restore healthy leaf growth and lead to larger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ. ni ofee ŋmeii wuji

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and misshapen instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛja lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, deep, and loose soil mounds to expand. If the ground is hard or compact, the growing tuber struggles to push through the dirt, causing it to become stunted or distorted.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni shwieɔ shi koni egbɛ eshwa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ Bulbs ni miida lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo etsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me not to plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes the same specific nutrients from the soil year after year. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores natural nitrogen to the soil and disrupts pest life cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. ni efoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ mli

english: What causes ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha ŋmeii ba mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: This leaf damage is commonly caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central funnel of the plant during the day and come out at night to eat the tender leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ koni amɛbaye tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii.

english: Twisted leaves with yellow patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the most reliable way to prevent this.
ga: Baai ni etsilɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ Adumɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ji gbɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their blossoms before growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ fɔfɔi dani midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot dry spells helps the blossoms stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛbote la ni naa wa mli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why should I trim off some of the lower branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ekomɛi kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Trimming extra lower branches redirects the plant's energy away from unnecessary foliage and straight into producing larger, healthier fruits while improving airflow to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afolɔ babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe. ni eyaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow even when I plant right after the first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ moŋ?

english: The first rain of the year is often followed by a long dry spell that bakes the topsoil. Waiting until the rainy season fully sets in ensures young seedlings have enough continuous water to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli shãa lɛ sɛɛ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi kwraa koni dumɔwui bibii lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛhi shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when there are no big trees nearby to cover them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji komɛi bɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni baaha amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight causes intense heat stress and burns their delicate leaves. Retaining shade trees keeps the temperature lower, preserves soil moisture, and protects the young plants until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
