ga: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive because direct sunlight causes severe heat stress and burns the delicate leaves. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi. Maintain soil moisture and protect young plants until they are big enough to receive full sunlight.

english: Yellowing of the lower leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires a lot of nitrogen to grow, and when the soil lacks enough of it, the plant moves available nitrogen from the older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. and when the soil lacks enough Plants move available nitrogen away from old lower leaves to feed new growth above.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground before they are ready for me to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ makpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water for long periods, starving the roots of oxygen. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: What causes small green worms to eat holes right in the middle of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that lays eggs on corn leaves. The caterpillars crawl into the central leaves (the whorl) to feed on the tender growing point, which can destroy the stalk if not managed early.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa baa nɔ lɛ. Kplukai lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ (whorl) koni amɛye he ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ akpata tso lɛ shishi kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and soft before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo dani eshɛ po lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot and is caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit. It usually happens when watering is inconsistent, making it difficult for the plant roots to continuously take up calcium from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaya nɔ amɛjie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. Planting them after heavy-feeding crops like maize restores vital nutrients back into the soil naturally for the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ, baaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: During intense afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it up from the ground. Curling and drooping is a natural defense mechanism to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun and slow down water loss.
ga: Yɛ shwane hulu la mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Curling kɛ drooping ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛi ni haa hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants produce vines that need to spread their leaves high up toward sunlight to feed the growing tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to sun while keeping them off damp ground where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato tsei woɔ wain tsei ni esa akɛ amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi kɛya hulu la lɛ he koni amɛye amɛbua bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa amɛyaaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ hu.

english: Allowing too many shoots to grow around one plantain stem creates competition for food, water, and sunlight. Removing excess suckers ensures that all nutrients go into producing one large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Plantain kome pɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he, ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ana nɔmimaa akɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ baaha aduawai agbo kome pɛ ni tsii aba.

english: Why should I spread dry leaves or cut grass on the soil surface around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔ baai ni egboi anɔ loo mafo sũ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with organic material (mulching) prevents the sun from drying out the ground, keeps root zones cool, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly breaks down into rich food for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, ebaatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ jwɛi ni shwieɔ nɔ lɛ naa ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate intense direct sunlight because their root systems are tender and lose moisture rapidly. Planting shade trees or intercropping with plantains creates a protective canopy that reduces heat stress and maintains soil moisture while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ ahewɔ, ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni aduɔ loo ni akɛ dumɔwui woɔ mli lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa hulutsoo he haomɔ baa shi lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Which part of a cassava stem should I cut for planting to ensure it grows strong roots?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ afo kɛha dumɔ koni shishifãi lɛ awa?

english: Use the middle, mature part of a healthy cassava stem that is about 8 to 12 months old. Avoid the woody base, which is too dry, and the green top, which rots easily, because the middle section has the right balance of stored energy and active buds to sprout quickly.
ga: Kɛ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ fã ni eda lɛ atsu nii. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi ni egbi tsɔ lɛ he. kɛ ŋmeii ni eŋɔli ni fiteɔ oya Enɛ ji akɛ, fã ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni ato kɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ nii ni haa ekwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the ears are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani toi lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the tips of lower leaves usually means nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is a key nutrient for green leafy growth, so when the plant runs short, it moves available nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed the newer growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ tsei fioo pɛ eshwɛ lɛ Ejieɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei heei ni eda yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil better for maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas partner with natural soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When these plants die and decompose, they leave this natural fertilizer in the soil, boosting fertility for subsequent heavy feeders like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ sũ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ feɔ ekome yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛfiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ gboi ni amɛfite lɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni kooloi ni yeɔ niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ afɔmɔ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I tell if the ground has enough moisture to plant my corn seeds after the early rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the rain soaks at least 15 centimeters (about the depth of a hand-span) deep into the soil. Planting after just a light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up if a hot spell follows before the roots reach deeper water.
ga: Wait until the rain has penetrated at least 15 centimeters deep into the soil (about the depth of the palm of your hand). Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. It can cause seeds to germinate and dry out if intense heat is applied before the roots reach deep water.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting up wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maŋɔ be kɛto tsei ahe gbɛjianɔ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves to capture sunlight for photosynthesis, which creates the energy needed to build big underground tubers. If vines lay on the hot ground, leaves get shaded by each other, stay humid, and become prone to fungal diseases like anthracnose.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la kɛha fotosintɛsis. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ akɛ wain tso lɛ fɔ he ko ni mli edɔ lɛ, baai lɛ baaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ oshara mli kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep dropping off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ tomato?

english: Flower drop in tomatoes usually happens when air temperatures get extremely high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination inside the blossom, causing the plant to shed the unfertilized flowers to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa. Ha tsei ajie fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: What is causing ragged holes in the central whorl leaves of my young corn and leaving sawdust-like dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni miiha buji miigba yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛmiishi muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the growing funnel of the corn plant during the day to feed on young leaves. Early detection is key, as spraying biological or mild chemical controls into the funnel before the pest burrows too deep protects the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Abuɔ mra be mli ni ana lɛ akɛ nɔ titri ni he hiaa Enɛ ji akɛ, kɛ́ afɔ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ko ni haa mɔ he waaa lɛ awo ŋmeii lɛ amli dani afu ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ he ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and pale even if there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛshwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that aggressively steal water, soil nutrients, and light away from your crops. Even with good rain, crops suffer from nutrient starvation because the weeds absorb most of the soil's nourishment first.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ni okɛ la awo onibii amli oya bɔni afee ni kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ baaná he sɛɛ lolo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ ji mɛi ni shwieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: When is the safest time to place fertilizer around my crops so the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni nugbɔ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not during heavy downpours or on flooded ground. Placing fertilizer in small ring holes buried slightly under the soil near the plant's root zone keeps rain from washing it away and puts the nutrients right where the roots can absorb them.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ring bu bibii amli Afuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi fioo yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni nugbɔ lɛ akaho. ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ hiɔ he ko ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: I want to start farming this season, how do I know which crop will give me a good harvest on my land?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi okwaayeli yɛ be nɛɛ mli. Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni baawo yibii kpakpai yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Checking your soil type, understanding local rainfall patterns, and choosing seeds that match your region's climate ensure your crops get the right environment to grow well and avoid failure.
ga: Shikpɔŋ henɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shishinumɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ halamɔ. Ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná shihilɛ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ shigbeemɔ he.

english: Why do crops grow very well on my neighbor's farm but perform poorly on my field right next door?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli shi ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ mishia lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops respond to small differences in soil depth, underground water drainage, shade from nearby trees, and how deeply the soil was plowed before planting.
ga: Tsei tsuɔ srɔtofeemɔi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ mli lɛ ahe nii. shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni hoɔ Shade ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli Ni te obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ oha tɛŋŋ dani odu?

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the crop lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that too much standing water around the roots is suffocating the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo nu yɛ lolo ni ebɔle he Shishifãi babaoo tsɔ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Tomato plants often shed their flowers when temperatures get too high, when the air is extremely dry, or when the plant is not receiving consistent water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu daa

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small and thin even though the branches and leaves on top look big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ waa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ aniji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or foliage growth is overstimulated, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves instead of storing starch in its underground roots.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo ebaa lɛ shweremɔ fe nine lɛ, ekanyaa. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ebaai lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛnáa hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Hot sun makes leaves lose water faster than roots can absorb it from the soil, causing temporary afternoon wilting as the plant tries to save moisture until the cooler evening.
ga: Hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haa baa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko yɛ shwane mli beni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ.

english: How do I stop insects and birds from destroying my seeds immediately after I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi anaa koni amɛkafite dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ?

english: Planting seeds at the correct recommended depth and using approved seed treatments or light mulch coverings protect the seeds until they sprout safely above ground.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ Ni akɛ dumɔwui ahe tsofafeemɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaakwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested grains mold and spoil quickly after I store them inside my house?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfiteɔ oya beni mikɛto shĩa mli lɛ?

english: Grains trap moisture inside; if they are not dried thoroughly under the sun until the moisture level drops low enough, mold and insects will thrive inside the storage bags.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa toɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli. Kɛji hulu lɛ egbiko kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi bɔ ni sa. Mold kɛ kooloi bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ amli.

english: How can I prevent my harvested vegetables from spoiling quickly while waiting for buyers at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ anaa koni ekafite oya be mli ni mimɛɔ mɛi ni baahe nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting crops during the cool early morning hours and storing them in well-ventilated, shaded crates helps keep them fresh and prevents heat buildup that speeds up decay.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ leebi maŋkpa ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli ni akɛto adekai ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaatsi dɔlɛ ni buaa amɛhe naa ni haa amɛfiteɔ oya lɛ naa.

english: Why do crop prices drop so low when everybody harvests at the same time, and what can I do to protect my income?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara baa shi nɛkɛ be mli ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kome mli lɛ? Ni mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mikɛbu shika ni mináa lɛ he?

english: When the market is flooded with crops at peak harvest, prices fall due to high supply; staggering your planting dates or processing fresh crops into dried forms allows you to sell later when prices rise.
ga: Beni jara lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ Jara hu ba shi yɛ nibii ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ gbi ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ toɔ he loo okɛ nibii heei ni adu lɛ tsuɔ nii koni egbi lɛ, no haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ amɛ sɛɛ mli kɛ́ amɛjara wa.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant plantain trees next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing essential shade and trapping soil moisture to help the young cocoa survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi koni eye ebua kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet and humid weather. You can protect your trees by pruning extra branches to let sunlight and air in, and by removing infected pods immediately so the disease does not spread.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Obaanyɛ obu tso lɛ he kɛtsɔ niji krokomɛi ni ooofo koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build healthy green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted animal manure will help them turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my maize plants roll up their leaves like tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural defense against heat. By curling its leaves, the maize plant reduces the amount of surface exposed to the burning sun, helping it conserve water inside its stem until the air cools down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Abɛi haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ tsɔne lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why are my cassava roots so small and woody even though the plant grew very tall with plenty of leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei lɛ? Nakai sweet potato tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo?

english: When cassava gets too much shade or too much nitrogen from soil, it spends all its energy building stems and leafy leaves instead of growing tubers downstairs. Plant cassava in full sunlight and avoid high-nitrogen fertilizers to get large, soft roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ naa hulutsoo babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ebaakɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai kɛ baai amli moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Dumɔ ŋmei yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo he koni onine ashɛ shishifãi wuji ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɔ.

english: How can I tell that my white yam is fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potatoes yɛŋ lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam is ready for harvesting when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up at the end of the rainy season. This shows that the plant has finished moving all its food and energy from the leaves down into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ejie eniyenii kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ baai lɛ amli kɛtee ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upwards and stop the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus transmitted by these insects. You can control them by spraying soapy water mixed with neem oil or using a recommended insecticide early in the morning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ Obaanyɛ okudɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛ saamɔ ni akɛ neem fɔ efutu mli lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ ni oookɛtsu nii leebi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young corn plants, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a pest that nests inside the central funnel of young corn. You can manage them by dropping a small pinch of clean dry sand or wood ash directly into the center of each plant funnel to destroy the worm.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni feɔ amɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii abifao lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋã ni egbi loo tso sũ ni mli tse bibioo ko atsu amɛhe nii. Okɛwo tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting a crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but groundnuts and cowpeas put nutrients back in. These legume plants have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and enrich the soil naturally for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no beneficial insects around to pollinate them. Keeping the soil moist around the roots with mulch helps protect the flowers so fruit can grow.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsu shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ he nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni aduawai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in a open field without bigger trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong direct sunlight and harsh winds. Planting shade crops like plantain or keeping selected tall trees creates a cool microclimate that protects young cocoa roots and leaves while they establish.
ga: Young cacao trees cannot tolerate strong sunlight and strong winds. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ loo tsei kakadaji ni ahala lɛ akwɛmɔ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni buɔ kookoo shishifãi bibii kɛ baai ahe be mli ni aduɔ lɛ baa.

english: Can I plant cassava on the same plot with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: It is not recommended because cassava grows very aggressively and consumes massive amounts of soil water and nutrients, which leaves your young cocoa trees stunted and weak.
ga: Akɛ enɛ haaa ejaakɛ ŋmei daa oya ni eyeɔ shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa o-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn completely black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet conditions. Excessive moisture and lack of sunlight on the farm help the fungus spread rapidly from pod to pod.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ hulu la ni bɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why are the branches of my cocoa trees swelling up and the leaves turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo niji lɛ efu ni baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is a key symptom of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is spread by small insects called mealybugs. The virus attacks the plant's food transport system, leading to decline and eventual tree death.
ga: Enɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi titri ko. Virus tutuaa tsei aniyenii gbɛjianɔtoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ fiteɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: What are these small bugs making dark patches on my green cocoa pods and young shoots?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ni kɛ okadii diji ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji kɛ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: Those insects are likely mirids (capsids). They bite into the tree tissue to suck sap and inject poison that kills the plant tissues, leading to reduced yield and dead twigs.
ga: Ekolɛ kooloi bibii lɛ ji mirids (capsids). Amɛkɔɔ tso mli fãji koni amɛmu nu lɛ ni amɛkɛ tsofa fɔŋ ni fiteɔ tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ woɔ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei niji gboiɔ.

english: Why do many flowers appear on my cocoa tree but most fall off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii babaoo jeɔ kpo yɛ mikoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce more flowers than they can support, but excessive flower drop happens when the tree lacks nutrients, experiences water stress, or lacks insects like midges for proper pollination.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Shi fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nu mli haomɔ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ midges ni bɛ kɛha pollination ni sa

english: During Harmattan, dry air and low soil moisture force cocoa trees to shed leaves to conserve water, which temporarily stops new pod formation and slows down growth.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fioo lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Enɛ haa pod heei ni afeɔ lɛ kpaɔ be kukuoo ko ni ehaa edalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to prune and cut excess branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni mafolɔ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning allows sunlight and air to move freely through the farm, which dries up dampness that causes fungal diseases and encourages the tree to produce more flowers and pods.
ga: Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa lɛ agbi. ni ekanyaa tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo

english: Why should I remove those green leafy plants growing directly on my cocoa tree branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei eŋɔli fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo niji anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Those plants are mistletoes, which are parasites that sink roots into your cocoa tree to steal water and food, slowly weakening your cocoa trees and reducing pod output.
ga: Nakai tsei lɛ ji mistletoe. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ cacao tso lɛ mli koni eju nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa kokoo tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ fiofio. ni ekɛ pod yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi

english: Why do weeds lower my crop harvest even if I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will steal the applied fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your crop roots get a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. ni ebaaju ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni akɛfata he dani tsei shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or when the ground is too waterlogged, preventing the roots from taking up nutrients effectively.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often the plant's natural way to protect itself from losing water under intense heat, though it can also be a sign of a viral infection spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni abɔleɔ he lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni elaajeɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi lɛ he. Eyɛ mli akɛ enɛ baanyɛ afee hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi moŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in overly shaded, wet, and cool conditions when air cannot flow through the farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ, hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow much better when I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the farm before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, leaving rich natural fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does fertilizer burn my crops if I drop it directly against the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shãa miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji mikɛshwie tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts that suck water out of plant roots and stems if touched directly, so it must be placed a short distance away in the soil.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baajie nu kɛjɛ tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli kɛji amɛkɛ amɛhe kpe tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ fioo.

english: Too many shoots fight with the main tree for soil food and water; removing extra shoots leaves more energy for the main plantain to produce a bigger, heavier bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ tso ni da ni tsii.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food; climbing up a stake exposes the leaves to sunlight, which builds large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Tso lɛ nɔ kwɔɔ haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and weak with small yields when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they stretch tall to fight each other for sunlight while competing underneath for limited water and soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛmiitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni fa fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when water sits on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni nu ehi miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns the roots by blocking oxygen, which causes soil fungi and bacteria to quickly decay the tubers before harvest.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ oya dani akpaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without producing any fruit during heavy heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ewooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High temperatures stress the plant, causing it to drop flowers as a survival trick to save water and energy until weather conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need plantains planted right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu dumɔwu yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under strong sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large, broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants, keeping the soil cool and moist so the seedlings can survive their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut down some of the small suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: If too many suckers grow around one stem, they all compete for the same food, water, and sunlight in the soil. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two healthy ones, ensuring the main plant gets enough nourishment to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ tso kome he. Amɛ fɛɛ amɛshiɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kome ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over so easily when heavy winds blow or when the fruit bunch gets big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa loo kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; their roots spread out near the surface of the soil. When the fruit bunch grows heavy or strong winds blow, the shallow root system cannot support the top weight, which is why farmers use wooden props or bamboo poles to support the plants.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ gbɛ eshwa he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji akɛ aduawai akui lɛ miitsu nii waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ miitswa waa lɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ tsɔne ni tsii fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ okwaafoi kɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tsei lɛ ahe loo ŋmei tsei tsuɔ nii kɛfiɔ tsei lɛ asɛɛ.

english: How can I tell when my green plantains are mature enough to harvest for the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-plantains eŋɔli lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa kɛha jara?

english: As plantains grow, their sharp, flat sides gradually become rounded and plump. When the ridges on the skin become smooth and the top leaf turns yellow, the plantain bunch is fully grown and ready to be cut down even while still green.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ dara Efãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ fiofio Efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Beni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Plantain tsei lɛ akui lɛ edara kwraa ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaafolɔ amɛ be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔji lolo po.

english: What causes my plantain leaves to turn yellow and dry up before the fruit bunch has mature fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani aduawai akui lɛ shwereɔ?

english: Early leaf yellowing is often caused by leaf spot diseases or root damage from microscopic worms called nematodes. These diseases stop the plant from carrying water and nutrients from the soil up to the leaves and fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ mra ji baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ loo shishifãi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Helai nɛɛ haaa tsei lɛ anyɛ ajie nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashɛ baai kɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why am I finding small holes and dark rotted spots at the bottom stem of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Ni ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: This damage is usually caused by plantain stem weevils (borers). The adult beetles lay eggs inside the stem base, and the larvae hatch and eat tunnels through the plant stem, weakening it and causing it to rot or snap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei ni ji plantain ŋmei (borer) lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Plantain ŋmeii ni eda lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Ni ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ekpɔtɔɔ loo ekuɔ.

english: Why is it beneficial to leave dry leaves and plant cut-offs around the roots of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ahe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Covering the ground with organic material (mulching) blocks hot sunlight from drying out the soil, keeps moisture around the roots, stops weeds from growing, and slowly breaks down into free fertilizer for the crops.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my crops produce big harvests in the first year but yield smaller fruits after two or three years on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli shi ewoɔ yibii fioo yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the soil every time they grow and yield fruit. If manure or fertilizer is not added back to the farm, the soil loses its strength over time, resulting in smaller harvests.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaadara ni amɛwo yibii. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, okɛku sɛɛ kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Why do plantain leaves droop down and split during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbalaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains store a lot of water in their soft stems. When rainfall stops during the dry season, the plant folds or splits its leaves to reduce water loss through evaporation and protect itself from excessive heat.
ga: Plantains toɔ nu babaoo yɛ amɛ tsei bibii lɛ amli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe loo amɛjaraa amɛbaai lɛ amli koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. ni obu ohe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he

english: Why is it bad to plant my plantain suckers very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting suckers too close together forces the plants to fight for sunlight, causing them to grow tall and thin with weak stems. Proper spacing allows sunlight to reach all leaves and ensures each plant gets enough soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ ahe ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How far apart should I plant my plantain suckers so they don't choke each other?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu plantain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkatsi mi?

english: Plantain plants need about 2 to 3 meters of space between each other. Giving them enough space ensures their wide leaves get enough sunlight and their roots do not fight for nutrients in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ahe miihia ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai 2 kɛyashi 3. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akaŋ.

english: What happens if I plant cassava and plantains together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmei kɛ plantain fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Intercropping plantains with cassava works well because cassava grows lower while plantains grow tall. However, you must space them properly so the cassava roots do not steal all the soil food before the plantains establish.
ga: Kɛ akɛ ŋmei woɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmei lɛ daa shi yɛ be mli ni plantains lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ amɛ abɔ he jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ akaju shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii fɛɛ dani ŋmei tsei lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo.

english: Why do my crops grow green and fast at first, but then slow down when flowering starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Shi ebaa shi kɛji ebɔi fɔfɔii lɛ pɛ?

english: Flowering and fruiting require a lot of extra energy and nutrients like potassium from the soil. If the soil lacks these nutrients, the crop slows down during this high-energy stage.
ga: Fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo biɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛ niyenii krokomɛi, tamɔ potassium ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ Dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ be mli ni hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm has enough food for my plantain crops to give big bunches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha mi-plantains lɛ akwɛ jwɛi wuji?

english: Good soil for plantains is dark, rich in organic matter (mulch), and drains water easily without staying waterlogged. If leaves turn pale yellow early, the soil usually lacks key nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha plantains ji shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ. Eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli (mulch) babaoo ni nu hoɔ oya ni nu bɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young plantain plants turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Lower leaves turning yellow is often a sign of nutrient deficiency, natural aging of older leaves, or water stress when the soil is either too dry or completely waterlogged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa. Baai momoi lɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ loo nu he haomɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ kwraa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain stems look weak and bend easily after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛkuɔ amɛhe oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive water in the soil can rot plantain roots and soften the stem structure. Without strong root support in wet soil, the heavy plant struggles to hold itself up.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha plantain shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee mlɛo. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa ni fiɔ esɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ bɛ lɛ, Tsei ni tsii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye amɛbua amɛhe.

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Strong winds can easily blow them down unless you prop them up with sturdy wooden poles.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. kɛ muji babaoo baa Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ amɛ shi oya ja okɛ tsei ni wa fi amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my young plantain plants regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ehe miihia ni madu mi-plantains bibii lɛ daa.

english: Weeds steal sunlight, soil water, and fertilizer directly from the plantain's shallow roots, which prevents young plants from growing strong stems.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ plantain lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ, ni no haaa tso bibioo lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why are there small holes and dark brown lines inside the stems of my plantain crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Those tunnels are caused by plantain stem borers or root weevils. Their larvae eat through the inner stem, weakening the crop and reducing fruit size.
ga: Plantain tso lɛ shishi ŋmeii loo shishifãi amli ŋmeii kɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ baa. Amɛ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa aduawai lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: How does the dry harmattan season affect the way my plantains grow compared to the rainy season?
ga: Te Harmattan be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ saa dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ he?

english: During the dry season, plantains slow down their growth and may shed leaves to save water. Supplying mulch around the base helps retain soil moisture until the rains return.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Plantains lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Mulch ni bɔleɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ yaa nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants keep dying when I clear all the big shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade from larger trees or plantains because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaf tissues and dries up the soil moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baa lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa sũ mli nu ni he hiaa koni amɛhi shi lɛ agbi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, a vital nutrient maize needs in large amounts to grow healthy green leaves and big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmãa, ni ehe hiaa niyenii babaoo koni enyɛ ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ ŋmãa wuji.

english: Why does my farm soil get hard like rock during the dry season, and how can I fix it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter; adding leaves, crop stems, or manure as mulch holds moisture in the soil and keeps it soft and easy for roots to grow through.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ baai, tsei ashishifãi, loo ŋmɔtɔ fata he akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo

english: Why do other farmers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds the maize and improves harvest yields.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa lɛ ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready to harvest if I cannot see them underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa? Kɛji onaaa tubers lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, which you can tell when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil base cracks open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ole be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ mli gbala

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows leaves to catch maximum sunlight to feed the growing tubers below, while keeping foliage off the wet ground prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛha ŋmeii ni miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, Akɛ baai lɛ aaatsi he ko ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi koni akɛtsi baai helai anaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up tightly and preventing the fruits from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛtsiɔ aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or by the plant trying to protect itself from extreme heat and dry soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tsei amli helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer heat stress, experience erratic watering, or have too much nitrogen fertilizer which pushes leaf growth over fruit growth.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛkɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kpe. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be Aloo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni haa baai lɛ daa fe aduawai lɛ.

english: Leaving too many young shoots causes them to fight with the main plant for food and water, resulting in thin trees and small, weak plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii bibii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ plantain tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why does valley rice grow well standing in flooded water while my maize rots in waterlogged soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jɔɔ mli ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu afua mli lɛ? Be mli ni mi-ŋma lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have specialized internal air tubes that transport oxygen down to their roots underwater, whereas maize roots suffocate and rot when submerged for too long.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that dry out quickly in direct sunlight. Plantain trees planted alongside cocoa provide living shade that protects the young trees from heat until they grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Plantains ni adu yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ ahe waa.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, moist conditions. Pruning excess leaves to let sunlight and fresh air flow through the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afo baai ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to grow good maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kpakpa nɔ?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, holds moisture well, and breaks apart easily in your hand. If your soil is light-colored, hard, or sandy, mixing in dry farm waste or manure helps restore its nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ su ni tsuɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni efoɔ oya kɛ́ eyɛ onine mli Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli tse, ewa, loo ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ, ŋmɔ mli jwɛi loo ŋmei ni egbi ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Maize takes away a lot of nitrogen from the soil, but legumes like groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground. Rotating these crops naturally feeds your soil for the next season.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmeii, jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Nibii nɛɛ ni oootsake lɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my crop yields change so much from one year to another even when I plant on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni miduɔ lɛ srɔtoi babaoo kɛjɛɔ afi kome mli kɛyaa afi kroko mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miida yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ.

english: Yields fluctuate because rainfall patterns and sunshine change every year. Shifts in when the rains start or stop directly affect how well your plants absorb soil nutrients during critical growth periods.
ga: Yibiiwoo lɛ tsakeɔ be mli ni nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ afi kɛyaa afi lɛ. Tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi loo ekpaa lɛ saa bɔ ni otsei lɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛdalɛ bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant my seeds very close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they struggle against each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant grows tall and yields bigger harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How do weeds hurt my vegetables if I leave them in the bed?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye mi aduawai lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ?

english: Weeds grow faster than farm crops and steal water, fertilizer, and light before your crops can use them. Removing weeds early allows your vegetables to grow without stress.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ye obua o-vegetables lɛ ni amɛdara ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Curled, yellow leaves are usually caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny white insects or infected planting stems. Using disease-resistant stems for new planting stops this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cassava mosaic hela kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kplukai bibii yɛŋ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ Tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔwui heei amli lɛ haa naagba nɛɛ kpaa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from stress caused by dry soil, high temperatures, or uneven watering. Giving your plants consistent moisture during hot periods helps flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛna haomɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni egbi, latsaa ni naa wa, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ kɛbaa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha tso lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or grow mold so quickly inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ miifite loo miifee ŋmãa oya yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize spoils when it is stored while still holding water inside the grain. Drying your corn fully on clean mats in the sun before putting it into bags prevents mold and insect damage.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ nu ni ato yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lolo lɛ to. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ ŋtayaai ni he tse nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani okɛwo kotoku lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa kɛ kooloi akafite lɛ.

english: Why are my maize crops remaining small and yellow even though I don't see any pests or insects on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ ji bibii ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ lɛ? Ni minaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai loo kooloi bibii komɛi?

english: Crops often stop growing due to a lack of proper nutrients in the soil or heavy rain washing away fertilizers. This is a growth abnormality caused by poor soil feeding rather than an illness or insect attack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei kpaɔ dalɛ yɛ niyenii ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji dalɛ he naagba ko ni shikpɔŋ ni ayeee jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛbaa. Nɔ ni fe hela loo kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ

english: Why does my cassava plant have very bushy leaves above ground but small, thin tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitsei bibii komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves instead of expanding its underground roots. This leaf-tuber imbalance is a nutritional growth behavior, not a crop disease.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi. Baai kɛ tuber asymmetry ji niyenii ni haa mɔ daa lɛ he subaŋ, shi jeee tso hela.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my plantain suckers turning brown and dying while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: As plantains grow bigger, they naturally discard their older, lower leaves to focus energy and water on expanding new top leaves. This shed of old foliage is a normal growth pattern rather than a sickness.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ Amɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛsu mli amɛshwieɔ baai ni egbɔ, ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ kɛ nu lɛ ama ŋwɛi baai heei ni miida lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ baai momoi ni shwieɔ shi nɛɛ ji nɔ ko ni yaa nɔ daa moŋ fe hela.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning purple?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ purple lɛ?

english: Purple leaves usually happen when plants cannot draw phosphorus from the soil, often because the soil is too cold, waterlogged, or compacted for young roots to work properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie fɔsfɔs kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ tsɔ, nu eyi mli obɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛŋ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato fruits developing a black, sunken rot at the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli ewo diŋ ni egboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This issue, called blossom-end rot, is not an infectious disease but a growth breakdown caused by a lack of calcium and irregular watering while the fruit is forming.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ jeee hela ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ. Shi moŋ, eji shweremɔ ni fiteɔ ni jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ mli baa lɛ.

english: Why are some crops on one side of my farm growing taller than the same crops on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa fe tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ afã kroko lɛ?

english: Variations in soil depth, nutrient concentration, shade, or water pooling across different areas of a field cause crops to grow unevenly even if planted at the exact same time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ mli tsakemɔ Niyenii ni fa babaoo, hulutsoo, loo nu ni fa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli hei srɔtoi lɛ haa tsei lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ be kome mli po.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop in the middle of the day even though I gave them water in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ gbi mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat makes leaves evaporate water faster than roots can draw it from the ground. The plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from losing moisture, which is heat stress rather than a disease.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baafite lɛ he. ni ji dɔlɛ he haomɔ fe hela.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without turning into any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high or rainfall is very irregular, pepper plants get stressed and drop their blossoms to save energy. It is an environmental reaction rather than an illness.
ga: Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee. Pepper tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Eji shihilɛ mli nifeemɔ ko moŋ fe hela ko.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa saplings curling into strange shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee naakpɛɛ nii lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds and hot sun can dry out soft, newly forming leaves faster than they can expand, causing permanent leaf distortion as they mature.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha baai bibii ni afee ehee lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ daa be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why is my okra plant growing very tall and leafy but refusing to produce any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai shi ewooo ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Okra plants often stay in a vegetative growth phase when they receive too much water or shade, delaying fruit production until environmental conditions trigger them to flower.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Roselle tsei lɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ mli beni amɛnáa nu loo hulutsoo be babaoo lɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ afeemɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛyashiɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baaha fɔfɔii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Master, why do we need to make mounds of dirt to plant yams instead of just putting them flat in the ground?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔma sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni wɔkɛdu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔkɛaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Making mounds loosens the soil so yam tubers can easily expand underground without fighting hard earth. It also helps excess water drain away so the seed yam does not rot.
ga: Gɔji ni afeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa abɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ejieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ koni sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb sticks or stakes as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei aniji loo tsei anɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for the tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and air, preventing diseases and helping the plant produce larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I tell if my village land has good soil for growing yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni abaanyɛ adu ŋmei?

english: Good yam soil is deep, soft, dark, and loose enough to drain water easily. If the soil is heavy clay or very rocky, the tubers cannot grow straight or deep.
ga: Sweet potato shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ediŋ, ni eyɛ mlɛo bɔ ni sa ni nu baanyɛ atsɔ mli oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo eyɛ tɛi babaoo Tubers lɛ hu nyɛŋ adara tɛ̃ɛ loo ebote mli.

english: Why do crops usually grow faster and greener when planted close to a riverbank?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ faa naa lɛ?

english: Soil along riverbanks is rich in nutrients washed down from surrounding land, and it holds moisture for longer periods, providing plants with a steady supply of food and water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ faai lɛ anaa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ kɛbaa shi. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ Kwɛmɔ ni tsei lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu daa.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my crops directly next to the riverbank during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu tsei yɛ faa lɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: It can be risky because heavy rains cause rivers to overflow, which can flood your farm and rot crops like yams underground. It is best to plant slightly higher up from the river's edge.
ga: Oshara baanyɛ aba ejaakɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa faa lɛ hoɔ babaoo. Enɛ baanyɛ aha oŋmɔ lɛ mli atsɔ nu ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii agboi, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ fioo kɛjɛ faa lɛ naa.

english: How will having a water works or irrigation project in our village help my crops during the dry season?
ga: Te nu nitsumɔhe loo nu shwiemɔ nitsumɔ ko ni miyɔɔ yɛ wɔ akrowa lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: An irrigation system brings water directly to your fields when rain stops, allowing you to keep growing crops like yams and vegetables all year round instead of waiting for the rainy season.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ kɛ nu baa oŋmɔji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ aduawai afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ be lɛ

english: How do I know if my yam crop is getting too much water from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛmiijɛ amɛŋmɔji amli?

english: When yams sit in too much standing water, their leaves turn yellow and the roots starve for air, causing the tubers underground to decay and rot.
ga: Kɛ nu ni ekã shi babaoo yɛ sweet potato lɛ mli lɛ Ebaai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do extension officers come to walk through our farm land before advising us on what to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ nyiɛɔ wɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli dani amɛwoɔ ŋaa yɛ nɔ ni esa akɛ adu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Officers check the soil depth, water availability, and sunlight on your specific land so they can recommend the exact crops that will yield the best harvest there.
ga: Amralo ko kwɛɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ha. nu kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ lɛ nɔ Koni onyɛ otsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni baaha yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ nakai kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the vines and leaves of my yam plants turn brown and die off when harvest time is coming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When yams mature, the plant stops growing above ground and sends all its remaining energy into the underground tuber, causing the leaves and vines to naturally dry up.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ majeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting shoots in the barn even when I haven't planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ni mikwɛɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yams are living tubers that rest after harvest; once their natural resting phase ends, warmth and air signal the yam to sprout so it can try to grow a new plant.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Beni adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ baatsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ koni amɛka tsei heei akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and leafy. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer around the base of the plant will help restore its green color and health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ su ni eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why did my crops wither and burn after I put chemical fertilizer directly around their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ebɔle tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is very strong and draws moisture out of plant stems and roots if it touches them directly. You should always apply fertilizer a few inches away from the stem in moist soil so the roots can draw in the nutrients safely.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he wa waa ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli kɛji amɛkɛ amɛhe kpe tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: What causes my maize crop leaves to suddenly look ragged with holes eaten into them overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-abele baai lɛ fee tamɔ nɔ ni etse ni bu eyi mli obɔ nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central leaves during the day and feed heavily on the plant at night. Catching them early and applying organic or recommended sprays can stop them from destroying the growing tips.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ waa gbɛkɛ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛnaa koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do the stems of my tomato plants wilt and die even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tomato tso lɛ he lɛ mli efɔ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by soil-borne fungi or bacteria that attack the plant's stem base, blocking water from moving up into the leaves. Avoiding planting tomatoes in the same wet spot year after year helps stop these organisms from building up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai loo muawai ni tutuaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ aya ŋwɛi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ ajie tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome ni nu yɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ akakwɛ̃.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests to live in the ground. Rotating with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts refills the soil with nitrogen and breaks the lifecycle of pests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyiɔ kɛ nitrogen. ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ mli

english: Why do experienced farmers plant groundnuts alongside their main crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ ŋmei ahe lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which means their roots naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil. This acts like free fertilizer for neighboring plants like maize.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell that can scorch newly germinated seedlings. It is safer to wait until the rains become regular so the young seeds have continuous soil moisture to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ be fɛɛ be koni eha dumɔwui bibii lɛ aya nɔ amɛdara kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with many leaves, but the roots underneath are small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing big tops and leaves instead of storage roots. Cassava needs potassium-rich soil to develop thick, starchy tubers underneath.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji moŋ fe ni eeekpa shishifãi. Shikpɔŋ ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia Cassava koni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ yɛ amɛshishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I cut down all the large shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ mifolɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young and mid-age cocoa trees need partial shade to keep cool and prevent soil water from evaporating. Full, direct sunlight stresses the cocoa plants, causing flowers to drop early and reducing pod yields.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii kɛ mɛi ni eye afii teŋgbɛ lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛtsi nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ maa kookoo tso lɛ nɔ mi. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya, ni ehaa pod lɛ yibii lɛ baa shi.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when plants suffer from extreme heat stress, poor soil moisture, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees. Providing light shade and consistent watering helps the flowers stay on the stem and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa Shade ni mli tse kɛ nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ ahiɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct intense sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects the young leaves from burning and helps keep moisture in the soil during the dry season.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebuɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too waterlogged. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or poultry manure helps the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli tsɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes into my maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Botemɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni oshi muji yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that attack corn plants. Clearing surrounding weeds early and applying recommended treatments into the center of the leaves can control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ awo baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ jwɛi lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in heavy soil that holds too much water during rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away so the tubers remain healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ
