english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same field where I harvested maize last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ mli nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas naturally trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground. Planting them restores nutrients that heavy feeder crops like maize took out of the soil.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ akwɛmɔ haa niyenii ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa jieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my crops when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to wait until the soil stays consistently wet for several days after the first rain. Planting too quickly after the very first light rain can burn seeds if a dry spell briefly returns.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ashã kɛji hɔmɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba be kukuoo ko.

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or unbalanced soil nutrients cause tomato plants stress, which makes flowers drop off. Regular watering at the base of the plant helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni etsɔɔ tomato.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is often caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or viruses they spread. Spraying organic or approved treatments early keeps these insects off the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akagbee shi kɛjɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Plantain trees fall over when pests weaken their shallow roots or when heavy fruit bunches pull them down during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with wooden poles helps keep the tree standing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ha shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ gbɔjɔ loo kɛ́ aduawai akui ni tsii gbala amɛ kɛba shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni akɛfee tso lɛ fiɔ tso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow so slowly and look thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitso titri lɛ daa blɛoo ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crop's roots. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting gives your crops full access to food so they grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi lɛ to he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni amɛdara oya.

english: Officer, why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die whenever the dry season starts?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts like a living umbrella, protecting them from heat and keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, kɛ cocoa tsei bibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: My maize leaves are turning yellow from the middle and dying off early, what is happening to them?
ga: Mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ ni amɛmiigboi oya. Mɛni ba a nɔ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is lacking key soil nutrients, especially nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food plants use to stay green, grow tall, and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli, amɛdara, ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant my cassava sticks very close together on the farm, won't I harvest more tubers from my land?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani minyɛŋ makpa bulbs babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: No, planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each crop enough space leads to bigger, heavier roots rather than many tiny, useless ones.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ha tso fɛɛ tso lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni dara ni tsii fe shishifãi bibii lɛ aba. bɛ sɛɛnamɔ

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off without turning into any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Flowers often fall off when the plant suffers from heat stress, erratic watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which tricks the plant into growing leaves instead of producing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: People say planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with maize improves the soil, is that true?
ga: Mɛi kɛɔ akɛ, kɛ́ adu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni aduɔ ŋmei lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo. Ani eji anɔkwale?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, naturally feeding the maize growing beside them.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Taakɛ eji lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Vegetable leaves curl during peak afternoon heat to reduce surface area and stop water from evaporating too fast; they usually recover as the sun goes down.
ga: Aduawai ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛhe waaa kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: My plantain trees keep growing many small shoots at the base, should I leave all of them to grow?
ga: Mi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Lots at the base Ani esa akɛ maha fɛɛ ada?

english: No, leaving too many shoots forces the parent tree to share its nutrients with too many stems. Pruning extra shoots and leaving only two or three ensures large, healthy plantain bunches.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo ni agbele mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ eshishifã lɛ agba niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo tsɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli ni ashi baai enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, no haa plantain lɛ feɔ agbo ni ehe wa.

english: Why do some of my planted maize seeds fail to sprout out of the soil entirely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if the soil lacks enough moisture, if they are buried too deep, if pests eat them underwater, or if the seeds were improperly dried and stored before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ Kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui yɛ nu shishi loo kɛji akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni akɛto dani adu.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is fully mature and ready for harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava shows signs of maturity when its lower leaves start turning yellow and falling off naturally, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack open.
ga: Cassava jieɔ dalɛ he okadii akpo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so quickly inside the barn shortly after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpaa lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly when bruised or cut during digging, exposed to direct hot sun, or stored in a place without good airflow, which allows decay fungus to attack the tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ loo afo amɛ yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ. Ha egbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli Aloo okɛto he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your soil is short on nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to build strong leaves, so when it runs out, the plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ efo lɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my maize ears have missing kernels and empty spots at the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni elaaje kɛ hei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Incomplete kernels happen when pollination is interrupted, often by dry weather or high heat when the silks first appear. Without enough moisture, the pollen cannot fertilize every silk, leading to empty gaps on the cob.
ga: Dumɔwui ni edako lɛ baa kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ kpa. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa beni siliki lɛ jeɔ kpo klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Pollen nyɛŋ afee siliki kpãai fɛɛ fɔmɔ nii. ni feɔ ŋmeii yɛ cob lɛ nɔ

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight and need shade to survive. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa from harsh heat while retaining moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni ehe hiaa ni amɛná hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel while still hanging on the trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, damp, and overly shaded conditions. Pruning dense branches lets sunlight and air flow through, which keeps the bark dry and stops the fungus from multiplying.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, edɔ, kɛ shade babaoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafa babaoo.

english: How can I tell when my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the whole root?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni mikɛ shishifã muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can tell cassava is maturing when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem. You will also notice the soil around the base of the plant cracking as the roots swell underneath.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei miikwɛ̃ kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni eshiɔ tso ni nɔ ko bɛ mli Obaayɔse shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ fãa beni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Does putting wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb really help the tubers grow larger?
ga: Ani tso ni mikɛtoɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ koni ekwɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Yes, trailing vines up stakes lifts the leaves off the ground so they catch maximum sunlight. More sunlight allows the plant to produce extra food energy, which travels down to swell the tuber underground.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, wain tsei ni hoɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ aya nɔ babaoo. Hulu la babaoo haa tsei feɔ niyenii hewalɛ kroko. ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni eha tuber lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: What causes small green caterpillars to hide inside the central funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This is likely the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that crawls into the central whorl of young corn plants to feed on delicate leaves. Catching them early and applying natural sprays like neem leaf extract can protect the growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ koni eye baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem baa mli nu atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛdalɛ naa.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without forming any fresh fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii hee ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Keeping soil moisture steady with regular watering encourages the plant to hold its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa kɛtee he ni edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni oooha ehi shi daa kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upwards and look small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Upward leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves. Spraying with soapy water or appropriate neem-based remedies helps control these pests and restores leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo tsofai ni akɛ neem fee lɛ shwie nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni eha baai lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which works with helpful soil microbes to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When groundnut roots decay, that natural fertilizer remains behind to feed future crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛkɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Adebɔɔ mli ŋmei baakã he ahi shi koni akɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under the full hot sun. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that create living shade umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa plants cool and moist until they grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo baa. Ha cacao tsei bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain, they steal water and nutrients from the soil. Cutting them down so only one or two strong shoots remain ensures the mother plant has enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Beni ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo ni miida yɛ plantain wulu lɛ he lɛ fa babaoo. Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo lɛ ekoŋŋ koni eshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso nyɛ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it uses to stay green and grow big cobs. Applying compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early helps the plant regain its green color.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn tsei lɛ miiye nitrogen hɔmɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛkwɛ ŋmɔji anɔ ni akɛkwɛ ŋmɔji wuji anɔ. Kompost loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with lots of leaves but only produce tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii. Shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or plants are packed too closely together, cassava puts all its energy into leaf growth instead of root growth. Proper plant spacing and balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to store food in the tubers instead.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ebaai lɛ akwɛmɔ mli. Yɛ shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ najiaŋ Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛtoɔ niyenii yɛ bulb lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Yam vines produce bigger tubers when leaves are lifted off the ground into direct sunlight, allowing them to capture energy more efficiently. Lifting the vines off the soil also protects the leaves from dampness and rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji kɛji ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ fitemɔ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers drop off without forming fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly from very dry to very wet. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering and mulching helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛyaa nɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Curled or puckered leaves on pepper plants are usually a reaction to tiny pests like aphids or thrips sucking the sap from undersides of the leaves. Spraying early with organic solutions like neem oil stops the insects and allows normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ neem fɔ shwie nɔ mra lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ akpa ni ebaaha baai lɛ ada bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop in the hot afternoon sun but look fresh again early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛ hejɔɔmɔ leebi lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, water evaporates from the leaves faster than the roots can pull water from the soil, causing temporary wilting to conserve moisture. As long as the soil has water, the plant recovers overnight when temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔɔ. Nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa amɛgbiɔ be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ nu lɛ Tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ nyɔɔŋ kome mli kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi pɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with dark green powder inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This behavior is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the soft inner leaves of the maize plant. Putting clean sand or neem powder into the center funnel early in the morning suffocates the caterpillars before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ subaŋ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei amli baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋã ni he tse loo neem powda fata ŋã ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ he leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have tiny nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth. When the plants decay, they release natural fertilizer into the ground for the next crop to use.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni tsei lɛ fiteɔ lɛ, amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my maize grains rot or turn moldy in storage even after I dried them under the sun for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ fite loo etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ gbii babaoo ehi hulu lɛ mli bianɛ moŋ.

english: If grains are bagged when their internal moisture level is still high—above the safe 12.5% target—trapped dampness creates heat that allows mold and insects to grow rapidly inside the storage bags.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo kotoku mli yɛ be mli ni mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fa lolo—ni fe nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ. 12.5%—Fɛ̃i ni amɔ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa ni haa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii daa oya yɛ kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli.

english: What happens to my harvested seeds if I leave them drying in the hot sun for too long?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ anɔ? Kɛji mishi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ,.

english: Over-drying crops reduces their total weight, makes the grains brittle so they break into powder during milling, and destroys the seed's ability to germinate if saved for next season.
ga: Tsei ni agbiɔ fe nine lɛ haa amɛtsiimɔ fɛɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ashɛɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ, etsɔɔ powda. ni efiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why does the inside of my grain bag feel hot when I put my hand inside it after a few weeks of storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cereal kotoku lɛ mli lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ waa kɛ́ mikɛ minine wo mli beni mikɛto otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heat inside a bag means the crop was stored with high moisture. The grains and hidden fungi are actively breathing and generating heat, which will distort the grain quality and spoil the entire bag if not dried immediately.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ toɔ he ko ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Nibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ ŋmeii muɔ kɛboteɔ mli ni amɛfeɔ dɔlɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaafite kotokui lɛ kɛji akɛ agbiko amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How can I easily test if my dried maize is at the right moisture level for safe storage without using expensive tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka makwɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛha nitoohe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni nibii ni jara wa fataaa he?

english: A simple field test is to press a grain hard with your thumbnail or bite it; if it breaks cleanly with a sharp snap instead of denting, the moisture level has dropped low enough (around 12.5%) for long-term storage.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo mli kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo Etsɔɔ akɛ, esa akɛ anyɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ waa. Kɛtsɔ oshishifa loo kɛtsɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa ko ni ooomɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛji akɛ akumɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmãa ni mli wa moŋ fe ni aaakpã mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baa shi bɔ ni sa (aaafee 12.5%) koni akɛto be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow and drooping even though I water them heavily every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ? Ani oooha nu babaoo daa gbi?

english: Giving crops too much water drowns the roots by pushing out air from the soil. Damaged roots rot and cannot take up food, causing the leaves to turn yellow and wilt despite the wet soil.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo onibii amli fe nine lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaafee nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ aye. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ po nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato fruits cracking open on the sides before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi dani amɛfeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: Fruit cracking happens when crops experience a sudden burst of heavy water after a dry period. The inside of the tomato expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the fruit to split.
ga: Yibii amli fãmɔ baa kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii na nu afua ni baa trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni ehewolo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã, ni no haa aduawai lɛ mli gbalaa.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings fail to sprout when I plant them immediately after the first light rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: A light rain only wets the top surface of the ground, while the soil deeper down remains dry and hot, drying out the cassava stem cuttings before they can grow roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ baaha ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ pɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ kã he egbi ni edɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmei niji lɛ agbi dani amɛ shishifãi akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings grow very tall and thin instead of standing strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ miida waa ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadamɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seedlings grow tall and weak when they do not get enough direct sunlight. They stretch upwards searching for light, resulting in fragile stems that easily fall over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛkpã amɛhe kɛtee ŋwɛi koni amɛyatao la. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Why are the maize plants in the middle of my field smaller with thinner cobs than the ones at the outer edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji bibii ni amɛyɛ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Plants at the edges receive extra light and air, while closely crowded plants in the center compete heavily against each other for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ baaná la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kroko. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ waa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my groundnuts so the pods do not snap off under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? koni ŋmeii lɛ akajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Groundnuts are mature when the inside of the pod shell turns dark brown when opened and the outer leaves begin to yellow; waiting too long causes the stems to rot and snap during pulling.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ amli tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ kɛji agbele naa. ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ Mɛmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛkuɔ yɛ be mli ni agbalaa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants take around 8 to 12 months before the tubers are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ heɔ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 dani eshishifãi lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava needs several months of sunlight and rain to produce energy and store it as starch in its underground roots. Harvesting too early results in thin, watery roots rather than thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Hulu la kɛ nugbɔ he miihia cassava nyɔji babaoo koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ni ekɛ starch ato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baa moŋ fe ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Why does my plantain tree take almost a full year to produce a single bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ heɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi muu fɛɛ dani ewoɔ yibii akuu kome pɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants must first grow a strong root system and many large leaves to collect sunlight. Only after storing enough energy can the plant send out a flower stalk and develop a heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ baai wuji babaoo klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛbua hulu la naa. Beni akɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa eto pɛ kɛkɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ atsu fɔfɔii ahe ŋmeii ni etsɔ aduawai akui ni tsii.

english: Why do insects like bees visit my crop flowers, and does this help my yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii yasaraa fɔfɔi ni miduɔ lɛ? Ni ani enɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi koni mawo yibii?

english: Insects are attracted to the sweet nectar inside flowers and carry pollen from flower to flower as they move. This process, called pollination, triggers the flower to develop into actual fruits or seeds.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbalaa kooloi. ni amɛwoɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ beni amɛyaa lɛ. Atsɛɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ pollination. Wo fɔfɔii lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa blossoms sometimes drop off the trunk without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off if tiny pollinating insects called midges are absent, or if the tree lacks water and nutrients. Keeping proper shade trees helps retain moisture and encourages pollinating insects.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni feɔ fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai Tso lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ewoɔ kooloi ni feɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: How does maize produce ears of corn from the tassels at the top of the stalk?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmãa lɛ toi jɛɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ mli?

english: The tassel at the top is the male part that releases pollen into the wind, while the silks lower down are the female parts. When pollen falls onto a silk strand, it forms a single corn grain on the cob.
ga: Tassels ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ji mɛi ni jieɔ pollen kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ anɔ̃. Siliki fã ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji yoo lɛ teemɔŋ fã. Kɛji pollen gbee siliki lɛ nɔ Abɛi ŋmei kome pɛ baafee ŋmei ŋmei lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant maize on the exact same piece of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, lowering your yield over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has enough natural food to support my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Healthy soil is typically dark in color, feels crumbly, and holds water well after rain. If your young crops turn pale yellow despite getting rain, the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ su tsuɔ, enuɔ he akɛ egbɔjɔ, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ odumɔwui lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantain plants provide broad leaves that shield the young cocoa from heat while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I remove weeds around my pepper seedlings early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Pepper tsei yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal water, fertilizer, and light from your young plants. Clearing them early ensures your peppers get all the nutrients they need to establish strong stems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli. Hetsemɔ mra Enɛ baaha o-peppers lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and turn yellow during the dry heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Hot, dry conditions cause tomatoes to curl their leaves to save water. Heat also encourages tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies to attack the plant and spread leaf-yellowing viruses.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ haa tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛbu nu he. Dɔlɛ lɛ hu woɔ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua tsei ni amɛgbɛ helai ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct intense sunlight and high heat. Leaving some tall trees or planting plantains around them provides living shade that protects the tender leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ lɛ Ha ehi shi loo dumɔ dumɔwui ebɔle he. Tsei haa hulutsoo ni buɔ baai bibii ahe koni amɛkashã, ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and soft when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a mold-like organism that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and humid weather through splashing rain. Pruning extra cocoa branches lets air and sunlight into the farm, which dries out the pods and helps stop the spread.
ga: Nibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i, kɛ fɛ̃i shihilɛi amli kɛtsɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji baa. Afoɔ kookoo niji krokomɛi amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni eye ebua ni akpa shweremɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize are usually a sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔji kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When the leaves and roots decay, they leave behind natural food that fertilizes the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain stem for food and water in the soil. By keeping only one or two strong suckers, all the plant's energy goes into producing a much larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi. Tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa koni ekɛfee plantains ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my young cassava plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Cassava tsei bibii yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Weeds grow faster than young cassava and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Keeping the field clean during the first three months allows the cassava roots to expand fully underground.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi kwraa.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up into the sunlight where they can manufacture food efficiently. It also keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing fungal leaf diseases from spoiling the crop.
ga: Staking baaha hulu la ashɛ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee niyenii jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ehaa baai lɛ hu ehiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Tsi fungal leaf helai ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground if I leave them in the soil during very heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the ground stays completely soaked for a long time, the roots cannot get air and excess water encourages rot-causing organisms to enter the tuber.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aná kɔɔyɔɔ. Ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ woɔ nibii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛbote ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: What causes the leaves on my tomato plants to curl up and stop growing leaves or fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa baai loo aduawai lɛ daalɛ kpaa?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects like whiteflies. Managing insect pests early and removing infected plants stops the disease from spreading across your entire tomato bed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Tsɔɔmɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra. Ni tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã o-tomato saatso lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from stress, especially during sudden hot dry spells or long periods without water. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch or regular watering helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ, ni egbiɔ trukaa loo be kakadaŋŋ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow before the crop is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ebaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. When nitrogen runs low in the soil, the plant moves what little it has from older bottom leaves to feed the new growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ nitrogen fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and gives soil pests and diseases a permanent home, causing your harvests to get smaller each year.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ shihilɛhe ni hiɔ shi daa. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee bibioo daa afi.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on my farm before planting young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees have broad leaves that create living umbrellas, providing the essential shade and cool air young cocoa needs to survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hɔɔŋ baa. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa kooloi bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots staying very thin even though the plant leaves look healthy and tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ waa eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛlɛ moŋ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or given too much leaf-growing fertilizer, they spend all their energy growing tall stems and leaves above ground instead of storing food in roots underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo akɛ ŋmei babaoo wo baai lɛ ahe. Ebaahe nakai be lɛ fɛɛ dani ŋmeii kɛ baai akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: What happens to my yield if I let my yam vines trail along the ground instead of staking them on tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji miha sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ amɛ baawo tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: Staking gets yam leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to make food for big tubers. Leaves trailing on the ground get dirty, catch fungal diseases in wet soil, and produce much smaller yams.
ga: Staking baajie sweet potato baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha bulb agboi lɛ niyenii. Baai ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ muji. Fungal hela ni baa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa sweet potato bibii babaoo baa.

english: How do weeds growing close to my crops actually reduce my final harvest?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aha minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ aba shi aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal soil fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crops. When weeds take these essential nutrients, your crops become weak and cannot produce full yields.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ nine shɛ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ nɔ lɛ, Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo amɛyibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Upward curling in pepper leaves is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from tender leaves, or passing a virus to the plant that distorts leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ haa tsei ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures become too hot or when the plant experiences water stress. Severe heat prevents pollination, so the plant drops its flowers to save water and survival energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa tsiɔ pollination naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha wala.

english: Why do my crops fail if I sow my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell called a false start. Sowing too early causes seeds to germinate and then dry up and die in hot soil before regular rains resume.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ale lɛ akɛ amale shishijee nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. No sɛɛ lɛ, egbiɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop in the hot afternoon heat even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: In hot afternoon sun, plants lose water through leaf pores faster than roots can drink it up. Leaves wilt temporarily to protect themselves from losing more water, then bounce back as temperatures cool in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni nu akafite ekoŋŋ. Kɛkɛ ni ekoŋŋ beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct, harsh sunlight dries out their delicate leaves and strips the soil of moisture. Keeping shade trees creates a cool microclimate that protects seedling roots until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛná hɔnɔ fioo koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbi ni ebaagbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ bibioo ko ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow starting from the bottom of the stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, an essential food crop nutrient. The maize plant pulls remaining nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new leaves at the top, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha niyenii tsei Abele tsei gbalaa nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts alongside my maize help my crops grow better without extra chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ fataaa he lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means their roots work with beneficial soil bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. This extra nitrogen naturally feeds the neighboring maize plants and improves overall soil health.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni fata he nɛɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong winds right when the bunches start to mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli kɛji tsei lɛ aniji je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that stay near the top of the soil rather than anchoring deep underground. As heavy fruit bunches grow, the plant becomes top-heavy, so supporting the stem with wooden stakes or bamboo props prevents them from tipping over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaahi shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu agbo ko kwɛ̃ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni akɛfiɔ tsɔne lɛ he lɛ fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekatsɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to clear and heap soil into high mounds before planting yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow large and deep beneath the ground. High mounds keep the soil loose and airy so the tubers can expand easily without resistance, while also protecting the roots from suffocating in waterlogged soil during heavy rains.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu yɔɔ mli. Bɔni afee ni yitso lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni nɔ ko akatsi enaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkafo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my mature cassava roots start to rot rapidly if I leave them buried during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy after reaching full growth. Excessive rainwater fills up all air spaces in the soil, effectively drowning the roots and creating conditions for fungus and rot to spread quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ beni amɛdara sɛɛ. Nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa shihilɛi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ baa.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and side shoots from my tomato plants instead of letting them all grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tomato tso lɛ niji kɛ esɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: When a tomato plant grows too many leaves and shoots, it wastes its energy maintenance rather than making fruit. Removing minor extra branches forces the plant to direct all its food and water into producing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji tomato tso ko yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii babaoo Ebaafite hewalɛ yɛ ekwɛmɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni abaakpa lɛ baabi ni tso lɛ akudɔ eniyenii kɛ nu lɛ fɛɛ koni ekɛwo tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do pests get worse every season if I plant pepper on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ feɔ basabasa daa afi kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously allows pests and diseases specific to that plant to stay and multiply in the soil year after year. Rotating to a completely different crop breaks their life cycle because the returning pests find no food source.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ayaa nɔ akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ haa tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai hiɔ shi ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Kɛ́ atsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaafite ewala shihilɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kooloi ni nyɛɛɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba koni amɛyatao niyenii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce tiny yields even if I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ mishwieɔ amɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most domestic crops, allowing them to steal soil nutrients, fertilizers, water, and sunlight before your crops can reach them, effectively starving your plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe shia tsei babaoo. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la dani ŋmɔshi nibii shɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper blossoms keep falling off the plant before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo peppers lɛ?

english: Blossom drop happens when plants suffer from extreme heat or sudden water stress. When temperatures spike or moisture levels fluctuate wildly, the plant drops its flowers to conserve energy and keep itself alive.
ga: Blossom drop baa kɛji tso lɛ na trukaa hulutsoo loo nu he haomɔ. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ loo hulutsoo be lɛ tsakeɔ waa lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect their tender leaves from direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains creates a cooler environment and holds moisture in the soil, helping the cocoa survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ loo adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ tamɔ plantains lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eye ebua kookoo ni ehi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to spread their leaves in full sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves elevated, catching more sun and preventing fungal diseases from spreading from damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛjie amɛbaai lɛ akpo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Na hulu la babaoo Ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during long dry spells like the harmattan to stop losing water through leaf evaporation. This helps the plant survive on underground water until the rainy season returns.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli, tamɔ Harmatta, koni amɛkpa nu ni fiteɔ yɛ baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu mli kɛyashiɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the middle of hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Maize rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to direct sunlight, which conserves internal water and prevents the plant from drying out during the hottest hours of the day.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ emli ni ehaaa tso lɛ agbi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into any fruits when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato plant stress, making pollen inactive so flowers cannot be fertilized. When flowers fail to pollinate, the plant drops them to conserve energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Ehaa pollen lɛ tsuuu nii Anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ fɔmɔ nii. Beni anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ pollination lɛ Ashwieɔ tsei koni akɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are tiny insects causing my pepper leaves to wrinkle and curl up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii Ko ni haa pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ?

english: Insects like aphids or thrips hide on the undersides of leaves to suck out nutrients and sap. This loss of fluid distorts leaf growth, causing them to curl, wrinkle, and stunt plant growth.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ aphids loo thrips Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai ashishi koni ekɛnu niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu. Nu nɛɛ ni laajeɔ lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ dalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni egbɔjɔɔ, ni tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ ada.

english: Why do caterpillars eat the inside leaves of my maize plants right at the centre core?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ yɛ amɛmligbɛ lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm lay eggs in the soft center (funnel) of maize plants because the young, tender leaves inside provide rich nutrition and shelter from heat and predators.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo (cones) lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii babaoo kɛ he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same field drains specific soil nutrients like nitrogen and allows maize-loving pests and soil diseases to build up, leading to lower yields over time.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni sumɔɔ abele kɛ sũ mli helai ni baa lɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why does adding dried animal manure to my farm make my soil stay moist longer than using chemical fertilizers alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Animal manure adds organic material that acts like a sponge in the soil, improving its structure so it can hold water and nutrients longer, whereas chemical fertilizers only feed the plant directly.
ga: Manure kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fataa he. Afee bɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ koni enyɛ ehiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ haa tsei niyenii tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my cassava plants produce smaller roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-cassava tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miifee bibioo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with crops for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. When weeds crowd cassava, the plant gets fewer resources to build and store food in its root tubers.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, hulu la kɛ nu. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ ye ŋmei nɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ baaná nibii fioo ni ekɛbaafee niyenii ni ekɛto eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil or are getting waterlogged. Applying the right fertilizer, like NPK, at the correct stage helps the leaves turn green again and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa, tamɔ NPK, wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer right next to the stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ mitsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ he?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the tender skin and roots of the plant. It is best to apply it in a small ring a few inches away where the roots can safely reach and absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni akɛwo mli yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli. He ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he ni amɛŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems very close to each other on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving them proper spacing allows each plant to grow large, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up, resulting in poorer harvests over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What causes small holes in my young corn leaves and why is it dangerous for my harvest?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ anɔ Ni mɛni hewɔ eyeɔ mikpamɔ lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Small holes are usually caused by pests like fall armyworms eating the leaves. If they damage the central growing point of the plant, the corn will be unable to grow properly or produce full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni amɛye baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii baa. Kɛji efite tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni edaa lɛ, Abɛi nyɛŋ ada jogbaŋŋ loo ekɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow poorly even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm by stealing the water, sunlight, and plant food meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures your main crops get everything they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aná nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from stress, such as direct heat from intense sunlight, lack of moisture, or insect attacks. Maintaining moderate shade helps protect flowers so they can turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa mli tɛ̃ɛ. Fɛ̃i ni bɛ loo kooloi ni baatutua amɛ Shade ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛtsɔmɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: How do I know when it is safe to plant my seeds after the first rain comes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ eba lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain of the season is often followed by dry spells that can kill young sprouts. It is safer to wait until the soil stays moist several inches deep for a few days before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ ni baanyɛ agbe tsei bibii lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baashɛ inchii babaoo gbii fioo komɛi dani odu.

english: How does covering the soil with dry grass around my crops help them grow?
ga: Mulching shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni ebɔle he Te mi ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa mi tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves creates mulch, which keeps the soil cool during hot days, holds moisture in the ground longer, and stops weeds from sprouting easily.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: Why don't the seeds I saved from my last hybrid maize harvest grow as well as the original store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ tamɔ shishijee dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields for only one generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose their special strength, leading to uneven growth and smaller yields the following season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ kome pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and turn brown when planted in an open sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ mli egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. They need shade cover when they are young to protect their soft leaves from burning and to keep the soil around their roots moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛhe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Does cocoa grow better in complete open sunlight or under shade trees?
ga: Ani kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ loo yɛ tsei ashishi?

english: Cocoa grows best with moderate shade. While full sunshine can cause fast early growth, providing shade cover protects the trees from heat stress and ensures they stay healthy for many years.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha tsei lɛ adara oya moŋ, shi hulutsoo ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi afii babaoo.

english: Why does the soil around my cocoa trees dry out so quickly during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Without shade trees or ground cover to block direct sunlight, intense sun heat evaporates soil moisture very fast, leaving root systems dry and struggling to feed the plant.
ga: Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ko bɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ oya. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ena niyenii kɛha tso lɛ.

english: Since cocoa naturally grows in warm sunny countries like Ghana, why can too much sunshine be harmful to it?
ga: Akɛni kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ maji ni mli edɔ ni hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ Ghana lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ yeɔ kookoo awui lɛ?

english: Cocoa naturally evolved as an under-canopy forest plant. Even though it likes warm weather, direct prolonged sunshine without shade overworks the tree, causing leaf damage and moisture loss.
ga: Cocoa ba kɛjɛ adebɔɔ naa akɛ koo mli tso ko ni yɔɔ tsei ashishi. Eyɛ mli akɛ esumɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ moŋ Shi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hu sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees look strong and full at first, but become thin and sparse after several years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ ni eyi obɔ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Shi ebafeɔ mlɛo ni eyɛ mlɛo yɛ afii babaoo sɛɛ?

english: When cocoa trees stand alone without shade cover, the long-term exposure to intense sun and heat wears them out over time, causing them to lose leaves and become sparse as they age.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ pɛ damɔ shi ni ebɛ hulutsoo. Hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaha kookoo tso lɛ afite yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: My cocoa farm produced a heavy harvest in the first few years without shade trees, so why is my yield dropping now?
ga: Mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ wo aduawai babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ minitsumɔ lɛ miiba shi bianɛ lɛ?

english: Full sun can stimulate high early yields, but without shade cover to protect the soil and trees, the plants become exhausted quickly, leading to poor health and lower yields in the long run.
ga: Hulu la babaoo baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba mra. Shi kɛ́ hulutsoo bɛ ni baabu shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ Tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ oya. Enɛ haa mɔ náaa hewalɛ kpakpa, ni nibii ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my mature cocoa trees falling off and leaving the branches bare?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho, ni amɛmiishi niji lɛ efolo lɛ?

english: Excessive sun heat forces cocoa trees to shed their leaves to reduce water loss. Providing taller shade trees helps create a cool environment that prevents premature leaf drop.
ga: Hulu lɛ mli dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni akɛ shade woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni tsiɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ naa.

english: Is it safe to plant a cocoa farm without leaving any big trees around?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu kookoo ŋmɔ ni ashiii tsei wuji abɔle he?

english: Planting cocoa completely in the open leaves the crops vulnerable to intense sun and harsh weather. Integrating shade trees creates a stable protective environment for long-term farming.
ga: Cocoa ni aduɔ kwraa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ haa hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ waa. Tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni buɔ mɔ he ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛha okwaayeli ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: How do taller trees planted on my farm help protect my cocoa crop?
ga: Te tsei kakadaji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ buɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Taller trees act as a natural shield by blocking scorching sun rays, reducing dry wind exposure, and keeping the climate beneath them humid and safe for cocoa trees.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gãimlibi kɛtsɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ nɔ ni oha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni efee shweshweeshwe aha kookoo tsei lɛ.

english: Can I plant temporary crops alongside my cocoa trees to help them grow better initially?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu be kukuoo mli tsei yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli?

english: Yes, planting fast-growing crops alongside young cocoa provides essential overhead shade and wind protection during the early stage when cocoa plants are most delicate.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni daa oya ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa ŋwɛi hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hebuu ni he hiaa waa yɛ shishijee bei amli. He ni kookoo tso lɛ waaa fe fɛɛ lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight when they are small. Leaving some mature trees or planting plantains provides shade and keeps the air humid, protecting the young leaves from burning until the cocoa plants grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Tsei ni eda ni ashiɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Tsi baai bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã kɛyashi cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does my yam crop need tall wooden stakes to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni ekɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam is a vine that produces food for its underground tubers through its leaves. Lifting the vines on stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight and keeps them off the damp soil, which prevents leaf decay and fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kɛ niyenii haa ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. ni etsĩ enaa koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai ni fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plants regain green leaves and grow rapidly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with large leaves, but the roots under the ground remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ daraaa lolo.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and lacks potassium, cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of expanding its roots. Using balanced soil nutrients ensures the plant directs food downward to swell the tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo ni potassium bɛ mli lɛ, Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ koni ekwɛ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Niyenii mli nibii ni sa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baa shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ amli alɛɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow better when I plant them in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas feed on nitrogen from the air and share it with the soil, which naturally fertilizes neighboring crops like maize. In return, the tall maize stalks provide light support and space balance for the farm.
ga: Cowpeas heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ jaa. Eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa. Abɛi tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛwoɔ la lɛ he nyɔmɔ ni ehaa he ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ekome.

english: Why do my plantain leaves roll inward and droop during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni nu lɛ mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing moisture in dry, hot wind. Covering the soil around the base with dry plant material (mulching) retains soil water and reduces stress during dry weather.
ga: Akɛ plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ akafite. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa haomɔ baa shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my garden egg flowers drop off without turning into fruits during hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause plants to drop flowers to conserve energy and survive. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my pepper plants wilting in the afternoon heat even though I watered them this morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho ŋmɛnɛ gbɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ha lɛ ŋmɛnɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During intense heat, leaves lose water faster than roots can absorb it from the soil. As long as the plants recover by evening, it is normal, but placing mulch around the stems keeps the roots cool and reduces wilting.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ he baajɔ lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ, no lɛ ehi. Shi kɛ́ akɛ sũ wo tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants take so long to show fruits after they start producing green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii beni ebɔi baai eŋɔlii lɛ akwɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants must first build a strong structure of stems and leaves to gather sunlight. Once the plant accumulates enough energy, it shifts its focus to flowering and setting fruit.
ga: Esa akɛ tomato tsei ama tsotso kɛ baa gbɛjianɔtoo ni wa koni amɛbua hulu la naa. Kɛ tsei bua hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa naa Ebaatsake ejwɛŋmɔ kɛya fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers take almost a full year to mature when the top leaves look fully grown in a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ he nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi muu fɛɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ? Beni baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara kwraa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf growth happens first so the plant can make food, while tuber enlargement happens slowly over time beneath the ground. The plant continuously transfers energy from the leaves into the roots bit by bit until harvest.
ga: Baai lɛ daalɛ baa klɛŋklɛŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, yitso lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ baa fiofio. Beni be hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Tsei yaa nɔ amɛjieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli fiofio kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa amɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that provide shade and trap soil moisture, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Buu kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant takes nitrogen away from its older, bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do small black beetles destroy my harvested maize inside stored bags even when the bags are tied shut?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ yɛ kotokui ni ato mli lɛ amli eyɛ mli akɛ akpɛtɛ kotokui lɛ ahe moŋ?

english: These beetles are grain weevils. Microscopic weevil eggs are often brought in from the field on the ears or exist inside reused storage bags, hatching inside the sealed bag when temperatures are warm.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmãa ŋmeii. Bei pii lɛ, akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni ji weevil ŋmeii lɛ baa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ toi nɔ loo akɛwoɔ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ nii amli ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ amli. Amɛfɔɔ yɛ kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ.

english: Heavy rains in poorly drained soil cause waterlogging, which suffocates the cassava roots by cutting off oxygen and creates an ideal environment for water molds and fungal rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa nu mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii.

english: Why shouldn't I build my yam mounds too close to each other on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ matswaa ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams need ample underground space to expand into large tubers. Spacing mounds too close together forces plants to compete for soil nutrients, water, and space, resulting in smaller yams.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia sweet potato koni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Pile ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa sweet potato bibii baa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into cups during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to direct sunlight, which cuts down on water loss through transpiration.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni baa baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ nu ni faaa lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without producing any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: High afternoon temperatures can sterilize tomato pollen, preventing fertilization. When a blossom fails to pollinate, the plant drops the flower to save energy.
ga: He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ agbe tomato mli ŋmeii lɛ ni etsĩ fɔmɔ naa. Kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ afee amɛ pollin. Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why does burning my cleared land before planting reduce my soil yield over time?
