ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa dani aduɔ nii lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Burning destroys essential organic matter, kills beneficial earthworms and microbes, and leaves the topsoil bare and vulnerable to erosion during heavy rains.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaanyɛ efo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the first rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that are adapted to local soil conditions, allowing them to absorb early moisture and nutrients much faster than cultivated seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛfee nɔ ni sa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shishijee mli oya kwraa fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly swarm and eat my cabbage crop right after the dry season ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shwieɔ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ anɔ trukaa beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: Adult moths emerge and lay hundreds of eggs on the tender new leaves produced by cabbages right after the first rains arrive, leading to a sudden population burst of caterpillars.
ga: Kplukai ni eda lɛ jeɔ kpo ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni kaabaji feɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ tee hiɛ trukaa.

english: If I keep adding more chemical fertilizer to my maize, will it keep producing bigger cobs?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa kroko ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ fata ŋmãa lɛ he Ani ŋmãa baawo ŋmãa wuji?

english: Not necessarily. Giving crops too much fertilizer can burn their root systems, damage the soil, or cause the plant to grow thick leaves without producing large grains.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã. ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ Aloo ehaa tsei lɛ baa ni mli edɔ ni amɛwooo dumɔwui wuji.

english: This happens when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. To survive, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves and sends it up to feed the newer growth at the top.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni ehi shi Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha tsei heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight. This competition results in weak stems and very small tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yitsei bibii waa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and yellow even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal essential soil nutrients like nitrogen before crop roots can absorb them, leaving the main crop malnourished despite enough rain.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, dani tsei lɛ shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ faaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and heat. Without shade trees or plantains acting as natural umbrellas, the seedlings burn and lose moisture faster than their roots can take it up.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei loo tsei bibii ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo bɛ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baashã ni amɛbaafite ŋmɔtɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can spread out and capture maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which is then sent down to feed and swell the underground tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Hulu la lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, atsuɔ kɛyaa shi koni eyaye nii ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defense against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant hides part of its leaf surface from direct sun to stop water from evaporating too fast.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ fã ko teeɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ koni nu lɛ akaho oya tsɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat, drought, or poor nutrition. Shedding flowers allows the plant to save its energy for basic survival rather than producing fruit.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo niyenii ni esaaa hao amɛ. Fɔfɔi ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why does my tomato plant have so many leafy branches but very few tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo shi tomato fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: When tomato plants receive excess nutrients or are left unpruned, they put all their energy into making leafy stems rather than channeling energy into flowering and fruiting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa fe nine loo afolɔɔɔ amɛhe lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakudɔ lɛ kɛya fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo nɔ.

english: Why does my crop yield drop so much if I plant cassava on the exact same piece of land three seasons in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi waa kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ bei etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to recover, while also allowing crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa jɛmɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I clear all the bushes and weeds off my land before planting my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei?

english: Clearing weeds removes competition so your young cassava plants get all the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients they need to grow strong and produce large roots.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ, o-cassava tsei bibii lɛ baaná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo shishifãi wuji.

english: Is it better to burn the weeds I clear from my field, or should I leave them on the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ loo esa akɛ mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving cleared bushes on top of the soil to rot creates a natural cover that keeps the soil cool, holds water, and fertilizes your crops naturally as it breaks down.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi tsei bibii ni he tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛgbo lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa nu hiɔ shi, ni ehaa onibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen nutrients or the ground is soaked with too much standing water, which prevents roots from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ kɛ nu ni ekã shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ dani pepper lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat or lack of water. Keeping soil moist and using mulch around the base protects flowers so they turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo he. Konu lɛ buɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni etsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my tomatoes get dark, rotten spots at the bottom of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Dark spots on tomato bottoms usually happen when the soil moisture changes too drastically, preventing the plant from taking up calcium evenly as the fruit grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsake tsɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aná calcium babaoo tamɔ bɔ ni amɛnáa lɛ. ekomefeemɔ beni aduawai lɛ daraa lɛ

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ he kome?

english: Seeds planted too close together fight each other for food and light, resulting in tall, thin stalks with small or missing maize cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baatswa niyenii kɛ la he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ni bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily when the wind blows hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ miitswa waa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the top of the soil. Planting them deep in wide holes and mounding rich soil around the stem gives them a strong anchor against wind.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ bu ni mli kwɔ mli shɔŋŋ ni akɛ sũ ni jara wa to tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha amɛná ŋshɔkei ni wa ni amɛte shi amɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden sticks to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ? Koni okwɔ ŋwɛi?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tuber underground. Lifting the leaves off the ground on sticks gives them light and keeps them free from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkpɛ ni helai akaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is healthy enough to start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Healthy soil crumbles easily in your hand, feels slightly damp, and has a dark color from rich decayed leaves and natural plant matter.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ oniji amli. Enuɔ he akɛ edɔ fioo ni eyɛ su ni tsuɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei amli.

english: Harmattan winds suck moisture out of cocoa leaves quickly. Planting tall plantains next to cocoa trees provides living shade and holds moisture to keep cocoa alive during hot, dry winds.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai amli oya. Dumɔwui kakadaji ni aduɔ yɛ Cocoa tso lɛ masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni ehi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant different crops like groundnuts together with my maize instead of growing only maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu ŋmãa kɛkɛ

english: Growing groundnuts alongside maize protects your farm. Groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and feed the soil naturally, while planting more than one crop ensures you still have something to harvest and sell if rain fails or pests attack one crop.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he. Peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛ niyenii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni fe ekome ni ooodu lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oyɛ nɔ ko ni obaakpa ni ohɔ̃ɔ lolo kɛji nugbɔ nɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii tutua ŋmɔshi nibii kome lɛ,

english: Planting cassava in the same spot continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets cassava pests build up in the ground. Rotating cassava with legumes like cowpeas gives the soil time to recover and stay fertile.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be fɛɛ be. ni eha ŋmei mli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmei tamɔ tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ni ekwɛ bɔ ni ewoɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the rain falls too much for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Excessive rain floods the roots and washes away nitrogen, which is the nutrient plants need to stay green. Without air in the soaked soil and enough nitrogen, the plant leaves lose their bright green color and turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ nitrogen lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ lɛ mli ni nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ mli lɛ. Tsei ahe baai lɛ hu baafite amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ lɛ ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during the middle of the afternoon when the sun is strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in strong heat is a plant's natural defense to survive. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, helping it trap moisture and stop water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa be mli lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛha wala. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ.

english: In the dry season, wild plants dry up, so insects flock to your green, watered farm for food and water. Additionally, heavy rain during the wet season naturally knocks insects off plants and destroys their eggs.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, koo mli tsei gbɛ́ɔ. Kplukai baa oŋmɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he ni nu kɛ niyenii yɔɔ lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ hu haa kooloi bibii shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛwuji lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if my land is better suited for planting swamp rice or root crops like cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo tuber ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa?

english: It depends on how water sits on your land. Rice loves wet, heavy soil that holds water for long periods, whereas cassava roots need loose, well-drained soil because too much standing water causes cassava roots to rot.
ga: Edamɔ he ni nu lɛ yɔɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Omɔ sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ, ni tsii ni hiɛɔ nu be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot so quickly after I dig them up from the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they get cut or bruised by tools during harvest, or if they are stacked in hot places without air. Storing undamaged yams off the ground in a cool, shady, and airy barn keeps them fresh much longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ŋmɔ loo atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. aloo kɛji akɛ ato he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potatoes ni efiteee lɛ to shikpɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What must I do to my chili peppers so that buyers will purchase them for higher prices or export?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ afee aha chili ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ aná jara ni nɔ kwɔ loo amɛkɛya maŋsɛɛ?

english: High-paying buyers and exporters look for peppers that are uniform in size, bright in color, completely free of insect spots or chemical residues, and packed in clean containers to prevent damage during transport.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii babaoo kɛ mɛi ni kɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ taoɔ ŋmeii ni dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe, ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛo, ni ŋmeii loo tsofai ni eshwɛɛɛ amɛhe lɛ bɛ mli. ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsii ni mli tse amli koni akafite beni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Why do tree crops like cashew or cocoa bring in money at different times of the year compared to crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cashew nuts loo cocoa haa anáa shika yɛ afi lɛ mli bei srɔtoi amli kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Grains like maize grow and yield quickly within a few months of planting, while tree crops like cocoa or cashew take years to mature but then yield fruit every year during specific harvest seasons for decades.
ga: Ŋmãa, tamɔ ŋmãa, kwɛ̃ɔ ni ewoɔ yibii oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ. yɛ be mli ni tsei tamɔ kookoo loo cashew nuts Eheɔ afii babaoo dani ekwɛɔ. Mohu ɔ, e wo ngma daa jeha ngɛ ngma kpami be pɔtɛɛ ko mi jehahi babauu.

english: How do cowpeas help improve my soil naturally for the next planting season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ aha cowpea aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Cowpeas have small bumps on their roots containing friendly bacteria that pull nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into food for the plant. When the cowpea plant dies and decays, that nitrogen stays in the soil as free fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ bɔɔt bibii. Muawai ni yɔɔ naanyobɔɔ mli ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfeɔ lɛ tsei aniyenii lɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni tsina tsei lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I ask an extension officer to visit and inspect my farm regularly instead of just buying financial inputs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabi mi-extension officer lɛ ni ebasara miŋmɔ lɛ ni ekwɛ mli daa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni shika he nibii pɛ aheɔ lɛ

english: Regular farm monitoring by an expert helps catch pests, crop stress, and soil issues early, ensuring your crops grow healthy even if you already have funding.
ga: Nileelɔi ni baakwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ baaye abua ni amɔmɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli lɛ ahe haomɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ naagbai mra Ehaa onibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji oyɛ shika momo po.

english: Is heavy rainfall a sign that I should immediately start planting my crops anywhere on my land?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he fɛɛ he?

english: No, rain alone does not mean every plot is ready for planting; putting seeds in unsuited or poorly prepared soil during rains can drown roots or rot seeds.
ga: Jeee akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ kɛkɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui wo shikpɔŋ ni esaaa loo asaaa he jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi loo dumɔwui lɛ agbo.

english: Can I plant rice on any piece of land I own as long as the rainy season has started?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Te nɔ ni manyɛ maná? Shii abɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Rice requires specific low-lying or water-retaining land to thrive, so planting it on high or dry ground—even during heavy rains—will result in poor crop yield.
ga: Omɔ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi loo hei ni nu yɔɔ titri lɛ koni ekwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli po lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akawo jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and fail to grow well even when it rains heavily every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa daa gbi lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess rain on land without proper drainage chokes the plant roots of oxygen and washes away essential soil nutrients, causing crops to starve in wet soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: How does walking through my fields routinely help prevent my crops from failing?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nyiɛmɔ ni mifeɔ daa yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anaa koni ekafite?

english: Routine walk-throughs allow you to spot early signs of land degradation, insect attacks, or poor seed growth so you can correct them before losing the entire harvest.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ ni ooofee daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miifite, kooloi bibii loo dumɔwui ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ mra. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ osaa dani onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ afite.

english: Why does my soil dry out quickly and ruin my crops shortly after a big rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kpele ko sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Different soil types hold water differently; sandy or sloped land drains moisture too fast, leaving crop roots thirsty soon after the rain stops.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni shikpɔŋ henɔ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ toɔ nu ehaa. He ni ŋã yɔɔ loo he ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu oya tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa pɛ kɛkɛ ni kumai yeɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why is following step-by-step guidance from station officers better than just planting whenever the weather feels right?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooonyiɛ tsɔnedaamɔhe nitsulɔi lɛ agbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ he lɛ sɛɛ fe ni ooodu tsei beni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ hi lɛ?

english: Station officers base their advice on tested land and crop management strategies, protecting you from common mistakes like planting in unsuitable locations during unpredictable rains.
ga: Station nitsulɔi lɛ baawo ŋaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aka akwɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔtoo he. Ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ tɔmɔi ni afɔɔ feemɔ tamɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ hei ni esaaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli.

english: Why does my rice crop perform poorly when planted on dry ground during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rice roots need sustained moisture levels in the ground; dry land sheds water too fast, leaving the rice plants stunted even when rainfall is frequent.
ga: Omɔ shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yaa nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa nu hoɔ oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ shii abɔ moŋ.

english: What happens to my seeds if I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The first rain often wet only the top layer of soil; if a dry spell follows, the newly germinated seeds will dry up and die before deep soil moisture builds up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Kɛji hɔmɔ ba nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ buaa ehe naa.

english: How do I know if the land I occupy is actually good for the specific crop I want to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni miyɔɔ lɛ hi diɛŋtsɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni misumɔɔ ni madu lɛ?

english: Crops react differently to soil depth, slope, and water retention, so getting your land assessed before planting prevents wasted seeds and failed harvests.
ga: Tsei feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, ŋshɔ lɛ shishi kɛ nu ni amɛhiɔ mli lɛ he, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani odu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni dumɔwui ni elaaje kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni baaa lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the soil, so applying a nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting under the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and cannot drain away during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess water to run off, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni enyɛŋ ejɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and weak even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight from your crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting gives your crops full access to the soil's strength so they can grow thick stems and good yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ he. Koni ená tsei ni mli tse ni ewo yibii kpakpai

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers keep dropping off without producing any peppers during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper baaa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes stress to pepper plants, making them drop flowers to save water and energy. Watering early in the morning and using grass mulching around the base keeps the soil cool so the flowers stay on.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Dumɔ fɔfɔii koni okɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ akafite. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi kɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my tomatoes crack open right when they start turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ fãa trukaa kɛ́ ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they take in too much water all at once after a dry spell. The fruit inside swells faster than the skin can stretch, so keeping soil moisture steady with regular watering prevents cracking.
ga: Tomato baatswa kɛji enine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ shikome yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baafu oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛre. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni oooha ehi shi daa kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ baatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ naa.

english: The first rain is often a 'false rain' followed by a dry hot spell. If you plant immediately, the dry weather can scorch the young sprouts; waiting for continuous rains ensures your seeds have enough moisture to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji ‘amale nugbɔ’ ni hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii ashã. Nugbɔ ni yaa nɔ nɛɔ lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Planting plantain trees alongside your young cocoa provides temporary shade that protects the cocoa seedlings until they are old and tough enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do many of my cocoa flowers drop off the trunk without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny beneficial insects to pollinate them, and the tree needs adequate soil moisture. If insects are missing or the tree is thirsty, flowers drop; keeping some natural shade attracts pollinators and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli, ni tsei lɛ hu he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji kooloi bibii lɛ laaje loo kumai ye tso lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi Adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baagbala ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines to climb on wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maye mabua sweet potato wain tso ko ni ekwɔ tso ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines catch sunlight through their leaves to feed the tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground, allowing the vine to capture maximum sunlight and grow larger, healthier yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ naa hulu la kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa wain tsei lɛ náa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ agbo ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my plantain suckers dry out and turn brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Old bottom leaves naturally die as the plant channels food to new leaves at the top. However, if leaves dry too quickly, it may be a sign of leaf spot disease or low water, so cutting off dead leaves helps maintain plant health.
ga: Baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ gboiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe beni tso lɛ kɛ niyenii yaa baa heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ gĩ oya tsɔ lɛ, Ebaanyɛ efee baai lɛ ahe hela loo nu ni bɛ lɛ he okadi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afo baai ni egboi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize is missing nitrogen because heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the soil where roots cannot reach, or standing water is drowning the root system.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ lɛ. Aloo nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they face extreme stress, usually from high temperatures, irregular watering, or using too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes the plant produce leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔ ni naa wa kpe. Bei pii lɛ, ejɛɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo, ni haa tsei lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies, or it can be the plant's natural reaction to extreme heat and dry conditions to save water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Aloo ebaanyɛ efee bɔ ni tso ko feɔ enii ehaa yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli koni ekɛbu nu he.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops very close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same water and nutrients in the soil, and their leaves block sunlight from each other, leading to weak plants and small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot handle full sunlight; they need shade trees to protect them from intense solar heat and to keep the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do weeds stop my crops from growing big even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miitsi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are stronger than crops, so they quickly steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops before the crops get a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ oya dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why are my yams growing short, twisted, and small instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ kuku, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ bibioo moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose, and deep soil to push downward easily; hard or stony soil blocks their natural growth, resulting in misshapen tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya shi oya. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi tsiɔ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ naa. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ejaaa.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature enough to dig up for market?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ aya jara nɔ?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves yellow and fall off, the soil near the stem cracks, or around 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli egbɛ eshwa. Aloo aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ, ni enɛ damɔ tso lɛ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ.

english: How should I change my crop watering schedule during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ matsake be ni mikɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yɛ harmath be ni mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: Dry harmattan winds strip moisture from soil rapidly, so crops need extra watering early in the morning and late in the evening to keep roots cool and hydrated.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu babaoo leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my harvested plantains turn soft and yellow so fast before I can get them to buyers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ oya dani eshɛɔ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains produce a natural ripening gas called ethylene after harvest, and exposure to sunlight or tight, warm storage speeds up this gas, causing them to spoil quickly.
ga: Plantains jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa mɔ shwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Ni hulu la loo he ko ni mli edɔ ni mli wa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baaha gas nɛɛ aya oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: Should I only plant food crops that my family eats, or is it better to clear land for cash crops like cocoa?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu niyenii ni miweku lɛ yeɔ lɛ pɛ? Aloo esa akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni akɛduɔ shika tamɔ kookoo?

english: Combining both is best for farm stability; growing staple food crops like cassava and maize ensures food security for your household, while cash crops provide dedicated income to pay for school fees, health needs, and farm supplies.
ga: Enyɔ lɛ ni akɛaafee ekome lɛ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔ mli shifimɔ. Niyenii nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe baa oshia lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni shika ni aduɔ lɛ haa shika pɛ ni akɛwoɔ skul nyɔmɔ. hewalɛnamɔ he hiamɔ nii kɛ okwaayeli he nibii

english: Is it a good idea for me to plant pepper and cassava on the same farm plot at the same time?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ abaadu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, intercropping pepper with cassava works very well because pepper grows fast and can be harvested in a few months before the cassava grows tall and creates too much shade.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli dani ŋmeii lɛ adara tsɔ ni ekɛ hulutsoo babaoo aba.

english: Why do my tomatoes die from rot during the heavy rainy season while my cocoyam grows very well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi gboiɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-kookoo lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa?

english: Tomatoes are sensitive to excessive leaf moisture and suffer from fungal diseases in wet weather, whereas cocoyam naturally thrives in damp soil and heavy rain conditions.
ga: Tomato nuɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ he waa, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ yeɔ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my land is better suited for planting cassava or planting swamp rice?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cassava needs well-drained, loose soil on upland ground because wet soil rots its roots, while rice needs low-lying areas or valley bottoms that naturally hold water for long periods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia cassava yɛ gɔŋji amli hei ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Omɔ he miihia shikpɔŋ kplanaa loo jɔɔ lɛ shishi ni baanyɛ ahi nu mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my soil nutrients seem to disappear completely after I harvest yam from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni niyenii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ kwraa beni mikpa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are heavy feeders that consume high amounts of nitrogen and potassium to grow large tubers, which is why land used for yam needs resting or nutrient-restoring crops like beans afterwards.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji niyenii ni tsii ni amɛkɛ nitrogen kɛ potassium babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛdu ŋmeii wuji. Enɛ hewɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ sweet potato lɛ damɔ hejɔɔmɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni aku sɛɛ akɛba lɛ nɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Do I need to burn all the grass and cleared bush on my land before I plant my beans?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mashã jwɛi kɛ brɔshi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani madu ŋmeii?

english: Burning clears the land quickly but destroys beneficial soil organisms and natural fertilizer; leaving cleared vegetation to decay on top of the soil helps retain moisture and enriches the earth.
ga: Shãa haa sũ lɛ mli tseɔ oya shi efiteɔ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei ni egboi lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa.

english: Why do my crops yield less food every year when I plant maize on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil drains the exact same nutrients every season and allows maize pests to build up; rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ daa be mli, ni ehaa abɛi mli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce smaller tubers every time I re-use stems from my previous year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii be fɛɛ be ni akɛ ŋmeii ni jɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Re-using old stem cuttings year after year can pass hidden viral diseases down to new plants, whereas getting fresh, disease-free stems gives you healthier plants and larger yields.
ga: Niji momo ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ baanyɛ agbala helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amli kɛya tsei heei anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ oyɛ tsei niji heei ni hela bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oná hewalɛ ni owo yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant my seeds very close together just to fit more crops on my small farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants with very low yields instead of healthy, high-yielding crops.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei komɛi woɔ yibii fioo kwraa. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ woɔ yiblii babauu nɛ e ngɛ he wami.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my rain-fed maize in southern Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ?

english: You should plant after the major rainy season has fully established, usually around April, so the seeds receive consistent moisture needed for germination and early root growth.
ga: Esa akɛ odu lɛ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ eje shishi lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee April. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya kɛ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my crop plants yield less when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight over the same soil nutrients and water, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough light, water, and food to grow strong and produce a healthy harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow big leafy branches but small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai wuji shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen or is too hard, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below. Soft soil with balanced nutrients encourages the cassava to grow larger roots.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ wa tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni ja yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei ni shishifãi wuji daa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and grow stems. Adding the right fertilizer helps the plant regain its bright green color and build strong ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ amɛ eŋɔli kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa amɛsu ni mli tse kɛ amɛtoi ni wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need shade trees planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu tso ko ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under the hot, direct sun. Shade plants like plantains or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and retaining soil moisture until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei tamɔ tsei bibii loo shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli shade. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa.

english: In hot afternoon weather, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. They temporarily droop to save moisture, but they usually bounce back once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaatsi amɛhe be kukuoo ko koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Shi amɛfɔɔ sɛɛkuu be mli ni gbɛkɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet and shady conditions. Pruning excess branches and clearing weeds allows air and light to dry the pods, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ojie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi. ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences water stress. Without constant soil moisture and moderate temperatures, the flowers drop instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni sa bɛ be fɛɛ be. Fɔfɔi baagbee shi yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: How do chemical sprays protect my crops from insect attacks?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Crop protection chemicals work either by killing insects when they touch the plant or by absorbing into the plant's leaves so that any bug taking a bite gets stopped before it destroys the crop.
ga: Tsofai ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni amɛgbeɔ kɛji amɛkɛ tsei kpe lɛ nɔ loo kɛtsɔ amɛ ni amɛwoɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli koni amɛkpa kooloi ni ŋmɔɔ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my farm crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to survive tough conditions, so they absorb rain and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing vital resources from your plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nibii ni he hiaa yɛ otsei lɛ amli.

english: Why does planting beans alongside my maize help my soil stay fertile?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural plant food in the ground. This feeds neighboring crops like maize and keeps the soil healthy for future seasons.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ aye niyenii ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: If I mix fertilizer with water to feed my vegetables and have some left over at the end of the day, can I keep it to use next week?
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu nu mli koni aduawai lɛ aná nɔ ni fa fe nine ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii yɛ gbi lɛ naagbee Ani manyɛ makɛto kɛha otsi ni baa lɛ?

english: No, mixed liquid fertilizer loses its nutrients quickly and can spoil or harm plants if left to sit. It is best to use all of it immediately on other hungry crops or pour it onto your compost pile so the food does not go to waste.
ga: Dabi, nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya, ni kɛ́ akwɛɛɛ tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite loo eye amɛ awui. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛbaatsu nii shikome yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Aloo shwiemɔ awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ mli koni niyenii akafite.

english: I have some maize seeds left over after planting my field. How can I keep them so they do not get ruined before the next rainy season?
ga: Miyɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi ni eshwɛ beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ. Te abaafee tɛŋŋ abu he koni ekafite dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba?

english: Dry the seeds thoroughly in the sun and store them in an airtight container mixed with clean wood ash or safe storage powder. Keep the container in a cool, dry room to protect the seeds from moisture and weevils.
ga: Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni akɛ tso sũ ni he tse loo powda ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe efutu mli. Kɛ tsɛnsi lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi koni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii ahe.

english: Can I use dry cocoa husks and crop remains to feed my soil instead of burning them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ?

english: Yes, burning crop leftovers wastes valuable soil food. If you leave crop remains to rot on the farm or turn them into compost, they break down into rich natural food that keeps the soil moist and reduces the amount of fertilizer you need to buy.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jara wa. Kɛji oha ŋmɔshi nibii fite yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli loo otsake amɛ ofee ŋmɔshi nibii. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni fa babaoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni esa akɛ ohe lɛ baa shi.

english: If I have leftover chicken manure after feeding my yam farm, can I put it directly around my young tomato seedlings?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ miyɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ beni mikwɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ hu? Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei awo tomato dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure is very strong and will burn the tender roots of young tomatoes. You should heap the leftover manure with dry leaves and let it rot into dark compost before feeding it to your tomatoes.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa waa ni ebaashã tomato bibii lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ ato baai ni egboi ahe ni oha egbo ni etsɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli dani okɛfata o-tomato lɛ he.

english: What should I do with the small amount of chemical spray left in my knapsack sprayer after treating my cabbage farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ tsofa fioo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ misɛɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli beni mikwɛ mi-cabbage ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Never pour chemical leftovers into streams or near water sources. Dilute the leftover liquid with extra water and spray it on the outer edges of the farm away from food crops so it breaks down safely without wasting or polluting the environment.
ga: Kaawo tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ amli yɛ faai amli loo he ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhei. Okɛ nu kroko awo nu ni eshwɛ lɛ mli. ni okɛshwie ŋmɔ lɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akabɔ he. Koni efite shweshweeshwe ni efiteee loo ekɛ shihilɛ mli mujiwoo baaa.

english: Why do I need to give my maize farm different types of fertilizer when it is young compared to when it is about to show flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi beni eji gbekɛ kɛ be mli ni ebɛŋkɛ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Crops need different food at different growth stages. Young maize needs nitrogen to build strong roots and green leaves, but when it starts flowering, it needs phosphorus and potassium to form big, heavy corn ears.
ga: Tsei biɔ niyenii srɔtoi yɛ amɛdalɛ mli fãi srɔtoi amli. Nitrogen he miihia abifao koni ená shishifãi ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Shi kɛ́ ebɔi fɔfɔi lɛ Ehe miihia ni ekɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium afee ŋmãa toi agboi ni tsii.

english: Is it bad if I apply all the fertilizer for my tomato plants at once on the day I plant them?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɛɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be kome mli yɛ gbi ni midu amɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, giving all the food at once can burn the young roots, and heavy rains will wash most of it away before the plant can use it. It is better to split the food into two or three small meals as the plants grow.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, niyenii fɛɛ ni ayeɔ shikome lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi bibii. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shishifãi lɛ ateŋ babaoo kɛyaa dani tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkɛtsuɔ nii. Esa akɛ aja niyenii lɛ mli awo niyenii bibii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Be ni tsei lɛ daraa

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the cassava plant is hungry for nitrogen food or is suffering from dry soil. Adding well-rotted manure or compost around the base will give the plant the nutrients it needs to produce green leaves again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye yucca tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi miipiŋ. Nibii ni egbo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants roll their leaves to conserve water and protect themselves from scorching heat. If the leaves bounce back and stand straight in the cool evening, the crop is fine, but if they remain limp, the plants need water.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ, shi kɛji amɛtee nɔ amɛgbɔjɔ lɛ, nu he miihia Tsei hu.

english: My cocoa seedlings are not growing taller even though I water them regularly. What is wrong with them?
ga: Mi-cocoa tso lɛ edaaa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa moŋ. Mɛni ba a nɔ?

english: Water alone is not enough food for growing seedlings. They need nutrients from rich topsoil or compost, and they also need partial shade from plantain trees so the harsh sun does not stunt their growth.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa kɛha dumɔwui ni akwɛ̃ɔ. Niyenii nibii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo mli lɛ he miihia amɛ. Ehe miihia hu ni ená hulutsoo fioo kɛjɛ plantain lɛ mli. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akatsĩ dalɛ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmã tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, a key nutrient maize needs to stay green and grow strong cobs. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele, ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri lɛ he miihia koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why do people say I shouldn't apply chemical fertilizer when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi miikɛɛ akɛ esaaa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve properly so roots can absorb it safely. Applying concentrated fertilizer to dry soil will burn and damage the plant's roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ewo muji tsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, eshãa ni efiteɔ tsei shishifãi moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or beans on my field before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are special crops that naturally grab nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When you plant maize after them, the maize uses that stored nitrogen to grow taller and yield more without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa kɛ nitrogen ni ato lɛ baatsu nii ni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo ni ŋmãa ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and thin bark that burn easily in direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted next to them to block the harsh heat and keep the surrounding air cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ amɛhewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ tsiɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when strong winds and rain come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and very heavy tops, especially when bearing fruit bunches. Supporting them with strong wooden props or mounding soil around the base helps anchor them against heavy winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii waa. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ aduawai lɛ yɛ tso yibii amli. Kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ loo muji ni abua naa ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afi amɛsɛɛ. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni emɔ amɛ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why am I seeing small ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes inside the growing center of young maize are a classic sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide deep inside the leaves to eat the softest parts of the plant, requiring early inspection and targeted spraying or ash treatment to control.
ga: Bu ko ni etse ehe yɛ ŋmãa bibii ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmãa lɛ he okadi ni ale waa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ akwɛ enɛ mli mra. ni akudɔ sũ ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo ajieɔ lɛ yɛ bɔ ni akɛmamɔ shi lɛ naa.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava bushes curl up and turn yellowish-green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Curled and distorted cassava leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant stem cuttings from the agriculture officer prevents this virus from taking over your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baa ni ebɔle ehe ni efite lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ okwaayeli nitsulɔi aŋɔ ŋmeii ni nyɛɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akaŋɔ onibii lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops must fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every single plant enough space and food to grow thick stalks and big fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Esa akɛ Dumɔwui lɛ atswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing huge bushy leaves above ground but giving me very small tubers beneath the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen or too little potassium, cassava spends all its energy producing leaves instead of roots. Excessive shade or very compacted soil also prevents tubers from swelling properly.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo potassium fioo tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa baai yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Shade ni fa fe nine loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa hu tsiɔ bulbs lɛ anaa koni ekafu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, lack of water, or poor nutrients. Regular watering at the root level and mulching the soil helps keep the roots cool and saves the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni esaaa ni amɛyeɔ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafitemɔ.

english: Why should I turn my harvested cassava into gari instead of just selling the fresh tubers from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ Gari ato ŋmei ni akpa lɛ najiaŋ moŋ fe ni mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fresh cassava tubers spoil within two to three days after harvest, forcing you to accept low prices from buyers. Processing cassava into gari removes the water, allowing you to store the product for months and sell it when market prices are higher.
ga: Cassava shishifãi heei lɛ baafite yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ okpɛlɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ kɛjɛ hɔlɔlɔ lɛ dɛŋ. Kɛ́ afee cassava ni afee lɛ gari lɛ, ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ mli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nibii toɔ nyɔji babaoo ni ohɔ̃ɔ kɛji jara lɛ tee hiɛ.

english: What is the thick starch liquid left behind when I squeeze cassava dough, and how can I use it?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashɛre tapioka ashikiŋsha lɛ Tapioka ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa lɛ Mɛni baashwɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, te abaafee tɛŋŋ akɛtsu nii?

english: That thick liquid settles into pure cassava starch (often called agolima). Instead of throwing it away, you can collect and dry it to sell separately for baking or laundry starch, creating extra income from your harvest.
ga: Nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ tapioca ŋmɔtɔ krɔŋŋ. (bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ agolima) yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshɛrɛ lɛ Obaanyɛ obua amɛnaa ni ogbi ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ srɔtoi kɛha ŋmɔtɔ loo atadei ahe ashikishaŋ. Na shika kroko kɛjɛ okpamɔ lɛ mli.

english: Can I make more money if I process part of my cassava harvest and sell part of it fresh?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná shika babaoo? Kɛji mikɛ ŋmei ko tsu nii ni mihɔ̃ɔ ŋmei hee ko,

english: Yes, combining both methods reduces your risk. Selling some fresh cassava provides immediate cash to pay laborers, while processing the rest into gari or starch protects your remaining crop from rotting and gives you a higher long-term profit.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛi enyɔ lɛ ni okɛaafee ekome lɛ haa oshara ni yɔɔ ohe lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ ahɔ̃ɔ ŋmei hee lɛ eko lɛ, ebaaha aná shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni awo nitsulɔi lɛ nyɔmɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ooofee lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ lɛ baabu onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite, ni ebaaha oná sɛɛnamɔi babaoo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How can I estimate how many 50-kilogram bags of cassava my land will produce before harvesting everything?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmeii 50 kg enyiɛ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ baawo lɛ he akɔntaa dani akpa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: You can estimate your total yield by harvesting a few random cassava stands, weighing their tubers, and multiplying that average weight by the total number of stands planted on your field.
ga: Obaanyɛ osusu yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei fioo komɛi ni ooohala trukaa ni okɛ ŋmeii lɛ asusu he lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ nakai shwiili lɛ mlijaa mlijaa lɛ ato ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ ayibɔ he.

english: Why is it better to sell my cassava crop by weight in kilograms rather than by filling traditional market baskets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaahɔ̃ɔ ŋmei yɛ kilogram mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahɔ̃ɔ amɛ yɛ tsɛnsii ni eyi obɔ mli yɛ kusum jarayeli hei lɛ?

english: Market baskets can vary in size, and buyers often push down fresh cassava to fit more than you are paid for. Weighing tubers in kilograms gives an exact measurement, ensuring you receive a fair price for the actual weight you produced.
ga: Jarayeli tsɛnsii lɛ baanyɛ afee srɔtoi. Ni bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ tsiɔ ŋmei hee kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ ŋmei babaoo ni onine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ akpã gbee. Kɛ́ akɛ yitso lɛ tsiimɔ wo kilogram mli lɛ, ebaaha aná susumɔ ni ja. Enɛ haa onine shɛɔ jara ni sa nɔ kɛha shwiili diɛŋtsɛ ni ofeɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my cassava tubers are big enough to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Look at the soil around the base of the plant stem; if you see cracking on the ground surface, it usually means the expanding tubers underneath are swelling and reaching maturity.
ga: Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he kɛji ona ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, tsɔne ni mli elɛɛ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baafu ni ebaada.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with large leafy stems but yield small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Ani eyɛ tso agbo ni baai yɔɔ mli shi eyɛ yitso bibioo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil or excess shade causes the plant to put all its energy into growing top leaves and stems instead of transferring food down into the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo hulutsoo babaoo haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida kɛ ŋwɛi tsei lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛya shi kɛya yitso lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Why does cassava turn dark brown or black inside just a few days after I dig it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava roots are cut from the stem, exposure to air triggers natural deterioration. To prevent this discoloration, leave tubers buried in soil until you are ready to process or eat them within 48 hours.
ga: Beni afoɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli nibii afite. Bɔni afee ni akatsake amɛhe Shimɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaatsu he nii loo oye amɛ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli.

english: Why does gari made from some cassava varieties feel crisp and heavy, while gari from other varieties turns out light and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni Gari ni jɛ ŋmei srɔtoi krokomɛi amli lɛ mli lɛɛ lɛ, eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ blɛoo?

english: Cassava varieties differ in starch and water content. Varieties rich in starch yield heavy, crisp gari, whereas high-moisture varieties lose most of their weight as liquid during squeezing, resulting in lighter yields.
ga: Cassava henɔi lɛ yɛ starch kɛ nu falɛ srɔtoi. Starch henɔi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ yibii ni tsii ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ, amɛhewalɛ babaoo baa shi yɛ nu mli yɛ be mli ni amɛmiimiɔ amɛmli lɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Does planting cassava stem cuttings slanted into the ground produce better tubers than planting them horizontally?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni hi fe ŋmeii ni adu yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ aba?

english: Slanted planting makes tubers cluster in one direction, making manual digging easier, while horizontal planting produces tubers all along the stem buried in the ground, which can yield more total tubers but requires deeper digging.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa bulb lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ akɛ nine baatsu nii yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ shishi fɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha oná yitsei babaoo shi ebiɔ ni otsa mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed to build green tissue and grow strong. It can also happen when soil becomes waterlogged, preventing roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli fãji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with huge leaves, but the roots underground stay small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo?

english: When soil has excess nitrogen or when plants receive too much shade, cassava directs its energy into growing top stems and leaves rather than storing energy in underground starch tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ náa hulutsoo babaoo. Yucca kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli lɛ

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the branch before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly during rainy periods when moisture stays trapped on pods due to high humidity and poor air circulation.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Fɛ̃i ŋmɛɔ pods lɛ amli yɛ fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into tight rolls and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically triggered by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites hiding under leaves, or by viruses transmitted by insects that disrupt normal plant tissue growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni tsiɔ tsei amli fãji lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara bɔ ni sa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my yam leaves turning brown and drying up months before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi nyɔji komɛi dani akpamɔ lɛ?

english: Premature leaf drying in yam is usually caused by a fungal leaf disease called anthracnose or severe water stress, which stops the leaves from producing food for the underground tuber.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose loo nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ afee niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers drying up and falling off the stem instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or poor pollination, causing the plant to abort fruit production to survive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo pollination ni ehiii Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kpaɔ yibii koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my fruiting plantain trees fall over so easily even during light wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni waaa po mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are frequently weakened underground by pests like nematodes or stem borers, destroying the anchor system needed to support heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ haa plantain shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ fiteɔ ŋshɔŋloo gbɛjianɔtoo ni he hiaa koni akɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops yield much smaller cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Overcrowded crops compete aggressively with each other for limited sunlight, soil moisture, and nutrients, leaving each plant with fewer resources to produce large cobs.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la he akaŋ waa. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náaa nibii fioo ni ekɛbaawo ŋmɔtɔ wuji.

english: Why should I wait for the rains to settle properly before sowing my seeds into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Seeds require continuous soil moisture to germinate and build initial roots; planting during unpredictable early rains leaves seeds vulnerable to drying out and dying in hot soil.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa shikpɔŋ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishijee shishifãi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ oshara mli akɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young crops grow so slowly when weeds are left uncleaned around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ he tseee lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that consume soil nutrients and water much faster than young crops, effectively starving the crops of the resources needed for growth.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ oya ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii oya fe tsei bibii. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara lɛ jeɔ amɛdɛŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains near my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide essential shade and moisture to protect young cocoa plants during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni akɛbu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is a key food plant needs to grow strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Does it matter which direction I insert cassava cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei niji lɛ awo?

english: Yes, planting cassava cuttings upside down prevents them from growing properly. The small buds on the stem must always point upwards toward the sky so roots and stems can grow out correctly.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ haaa amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I have to construct raised mounds of soil before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow big underground, so loose raised mounds make it easy for tubers to expand smoothly. Mounds also prevent water from pooling around the roots, which stops the tubers from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, gɔŋ ni awó nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ jogbaŋŋ. Gɔŋ lɛ hu tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa bulb lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too hot or when the soil dries out completely. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing light shade during extreme heat helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas between my rows of maize help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds the maize crop and improves soil fertility without needing extra expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmãa babaoo ni tsofai ni jara wa babaoo he ehiaaa.

english: Why should I avoid spreading my fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away loose fertilizer from your field before plant roots can soak it up. It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is already moist after a light rain so it sinks gently into the root zone.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe lɛ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. koni shikpɔŋ lɛ atsɔ fiofio kɛbote shishifãi lɛ amli

english: Why are tiny caterpillars destroying the deep inner leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni mikɛfite mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are fall armyworms, a common pest that hides deep inside the growing center of corn plants. Dropping safe ash, neem oil, or recommended control agents into the central funnel stops them from destroying the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji cutworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Sũ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, neem fɔ, loo nɔ ko ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛyeɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ baatsi enaa koni ekafite tso lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my pepper seeds close together in the main garden field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ pepper dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ abɔɔ wulu lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded together, they struggle against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leading to weak stems and small fruits. Proper spacing gives each plant room to grow big fruits and reduces plant diseases.
ga: Kɛji abua pepper tsei anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni ehaa tsei ahe helai baa shi.

english: Why do weeds cause my young crops to grow so slowly if I leave them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients your plants need. Clearing weeds early leaves all the soil nourishment for your crops to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ niyenii bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow even after I water them from my new borehole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu shwieɔ amɛ nu kɛjɛɔ nubu hee mli moŋ?

english: Borehole water can sometimes contain high levels of salts or harsh minerals like iron that damage plant roots. Overwatering with mineral-heavy underground water can also suffocate the roots, preventing them from absorbing necessary nutrients.
ga: Bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmeii loo nibii ni mli wa, tamɔ dade baanyɛ ahi nu ni akɛwoɔ nubu mli lɛ mli babaoo. ni baanyɛ akpata tsei ashishifãi ahiɛ Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ minerals wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ, ni enɛ haaa amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Can I use underground well water that tastes salty to irrigate my tomato farm?
