ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli edɔ awo mi-tomato ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu?

english: Using salty underground water directly can harm your tomatoes. Salt builds up in the soil over time, making it hard for roots to absorb moisture, which leads to leaf burning, stunted growth, and poor fruit yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli edɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye tomato awui. Nuŋ buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai shãa dalɛ stalls kɛ aduawai ni ehiii

english: Why do my maize plants turn pale yellow and stay small during the early rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ bibioo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Pale yellow and stunted maize usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Heavy early rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil beyond the reach of young roots, leaving the crop hungry for nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Leebi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my okra plants grow very tall with big leaves but produce almost no pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing lush stems and leaves instead of flowers and pods. Switching to a balanced fertilizer encourages the plant to set fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ma tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants roll up and shed during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during long dry spells to conserve water and protect itself from drought. Once regular rains return, the plant will sprout new leaves and resume growth.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ daa Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without turning into small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant experiences high heat, irregular watering, or severe dry spells. The plant naturally sheds its flowers to survive when environmental conditions are too harsh to support fruit growth.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ daa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa leaves curl up and burn when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight or strong dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa trees until their root systems grow strong enough to handle heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu hulutsoo lɛ he nii.

english: Why are my plantain suckers taking a very long time to shoot out leaves after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani etswaa baai beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need warm, loose, and moist soil to wake up and sprout. Planting them too deep or in hard, compacted soil delays root development and keeps new shoots from breaking through.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni etse, ni efɔ koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaatsi ŋmeii heei ni baa lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo mli.

english: Why do my yam leaves get dark spots and die off before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Dark spots on yam leaves are typically caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose, which thrives in warm, humid weather. This damages the leaves and prevents the yam tuber underground from swelling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. Amɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i mli. Enɛ baafite baai lɛ ni ebaatsi sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafuu.

english: Why are my garden egg fruits coming out tiny and bitter instead of plump and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Garden eggs become small and bitter when the plant experiences water shortages or lacks essential soil nutrients like potassium during fruit formation. Regular watering and good organic manure prevent this.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ tsei lɛ na nu ni faaa loo amɛnáaa sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium, yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why are the young leaves on my cocoa seedlings turning yellow and dry at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct sunlight and wind. Without shade plants like plantains or shade trees to cover them, full sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the soil, turning the leaves yellow and crisp.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo hulutsoo tsei bɛ lɛ, Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Is it good for my farm if I plant beans in the same rows as my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛji midu ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize benefits both crops. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil to nourish the maize, while the tall maize stalks give climbing beans support to grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Beans mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni kwɔɔ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why am I seeing small ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny worms hiding inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Ayɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ. Akɛtee baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds inside the leaf funnel of young maize plants. The caterpillar hides deep inside the plant shoot during the day to protect itself while eating the soft leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ tsei ashishifãi amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛbu amɛhe he be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my yam leaves and vines develop dark black spots and dry up quickly during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potatoes kɛ wain tsei lɛ anɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is a fungal disease called anthracnose. High humidity and splashing rain help the fungus spread rapidly from leaf to leaf across the field, causing the vine to dry up early.
ga: Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose. Fɛ̃i ni mli wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ baa kome nɔ kɛyaa baa kroko nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Ehaa wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya

english: Why do my maize plants remain short and pale green even when the rains are good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ kuku lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ moŋ?

english: Pale green leaves and stunted growth usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Rain helps the plant absorb food, but if nitrogen is missing from the soil, the crop cannot build strong stems or green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii. Shi kɛji nitrogen lɛ laaje kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni adu lɛ hu nyɛŋ afee ŋmeii ni wa loo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: What will happen to my pepper plants if I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Crowded pepper plants compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Poor airflow between closely planted crops also creates a damp atmosphere where fungal diseases easily spread.
ga: Pepper tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni hoɔ yɛ tsei ni adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ lɛ hu haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or heavy rainfall. High heat or water stress prevents proper pollination, causing the flower stem to weaken and fall off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nugbɔ nɛ waa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu mli haomɔ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Ehaa fɔfɔii ahe tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Mature cassava plants show visible signs like lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, stems thickening, and cracks appearing in the soil around the base of the stem where the tubers are expanding.
ga: Cassava tsei ni eda lɛ baajie okadii ni anaa tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi, kɛ ŋmeii ni jeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi he ni ŋmeii lɛ egbɛ eshwã lɛ mli.

english: Why did many of the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest fail to sprout after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their ability to sprout if stored in warm, damp places or if attacked by insects like weevils. Moisture causes seeds to mold or age rapidly, which kills the living embryo inside.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ aha amɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii tutua amɛ. Fɛ̃i haa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ loo amɛdaraa oya. ni gbeɔ fɔmɔ kotoku ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ emli lɛ

english: Why do weeds slow down my crop growth so much when the plants are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ waa yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Young crop sprouts have small leaves and shallow roots. Weeds grow rapidly and steal sunlight, moisture, and soil nutrients before the young crop roots are established enough to compete.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli dani shishifãi bibii lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye akaŋ.

english: How can I protect my farm crops from grasscutters that keep coming to eat them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe kɛjɛ jwɛi ŋmɔlɔi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe?

english: Grasscutters are attracted to soft stems like cassava, sugar cane, and young maize. You can reduce their damage by clearing the tall weeds surrounding your farm to remove their hiding places, setting up physical wire mesh barriers around vulnerable plots, or planting border crops that deter them.
ga: Mɛi ni shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ sumɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ ŋmei bibii. Obaanyɛ oha nɔ ni efite lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. Famɔ onɔ̃ lɛ koni ojie amɛhe ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Kɛ waya mesh gbɛtsii nii awo shikpɔji ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ ahe. loo adu husu tsei ni tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes in the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides inside the growing tip of maize plants. You can manage them by inspecting leaves early, dropping a small handful of dry clean ash or sand into the central leaf funnel, or using recommended organic or chemical sprays before they cause severe damage.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni oookwɛ mra lɛ nɔ. Okɛ sũ ni egbi loo ŋã fioo ko awo funnel ni yɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli. Aloo okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite nii waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees curling up and turning brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight and high heat on their own. They dry out quickly because their roots are not yet deep enough, which is why planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Amɛgbiɔ oya ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ.

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tip and moving down the central vein is a clear sign that your soil lacks nitrogen. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure near the base of the plant will help restore the green color and boost plant growth.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naagbee ni etsɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo shishitoo lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and drop their leaves when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebaa lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants hate standing water around their roots. Excessive water drowns the roots by cutting off oxygen, leading to root rot, which makes the plant wilt as if it lacks water; planting on raised soil ridges helps rainwater drain away.
ga: Pepper tsei sumɔɔɔ nu ni damɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu babaoo baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baafo mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ tamɔ nɔ ni nu etã emli. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Is it beneficial to plant cowpeas in the same plot together with my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaadu cowpea yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize improves your soil naturally. Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds the neighboring maize plants and reduces your need for expensive fertilizers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa du tsina ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii, ni ehaa ŋmãa ni jara wa he hiaa lɛ baa shi

english: What will happen if I plant my plantain suckers too close to one another?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When plantains are overcrowded, their broad leaves block sunlight from reaching each other, and their roots compete heavily for soil nutrients and water. This results in thin stems, delayed fruiting, and very small bunches.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei bibii, yibiiwoo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ kui bibii waa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves look twisted with yellow patches, and why are the roots growing small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni mɛni hewɔ shishifãi lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ?

english: This leaf twisting is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, spread by tiny whitefly insects and infected planting stems. You can solve this by removing infected plants immediately and planting stem cuttings from disease-resistant cassava varieties.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa. kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Obaanyɛ osaa enɛ kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. kɛ tsei ni afolɔ kɛjɛ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ amli.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely, or if there is excessive nitrogen fertilizer causing leaves to grow instead of fruits. Regular morning watering and balanced nutrients help hold the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli ni haa baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa leebi kɛ niyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my yams under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii?

english: Yams are ready for full harvest when the green leaves and vines above the ground naturally turn yellow and dry up. This signal means the plant has finished transferring all its food energy down into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni yeɔ emuu beni baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwoɔ bulb lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: When my crops suddenly dry up and die, how do I know if it is a real plant disease or if someone cast a spiritual spell on my farm?
ga: Kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩ trukaa ni amɛgboi Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso hela ji lɛ diɛŋtsɛ loo mɔ ko etswa miŋmɔ lɛ he shɛɛ sane?

english: Crop failure is caused by biological diseases (like fungi, bacteria, or viruses), pest attacks, or lack of nutrients in the soil, not spiritual spells. Looking closely at leaves, stems, and roots for insects, spots, or rot helps identify the physical cause so it can be treated with proper farming practices or spraying.
ga: Helai ni wala yɔɔ mli (tamɔ ŋmei, muawai, loo muawai), tsɛŋemɔ helai, loo niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ tsei fitemɔ baa. Jeee mumɔŋ shɛɛ sane ni. Kɛ́ okwɛ kooloi bibii, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai, tsei ahe, kɛ shishifãi anɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ana nɔ ni kɛ hela lɛ baa yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ bɔni afee ni anyɛ atsa kɛtsɔ okwaayeli loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing water in extreme heat, or because tiny insects like whiteflies have infected them with a virus. Watering early in the day and managing insects keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ emɔ hela nɛɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli mra kɛ kooloi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: I noticed small holes in my young maize leaves and saw dark dirt inside the stems. What is causing this?
ga: Miyɔse bu bibioo ko. yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ ni abaanyɛ ana muji ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli Mɛni kɛ enɛ ba?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center of the maize plant to eat the fresh leaves. Checking your farm regularly allows you to catch and spray them before they ruin your harvest.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ koni amɛye baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ omɔɔ ni okɛ tsofa shwieɔ nɔ dani efiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with lots of leaves, but the tubers underground remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or foliage growth isn't managed, cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of underground roots. Cassava needs balanced soil nutrients, especially potassium, to form thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia Cassava. titri lɛ potassium koni ekɛfee yitso ni mli tse ni tsii

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but most of them drop off without forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee kookoo ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers they cannot feed, but severe heat, lack of soil moisture, or poor shade cause them to shed even more. Maintaining good shade trees and soil moisture helps flowers mature into pods.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye. Shi dɔlɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo hulutsoo ni ehiii lɛ haa amɛshwieɔ babaoo. Tso lɛ ni oooha ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why is it important for me to keep records of planting dates and when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋma gbii ni adu kɛ be ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he saji awo wolo nɔ lɛ?

english: Keeping written records helps you track when your crops need fertilizer or water, prevents you from spraying chemical treatments too late, and shows whether your farm made a profit or loss at harvest time.
ga: Nibii ni aŋmala ashwie shi ni oooŋmala lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ be ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu he hiaa bo. Etsiɔ bo gbɛ ni okɛ tsofai akashwie shi blɛoo tsɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ ná sɛɛnamɔ loo efite nii yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small farm plot?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani minɔ ni?

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin plants and small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant room to grow strong and yield more harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsũ fɛɛ tsũ ni daa lɛ mli hewalɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their crop roots with dry grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmeii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or organic matter (mulching) keeps the ground cool, traps moisture so you water less, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli (mulching) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to multiply in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ tso lɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa helai lɛ asɛɛkuu.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable farm in the bright afternoon heat or early in the morning?
ga: Okɛ nu awo aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli shwane mli. Aloo ani leebi hi fe no?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the roots to soak up water before the sun gets too hot, stopping the water from evaporating quickly into the air.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily dry out and burn under full sunlight. Fast-growing shade plants like plantains act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: How close together should I plant my young cocoa seedlings in the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mabɛŋkɛ tɛŋŋ?

english: Spacing cocoa trees about 3 meters apart ensures they have enough room for their roots to gather soil nutrients and their leaves to catch sunlight without crowding and competing with each other.
ga: Aaafee mitai 3 ni kã kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ abua niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni baai lɛ hu aná hulu la ni amɛfeee ekome ni amɛfeee akaŋshii.

english: Why do small white sticky bugs appear on my cocoa stems and attract so many ants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ No hewɔ lɛ ejie ehe kpo yɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ ni egbala ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Those white spots are mealybugs, which suck juice from the cocoa plant and secrete sweet liquid that ants feed on. Mealybugs are dangerous because they can carry and spread the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus from sick trees to healthy ones.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ ji mealybugs. ni shwieɔ cacao tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni ejieɔ nu ni ŋɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ lɛ kpo. Mealybugs lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ ebaanyɛ ekɛ cocoa bud virus lɛ aya tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: What causes black spots to spread rapidly over my cocoa pods when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, and shady environments. Excess water on the pods allows the fungus to grow and quickly turn healthy green pods black.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ hulutsoo kɛbaa. Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ji eŋɔli lɛ feɔ diŋ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants covered in small holes and chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ ni aaaye lɛ?

english: Chewed holes on maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm. They hide in the central leaves of the plant during the day and eat the tender leaf tissue, which slows down the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ahe lɛ baa. Amɛ teɔ shi yɛ tsei baai lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi mli ni amɛ yeɔ baai bibii, ni no haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many tiny flowers, but the tiny pods shrivel up and die before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei yɛ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo nɛkɛ, shi ŋmeii bibii lɛ gboiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is called 'cherelle wilt.' It happens naturally when the tree cannot carry all the pods it started making, but it can also be triggered by dry weather, nutrient shortages, or insect damage.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ‘Cherelle wilt’ ni baa yɛ adebɔɔ mli beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ atere ŋmeii fɛɛ ni ebɔi feemɔ lɛ dɔŋŋ lɛ. Shi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hu baanyɛ akanya lɛ. niyenii ni esaaa loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii

english: During the dry harmattan season, cocoa trees drop leaves to save water. Shedding leaves reduces the amount of moisture the tree loses through evaporation, helping it survive until the rain returns.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ, Cocoa tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi koni amɛkɛhere nu. Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ haa nu ni tso lɛ laajeɔ kɛyaa lasu mli lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will know it is ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack open from the growing tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaale akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb ni miida yɛ eshishi lɛ he.

english: Why should I cut off dead or crowded branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ kɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead wood and opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and fresh air can move through. Good airflow reduces dampness, which helps prevent pod diseases like Black Pod.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei ni egboi lɛ, ni egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ black pod helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ naa.

english: Why does burning my land before planting make my crops struggle later in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni mishãa dani miduɔ nii lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo yɛ be ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa naagbee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the natural layer of dead leaves and organic matter that holds moisture and feeds the soil. Without this layer, the soil bakes hard in the sun and loses important nutrients that crops need to grow.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli baai ni egboi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ shãa waa yɛ hulu lɛ mli ni efiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and dropping off when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la lɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight because their leaves are sensitive and dry out quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates living umbrellas that protect the cocoa trees and keep the soil moist while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaai lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when I leave all the young suckers growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain tree, they all compete for the same nutrients and water in the soil. Pruning away extra suckers and leaving just one or two allows the main tree to focus its energy on growing large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantain tso agbo ko ni tsii ni ekwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when heavy rains stay for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need soil that drains water easily. When heavy rains leave standing water in the field, oxygen cannot reach the roots, which causes fungal rot and destroys the tubers underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ashiɔ nu damɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb up as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso awo mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ koni makwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food that travels down to build big tubers. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes spreads the leaves out for better sunlight and keeps them away from damp ground diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shi koni amɛfee bulbs agboi. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba mli. ni etsĩ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ naa

english: Yellowing of the lower leaves on maize usually means the soil is running out of nitrogen, which the crop needs to stay green and produce strong ears. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo toi ni mli wa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my land help my maize crop grow better in the next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize in that same field later, the maize feeds on this stored nitrogen to grow strong without needing as much artificial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ sɛɛ mli lɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ, ŋmãa yeɔ nɛkɛ nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa babaoo awo mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the moisture in the soil steady through regular watering and mulching helps the flowers stay on the plant and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ kɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up tightly and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or mites sucking the sap from the young leaves, or by viruses carried by insects. Controlling these sap-sucking pests early prevents the leaves from twisting and stunting the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni shwieɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ Kudɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ mra. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tso lɛ ni amɛkafee lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do caterpillars hide deep inside the central funnel of my young maize plants during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworm caterpillars hide deep inside the central funnel of the maize plant during hot hours to protect themselves from sunlight and birds while eating the soft leaf shoots. Applying treatments directly into the funnel early in the morning gives the best control.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Koni okɛbu ohe kɛjɛ hulu kɛ okpoi ahe beni oyeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ wo ŋmei lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, no haa anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I water my vegetable garden early in the morning instead of at noon when the sun is hottest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ nu awo o-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli leebi moŋ fe shwane be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning gives the soil time to soak up moisture before the heat of the day. Watering at midday causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the crop roots can drink it.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or planting leguminous crops like beans in that soil previously helps keep the leaves green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he loo ni aduɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsutsu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of leafy foliage but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ baa babaoo shi ŋmɔtɔi lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: When cowpea plants get too much nitrogen from enriched soil or fertilizer, they spend all their energy making big leaves instead of producing flowers and beans.
ga: Kɛji cowpea tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ baai wuji moŋ fe ni amɛaafee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and feed it back into the soil, leaving your land fertile for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I clear old, rotten cocoa pods from my trees instead of leaving them there?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie kookoo ŋmeii ni egbɔ ni miifite lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashi amɛ yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Leaving diseased, black pods on your trees allows fungus spores to spread through rain droplets to fresh pods, creating bigger crop loss in future harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii diji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛtsɔ nugbɔshiimɔ mli kɛya ŋmeii heei amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fiteɔ yɛ wɔsɛɛ kpamɔ mli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites that spread viruses to the plant. Controlling these pests early keeps the plant healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhe wa

english: What makes my harvested yams start rotting inside the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yams rot in storage when damaged or bruised tubers are exposed to heat and poor airflow. Sorting out cut yams and keeping the barn well-ventilated stops rot from spreading.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni efite loo ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ wo hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii mli. Gbalamɔ sweet potatoes ni afo lɛ mli ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ ahi greenhouse lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Tsi naa koni ekafite

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get extremely high or when the soil goes from dry to wet too quickly. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli oya tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard and woody when I leave them long in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: As cassava grows past its maturity period, the plant converts its soft edible starch into tough fiber, making the roots hard, dry, and unpleasant to eat.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ da kɛho eshishijee be lɛ he lɛ Tso lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ayeɔ lɛ ewoɔ ŋmei ni wa mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni wa, ni egbi, ni ŋɔɔɔɔ.

english: Why is it better for me to plant at the very start of the major rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Planting early gives young roots time to grow deep into the ground while moisture is consistent, helping the crop survive sudden dry spells later in the season.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ be ni amɛdaraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yaa nɔ daa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni baa trukaa lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm land is healthy enough for growing vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa kɛha aduawai adumɔ?

english: Healthy farm soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand without forming hard blocks, holds moisture well after rain, and contains beneficial insects like earthworms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kpakpai amli lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Efoɔ mlɛo yɛ nine mli ni efeee ŋmeii ni wa. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that scorch easily under direct sunshine. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a protective canopy and traps soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to endure direct light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo tsei bibii woɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he ni ehi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize plants automatically shift available nitrogen from older lower leaves to nourish growing top leaves, signaling that your soil needs compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abele tsei tsakeɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do experienced farmers suggest planting groundnuts together with maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which can capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Planting groundnuts with maize enriches the soil naturally, providing free nitrogen to help the maize grow healthier.
ga: Abɛi fata legume weku lɛ he, ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko koni eye ebua ŋmãa lɛ ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Why does my plantain crop yield very small bunches when I leave all the young suckers growing around the mother stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ mishi ŋmeii bibii ni bɔle nyɛ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around a single plantain stem, they all fight for the same water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Pruning extra suckers to keep only two or three strong ones allows the mother plant to focus its energy on producing large fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe Plantain kome Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi babaoo koni tso lɛ yibii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai akui wuji ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I get smaller harvests when I sow my maize seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii fioo nɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting maize seeds too close together causes plants to compete heavily for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant adequate spacing ensures strong stems and larger, fully filled cobs.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu babaoo Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni da ni eyi obɔ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in dark, damp, and humid conditions. Pruning excess tree branches and clearing weeds allows sunlight and dry air to flow through the farm, keeping the disease away.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Eji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni edɔ, kɛ hei ni edɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ etsĩ helai anaa

english: Curling pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking sap from the underside of leaves, or by intense heat stress. Checking under the leaves for pests and keeping the soil moist helps prevent leaf curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ mli Kwɛmɔ baa lɛ shishi kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground after heavy rain floods my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Standing water fills soil pores and drowns the roots, leading to decay. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away safely so the tubers stay firm.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. kɛ fitemɔ baa Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe koni eha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without producing fruit during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants, causing their blossoms to drop off to save water and energy. Mulching around the base of the plant with dried grass keeps the roots cool and preserves soil water, allowing fruit to set.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into sunlight to produce food for growing large tubers below ground. Staking holds the foliage up off the damp ground where soil rot and leaf spot diseases easily attack.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ hei ni kwɔ waa koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa tsei ahe tsei lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni sũ ni fiteɔ kɛ tsei ahe helai tutuaa amɛ oya lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and dry during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to cover them, the intense sun scorches their leaves and dries them out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baaha hulutsoo lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha amɛgbi.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly into little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tips mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a vital nutrient in the soil that keeps leaves green and healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cowpeas and beans take natural nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, which feeds and enriches the soil for nearby crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the dirt when heavy rains fall for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe under water and harmful rot organisms quickly grow.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ nu shishi. Ni nibii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ daa oya.

english: Why is it dangerous for me to sow my seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛha mi akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a hot, dry period before the full rainy season starts, which can dry up and kill young germinating seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ latsaa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui bibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plants before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ewo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant experiences sudden changes between very dry and very wet soil.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na tsakemɔ ko trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ waa teŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to expose their leaves to sunlight, which gives the plant the energy it needs to swell and produce large tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfuu ni ekɛ bulbs agboi aba.

english: Allowing too many shoots to grow around one plantain tree causes them to fight for the same water and food, which leaves you with small, thin bunches of plantain.
ga: Ni aaaŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ Dumɔwu kome pɛ he lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii kome he. Enɛ baaha okɛ plantains bibioo ko ahi ohe.

english: Why are small green worms eating the deep inside leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi-babi corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, pests that crawl into the central leaves of young maize to feed on the fresh, tender parts of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni shwieɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ ehee ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: How do liquid chemicals get inside my crops when I spray them on the leaves?
ga: Te tsofai ni ji nu lɛ boteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ́ mikɛshwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Leaves have tiny pores that open up during the day. When you spray liquid chemicals onto healthy leaves, the crop absorbs the liquid through these pores, allowing the medicine or nutrients to move throughout the plant.
ga: Baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni gbeleɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni ji nu shwie baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ lɛ, Crops lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsofa loo niyenii mli nibii tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is it important to make sure chemical spray covers the entire crop and not just the top leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ koni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ? Jeee baa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ.

english: Pests and diseases usually hide under the lower leaves where it is cool and moist. Covering the whole plant ensures no harmful insects or fungi escape treatment, giving your crop total protection.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shishigbɛ baai ni mli ejɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ ashishi. Kɛ́ aha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa koni kooloi bibii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ko akajo foi. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ hebuu ni yeɔ emuu haa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What happens to the chemical on my crops if rain falls immediately after I finish spraying?
ga: Mɛni baaba tsofai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ beni migbe tsofai lɛ ashwiemɔ naa pɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes the chemical off the leaves before the crop can absorb it, wasting your money and labor. It is best to spray on clear days when it will not rain for at least two to four hours.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ ahe dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shika kɛ nitsumɔ fɛɛ ni afiteɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ yɛ gbi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi ni kɛ hoo lɛ, nugbɔ enɛɛɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai enyɔ kɛyashi ejwɛ.

english: Does walking too fast while spraying chemical on my farm affect how well it works?
ga: Ani nyiɛmɔ oya tsɔ beni mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ saa nitsumɔ he?

english: Walking too fast means your crops will not receive enough spray to protect them. Walking at a steady, moderate pace ensures the right amount of chemical lands on the crops to clear pests effectively.
ga: Oyaiyeli ni oooya lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enine shɛɛɛ tsofa ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baabu amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Nyiɛmɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ oyaiyeli ni sa mli lɛ haa tsofai ni sa lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ koni egbe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my knapsack sprayer apply more chemical on some rows of crops than on others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mispack sprayer lɛ kɛ tsofai babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi anɔ fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Unsteady pumping pressure or a worn-out nozzle tip causes uneven spray flow. Servicing your sprayer and replacing worn nozzles ensures a uniform spray so every crop gets equal treatment.
ga: Pɔmpiŋ hewalɛ ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo nozzle tip ni efite lɛ kɛ spray ni hoɔ ni ejaaa baa. O-sprayer lɛ he nitsumɔ kɛ nozzles ni efite lɛ najiaŋdamɔlɔ baaha spray lɛ hetooi lɛ aya nɔ daa. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ aná kwɛmɔ ni tamɔ amɛhe.

english: When is the best time of day to spray my crops so the chemical works properly?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ koni tsofai lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Early morning or cool evening is best. During hot afternoons, liquid chemicals evaporate quickly before the plant absorbs them, and strong sunlight can cause liquid on leaves to burn the crop.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsofai ni ji nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ashã ŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different agrochemicals together in one spray tank?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ okwaayeli mli tsofai enyɔ baafutu yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa nɔ lɛ kome mli?

english: Not always. Some chemicals react badly when mixed together, which can burn your crop leaves or stop the chemicals from working. Always ask an extension officer before mixing different inputs.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Tsofai komɛi kɛ amɛhe futu mli lɛ, amɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. ni baanyɛ ashã ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai loo ekpa tsofai anitsumɔ Esa akɛ obi extension officer lɛ dani okɛ nibii srɔtoi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ afutu.

english: Why do pests keep destroying my crops even though I spray the same chemical every week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai yaa nɔ efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shwieɔ nɔ daa otsi moŋ.

english: When you use the exact same chemical continuously, insects build resistance and survive it. Alternating between different approved chemical types prevents pests from becoming immune.
ga: Kɛ okɛ tsofai nɛɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii be fɛɛ be lɛ, kooloi baatswa amɛhe shi ni amɛhi shi. Tsofai srɔtoi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ateŋ tsakemɔ baabu he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni gbɔmɔtso lɛ nyɛɔ ewuɔ eshiɔ hela lɛ ahe

english: Why are the tips of my crop leaves turning yellow and dry after I applied pesticide?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the chemical mixture is too strong or applied during hot direct sunlight. High chemical strength stresses the plant and burns the sensitive leaf edges.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ akɛwo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Etsofa hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni eshãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe.

english: How does weedicide kill weeds in my farm without destroying my main crop?
ga: Te tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ ni efiteee miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ?

english: Selective weedicides target specific types of weeds without harming crops like maize or cassava. Once sprayed on weed leaves, the chemical travels down through the stems to kill the roots completely.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahalaa lɛ tsɔɔ jwɛi srɔtoi komɛi anɔ ni eyeee ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa awui. Kɛji akɛ afɔse jwɛi baai lɛ Tsofai lɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli koni egbe shishifãi lɛ kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil, or the ground is too waterlogged, which prevents the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: What is causing the leaves on my cassava plants to curl up and shrink?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi?

english: This leaf curling is usually caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that feed on the plant's sap and pass on the virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ tsei amli nu lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwãa

english: You should wait until rain has soaked the soil at least finger-length deep. Planting in dry or slightly damp soil can cause seeds to rot or dry out before they sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hoo lɛ inchi kome. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nɔ ni edɔ fioo nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo amɛgbi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why should I space my cassava cuttings far apart instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala mi-cassava niji lɛ amli moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, which results in thin, small tubers instead of big, healthy ones.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ yitsei wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why does my land yield less crop when I plant maize on the same plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Maize continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil. Rotating your plot with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni oootsake Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to resist local pests and dry spells, giving you a higher and more uniform harvest compared to old saved seeds.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmaa ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui momo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra sucker shoots from my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi-plantain lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If a plantain tree has too many suckers, the main plant wastes energy trying to feed all of them, which makes your main bunch of plantains very small.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwu lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ Tso titri lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha amɛ fɛɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa o-plantains kuu titri lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa.

english: Flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from high heat, insufficient water, or when tiny pests like thrips damage the flower stalks.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips fiteɔ fɔfɔii ahe tsei.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak even after I put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔji lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than your crops and will drink up the water and fertilizer before your crops get a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛbaanu nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: How do I know the right month of the year to start planting my crops so they don't dry up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli nyɔŋ ni sa akɛ maje tsei shishi koni amɛkagbi?

english: Planting should match the main rainy season in your area—usually starting around March or April in southern Ghana and May or June in the north. Planting too early before regular rains begin causes seeds to dry out and die in the hot soil.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ akpã gbee. Bei pii lɛ, ejeɔ shishi aaafee March loo April yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ. kɛ May loo June yɛ kooyigbɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ, dani nugbɔ anɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves dry up and turn yellow during the hot months between December and February?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ December kɛ February nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: During the dry Harmattan season, hot dry winds and lack of rain cause crops to lose water faster than their roots can absorb it. Plants react by dropping or yellowing their leaves to conserve energy and survive the dry stretch.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Tsei feɔ amɛnii kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli.

english: What can I do if the rainy season starts late or ends earlier than usual in my region?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi sɛɛ loo egbeɔ naa mra fe bɔ ni eji yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: You can plant early-maturing or short-duration crop varieties that only need 60 to 90 days to harvest. This allows the crop to fully yield produce even if the rainy season is shorter than normal.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra loo ni yeɔ be kukuoo ni biɔ gbii 60 kɛyashi 90 pɛ dani akpa, ni enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná amɛkpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ po.

english: Why do I get a much bigger harvest during the rainy season compared to the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii babaoo nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli kɛ akɛtoɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ he lɛ?

english: Crops need a steady supply of water to transport food and nutrients from the soil to their stems and fruits. Regular rainfall allows plants to grow fuller leaves, flowers, and fruits, resulting in a higher total volume at harvest.
ga: Tsei hia nu ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛkɛ niyenii kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛshishifãi kɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai, fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni eyi obɔ, ni no haa amɛyibɔ ​​fɛɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Is there a simple way to keep water in my soil for longer when rain stops falling for a few weeks?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aaatsɔ nɔ aha nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ otsii fioo komɛi?

english: You can practice mulching by covering the bare soil around your crop roots with dried grass, leaves, or crop stalks. This natural cover blocks direct sunlight from drying out the earth and keeps the soil moist longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ mulch awo mli kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni oooha nɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi ni egbi, baai loo tso shishifãi. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can too much heavy rain during the wet months actually destroy my crops?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, excessive water fills all the air spaces in the soil, which can suffocate plant roots and cause root rot. Heavy rain can also wash away essential soil nutrients and encourage damp fungal diseases on leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli eyiɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ewo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni mli ewo fɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: What kind of crops can I grow during the dry times of the year when there is very little rain?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Drought-tolerant crops like cassava, cowpeas, millet, and sorghum are best for dry periods. These crops have deep roots or tough leaves that allow them to store water and produce yields with minimal moisture.
ga: Nibii ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ji nɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha hɔmɔ be lɛ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai ni wa ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do my plants produce flowers at a specific time of the year instead of flowering all year round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ afi lɛ mli bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plants respond to environmental signals like changes in temperature, rainfall, and daylight length throughout the year. They naturally flower when weather conditions are most favorable for those flowers to successfully set seeds and fruit.
ga: Tsei tsuɔ shihilɛ mli okadii tamɔ hulutsoo tsakemɔi, nugbɔshiimɔ, kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ ahe nii. Taakɛ eji lɛ, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi hi koni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ awo dumɔwui kɛ aduawai yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Should I apply my fertilizer right before a heavy rain storm or after the rain has passed?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani ahum aba loo beni nugbɔ lɛ eho sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer right after a light rain when the ground is moist, or just before a gentle shower. Heavy rain right after application will wash the fertilizer away before the roots can draw it in.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ nɛ fioo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. aloo dani okɛ ohe awo nu mli fioo Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ baaho ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ awo mli.

english: Why do my crops spoil so quickly after a huge major harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ kpamɔ be wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Large harvest volumes combined with high humidity after the rainy season create perfect conditions for mold and pests. Keeping harvested crops raised off the ground in a well-ventilated, dry shed prevents spoilage.
ga: Nikpamɔ babaoo ni akɛfataa hulutsoo be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ he lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ to he ko ni egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite.

english: How many years does it usually take for a newly planted young cocoa tree to start bearing fruit?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Hybrid cocoa trees typically start flowering and producing pods about two to three years after planting, provided they receive proper care, weeding, and water during their early growth stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni akɛfee tsofa kroko lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii aaafee afii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni adu amɛ. Esa akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ, ajie jwɛi kɛ nu yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Why are the small flowers on my young cocoa trees falling off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop many of their early flowers if the tree is still too young, stressed by drought, or lacking proper soil nutrients to support the heavy weight of developing pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shishijee mli. Shi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji tso lɛ ji gbekɛ tsɔ lolo. ni hɔmɔ loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛɔ enɔ koni eye ebua ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds regularly around my cocoa trees during their first two years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Cacao tsei daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Weeds compete with young cocoa roots for soil nutrients, water, and space. Keeping the farm clean helps young trees grow faster and prevents dangerous pests from hiding near the trunk.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya, ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ akahi tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to inspect and cut off extra shoots or dead branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo amɛniji ni egboi lɛ amli ni mafolɔ amɛ?

english: Trimming excess shoots (chupons) and dead branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the inner tree, directing the plant's energy into making healthy branches and pods instead of waste growth.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine (chupon) kɛ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ feɔ niji kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi aya hiɛ lɛ

english: What causes my young cocoa pods to turn black and dry up on the branches?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ?

english: This is commonly caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, overly shady conditions. Removing infected pods immediately prevents the disease from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: What should I do when I notice insects eating the fresh young leaves of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina akɛ kooloi bibii miiye mi-kokoo tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ?

english: Insect attack on young leaves reduces the tree's ability to make food. You should consult an extension officer to recommend approved organic or chemical sprays that protect new shoots.
ga: Kplukai tutuaa baai bibii, ni no haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii. Esa akɛ oyabi o-extension agent lɛ koni etsɔɔ bo tsofa loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni buɔ tsei heei ahe lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees need fertilizer to help them grow and yield better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaye abua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: If your cocoa leaves start turning pale yellow, grow very slowly, or produce very few flowers, the soil may be depleted of key nutrients like nitrogen or potassium.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛdaraa blɛoo waa, loo amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi fioo ko pɛ. Nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hu baanyɛ afite.

english: Is it good to leave fallen cocoa leaves on the ground beneath my trees?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ oooshi kookoo baai ni egbee shi lɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi?

english: Yes, dry leaf mulch acts like a protective blanket that keeps soil moist, suppresses weed growth, and gradually breaks down into natural fertilizer for the cocoa roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kookoo shishifãi amli.

english: How do I know when a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ makpa?

english: A cocoa pod is ready to harvest when its skin changes color completely from green or deep red to a yellow or orange-yellow shade.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛhewolo lɛ tsake kwraa kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees droop and wilt during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees wilt during the dry season to conserve water. Providing temporary shade trees helps protect young cocoa trees from drying out completely during severe hot weather.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛbu nu he. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient found in the soil. Rain can wash this nutrient away, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the leaves regain their deep green color and energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nugbɔ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii nɛɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat ragged holes in the middle of my maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni etse yɛ mi-abɛi lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on the soft center of maize plants. Spotting them early allows you to apply recommended organic or chemical controls before they destroy the growing point of the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Amɛtaomɔ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ atsu nii. dani amɛfiteɔ hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout when I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain after a long dry season often only wets the top surface of the soil and dries out quickly. If a hot dry spell follows, the seeds dry out and die; it is safer to wait until the soil is deeply moist from regular rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ haa ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni egbiɔ oya. Kɛji latsaa kɛ hɔmɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ waa kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mli.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ tsina loo ŋmeii afata ŋmeii ahe lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas grab nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, feeding the cassava naturally. They also cover the ground quickly, preventing weeds from taking over and keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmei lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ muji oya hu koni jwɛi akaye nɔ ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed, usually from extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of water during flowering. Keeping the soil moist with mulch and regular watering helps the plant hold onto its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛhao. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli fũu kɛ nu ni awoɔ lɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seed yams very close together on the same heap?
