ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ sweet potato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋtayaa kome mli lɛ?

english: When yams are planted too close, their roots and tubers fight underground for space, water, and nutrients. Giving each seed yam enough space ensures you harvest large, heavy tubers instead of many thin, small ones.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu sweet potatoes ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ oha sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okpa ŋmeii wuji ni tsii. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, yitsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo babaoo yɛ.

english: Why did my crops scorch and die after I poured fertilizer directly against their main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer acts like salt; when placed directly against a stem, it sucks moisture out of the plant's roots and burns them. Fertilizer should always be applied a few inches away from the stem in damp soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmei. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ Ejieɔ nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ni eshãa. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi inchii fioo komɛi.

english: How do I know if my land has the right soil for growing groundnuts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii akwɛmɔ?

english: Groundnuts need loose, sandy soil that drains water easily so the flowering stems can push underground to grow nuts. Heavy clay soil holds too much water and becomes too hard, making it difficult for groundnuts to form.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ, ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia ŋmeii. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ashɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni akɛdu ŋmeii. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo tsɔ ni eyɛ mlɛo tsɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ ŋmeii baafee.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant again during the next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahere dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli ni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one powerful harvest; saving seeds from that harvest results in weak plants with low yields the following year. It is best to purchase fresh certified seeds each planting season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli baa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: How can I stop small insects from turning my stored dried maize into powder?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmãa ni egbi ni ato lɛ nɔ amɛfee powda?

english: Storage insects like weevils thrive when grain is slightly wet or exposed to air. Drying your maize until it is completely hard and storing it in airtight bags prevents insects from getting oxygen and living inside the grain.
ga: Kplukai ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ edɔ fioo loo amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni amɛhi ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Why do some farmers plant plantains together with young cocoa trees in the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ plantains kɛ cocoa tsei bibii feɔ ekome yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight can burn their delicate leaves. Plantains grow fast and provide large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, overly shaded conditions during the heavy rainy season, spreading quickly if infected pods are not removed.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji ajieee ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left from its older lower leaves up to feed the newer leaves on top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, leading to lower yields over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Weeds compete directly with your main crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, effectively stealing the resources your crops need to grow strong and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ohe lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ juɔ nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that hides inside the central funnel of young maize plants and eats the tender green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ni eyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Early morning is best because the soil can absorb the water before the heat of the sun causes it to evaporate, ensuring the roots get enough moisture.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu dani la ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ aha etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. koni shishifãi lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops after planting them?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli beni midu nii sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the soil is moist and when the crop is actively growing—usually a few weeks after germination—so the roots can easily drink up the nutrients.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2-3 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii mli hewalɛ mlɛo.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully matured and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, the stem turns woody, and a quick test digging reveals large, firm roots beneath the surface.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ tsɔɔ tso. Ni oyaiyeli ni akɛka lɛ jie shishifãi wuji ni wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ kpo.

english: Why do seeds bought from an agro-shop often grow better than seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aheɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shwapoi amli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds from agro-shops are specially bred to produce high yields and resist diseases, whereas seeds saved from previous harvests gradually lose these strong qualities over time.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli shwapoi amli lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛte shi amɛwo helai. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ fiofio Efiteɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know which coconut variety is best for me to plant on my land in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei henɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makwɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ nɔ?

english: Ghana has many coconut varieties, mainly categorized into Dwarfs (which yield quickly and are easy to harvest) and Talls (which live longer and withstand harsh weather better). Your choice depends on whether you want quick sales for coconut water or long-term production for oil.
ga: Ghana yɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi babaoo. Ajara amɛteŋ babaoo mli awo dwarf henɔi amli. Ayɛ ŋmei srɔtoi (ni woɔ yibii mra ni ekpamɔ waaa) kɛ ŋmei srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ (ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa amli). Nɔ ni obaahala lɛ damɔ kɛji oosumɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ o-coconut nu lɛ oya loo oosumɔ ni afee mu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: How can I tell if a young coconut seedling is healthy enough to buy and plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tso bibioo ko he wa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahe ni madu?

english: Look for seedlings with thick stems at the base, vibrant green leaves without spots, and strong germination roots. Avoid seedlings with pale yellow leaves or weak, thin trunks as they will grow slowly in the field.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui ni shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ mli tse. Baai lɛ yɛ eŋɔli ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he. kɛ shishifãi ni wa Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe ejaakɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ fiofio yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How far apart should I space my coconut trees when planting a new farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ ashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmeii tsei ateŋ kɛ́ adu ŋmɔ hee?

english: Coconut trees need plenty of sunlight and underground room for roots. Space Tall varieties about 8 to 9 meters apart, and Dwarf varieties around 6.5 to 7.5 meters apart to prevent them from shading each other and fighting for nutrients.
ga: Hulu la babaoo kɛ shishigbɛ tsũ he miihia ŋmei tsei kɛha amɛshishifãi lɛ. Space Tall henɔi lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 8 kɛyashi 9 ni dwarf henɔi lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 6.5 kɛyashi 7.5 koni amɛkafee amɛhe shade ni amɛkaye niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: How many years does it take for a coconut tree to start giving fruits after planting?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It depends on the variety type. Dwarf coconut varieties start producing fruits within 3 to 4 years, while Tall varieties usually take 6 to 8 years to begin fruiting.
ga: Edamɔ henɔi srɔtoi lɛ anɔ Akpɔlɔi ni kɛlɛ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, akpɔlɔi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Why are small coconut fruits falling off my young trees before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akokoobii bibii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Early fruit drop usually happens when trees face water stress during dry periods, nutrient shortages in the soil, or poor pollination. Giving the trees extra water and balanced fertilizers helps them hold onto their fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai ni fiteɔ mra lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii Kɛ́ akɛ nu kroko kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa ha tso lɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ yibii amli.

english: What causes coconut palm leaves to turn yellow and dry up from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are often a sign of nutrient deficiency (like nitrogen or potassium), drought, or diseases like Cape Saint Paul Wilt Disease, which is common in coastal parts of Ghana.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ (tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium) faaa, hɔmɔ, loo hela ko tamɔ Cape St. Paul’s wilt. Anaa amɛ yɛ Ghana ŋshɔnaa hei.

english: Do coconut trees need a lot of water to survive and yield well during the dry season?
ga: Ani nu babaoo he miihia ŋmei tsei koni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, coconut palms need consistent moisture to produce good fruit. Covering the soil around the base with dry leaves or husks (mulching) helps trap moisture in the soil during dry weather.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei tsei he hiaa be fɛɛ be koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmãa (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: What kind of soil is best for growing coconut trees in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmei tsei akwɛmɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Coconut palms grow best in deep, well-drained sandy-loam soils that retain moisture easily. They struggle in heavy clay soils where water settles, which causes roots to rot.
ga: Kokoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli oya lɛ nɔ. Amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ mli.

english: Can I grow food crops between my coconut trees while they are still small?
ga: Ani obaanyɛ odu niyenii yɛ ŋmei tsei ateŋ be mli ni obii lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, while coconut palms are small (during the first 3 to 4 years), you can plant crops like cassava, maize, legumes, or pineapples between the rows to maximize land use without harming the trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ ji bibioo po (yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli lɛ), obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, ŋmei loo ŋmei ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ koni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii babaoo ni eyeee tso lɛ awui.

english: How do I know when a coconut is ready to harvest for drinking water versus oil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii koni akɛtsu nii akɛ nu ni anuɔ yɛ fɔ najiaŋ?

english: For sweet drinking water, harvest the nuts at 7 to 8 months while the husk is still bright green. For oil extraction or copra, wait until 12 months when the outer husk turns brown and you hear water sloshing inside.
ga: Kɛha nu ni anuɔ ni ŋɔɔ Kpaa ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛye nyɔji 7 kɛyashi 8 ni ŋmeii lɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo lɛ. Kɛha mu loo kopra jiemɔ lɛ, mɛ kɛyashi nyɔji 12 beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni onuɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ gbɛɛmɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants suddenly full of small holes and caterpillar droppings inside the middle part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii trukaa lɛ? Ni ŋmeii afɔfɔi yɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars hide inside the growing center of the plant (the whorl) and eat the young leaves from the inside out. Spraying early in the morning or late evening when the worms are active helps get rid of them.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ (whorls) ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miitsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark brown and black from the bottom during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ nii waa kɛ ediŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and damp conditions. Pruning overcrowded tree branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods helps stop the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ejɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ koni hulu la aba ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the heat is too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Keeping the soil evenly damp and avoiding over-fertilizing helps the plant hold its flowers to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji la lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Why is it important for me to put sticks for my yam vines to climb on instead of leaving them to spread on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ niji ama mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ koni ekwɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha efo kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Lifting the vines with stakes exposes the leaves to maximum sunlight, which the plant needs to create energy. This energy goes underground to build bigger, heavier yam tubers while protecting the leaves from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ wo wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛfee hewalɛ Hewalɛ nɛɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: If too many shoots grow together, they steal water, light, and food from the mother plant. Leaving only one main plant, one medium shoot, and one small shoot (a mother, daughter, and granddaughter) ensures you get larger, healthier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo ebua amɛhe naa lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, kane, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Shi tso titri kome pɛ, teŋgbɛ tso kome, kɛ tso bibioo kome (nyɛ, biyoo, kɛ nabi yoo) koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ onine shɛ plantain tso ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do people spread dried grass on the soil around pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. Spreading dry grass or leaves keeps the soil damp during hot days, prevents weeds from growing, and cools the roots so the pepper plants do not dry out quickly.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni ooogbɛ ashwã lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ akagbi oya.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli, ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip of older leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the plant food responsible for keeping leaves green and helping crops grow tall and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why is it bad if I pour chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer right against the stem can burn the bark and delicate surface roots because fertilizer contains concentrated salts. Fertilizer should be placed in a small ring or line a few inches away from the stem where roots can safely absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. loo ekɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Why do people tell me to plant beans or groundnuts on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil. Planting beans, cowpeas, or groundnuts helps restore the soil because these plants naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground for the next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beans, cowpeas loo peanuts ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nɛɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up all the roots to check?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ efooo koni makwɛ?

english: Most cassava varieties are ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is ready when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and cracks begin to appear on the soil around the base of the stem due to swelling tubers underneath.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo efee klalo kɛha dumɔ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Ni ŋmeii bɔi kpojiemɔ yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli beni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but give me very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or too much shade, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo be babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines wither and dry up completely when it is close to harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni kpamɔ be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: The yam plant naturally dries up its upper leaves and stem when the underground tuber has finished growing and is fully mature for harvesting.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ haa amɛ ŋwɛi baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gĩɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa ni amɛdaraa kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize start turning yellow during continuous heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach, and saturated soil starves roots of air, turning maize leaves yellow from lack of nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees need fertilizer or if they just need more shade?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo hulutsoo babaoo?

english: If the leaves turn yellow between the green veins, the tree lacks nutrients and needs fertilizer. If the leaves look pale, brown, or burnt around the edges, the tree is getting too much sun and needs shade.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ Tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eshã yɛ eshishigbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni ená hulutsoo.

english: Why do I still need to weed around my crops even when the crops are much taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lolo eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ kɛlɛ kwraa fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Even small weeds steal nutrients and water from the soil that your crop roots need, and they can harbor pests and diseases that attack your crop.
ga: Jwɛi bibii po Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa onibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they get stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells, or lack of nutrients in the soil to preserve their energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Be ni hulutsoo be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ ni haa hewalɛ hiɔ shi lɛ bɛ

english: This rot happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering or dry soil while the fruit is growing.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea pods look healthy on the outside but end up empty inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ? Shi eyɛ shwɛm yɛ emli?

english: Tiny insects called pod-sucking bugs pierce the young green pods and suck out the developing seeds before they can mature.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pod suckers lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli ni amɛmuɔ dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ lɛ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why do armyworms attack my maize field more during dry spells between rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli, yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ lɛ?

english: Warm, dry conditions speed up the hatching of moth eggs, and weak, water-stressed maize plants are easier for armyworm caterpillars to feed on.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ baaha ŋmeii akui lɛ afɔ oya. Ni ŋmãa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nu haaa amɛhe afee shoo lɛ haa ewaa akɛ ŋmeii baaye amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop when the tree is stressed by dry weather, lacks nutrients, or when tiny insects attack them. Managing shade properly, mulching to keep soil moist, and controlling pests help flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua tsei lɛ miihao amɛ. Shade Management ni Sa Mulching koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop young fruit when the soil gets too dry, when the weather is extremely hot, or if there is a shortage of plant food. Regular watering and applying organic compost help keep the fruit attached to the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛyibii bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo niyenii ni akɛ tsei fee lɛ faaa lɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ he.

english: Yes, it matters a lot. You must plant cassava stems with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stems struggle to sprout properly and produce very few tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia waa. Okɛ o-cassava tso lɛ duɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu lɛ kɛtee shishi lɛ Ewa akɛ eshishifãi lɛ baadara ni bulbs fioo pɛ baaba.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on sticks so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves get, the more food the plant makes, resulting in bigger and healthier yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ baa lɛ náa lɛ, Babaoo ni tso lɛ woɔ niyenii lɛ, babaoo ni ewoɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa baa.

english: These extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree gets enough food to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers nɛɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo tso wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they naturally feed the soil, making it richer without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa ewoɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: It is best to water early in the morning. This allows the plants to drink before the sun gets hot, whereas afternoon watering causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before reaching the roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nuɔ nii dani hulu lɛ mli dɔɔ tsɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ nɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the roots of my crops rot when heavy rain flooded my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishifãi fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi ŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need to breathe air in the soil just like humans need air. When water stays trapped around the roots for too long, oxygen cannot reach them, causing the roots to drown and rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni tsei shishifãi lɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Taakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa adesai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu ŋmɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit a virus, or by severe heat stress. Using natural neem oil sprays and keeping soil moist helps protect the plants from this damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen if heavy rains wash nutrients away or if roots sit in waterlogged soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo shishifãi lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on maize to build up. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil fertility and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their pepper plants with dry leaves and straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves, known as mulching, keeps the soil moist by stopping water from evaporating in the heat. It also keeps the roots cool, prevents weeds from taking over, and adds organic matter to the soil as it decays.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni ehaaa efo yɛ latsaa be mli lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ ni amɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he beni efiteɔ lɛ

english: How can I tell when it is safe to start planting my crops after the first rains arrive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ eba lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season can be misleading, and planting too early might cause seeds to dry up if a long dry spell follows. Wait until the soil is thoroughly wet to a depth of about 15 centimeters and rainfall becomes regular.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ. Ni kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ ba. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ aaafee sɛntimita 15 ni nugbɔ lɛ falɛ aba shi pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How do I know if my cassava stems are good enough to cut and plant for the next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafolɔ ni madu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Choose stems from healthy, mature plants that are 8 to 18 months old, with no signs of diseases like mosaic spots or stem rot. Good planting stems should be thick, firm, and taken from the middle part of the stalk rather than the soft top.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 18, ni hela ko bɛ he okadi tamɔ mosaic spots loo tsei ni egbo lɛ amli. Esa akɛ tso ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni efee shiŋŋ, ni ejɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ moŋ fe ŋwɛigbɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a destructive caterpillar that feeds on the growing shoots of maize plants. Spotting them early and applying recommended insecticides or organic treatments like neem leaf extracts can save your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ. Ni aaana amɛ mra ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ neem baa mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii. lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni okpa nii

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop plants and make them look weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni ehaa amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds naturally adapt faster than cultivated crops to grab water, sunlight, and nutrients from the dirt. If left unchecked, they steal essential food from your crops, causing the crops to become stunted and yield less harvest.
ga: Jwɛi tsakeɔ amɛhe oya fe tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛjie nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛbaaju niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ onibii amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: During the Harmattan, hot dry winds cause cocoa trees to lose water faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. Without enough shade trees to protect them or adequate soil moisture, the tree sheds leaves to survive.
ga: Yɛ harmattan Hot beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo ni sa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa lɛ, Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I need to stick wooden poles in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves to catch maximum sunlight, which produces the energy needed to grow large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, reducing fungal diseases and boosting tuber size.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Ha fungal helai aba shi ni oha yitso lɛ aya hiɛ

english: Is it better to water my tomato plants early in the morning or late in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha tomato tsei lɛ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because it allows plants to absorb moisture before the heat of the day. Watering late in the afternoon leaves foliage wet overnight, which promotes fungal diseases that rot the leaves and fruit.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tso lɛ nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ baa. Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa baai kɛ aduawai fiteɔ baa.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture quickly. Keeping taller shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantains protects them while they grow strong roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa sũ mli nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ aha tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ loo adu tsei ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋma lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow during dry spells mostly due to a lack of water and nitrogen. When the soil is dry, roots cannot absorb essential nutrients, causing the plant to pull energy from older lower leaves to keep growing.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Nu kɛ nitrogen ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ titri ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛhe niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbalaa hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eya nɔ eda.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot inside the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Cassava root rot is usually caused by heavy waterlogging in poorly drained soil during intense rains. Excess standing water suffocates the roots and allows fungal pathogens in the soil to attack the tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni fa babaoo ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa sũ mli ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is tired and needs fertilizer to grow healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃?

english: If your crops grow very slowly, have pale or stunted leaves, and yield much smaller harvests than in previous years, your soil has lost key nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus and needs organic manure or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa blɛoo waa Na baai ni mli tse loo ni egbɔjɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ miifite niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. ni ehe miihia ni aná ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden heat stress. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination from taking place, so the plant sheds the unpollinated blossoms.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛna hulutsoo be mli haomɔ trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baatsi pollination ni sa naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest give me a smaller yield than certified seeds from agro-dealers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their vigor, genetic purity, and disease resistance over successive generations. Certified seeds are specially bred for hybrid vigor, giving them high yields, uniform growth, and better protection against local pests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ. fɔmɔ su mli hetsemɔ kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ yɛ wɔsɛɛ yinɔi amli. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha hybrid vigor, yibiiwoo ni fa, dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. ni ekɛ hebuu kpakpa aha kɛjɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: When crops are crowded too close together, they fight aggressively for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. This competition forces them to stretch upward for light rather than storing energy to form large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛgbala amɛhe koni amɛna la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabua hewalɛ naa koni amɛfee ŋmei agbo ko ni eyi obɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil season after season. It also allows pests and diseases that prefer that specific crop to build up in the soil and attack new plantings early.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ nakai tso lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutuaa tsei heei mra.

english: How do weeds reduce my crop yields even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii aba shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most cultivated crops and aggressively steal fertilizers, sunlight, and root space from your crops. They can also host insects and diseases that spread to your main plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, hulu la kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Amɛhiɛɔ kooloi kɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ hu.

english: Why do my harvested grains get ruined by insects when stored in normal woven sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii fiteɔ midumɔwui ni akpa lɛ kɛ́ akɛto kotokui ni akpɛ́ ni yɔɔ mlɛo amli lɛ?

english: Normal woven sacks allow air and humidity to pass through, creating warm, moist conditions where tiny grain insects like weevils can thrive, hatch, and feed on your stored harvest.
ga: Baagi ni akpɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo baa. Biɛ ji he ni dumɔwui bibii tamɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ ada, amɛfɔ ni amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need shade trees like plantains when I first plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ bɔ ni plantain lɛ fee beni midu lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full, hot sunlight. Planting plantains alongside them provides living shade that keeps the soil cool and moist, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Enɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why is it better to plant my maize in neat, straight rows instead of scattering the seeds around the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu abele yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo, ni ja lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows makes sure every plant gets its own space to catch sunlight, absorb water, and gather nutrients from the soil without choking neighboring plants. It also makes weeding much easier.
ga: Tso ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni enáa hulu la, eŋɔɔ nu, ni ebuaa niyenii mli hewalɛ naa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛtsiii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anaa. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. When soil lacks nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has to the top leaves, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and fade.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Leaf curling is often the plant's way of protecting itself from losing water in extreme heat, but it can also be caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a disease. Giving plants shade and keeping insects away stops this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni afolɔ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he. Shi kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni miigbɛ helai amɛshwã lɛ hu baanyɛ ekɛba. Tsei lɛ ni oooha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oootsi amɛ kɛjɛ he lɛ baaha enɛ akpa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on top of the soil for too long without draining, it suffocates the roots and encourages harmful fungal decay, leading to root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Nu haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbo.

english: Why should I spread dry leaves or grass on top of the soil around my vegetable beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Spreading dry organic material, called mulching, acts as a blanket for the soil. It blocks harsh sunlight from evaporating soil moisture, keeps the root area cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ baatsu nii akɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsĩɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: What causes tiny holes in my young maize leaves and powdery dirt inside the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli kɛ muji ni tamɔ powder ni yɔɔ baa teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This is caused by a caterpillar called the Fall Armyworm. It hides in the center fold of the maize plant where it eats the soft green tissue, leaving behind small holes and waste.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Eyeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Ashiɔ bu bibii kɛ jwɛi.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields in their first planting. If you save seeds from that harvest to plant again, the crop will grow unevenly and yield much less grain than the original seed.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Kɛji ohere dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ, du amɛ ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ebaawo dumɔwui fioo kwraa fe shishijee dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why should I wait a few weeks after my seeds sprout before putting chemical fertilizer near the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ otsii fioo komɛi beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ dani mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afata mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Very young sprouts have tender, delicate roots that can easily burn if they touch strong chemical fertilizers. Waiting until roots grow stronger ensures the plant safely absorbs the nutrients.
ga: Tsofai ni darako kwraa lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni baanyɛ ashã oya kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli lɛ wo mli. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ mli wa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Tsei baajie fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does my cocoa farm take several years to start producing pods, while my maize grows and yields in just three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe afii babaoo dani mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ ebɔi pods feemɔ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-abele lɛ daa ni ewoɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli.

english: Maize is a short-season grain crop that completes its whole life cycle quickly, whereas cocoa is a permanent tree crop that must first build deep roots and a strong trunk over time so it can continuously yield fruit for decades.
ga: Abɛi ji ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo ni ewala be fɛɛ yaa oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo ji tso ko ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni esa akɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa aba yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ bɔni afee ni ekɛ yibiiwoo aya nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: If big fruit trees grow strong on their own, why do I still need to put fertilizer around them?
ga: Kɛ́ tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baanyɛ eda agbo lɛ, mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni wɔkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii abɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Even strong trees consume nutrients from the soil every time they grow leaves and produce fruit. Adding fertilizer replaces those lost soil nutrients so the tree has the energy to give you large harvests year after year.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ po yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye niyenii ni elaaje yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaahã oná kpamɔ babaoo afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why should I cut off healthy branches from my cocoa trees during pruning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ kookoo tso nɔ yɛ be mli ni mifoɔ tso lɛ?

english: Removing excess branches lets sunlight and air circulate through the tree, which prevents fungal diseases like black pod and directs the tree's natural strength into producing bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji anaa, ni ekɛ tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Will planting shade trees like plantain or forest trees on my farm steal food and water from my young crops?
ga: Ani tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo koo mli tsei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli?

english: Young crops like cocoa burn easily under harsh sunlight. Shade trees act like living umbrellas to protect young plants from heat, and their fallen leaves rot to add rich organic fertilizer back into the soil.
ga: Nibii bibii tamɔ kookoo shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka koni amɛkɛbu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he. Ni amɛbaai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ koni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves during the dry Harmattan season, and does it mean they are dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ fɛɛ gbee shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ eegbo?

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally during dry weather to save water. The plant is not dead; it rests and stores energy inside the underground roots until the rain returns.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ejɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to plant my crops very close together if I want to get more harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ miisumɔ ni makpa nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ hu?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots fight underground for food and water, and their leaves block sunlight from each other, resulting in weak plants with smaller yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I buy improved hybrid seeds from the extension office instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛjɛ Extension Office lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ.

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over generations and yield less. Improved hybrid seeds are specially bred to grow faster, resist local pests and diseases, and yield much more crop.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛdara oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ewoɔ babaoo

english: Why does my field yield less maize every time I plant maize on the same plot season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the dirt to restore soil strength.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha sũ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and curling up even though there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves during good rain usually mean sap-sucking insects or plant viruses are attacking the crop, or that heavy rains have washed away essential nitrogen from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu loo tsei amli helai miitutua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do cover crops like mucuna help stop weeds from taking over my field without using chemical sprays?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni tamɔ mucilage lɛ atsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cover crops spread quickly across the ground like a dense carpet, blocking sunlight from weed seeds so they cannot sprout, while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya tamɔ kapɛti ni mli edɔ. Tsi hulu lɛ naa kɛjɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ahe koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing well if I do not put chemical fertilizer on the farm every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli daa be lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients like food out of the dirt every time they grow. If you harvest without replacing those nutrients through compost, manure, or fertilizer, the soil becomes hungry and exhausted, so future crops struggle to grow.
ga: Tsei jieɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ niyenii, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛji okpa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii kɛtsakeee nakai niyenii lɛ, Hɔmɔ baaye shikpɔŋ lɛ ni egbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant is starving for a nutrient called nitrogen. Nitrogen is what gives plants their deep green color and energy to grow strong leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ niyenii ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen lɛ. Nitrogen ji nɔ ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ, ni ehaa amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaa baa ni wa.

english: How can planting beans or cowpeas help my soil without me buying expensive fertilizer?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ ni miheee ŋmeii ni jara wa?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas have special roots that trap natural nitrogen from the air and feed it into the dirt. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil to feed your next crop for free.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yaka.

english: Why does my crop produce very big stems and leaves but almost no grain at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji waa shi eshwɛ fioo ni dumɔwui bɛ mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen but lacks nutrients like phosphorus or potassium. Nitrogen builds the green body of the plant, but phosphorus and potassium are needed to make fruits, seeds, and grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fa tsɔ shi niyenii tamɔ phosphorus loo potassium bɛ mli. Nitrogen ji nɔ ni feɔ tsei lɛ agbɔmɔtso lɛ eŋɔli. Shi phosphorus kɛ potassium he miihia koni akɛfee aduawai, dumɔwui, kɛ ŋmaa.

english: What happens to my plants if I plant too many seeds very close together in the same space?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ he kome?

english: When seeds are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of many big plants, you end up with tall, thin, weak plants that yield very little.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ tsei wuji babaoo najiaŋ lɛ, tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo pɛ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops wither even when there is enough rain in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii miigbo lɛ? Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Weeds are stronger and faster drinkers than most crops. They quickly steal the water and fertilizer from under your crop's roots, leaving your crop weak and dry.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ mli wa ni enuɔ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashishi oya. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why is it good practice to grow cassava together with short-term crops like groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ akɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei baadu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts grow fast, cover the bare soil to stop weeds, and mature early, while cassava grows slowly and takes up deeper soil space. They share the land without fighting for the same room at the same time.
ga: Peanuts daa oya. Ha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ koni jwɛi lɛ akpa ni amɛkwɛ oya, yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsuɔ nii. Amɛjaraa shikpɔŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛwu amɛha tsu kome yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why do crops planted at the very start of the rainy season grow faster than crops planted later in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: The first rains wake up beneficial bugs in the soil that break down leaves and release a rich burst of trapped food called a nitrogen flush, giving early crops a huge boost.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ teɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shi, ni amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ ni amɛjieɔ niyenii babaoo ni emɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen flush lɛ kpo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, mra be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ná hewalɛ babaoo.

english: How do my crops know when it is time to start making flowers and fruits?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛje fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Crops measure the world around them using daylight hours, changes in heat, and their own age. When these natural signals match what the plant expects, it stops making leaves and starts flowering.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la susuɔ jeŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ he. hulutsoo tsakemɔ kɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eafii Kɛji adebɔɔ mli okadii nɛɛ kɛ nɔ ni tso lɛ kpaa gbɛ lɛ kpã gbee lɛ, Ebaakpa baai feemɔ ni ebɔi fɔfɔi.

english: Why does cassava take almost a whole year to harvest while maize is ready in a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa heɔ afi lɛ mli be babaoo ni akɛkpaa ŋmãa yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Maize invests all its energy into quickly making seeds above ground before drying up, while cassava spends many months slowly packing food away underground into heavy storage roots.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ dumɔwui oya yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ dani amɛgbiɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmei heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani ekwɛɔ fiofio. Ekɛ niyenii toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shishifãi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ babaoo lɛ amli.

english: Do I need to cut down all the big trees on my land before I start planting my crops?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafolɔ tsei ni edara ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Not always; while crops like vegetables need full sunlight, leaving some trees provides useful shade, protects soil from drying out in severe heat, and helps prevent water erosion.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be; Yɛ be mli ni tsei tamɔ aduawai he hiaa hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ. Tsei komɛi ni ashiɔ amɛgbeleɔ lɛ hu haa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I know the right time to start clearing and ploughing my land for the main farming season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha okwaayeli be titri lɛ?

english: Land preparation should ideally begin just before the rains start so that the soil is ready to absorb moisture, allowing newly planted seeds to germinate immediately without drying up in hard ground.
ga: Esa akɛ aje shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ shishi dani nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛhaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ agbi.

english: Should I burn the trees and bush after clearing my field, or is there a better way?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã tsei kɛ jwɛi beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ loo gbɛ ni hi fe enɛ yɛ?

english: Burning clears the land fast, but it destroys rich topsoil organic matter and beneficial organisms; leaving cleared brush to rot or using it as mulch builds up long-term soil fertility.
ga: Shãa baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Shi ebaakpãtã nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ kɛ nibii babaoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ brɔshi ni he tse lɛ gbɛ ni egbo loo akɛtsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why is it necessary to break up hard soil before planting seeds for the first time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akumɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli dani adu dumɔwui klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Loosening hard soil allows crop roots to spread easily, helps rainwater soak deep into the ground instead of running off, and lets air reach the roots so the crop grows strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa mlɛo. Enɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni eeejo foi. ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ada waa

english: How can I tell if a piece of soil on my farm is good for growing vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha aduawai adumɔ?

english: Good vegetable soil is typically dark, soft to dig through, rich in decaying leaves, and drains water well without leaving standing pools that rot plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ efo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ mli Eyi obɔ kɛ baai ni fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni eshiuuu nu ŋshɔi ni ekã shi ni haa tsei shishifãi fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do crops planted on newly cleared forest land grow differently than those on old farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ koo shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ nɔ lɛ daa lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe blema ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Newly cleared virgin soil is rich in natural nutrients accumulated over years, causing initial crops to grow vigorously, whereas older farmland may need manure or fertilizer to perform as well.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajie ehee lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni abua naa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Ha tsei lɛ adara waa yɛ shishijee mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, okwaayeli ŋmɔji ni etsɛ waa lɛ baanyɛ abi ni akɛ ŋmɔji loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ nakai nɔŋŋ.

english: Can foreign vegetables like broccoli grow well in our soil and weather here in Ghana?
ga: Ani maŋsɛɛ aduawai tamɔ broccoli baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ wɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Yes, but they require cool temperatures—often growing best in high-altitude areas like the Ashanti highlands or during cooler months—along with moist, rich, well-drained soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ he miihia amɛ. Amɛfɔɔ dalɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ, tamɔ Ashanti Gɔŋkpɔ lɛ nɔ, loo yɛ nyɔji ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fata he.

english: Is directly putting seeds into the soil the only way to plant crops on my farm?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ pɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ tsei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, while direct seeding works for crops like corn, delicate vegetables are often started in nursery beds first and then transplanted as seedlings to ensure a higher survival rate.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ mli akɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ moŋ. Shi bei pii lɛ, ajeɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ashishi yɛ ŋmɔji amli klɛŋklɛŋ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ aduɔ amɛ akɛ dumɔwui koni amɛhi shi babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and weak when I plant them under heavy tree canopy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to produce their own food; when blocked by thick trees, they stretch unnaturally toward the light, becoming thin, weak, and yellow.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. Kɛ tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsi enaa lɛ Ebaakpã mli yɛ gbɛ ni jeee adebɔɔ nɔ kɛya la lɛ mli. Kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni egbɔjɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Does the depth at which I bury my seeds affect how they grow?
ga: Ani bɔ ni midumɔwui lɛ mli kwɔ ha lɛ saa amɛdalɛ he?

english: Yes, planting seeds too deep uses up all their stored energy before they reach the surface, while planting too shallow can cause seeds to dry out or get eaten by birds.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ yeɔ amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato lɛ dani amɛshɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbi loo okpoi aye amɛ.

english: Why should I make ridges or mounds in my field instead of planting directly into flat soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni madu tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Making ridges or mounds loosens the soil, which makes it much easier for root crops like yams and cassava to expand into large tubers. Ridging also creates channels that prevent heavy rain from washing away your topsoil or causing root rot.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi loo gɔji ni afee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa anáa shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei. Eyɛ mlɛo kwraa akɛ oootsɔ yitso agbo. Nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ hu haa gbɛ ko baa ni tsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ loo ekafite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Is it better to hire a tractor to prepare my land or clear it by hand with a hoe?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha trakta ni okɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ loo okɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii?

english: A tractor is much faster and turns over hard soil deep underground, which is great for large fields. However, for small or sloped plots, clearing by hand preserves the fertile topsoil and avoids disrupting the natural soil structure.
ga: Tractors are much faster and can turn over the hard soil underground. Enɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔji wuji. However, for small plots or sloping areas Hand-clearing helps preserve fertile topsoil and avoids disturbing the natural structure of the soil.

english: My maize leaves are turning yellow from the center of the leaf outward. What is wrong with my crop?
ga: Mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ kɛmiiya kponɔgbɛ. Mɛni ba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure will help restore the green color and keep the crop growing well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into fruits during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of moisture stress the tomato plant, causing it to drop its blossoms to survive. Watering your plants regularly around the roots early in the morning helps them retain their flowers and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ haoɔ tomato tsei. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛhi shi. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishifãi ni ajieɔ daa leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yibii amli.

english: I noticed small caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young corn. How do I stop them?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmeii bibii ni miiye mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: Those caterpillars are likely fall armyworms, which hide in the deep center whorl of the corn plant. You can control them by applying recommended crop protection products or natural neem leaf extracts early in the morning or late in the evening when they feed.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji asraafoi ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe tee ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ shɔŋŋ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ nibii ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii loo adebɔɔ mli neem baa mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Young crop seedlings are delicate and cannot compete with aggressive weeds. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the available sunlight, water, and soil nutrients they need to build strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni mli wa lɛ ashi akaŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa tsei lɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtswa shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantains next to my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu kookoo tso yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Tso bibioo ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo tsei bibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Planting cassava too closely causes the plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room for its leaves to gather sunlight and its roots to expand into big tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso lɛ baa lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baa lɛ baanyɛ abua hulu la naa, ni shishifãi lɛ hu agbɛ ashwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Alternating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are fully mature and ready to pull out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts are ready to harvest when the leaves start turning yellow and dropping. You can test by pulling up one plant; if the inside of the pods has dark brown markings and the nuts fill the shell tightly, it is time to harvest.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso kome ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli lɛ yɛ okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ. Nikpamɔ be eshɛ.

english: Yellow leaves during heavy rains usually mean nitrogen is being washed deep into the soil away from the roots, or that the ground is waterlogged, preventing roots from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my farmland needs manure or fertilizer before planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu?

english: If your previous crops grew slowly, had pale green leaves, or produced small yields, your soil is low on nutrients and needs organic manure or compost added before planting.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ dara blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo ewoɔ yibii fioo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani adu.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside shoot of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that loves hiding in the central leaves of young maize. If caught early, they can be controlled with approved treatments or local remedies like sprinkling clean dry sand into the plant whorl.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni sumɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe awo ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai amli. Kɛji ana oya lɛ Abaanyɛ akudɔ kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo maŋ lɛ mli tsofai, tamɔ ŋã ni he tse ni egbi ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and overly shaded conditions during the rainy season. Pruning extra branches to let light in helps prevent it.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Niji krokomɛi ni aaafolɔ koni la abote mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu amɛhe.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus carried by these insects. Controlling the insects early prevents the leaf curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Mra Kooloi Akwɛmɔ Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells as a natural defense to save water and stay alive in the heat. As soon as the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing its tubers.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii heei ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii heei.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the daytime temperatures get too hot, when the soil is too dry, or if there are no bees around to move pollen between the flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji ŋmeii bɛ ni baajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ

english: How can I tell when my plantain bunch is ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni plantains lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Plantains are ready for harvest when the individual fingers look full and rounded rather than sharp-edged, and the small leaf at the top of the bunch begins to turn yellow.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni inchi fɛɛ inchi tamɔ nɔ ni eyi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e hɛ mi nyami ɔmɛ peeɔ nɔ́ nɛ tso nyafii nɛ a ngɛ tso ɔ yi mi ɔ jeɔ sisi nɛ a peeɔ ngmami.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting cowpeas or beans alongside maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas grab nitrogen directly from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, which helps nourish the maize and improves soil fertility naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni haa ŋmãa lɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ

english: Why is it better to grow cassava and yam on raised soil mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ hi fe ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Making raised mounds keeps the soil loose and easy for tubers to expand big and deep, while also helping extra rain water drain away so the roots do not rot.
ga: Kɛ́ awó gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aakwɛ bulbs wuji ni mli kwɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ koni shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning red or yellow with swollen stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ tsuru loo ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ efuu lɛ?

english: This is a key sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus disease. The virus weakens the tree's internal system, causing leaf discoloration and swollen branches, which eventually leads to the tree dying if left untreated.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi titri ko ni tsɔɔ akɛ Cocoa Swole Shoot Virus lɛ. Virus lɛ haa tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ tsakeɔ su ni niji lɛ hu fuɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbo yɛ naagbee kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: Why do agriculture officers ask us to cut down cocoa trees that still have pods on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi biɔ ni wɔfolɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lolo lɛ?

english: Once a cocoa tree is infected with a deadly virus like swollen shoot, it cannot be cured. Even if it still produces pods, it acts as a carrier that spreads the disease to surrounding healthy trees, so cutting it down saves the rest of your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ helai ni naa wa, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ bote kookoo tsei lɛ, anyɛɛɛ atsa amɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ eyɛ pods mli lolo moŋ. Shi etsuɔ ​​nii hu akɛ nɔ ni kɛ helai baa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔ mli koni okɛhere oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ yiwala.

english: How can I tell if a disease is starting on my cocoa farm before all my trees get affected?
