ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli hela eba dani tsei lɛ fɛɛ emɔ amɛ?

english: Regularly inspect your farm for early signs such as unusually pale leaf veins, swollen young shoots, premature leaf dropping, or black spots on young pods so you can act before it spreads.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa kɛha mra be mli okadii tamɔ baa fãji ni tsuɔ waa, tsei bibii ni efuu, kɛ baai ni elaaje oya. loo ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ koni onyɛ ofee nɔ ko dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Do small insects like mealybugs really harm my cocoa trees, or are they harmless?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs lɛ yeɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Mealybugs are very dangerous because they carry crop viruses from sick trees to healthy ones as they feed on sap. Controlling these insects helps prevent major disease outbreaks on your farm.
ga: Mealybugs lɛ yɛ oshara waa ejaakɛ amɛwoɔ tsei ahe helai ni jɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli beni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Kɛ́ oye kooloi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ helai ni naa wa ni baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anaa.

english: If my neighbor's cocoa farm gets sick, can the disease spread to my farm?
ga: Kɛji hela mɔ okutsoŋnyo lɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ Ani hela nɛɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, crop diseases travel easily across farm borders through wind, shared farming tools, and moving insects like mealybugs. Keeping boundary trees healthy and monitored is essential.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahelai tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛfoɔ ŋmɔ husui amli mlɛo. Kɛ akɛ okwaayeli nibii tsu nii ekome kɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs ni ajieɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akwɛ husu tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do cocoa diseases seem to spread much faster during certain times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kookoo hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kwraa yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Warm and humid weather allows pests like mealybugs to reproduce faster and fungi to thrive. Disease transmission peaks when environmental conditions are ideal for these carriers.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mealybugs lɛ fɔɔ oya ni fungi lɛ hu shwereɔ. Helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ yaa hiɛ fe fɛɛ beni shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ sa kɛha nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ.

english: Why does cocoa not yield as much on my land as it did for my father decades ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo wooo yibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ bɔ ni mitsɛ fee afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Over time, soil nutrients get exhausted, and older trees become weaker and more susceptible to viruses. Replanting with modern, disease-resistant cocoa varieties restores farm productivity.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. Ni tsei ni edara lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ eye ebua ni ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: If I cut down sick cocoa trees, can I plant new cocoa seedlings on the same land right away?
ga: Kɛji mifo cacao tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ Ani manyɛ madu cacao dumɔwui heei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is best to clear all infected roots and wait for a short period while treating the area for pests. Planting shade crops first helps prepare the soil for healthy new cocoa seedlings.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie shishifãi fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni omɛ be kukuoo ko yɛ be mli ni otsaa he ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Shade tsei ni aduɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni esaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha kookoo dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I protect my young cocoa seedlings from dying during the hot dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu cacao tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa trees need temporary shade crops like plantains or bananas. Their large leaves block direct sun, keep the soil cool, and hold moisture around the seedling roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa amɛhe jɔɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo banana. Amɛbaai wuji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni amɛmɔɔ nu ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. dumɔwui shishifãi

english: Why is it important for all cocoa farmers in our community to tackle farm diseases together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni kookoo okwaafoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ afee ekome kɛtsu helai ni yɔɔ amɛŋmɔji amli lɛ ahe nii lɛ?

english: Viruses and pests do not stop at farm boundaries. If one farmer leaves infected trees untouched, insects will carry the disease back to surrounding clean farms, destroying everyone's hard work.
ga: Virus kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ekpaaa ŋmɔ husui lɛ anaa. If farmers leave infected trees untouched, Insects carry the disease back to surrounding clean farms. Nɔ ni fiteɔ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ nitsumɔ ni wa lɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is essential plant food. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure early in the plant's growth helps the leaves turn dark green and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tso lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni efee ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when the soil turns hard and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni egbi lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil makes it difficult for delicate roots to spread out and drink water or collect nutrients. Loosening the soil before planting allows roots to grow deep and absorb everything the plant needs to grow fast.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛnu nu loo amɛto niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛheɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekwɛ oya.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very thin and produce small ears when I plant many seeds together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛtoi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei babaoo amli lɛ? Dumɔwui yɛ be kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each seed enough space allows every plant to grow thick stalks and large, full ears.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ekwɛ̃ɔ shishifãi ni mli tse kɛ toii wuji.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all big shade trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Keeping taller trees or planting plantains nearby creates shade that protects the cocoa and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei akwɛmɔ koni amɛdara loo amɛdu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without forming fruits when it gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he lɛ?

english: Hot temperatures and dry winds stress tomato plants, causing them to drop flowers to save water. Watering the plants regularly at the roots early in the morning keeps them cool enough to form fruits.
ga: He ni latsaa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ ashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ashwie koni nu akafite. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ eshishigbɛ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do caterpillar pests suddenly swarm my farm right after a dry period ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baa miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ?

english: Insects lay eggs that hatch quickly when warm weather is followed by rain, creating a sudden outbreak of hungry caterpillars. Checking under leaves regularly lets you catch and remove pests before they multiply and damage crops.
ga: Kplukai lɛ woɔ wɔji ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ jeɔ kpo trukaa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni omɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ni ojie amɛ dani amɛshwere ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does covering the ground with dry bush grass help my pepper farm during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching yeɔ ebuaa mi pepper ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves keeps the hot sun from drying out the ground. This holds moisture near the roots longer, so your pepper plants stay healthy even with little rain.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, o-pepper tsei lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ fioo po sɛɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on my plot after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the dirt, but groundnuts naturally feed the soil by pulling nitrogen from the air into their roots. Planting groundnuts restores the land so your next crop grows better.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Peanuts ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni eha jɛmɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I use seeds saved from store-bought market maize for my next planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ jara nɔ ŋmãa ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ midumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Grains sold at the market are often treated for food or come from hybrid varieties that do not grow well a second time. Using certified planting seeds ensures every crop grows uniformly and yields a big harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akwɛɔ ŋmaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ akɛ niyenii loo ejɛɔ ŋmaa srɔtoi ni akɛfee ekome ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ daa pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil so fast before reaching the market in Accra?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani amɛshɛɔ jara ni yɔɔ Accra lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting crops during the hot afternoon traps heat inside the produce, causing rapid decay during transport. Harvesting early in the morning when crops are cool keeps them firm and fresh for longer journeys.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa nibii ni adu lɛ amli. Enɛ haa fitemɔ baa oya yɛ gbɛfaa mli. Nikpamɔ leebi beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ehaa ehe feɔ ehee kɛha gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow from the tip downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting at the tip usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants need plenty of nitrogen to stay green and build large cobs, so adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help them grow green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young corn leaves with tiny droppings left inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛni eshwɛ yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the center of the maize leaf funnel. Catching them early and applying an approved pesticide or neem solution inside the leaf whorl will destroy the pest before it damages the stem.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋmãa baa tsũi lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baakpata kooloi lɛ ahiɛ dani efite tso lɛ shishifã lɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to plant my cassava stem cuttings into the dirt?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni matsɔ nɔ madu mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stems have small raised buds or 'eyes' where new leaves will sprout. You must plant the stem cutting with these buds pointing upwards toward the sky so the plant can easily shoot leaves up and push roots down into the soil.
ga: Kasava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni baa heei baajɛ mli aba. Esa akɛ odu tsei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ajie baai lɛ ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: Yam vines produce long climbing stems that need sunlight to create food for the plant. Elevating the leaves off the ground with stakes keeps them dry, prevents leaves from rotting, and directs energy straight down into producing huge yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ tsei kakadaji ni he hiaa hulu la koni ekɛfee niyenii aha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛgbi. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni ekɛ hewalɛ haa sweet potato tubers babaoo feemɔ tɛ̃ɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them protects the young cocoa from intense heat and keeps the surrounding soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cocoa tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do I choose the right plantain sucker shoot from an old tree to start a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso momo ko mli koni mikɛje tso hee shishi?

english: Choose 'sword suckers', which are young shoots with narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a strong, wide base. These shoots have healthy root systems that grow faster and produce bigger plantain bunches than shoots that already have broad, flat leaves.
ga: Halamɔ ‘sword shoot’, ni ji tso bibioo ko ni baai lɛ mli tseee, ni tamɔ lance, ni eshishigbɛ lɛ mli kwɔ ni eyɛ shiŋŋ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa. Enɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaaha plantain tsei ni dara fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ momo lɛ aba.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when the plant lacks water, or if the soil lacks nutrients. Mulching the base of the plant to keep the roots cool and watering regularly during dry spells will help flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni nu bɛ tsei amli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛha tso lɛ shishi koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i, ni akɛ nu awo mli daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking the plant juices and spreading plant viruses. Spraying the leaves with soap water or recommended insecticides gets rid of these pests and keeps new leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaaha baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut flowers bend down and sink into the soil after they bloom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ kotoɔ shi ni amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants naturally produce their nuts underground. After the blossom on top is pollinated, the plant grows a long stem called a 'peg' that pushes down into the earth where the actual peanut pod expands and matures.
ga: Peanut tsei woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Beni afee fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ pollen sɛɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli he ni ŋmeii lɛ amli shwereɔ ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, but avoid doing it immediately before a heavy rainstorm. Heavy rains will wash the fertilizer away before the crop's roots can soak it up, wasting your effort and investment.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shi esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa aba. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Eji mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kɛ shika ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ fitemɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from sunlight and harsh wind. Without temporary shade crops like plantains planted nearby, intense heat scorches tender young cocoa leaves and dries out essential moisture from the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baashã kookoo baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers encourage me to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for growing larger tubers under the soil. It also keeps leaves away from damp soil, reducing fungal diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ hu kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the cobs mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize plants need in large amounts to grow healthy leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost early in the growth period prevents this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ŋmãa tsei he hiaa babaoo koni amɛkwɛ baai ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo mli mra yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my farm help the maize crop that I plant on the same land next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts have beneficial bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop harvest ends, this natural fertility stays behind to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei yɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ ba naagbee Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli babaoo nɛɛ baakã he ahi sɛɛ koni akɛye ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Does it matter which direction I face cassava stem cuttings when inserting them into the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ masusu gbɛ ni mikɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ lɛ kpeɔ lɛ he beni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the buds pointing upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the shoots struggle to reach the light, resulting in weak growth and significantly lower tuber yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ hiɛ shi lɛ, Shoots lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ená la. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ baa ni tuber yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water, food, and light from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them and keeping only two or three strong ones allows the plant to focus its power on producing large bunches.
ga: Tsobii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ mɛi babaoo lɛ ni ahiɛɔ enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii wuji ni eeefee lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small dark droppings inside the central stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ amli lɛ baa? Eyɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that burrows into the center of maize plants. Applying recommended biopesticides or neem extract early in the morning kills the pest before it destroys the plant's growing shoot.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni shwieɔ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ dani efite tso lɛ shishifãi ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling tightly upward and looking small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛfite lɛ?

english: Upward curling in pepper leaves is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant's juices and spreading viruses. Controlling these sap-sucking pests early protects the foliage and keeps fruits growing properly.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies kɛbaa. Emuɔ tsei amli nu ni egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ mra lɛ, ebaabu tso lɛ yibii lɛ ahe ni eye ebua ni aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off the stems without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience heat stress, extreme dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Watering plants regularly and placing organic mulch around the stems keeps the soil cool and helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. extremely dry soil or too much nitrogen fertilizer Water the plants regularly and mulch around them with organic mulch. Stems to keep the soil cool and help flowers turn into tomatoes.

english: Why is it risky to sow my maize or vegetable seeds right after the very first rain of the major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu mi ŋmãa loo aduawai dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell before regular rains truly start. Sowing too early causes seeds to germinate and then dry up and die; waiting for consistent moisture ensures seedlings survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni mli edɔ waa nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baaje shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi. Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ mɛmɔ haa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to measure 75 centimeters between my crop rows instead of just scattering seeds by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ masusu sɛntimita 75 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ minine baagbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã lɛ?

english: Measuring specific distances ensures that each plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water without competing with its neighbors. Spaced rows also make weeding and harvesting much easier for you.
ga: Gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko ni asusuɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ akutsoŋbii abɔ akaŋ Gbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ hu haa jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest because I have more plants in the field?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ejaakɛ miyɛ tsei babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting too close causes crops to fight each other for food and light, resulting in thin, weak plants with smaller yields. Giving plants proper space actually produces healthier crops and a bigger total harvest.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu yɛ niyenii kɛ la he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ahe gbɛ ni sa ha lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant my crops in straight rows instead of spreading them randomly across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows helps you manage your farm better. It leaves clear paths for walking, applying fertilizer, and clearing weeds without trampling your growing crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni oootsɔ nɔ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ni okɛ jwɛi awo mli ni okɛ ohe wooo ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant soybeans and sorghum together in the same field, or will one choke the other?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ soybeans kɛ sorghum yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli loo amɛbaagbe ekroko lɛ naa?

english: You can plant them together safely if you leave proper space between them. Soybeans add extra nitrogen nutrients to the soil, which actually helps tall crops like sorghum grow stronger.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu amɛ yɛ he kome shweshweeshwe kɛji oshi gbɛ ni sa yɛ amɛteŋ. Soybeans kɛ nitrogen niyenii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no yeɔ ebuaa tsei kakadaji tamɔ ŋmãa diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: How many rows of short crops like soybeans should I plant between tall crops like sorghum?
ga: Tsei kukuji tamɔ soybeans ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ enyiɛ esa akɛ madu yɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ sorghum ateŋ?

english: Planting two rows of soybeans in the space between sorghum rows works best. This arrangement allows the shorter soybeans to get enough sunlight while still enriching the soil for the sorghum.
ga: Soybeans ni ato he gbɛjianɔ enyɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ni yɔɔ sorghum ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɛkɛ hesaamɔ nɛɛ haa soybean kukuji lɛ naa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lolo kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my soybean plants make the soil better for other crops I plant later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean tso lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛhaa tsei krokomɛi ni miduɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soybeans are legumes that pull nitrogen out of the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. This leaves behind natural fertilizer that nourishes whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Soybeans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ shĩɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why does sorghum survive dry spells in northern Ghana much better than maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Sorghum has deep root systems that search far underground for water, and its leaves can roll up during dry spells to stop water from escaping, allowing it to survive drought.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni taoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ. Ni ebaai lɛ baanyɛ abɔle ehe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni nu akaje mli. Ha ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my sorghum plants roll up tightly during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sorghum baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural shield against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, saving precious water inside.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ hebuu. Tsei haa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu ni jara wa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ mli.

english: What happens if I plant my soybean seeds too deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ soybean dumɔwui wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Seeds planted too deep use up all their stored energy trying to push through the heavy dirt and may die before reaching the surface light. Planting them at the right depth helps them sprout quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baafite hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi dani amɛshɛ la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do my young soybean plants turn yellow when heavy rain floods my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Too much standing water suffocates the roots by blocking air in the soil. Without air, the roots cannot take up nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow from starvation.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava underground is ready to harvest if I cannot see the tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa? Ni kɛji akɛ minaaa ŋmei shishifã lɛ hu?

english: Cassava shows signs above ground when it is ready. The lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack as the expanding tubers push the earth upward.
ga: Yucca baajie okadii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akpo kɛ́ efee klalo. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii ni dara lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks in the ground for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni mi sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves high up into the light, keeps them off wet soil to prevent diseases, and leads to a much bigger harvest.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi yɛ la lɛ mli. Tsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ koni helai akabote mli. Ni ekɛ kpamɔ ni da kwraa fe no baa.

english: Why do my yams turn out small and bent when I plant them in hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ bibii ni ebɔleɔ ehe kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops that grow under the soil like yams need loose, soft earth to push through easily as they grow. Hard or rocky soil blocks their growth, forcing the tubers to stay small or become twisted.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, tamɔ sweet potatoes lɛ, he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛtsɔ mli mlɛo beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi tsiɔ dalɛ naa. ni haa yitso lɛ feɔ bibioo loo egbɛɔ eshwaa

english: Does cocoyam need a lot of water in the soil to produce well?
ga: Ani nu babaoo he miihia kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ewo yibii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, cocoyam thrives best in damp, moist soil that holds moisture well. If the soil becomes too dry for long periods, the leaves will wither and the underground corms will remain small.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, ni mli efɔ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ Baai lɛ baagboi. ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ baafee bibii lolo

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need partial shade from faster-growing plants like plantains to shelter them from extreme heat and retain moisture in their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eha amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Is it normal for my plantain tree to grow smaller shoots around its base, and should I remove them?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ mi-plantain lɛ baaná ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he, ni ani esa akɛ majie amɛ?

english: Yes, those small shoots are called suckers. You should cut away extra suckers so they do not steal water and nutrients from the main tree, but leave one strong sucker to take over after the main tree produces fruit.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Shi ha tso lɛ yibii kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aŋɔ gbɛhe lɛ beni tso titri lɛ ewo yibii sɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves split into thin strips whenever strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves are designed by nature to split along their veins during high winds. This reduces wind resistance so that the heavy wind passes through the leaf instead of snapping the main trunk of the plant.
ga: Afee plantain baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛgbala amɛhe yɛ amɛ fãji lɛ amli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ tso lɛ naa lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa atsɔ baai lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeekumɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or sudden dry conditions. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and adding grass mulch helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato baagbee shi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo hulutsoo loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden egg plants curling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli eggplant lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on garden eggs is commonly caused by small insects like aphids sucking the juice from the leaves. Early detection and applying organic insect control or neem oil can protect the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo neem fɔ lɛ anaa mra ni akudɔ amɛ. Ebaanyɛ ebu tsei ahe

english: Why is it important for me to walk through my crop field every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔji amli daa gbi lɛ?

english: Daily visits allow you to notice early signs of insect pests, diseases, or dry soil before major damage happens. Catching crop problems early makes them much easier and cheaper to treat.
ga: Daa gbi saramɔi haa onyɛɔ onaa tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he okadii mra dani nɔ ni fiteɔ nii waa baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe naagbai ni amɔmɔɔ mra Enɛ haa tsamɔ feɔ mlɛo ni ejara waaa kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plants regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants have to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to feed and produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Esa akɛ tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does the buyer offer me a lower price when there are small stones and dirt mixed with my harvested grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ haa mi jara ni baa shi yɛ be mli ni tɛi bibii kɛ muji efutu dumɔwui ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Buyers pay higher prices for clean crops because foreign materials like stones, dirt, and chaff damage processing machines and reduce food safety. Cleaning and sorting your harvest increases its market value.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ jara babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni he tse. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, maŋsɛɛ nibii tamɔ tɛi, muji, kɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii fiteɔ tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ. ni eha niyenii he shweshweeshwefeemɔ aba shi Onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ahe saamɔ kɛ amɛhe ni ooohala lɛ baaha jara ni eyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, shady conditions. Pruning extra tree branches to let sunlight and air reach the pods helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji krokomɛi ni aaafolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce much smaller yields if I leave them in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii babaoo kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow aggressively and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds early leaves all the soil nutrients available for your crops to grow big and produce well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aba koni onibii lɛ adara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruit during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the tomato plant, causing it to drop its flowers to conserve energy and water. Providing partial shade and watering regularly during hot spells helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Ha egbee shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Partial shade and regular watering during hot weather help the flowers bear fruit.

english: Why do small insects attack my stored dried maize after a few months in the storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects thrive in stored grain if the maize still contains moisture or if the storage space is damp. Thoroughly drying your grains in the sun until they are hard before storing them in airtight bags prevents insect infestation.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ŋmaa lɛ tee nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo kɛji akɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi amɛhe wa dani akɛwo vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why does cassava become soft and watery if I leave it in the ground for too long after maturity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni edara sɛɛ lɛ, efeɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu lɛ?

english: If cassava stays in the ground past its maturity period—especially during heavy rains—the plant starts using up its stored starch, turning the root watery and reducing its quality for cooking or processing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ tee nɔ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛteke shweremɔ be lɛ. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Tso lɛ baaje shishi ekɛ e-starch ni ekɛto lɛ atsu nii. Ha shishifãi lɛ aná nu ni oha bɔ ni ahoɔ nii loo bɔ ni atsuɔ he nii ahaa lɛ aba shi

english: Why shouldn't I burn the dry bushes on my land before planting my new crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi ni egbi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani miduɔ tsei heei?

english: Burning bush destroys the helpful organisms in the soil and burns away natural organic nutrients. Clearing without burning leaves organic matter that rots into rich compost, keeping the soil fertile for longer.
ga: Tsoi bibii ni ashãa lɛ gbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ni eshãa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãaa lɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii be kakadaŋŋ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to build green leaves. When there isn't enough nitrogen in the soil, the plant moves what little it has from its oldest leaves at the bottom to feed the growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves turn yellow and droop right after a heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper roots are sensitive to soaked, waterlogged soil because water pushes out the air that roots need to breathe. When roots suffocate in standing water, they stop taking up nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow and droop.
ga: Pepper shishifãi lɛ nuɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ he waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni esa akɛ shishifãi lɛ amu kɛje kpo lɛ. Kɛ shishifãi lɛ shwie shi yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli lɛ Amɛbaakpa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yeli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up tight when the hot afternoon sun comes out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ je kpo lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl up to reduce the leaf area exposed to the direct sun, which stops water from evaporating too quickly. It is the plant's natural way of saving water until the day cools down.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya tsɔ. Eji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear away all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under full sun. Large shade trees act like living umbrellas that protect young cocoa from harsh heat, wind, and fast drying of the soil during their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tsei ni eda ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kokoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ he yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant gets stressed by intense heat or dry soil. When conditions are too severe, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself rather than trying to feed fruits it cannot support.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha lɛ aduawai ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of thick green leaves but very few beans when I add fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi beans fioo pɛ yɔɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas make their own nitrogen naturally through their roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer tricks the plant into using all its energy to build leaves and stems instead of making flowers and seed pods.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ feɔ nitrogen kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ lakaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ eshishifãi amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔji

english: Why do my watermelon plants spread long vines all over the field before any fruit appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon tso lɛ yɛ wain tsei kakadaji ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Watermelon vines spread out wide to build a large factory of green leaves that gather sunlight. Only after the vine is large enough to create and store enough energy will the plant start forming heavy fruits.
ga: Watermelon wain tsei gbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he koni efee tsei agboi ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli ni buaa hulu la naa. Beni wain tso lɛ da bɔ ni sa pɛ kɛkɛ ni ebaanyɛ ebɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛto. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ baabɔi yibii ni tsii womɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of just trailing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooonyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves get maximum sunlight to make food, which is then sent down to grow a large tuber under the ground. Keeping leaves off the damp soil also prevents diseases from attacking the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛha hulu la ni fa babaoo aha amɛbaai lɛ ni akɛhoo nii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, atsuɔ amɛ shi koni amɛyadu bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akatutua tso lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees give smaller bunches when I let all the shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwereɔ bibii bibii beni mihaa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Extra plantain shoots act like additional mouths to feed, stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from the main plant. Cutting away extra suckers leaves all the food for the main tree to produce a bigger bunch.
ga: Plantain tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ niyenii, nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ jumɔ. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa niyenii lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ tso titri lɛ nɔ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts underground are fully ripe and ready to dig up without ruining the crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ atsa ni mifiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: You can check by pulling up two or three sample plants across your field and opening the pods. Groundnuts are mature when the inside wall of the pod turns dark brown or spotted and the nuts fit tightly inside their shells.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ ni oootsi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ogbele ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Peanuts lɛ eda kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli gbogboi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ. ni ŋmei lɛ baakã etsitsi lɛ mli shiŋŋ.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape from the tips inward, the maize is lacking nitrogen. Nitrogen is essential for leafy green growth, and when soil nutrients are low, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves.
ga: When the lower leaves turn yellow, forming a V shape from the inner tip. Shows that corn lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. and when nutrients in the soil are low Plants pull nitrogen from old lower leaves to supply to young upper leaves.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei dumɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that catch nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots with the help of beneficial soil bacteria. When the groundnut plant dies, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ globules bibii amli. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ayebuamɔ nɔ Kɛ́ ŋmei tso lɛ gbo Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the shade trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sun. Large shade trees like plantains or forest trees shield young cocoa from direct sun and preserve moisture in the air and soil until the cocoa grows strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo koo mli tsei yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni enine ashɛ la ni fa nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by very small insects like thrips, mites, or aphids sucking sap from the undersides of leaves, or spreading leaf curl viruses. Keeping the farm clean and spraying organic neem oil helps protect new foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo tsofai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ. Kɛ́ oha ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse ni okɛ organic neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai heei lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can harvest more crops from one plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Planted too closely, maize stalks must compete with each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. This competition leaves you with tall, weak plants that produce small or unfilled cobs instead of full, heavy ears.
ga: dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Esa akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ atswa akaŋ kɛha nu. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ hulu la. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ni eshɛɛɛ he yɛ toi ni eyi obɔ ni tsii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sun exposure to make food for the plant. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground where diseases spread, allowing maximum leaf area to absorb sunlight and send energy down to build big underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ egbɛ eshwa lɛ. Enɛ haa baa lɛ he lɛ ŋmɛɔ hulu la ni ekɛ hewalɛ baa shi koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it important to weed my farm when crops are still small instead of waiting until they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ moŋ fe ni mamɛ kɛyashi amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal water, light, and soil nutrients during the crop's most vital early development stage. Removing weeds early allows young crop roots to spread and establish without stress.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛtswaa shi ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow weak if I plant immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛji midu yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a hot dry spell before regular rains start. Seeds that germinate right after the first rain can easily scorch and dry out in the hot, dry soil before the main rainy season settles.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ be ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi sɛɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni amɛgbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ nɔ oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy or poorly drained soil, allowing root-rot fungi to thrive. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ ada. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high temperature stress, erratic watering, or poor pollination. Consistent watering and giving plants partial shade during scorching heat help flowers set into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa he haomɔ hewɔ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo pollination ni ehiii Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade from taller plants like plantains or shade trees to protect their leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni akɛbu baai lɛ ahe koni akashã amɛ. kɛ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow healthy ears. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by intense heat, a lack of water, or too much fertilizer. The plant drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival instead of making fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii

english: Why do my corn plants grow thin and weak with no big ears when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛbɛ toi wuji beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete against each other for sunlight, root space, and soil nutrients. This forces them to grow tall and thin searching for light instead of producing big corn ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛfee mɛi ni kwɔlɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛtao la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaná ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why does my field yield less harvest when I plant maize on the exact same patch of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Maize draws the same nutrients out of the soil every year. Planting it in the same spot continuously drains those specific nutrients and allows pests that feed on maize to build up in the soil.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baajie nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Beans and groundnuts have helpful bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crops you plant.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops look sickly even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal food, water, and root space directly from your crops. Even with good rain, the weeds end up taking most of the soil nutrients before your crops can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi Jwɛi hu nine shɛɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when we get too much heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When the soil stays soaked in water for too long, the roots suffocate, causing rot and fungi to destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni ŋmeii kpataa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do small green worms hide and eat inside the center leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ teeɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These worms, known as Fall Armyworms, hide inside the cool, moist funnel of young corn leaves to feed on new growth while staying safe from heat and predators.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmei bibii ni mli ejɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Yam leaves need to reach up high into the sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground where diseases spread easily.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ awo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulu la lɛ mli koni eha niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential food they need from the ground. This happens when the soil is tired or when heavy rains wash away nutrients, so adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps them turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fite. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they get stressed by sudden high heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. When the plant feels weak, it drops flowers to save its strength rather than trying to support fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ nu he akɛ egbɔjɔ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu ehewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oye obua aduawai lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them for too long in heavy or poorly drained soil. The excess water stops the roots from breathing and creates a wet home for rot-causing fungi.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu tsɔ amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ shia ni mli efɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up tight during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's way of protecting itself from losing water. By curling its leaves inward, the pepper plant shields itself from direct sunlight and dry wind to hold onto soil moisture.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ he. Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he koni amɛha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Plantain roots do not grow deep into the ground. When the bunch gets heavy and rain softens the soil, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground unless you support the trunk with strong wooden props.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsii ni nugbɔ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ fee blɛoo lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ oooshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ja okɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to produce energy that builds big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves dry, exposed to the sun, and safe from soil diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi yɛ hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa. Staking haa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ, hulu la shɛɔ amɛnɔ, ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ hu yeɔ amɛ awui.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very little yield when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Instead of growing thick trunks and heavy fruit, they waste energy stretching upward to reach the light.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli, moŋ lɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ aduawai ni tsii. Mohu ɔ, a puɛɔ he wami nɛ a ngɔɔ kɛ yaa hiɔwe ɔ konɛ a ná la.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, pests that lay eggs on young maize. The hatched caterpillars crawl inside the growing center of the plant where it is soft and moist, eating the new leaves before they can open up.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ. Kplukai ni efɔ lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ tso lɛ dalɛ mli. ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli edɔ Ye baai heei dani amɛgbele.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow small and produce very little harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ feɔ bibioo ni mikpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they grow faster than your crops and take away the water, fertilizer, and sunlight your plants need. When crops compete with weeds, they become weak and produce smaller yields.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛdaraa oya fe onibii ni oduɔ lɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Kɛ tsei kɛ jwɛi miitswa akaŋ lɛ Amɛbaafee mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do young cocoa plants die so quickly if I plant them in an open sunny field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya kɛji akɛ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and small root systems that burn easily under hot, direct sunlight. Fast-growing shade crops like plantain or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and moist while it gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo shade tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: Why are many farmers in Ghana choosing to plant soybeans instead of only maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ miihala akɛ amɛbaadu soybean yɛ ŋmãa kɛkɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Soybeans enrich the soil naturally by pulling nitrogen from the air into the earth. This reduces the amount of chemical fertilizer you need for your next crop while giving you seeds that sell well for food, cooking oil, and animal feed.
ga: Soybeans haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni he hiaa bo kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewoɔ dumɔwui ni ahɔ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛha niyenii. fɔ ni akɛhooɔ nii kɛ kooloi aniyenii

english: How does planting soybeans on my land help my future crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ soybeans ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miwɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Soybeans have small nodules on their roots that trap plant food in the soil. When the soybean crop is harvested, these nutrients remain in the ground, making the soil richer and healthier for the next crop you plant, like maize or cassava.
ga: Soya lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔ̃ɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Be ni esa akɛ akpa soybeans Niyenii nibii nɛɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: How can I tell that my soybeans are ready to be cut and harvested from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-soybeans lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Your soybeans are ready when the leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving dry brown pods on the plant. If you shake a pod and hear the seeds rattling inside like small stones, it is time to harvest.
ga: O soybean ɔmɛ pee klaalo ke e ba tsɔ ŋmɔŋ nɛ e je kpo. Ashiɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛji okpokpo pod lɛ ni onu dumɔwui lɛ ni miihoso yɛ mli tamɔ tɛi bibii lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni abaakpa nii.

english: Why do my soybean pods burst open and drop their seeds on the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean ŋmɔji lɛ mli gbalaa ni amɛshiɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Soybean pods naturally burst open to release their seeds when they become too dry in the hot sun. This is called pod shattering, and you can avoid losing your harvest by cutting the plants early in the morning when the pods are still slightly moist.
ga: Soybean ŋmeii lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ejie dumɔwui kɛji amɛgbi tsɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ pods lɛ mligbalamɔ. Ni obaanyɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni baafite lɛ kɛtsɔ tsei ni ooofolɔ leebi maŋkpa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ amli edɔ fioo lolo lɛ nɔ.

english: What useful things can I do with the dry husks and stalks left after threshing my soybeans?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ manyɛ mafee kɛ ŋmeii ni egbi kɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ beni migbe soybeans lɛ?

english: Nothing from the soybean plant needs to go to waste. You can burn the dry husks as clean fuel for household cooking, feed the leftover plant material to livestock, or turn it into natural compost for your farm.
ga: Nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ ni jɛɔ soybean tsei lɛ amli ni eyaaa yaka. Obaanyɛ oshã ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ ni ofee tsofa ni he tse kɛha shia niyenii. Ha kooloi niyenii ni eshwɛ ni akɛ tso fee lɛ. Aloo tsɔmɔ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to clear the bushes around the edges of my farm before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie brɔshi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ he dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Clearing the edges of your field keeps dangerous pests like snakes away from workers, creates a safe space to gather your harvested crops, and prevents accidental bushfires from spreading into your farm.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ anaa koni kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara, tamɔ onufui akabɛŋkɛ nitsulɔi. Feemɔ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni okɛbaabua onibii ni okpa lɛ anaa. ni otsi koo mli la ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ oshara mli lɛ naa.

english: Will burning the weeds on my farm before planting harm the crop soil?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mikɛshãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani miduɔ lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ awui?

english: Yes, heavy burning destroys the natural organic matter and good insects in the topsoil that feed your crops. It is better to clear the land manually or plough the dry weeds directly into the soil to act as natural fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, shãa ni naa wa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ kooloi kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ niji ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni aaatsɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can I extract cooking oil directly from the soybeans I harvest on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ majie fɔ ni akɛhooɔ nii kɛjɛ soybeans ni mikpaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Soybean seeds contain natural oil, but extracting it requires milling machine equipment that crushes and presses the dried seeds under heat to separate the clear vegetable oil from the rest of the seed.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli fɔ yɛ soybean dumɔwui amli. Shi bɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ lɛ biɔ ni akɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii ni akɛ la shwieɔ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ anɔ koni ekɛgbala tsofa-kɛ-ŋma mli fɔ ni mli tse lɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni eshwɛ lɛ amli.

english: What happens to the solid parts of the soybean after the oil has been squeezed out?
ga: Mɛni baa soybean lɛ fãi ni wa lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni atswa fɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The remaining solid material is ground into a rich powder called soybean meal or cake. It is packed with protein and is highly valuable for making commercial feed for poultry, pigs, and fish.
ga: Akɛ nibii ni wa ni eshwɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ powda ni mli ewo muji ni atsɛɔ lɛ soybean niyenii loo keeki. Protein eyi mli obɔ ni ejara wa waa akɛ jarayeli niyenii kɛha kooloi, tsinai kɛ loo.

english: Why do the leaves of my crop droop down during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaves droop in extreme heat to protect themselves by exposing less surface area to the hot sun. This helps the plant conserve internal water so it does not dry out before the cool evening comes.
ga: Shi amɛ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛtsɔ he ko fioo ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ nɔ. Helps the plant conserve water inside so it doesn't dry out before the cold snap arrives.

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that helps your maize grow tall and strong without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa oŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot periods to reduce their surface area, which keeps them from losing too much water through evaporation. It is the plant's natural way of protecting itself from drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi. Enɛ tsiɔ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he koni ekagbi.

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when the weather is too hot or when they lack enough water. It can also happen if you give them too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen babaoo wo ŋmɔ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Cassava drops its leaves in the dry season to conserve water and protect its roots underground. Once the rains return, the plant quickly sprouts fresh green leaves and continues growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ Tso lɛ shwereɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya ni eyaa nɔ edaa.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in wet, humid weather. Trimming thick tree branches to let in sunlight and fresh air helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. niji ni mli tse ni afoɔ Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are there small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with powdery dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Mɔ ni etse ni sũ bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the leaves and leaving behind their waste. Checking your field early and spraying recommended remedies while the plants are young prevents crop loss.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ baai kɛ jwɛi. Odumɔi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii akafite.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crops with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo he ni ebɔle he lɛ mli lɛ? Akɛ jwɛi loo baai ŋmɔɔ?

english: Covering the soil, called mulching, keeps the ground cool, stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the heat, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my crop seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin plants with small harvests.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa.

english: Cassava roots do not have a thick protective skin like yams, so they start to spoil rapidly as soon as they are exposed to air after harvesting. They need to be cooked, sold, or processed into gari within two to three days.
ga: Cassava shishifãi bɛ hewolo ni mli tse tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa kɔɔyɔɔ pɛ kɛkɛ ni ejeɔ shishi efiteɔ oya. Esa akɛ ahoo amɛ, ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ, loo afee amɛ gari yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds keep growing back so quickly even after I clear my farm with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ dade shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong root systems and hidden seeds in the soil that sprout as soon as they get sunlight and rain. Clearing with a cutlass only removes the top part, whereas using proper weed control chemicals attacks the roots and prevents them from regrowing quickly.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji amɛná hulu la kɛ nugbɔ pɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsɔne tsumɔ mli lɛ, ebaajie ŋwɛi fã lɛ pɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni ehaaa amɛfee ehee oya.

english: Why are small holes appearing on my young maize leaves, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Holes in maize leaves are usually caused by pests like fall armyworms eating the plant. Applying crop protection chemicals early kills these insects before they damage the growing point of the maize and destroy your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Tsofai ni buɔ tsei ahe ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Egbeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfiteɔ hei ni o-corn lɛ daa lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do yield-boosting chemicals actually help my crops produce more food?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofai ni haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwo niyenii babaoo?

english: Yield boosters feed your crops essential nutrients that might be missing from the soil. They give the plant extra energy to grow stronger roots, greener leaves, and produce bigger, heavier fruits or grains.
ga: Nibii ni haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ lɛ haa otsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ekolɛ ebɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Amɛhaa tsei hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa, baai eŋɔli, ni amɛwo aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji ni tsii.

english: What causes my tomato fruits to turn black and rot before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tomato lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo dani ekwɛ̃?

english: Fruit rot is often caused by fungal diseases that spread in humid weather or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Using protective chemicals like fungicides shields the tomatoes from fungal attack so they can ripen safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ aduawai fitemɔ baa. Tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ buɔ tomato he kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ahe koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why did my crops turn yellow and dry up after I sprayed weedkiller on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Certain weedkillers kill all plants they touch if sprayed directly on crops, or if mixed in doses that are too strong. You must use selective weedkillers that only target weeds, or use shields to protect your crops during spraying.
ga: Tsofai komɛi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ gbeɔ tsei fɛɛ ni kɛ amɛ kpeɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛfutu mli yɛ yibɔ ni mli wa tsɔ mli Esa akɛ Okɛ tsofa ni halaa jwɛi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ pɛ atsu nii. Aloo okɛ shield abu onibii ahe yɛ be mli ni okɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with lots of leaves but very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Ani eyɛ baai babaoo shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?
