english: When crops get too much nitrogen or lack balanced nutrients, they put all their energy into growing top leaves instead of roots. Growth management chemicals and balanced fertilizers help direct the plant's energy down into building bigger tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo loo amɛnáaa niyenii ni sa Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ he nii moŋ fe shishifãi. Tsofai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛkwɛɔ tso lɛ dalɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ shi kɛyaa bulbs wuji afeemɔ mli.

english: Can I spray my crops to protect them before I even see any insects on the farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni mikɛbu amɛhe dani mana kooloi bibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, preventive spraying creates a shield on the plant leaves. When insects arrive or hatch, the protective chemical stops them from feeding or laying eggs, keeping your farm safe before damage occurs.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ ahe. Kɛji kooloi bibii ba loo amɛfɔ Defense tsofai lɛ tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye nii loo amɛkawo ŋmeii. Ha oŋmɔ lɛ afee shweshweeshwe dani efite.

english: How do I know which chemical spray is safe and correct for my specific crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ja kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛi lɛ?

english: Every crop and plant problem requires a specific input and dosage. Visiting a recognized agricultural supply shop or talking to an extension officer ensures you get genuine, crop-safe products tailored to your farm's needs.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ kɛ tsei ahe naagba fɛɛ naagba biɔ saji pɔtɛɛi kɛ amɛyibɔ. Okwaayeli nibii ahe shwapo ko ni ale lɛ ni oooyasara loo okɛ sɛɛkpee najiaŋdamɔlɔ ko awie lɛ baaha onine ashɛ nibii ni ji anɔkwale, ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni kɛ oŋmɔ lɛ hiamɔ nii kpãa gbee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt and drop their flowers during short dry spells in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heat stress causes plants to drop flowers to save water and stay alive. Certain crop management inputs and anti-stress foliar sprays help plants retain water and hold onto their flowers until the rain returns.
ga: Dɔlɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli. Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ahe saji komɛi kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi anɔ ni tsiɔ haomɔ naa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: What can I do to stop insects from destroying my harvested maize while it is stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni kooloi akafite mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Storage pests like weevils attack dried grains if left unprotected. Applying approved post-harvest chemical dusts or liquid treatments preserves your stored grain and keeps insects away for many months.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe tamɔ ŋmeii baatutua ŋmaa ni egbi kɛji akɛ abuuu he. Tsofa mli sũ loo tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmaa ni ato lɛ he, ni ebaaha kooloi akabote jɛmɛ nyɔji babaoo.

english: Can I grow beans together with my plantains on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmeii kɛ plantains yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, planting beans alongside plantains is a great farming practice called intercropping. Beans naturally feed the soil with nitrogen, which helps your plantain stems grow thicker and produce bigger fruit bunches while protecting the ground from drying out.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ plantains masɛi lɛ ji okwaayeli nifeemɔ kpakpa ni ale lɛ akɛ intercropping. Beans lɛ kɛ nitrogen haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa plantain tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii wuji yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi.

english: Why do my crops grow faster and look greener on land where I previously planted beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ tsutsu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans are legumes, which means their roots pull natural nitrogen out of the air and put it directly into the dirt. When you harvest the beans, that natural food remains in the soil, acting like a free fertilizer for the next crops you plant.
ga: Beans ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Beni okpaa ŋmeii Adebɔɔ mli niyenii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: I noticed small round bumps on the roots of my bean plants—is this a crop disease?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmei bibioo ko ni yɔɔ kokroo. yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ shishifãi anɔ Ani tso hela ji enɛ?

english: No, those bumps are called root nodules and are a sign of healthy beans. They house beneficial organisms that turn air into soil food, so seeing them means your beans are actively improving your land's fertility.
ga: Dabi, atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ akɛ shishifãi ni ji ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ he okadi. Amɛhiɛɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni tsakeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ efeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ona amɛ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ o-beans lɛ miiha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ waa.

english: Is it better to burn the weeds after clearing my bush or leave them on top of the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaashã jwɛi lɛ kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli loo ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: It is better to leave cleared weeds to decompose on top of the soil as mulch. Burning kills beneficial soil life and destroys natural nutrients, whereas letting the cleared plant material rot builds rich soil and helps retain moisture.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ koni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni ajie lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛgboi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ baa shi jogbaŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why is my farm yielding smaller plantain bunches now compared to three years ago when I first planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ plantains bibii fe beni midu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants feed heavily on nutrients in the earth over time. Planting on the same land repeatedly without adding manure, compost, or crop rotation empties the soil of food, leading to smaller crop yields.
ga: Dumɔwui yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ fataaa he lɛ, niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ baafite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Why do extra young shoots keep coming up around the base of my plantain plant, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ? mi plantain shishitoo Ni ani esa akɛ mafo mli?

english: Those young shoots are called suckers, which are the plantain's natural way of spreading. You should leave only one or two strong suckers for future harvests and remove the rest so they do not steal food and water from the main bearing plant.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii, ni ji gbɛ ni plantain lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Esa akɛ oshi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ kpamɔ ni ojie ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tsei titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli.

english: Will spraying chemical weedkillers poison my soil and ruin my future harvests?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mikɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baafite mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ebaafite wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: When used correctly according to instructions, approved agricultural chemicals do not ruin the soil permanently. However, using too much or applying the wrong types can destroy soil health and leave harmful residues, so always consult an extension officer for proper usage.
ga: Kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi anaa lɛ, okwaayeli tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ daa. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ akɛtsu nii fe nine loo akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni eshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ oyabi o-extension officer lɛ koni ekɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do small holes appear in my harvested beans after a few weeks, and how do I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eje kpo yɛ mi-kɔfi ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ amli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: Those holes are caused by tiny insects called weevils that hatch inside the stored seeds. You can stop them by drying your harvested beans thoroughly under the sun and storing them in sealed, airtight bags or containers.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils ni fɔɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okpa amɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni okpa lɛ ni oooha amɛgbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. ni okɛto kotoku loo tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ naa mli

english: Why do my young plantain leaves dry up and turn yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young plantains have shallow roots and lose water quickly through their large leaves during heavy heat. Covering the root base with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool and moist, stopping the leaves from drying out.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ ni amɛfiteɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ baai wuji anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) ha shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi

english: How do I keep my harvested crops fresh so buyers from neighboring countries will give me a good price?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mikpamɔ lɛ afee ehee bɔni afee ni mɛi ni baahe nii kɛjɛ maji ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ amli lɛ aha mi jara kpakpa?

english: Harvest your crops at the right maturity time, keep them in a cool and shaded area after picking, and use airtight storage for dry crops like beans to ensure they stay fresh and pest-free for long transport.
ga: Kpaa onibii lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli beni okɛto sɛɛ. ni akɛ vacuum storage atsu nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi tamɔ ŋmeii koni ekwɛ akɛ amɛhi shi ehee ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli kɛha gbɛfaa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: I want to start growing watermelons on my farm, but how do I know if I have enough water for them?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi watermelon dumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Shi te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miyɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha mi-watermelon lɛ?

english: Watermelons are mostly made of water, so they require a steady supply throughout their growth. Before planting, you must check if you have a reliable water source nearby, such as a river, well, or dug-out pond, especially during the dry season.
ga: Nu ji nɔ ni akɛfeɔ watermelon babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, ebiɔ nu babaoo be fɛɛ be yɛ edalɛ be fɛɛ mli. Dani obaadu lɛ, kwɛmɔ kɛji nu jɛɛhe ko ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ faa, ŋshɔ, loo nubu ni atsa lɛ yɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli

english: What are the best natural sources of water I can use to irrigate my crops during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni ji adebɔɔ mli nu ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mikɛfɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Streams, shallow wells, harvested rainwater ponds, and rivers are the best low-cost water sources. The main requirement is ensuring the water is clean and easily accessible to your fields so you can water the soil consistently.
ga: Faai, nubui ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, nugbɔshiimɔ nubui, kɛ faai ji nu jɛɛhei ni jara waaa fe fɛɛ lɛ ekomɛi. Nɔ titri ni ataoɔ ji ni okwɛ koni nu lɛ mli atse ni eshɛ oŋmɔji lɛ ahe oya. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ nu afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: How do I tell if my soil is holding too much water for crops like watermelon?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ watermelon?

english: If rainwater stays pooled on top of your soil for days without soaking in, the land is too waterlogged. Watermelons need well-draining soil because excess trapped water rots their roots and kills the plant.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia watermelon ejaakɛ nu ni emɔ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ afite shishifãi lɛ ni egbe tso lɛ.

english: What basic essential items do I need to prepare before I begin planting watermelons?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ masaa mihe dani mabɔi watermelon ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: To start successfully, you need about six basic things: quality watermelon seeds, a reliable water source, proper land preparation tools, organic manure or fertilizer, pest protection, and a clear field layout.
ga: Bɔni afee ni obɔi nitsumɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, nibii titrii enumɔ he miihia bo: Watermelon dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ. nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ Shikpɔŋ he saamɔ nibii ni sa Organic fertilizer loo organic fertilizer Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shikpɔŋ he mfoniri ni mli ka shi faŋŋ

english: What is the very first step I should take when planning a new crop field?
ga: Mɛni ji klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ ni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ miito ŋmɔ hee he gbɛjianɔ?

english: The first step is checking your land's location and resources—specifically testing the soil condition and locating your water source—before buying seeds or clearing land.
ga: Nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni esa akɛ ofee ji ni otsɔɔ he ni oshikpɔŋ kɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɔɔ. Titri lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ shihilɛ kaa kɛ nu jɛɛhei ataomɔ. Dani obaahe dumɔwui loo obaajie shikpɔŋ

english: Why do watermelons require so much patience compared to some other quick vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ watermelon biɔ tsuishitoo babaoo kɛ akɛto aduawai krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Watermelons take about 80 to 90 days to mature and go through critical stages like vine spreading, flowering, and fruit swelling. Missing proper water or care during any of these stages can spoil the whole yield, so patience and daily care are key.
ga: Watermelon heɔ aaafee gbii 80 kɛyashi 90 dani ekwɛ̃ɔ ni etsɔɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ wain tso lɛ mligbɛlɛɛmɔ, fɔfɔii, kɛ aduawai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli. Nu ni sa loo kwɛmɔ ni sa ni bɛ yɛ nifeemɔ fɛɛ nifeemɔ mli Enɛɛmɛi baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsuishitoo kɛ daa gbi kwɛmɔ he miihia.

english: How should I structure the spacing in my field when setting up watermelon plants?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mato gbɛ ni kã mi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ beni miduɔ watermelon tsei lɛ?

english: Watermelon plants grow as crawling vines that spread wide across the ground. You need to space mounds roughly 1.5 to 2 meters apart so the vines have plenty of room to spread and capture sunlight without choking each other.
ga: Watermelon tsei daa ni amɛfeɔ wain tsei ni shwereɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Obaasumɔ ni oshi aaafee mitai 1.5 kɛyashi 2 yɛ gɔji lɛ ateŋ bɔni afee ni wain tsei lɛ aná he ko babaoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkpɛ ni amɛná hulu la ni amɛtsiii amɛhe gbɛ.

english: Why do my watermelon leaves droop or wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ watermelon baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgboɔ yɛ shwane be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watermelons have broad leaves that lose moisture quickly under strong heat. Drooping is the plant's natural defense to conserve water, signaling that the soil needs a deep watering at the root level.
ga: Watermelon yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi. Defoliation ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛbu nu he. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni mli kwɔ he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Why do extension officers encourage us to form farming groups rather than working alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ okwaayeli kui ahe gbɛjianɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkome amɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Working in a group allows farmers to share irrigation equipment, learn proper field setups together, negotiate better prices for seeds and fertilizers, and easily invite agricultural officers for training.
ga: Kuu mli nitsumɔ haa okwaafoi lɛ jaa nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ he nibii. Kasemɔ bɔ ni atoɔ he ni sa he gbɛjianɔ yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli. Tsɔɔmɔ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ nine yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ kɛha tsɔsemɔ

english: How does learning farm setups in a group help a beginner farmer like me avoid mistakes?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ bɔ ni atoɔ ŋmɔ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ kuu mli lɛ kasemɔ baanyɛ aye abua okwaafoi heei tamɔ mi ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ tɔmɔi ahe?

english: In a group setup, you can watch step-by-step demonstrations on a shared plot, see practical solutions to common water or pest problems, and get immediate guidance from experienced farmers before trying it on your own land.
ga: yɛ kuu ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ mli Obaanyɛ okwɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ni tsɔɔ nɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aja nɔ lɛ nɔ. Taomɔ bɔ ni ooofee osaa nu loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Ni ná ŋaawoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ adɛŋ dani oka lɛ okwɛ yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I plant food crops like plantain or cassava before putting cocoa seedlings on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains loo cassava? Dani madu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Food crops grow quickly and provide immediate food and income while creating essential temporary shade that protects young cocoa seedlings from scorching sun rays.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya ni amɛhaa niyenii kɛ shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ baa.

english: Can I grow food crops and cocoa trees on the exact same piece of land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii kɛ cacao tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, during the first two to three years of your cocoa farm, you can intercrop with plantain, cassava, or cocoyam to maximize land use until the cocoa canopy closes.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ loo etɛ ni akɛtsuɔ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ okɛ plantain, cassava loo cocoa awo mli koni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii babaoo kɛyashi be mli ni cocoa buu lɛ baakpa.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect their underground roots, sprouting new leaves automatically when the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Baai heei baakwɛ̃ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade plants around them to grow properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo abɔle cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are delicate and easily burn under intense direct sunlight; shade plants create a cooler microclimate that helps the seedlings establish strong roots.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ feɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ni yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting cocoa before the trees start giving me fruit?
ga: Kɛ́ odu kookoo lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties typically start producing pods within 2 to 3 years, whereas older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning pale yellow instead of rich green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or waterlogged roots that are unable to absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in waterlogged or heavy clay soil where excess rain cannot drain away, suffocating the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ. ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: How do I know if my farmland has the right soil for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ?

english: Good cocoa soil is deep, loose, rich in organic matter, and well-drained so water does not stand in pools after heavy rain.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ mli. ni etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ No hewɔ lɛ, nu ehiɛɛɛ nubu lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ.

english: Why do extension officers always advise us to plant right at the start of the major rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa be fɛɛ be akɛ adu tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting early gives crops continuous rain for several months, allowing them to build deep root systems before the next dry season arrives.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Ehaa tsei lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be nyɔji babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over during heavy winds and rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and top-heavy when carrying bunches, so supporting them with wooden props prevents wind from snapping or uprooting them.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛji awó ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tso fĩ esɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akakumɔ lɛ loo ekajie lɛ kɛjɛ eshishifãi amli.

english: Will my cassava crops still produce big tubers if I plant them under dense tree shade?
ga: Ani mi-cassava tso lɛ baawo ŋmeii wuji lolo kɛji midu lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii shishi?

english: Cassava needs direct, strong sunshine to produce food for root growth; planting it under heavy shade causes the leaves to grow tall while leaving the tubers small and undeveloped.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ená niyenii kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi bibii ni amɛdarako.

english: Does planting my cowpeas in full sunlight help them yield better than in shaded areas?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa yibii kpakpai baa fe he ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas thrive in full sunshine, using solar energy to build strong stems and produce healthy pods, whereas shaded plants become weak and yield fewer beans.
ga: Cowpeas daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ekɛ hulu hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ shade lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up into tight tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize leaves curl up on hot afternoons as a defense mechanism to reduce their surface area and minimize water loss during intense heat.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ shi.

english: Why do my leaf vegetables look weak and wilted at noon even if I watered them in the early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli leebi?

english: Intense midday sunshine causes water to evaporate from leaves faster than the roots can draw it from the soil, causing temporary wilting until the temperature drops.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and burning around the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, intense sunshine, and leaf burning is a sign of heat stress that requires shade crops like plantains to protect them.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Ni baai ni shãa lɛ ji dɔlɛ he haomɔ he okadi ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ni yɔɔ shade tamɔ plantains lɛ abu he.

english: How does intense heat and sunshine affect my tomato plants when they start flowering?
ga: Te dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ saa mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Extreme sun and heat can dry out tomato pollen, causing the flowers to drop off before setting fruit.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine kɛ dɔlɛ baanyɛ aha tomato pollen lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How does strong sunshine help my mangoes ripen while they are still on the tree?
ga: Te hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi mango lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Direct sunlight warms the fruit and triggers natural enzymes that convert stored starches into sugars, helping the mango ripen and sweeten naturally.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa aduawai lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli enzymes ni tsakeɔ starch ni ato lɛ feɔ sugar lɛ tsuɔ nii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni mango lɛ shwereɔ ni efeɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my harvested pepper seeds fail to sprout after I dry them directly under the harsh sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni migbi amɛ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Drying seeds under very harsh, direct sunlight can overheat and damage the living seed embryo inside, so seeds should be dried in a well-ventilated, shaded spot.
ga: Dumɔwui ni agbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ adɔ fe nine ni efite fɔmɔ kotokui ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni shade yɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster in open, sunlit cleared land compared to under dense crop foliage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ kɛ akɛto hei ni tsei ahe tsei babaoo yɔɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weed seeds require direct light to trigger germination, and open sunshine provides maximum light energy for rapid weed growth.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ he miihia kane tɛ̃ɛ koni eha amɛkwɛ̃. Ni hulu la ni agbele naa lɛ haa la hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ kɛha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ oya.

english: Why do young sunflower stems lean and follow the sun across the sky during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulutsoo fɔfɔi lɛ nyiɛɔ hulu lɛ sɛɛ kɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Sunflowers naturally turn their stems toward the sun as it moves from east to west to capture as much light as possible for photosynthesis, a process known as heliotropism.
ga: Hulu fɔfɔii lɛ tsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa hulu lɛ he beni amɛjɛɔ bokagbɛ kɛyaa anaigbɛ koni amɛmɔmɔ la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛha fotosintɛsis. Enɛ ji nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ heliotropism.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide temporary shade and moisture, helping the young cocoa seedlings survive their first few years until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa.

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak plants that produce tiny ears of corn instead of healthy, large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tso bibioo ko ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmãa toi bibii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona ŋmei agbo ni mli wa

english: Yam vines use stakes to lift their leaves up toward the sun. When leaves catch plenty of sunlight, the plant creates more food and energy, which it sends underground to grow larger tubers.
ga: Yiŋtoo titri ni yɔɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ ji ni ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ baafee niyenii kɛ hewalɛ babaoo. ni abaamaje shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an important food in the soil, or that waterlogged soil is preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli Aloo sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize relies on and allows maize pests to build up in the ground. Switching crops, especially by planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts, rebuilds soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi damɔ nɔ ni eye ebua abɛi mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ. Ebaatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ama shi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Covering the soil, called mulching, acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground during hot days, keeps root zones cool, and stops weeds from stealing food from your crops.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as very hot weather, dry soil, or poor nutrients. The plant drops flowers to save its energy to survive rather than produce peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni esaaa. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in the leaves and funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛhe ŋmeii lɛ egbɛ eshwa lɛ?

english: Small ragged holes in young maize are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on tender leaves. They hide inside the center funnel of the plant during the day to feed undisturbed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fall armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni niyenii akagbala amɛ.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems from my old harvest to plant a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii momo lɛ amli koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Select firm, healthy stems from the middle section of mature cassava plants that show no signs of pests or rotting. Stems from the middle store the right amount of food to sprout strong shoots and roots quickly.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmei tso ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo ŋmei bɛ mli. Tso ni jɛɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ toɔ niyenii ni sa koni ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi ni wa lɛ adara oya.

english: How can I tell if my pepper crops are getting too much water during heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: When pepper plants sit in waterlogged soil, their leaves turn yellow and start to wilt even though the soil is soaked. This happens because drowned roots rot and can no longer draw oxygen or nutrients from the soil.
ga: Beni pepper tso lɛ ta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaabɔi ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ shishifãi ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie kɔɔyɔɔ loo niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong, green leaves. Adding manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help them turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara waa.

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the soil is moist—like right after a gentle rain—and when the crop is actively growing. Applying it during dry spells can burn the roots, while applying it right before a heavy downpour can wash the food away.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, tamɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ fioo sɛɛ kɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii miida jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã. Yɛ be mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha niyenii lɛ afite.

english: Why do I need to clear only some trees instead of cutting everything down before planting my cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei komɛi amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mafo nɔ fɛɛ nɔ dani madu kookoo lɛ?

english: Cocoa plants thrive best under partial shade because full sunlight can dry out the soil and burn young cocoa leaves. Leaving some tall forest trees provides shade, retains soil moisture, and protects your cocoa from harsh heat.
ga: Kookoo tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be fioo yɔɔ lɛ ejaakɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni eshã kookoo baai bibii lɛ. Tsei kakadaji ni ashiɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli koni amɛha hulutsoo Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebu kookoo he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he

english: Why shouldn't I plant many maize seeds in one single hole to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds in one hole forces the seedlings to fight each other for the same small pocket of food and water. This results in thin, weak stalks that produce very small ears or no grain at all.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu kotokui bibii ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ, ni no haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shĩɔ toi bibii waa loo dumɔwui ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight to produce food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground into maximum sunlight, which prevents leaf diseases and produces much larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulb agbo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni efɔ lɛ kɛyashi ebaaná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ foliar helai anaa ni ehaa sweet potatoes ni dara babaoo baa.

english: Should I cut off the extra small suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani ajie tso titri lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving too many suckers causes them to fight with the mother plant for food and water, resulting in small plantain bunches. Pruning them to leave just one or two strong follow-up suckers ensures large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii babaoo ni ashiɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ haa amɛkɛ tso nyɛ lɛ wuɔ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ mli koni ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaawo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Does letting weeds grow around my crops harm them, or do they just share the sunlight?
ga: Aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiye amɛ awui loo amɛmiija hulu la lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Weeds actively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. If weeds are left to grow, your crops will become starved and produce a very small harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji aŋmɛ jwɛi gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo pɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long because the roots drown without air, allowing soil fungi to attack them. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ boteɔ nu mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough water. Extreme heat stresses the plant, forcing it to drop its flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato aduawai lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant as the fruit develops. It usually happens when watering is irregular, so keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant take up calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛná calcium ni sa.

english: What is the real difference between using my harvested maize as seed for next season and buying certified seed?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ dumɔwui kɛha be ni baa lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ hemɔ teŋ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred and treated to resist diseases and produce high yields, while standard harvested grain might not grow well, could carry diseases, or may not sprout evenly.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ ni atsaa amɛ koni helai akamɔ amɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ekolɛ dumɔwui ni akpaa yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ edaŋ jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aba loo ebaanyɛ ekwɛɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ

english: Can I sell the extra corn left in my barn as planting seeds to other farmers to make more money?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa ni eshwɛ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ maha okwaafoi krokomɛi koni maná shika babaoo?

english: No, grain stored in a barn is meant for eating or processing. To sell produce as seed, it must meet strict quality standards, have guaranteed germination rates, and be certified disease-free.
ga: Dabi, ŋmaa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji niyeli loo nitsumɔ pɛ. Kɛji akɛ abaahɔ̃ɔ nibii ni adu lɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ, esa akɛ eshɛ shishitoo mlai ni mli wa ni kɔɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe lɛ ahe. Eyɛ nɔmimaa akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ akɛ hela bɛ mli

english: If I bought certified seeds for planting but have leftovers, can I grind them into flour to eat or sell as food grain?
ga: Kɛ mihe dumɔwui ni awo he odase ni miyɛ ekomɛi ni eshwɛ lolo lɛ, Ani abaanyɛ atsɔ mli afee ashikishaŋ ni ayeɔ loo ahɔ̃ɔ akɛ dumɔwui?

english: No, certified seeds are treated with protective chemicals to prevent insect damage in the soil. Consuming treated seeds or selling them for food is dangerous to human health.
ga: Dabi, akɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii koni kooloi akafite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni atsa amɛ lɛ ni ayeɔ loo ni ahɔ̃ɔ akɛ niyenii lɛ yeɔ adesa hewalɛnamɔ awui.

english: Why should I spend money to buy new seed every season when I can just keep some of my harvested grain for free?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika kɛhe dumɔwui heei daa afi lɛ? Akɛni minyɛ mikɛ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi to yaka hewɔ lɛ.

english: Certified seeds produce much higher crop yields and resist local pests far better. The extra money you make from a bigger harvest usually covers the cost of buying fresh seed.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, shika kroko ni onáa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi wuji amli lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui heei ahe nyɔmɔwoo he nyɔmɔ.

english: How do I know when my maize crop is mature enough to harvest as grain so I can sell it to clear my farm debts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa akɛ ŋmaa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ koni akɛwo ŋmɔ mli nyɔmɔ?

english: Maize is ready to harvest as grain when the leaves turn dry and yellow, the silks on the cob turn brown, and the kernels become hard enough that your fingernail cannot dent them.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa akɛ ŋmaa kɛji baai lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Siliki kpãai ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaŋ otsitsii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why did the maize grains I took directly from my food storage fail to sprout when I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu lɛ?

english: Grains stored for food lose their vitality over time due to humidity, heat, or insect damage. Proper seeds are harvested early, dried carefully, and kept under controlled conditions to ensure they sprout.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ akɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ ŋmɔtɔ, dɔlɛ, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahewɔ. Kpaa dumɔwui ni sa lɛ mra. Gbi jogbaŋŋ. ni akɛtoɔ shihilɛi ni akudɔɔ mli koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do buyers pay less for my maize grain compared to cash crops like cocoa or cashew?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ he nyɔmɔ fioo kɛ akɛtoɔ shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo loo cashew nuts he lɛ?

english: Maize is a local food crop harvested by many farmers at the same time, which lowers local market prices. Cash crops like cocoa are sold to international markets with higher global demand.
ga: Abɛi ji maŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni okwaafoi babaoo kpaa yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haa jara baa shi yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ. Akɛ shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo hɔ̃ɔ majimaji ateŋ jarayeli hei ni jeŋ muu fɛɛ nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to sell my harvested grain immediately or store it for later when prices go up?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo mikɛto kɛha sɛɛ mli beni jara lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ?

english: Selling immediately helps pay off urgent farm expenses, but market prices are lowest during harvest. If you dry your grain properly, storing it for a few months lets you sell when prices rise.
ga: Kɛ́ ahɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni awo ŋmɔ mli nyɔmɔwoo ni he hiaa oya lɛ. Shi jara ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ baa shi fe fɛɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Kɛji ogbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ Okɛto nyɔji fioo lɛ baaye abua bo ni ohɔ̃ɔ kɛji ejara tee hiɛ.

english: Why does my harvested grain start rotting or molding after I pack it into bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ loo amɛhe miifee nɔ ko beni mikɛwo baagi mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain still holds moisture inside. If you put it into bags before drying it thoroughly under the sun, trapped moisture encourages mold to grow and ruins your grain.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli lolo. Kɛ okɛwo kotoku mli dani egbi yɛ hulu lɛ mli lɛ, Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How can I protect my stored grain from insects so I do not lose money when waiting for better prices?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe? Bɔni afee ni akafite shika yɛ be mli ni mɛɔ jara ni hi fe no lɛ?

english: Dry your grain until it is hard, clean your storehouse well, and use airtight hermetic storage bags (like PICS bags) which suffocate insects naturally without needing harmful chemicals.
ga: Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ koni ewa. Tsumɔ nitoohe lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ni okɛ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe ni akɛ vacuum efo mli (tamɔ PICS kotokui), ni baaha kooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ atsu nii ni akɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tsuuu nii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or the roots are drowning in excess water, which stops them from taking up the food they need.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ miiho yɛ nu ni fa fe nine mli. Enɛ haaa onyɛ oye niyenii ni osumɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of green leaves but produce very few beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or manure, the cowpea plant puts all its energy into growing green vines and leaves instead of making flowers and pods.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo ŋmeii babaoo Cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ wain tsei kɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaafee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Cassava roots rot when heavy rains cause water to collect in the soil around the roots, choking off air and allowing soil fungi to decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha nu bua ehe naa yɛ sũ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli, ni ehaa amɛmuɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl tightly upward during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to intense heat and conserve water, though persistent curling can also indicate insect-spread plant viruses.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulutsoo ni naa wa baa amɛnɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛ nu ahi mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ hela ko yɛ tso lɛ mli ni kooloo lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa moŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight, which allows the leaves to make food that travels back down to feed and grow large, heavy tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi kɛyaa shi kɛyaa niyenii ni edaa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow together, they steal water and nutrients from the main stem, resulting in small plantain bunches instead of a large yield.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni afee babaoo lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers fall off without developing into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers if the field gets too hot and dry or if there are no tiny midges—beneficial insects that live in moist leaf litter—around to pollinate the blooms.
ga: Cocoa tsei baafɔ kɛji he lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni hiɔ baai ni mli efɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ bɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers and small green peppers onto the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔii kɛ pepper bibii eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers and young fruit when they experience stress from sudden changes in temperature, irregular watering, or extreme sunshine to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii kɛji hulutsoo tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa lɛ ha amɛhao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be Aloo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa koni okɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do very small cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up while still tiny on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is called cherelle wilt; the cocoa tree naturally discards extra pods it knows it cannot feed with its current water and nutrient supply, though excess shade can worsen it.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni amɛle akɛ anyɛɛɛ akɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aha lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Shi kɛlɛ, hulutsoo be babaoo baanyɛ aha kookoo tsei lɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why are some of my maize stalks breaking easily and showing tiny holes with powdery dirt near the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ekomɛi fãa oya ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Muji yɛ tso lɛ masɛi.

english: Maize stem borer caterpillars hatch on the leaves and tunnel inside the stalk, eating the plant from the inside out and blocking food from reaching the maize ears.
ga: Abele stem borers lɛ fɔɔ yɛ baai kɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ anɔ. Ye tsei kɛjɛ mli kɛya kponɔgbɛ ni ehaa niyenii shɛɔ ŋmãa toi lɛ ahe

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants full of tiny holes and looking like someone chewed them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni etamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko miiye lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the maize leaves. They eat the tender growth at night, which can kill the whole plant if you do not clear them early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa baai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ gbɛkɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ akpata tso muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ kɛji ojieee amɛ mra.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, damp conditions. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air to dry the farm and reduce the rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fitemɔ baa shi.

english: Your soil likely has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium. Nitrogen makes leaves and stems grow big, but plants need potassium to swell their roots into big tubers.
ga: Ekolɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nitrogen babaoo tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen haa baai kɛ tsei ashishifãi daa. Shi tsei he miihia potassium koni amɛshishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans makes the soil better for the next season's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have helpful bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen food from the air and leave it in the dirt, acting like natural fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nibii ni ji nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni eshiɔ amɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my tomato plants turning light yellow instead of rich green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the plant is running out of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives leaves their dark green color and helps the plant grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does the ground around my garden dry up so fast even after I water it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle Mibɔɔ lɛ he lɛ gĩɔ oya waa kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo nɔ po lɛ?

english: Direct hot sun bakes bare dirt and evaporates water quickly. Covering the bare soil with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool and traps the water inside.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ shãa muji ni ehaa nu lɛ feɔ lasu oya. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ mli.

english: You should wait until the main rains start consistently and soak the soil deep down, rather than planting after the very first light shower which can dry out and scorch your seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔi titrii lɛ baaje shishi amɛba shi ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ waa. Moŋ lɛ, dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ fioo ni nɛ lɛ sɛɛ, ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛshã.

english: Why is it important to put wooden tall stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to generate food for the growing yam underground. Lifting the vines off the dirt also stops soil diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛha sweet potato ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ akatutua baai lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and yellow even if the soil looks good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds are fast thieves that aggressively drink the water, take the sunlight, and steal the plant food out of the soil before your crop gets a chance to use it.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni he yɔɔ oya ni nuɔ nu, amɛmuɔ hulu la, ni amɛjuɔ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛkɛkɛtsuɔ nii.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their soft leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains or keeping larger trees protects young cocoa until their roots and branches are mature enough to tolerate full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni eda ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo bibii ahe kɛyashi shishifãi kɛ eniji lɛ adara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tip usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong cobs.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, o-corn tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛfeɔ amɛ ŋmɔji kɛ amɛ ŋmeii ni wa lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I wait until the soil is wet before putting fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the plant roots can drink it. If you put dry fertilizer on dry soil under a hot sun, it can burn the plant roots or evaporate into the air and be wasted.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Tse lɛ shishifãi baanyɛ ashã loo amɛfo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfite.

english: Does it matter which direction I push my cassava stems into the ground?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni ashɛre ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the tiny leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new shoots to waste energy turning themselves around underground, leading to weak plants and small tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi ni aduɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ haa tsei ahe tsei heei fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ bulb bibii baa.

english: Planting seeds too close together causes the crops to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. This leaves you with tall, skinny plants that produce smaller fruits or smaller maize cobs than plants given enough room to grow.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa onáa tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni woɔ yibii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii fe tso ni yɔɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant experiences sudden drought. Stress from heat or lack of water forces the plant to drop flowers to save its own life.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ trukaa. Dɔlɛ mli haomɔ loo nu ni faaa yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni ehere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and look dead during hot afternoons even when the soil isn't completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egboi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiko kwraa moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, water evaporates from leaves faster than roots can drink it from the ground. The plant temporarily wilts to close its pores and hold onto moisture, usually recovering when the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nu shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛŋa eshishifãi lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juices underneath the leaves. Spraying with neem oil or appropriate pest control stops these insects from damaging new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofai krokomɛi ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves out to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the vine produce the food needed to swell and grow large underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa wain tso lɛ ni enáa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni ekwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do crops grow much better on land that was left to rest for a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ashi ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ afii fioo komɛi nɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving land to rest allows wild plants to grow, shed leaves, and decay, naturally putting rich food back into the soil. It also breaks the cycle of pests and diseases that build up when you plant the same crop every year.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe lɛ haa koo mli tsei kwɛ̃ɔ, amɛbaai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni amɛgboiɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, niyenii babaoo kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ hu mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to stay green and grow fast. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or keep the roots too wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda oya. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo eha shishifãi lɛ efɔ tsɔ.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the sap under the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects during dry, hot weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi ni edɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big leaves but producing small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from soil or heavy fertilizers, it spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei náa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii mli. Ekɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that dry out quickly under direct hot sun. They need shade from plants like plantain to protect them during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains amli koni ebu amɛhe yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over easily during rainy season winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have very shallow roots that do not go deep into the earth. When the soil becomes soft from rain and the heavy fruit bunch makes the tree top-heavy, strong winds easily pull the roots out.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ lɛ mli kɛ aduawai ni tsii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ haa tsei lɛ ayitsei lɛ nuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbalaa shishifãi lɛ oya.

english: Why are flowers dropping off my tomato plants without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or lack of nutrients like phosphorus that help flowers develop into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful bacteria in the soil to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the cowpea roots rot, they leave free nitrogen fertilizer in the soil for your maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji cowpea shishifãi lɛ egbo Ebaashi nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha o-corn lɛ.

english: Why do groundnut flower stems push themselves down into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: That is natural for groundnuts. After the flower is pollinated above ground, the plant produces a growing stem called a peg that pushes into the dark, moist soil where the groundnut pods actually form and grow.
ga: No ji adebɔɔ naa nɔ kɛha ŋmeii. Beni fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni edɔ lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni pods lɛ feɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ.

english: Why do weeds come up faster than my crops right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are naturally adapted to survive harsh dry conditions in the soil and can sprout very quickly with tiny amounts of rain, while crop seeds take longer to absorb water and start growing.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ̃ oya waa kɛ́ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui heɔ be babaoo dani amɛ nu nu ni amɛ jeɔ dalɛ shishi.

english: Why are small green fruits dropping off my mango tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mango tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Trees drop extra fruit when they do not have enough water or nutrients to feed all of them to maturity, or when fruit fly pests damage the young fruits inside.
ga: Tsei lɛ baawo yibii krokomɛi kɛ́ amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛ fɛɛ amɛhi shi kɛyashi amɛdara. aloo beni tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why am I finding small white eggs and tiny white grubs in the soil around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ lɛ? Kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ ni yɔɔ sũ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ mli.

english: White grubs in the soil are usually the larvae of beetles that lay their eggs underground. They feed on young crop roots, which can stunt your plants or cause them to wilt if not controlled early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmeii bibii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Amɛyeɔ tsei bibii ashishifãi ni baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afee shoo loo eha amɛgboi kɛji akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I do not give it enough fertilizer while it is growing?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa haaa lɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Crops that lack proper feeding grow weak, turn yellow, and stay small. Without enough nutrients in the soil, they will produce tiny, underdeveloped ears or fail to yield any grain at all.
ga: Tsei ni niyenii ni sa haaa amɛ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ bibioo Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Amɛwoɔ toi bibii ni edako jogbaŋŋ loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui kwraa.

english: Why does my cassava crop take up to a full year before it is ready for harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ heɔ afi muu fɛɛ dani eshɛɔ he ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava uses its first few months to build leaves and stems above ground. Only later does it focus on storing food underground to expand into the big tubers you harvest, which takes 9 to 12 months.
ga: Yucca heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ dani ewoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, nɔ ni akɛjwɛŋmɔ maa nɔ ji niyenii lɛ ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni eda ni etsɔ bulb agbo ni okpaa, ni enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12.

english: Why do my yam vines look dry and dead during the dry season even though the tuber inside the ground is still alive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi ni egbo yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam plants go into a sleeping state called dormancy to survive hot, dry weather. The top vine dies back to save water, but the tuber underground remains healthy and ready to sprout when rains return.
ga: Sweet potato tsei boteɔ wɔɔhe shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy mli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Wein tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gboiɔ koni amɛbu nu he. Shi shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ miiya nɔ waa lolo ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ba ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if insect pests are attacking my stored grains in the barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai miitutua ŋmaa ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You will notice powdery dust around the bottom of bags, see tiny holes in the seeds where beetles have hatched, and sometimes hear faint rustling sounds as the insects move inside the stored grain.
ga: Obaana ashikishaŋ ni ebɔle kotoku lɛ shishi, kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli he ni ŋmeii lɛ efɔ yɛ lɛ. Ni bei komɛi lɛ, minuɔ gbee ko ni miitswa blɛoo. Beni kooloi bibii lɛ yaa dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: How do caterpillar pests end up on my vegetable leaves when I did not plant them there?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwieɔ mi-vegetables baai lɛ anɔ? Akɛni miduuu jɛmɛ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Adult moths and butterflies fly across your farm and lay tiny eggs on the underside of crop leaves. When these eggs hatch, small caterpillars emerge and immediately start eating the leaves.
ga: Kplukai kɛ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ foɔ kɛtsɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ tsei ahe baai lɛ ashishi. Nɛkɛ wɔji nɛɛ fɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii. Amɛbaaje kpo ni amɛbaabɔi baai yeli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil is too weak to feed my crops properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your crops grow very slowly, have pale yellow leaves, and produce undersized fruit, your soil lacks essential nutrients and needs manure, compost, or fertilizer added to nourish the plants.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo waa Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni ekɛ yibii babaoo hu baaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo mli koni ekɛha otsei lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants staying tiny and refusing to sprout new branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ji bibioo nɛkɛ ni ekpooɔ ni ekɛ niji heei baaje kpo lɛ?

english: When young plants don't get enough water, food, or sunlight, or if hidden root pests are damaging them underneath, their growth freezes and they stay stunted.
ga: Beni tsei bibii lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu, niyenii loo hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ miifite tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Dalɛ baafee mlɛo ni amɛ hu amɛbaafee mlɛo.

english: How do I know when my crops have finished growing and are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbe naa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Crops show clear physical signs when mature, such as lower leaves turning yellow and drying up, stems dropping, or fruits changing color and reaching their full size.
ga: Tsei jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ. fallen trunk Aloo aduawai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su ni eyiɔ obɔ kɛ dalɛ.

english: What causes my young crops to droop and look lifeless in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni haa midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ mli yɛ shwane mli?

english: High heat causes plants to lose water from their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. They droop temporarily during the hottest hours to reduce water loss and protect themselves.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of just saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Certified seeds are carefully selected and tested to ensure high germination rates, strong disease resistance, and bigger yields. Using old saved seeds often leads to weaker plants and lower harvests because diseases pass down from the parent plant.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Helai ahe hewalɛ ni hi ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni etsɛ ni ato lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi be mli ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What causes my seeds to rot underground instead of sprouting after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni haa midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ beni midu sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds rot mainly when planted too deep in waterlogged soil that lacks air, or when fungi attack them before they can germinate. Planting in well-drained soil at the right depth helps them sprout quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ titri kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ nɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni ŋmeii tutuaa dumɔwui dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flowers down into the soil after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts develop their pods underground. After the yellow flower on top is pollinated, the plant grows a long stem called a peg that pushes into the dirt so the peanut can safely grow into a full pod beneath the soil.
ga: Peanuts feɔ pods yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni afee fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pollination sɛɛ. Tsei yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do I know when my groundnut crop is ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-peanut ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ?

english: You can check by pulling up a few test plants and opening the pods. If the inner pod lining has dark brown or black veins and the nuts fill the shell completely, your crop is mature and ready to harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ kaa tsei fioo komɛi ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi ni ogbele ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni ajie amɛhe ŋmeii Etsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why does rice need so much water on the field compared to crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa biɔ nu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants have very shallow root systems that cannot reach deep groundwater. They need consistent surface moisture to absorb essential soil nutrients and develop healthy grain heads.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Ehe miihia ni amɛná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛná ŋmaa yitsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young rice crop turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-rice tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually show that the rice plant is starving for nitrogen or suffering in poorly drained, airless soil. Applying the right balance of fertilizer early on restores green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmã tsei lɛ amli loo amɛyɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ mra lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers say planting beans improves the richness of my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa lɛ?

english: Bean roots have small nodules containing helpful bacteria that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. This naturally enriches the soil for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Bean shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni yɔɔ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my bean flowers dropping off the plant before producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Bean plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, severe drought, or pest attacks like flower thrips. Keeping the soil moist and managing pests saves the flowers so pods can form.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ baagbo kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni pods lɛ afee.

english: Why does millet manage to grow well in dry weather where my other crops wither and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ? He ni miŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ shwieɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: Millet has deep, efficient roots and specialized leaves that prevent water loss. This makes it extremely tough during dry spells, allowing it to produce grains even with low rainfall.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ baai krɛdɛɛi ni tsiɔ nu ni sɛɛ efoɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa ewaa titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ aduɔ dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ fioo po nɛɔ lɛ.

english: When is the right time to harvest my millet head so birds do not ruin it?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa bulbs koni okpoi akafite amɛ?

english: Harvest your millet when the seed heads turn hard and golden-brown, and the main leaves begin to dry up. Harvesting promptly prevents birds and mold from destroying your harvest.
ga: Kpaa ŋmãa lɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ wa ni amɛfee shika tsuru. ni baai titrii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ Nikpamɔ oya lɛ baatsi okpoi kɛ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkafite onibii lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or get moldy so quickly after I bring it inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo ehiɛɔ oya beni mikɛba maŋsɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize spoils quickly if it is not dried properly before storage. High moisture attracts mold and insects, so drying your grain under the sun until it is completely hard prevents spoilage and keeps it safe for a long time.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ agbiko lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ni ooogbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite ni ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I store my dried grains so they last for up to two years without insects destroying them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ ato kɛyashi afii enyɔ ni kooloi bibii efiteee?

english: You can keep grains safe for long periods by using airtight storage containers or hermetic bags (like PICS bags) and keeping them off the ground in a cool, dry room to cut off air and moisture that pests need to survive.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmaa ato he ko shweshweeshwe be kakadaŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsɛnsi ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo vacuum bag (tamɔ PICS bag) nɔ ni okɛto shikpɔŋ yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni mli egbi mli. Koni efo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to sort through my crops before I pack them away in my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mahala miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani mikɛwo nitoohe lɛ?

english: Sorting allows you to remove crops that are already damaged, bruised, or infested. If you leave bad grains or tubers mixed with good ones, the rot and insects will quickly spread to the healthy harvest.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ ojieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite momo, ni egbɔjɔ, loo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Kɛji oshi dumɔwui gbohii loo ŋmeii ni akɛ dumɔwui kpakpai efutu mli lɛ, Rot kɛ kooloi ahelai baagbɛ ashwã oya kɛyakpamɔ ni ehiii nɔ.

english: Why do my stored yams start to rot even when I stack them inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ lɛ? Ni mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli?
