english: Yams rot easily if there is no air movement around them or if they are piled directly on top of each other on the floor. Storing them upright on raised wooden racks in a well-ventilated yam barn keeps them dry and fresh.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ amɛhe. aloo kɛji akɛ ato shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Ato shi jaŋŋ yɛ tso shĩa ko ni awo nɔ yɛ sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Ehaa egbiɔ ni efeɔ ehee.

english: What causes my cassava to turn dark and spoil just a few days after I harvest it?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava roots naturally react with oxygen and break down rapidly once dug out of the soil. To prevent this, cassava should either be eaten right away or processed into long-lasting products like gari or cassava flour within two days of harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii tsuɔ nii lɛ feɔ ekome yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni kɛ́ atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, efiteɔ oya. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ enɛ naa lɛ esa akɛ aye Cassava amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo afee lɛ nibii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ gari loo cassava ashikiŋsha yɛ gbii enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni akpa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I place my bags of harvested grain directly on the concrete floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ kotokui woɔ kɔnkrit nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Concrete floors draw moisture up from the ground, which gets absorbed by the bags at the bottom. Placing your bags on raised wooden pallets keeps them off the cold floor and stops mold from growing.
ga: Kɔnkrit shikpɔŋ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi. ni kotoku ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baaŋɔ mli Kɛ́ okɛ kotokui wo tsei ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha fɛ̃i akabote mli, ni ebaaha ŋmeii akakwɛ̃.

english: How do I test if my harvested cowpeas are dry enough for long-term storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji mi-cowpea ni akpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ?

english: You can test dry cowpeas by biting down gently on a grain. If it makes a sharp cracking sound and your fingernail cannot leave an dent in the skin, it is dry enough to be stored safely without rotting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka tsina ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni oooye lɛ fioo lɛ nɔ. Kɛji efee gbee ni naa wa ni tswaa Ni otsitsii lɛ eshiŋ ŋmeii yɛ ohewolo nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto shweshweeshwe ni efiteee.

english: Why do some of my crops spoil faster when I store different types together in the same space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛ tsei babaoo to he kome lɛ?

english: Different crops release different amounts of moisture and heat as they rest. Storing wet crops next to dry ones transfers moisture, which creates a hot, humid environment that speeds up rotting for all the crops in that room.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ srɔtoi yɛ be mli ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe lɛ. Nibii ni efɔ ni akɛtoɔ tsei ni egbi lɛ ahe lɛ baajie fɛ̃i kɛya. ni haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tsu lɛ mli lɛ agbo oya.

english: How does keeping my storage room cool and dark help preserve my harvested food?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ mli ni aaaha efee fɛ̃i ni edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni akpa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Insects, mold, and rot thrive in warm, damp, and lit spaces. Keeping your storehouse cool, dry, and dark slows down insect breeding and prevents stored food from breaking down too quickly.
ga: Koolooi, ŋmei, kɛ fitemɔ yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni edɔɔ, efɔ, la eyi mli obɔ. Kɛji oha onitoohe lɛ mli ejɔɔ, egbi, ni edɔ lɛ, ebaaha koolooi kɛ amɛhe afee yakayaka nii. ni otsi niyenii ni ato lɛ naa koni ekafite oya tsɔ

english: What causes my stored bag of grain to feel warm when I put my hand inside it?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-rice kotoku ni mikɛto lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ mi kɛ́ mikɛ minine wo mli?

english: A warm bag of grain is a sign that insects or mold are actively living and breeding inside it, generating heat from trapped moisture. When this happens, the grain needs to be taken out, sun-dried again, and put into a clean container.
ga: Dumɔwui kotoku ni mli edɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii loo ŋmeii miihi shi ni amɛmiifɔ bii yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ baa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ enɛ ba lɛ Esa akɛ ajie dumɔwui lɛ. Hulu lɛ ekoŋŋ ni okɛwo tsɛnsi ni mli tse mli

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when rain does not fall for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: When water is low, maize plants struggle to take up nitrogen from the soil, which is the nutrient responsible for deep green leaves. Yellowing is the crop's natural stress signal that it lacks nitrogen and water to produce food properly.
ga: Kɛ nu fioo pɛ eshwɛ lɛ Abɛi tsei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛjie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli Yellow ji adebɔɔ mli haomɔ he okadi ni tsɔɔ tsei ni bɛ nitrogen kɛ nu ni baaha amɛye niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die during the hot, dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade crops like plantain or shade trees to cover them, the sun dries out their soil moisture and burns their foliage before they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaa bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la hu baaha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni eshã baai lɛ dani amɛdara.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their blossoms before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of soil nutrients like calcium and boron. The plant drops flowers to save its energy for survival rather than fruit production.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium kɛ boron Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, sunken spots at the bottom while still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit while it forms. It usually happens when dry soil prevents the roots from carrying soil minerals up to the fruit smoothly.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni efeɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa beni shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ sũ mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ aduawai lɛ ahe.

english: How can I keep my farm soil moist for longer without spending money on continuous watering?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni mikɛ shika tsuuu nii yɛ nu ni mikɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ he?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, blocks the sun from heating up the soil. This keeps moisture trapped in the ground longer and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu la lɛ naa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ akadɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ, ni jwɛi lɛ akaye nɔ.

english: Why should I plant cassava together with leguminous crops like cowpea on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei tamɔ tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Cowpea plants capture nitrogen directly from the air and feed it back into the soil through their roots. Planting them alongside heavy-feeding crops like cassava enriches the soil naturally without needing extra artificial fertilizers.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei ni yeɔ kooloi babaoo, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfee lɛ afata he.

english: How do weeds actually slow down the growth of my cassava crops if I do not clear them early?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha mi-cassava tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji mijieee amɛ mra?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal light, water, and soil nutrients meant for your plants. Early weeding stops pests from hiding in the field and allows your crops to grow strong without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akatee ŋmɔji amli. ni oye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara waa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: How does spacing my maize plants out in straight rows help them yield bigger ears?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmãa tsei ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ toi wuji?

english: Planting in organized rows gives every single plant equal access to sunlight, air movement, and soil nutrients. It also makes it easier to weed and care for the farm without accidentally stepping on young plants.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni nyiɛɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo hu akɛ abaajie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni anáaa tsei bibii anɔ yɛ oshara mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers stay small and crooked underground instead of growing long and big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee agbo lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep, and well-drained soil mounds to expand. Hard or stony ground blocks the tuber from growing straight down, while poor soil fertility limits how much food the plant can store in the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia gɔŋ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni egbɛ eshwa. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi tsiɔ bulbs naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ shi tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ haa niyenii ni tsei baanyɛ ato yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my vegetable crops grow strong leaf shoots but fail to produce large yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shi amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Using fertilizers that are too high in nitrogen makes plants spend all their energy growing tall green leaves instead of flowers and fruits. Balancing soil feed with phosphorus and potassium promotes strong fruit growth.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai ni kɛlɛ, ni ji eŋɔli yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ to phosphorus kɛ potassium he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants suddenly full of holes and looking eaten?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai eyi kɛ bu ni etamɔ nɔ ni aye lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed inside the central leaves of the plant. Catching them early with recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract prevents them from destroying the growing point of the maize.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛba lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei ni ŋmãa lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra non-fruiting branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni wooo yibii kɛjɛ mi cacao tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can circulate freely. This keeps the farm dry, which prevents fungal diseases like black pod rot and helps the tree put its energy into producing cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod rot naa, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do I need to leave tall shade trees on my cocoa farm instead of cutting them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishi tsei kakadaji lɛ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mafo tsei lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa naturally grows best in partial shade. Tall shade trees protect young and mature cocoa from harsh sunlight, conserve soil moisture during the dry season, and prolong the productive life of your farm.
ga: Cocoa daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ shade lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii kɛ mɛi ni eda lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni oha nibii ni afeɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashihilɛ aya hiɛ

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally during dry periods to conserve water and protect its roots underground. Once the rainy season starts again, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Kɛji akɛ ebote nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni ebaada bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to manufacture food for the roots. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight, prevents leaves from rotting on wet soil, and results in larger tubers.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha amɛshishifãi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni da fe tsutsu lɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over in strong winds right when the fruit bunches grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ aduawai wuji pɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and become top-heavy when bearing fruit. Heaping extra soil around the base and supporting heavy fruiting stems with bamboo or wooden props stops them from falling over.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe wa kɛji amɛwo yibii. Okɛ shikpɔŋ krokomɛi ato Base lɛ he ni okɛ ŋmeii loo tsei afi tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: How do I know if my soil needs chemical fertilizer or animal manure?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia tsofai loo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If crop leaves look pale yellow and growth is slow, the soil lacks essential nutrients. Animal manure builds long-term soil health and holds water, while chemical fertilizer provides quick food for fast-growing crops like maize.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edalɛ yaa hiɛ fioo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Manure maa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei ni daa oya tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ niyenii oya.

english: Why do some farmers plant cowpeas or groundnuts in between their maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and naturally fertilize the soil. Intercropping them with maize improves soil fertility, suppresses weed growth, and gives you two crops from the same land.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Tsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa Ni ehaa onine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping soil continuously moist with grass mulch helps stabilize soil temperature and moisture.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because plants absorb moisture before the day gets hot. Evening watering leaves foliage wet overnight, which encourages fungal diseases to grow on leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli gbɛkɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baa

english: How do I know when it is the right time to start planting my seeds after the first rains fall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje dumɔwui adumɔ shishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the rains become steady, usually after two or three good rains that thoroughly soak the soil. Planting after just the very first rain can kill your seeds if a long dry stretch follows.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ be fɛɛ be. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbo kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni amɛgbi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: If maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants will fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and tall with very small ears of corn or no yield at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmãa toi bibii waa loo amɛwooo nɔ ko kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer can fix this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the specific nutrients maize needs from the soil and allows pests that feed on maize to build up. Alternating with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients back into the land.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, holds moisture well without staying waterlogged, crumbles easily in your hands, and contains living organisms like earthworms.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli. Efoɔ oya yɛ nine mli, ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli.

english: Why do insects seem to damage my crops much more during the dry season than the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, wild plants dry up, so insects move to your green farm crops looking for water and food. Heat also causes pest populations to multiply much faster.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, koo mli tsei baagbi. No sɛɛ lɛ, kooloi bibii yaa oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli koni amɛyatao nu kɛ niyenii. Dɔlɛ hu haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ oya.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and look stunted during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl to protect the plant from losing too much water in extreme heat, but severe curling can also be a sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by small whiteflies.
ga: Yucca baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ebu tso lɛ he koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Shi ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ afee ŋmɔlɔ mosaic hela he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Why is it good practice to plant plantain trees alongside young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs to survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hɔɔŋ. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ haa.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my cassava on the same farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with cassava works well because cowpeas cover the ground quickly to prevent weeds and add nitrogen to the soil while the cassava grows slowly overhead.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmei lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya koni jwɛi akabote mli ni ekɛ nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa fiofio yɛ yiteŋ lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested corn rot or develop mold when I store it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji akɛ akɛto kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Corn rots in storage when it is bagged before it is completely dry. Any remaining moisture allows fungi and mold to grow, so corn must be thoroughly dried in the sun until the kernels are hard before storing.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa. Fɛ̃i fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani akɛto.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning when the sun is very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves are tender and easily damaged. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted alongside them to filter the sunlight and keep the soil moist while their roots mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛfiteɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. koni ekɛjie hulu la lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are my young maize plants developing ragged holes in their leaves with tiny caterpillars hiding inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ bu yɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Ekɛ ehe ewo koni lɛ mli

english: This is characteristic of the Fall Armyworm. The moths lay eggs on the leaves, and once hatched, the caterpillars crawl deep into the central leaf funnel where it is dark and moist to feed safely away from heat and predators.
ga: Enɛ ji bɔ ni Fall Armyworm lɛ yɔɔ. Kpɔŋɔ lɛ woɔ ewui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni kɛ́ efɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Eji he ko ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni edɔ ni abaanyɛ aye nii yɛ shweshweeshwe, ni dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop almost all their leaves during the dry season, and does it mean the plant is dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miigbo?

english: Dropping leaves during hot, dry weather is the cassava plant's natural way of saving water. The plant is not dying; it goes into a resting phase to protect itself until the rains return, relying on energy stored in its underground roots.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni egbi lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni ŋmei tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ. Tso lɛ gbooo, eyaa hejɔɔmɔ mli koni ebu ehe he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plants before any tomatoes start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures become too high or when there is sudden water stress. Severe heat damages the pollen, preventing fertilization, which causes the plant to discard the unpollinated blooms.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen ŋmeii. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Enɛ haa tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi ni fɔmɔ bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I leave all the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ midumɔwui titrii lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Leaving too many shoots (suckers) forces the main mother plant to share soil nutrients and water with them. Pruning away excess suckers directs maximum food back to the main plant, resulting in larger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ amɛ agba niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ he sane. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ekɛ niyenii babaoo kuɔ sɛɛ baa tso titri lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantain tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very tall with dark green leaves, but the corn cobs remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa lɛ? Shi ŋmãa lɛ ji bibioo lolo.

english: This usually happens when there is an imbalance of nutrients in the soil, such as too much nitrogen and not enough phosphorus or potassium. Excess nitrogen encourages lush stem and leaf growth at the expense of fruit and grain production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ eshɛɛɛ he, tamɔ nitrogen babaoo. ni fɔsfɔs loo potasium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii kɛ baai lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa aduawai kɛ dumɔwui lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb tall sticks to produce big tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji aba lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to capture as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which is then sent down into the soil to expand and build the tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, atsuɔ amɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee bulbs.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking into tight clusters?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by sap-sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids, or by a virus carried by these insects. As they suck the juices from young leaves, the leaf tissues distort and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ hiɛɔ beni emuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ kɛbaa Baai lɛ amli fãji lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow well when standing in water, while my other crops die if flooded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-flat rice lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu mli lɛ? be mli ni tsei krokomɛi Ani minɔ lɛ baagbo kɛji nu afua ba enɔ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels in their stems that transport oxygen down to their roots, allowing them to survive underwater. Flooding also prevents common land weeds from growing and competing with the rice.
ga: Rice plants have special internal air chambers that transport oxygen down to the roots. Ehaa anyɛɔ ahiɔ shi yɛ nu shishi. Flooding also prevents common soil weeds from growing and competing with rice.

english: Why do my cowpea roots have small round bumps on them, and are they a disease I should clean off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? Ni ani amɛji helai ni esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ mihe?

english: Those small bumps are root nodules, which are very beneficial. They house friendly soil bacteria that take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer that feeds the cowpea plant and improves the soil for future crops.
ga: Those little bumps are root lumps, which are very useful. Amɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ su ni heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsina tsei niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashia.

english: Can I really get a good harvest if I am farming on a small piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná ŋmaa kpakpa diɛŋtsɛ kɛji midu nii yɛ he bibioo ko?

english: Yes, even a small plot can produce high yields if managed properly. Using high-yielding crop varieties, proper plant spacing, timely weeding, and efficient soil nourishment allows you to maximize output from limited land.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔji bibii po Ebaanyɛ ekɛ sɛɛnamɔi babaoo aba kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni mɔɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Ehaa onyɛɔ owoɔ yibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ he ko ni faaa.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that dry out quickly under direct sun. They need partial shade from food crops like plantains or shade trees during their early years to keep the soil moist and protect them from harsh heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli yɛ amɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin, weak, and produce smaller harvests compared to crops planted with proper spacing.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii, amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko kɛ akɛto tsei ni adu yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are missing key nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged. Adding organic manure or the right fertilizer can restore nutrients and help leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha niyenii mli hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ, ni eye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: If I add a lot of fertilizer to my farm, will my crops grow twice as fast?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata ŋmɔ lɛ he Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya shii enyɔ?

english: No, using too much fertilizer can burn the roots of your crops and damage the soil. It is best to follow recommended application amounts so plants get just enough nutrients to grow healthily.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooonyiɛ tsofa ni akɛhaa lɛ sɛɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my crops drop off before turning into fruits or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers usually drop off due to plant stress, such as severe dry weather, insect damage, or a lack of specific nutrients like potassium. Keeping plants watered and managing pests helps flowers stay on and produce pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi yɛ tsei lɛ ahe haomɔi tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii, loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ tamɔ potassium ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do some cocoa farms produce many pods while others nearby produce very few?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: High-yielding cocoa farms usually benefit from good pruning practices, regular pest and disease control, proper soil nutrition, and the use of modern, improved cocoa varieties that naturally produce more pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ náa ŋmɔji ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he sɛɛ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui daa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni sa kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni kɛ adebɔɔ mli woɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii.

english: Why is it necessary to cut off weak branches and excess leaves from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ niji bibii kɛ baai ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unproductive branches so sunlight and air can reach all parts of the tree. This reduces fungal diseases like black pod and allows the tree to send its energy directly into growing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ajieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ hei fɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni etsɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers encourage planting different crops together on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi adumɔ he hewalɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Intercropping allows plants to help one another. For instance, growing food crops alongside young cash crops provides temporary shade, reduces soil erosion, and improves overall farm productivity from one field.
ga: Tsei ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ haa tsei lɛ yeɔ amɛbuaa amɛhe. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shika ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Ha shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi ni oha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ kɛjɛ he kome.

english: How does the start of the rainy season affect when I should plant my crops?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee saa be ni esa akɛ adu nii lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting immediately after the first major, consistent rains ensures seeds have enough moisture to germinate and establish strong root systems before any dry spell occurs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli wa dani hɔmɔ be ko aba.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight and dry wind. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains or shade trees around them acts as a canopy, protecting the cocoa from intense heat and keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ dumɔwui loo shade tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta Ebuɔ kookoo he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my maize plants keep falling over whenever strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over easily when their root system is shallow or weakened by soil insects and shallow planting. Mound soil around the base of the stems (earthing up) during weeding to give the roots a stronger anchor in the ground.
ga: Abɛi gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ dumɔ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ hewɔ. Okɛ sũ abɔle tso lɛ shishi (shikpɔŋ) yɛ jwɛi shwiemɔ be mli koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ akpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni akuuu mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open from the expanding tubers below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni eshi tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ bulb ni mli elɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out small and crooked instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand easily downwards. If the soil is hard, stony, or compacted, the growing tuber struggles to push through, resulting in small, bent, or deformed shapes.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa kɛya shi oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, bulbs ni miida lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ bibioo, ni ebɔle ehe loo efite.

english: Why does my plantain tree suddenly collapse right when the fruit bunch is growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji aduawai akutsei lɛ je shishi amɛdara pɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that can be destroyed under the soil by pests like banana weevils or microscopic worms. Prop up heavy bunches with strong wooden Y-sticks and plant clean stems to prevent the tree from toppling.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni kooloi tamɔ banana ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ abote shikpɔŋ shishi. Fiɔ kuu lɛ sɛɛ waa Kɛ tso ni mli wa ni tamɔ Y atsu nii ni odu tso lɛ shishi ni he tse koni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why are the bottom tips of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting while on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ najiaŋdamɔlɔi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This rot happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering. Water your tomato plants consistently and add wood ash or lime to the soil to provide the necessary calcium.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Okɛ nu awo o-tomato tsei lɛ amli daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo lime awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha calcium ni he hiaa lɛ aba.

english: What is making ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the center core?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center shoot of the maize plant. Check your farm early in the morning to apply recommended organic ash solutions or targeted pest controls directly into the plant funnel.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi ni okɛ organic ash solution ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small cups and refusing to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛkpoo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids that attack young leaves and spread plant viruses. Spraying the leaves with neem leaf extract or mild soap solutions helps clear these insects so the plant can grow normally.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni tutuaa baai bibii ni egbɛɔ helai eshwaa tsei amli Ni akɛ neem baa mli nu loo samla ni mli ejɔ baashwie baa lɛ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ adara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are all the flowers falling off my cashew trees without producing any nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ nɔ ni ŋmeii ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cashew flowers drop off mainly due to insect attacks or fungal diseases that thrive during damp weather. Pruning old branches to let sunlight into the canopy keeps the tree dry and reduces the disease and insect attack on flowers.
ga: Cashew fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni yaa hiɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Niji ni egbɔ ni afolɔ koni hulu la ashɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni egbiɔ. ni eha helai kɛ kooloi ni tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ aba shi

english: Cowpeas and beans draw nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant finishes growing and rots into the soil, it leaves behind natural fertilizer that feeds the next crop without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong leaves. This often happens when the soil is poor or when heavy rains wash nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with big leaves but only give me tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in very rich soil, it spends all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots below ground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why did my crops burn and die after I placed dry fertilizer right at the base of their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ewo tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is very strong like salt. Placing it directly against the stem pulls water out of the plant's roots and burns them. You should always apply fertilizer a few inches away from the stem in moist soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he wa waa tamɔ ŋmei. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni eshã amɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi inchii fioo komɛi.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa trees need to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition forces them to stretch tall and thin instead of growing thick and strong.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ nyɛ amɛnɔ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee shwiili moŋ fe ni amɛaatsɔ shwiili ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up and droop during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense to protect itself from losing water in intense heat. The plant reduces its leaf size exposed to the sun to conserve moisture until the air cools down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni elaajeɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. Tsei lɛ baaha amɛbaai ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ anɔ aba shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do flowers drop off my tomato plants without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when they experience water stress. The plant aborts the flowers to save its own life when conditions are too harsh to produce fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛkɛ nu he haomɔ kpe. Tso lɛ baashi efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala beni shihilɛi lɛ mli bawo wu tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ewo yibii lɛ.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the soil when I plant right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni miduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain often warms up dry soil without providing enough lasting moisture. If heat builds up in the soil without follow-up rain, seeds suffocate and rot before they can sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa haaa. Kɛji dɔlɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be fɛɛ be. Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to harsh local conditions. They are aggressive feeders that pull water and nutrients from the soil much faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ebɔ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe. Amɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the young leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and curling upward into tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curled and twisted pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or aphids feeding on the juice underneath new leaves, causing them to deform as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai heei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ haa amɛfiteɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is usually black pod disease, a fungal infection triggered by high humidity and heavy rainfall. Clearing weeds, pruning branches to let in sunlight, and removing infected pods helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛbaa. weeding Tsei ni afolɔ koni hulu la ashɛ he ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do diseased pods need to be removed from the farm instead of just being left on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Diseased pods left on the farm ground still hold live fungus spores. Raindrops bounce off the ground and splash these spores back onto healthy trees, continuing the cycle of infection.
ga: Infected pods left on the farm floor still contain live fungal spores. Raindrops bounce off the ground and splash these spores back onto healthy plants. ni no hewɔ lɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ yaa nɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut down a cocoa tree if it has a virus disease instead of just treating it with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ? Cocoa tsei ni yɔɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli Yɛ tsofa kɛkɛ ni akɛbaatsa lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Viral diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus live inside the tree's sap system, where chemical sprays cannot reach. Cutting down the infected tree and neighboring trees is the only known way to protect the rest of your farm from infection.
ga: Helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli, tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli. ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ afolɔmɔ ji gbɛ pɛ ni ale ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hela he.

english: Is it normal for new leaves on my crops to grow small and twisted?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baafee bibii ni efite?

english: No, small or twisted leaves are often caused by sap-sucking insects or viral infections that damage the growing shoots. Extension officers can help identify whether you need targeted spraying or tree removal.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu loo helai ni baa mɔ nɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai bibii loo ni efite lɛ baa. Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni amɛna kɛji ehe miihia ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tso ni ajieɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do insects like capsids attack my cocoa trees mostly when new shoots appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids lɛ tutuaa mi-cocoa tsei lɛ babaoo kɛ́ ŋmeii heei je kpo lɛ?

english: Capsids prefer soft, tender growth because it is easier to pierce and full of moisture. When cocoa trees flush with fresh leaves, capsids multiply quickly to feed on the young tissue.
ga: Capsids sumɔɔ ni amɛdara blɛoo ejaakɛ amɛboteɔ mli oya ni ŋmɔtɔ eyi mli obɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai heei ha kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ, Capsids lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya ni eyeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo.

english: What makes my cocoa trees dry up and look burned during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo tsei lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛshã yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli?

english: Dry winds and direct hot sun during the harmattan dry out soil moisture faster than roots can absorb it. Shade trees and mulching around the root area keep soil cool and retain water.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ harmattana beaŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ mli egbiɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Tsei ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli kɛ shishifãi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni nu hu hiɔ shi.

english: How does too much standing water in my farm affect my crops during heavy rains?
ga: Te nu ni damɔ shi fe nine yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Waterlogged soil starves plant roots of air, causing them to rot. Damaged roots cannot absorb nutrients, making the plant weak and easy target for fungal diseases.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ehaa helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baanyɛ atswa lɛ oya.

english: What causes the leaves on my cocoa trees to turn yellow and drop off early?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean a lack of vital soil nutrients like nitrogen, or severe root damage from pests or excess water. Applying compost, manure, or balanced fertilizer helps restore leaf health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ faaa, loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ waa kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo nu ni fa fe nine lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees stop bearing pods even though the leaves look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ekomɛi ekpa ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Trees can stop producing if they are getting too much dense shade, lacking flower-boosting nutrients like phosphorus, or silently carrying early-stage viral diseases that drain energy away from pod production.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ akpa yibiiwoo kɛji amɛná hulutsoo ni mli wa tsɔ. Niyenii ni haa fɔfɔi yaa hiɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ, loo hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa ni yɔɔ dioo mra. No baajie hewalɛ kɛjɛ pods lɛ afeemɔ mli.

english: How does keeping shade trees on my cocoa farm help my crops stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Shade trees act as a natural shield against hot sunshine, reduce wind damage, hold soil moisture during dry spells, and create a cooler climate that slows down insect pest breeding.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ aba shi Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afɔɔ shi lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there is hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight when they are small. Planting shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa protects the young cocoa trees from burning and keeps the soil moist until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ tsei lɛ ahe waa.

english: Why are the leaves of my corn plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on corn usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food corn needs to grow well. Applying animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and boost crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Koolooi amli ŋmeii loo nitrogen ŋmeii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ, ni ehaa tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the leaves inside the center of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young corn leaves. You can protect your farm by spraying approved organic or chemical treatments early, or putting clean dry sand/ash into the plant funnels.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ mra lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ ŋã/ashwishwɛ ni mli tse ni egbi awo ŋã ni aduɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know which direction to push a cassava stick into the ground when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni esa akɛ matsi ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Look at the small buds or raised notches on the cassava stem where leaves used to grow; these buds must point upward toward the sky. Planting the stem upside down causes low sprouts and poor crop yield.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. loo okadii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ yɛ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii hu akawo yibii kpakpai.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture maximum sunlight for making plant food. When leaves receive full sunlight, the plant directs more energy underground to grow larger tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni akɛ tsei fee. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa lɛ Tso lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, sunken patches at the bottom before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efoɔ shishi dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or irregular watering during fruit growth. Keeping the soil steadily moist and adding lime or manure helps prevent these black spots.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. This is caused by a lack of calcium in plants or inconsistent watering during fruit growth. Keeping the soil moist and adding lime or manure will help prevent these dark spots.

english: Why are flowers falling off my pepper plants without producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni pepper yibii ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat or heat stress combined with dry soil. Watering regularly during hot weather and providing light shade helps flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi fata he lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Is it safe to plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait for two or three steady rains so the soil is thoroughly wet. The first rain often dries up quickly, which can scorch newly germinated seeds in the dry ground.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ gbiɔ oya. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ashã shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry weeds and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ ni jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the ground with dry materials, called mulching, acts like a blanket to keep soil cool, stop water from drying up in the heat, and slowly decompose into natural soil nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Prevents water from drying out when heated and gradually decomposes into natural nutrients in the soil.

english: Can I plant cowpeas or beans together on the same land with my corn?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmeii?

english: Yes, beans and corn grow well together because beans pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, naturally fertilizing the corn and improving your overall harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii feɔ ekome kɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa o-abele lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa o-ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and make food, or when the ground is waterlogged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. This is the main nutrient that plants need to stay green for cooking. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the hot afternoon even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil, so they temporarily droop to save moisture and recover by evening.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or water is inconsistent, which prevents proper pollination and fruit formation.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ pollination ni sa kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ naa.

english: What makes my vegetable crops grow very slowly and stay small even though I clear weeds regularly?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-aduawai lɛ daaa blɛoo waa ni amɛfeɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ amɛ jwɛi daa moŋ?

english: Stunted growth usually happens when the soil is depleted of nutrients or packed too tightly, making it hard for roots to expand and feed the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shweremɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛalɛɛ ni amɛye amɛbua tso lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting plantains alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains yɛ mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight; fast-growing plantain trees provide necessary shade and maintain soil moisture while the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. The rapidly growing seedlings will provide necessary shade and maintain soil moisture as the cocoa matures.

english: Why should I rotate my maize crop with groundnuts or beans instead of planting maize every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, while legumes like groundnuts put nitrogen back into the earth naturally, keeping the land fertile for future crops.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Meanwhile, legumes such as peanuts naturally return nitrogen to the soil. Koni akwɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my tall maize plants fall over whenever heavy rains hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over when roots are shallow or the soil is too loose; piling up earth around the base of the plant gives roots a stronger grip.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to swell and crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How does spreading dry grass or dead leaves around my crops help them during dry periods?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛbɔleɔ Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material acts as a blanket that stops the sun from evaporating water, keeping the dirt moist and cool for longer.
ga: Tsoi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ hulu lɛ mli. Ehaa muji feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my land than the actual seeds I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh soils and absorb nutrients rapidly, whereas domesticated crops require extra care, proper soil preparation, and time to establish.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ ni amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shĩa lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko. Shikpɔŋ he saamɔ ni sa kɛ adebɔɔ be

english: Officer, can cold night temperatures really harm my crops here in Ghana?
ga: Amralofoi Ani fɛ̃i ni baa gbɛkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ awui?

english: Yes. When night temperatures drop significantly down to around 10 to 12 degrees Celsius, tropical plants suffer from cold stress, which slows down their internal processes and retards overall growth.
ga: Hɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ ba shi waa kɛyashɛ aaafee degree Celsius 10 kɛyashi 12 lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni latsaa yɔɔ lɛ naa fɛ̃i he haomɔ. Enɛ haa mligbɛ nifeemɔi lɛ baa shi ni ehaa dalɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my plants look stressed during the dry season even when there is strong sunlight during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiifee basaa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, hot sunny mornings are often followed by very cold nights. This severe temperature fluctuation creates intense stress for the plants, making it hard for them to recover between day and night.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Bei pii lɛ, gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i waa nyiɛɔ leebi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo be ni tsakeɔ waa nɛɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaaná hewalɛ yɛ shwane kɛ gbɛkɛ teŋ.

english: How do I know if the night weather is getting too cold for my crops to grow properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji gbɛkɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ miifee fɛ̃i tsɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: A good practical rule is that if the night is cold enough that you feel freezing and need a thick blanket to sleep, your crops are also feeling that cold stress, which slows down their leaf growth.
ga: Mla kpakpa ni esa akɛ otsɔ nɔ otsu he nii ji: Kɛ́ fɛ̃i miiho waa gbɛkɛ ni omiifee ais ni ehe miihia ni owo atadei ni mli tse ni okɛwɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanu fɛ̃i lɛ he haomɔ he. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ adara blɛoo.

english: Are tropical crops in Ghana sensitive to temperatures as low as 10 or 12 degrees Celsius?
ga: Ani tsei ni yɔɔ Ghana shikpɔji ni mli edɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ nuɔ he waa kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi tamɔ digrii Celsius 10 loo 12?

english: Yes, tropical crops are adapted to warm weather, so when temperatures drop near 10 degrees at night, it chills the plants and temporarily stunts their natural development.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tropical tsei lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi ni ebɛŋkɛ digrii 10 gbɛkɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni ebaatsi bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ naa yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Why is it so important for my crop leaves to grow very well early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mitso lɛ baai lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Strong and healthy leaf growth is essential because leaves capture sunlight to make food for the plant, giving it the strength needed to withstand adverse weather conditions like cold nights.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adalɛ he hiaa ejaakɛ baa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ hulu la ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Enɛ haa enáa hewalɛ ni ekɛdamɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii tamɔ gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my crop leaves look weak or stunted after a cold night during the harmattan?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa loo amɛhe ejɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i eho yɛ harmatta beaŋ lɛ?

english: Extreme drops in night temperature weaken the leaves because the cold prevents the plant from transporting nutrients efficiently, causing leaf expansion to slow down.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni baa shi oya gbɛkɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ejaakɛ fɛ̃i lɛ haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ mli lɛɛɔ blɛoo.

english: Why do my young plants stop growing even when they get plenty of morning sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛnáa leebi hulu babaoo moŋ?

english: Even with strong morning sunlight, if the plants experience freezing cold temperatures the night before, their growth cycle gets disrupted and leaf development stalls.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ leebi lɛ moŋ Shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ na fɛ̃i gbɛkɛ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ hu? Amɛdalɛ gbɛ lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ adalɛ hu fiteɔ.

english: Does strong afternoon sunlight compensate for cold night temperatures on my farm?
ga: Ani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ awo fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he nyɔmɔ?

english: No, intense daytime heat combined with low night temperatures actually doubles the weather stress on the plant, making leaves struggle to grow properly.
ga: Dabi, hulutsoo ni naa wa ni baa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛ gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni baa shi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he haomɔ ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ toi enyɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetables take much longer to mature during the dry, cold months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji ni fɛ̃i kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: The cold night air during the dry season forces plants into a survival mode, slowing down their leaf expansion and delaying overall growth and maturity.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Ha baai lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ aba shi ni oha amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛshweremɔ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: What happens to the leaves of my plants when night temperatures drop sharply during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni baa mitso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ ba shi waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Sharp drops in night temperature cause the leaves to chill, reducing their ability to photosynthesize effectively once the sun comes up the next morning.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni baa shi waa gbɛkɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ amli jɔɔ. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛfeɔ fotosintɛsis jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ te shi enɔ jetsɛremɔ.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow, it usually means the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to stay green and grow tall. Adding well-rotted manure or NPK fertilizer helps restore the plant's health.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ko ni he hiaa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have wide leaves that create natural shade, keeping the cocoa cool and protecting the soil from drying out during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed all their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ shwie shi yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves in dry weather to save water and protect itself from drought. The plant is still alive underground, saving its energy inside the roots until the rains come back.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Tso lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers if they lack sufficient water, if pests attack the blossoms, or if the soil lacks potassium. Providing light shade and controlling sap-sucking insects helps the tree hold onto its flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Kplukai fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shade ni akɛhaa kɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ akudɔmɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Yam roots need soft, deep, and well-mounded soil to grow downward easily. Hard or stony soil blocks the tuber, causing it to bend, split, or stay small.
ga: Sweet potato shishifãi hia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛdara kɛya shi oya. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo tɛi komɛi yɛ ni tsiɔ yitso lɛ naa, ni no haa ekɔɔ, efoɔ, loo efeɔ bibioo.

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium or uneven watering while the fruit is forming. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying compost helps stop it.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifɔlɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa shweremɔ.

english: Why do some cowpea crops spread across the soil while others stand up like bushes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina tsei komɛi gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi teɔ shi tamɔ tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants come in different varieties. Spreading types crawl across the ground to protect the soil from sun and weeds, while bush varieties grow upright to make harvesting easier.
ga: Ayɛ tsina tsei srɔtoi babaoo. Henɔi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ jwɛi ahe. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ daa ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ koni eha ŋmaakpamɔ afee mlɛo.
